preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Treatment Refusal (by Both Patient and Physician)
preguntas.subtema: The provider's refusal · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k212 · CMA II.E.4 · RMA I.C.4 · NCMA 4.1
preguntas.pregunta: May a physician decline to take on a patient or to provide a treatment that has been requested?
opciones: Yes, as when the treatment is not indicated by the history given
Yes, but only where another provider has already agreed to take over
No, once the person has been registered as a patient of the practice
No, unless an emergency elsewhere makes the schedule impossible
preguntas.explicacion: The right runs in both directions. A physician may in many circumstances decline to enter the relationship or to give a treatment: a referral may arrive for one particular treatment and taking it on look unwarranted, or the history provided may not indicate the treatment at all. The privilege is old, going back to the Hippocratic era, yet no law protects it as broadly as the profession claims, and the laws that do protect it usually rest on freedom of religion.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Crutches", Preparation; and MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using crutches
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.b · RMA III.H.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: Axillary crutches are being fitted. Where should the shoulder pad sit and how should the elbow be?
opciones: About two finger widths below the axilla, with the elbow flexed some 30 degrees
Snug against the axilla itself, with the elbow flexed to about 30 degrees
About two finger widths below the axilla, with the elbow held nearly straight
About four finger widths below the axilla, with the elbow flexed to 90 degrees
preguntas.explicacion: The pad stops roughly two inches, or two fingers, short of the armpit with the shoulder relaxed, the grip is set so the elbow bends about 30 degrees, and the tips rest some six inches outside the feet. The patient is told never to rest the armpit on the pad. Patient handouts give the gap as one to one and a half inches, measured the same way.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(ix) and (d)(3)(ix)(D), Gloves
preguntas.subtema: Glove exception for blood donation · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: In which setting may an employer decide that gloves are not routinely required for every phlebotomy?
opciones: A volunteer blood donation center, under conditions such as gloves for trainees
A clinical laboratory, if it applies Universal Precautions to all specimens
An outpatient draw station, if the phlebotomist has no cuts on the hands
Any facility, if the employee documents that gloves reduce manual dexterity
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix) requires gloves for vascular access procedures with one carve-out, (d)(3)(ix)(D): a volunteer blood donation center whose employer judges routine gloving unnecessary. Even there the employer must periodically reevaluate the policy, make gloves available to anyone who wants them, never discourage their use, and require them when the employee has cuts or breaks in the skin, when hand contamination is likely such as with an uncooperative donor, and during phlebotomy training. No other setting gets the exception.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Expert Witness", Function
preguntas.subtema: Legal terms · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What is the medical expert witness first asked to do in a malpractice case?
opciones: Establish the standard of care that applied to that case
Establish the damages the patient's family should receive
Establish whether the defendant's license should be revoked
Establish which of the two parties told the truth in discovery
preguntas.explicacion: The expert's role has three parts, and the first is establishing what standard of care applies to the case at hand. Next comes an opinion on whether the care departed from it, and only then, if it did, an opinion on whether that caused the injury alleged. Damages are for the jury, and licensure is a matter for the state board.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1 and Annex E; and OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii)
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: After a draw with an evacuated tube system, how does the WHO say the needle and holder should be disposed of?
opciones: Discard barrel and needle together as a single unit whenever possible
Unscrew the needle by hand and drop it into the sharps container, keeping the barrel
Recap the needle with both hands, then remove it from the barrel for reuse
Leave the needle on the barrel and place both in the regulated-waste bag
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 says to discard the barrel and needle as a single entity where possible; if the barrel must be reused, the needle is removed with a one-hand scoop technique or with a sharps container that has a needle removal hold, always one-handed. Annex E adds that an exposed used needle is never disassembled with bare hands, and OSHA prohibits two-handed recapping and removal except where no alternative is feasible.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Section 4, Scope
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which products fall outside the scope of the FDA guidance on sharps injury prevention features?
opciones: Sharps containers and needle recapping devices
Winged sets and retractable safety lancet devices
Insulin syringes and their orange needle covers
Blood collection needles fitted with a shield
preguntas.explicacion: That guidance covers medical devices carrying an active or a passive component that guards the user against a sharps injury. It says plainly that it does not deal with sharps containers or with needle recapping devices, which are handled by separate guidance of their own.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b(1) · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: The beat under the fingers is irregular. How is the rate counted?
opciones: For a full minute, because a longer count is more accurate when the rhythm is irregular
For 15 seconds and multiplied by 4, which keeps the intake moving without losing accuracy
For 10 seconds and multiplied by 6, then repeated on the opposite wrist for comparison
For 30 seconds and multiplied by 2, then rounded to the nearest multiple of 10 beats
preguntas.explicacion: Short counts multiplied up are usually good enough on a regular pulse: 30 seconds doubled, or even 10 or 15 seconds multiplied by 6 or 4. An irregular rhythm breaks that assumption, because the beats are not evenly spread, so the count runs the full minute. Rounding a recorded value to the nearest ten is a documented error, not a rule.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Venipuncture technique · CPT D3 3E k9 k56 k60 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's coagulation panel keeps coming back hemolyzed. Which two features of the draw are singled out to protect it?
opciones: An atraumatic venipuncture and as little tourniquet time as possible
A large tube volume and as long a tourniquet time as the vein allows
A fasting patient and a puncture placed over the basilic vein instead
A second discard tube and a needle finer than twenty-three gauge
preguntas.explicacion: For coagulation work the puncture should be atraumatic and made without delay, and the tourniquet should stay on as briefly as possible, because both faults produce artifacts such as hemolysis. The gauge suggested runs from nineteen to twenty-two, with the wider end preferred for factor assays.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Steps 10 and 11
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5D k89 · PBT III.D · CCMA 3E14 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic's driver takes blood samples to the hospital laboratory every afternoon. Besides a rack or padded holder for the tubes, what must the vehicle carry according to WHO?
opciones: A blood spillage kit, so that a broken sample can be cleaned up safely on the way
A portable centrifuge, so that serum can be separated if the trip is delayed
A carbon dioxide incubator, so that culture specimens keep their organisms viable
A second set of empty tubes, so that a broken sample can be recollected on arrival
preguntas.explicacion: For transporting blood samples outside a hospital, WHO asks that the vehicle be equipped with a blood spillage kit, because a sample can break during transport just as it can in the phlebotomy area; the spill is then handled with gloves and, for large spills, a gown or apron, paper towels that go into infectious waste, and a freshly prepared bleach solution. Multiple tubes travel in a rack or padded holder precisely to avoid that breakage.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose screening tests during pregnancy (007562), How the Test is Performed and How to Prepare for the Test
preguntas.subtema: Gestational screening preparation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.D patient preparation · CCMA 3E k139 fasting · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for the first step of two-step gestational screening asks what she should do about food beforehand. What do you tell her?
opciones: No fast and no diet change: the screening step needs neither one
No food or drink, apart from sips of water, for 8 to 14 hours before
Eat an unrestricted diet with 150 g of carbohydrate a day for 3 days
Eat a light breakfast exactly one hour before the appointment time
preguntas.explicacion: For the screening step the patient does not have to prepare or change her diet in any way: she drinks the glucose liquid and blood is drawn one hour later. The 8-to-14-hour fast belongs to the 3-hour follow-up test and to the one-step 75 g test; the three-day carbohydrate load is a condition of the nonpregnant diagnostic OGTT. Eating normally in the days before is the only instruction given.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1; and Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: Site by age · CPT D3 k55 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.5
preguntas.pregunta: A 4-month-old infant weighing 5 kg needs a capillary specimen. Which site does WHO Table 7.1 indicate, and where on it is the lancet placed?
opciones: The heel, on the medial or lateral plantar surface
The heel, on the posterior curve where skin is thickest
The middle or ring finger, on the side of the ball
The thumb or index finger, on the side of the ball
preguntas.explicacion: Table 7.1 assigns the heel-prick to infants from birth to about 6 months and roughly 3 to 10 kg, and the lancet goes on the medial or the lateral plantar surface; the finger-prick is for children over 6 months and over 10 kg. Chapter 7 says the posterior heel should be avoided because the bone lies only 2.33 mm beneath the skin, and the table itself warns against the thumb and index finger.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medicaid: Summary
preguntas.subtema: Government insurance plans · CCMA 5 k181 · CMAA 6 k74 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient moving to another state asks whether her Medicaid will work the same way there. How are the rules set?
opciones: The federal government sets general guidelines and each state writes its own rules
The federal government writes one single set of rules that applies in every one of the states
Each state writes its rules with no federal guideline of any kind standing above
The insurance marketplace in each state writes the rules for its own state plans
preguntas.explicacion: Medicaid, a government health insurance, helps a great many people on low incomes meet their medical bills. General guidelines for the program come from the federal government, but the rules belong to each state, and a state may ask the person to pay part of the cost of some services. Eligibility can turn on age, on pregnancy, on blindness, on disability, on income and resources, and on immigration status.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E types of consent · CCMA 3E1 · CMA E.3.b (both outlines) · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: For a routine venipuncture, what form of consent does WHO step 2 describe obtaining?
opciones: Verbal consent, after discussing the test with the patient
Written consent, signed by the patient and witnessed by staff
Implied consent, shown by the patient's presence in the clinic
Consent given by the ordering physician on the laboratory form
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO step reads: discuss the test to be performed and obtain verbal consent, adding that the patient can refuse at any point before the sampling. StatPearls describes written documentation for informed consent in general, but the WHO phlebotomy step relies on a spoken yes after an explanation. Nothing in either source lets the requester's signature stand in for the patient.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, Chapter 2.5, Table 2.5b: PQRSTU Focused Questions
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.4.b · CCMA 3A3 · NCMA 2B.4
preguntas.pregunta: In the PQRSTU framework, what does the letter U ask the patient?
opciones: What the patient believes is causing the symptom they came in with
How long the symptom has lasted and whether it comes and then goes
Whether any activity makes the symptom better or makes it worse
Where the symptom is felt and whether it moves somewhere else
preguntas.explicacion: U stands for understanding, and it asks the patient what they think is behind the problem. Provocation and palliation cover what worsens and what relieves it, region covers where it sits and whether it radiates, and timing covers when it began and whether it is constant. The framework is used for pain and works just as well for nausea, itching or breathlessness.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010); and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Capillaries
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k3 k7 (applied D3 k71) · PBT I.B.1 I.A.4 · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2 EKB 3
preguntas.pregunta: How are the vessels sampled in a capillary blood collection best described?
opciones: The smallest vessels, 5–10 μm wide, connecting arterioles and venules
The smallest arteries, about 30 μm wide, connecting arteries to capillaries
Thin-walled vessels, 8–100 μm wide, that carry blood on toward the veins
Superficial veins that run in the roof of the cubital fossa of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Capillaries are the body's smallest vessels, 5 to 10 micrometers across, linking arterioles and venules; a capillary sample is usually taken by heel or finger prick, and the narrowest capillaries just fit one erythrocyte. Arterioles average 30 micrometers or less and venules 8 to 100 micrometers, and the superficial veins of the cubital fossa are venipuncture sites, not capillaries.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k157 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: How is the machine calibrated on the voltage axis?
opciones: A signal of 1 mV moves the stylus 1 cm on the paper
A signal of 1 mV moves the stylus 1 mm on the paper
A signal of 5 mV moves the stylus 1 cm on the paper
A signal of 1 mV moves the stylus 5 cm on the paper
preguntas.explicacion: The machine is set so that one millivolt deflects the stylus by one centimeter, which is ten small squares tall. That is the standardization mark printed at the edge of the tracing, and if it is not the expected height the amplitudes on that recording cannot be compared with anything.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Bronchodilators", Adverse Effects and Mechanism of Action
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k16 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: Minutes after using a short-acting inhaler a patient reports shaky hands and a pounding heart. What explains it?
opciones: Beta-2 agonists also stir the sympathetic system, producing tremor and palpitations
Beta-2 agonists damp the sympathetic system, so the heart slows and the hands shake
Anticholinergic inhalers give tremor, dry mouth and retention within a few minutes
Paradoxical bronchospasm always opens with tremor before the airways start closing
preguntas.explicacion: The usual adverse effects of a bronchodilator come from sympathetic activation: tremor, nervousness, palpitations the patient can feel, and muscle cramps. The severe ones are paradoxical narrowing of the airway, low potassium and, rarely, myocardial infarction. Anticholinergic inhalers give a different picture, with dry mouth, urinary retention, tachycardia and constipation, and delirium in older adults.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth coverage · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with commercial insurance asks whether her plan will pay for a video visit on the same terms as an office visit. What settles that?
opciones: State parity laws, which vary and set coverage and payment
Federal law, which makes every plan pay them at the same rate
Medicare's rules, which private insurers are obliged to follow
Whether she lives in a rural area, which coverage still requires
preguntas.explicacion: Parity laws for private insurers are set state by state and they differ, so both whether a telehealth visit is covered and how much is paid for it depend on where the plan is written. Medicaid policies likewise vary by state. The rural location requirement belonged to Medicare's old originating-site rules, which were waived.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI - How to Enroll, Enrollment Information for Providers
preguntas.subtema: Eligibility without HETS · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A small practice bills Original Medicare on paper and therefore loses its HETS access. How can it still check a patient's Medicare eligibility?
opciones: By registering to use the secure internet portal its Medicare contractor provides
By telephoning the beneficiary's Medicare Advantage plan for a coverage answer
By routing the eligibility request through any clearinghouse already enrolled in HETS
By asking the patient to print her eligibility record from her own online account
preguntas.explicacion: A provider that skips the enrollment steps, or that does not send Original Medicare claims electronically, loses access to HETS. The route left open is to register for the secure internet portal of a Medicare Administrative Contractor and check eligibility there. A clearinghouse cannot stand in for the provider: enrollment is the provider's own act.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3, Hospitalized patients
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications and IV access · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse is about to insert an IV cannula and asks whether the blood tests can be drawn at the same time. What does the WHO say?
opciones: It is acceptable but not ideal, when the cannula is first inserted and before the fluids are connected
It is the preferred method, because it spares the patient a second puncture and gives identical results
It is never acceptable; specimens from any in-dwelling device carry a risk of contamination
It is acceptable only for blood cultures, which must be drawn before any fluid is connected
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 calls it acceptable though not ideal to draw blood as an in-dwelling venous device is first put in, before the cannula is connected to the intravenous fluids. The same passage forbids drawing from an access that is already in use because of false results, and notes that central line specimens taken by nurses or physicians under protocol carry a contamination risk.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Steam Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d (2027 I.C.5.b(3)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: A prevacuum steam sterilizer is loaded with wrapped supplies. What is the shortest exposure recognized for that cycle?
opciones: 4 minutes at 132 °C (270 °F)
4 minutes at 121 °C (250 °F)
30 minutes at 132 °C (270 °F)
3 minutes at 134 °C (273 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: A prevacuum sterilizer has a pump that pulls the air out of the chamber and the load before steam enters, so penetration is almost instantaneous even into porous loads and four minutes at 132 °C suffices for wrapped supplies. Thirty minutes at 121 °C is the gravity figure, and 134 °C for 3.5 minutes is the run used for the daily air-removal test, not for a load.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Physiologic Variants
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which of the superficial arm veins is typically the larger of the two?
opciones: The basilic vein, although the cephalic is sometimes larger
The cephalic vein, although the basilic is sometimes larger
The median cubital vein, which is larger than either of them
Both are the same calibre, since they drain equal territories
preguntas.explicacion: Size varies a great deal between patients, but the basilic is usually the larger superficial vein of the arm and sometimes the cephalic takes that place. Calibre alone does not decide the puncture: an artery and a nerve travel with the basilic, which makes it the riskier of the two.

preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Ethics
preguntas.subtema: Codes of ethics · CCMA 7C · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: Which principle appears in the AAMA Code of Ethics?
opciones: Respecting confidential information unless disclosure is legally required
Reporting any coworker who deviates from the practice's written protocol
Refusing to assist with a procedure the assistant personally disagrees with
Referring every request for records straight to the practice's own attorney
preguntas.explicacion: The code sets out five principles that members pledge to strive toward: rendering service with full respect for human dignity; respecting confidential information gained through employment unless the law authorizes or responsible duty requires disclosure; upholding the profession's honor and its high principles and accepting its disciplines; continually improving knowledge and skills; and taking part in community health activities.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Portal self-service · CMAA 4E k56 · CCMA 5U k172 · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.6.c · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has just moved and wants the practice to hold her new address without her having to call in. Which portal functions does ONC list?
opciones: Updating her own contact information, and downloading and completing forms
Updating her own contact information, and correcting an error in her diagnosis
Downloading and completing forms, and reading the clinician's own progress notes
Updating the image of her insurance card, and signing the notice of privacy practices
preguntas.explicacion: A portal opens round-the-clock access to allergies, medications, immunizations, recent visits, discharge summaries and results. Some go further, letting the patient message the clinician securely, ask for a refill, book a non-urgent appointment, look up benefits and coverage, pay, correct contact details, download forms and complete them, and read educational material.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A draw with a needle and syringe has finished. How are the two treated at the moment of disposal?
opciones: As a single unit, dropped straight into a robust sharps container
As two items, the needle in the sharps bin and the syringe in waste
As a single unit, but only after the needle has been re-sheathed
As two items, the syringe rinsed first and the needle discarded
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction treats a needle and syringe as one unit and asks for the used device to go immediately into a robust sharps container. The prohibition on the other side of the table is equally plain: an unprotected needle is never left lying outside that container.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Table 1; and PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process. Annals of Laboratory Medicine 2012 (PubMed Central PMC3255486, acceso abierto)" (PMC3255486)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A lavender tube arrives in the emergency laboratory with no label at all, together with a requisition for a CBC. According to the rejection criteria used by emergency laboratories, what happens to it?
opciones: It is rejected as a misidentified specimen and a new sample is requested
It is accepted if the requisition in the bag identifies the patient
It is held at 4 °C for up to 24 hours until the ward sends a label to attach to it
It is tested and the result is reported with a comment about the label
preguntas.explicacion: Unlabeled, mislabeled and mismatched samples all count as misidentification, which sits among the standing grounds on which the emergency laboratory rejects work, next to missing barcodes, the wrong container, too little volume, hemolysis, lipemia and clots. A requisition in the bag does not identify the tube; parking the sample until a label appears is relabeling by another name; and issuing a result from an unidentified tube is what those criteria exist to prevent.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: What does the blood culture bottle in the WHO order-of-draw table contain, and what is it used for?
opciones: A broth mixture that keeps microorganisms viable; aerobes, anaerobes and fungi
Sodium citrate that removes calcium; coagulation tests such as prothrombin time
Acid-citrate-dextrose that inactivates complement; HLA typing and DNA studies
A clot activator that yields serum; chemistries, serology and cross-match
preguntas.explicacion: Row 1 of Table 2.3 describes the yellow-black striped blood culture bottle: its additive is a broth mixture, its mode of action is to preserve the viability of microorganisms, and its uses are microbiology for aerobes, anaerobes and fungi. The other three descriptions are the rows for the light blue citrate tube, the pale yellow ACD tube and the red clot activator tube.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, PSNet Patient Safety Primer: Reporting Patient Safety Events
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 6 k211 · CMA I.B.11.c · 2027 I.B.10.c · CMAA 3 k44 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: Which feature does an effective event reporting system need?
opciones: A set way of reviewing the reports and turning them into action plans
A rule that names the reporter in the summary sent to the whole staff
A limit that lets only licensed providers file a report of an event
A yearly deadline by which all of the reports of the year are filed
preguntas.explicacion: Four attributes make the system work: an environment that supports reporting and guards the privacy of whoever reports, reports coming in from a broad range of personnel, summaries shared promptly, and a structured way of reviewing reports and building action plans. Reporting is usually confidential, with legal protection short of misconduct.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Measuring Your Blood Pressure: Things that can affect a reading
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives after a cigarette and a coffee. What does the technique call for?
opciones: Wait until 30 minutes have passed since the caffeine, the smoking or any exercise
Wait five minutes seated, which is enough to clear the effect of either of them
Take the reading now and add a note, since the effect of both is under 2 mm Hg
Wait 60 minutes, which is the interval given for caffeine, nicotine and exertion
preguntas.explicacion: Caffeine, nicotine and exercise inside the previous half hour all push the reading up, so the measurement is delayed until 30 minutes have gone by. Smoking within that window can raise the systolic value by as much as 20 mm Hg, far from a rounding error. The five minutes seated is a separate requirement that comes after.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k89 k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D4 k112 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: An accessioning clerk scans a specimen barcode and the screen fills with far more than the patient's name. What kind of data does such a barcode key typically pull up?
opciones: Tube and specimen type, print and collection times, the ward, and who drew it
Only the patient's names and hospital number, kept short to avoid misreads
The analyser assigned to the tube and the position it holds in the rack
The insurance carrier, the diagnosis code and the billing account number
preguntas.explicacion: In the hospital that published its rejection audit, a nine-digit internal barcode identified name, surname, gender, age, tube type, specimen type, the time the label was printed, the collection date and time, the service where the specimen was taken, the tests requested, the ordering physician and the phlebotomist. Access to those databases is restricted to clinical and laboratory staff.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5)(i), (ii) and (iii), Sharps injury log
preguntas.subtema: Who keeps the sharps log · CPT D1 k12 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which employers must keep a sharps injury log, and how must the log treat the injured worker?
opciones: Those that must keep injury records under 29 CFR part 1904, protecting the worker's confidentiality
Every employer with a single exposed worker, listing the worker's name for follow-up
Only hospitals accredited by CMS-approved organizations, identifying each worker by badge number
Only employers who have had an exposure incident, keeping the log for 30 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(5)(ii) hands the sharps injury log to any employer that already keeps the 29 CFR part 1904 log of injuries and illnesses at work, and (h)(5)(iii) holds it for the period 1904.33 sets. The entries are written so that the injured employee's confidentiality is protected, which is the opposite of listing names. Accreditation is not the test, and the 30-year period belongs to the employee medical record in (h)(1)(iv).

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(x), Engineering and Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Food storage near specimens · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: According to the standard, where may staff food and drink NOT be kept?
opciones: In refrigerators, cabinets or on benchtops where blood or OPIM is present
In any refrigerator inside the laboratory building, labeled or not
In a break-room refrigerator that lacks a fluorescent orange biohazard label
In any refrigerator that is not inspected and decontaminated on a set schedule
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(x) keeps food and drink out of any refrigerator, freezer, shelf, cabinet, countertop or benchtop that holds blood or another potentially infectious material. What decides is whether blood or OPIM is in that space, not which building it sits in or what the door says. The labels of (g)(1)(i)(A) go on refrigerators that contain blood, which is the reverse situation; a break-room refrigerator with no specimens in it needs no label and may hold lunches.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding, First Aid and DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: Soaked dressings · CPT D1 1M k37 · CMA I.B.9.a / 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
preguntas.pregunta: The dressing on a bleeding wound soaks through. What does first-aid guidance say to do?
opciones: Do not remove it; place another cloth on top and keep pressing
Remove it, rinse the wound with water, and apply a clean one
Remove it to inspect the wound, then apply a tighter bandage
Loosen the pressure so the clot is not disturbed, then re-dress
preguntas.explicacion: When blood seeps through the material held on a wound, the dressing is not removed; another cloth is placed over the first and pressure continues, and medical attention is sought right away. The guidance is equally clear on what not to do: do not peek to see whether bleeding has stopped, do not remove a dressing that has become soaked, do not probe the wound, and do not try to clean a large wound or one whose bleeding has just been brought under control. The less the wound is disturbed, the better the chance of controlling the bleeding.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: Fingerstick site · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.4 · CCMA 3D2 · CMA I.C.10.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.ii · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: For an adult fingerstick glucose, which puncture site does the procedure recommend, and which fingers are avoided?
opciones: The side of the fingertip of the 2nd, 3rd or 4th finger; the thumb, index and little finger are avoided
The center of the fingertip pad of the index finger, because it has the thickest tissue over the bone
The side of the fingertip of the little finger, because it is the least sensitive and heals the fastest
The center of the thumb pad, because its larger surface yields the biggest drop with the least squeezing
preguntas.explicacion: Puncture goes into the side of the fingertip, at its far end, on the second, third or fourth finger, where the tissue is deep enough to keep the bone out of reach. The fifth finger is avoided for tissue that may be too shallow, the thumb and index finger for being more sensitive. Lancet depth is held to 2.0 mm or less, and alternate sites such as forearm or palm are used only where the device's instructions allow them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which chest electrode is positioned before V3, and why?
opciones: V4, because V3 is then placed midway between V2 and V4
V5, because V3 is then placed midway between V2 and V5
V6, because V3 is then placed midway between V2 and V6
V1, because V3 is then placed midway between V1 and V4
preguntas.explicacion: V3 has no landmark of its own: it is defined by the two electrodes on either side of it. So V4 goes on first, at the fifth intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line, and V3 is then dropped exactly halfway between V2 and V4. V5 is placed the same way, halfway between V4 and V6.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview of the Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples
preguntas.subtema: CSF never refrigerated · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k117 · CMA I.C.8.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.a.vi · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen for culture will not be processed for another hour. Where should it be kept?
opciones: At room temperature or in a carbon dioxide incubator, never in the refrigerator
In the refrigerator at 4 degrees, the same as a urine specimen that is held for culture
On ice at the bedside, so the cell count is not altered before it is read
In a freezer at −70 degrees, the way a viral culture specimen is transported
preguntas.explicacion: Cold kills the very organisms the culture is hunting: Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitidis lose viability at low temperature, so cerebrospinal fluid for microbiology waits at room temperature, or in a carbon dioxide incubator, until it is examined. Refrigeration is the rule for urine, and freezing at −70 degrees Celsius is how viral culture specimens travel.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F 2M · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which question in the WHO Annex C script asks for the patient's consent?
opciones: 'Are you willing to be tested?'
'Have you ever had blood taken before?'
'How are you feeling at the moment?'
'Did you understand what I explained?'
preguntas.explicacion: After describing the needle, the tests and where results go, the script asks three things in a row: whether the patient has questions, whether they understood, and whether they are willing to be tested. The last is the consent question. The questions about earlier draws and current feelings belong to the second part of the script, the pre-draw interview.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Physician Self-Referral Law
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Under the physician self-referral law, what counts as a financial relationship with an entity?
opciones: An ownership or investment interest, or a compensation deal
An ownership interest only, whether it is direct or indirect
A compensation arrangement only, and only where it is direct
Any referral sent to an entity inside the same medical group
preguntas.explicacion: The law reaches a physician who refers designated health services to an entity where he, or someone in his immediate family, holds a financial relationship. That relationship may be an interest of ownership or investment in the entity, or else a compensation arrangement with it, and either sort may be direct or indirect.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Reduction and Prevention", Function: Active and Latent Errors
preguntas.subtema: Incident reporting · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between an active error and a latent error?
opciones: The active one is the act that harms; the latent one is a flaw lying in wait
The active one is caught in time; the latent one reaches the patient later
The active one is reported at once; the latent one is found on later audit
The active one involves a device; the latent one involves a staff decision
preguntas.explicacion: An active error is a specific event that harms the patient and involves the professional delivering the care, operating on the wrong eye for instance. A latent error is a failure built into the process: faulty equipment, poor system design, a weak organizational structure, able to sit unnoticed for a long time. A ventilator that malfunctions is latent; not checking it before use is active.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A lipid panel reports HDL and LDL. Which statement matches those two abbreviations?
opciones: HDL is high density lipoprotein, the good cholesterol; LDL is the bad one
HDL is heavy density lipoprotein, the bad cholesterol; LDL is the good one
HDL is high dietary lipid, the good cholesterol; LDL is the low dietary lipid
HDL is hepatic density lipase, the good enzyme; LDL is the liver-derived one
preguntas.explicacion: HDL is high density lipoprotein, described as the good cholesterol, and LDL is low density lipoprotein, the bad one. Both are types of cholesterol carried in the blood, and both appear on the same panel, so mixing them up reverses the meaning of the whole result for the patient.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What are the sixty lifetime reserve days of Medicare Part A used for?
opciones: Days ninety-one to a hundred and fifty of an inpatient stay, at $868 a day
Days sixty-one to ninety of an inpatient stay, which are charged at $434 a day
Days twenty-one to a hundred of a skilled nursing stay, at $217 for each day
The first sixty days of every benefit period, which carry no charge at all
preguntas.explicacion: The lifetime reserve days are the sixty extra inpatient days that carry the patient from day ninety-one to day a hundred and fifty, at $868 a day in 2026, and once they are used they are gone. Days sixty-one to ninety are charged at $434, and the skilled nursing rate of $217 belongs to a different benefit altogether.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fecal culture (003758), How the Test is Performed; and Stool ova and parasites exam (003756), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Stool free of urine and water · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient collecting a stool sample for culture asks whether it matters if urine or toilet water gets into it. What is the answer?
opciones: Yes: urine, toilet water and toilet tissue must all be kept out of the sample
Only urine matters; toilet water is acceptable because the sample is cultured anyway
Only toilet tissue matters, because paper fibers block the culture medium
It matters only for occult blood cards, not for a culture or a parasite exam
preguntas.explicacion: Stool for culture or for parasites must not be mixed with urine, water or toilet tissue. The patient can catch it on plastic wrap laid loosely over the bowl and held by the seat, in a container that fits on the toilet, or with the special tissue in a kit, then transfer it to the clean container provided and return it as soon as possible. The occult blood card has the same rule about urine.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Setup walk-through · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Walking a new patient through the setup, which two points does the guidance want covered so she can find her way back to the appointment?
opciones: How the invitation will reach her and what it looks like, and how to make a shortcut to the app
How the invitation will reach her and what it looks like, and how to reset her account password
How to make a shortcut to the app, and how to record the visit for her own notes afterwards
How to reset her account password, and how to reach the vendor's own help desk out of hours
preguntas.explicacion: The setup walk-through covers installing any software, updating the browser and unblocking plugins, opening the platform, checking that camera and audio work, and which features she will actually need so she is not overwhelmed. It also covers how to find the application again or set up a shortcut, and how the appointment invitation will be shared and what it will look like.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Personnel and Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
preguntas.subtema: Scope of practice · CPT D3 k55 · D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 3E7 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.A · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic is deciding who may draw blood on its premises. Which staff are named as able to perform phlebotomy?
opciones: A physician, a nurse, a laboratory technician or a certified phlebotomist
A certified phlebotomist only, in every health-care setting without exception
A physician or a nurse only, since the others may not handle sharps at all
A laboratory technician or a physician only, and never a nurse on a ward
preguntas.explicacion: The procedure may be carried out by a physician, a nurse, a laboratory technician or a certified phlebotomist. For complex cases where venous access is difficult, the advice is to bring in a certified phlebotomist, and supervision plus structured training is expected of everyone who draws blood.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes is seen every three months for that condition. How often may the chronic disease be coded?
opciones: At every visit where it is treated, as many times as she gets care for it
Once a year, at the first encounter of the calendar year for the patient
Only when it is worse than it was at the previous visit for the patient
Only at the visit where it was first established as a definitive diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: The outpatient guidelines let a chronic disease under ongoing treatment be reported at every encounter where the patient is treated or cared for. There is no yearly limit and no requirement that the condition has worsened. What must be true is that the condition requires or affects the care given at that visit.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2 Immobilize the child
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B k80 assisting with pediatric collection · PBT II.B age-specific needs · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10
preguntas.pregunta: A parent will hold a 3-year-old on their lap for a finger-prick. How should the parent hold the child?
opciones: Legs crossed around the child's legs, one arm across the chest tucking the free arm, the other hand grasping the elbow and wrist palm down
Child facing the parent chest to chest, arms wrapped around the child's back, with the puncture hand held out by the phlebotomist alone
Child lying face up across the parent's knees, the parent holding both wrists above the head so neither hand can move
Child seated beside the parent, the parent holding only the puncture hand while the phlebotomist steadies the shoulders
preguntas.explicacion: A child is immobilized for a finger-prick by asking the parent to sit in the phlebotomy chair with the child on their lap, cross their legs around the child's legs, extend an arm across the child's chest and tuck the free arm under their own, grasp the elbow of the puncture arm, and use the other arm to hold the wrist palm down. A helper is essential for safety and success.

preguntas.subtema: Employee access timing · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA II.B.5.c · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory technician asks to see his own exposure records. How quickly must the employer act under the OSHA access standard?
opciones: Within 15 working days, or tell him why it is late and when it will be ready
Within 30 calendar days, with one extension of 30 days if the file is off site
Within 60 calendar days, since the records are held for the employer's own use
Within 15 calendar days, counting the day the written request was received
preguntas.explicacion: Access is owed at a time, a place and in a manner that are reasonable. Where the employer cannot manage that inside 15 working days, it has to say so within those same 15 working days, telling the employee why it is late and the soonest date on which the record will be available. Thirty days with one extension is the HIPAA right of access, which is a different rule.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.1 Placement of the Precordial Electrodes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: Why are only bony landmarks used to locate the chest electrode positions?
opciones: A slight displacement already changes the pattern considerably
A slight displacement already lowers the standardization mark
Soft landmarks let the electrodes come loose during the run
Soft landmarks push the electrodes over onto breast tissue
preguntas.explicacion: Chest placement is often done too casually, and it has to be as exact and as repeatable as possible, which is why the bony landmarks are the ones used. The reason is blunt: even a small shift of one of these electrodes can change the pattern a great deal.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Difficult situations · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k16 · NCMA EKB 22
preguntas.pregunta: How is workplace violence defined for health care settings?
opciones: An act or threat on a spectrum from verbal abuse to lethal assault at work
An act against a worker on duty that leaves some physical injury behind
An act with criminal intent by someone with no tie to the organization
An act by a patient, a former patient or a visitor against the staff
preguntas.explicacion: There is no universal definition, but the one used comes from the occupational safety and health institute: a threat or an act along a spectrum that starts at verbal abuse and reaches physical and even lethal assault against people at work. Injury is not required. The last two options describe types I and II, which are categories inside that definition, not the definition.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: In the alphabetic index one code appears in brackets right after another. What does that tell the coder?
opciones: It is the manifestation code, and it is always sequenced second
It is a synonym of the code before it, so only one is reported
It is a nonessential modifier that may be present or absent
It is the default code for that term when no detail is given
preguntas.explicacion: Brackets do different work in the two parts of the classification. In the tabular list they hold synonyms, alternative wording or a phrase that explains; in the alphabetic index they identify manifestation codes, which are listed after the etiology code and are always sequenced second. Nonessential modifiers are the terms inside parentheses.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Preferred Provider Organization (PPO)
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which feature separates a PPO from an HMO?
opciones: Care outside the network is still covered, but the patient pays an extra cost for it
Care outside the network is covered only when the emergency room treats the patient
Care from a specialist is covered only after the primary care doctor orders it
Care is covered only after a high yearly deductible paired with a savings account
preguntas.explicacion: A PPO contracts with hospitals and doctors to build a network, charges the patient less for using it, and still allows outside providers at an additional cost. An HMO limits payment to its own contracted providers apart from emergencies, and a point of service plan is the one that demands the primary care doctor's referral for specialists. The deductible-plus-savings-account design belongs to an HSA-eligible plan.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Security Rule
preguntas.subtema: Security Rule safeguards · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: The HIPAA Security Rule requires which three categories of safeguards for electronic PHI?
opciones: Administrative, physical and technical
Clinical, financial and operational
Encryption, passwords and firewalls
Privacy, transactions and enforcement rules
preguntas.explicacion: While the Privacy Rule covers all PHI, the Security Rule is specific to electronic PHI and organizes protection into administrative safeguards, such as written procedures, a designated official, access authorization, training, backups and audits; physical safeguards, such as controlling access to hardware, keeping monitors out of public view and training contractors; and technical safeguards, such as access controls, protection of transmissions over open networks and integrity checks. Encryption, passwords and firewalls are tools within those categories, and privacy, transactions and enforcement are separate HIPAA rules.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions: CLIA certificate (4) Certificate of registration; CLIA-exempt laboratory
preguntas.subtema: Registration certificate · CPT D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1 · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: What does a CLIA certificate of registration allow a laboratory to do?
opciones: Moderate or high complexity testing until a CMS survey confirms compliance
Waived testing only, until the laboratory applies for accreditation
PPM procedures by a dentist, with no other testing permitted
Testing in a State exempt from CLIA, after the State licenses the laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: A registration certificate lets an entity run moderate or high complexity testing, or both, until CMS or its agent has surveyed it and found it compliant, or until an approved organization accredits it. Waived testing needs only a certificate of waiver, PPM procedures have a certificate of their own, and a CLIA-exempt laboratory is one licensed by a State whose requirements CMS has judged equal to CLIA or stricter, which takes it out of the federal certificate system altogether.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.1
preguntas.subtema: Disaster recovery plans · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: An audit finds that the disaster recovery plan for the servers and network behind the record system was last looked at three years ago. What does the guidance ask for?
opciones: A review at least once a year, of plans the practice is required to have
A review at least once every two years, on the cycle set for the downtime policy
A review at least once a quarter, on the cycle set for testing the backup site
A review at least once every five years, unless the system was replaced sooner
preguntas.explicacion: Disaster recovery plans covering the infrastructure that runs the applications critical to clinical and administrative work have to exist and to be reviewed at least once a year, and the practice carries the guide's strongest rating. Duplicated hardware, redundant networks and replicated data all belong inside those plans.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 7.1.4 and 7.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3Q k73 bandaging by age · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E9 postprocedural care · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: A capillary collection on an infant is finished. What is done at the puncture site?
opciones: Apply firm pressure until the bleeding stops, and watch the site afterwards
Apply an adhesive strip at once, since infants bleed longer than adults
Leave it uncovered and unpressed so that a clot forms without disturbance
Massage the site gently to disperse any hematoma that has started to form
preguntas.explicacion: At the end of the collection, firm pressure goes on the site until the bleeding stops. Repeated adhesive strips are what break down the skin of the very young and the very old, and that is headed off by pressing well and keeping an eye on the puncture afterwards. Massage is avoided because it hemolyses.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5E k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A neonatal unit's hemolysis rate is near 40 %. Which combination of measures cut the rate to under 30 % in the quality project cited?
opciones: Heel warmers for consistent warming before the draw, education in correct collection technique, and monitoring with feedback to collectors
Switching every newborn draw from heel stick to venipuncture, and sending all tubes by hand rather than through the pneumatic tube
Adding an automated hemolysis index to the analyzer, and reporting all results regardless of the index with a cautionary comment
Replacing microtubes with full-size evacuated tubes, so that the fill volume meets the required blood-to-anticoagulant ratio
preguntas.explicacion: At one academic medical center the neonatal unit's hemolysis rate was near or above 40 % in 2012 and fell to 28.6 % within a few months after changes that included heel warmers, to get more consistent warming before drawing, and increased education in correct blood withdrawal technique; the authors stress that monitoring and feedback to the collecting personnel keep the improvement. In the newborn series most hemolysis was in vitro, produced by the difficult collection itself.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pulse Oximetry", Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k51 · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient rescued from a house fire has an oximeter reading of 99% but is confused and breathless. Why is the reading unhelpful?
opciones: Carbon monoxide bound to hemoglobin changes the absorption and gives a false value
Smoke particles on the fingertip block the light and drive the display upward
The high reading is real, so a cause outside the lungs is what has to be sought
Soot cools the skin, and cold readings always drift toward the top of the scale
preguntas.explicacion: Carboxyhemoglobinemia and methemoglobinemia are dyshemoglobinemias: they change the color of the blood and its absorption spectrum, so the display can look reassuring while the patient is not oxygenating. Confirmation in those cases comes from a co-oximeter, and intravenous dyes such as methylene blue cause falsely low readings.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Emancipated Minor", section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about the 'mature minor' doctrine is correct?
opciones: Recognized in very few states, usually for minors 12 or older who show adequate capacity
Recognized in every state for minors 16 or older who still live with their parents
It applies automatically to any minor who is married or serving in the military
It applies to any unaccompanied minor screened in an emergency department
preguntas.explicacion: The doctrine is recognized in very few states and usually reaches minors of 12 or older who show the maturity to grasp what a treatment risks, what it offers, what else could be done and how it is likely to end; it is often restricted further by age, by whether a parent is available and by the clinical situation. Marriage and military service are grounds for emancipation, and emergency screening falls under EMTALA.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 5.1 Layers of the Skin
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(1) (2027 I.C.6.f(1)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which two layers make up the skin itself, and what lies immediately beneath them?
opciones: Epidermis and dermis, over a hypodermis of loose and fatty tissue
Dermis and hypodermis, over an epidermis of loose and fatty tissue
Epidermis and hypodermis, over a dermis of loose and fatty tissue
Epidermis and dermis, over a deep fascia of dense epithelial tissue
preguntas.explicacion: The skin has two main layers: the epidermis of closely packed epithelial cells on top and the dermis of dense irregular connective tissue below, holding blood vessels, hair follicles and sweat glands. Under both lies the hypodermis, mostly loose connective and fatty tissue, which cushions and insulates.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Numbers and Amounts; Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: After a stroke a patient is paralyzed down one side and the note reads hemiplegia. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A prefix meaning half plus an ending meaning paralysis
A prefix meaning half plus an ending meaning difficult speech
A prefix meaning one plus an ending meaning paralysis
A prefix meaning both sides plus an ending meaning movement
preguntas.explicacion: Hemi- means half and -plegia means paralysis, so the term describes paralysis of half the body. The endings that slip into its place point elsewhere: -phasia is speech, -praxia is movement and -plasia is growth. One and both sides are mono- and ambi-, and semi- is a second part meaning half.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Auto-disable (AD) syringes
preguntas.subtema: Safety-engineered devices · CPT D3 k66 k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why does the WHO device table state that auto-disable (AD) syringes are NOT recommended for drawing blood?
opciones: Their mechanism can trigger during probing, forcing a new puncture, and they do not prevent needle-sticks
Their sleeve cannot cover the needle while the syringe is full of blood or during transfer
The air in their tubing means the first tube has to be drawn without additive or discarded
Their needle-locking mechanism requires additional training and has a high cost
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 lists auto-disable syringes under passive devices with the note that they are designed to prevent reuse, not needle-sticks: during probing the safety mechanism can activate and require a new venepuncture, blood transfer is still needed, air in the syringe can affect results, and they offer no needle-stick protection. The sleeve limitation belongs to self re-sheathing devices, and the air in the tubing to winged needles.

preguntas.fuente: NHLBI, DASH Eating Plan: daily and weekly servings
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k26 cardiovascular and hypertension · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(c) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(c) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: What sodium targets does the DASH eating plan set?
opciones: 2,300 mg a day, with 1,500 mg lowering blood pressure further
2,300 mg a day, with 1,800 mg lowering blood pressure further
1,500 mg a day, with 1,000 mg lowering blood pressure further
3,400 mg a day, with 2,300 mg lowering blood pressure further
preguntas.explicacion: DASH, short for Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension, sets sodium at 2,300 mg a day in its sample pattern and notes that going down to 1,500 mg brings blood pressure down further still. The 3,400 mg figure is roughly what people actually eat, not a target of any plan.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Network plan; and Glossary: Preferred provider
preguntas.subtema: In-network and out-of-network coverage · CMAA 4 k61 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Why do insurers build networks of contracted providers?
opciones: The contract sets a discounted price for the services and supplies members receive
The contract lets the insurer set the medical standards the providers must follow
The contract obliges providers to accept every patient regardless of their coverage
The contract shifts the whole cost of denied claims onto the contracted provider
preguntas.explicacion: A network plan holds contracts with hospitals, doctors, pharmacies and other providers to furnish services and supplies to its members at a reduced price, which is why staying inside the network costs the patient less. The contract is about price and participation. It does not write clinical standards, does not force a provider to take patients from other plans, and does not decide who absorbs a denial.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Vacuum extraction systems
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A service cannot afford to throw away tube holders and must reuse them. How is the used needle taken off?
opciones: With a one-hand scoop, or a sharps container that has a removal hold
With both hands, holding the holder still while the needle unscrews
By pressing the holder against the bench until the needle drops free
By recapping the needle two-handed and then unscrewing the holder
preguntas.explicacion: Where possible the barrel and the needle are discarded together as one item. If the barrel really has to be reused, the sharp end is covered with a one-hand scoop before it is removed, or else a sharps container fitted with a needle removal hold, again one-handed.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic drug levels (003430), Normal Results
preguntas.subtema: Peak and trough levels · CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which target levels correspond to gentamicin?
opciones: Peak 5 to 10 mcg/mL and trough 0.5 to 2 mcg/mL
Peak 20 to 25 mcg/mL and trough 5 to 10 mcg/mL
Peak 10 to 20 mcg/mL and trough 4 to 12 mcg/mL
Peak 0.8 to 2.0 ng/mL and trough 0.2 to 1.0 ng/mL
preguntas.explicacion: Gentamicin is monitored with a peak of 5 to 10 mcg/mL and a trough of 0.5 to 2 mcg/mL. Tobramycin shares the same peak range with a trough of 0 to 2, while amikacin runs much higher, 20 to 25 at peak and 5 to 10 at trough. Total phenytoin is 10 to 20 mcg/mL and carbamazepine 4 to 12, and digoxin is reported in ng/mL, not mcg/mL.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Snellen Chart", Issues of Concern: Snellen Chart Procedure
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(10)(b)(ii) · RMA III.F.5.a · NCMA 2B.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's distance vision is being screened with a wall chart. How is the test set up?
opciones: Twenty feet from the chart, worse eye tested first with the other covered
Twenty feet from the chart, better eye tested first with the other covered
Fourteen inches from the chart, both eyes tested together and then singly
Twenty feet from the chart, both eyes uncovered so the lines are compared
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits 20 feet away in a well-lit room, wearing whatever distance correction they own; a mirror can stand in for the distance where the room is short. Eyes are tested one at a time starting with the weaker one, the other covered by the patient or an occluder, and the smallest line read is the acuity.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Reasons for Termination
preguntas.subtema: No-show consequences · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice reviews why patients were formally dismissed. In the study of 536 terminations, which reason came first?
opciones: Repeated appointment no-shows, which accounted for 38% of the cases reviewed
Disrespectful or disruptive behavior, which accounted for 22% of the cases reviewed
Violating an opioid agreement, which accounted for 4% of the cases reviewed
Non-adherence with the treatment plan, which accounted for 3% of the cases reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: Researchers went back over 536 formal terminations in primary care practices. Missed appointments led the count at 38%, followed by disrespectful or disruptive conduct at 22%, self- termination at 15%, breaking an opioid agreement at 4%, non-adherence at 3%, and illegal acts such as altering a prescription at 2%. No-shows are the commonest documented ground.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Implementation order · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A group has decided to try open access scheduling. Which two steps does the guide put at the very start of the work?
opciones: Measuring supply and demand as precisely as it can, and forming a test team of willing providers
Measuring supply and demand as precisely as it can, and switching every clinic over on one day
Working the appointment backlog down first, and only afterwards measuring the real demand
Buying a scheduling module for the record system, and forming a test team of willing providers
preguntas.explicacion: The literature says a practice can put the model in place within a few months by working through the steps in order. It starts by measuring supply and demand as precisely as possible, then sets up a test team of providers willing to try the system. Reducing the backlog comes after that, and it is the hard part: six to eight weeks of extra work.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Blood Volume
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with two days of vomiting is dehydrated but still has a normal blood pressure. How much blood volume can be lost before symptoms appear, and what is the condition called?
opciones: 10 to 20 percent; the condition is hypovolemia, treated with IV fluids
25 percent, the minimum pulse pressure as a share of the systolic value
5 percent, the share of the blood that sits in the systemic capillaries
Less than 1 percent, the share of the sample that forms the buffy coat
preguntas.explicacion: Low blood volume is hypovolemia; it follows blood loss, dehydration, vomiting, bad burns or certain drugs given against hypertension, and the body's other controls hold pressure up so well that nothing shows until a tenth to a fifth of the volume is gone. The usual treatment is fluid by vein. The other percentages are real figures, but they measure other things.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.3 Order of draw
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3P k72 · PBT II.H.2 capillary vs II.H.1 venous · CCMA k130 · NCMA 2C.7 · RMA III.C.4 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: How does the capillary order of draw relate to the venipuncture order of draw?
opciones: It runs in the reverse of the venipuncture order
It is identical to the venipuncture order of draw
It matches the venous order for two tubes only
It has no fixed order, as microtubes lack additives
preguntas.explicacion: Hematology first, then chemistry, then blood bank: on a skin puncture the sequence runs backwards to the venous one, and the reason is platelet clumping. What fixes the order is the kind of specimen, not the container it goes into. Past two specimens, a vein tends to give the laboratory better numbers.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: How the notice is sent · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.3.f · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: An office manager proposes sending termination notices through the patient portal instead of by post. Where does that stand at present?
opciones: One state endorses a compliant portal message with a read receipt, but certified mail is still preferred
Every state now accepts a compliant portal message, and certified mail has been retired for this
No state accepts an electronic notice, because a termination notice has to carry a signature
One state endorses a portal message, and only where the patient never opened the mailed letter
preguntas.explicacion: Notices of termination are always given in writing, and many states require them by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the most recent address on file, with the receipt and a copy kept in the record. At least one state now endorses electronic messages sent through the patient portal that tell the sender whether the message has been viewed; that may become the preferred method, but certified mail is the preferred means today.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.4: Description of Procedure, and ch. 18.3, Table 18.2
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.d(2) · RMA III.G.2.b · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which needle, volume and site match an intradermal injection?
opciones: 26 to 27 gauge, a quarter to half an inch, 0.1 mL, upper third of the forearm
25 to 31 gauge, half to five eighths of an inch, 1 mL, outer upper arm
18 to 25 gauge, half to an inch and a half, 2 mL, ventrogluteal site
22 to 25 gauge, one inch, 0.5 mL, deltoid three finger widths down
preguntas.explicacion: An intradermal injection is drawn in a tuberculin syringe whose scale runs in tenths and hundredths of a mL, with a 26 or 27 gauge needle a quarter to half an inch long, and the total volume is 0.1 mL. The sites are the forearm's upper third, the outer upper arms and the skin between the scapulae; for tuberculosis testing the forearm is the one recommended at any age. The other rows describe subcutaneous and intramuscular injections.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section Can I drink anything besides water during a fast
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Before a fasting lipid panel the patient drank two bottles of lemon-flavored sparkling water. Does that keep the fast?
opciones: Not acceptable; only plain water is allowed, and flavored water may contain sweeteners
Acceptable; any water, still or sparkling, keeps the fast intact regardless of flavoring
Acceptable if the label shows zero calories, since only calories can break a fast
Acceptable, but only up to one bottle, since larger volumes dilute the sample
preguntas.explicacion: Plain water is what a fast allows, and the warning is explicit about water that is flavored, whether lemon or carbonated, since it may carry sugar or artificial sweeteners. Drinking plain water freely actually helps: fuller veins make the sample easier to get, so the volume of plain water is not the problem.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Steps 4 and 9; and StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene and gloves · CPT D3 3A · D1 1K k35 · PBT II.F VI.G · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: When is hand hygiene performed in relation to a single venous draw?
opciones: Before the gloves go on, and again once the procedure is over
Before the gloves go on, and not again until the next patient
Only after the gloves come off, since the gloves cover the hands
Only when the gloves tore or blood reached the skin underneath
preguntas.explicacion: Hands are cleaned before the gloves go on, and the closing step asks for hand hygiene to be performed again, in the same way, once the procedure has finished. A new unused pair of gloves and a careful wash both before and after are recommended for every patient.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance, alcohol content and fire safety; and CDC, To Test or Not to Test? Considerations for Waived Testing (2024)
preguntas.subtema: Alcohol-based hand rub · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k102 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: What alcohol concentration does the CDC recommend for hand sanitizer used in healthcare settings?
opciones: At least 60 percent, and under the Life Safety Code no more than 95 percent
At least 70 percent, the concentration used to disinfect the skin before venipuncture
At least 50 percent, matching the 1:10 dilution used for blood spills
At least 95 percent, since lower concentrations do not kill spores
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohol-based hand sanitizer for healthcare should contain at least 60 percent alcohol, and the Life Safety Code provisions it cites cap the content at 95 percent by volume for fire safety, with limits on dispenser size and distance from ignition sources. Seventy percent alcohol is WHO's skin preparation before drawing blood, a different use. The 1:10 dilution is WHO's bleach mixture for spills, and no alcohol concentration kills spores, which is why C. difficile care calls for soap and water.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Serious Threat to Health or Safety
preguntas.subtema: Threat disclosures · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.5 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient tells the clinician of a specific, credible plan to harm a named neighbor. What does the Privacy Rule allow?
opciones: Disclosure to someone able to lessen a serious and imminent threat, including the person targeted
Disclosure to the local newspaper, so that the community can protect itself from the threat
Disclosure only after a court has issued an order authorizing the release of the information
No disclosure at all, since threats made during treatment fall under psychotherapy notes
preguntas.explicacion: Among the twelve public interest purposes there is one that lets a covered entity disclose what it judges necessary in order to head off or reduce a threat that is serious and imminent to a person or to the public, provided the disclosure goes to somebody thought able to prevent or lessen it; the rule names the person being threatened as a permissible recipient. The same paragraph permits telling law enforcement whatever would help in identifying an escapee or a violent criminal, or in catching one.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Basic expectations · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which instruction belongs to the basic expectations a practice sets out before a patient's first video appointment?
opciones: What she should do if she cannot attend, and what if either side cannot connect
Which insurer will be billed for the appointment and what her share will come to
How the clinician will write the appointment up in her record once it is finished
Which pharmacy any prescription written during the appointment will be sent to
preguntas.explicacion: Basic expectations cover treating the video appointment as she would an in-person one, who needs to be present, how she will connect, that she should not hesitate to ask questions, and what to do if she cannot make the appointment or if either side has trouble connecting. Billing, documentation and the pharmacy belong to other parts of the workflow.
