preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.1.4, Patient cooperation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2M · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: What should every patient who undergoes phlebotomy receive, according to the WHO's marker of quality of care called patient cooperation?
opciones: Clear information about the procedure, either written or verbal
A signed written consent form filed in the medical record
A copy of the laboratory results within 24 hours of the draw
A printed list of the tube colors and additives used
preguntas.explicacion: Patient involvement and cooperation are treated as an essential marker of quality in phlebotomy, and clear information, written or verbal, is to be available to each patient, with a sample explanation text provided in the annexes. Consent for a routine draw is verbal, results go back to the ordering clinician, and tube details belong to the laboratory, not to patient information.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: How to make a sling — Considerations; and StatPearls, "Splinting", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.2.d · NCMA 2B.13 · CCMA 3B12
preguntas.pregunta: A splint has just been applied. What is checked immediately afterward?
opciones: Skin color, circulation and sensation in the limb beyond the splint
The alignment of the fracture, by repeating the imaging that was ordered
The temperature of the plaster, which must have finished setting hard
The patient's ability to bear weight on the limb that has been splinted
preguntas.explicacion: Neurovascular status is assessed before the splint goes on and again after. Skin that turns cool, pale or blue, or numbness and tingling beyond the splint, means the bandage is loosened at once. Excess pressure over the elbow, knee or heel can damage skin, so those areas get extra padding. Pain that is worse after splinting means the splint comes off.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Credentialing", Issues of Concern: National Practitioner Data Bank
preguntas.subtema: Credentialing · RMA I.C.2.a · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: What does the National Practitioner Data Bank hold?
opciones: Malpractice payments, loss of privileges, license action and exclusions
The continuing education credits that every credentialed professional earns
The list of procedures each practitioner is privileged to perform
The primary source verifications a hospital has completed this year
preguntas.explicacion: The federal data bank gathers negative reports: complaints, malpractice cases and awards, loss of privileges, suspension or revocation of a license, professional society membership actions and exclusion from Medicare or Medicaid. Congress created it to protect the public and cut fraud and abuse. Access is limited, and many states require the data when applying for a license.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Lactose intolerance — Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(e) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with lactose intolerance asks whether she must give up milk entirely. What is accurate?
opciones: Most people tolerate about half a cup at a time; lactase products also help
Most people tolerate about three cups at a time if spread across the day
All dairy has to go, because any lactose at all will bring symptoms back
Only lactose-free products work, since lactase drops are not sold to patients
preguntas.explicacion: Cutting back on the milk products that carry lactose usually settles the symptoms, and most people with a low lactase level handle up to about half a cup, roughly 2 to 4 ounces, at one sitting; servings above 8 ounces are what tend to cause trouble. Lactase can also be added to milk or taken as capsules or chewable tablets.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination (one-pager, April 2025), SOP model step 13a-b; and Overview (2022), section 4 Blood Culture Collection Site
preguntas.subtema: Locations for cultures · CPT D4 4A k75 · PBT II.E site selection · CCMA 3E k139 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: The first blood culture set has just been drawn from the left antecubital fossa. Where should the second set come from?
opciones: A separate venipuncture, preferably the right antecubital fossa
The same venipuncture, by attaching a second pair of bottles
The patient's existing peripheral IV catheter, to avoid a second stick
A central line, since catheter draws are less often contaminated
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's 2025 procedure repeats the whole sequence for the second set and specifies a separate venipuncture site, with the upper extremity preferred and the right and left antecubital fossae used when possible. Peripheral venipuncture has consistently shown lower contamination than draws through existing central venous catheters, so catheter draws are reserved for suspected catheter-associated infection, when both a peripheral and a catheter set are taken.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A PT/INR, a CBC and a plasma glucose are ordered together. Which sequence of tubes follows the WHO order of draw?
opciones: Light blue citrate, purple EDTA, light gray fluoride
Purple EDTA first, light blue citrate, light gray fluoride
Light gray fluoride, light blue citrate, purple EDTA
Light blue citrate, light gray fluoride, purple EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: The citrate tube is position 3, EDTA is position 8 and the oxalate/fluoride tube is position 10 in Table 2.3, so the sequence is light blue, purple, gray. The table marks all three as tubes that require a full draw, and for the gray tube adds that a short draw may cause hemolysis; that detail affects fill level, not the order.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which structures does the bicipital aponeurosis partly cover in the roof of the cubital fossa?
opciones: The median nerve, the brachial artery and the ulnar artery
The median cubital vein, the cephalic vein and the radial nerve
The basilic vein, the ulnar nerve and the biceps tendon itself
The brachial artery only, the veins running above the sheet of tendon
preguntas.explicacion: The roof of the fossa is skin and fascia reinforced by the bicipital aponeurosis, a tendon-like sheet off the biceps that forms a partial covering over the median nerve, the brachial artery and the ulnar artery. The median cubital vein runs within that roof, superficial to the sheet.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Phlebotomy and Medical Lab Technology; and 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k1 k4 (applied D3) · PBT I.B.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders blood gases. Which type of sample is used, and in what units is the PO2 reported?
opciones: Blood from an arterial stick; the PO2 is recorded in mm Hg
A venous sample from the median cubital vein; the PO2 in percent
A capillary sample from the heel; the oxygen recorded in mm Hg
A pulse oximeter reading from the fingertip; saturation in mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: An arterial stick is used to analyze blood gases, and oxygen measured directly as free oxygen in plasma after an arterial stick is expressed as the partial pressure of oxygen, PO2, in millimeters of mercury. The pulse oximeter is a different measure: it reports percent saturation of hemoglobin, normally 95 to 100 percent, from light passed through a fingertip.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Storing and Shipping
preguntas.subtema: Respiratory specimen storage · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k117 · CMA I.C.8.c.(1) · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: A respiratory specimen in viral transport medium will not ship to the public health laboratory for five days. How should it be stored?
opciones: Frozen at −70 degrees Celsius, because the delay runs past 3 to 4 days
Refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius, the same as for a same-day shipment
Frozen at −20 degrees Celsius, because the delay runs past 3 to 4 days
At room temperature, the way cerebrospinal fluid for culture is held
preguntas.explicacion: Specimens go into viral transport medium and straight onto refrigerant gel packs or into a refrigerator at 4 degrees Celsius, and they are kept at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius until shipment. Once the delay will exceed 3 to 4 days the specimen is frozen at −70 degrees Celsius instead. Room temperature is the rule for cerebrospinal fluid and other body fluids going for culture.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 Equipment and supplies for paediatric patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B k80 · PBT II.J syringes · CCMA 3E3 supplies · NCMA 2C.4 equipment by age
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist attaches a 10 mL syringe to a butterfly for a 2-year-old. What is the rule on syringe size in children?
opciones: Use a 1 to 5 mL syringe; the vacuum from drawing with a larger syringe often collapses the vein
Use a 10 to 20 mL syringe; a small syringe cannot generate enough vacuum to fill through a butterfly
Use any size, since the syringe barrel does not affect the vein; only needle gauge matters
Use a 1 to 5 mL auto-disable syringe, which the WHO recommends for all pediatric draws
preguntas.explicacion: The syringe barrel should hold 1 to 5 mL depending on what has to be collected, because the vacuum a bigger syringe pulls will often collapse the vein. Where an evacuated tube is used instead, it should be a small-volume one, 1 mL or 5 mL, with low vacuum. Auto-disable syringes belong to injection; phlebotomy is not what they are for.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Facility Directories
preguntas.subtema: Directory and callers · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A caller asks for a patient by name and wants to know how he is doing. What does the facility directory provision allow?
opciones: Giving the general condition and location, if the patient had a chance to agree or object
Giving the full diagnosis and treatment plan, since the caller already knew the patient's name
Withholding both, because condition and location are never releasable to an outside caller
Giving the religious affiliation to any caller, since clergy need not ask for the patient by name
preguntas.explicacion: On informal permission, asked for outright or arising from circumstances that plainly give the patient a chance to object, a directory may carry the patient's name, where he is, how he is doing in general terms, and his religious affiliation. Condition and location may then be released to anyone who asks for the patient by name. Religious affiliation goes to clergy, and clergy alone are excused from asking by name.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Aging changes in vital signs
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k55 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient on a beta blocker and digoxin has a pulse of 54 beats per minute. How is that finding weighed?
opciones: Both drugs are known to slow the pulse, so the value is read against the medication list
Neither drug affects rate, so a value of 54 always points to a conduction problem
Both drugs speed the pulse, so 54 means the patient has been missing doses lately
The value can be dismissed, because resting rate normally falls below 60 after age 65
preguntas.explicacion: Medicines are part of the reading. Digoxin, used in heart failure, and the beta blockers can both slow the pulse, so a rate in the fifties on those drugs is interpreted with the list in hand. Resting heart rate does not itself drop with age, so age alone does not explain the value.

preguntas.subtema: Record content on complications · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A record is being reviewed for completeness after a stay in which the patient reacted badly to an anesthetic. Which entry does the condition of participation require?
opciones: Documentation of the unfavorable reaction, alongside complications and infections acquired
Documentation of the unfavorable reaction, alongside the manufacturer's lot and expiry
Documentation of the unfavorable reaction, alongside a report filed with the state board
Documentation of the unfavorable reaction, alongside a note in the discharge instructions
preguntas.explicacion: The list of things every record must document, as appropriate, includes complications, infections acquired in the hospital, and unfavorable reactions to drugs and to anesthesia. On the same list sit the admitting diagnosis, the results of all consultative evaluations with the findings of the staff involved, and the orders, notes and reports of treatment.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1249, Standard: Preanalytic systems quality assessment
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k92 · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Rejections keep repeating in one ward, and the laboratory director asks what CLIA expects beyond simply counting them. What does the preanalytic quality assessment standard require?
opciones: Reviewing whether corrective actions worked, revising procedures and telling staff
Reporting the recurring problem to the accrediting organization each quarter
Suspending testing for that ward until its collection practice is re-approved
Repeating the proficiency testing challenge for every affected specialty
preguntas.explicacion: The standard asks for written policies and for a mechanism that runs continuously to monitor and assess the test request and specimen handling systems, and to correct problems where they appear. That assessment has to take in a review of how well the corrective actions worked, a revision of the policies so the problem does not return, and discussion of the reviews with the staff concerned, all of it documented.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: In the classic stat-laboratory series of preanalytical errors, which problem dominated the hematology samples?
opciones: Clotted samples
Hemolysed samples
Lost samples
Wrong tube samples
preguntas.explicacion: In that stat laboratory the preanalytical error types reported most often were hemolysed samples, 46.4 % in biochemistry, and clotted samples, 43.2 % in hematology, followed by lost samples at 6.4 %, an inadequate ratio of sample to anticoagulant at 2.9 %, patient misidentification at 0.7 %, the wrong collection tube at 0.3 % and missing test requests at 0.1 %. The core laboratory of the same institution had put clotted specimens at 55.8 % of its rejections, with inadequate volume next at 29.3 %.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.1 Placement of the Precordial Electrodes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which landmark is used to count down to the right intercostal space for the chest leads?
opciones: The sternal angle, known as the angle of Louis
The xiphoid process, at the lower end of the sternum
The clavicle, counting downward from the first rib
The nipple, taken as the level of the fourth space
preguntas.explicacion: Only bony landmarks give a placement that can be repeated from visit to visit. Two fingers find the sternal angle, then walk down the spaces on the right border of the sternum until the fourth one is reached. Even a small displacement of a chest electrode can change the pattern considerably.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Law Enforcement Purposes
preguntas.subtema: Law enforcement · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.5 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: Which request from a law enforcement official may a covered entity answer under the law enforcement purpose?
opciones: A request for information to identify or locate a suspect, fugitive, witness or missing person
A request to browse the day's schedule for names that might be worth interviewing later
A request for a patient's whole chart because the officer believes a crime may have occurred
A request for records of every patient treated for a gunshot wound in the past five years
preguntas.explicacion: Six circumstances, each with its conditions, let information reach law enforcement: where the law requires it, court orders, warrants and subpoenas included; to pin down or find a suspect, a fugitive, a material witness or a missing person; about a victim, or someone believed to be one; to flag a death that may have been criminal; where the information is evidence of a crime committed on the premises; and in a medical emergency away from the premises.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Airborne Precautions; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Airborne pathogens · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k96 · CMA I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which infections does the CDC give as examples requiring Airborne Precautions?
opciones: Measles, chickenpox, tuberculosis and disseminated herpes zoster
Influenza, pertussis and mumps, which travel in respiratory droplets
Clostridioides difficile, scabies and multidrug-resistant organisms
Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV, the bloodborne pathogens
preguntas.explicacion: Four infections travel on droplet nuclei that hang in the air, and they are the examples given for Airborne Precautions: measles, chickenpox, tuberculosis and disseminated herpes zoster. Smallpox sits on the same list, and susceptible staff are kept out of those rooms when immune colleagues are available. Influenza, pertussis and mumps are droplet infections; C. difficile, scabies and multidrug-resistant organisms fall under Contact Precautions. The three bloodborne viruses are not an isolation category at all: Standard Precautions and the OSHA standard cover them.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Fire Hazards, Requirements, 29 CFR 1910.36 and 1910.37
preguntas.subtema: Exit routes · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45
preguntas.pregunta: Which requirement applies to exit routes under OSHA's Subpart E?
opciones: Exit doors must be unlocked and routes kept free and unobstructed at all times
Exit doors may be locked during night shifts if a key is kept at the desk
Exit routes may be used for temporary storage if a path 3 feet wide remains
Exit routes must be marked but need not be lighted when the building is closed
preguntas.explicacion: The exit route rules of 29 CFR 1910.34 through 1910.37 require an adequate number of routes of sufficient capacity, discharging directly outside or to a safe open space large enough for the occupants, adequately lighted and marked, with an operable employee alarm system, exit doors unlocked, and routes free and unobstructed at all times. Compliance with the NFPA 101 Life Safety Code or the International Fire Code exit provisions is deemed to satisfy those sections. Locking, storage and unlit exits all violate the rules.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Acute Otitis Media", History and Physical and Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(10) (2027 I.C.6.g(10)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A toddler is tugging at one ear, is irritable and has a low-grade fever. Which finding on otoscopy would support acute otitis media?
opciones: Moderate to severe bulging of the tympanic membrane
Moderate to severe swelling of the external auditory canal
A pale tympanic membrane that moves briskly on insufflation
Tenderness over the mastoid region behind the affected ear
preguntas.explicacion: Ear pain is the most reliable indicator, but small children often show only irritability, poor feeding or disturbed sleep, and about two-thirds run a low-grade fever. The diagnosis rests on history and examination, with no laboratory test or imaging: bulging of the tympanic membrane, or new discharge, is what confirms it. Marked canal swelling points to otitis externa, and mastoid tenderness raises the question of mastoiditis.

preguntas.fuente: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, Guideline 1
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A mother of a 4-month-old asks what the Dietary Guidelines say about feeding at this stage. What is the recommendation?
opciones: Human milk alone for about the first 6 months, with vitamin D from soon after birth
Human milk alone for about the first 6 months, with iron drops from soon after birth
Human milk with complementary foods already introduced at about 4 months of age
Human milk alone for about the first 12 months, with no supplement of any kind
preguntas.explicacion: The first guideline covers every life stage. For roughly the first half year infants are fed human milk alone, with supplemental vitamin D starting soon after birth; iron-fortified formula is the substitute when human milk is not available. Nutrient-dense complementary foods come in at about 6 months, not at 4.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(d), Uses and disclosures of de-identified protected health information; 164.502(f)
preguntas.subtema: De-identified information · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: Which health information falls outside the requirements of the HIPAA Privacy Rule?
opciones: De-identified information, with no code that would allow re-identification disclosed
Health information about a patient who died more than 6 years before the request
Health information kept only on paper charts and never transmitted electronically anywhere
Health information spoken aloud rather than written or stored
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(d) says information that meets the de-identification standard of 164.514 is not individually identifiable and the Privacy Rule does not apply to it, with two provisos: disclosing a code or other means of re-identification is itself a disclosure of PHI, and re-identified information is PHI again. Paper and spoken information remain protected, which is why elevator conversations and unattended charts are violations, and a deceased person's information stays protected for 50 years after death.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Healthy Eating & Physical Activity for Weight Management — Get regular physical activity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(a) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(a) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition b · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting a weight management plan asks how much activity is advised for healthy adults. What is recommended?
opciones: 150 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity plus strength work on 2 days
150 minutes a week of vigorous aerobic activity plus strength work on 5 days
75 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity plus strength work on 2 days
300 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity with no strength work needed
preguntas.explicacion: Healthy adults are told to get at least 150 minutes a week of moderate-intensity aerobic activity, brisk walking or dancing being the usual examples, together with muscle-strengthening work covering all the major muscle groups on two or more days. Moderate intensity speeds the heart and the breathing without overworking the person.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Competence in the Care of LGBTQ Patients", section Issues of Concern, How to Create A Practice That Welcomes Members of the LGBTQ Community
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k18 · CCMA 6 k194 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which change to the intake forms is recommended so a practice welcomes patients from the LGBTQ community?
opciones: Add the term partner beside spouse, and include transgender as an option
Add a field for the sex assigned at birth and leave the rest unchanged
Add a note asking staff to record the patient's appearance and manner
Add a required field naming the patient's next of kin and their gender
preguntas.explicacion: Among the steps toward a welcoming practice: staff are trained to use each patient's name and the pronouns that patient has chosen, and the intake forms carry the word partner alongside spouse, with transgender offered as an option. Forgetting gender-neutral terms such as partner is listed as a challenge, as is drawing conclusions about behavior from appearance.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: On what schedule does the Inspector General say the List of Excluded Individuals/Entities must be checked, and on what other occasion?
opciones: Every month, and again in connection with any new enrollment in the program
Every year, and again whenever a claim comes back denied for a coding error
Every three years, the same interval an employer keeps its training records
Only when the Inspector General writes to say an employee has been excluded
preguntas.explicacion: The exclusions program states the schedule outright: the list is to be consulted once a month, and again at any fresh enrollment, so that nobody excluded from the federal programs is enrolled or kept enrolled in a state Medicaid program. The monthly supplement files exist for exactly that, listing what was added or removed in the month. A practice runs the same check before it hires, because civil monetary penalties can fall on whoever employs someone on the list.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k55 · CMA I.A.1.b(1) · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has just climbed the stairs asks why the pulse is not taken immediately. What is the reason?
opciones: A resting heart rate requires the patient to have been at rest for at least 10 minutes
A resting heart rate requires the patient to have been at rest for at least 30 minutes
The pulse cannot be counted at all while the rhythm is still faster than 100 beats a minute
The pulse must be taken at the same hour each visit for the values to be comparable
preguntas.explicacion: The figure charted as the resting heart rate only means something if the patient has been resting, and 10 minutes is the interval given for that. A rate taken during or just after exercise is an exercise heart rate and says something different: it reports fitness, not baseline.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(x), Masks, Eye Protection, and Face Shields
preguntas.subtema: Face and eye protection · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Under the bloodborne pathogens standard, when must a mask with eye protection or a face shield be worn?
opciones: When blood may splash or spray and contamination of the eyes, nose or mouth can be anticipated
Whenever gloves are worn, since hand contact with blood implies facial exposure
Whenever gross contamination is anticipated, as with autopsies or orthopedic surgery
Whenever the patient is on Droplet Precautions, but not for routine venipuncture
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(x) ties facial protection to the task: a mask with goggles, or with glasses carrying solid side shields, or a chin-length face shield, goes on whenever blood or OPIM may splash, spray, spatter or fly in droplets and contamination of the eyes, the nose or the mouth can reasonably be anticipated. Gloves have their own trigger in (d)(3)(ix). Gross contamination, as at an autopsy, is what triggers caps, hoods and shoe covers in (d)(3)(xii). Droplet Precautions are a CDC isolation category, not the test this paragraph applies.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.3 A-C Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k148 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: Interference is still on the tracing after every electrode has been checked. Where does the search go next?
opciones: To the equipment near the room, following the guide step by step
To the calibration of the unit, using the external calibrator on it
To the age of the electrodes, changing the whole card being used
To the patient's jewelry, taking off the wristwatch and the rings
preguntas.explicacion: Alternating-current interference comes from one of two places: poor contact at an electrode or equipment near the room. With contact ruled out, the technician works through the trouble-shooting guide. Watches, glasses, rings and bracelets are not a cause.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abandonment", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Abandonment · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.d(2) · NCMA 4.9 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants to dismiss a patient and asks which grounds are recognized as lawful for doing so. Which set of reasons is it?
opciones: Repeated noncompliance with agreed treatment, threatening behavior, unreasonable non-payment, closing the practice
Repeated noncompliance with agreed treatment, threatening behavior, a diagnosis outside the practice's specialty
Repeated noncompliance with agreed treatment, unreasonable non-payment, a complaint filed against the clinician
Repeated noncompliance with agreed treatment, threatening behavior, and any patient the clinician finds difficult
preguntas.explicacion: The list of lawful grounds is short and specific: the person keeps breaking the treatment and follow-up plan that was agreed with them; the person is disruptive or threatening; the person will not pay without a reasonable cause; or the clinician is closing the practice or retiring. Misleading answers about the history, drug-seeking and a sentinel event at the office also belong there. Being difficult is not on the list, and neither is having complained; the effort to repair the relationship comes first and goes in writing.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", sections Continuing Education Activity and Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: What is syncope?
opciones: A brief loss of consciousness and of postural tone, righting itself, from reduced cerebral perfusion
A brief seizure with loss of sphincter control and confusion on waking, from an acute neurologic event
A feeling that one is about to pass out without actually losing consciousness, caused by cerebral hypoperfusion
A prolonged loss of consciousness lasting several minutes, from a fall in blood glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Syncope is a passing loss of consciousness and of postural tone that rights itself, and it comes from a drop in cerebral perfusion. The feeling of being about to pass out without doing so is what the chapter calls near syncope or presyncope, and an episode that runs beyond a few minutes is not syncope at all but more likely a seizure. Hypoglycemia is listed among conditions that mimic fainting.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime policy · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: How often does the contingency planning guidance expect a written downtime and recovery policy to be reviewed?
opciones: At least every two years, and a paper copy is kept in the units and off site
At least every six months, and a paper copy is filed with the software vendor
At least every five years, and a paper copy is posted in the waiting area
Only after a downtime occurs, and a paper copy goes to each staff member
preguntas.explicacion: The written policy is what makes everyone act the same way during a planned or unplanned outage: when a downtime is declared, who leads it on the clinical and the technical side, how people are told, and how the information gathered on paper gets back into the system. It is reviewed at least every two years, and a printed copy lives both in the units and in a safe off-site place.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: What the patient gathers · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is booked for a video visit about a sore throat. Which items does the guidance have the office ask her to gather, beyond her medicines and her pharmacy's details?
opciones: Measurements such as weight and temperature, and a flashlight or the light on her telephone
Measurements such as weight and temperature, and a mirror so she can see her own throat
A flashlight or the light on her telephone, and a tongue depressor bought from the pharmacy
Measurements such as blood pressure and pulse, and a flashlight or the light on her telephone
preguntas.explicacion: Depending on what the appointment is for, the patient may be asked to have ready a list of her current medicines or the bottles themselves, her medical history, the symptoms and questions she wants to raise, her pharmacy's contact details, measurements such as weight and temperature, and a flashlight or the light on her smartphone if her throat has to be looked at.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which group of donors was fainting most often reported in?
opciones: Female donors giving for the first time
Male donors over fifty giving again
Male donors under thirty giving again
Female donors over sixty giving again
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting was reported in 5.3 percent of cases and usually happened in first-time female blood donors, while vasovagal attacks occurred occasionally and ranged from mild to severe. It is a reminder to ask about earlier faints and to have the chair ready for a reaction.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k149 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which patient is most likely to put muscle tremor on the tracing?
opciones: One who is cold, tense or has a nerve or muscle disorder
One who has a slow heart rate or a first-degree block
One whose chest hair keeps the electrodes from sticking
One whose lead wires were left looped across the table
preguntas.explicacion: Tremor signals come from skeletal muscle, so the patients who produce them are the ones who are shivering, tense, or living with a muscle or nerve disorder. Hair under an electrode and looped wires cause different faults: electrodes that fall off and interference from the room current.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Risk of Infection After a Needlestick Injury: HIV; StatPearls, "Needlestick", Etiology: HIV
preguntas.subtema: What makes an exposure worse · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which circumstances raise the chance that a needlestick from an HIV-positive patient transmits the virus?
opciones: A visibly bloody device, a needle that was in a vein or artery, and a deep injury
A solid needle, a superficial scratch, and contact limited to intact skin
A small-bore needle, a source on treatment, and a splash onto the forearm
A used lancet, a gloved hand, and a source patient with a low viral load
preguntas.explicacion: The average risk after a percutaneous injury with HIV-infected blood is about 0.3 percent, but it is not the same for every injury. A case-control study found the risk higher when the worker met a larger quantity of blood, which showed up as a visibly bloody device, a procedure that put the needle in a vein or an artery, or a deep injury. Large-bore hollow needles and a source with a high viral load point the same way; intact skin carries no meaningful risk at all.

preguntas.subtema: Data backup plan · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which task does the data backup plan specification of the contingency plan standard require?
opciones: Creating and keeping copies of the information that can be retrieved exactly
Restoring the information that was lost once the systems are running again
Keeping critical processes going while the office works in emergency mode
Ranking which applications and data matter most to the rest of the planning
preguntas.explicacion: The contingency plan standard splits into five specifications, and the wording of each decides the answer. The data backup plan is about making and maintaining retrievable exact copies beforehand; restoring what was lost is the disaster recovery plan, and the criticality analysis is the addressable one that ranks them.

preguntas.subtema: Termination procedures · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant resigns on a Friday. Which addressable specification tells the practice what to do about her access to the system?
opciones: Termination procedures, which end access when the working arrangement finishes
Access establishment and modification, which reviews and changes a user's rights
Workforce clearance, which decides whether her access was appropriate to start
Authorization and supervision, which covers staff working where records are open
preguntas.explicacion: Workforce security carries three addressable specifications: authorization and supervision, the workforce clearance procedure, and termination procedures, which is the one written for the moment an employment or other arrangement ends. The first two ask about somebody who is still working there. Access establishment and modification is not in this standard at all: it sits under information access management.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Does Pneumatic Tube System Transport Contribute to Hemolysis in ED Blood Samples?" (West J Emerg Med 2016, PMC5017839), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.D.4 · CCMA 3E k144 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: After installing a longer, faster pneumatic tube route, a laboratory sees more hemolysed samples. Which change in how tubes are sent is supported by the literature as reducing transport hemolysis?
opciones: Using padded inserts inside the carriers, gel tubes and properly filled tubes
Sending tubes uncapped so that pressure changes do not build up inside them
Sending each tube in its own carrier at the highest speed to shorten travel time
Loading each carrier to full capacity so the tubes cannot shift during accelerations
preguntas.explicacion: Variables shown to increase hemolysis during transport are rapid accelerations and decelerations, greater length of travel and high speeds; variables shown to reduce it are gel tubes, properly filled tubes and padded inserts within the canisters. Higher speed works in the wrong direction, and neither uncapping the tubes nor packing the carrier full appears among the variables the study lists.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Physical Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Media disposal · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: The practice is retiring three computers and donating them to a school. Which Security Rule standard governs that?
opciones: Device and media controls, which require removing ePHI before media are reused
Workforce security, which requires authorization and supervision of staff who reach ePHI
Information access management, which limits access to what a person's role calls for
Security incident procedures, which require identifying and responding to known incidents
preguntas.explicacion: Device and media controls are a physical safeguard, and they cover hardware and electronic media that hold ePHI: arriving at the facility and leaving it, moving around inside it, and finally being disposed of, both the information and the equipment. On top of that comes an explicit duty: strip the ePHI off electronic media before those media are put back into use by anyone else.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's right to refuse care is founded on which ethical principle?
opciones: Autonomy, the right to make informed decisions about one's own care
Beneficence, which asks that actions be taken for the patient's benefit
Non-maleficence, which requires steps be taken so no one is harmed
Justice, which spreads benefits and risks evenly and without bias
preguntas.explicacion: Refusal of care rests on autonomy: a person may make informed decisions about their own health care, and staff are not to push their own beliefs, or their own decisions, onto the patient. Beneficence, non-maleficence and justice stand alongside autonomy and guide the same difficult situations, but the refusal itself does not rest on them.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: battery
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(6) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: What defeats a claim of battery?
opciones: Consent, whether it was expressed or implied by taking part
Absence of any lasting injury from the contact that occurred
Absence of an intention to hurt the person who was touched
Presence of a witness who saw the contact and thought it fine
preguntas.explicacion: Battery is intentional harmful or offensive contact without consent, so consent is the defense — express, such as agreeing, or implied, such as joining in a sport. No actual damages need be shown, because the contact itself counts as the injury. Intending the contact is enough; the defendant does not have to have meant it to be harmful.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(a)(1) and (a)(2), Permitted and required disclosures; and HHS, Office for Civil Rights, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule
preguntas.subtema: Required disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: In which two situations is a covered entity REQUIRED, rather than merely permitted, to disclose protected health information?
opciones: To the individual who requests access or an accounting, and to HHS investigating compliance
To law enforcement on request, and to the patient's employer for workers' compensation
To any treating provider, and to the health plan paying the claim, on request
To public health authorities, and to a coroner or medical examiner determining cause of death
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(a)(2) names only two required disclosures: to the individual when requested under the right of access or the right to an accounting of disclosures, and to the Secretary of HHS when required to investigate or determine the entity's compliance. Everything else in the rule, treatment, payment, operations, public health, law enforcement, coroners and workers' compensation, is permitted under conditions but not compelled by HIPAA itself, although other laws may require some of those reports.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: The tape on a pack has changed color after the cycle. What has that told the staff?
opciones: Only that the pack was run through a sterilization cycle, not that sterility was achieved
That the pack is sterile, since the ink reacts only when every parameter has been met
That the resistant spores inside the pack were inactivated during the exposure period
That the air was fully removed from the chamber before the steam was admitted to it
preguntas.explicacion: A chemical indicator is cheap, convenient and limited: affixed outside each pack, it shows the package went through a cycle, and it does not prove sterilization happened. Only a biological indicator made of resistant spores measures the killing power of the process directly, and an indicator inside the pack is preferred as well, to verify the sterilant got in.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Beta Blockers", Contraindications and Mechanism of Action
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.d · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with asthma needs a beta blocker for a cardiac problem. Which choice fits current recommendations?
opciones: A beta-1 selective agent such as atenolol, bisoprolol, metoprolol or esmolol
A non-selective agent such as propranolol, which binds beta-1 and beta-2 alike
Sotalol, whose potassium channel blockade also protects the airway from spasm
Labetalol, whose alpha-1 blockade cancels the airway effect of beta-2 blockade
preguntas.explicacion: Beta blockers were once ruled out in asthma altogether. Recommendations now allow the cardio-selective ones, which bind only beta-1, while the non-selective agents remain out because beta-2 blockade can bring on bronchospasm. Sotalol's extra effect is on potassium channels and it prolongs the QT interval; the alpha-1 blockade of carvedilol and labetalol helps blood pressure, not breathing.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Disorders of Erythrocytes
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with sickle cell disease has painful joints and a history of stroke. What is the underlying defect, and why do the cells block small vessels?
opciones: Abnormal hemoglobin S deforms the cells so they lodge in narrow capillaries
Overproduction of red cells raises viscosity and slows flow in capillaries
Antibodies agglutinate the red cells into clumps that block small vessels
Thrombocytosis triggers unwanted clots that occlude the small vessels
preguntas.explicacion: Sickle cell disease is a genetic disorder in which an abnormal hemoglobin, hemoglobin S, delivers less oxygen and makes erythrocytes take a sickle or crescent shape, especially when oxygen is low. Those cells cannot fold to squeeze through narrow capillaries, so they lodge and block flow, causing problems from painful joints to strokes. Agglutination is the transfusion-reaction mechanism, not this one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Patient Safety and Early Detection of Clinical Deterioration
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · RMA III.E.3 Respiration b · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is the earliest and most sensitive warning that a patient is deteriorating?
opciones: A rising respiratory rate, which usually moves before the pressure falls
A falling blood pressure, which moves before the other measurements shift
A rising temperature, which is the first of the vital signs to change
A falling oxygen saturation, which precedes any change in the breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Breathing changes early. Tachypnea is a more accurate and earlier marker of deterioration than hypotension, and it commonly comes before hypoxemia as well; one study found that a rate above 35 breaths a minute was the single strongest predictor of a life-threatening event. It is also the value most often left uncounted.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.520(b)(1), Required elements of the notice
preguntas.subtema: Content of the notice · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement must appear prominently at the top of a notice of privacy practices?
opciones: A header stating how medical information may be used and disclosed and how to access it
The names of every business associate that may receive the patient's information during care
The civil penalty amounts for HIPAA violations, from $100 up to $50,000 per violation
A list of the 18 identifiers that turn health information into protected information
preguntas.explicacion: The notice must be written in plain language and open with a prominently displayed header telling the reader that it describes how medical information about them may be used and disclosed and how they can get access to it, and asking them to review it carefully. It then describes uses for treatment, payment and operations with examples, the other permitted purposes, the uses that require authorization, the individual's rights, the entity's duties, how to complain without retaliation, a contact person and the effective date. Business associate names, penalty tables and identifier lists are not required elements.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques), Open-ended questioning
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k40 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 k126 · CMA I.A.3.b / 2027 A.3.b · RMA I.D.1.c · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: To open the pre-draw interview, which question follows the principle of open-ended questioning first?
opciones: 'How have blood draws gone for you in the past?'
'Have you ever fainted during a blood draw?'
'You're not scared of needles, are you?'
'Did you fast for twelve hours like the doctor said?'
preguntas.explicacion: The technique table says to begin with open-ended questions that allow a free-flowing account, and to move to closed-ended questions afterwards. The other three are closed or leading: the fainting question is a legitimate item from the WHO Annex C interview, but it invites a yes or no, and the leading question about needles steers the answer.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.C Proficiency Testing · NCMA 4.12 comply with CLIA
preguntas.pregunta: A technologist texts a friend at another hospital laboratory to compare answers on the current proficiency testing event, before the due date. Under CLIA, what has happened?
opciones: A prohibited inter-laboratory communication about PT results before the program's reporting date
A permitted consultation, because the two laboratories do not belong to the same corporation or system
A reportable referral, because discussing the results counts as sending the sample elsewhere
A documentation lapse, correctable by noting the exchange in the proficiency testing record
preguntas.explicacion: A laboratory testing PT samples may hold no inter-laboratory communication at all about the results until the date the program's results are due, and the ban reaches across sites and across separate locations of one laboratory, so common ownership excuses nothing. Referral is a different violation: that means sending the sample, or a part of it, to another laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Demand surges · CMAA 4A k53 · CCMA 5C k173 · CMA III.H.1.c · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Every September the same clinic is swamped by school physicals and flu shots. What does the open access guidance tell it to prepare?
opciones: A contingency plan naming who can supplement or stand in for each physician those days
A block of the schedule set aside weeks ahead for the physicals and the flu shots
A waiting list of patients willing to come in whenever another patient cancels
Another six to eight weeks of longer days, as when the practice cleared its backlog
preguntas.explicacion: The model asks for a contingency plan for days, or parts of days, when demand far outstrips the physicians available, and that plan has to say who can supplement or substitute for each of them. The guidance also tells the group to be proactive about the surges it can predict, and names school physicals and flu shots as the examples.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube for a prothrombin time is put in the specimen refrigerator to await pick-up. Why is that the wrong choice?
opciones: Whole blood for these assays is held at room temperature, not chilled
Whole blood for these assays is held frozen, and chilling is not enough
Refrigeration bursts the red cells and haemolyses the whole specimen
Refrigeration hardens the gel barrier and traps the plasma underneath
preguntas.explicacion: Whole blood drawn for clotting tests is kept at room temperature, roughly eighteen to twenty-four degrees, and refrigeration is avoided because cold can activate factor VII. Chilling whole blood also lowers factor VIII and von Willebrand factor, which can imitate a bleeding disorder.

preguntas.fuente: govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430, sec. 2(4) and 2(8); StatPearls, "Needlestick", Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: Scale of sharps injuries · CPT D1 k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: How many percutaneous injuries, needlesticks among them, did Congress estimate happen each year among U.S. healthcare workers when it passed the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act?
opciones: 6 to 8 million
380,000 in all settings
preguntas.explicacion: Section 2 of the Act cites CDC estimates published in March 2000: over 380,000 percutaneous injuries a year from contaminated sharps in U.S. hospital settings alone, and between 600,000 and 800,000 such injuries, needlesticks among them, once every healthcare setting is counted. The same findings put at 62 to 88 percent the share of sharps injuries that safer devices could prevent. StatPearls lands nearby, about 600,000 a year, and adds that close to half are never reported.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Types of telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Remote patient monitoring · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is listing what its remote monitoring program will accept. Which group of devices does the guidance name?
opciones: Pacemakers, glucose meters, blood pressure monitors, heart rate monitors, wireless scales, oximeters
Blood pressure monitors, fitness trackers, applications that record exercise, and dose reminders
Glucose meters, oximeters, wireless scales, and applications that store discharge instructions
Pacemakers, oximeters, secure messaging platforms, and applications that store health education
preguntas.explicacion: Remote patient monitoring means patient data and clinical information traveling to the provider, whether from devices kept in the home or keyed in and sent electronically by the patient. Named as examples: pacemakers, glucose meters, blood pressure monitors, heart rate monitors, wireless scales and oximeters. Fitness trackers, exercise applications and medicine reminders belong to mobile health, not here.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", sections Introduction and Other Issues (Human Clinical Studies)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: 'If you don't let me draw this, the doctor is going to be very upset with you.' Which requirement of valid consent does this remark violate?
opciones: Voluntariness: the decision must be made free of coercion
Disclosure: the risks of the procedure were never fully listed
Capacity: the patient's understanding was never assessed
Documentation: the consent form was never signed
preguntas.explicacion: Valid consent requires a patient competent to make a voluntary decision, and clinicians must avoid creating any sense of coercion toward their recommendation; the research-consent list names the voluntary nature of the decision as one of three elements. Pressure through a third party's displeasure attacks that element directly, whatever was disclosed or signed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship", Issues of Concern; and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Termination of care · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.d(1) · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who cannot pay is in a critical stage of illness. What does the duty to avoid abandonment require?
opciones: Care continues until the patient is stable, whatever the ability to pay
Care continues for 30 days from the notice, then stops at the deadline
Care stops, but the practice must file the records with the state board
Care stops, provided the patient is handed a list of low-cost clinics
preguntas.explicacion: In an emergency, or while the patient is critically ill, termination has to wait until she is medically stable. Abandonment cases have consistently affirmed the responsibility to go on caring for someone at a critical stage of illness whatever her ability to pay, and one court held a psychiatrist liable where a foreseeable risk of self-harm was involved.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare Summary Notice (MSN)
preguntas.subtema: Accessible formats · CMAA 5 k65, k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA II.F.1.c(2) / 2027 II.F.1.d(3) · RMA II.A.2 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with very low vision says she cannot read her Medicare summary notice. What can she be told is available?
opciones: The notice in an accessible format, large print or Braille among them
The notice read out by a Medicare representative over the telephone
The notice in large print, but only for the electronic version of it
The notice in an accessible format, once her provider requests it for her
preguntas.explicacion: The summary notice can be had in an accessible format where the beneficiary needs one, with large print and Braille given as the examples. Electronic delivery is a separate choice, and it brings an e-mail carrying a link to the notice for any month in which a claim has been processed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Oral Antidiabetic Medications", Adverse Effects and Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.c · NCMA 1.4
preguntas.pregunta: Among the oral antidiabetic agents, which one carries the highest hypoglycemia risk because of its long half-life and active metabolites?
opciones: Glyburide
Glipizide
Glimepiride
Repaglinide
preguntas.explicacion: All three sulfonylureas listed can push the glucose down, but glyburide carries the greatest risk: it lingers and leaves active metabolites behind, which is also why it is avoided once the eGFR falls under 30. For that same reason glimepiride or glipizide tends to be chosen ahead of it. Repaglinide is a meglitinide; hypoglycemia is its main adverse effect too, but it is usually milder because the drug acts briefly.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 5: Fire-Fighting Measures
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 5 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 VI.G.2 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which safety data sheet section tells you which extinguishing agent is right for a fire involving that chemical, and which is not?
opciones: Section 5, which also warns about products given off as it burns
Section 6, which also covers containment and cleanup after a spill
Section 9, which also gives the flash point and the boiling range
Section 7, which also covers safe storage and incompatible products
preguntas.explicacion: Section 5 is written for the fire: which extinguishing equipment is suitable and which is not appropriate for a given situation, the specific hazards the chemical develops while burning, such as hazardous combustion products, and any special protection or precautions for the people fighting it. The flash point in section 9 tells you the chemical can burn; section 5 tells you what to do about it, and section 6 begins where the release has not caught fire.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", Prognosis; Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: Go now, not tomorrow · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stuck at the end of her shift and says she will go to occupational health tomorrow. What is the recommendation?
opciones: Be seen at once, rather than waiting twelve to seventy-two hours for a visit
Be seen within seven days, the deadline that applies to hepatitis B treatment
Be seen at the end of the shift, once the incident report has been written
Be seen within ninety days, while the baseline sample is being preserved
preguntas.explicacion: Follow-up with occupational health should be immediate rather than delayed by twelve to seventy-two hours, because the decisions that depend on it are time-sensitive: baseline testing, hepatitis B immune globulin within about a day, and antiretroviral prophylaxis started preferably within hours. The ninety days is how long a baseline sample is preserved when the employee does not consent to HIV testing on the spot, not a period in which to be seen.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Fixed Recessed Needle
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What is recommended for a device whose sharp sits recessed inside a fixed housing?
opciones: The housing extends past the sharp and keeps fingers out
The housing retracts on activation and exposes the used sharp
The housing is removed before disposal so the bin fills slowly
The housing is colored orange to match an insulin syringe hub
preguntas.explicacion: For a fixed recessed needle the housing has to reach past the sharp, covering it completely and keeping fingers off. Color is a separate recommendation: it should serve a definite purpose, such as telling models or sizes apart, and follow conventions users already know.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth preparation · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4H k62 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: How early should a patient be told to connect for a video appointment, and why?
opciones: Fifteen minutes early, to leave room for last-minute troubleshooting
Thirty minutes early, so staff can complete the whole intake by telephone
Five minutes early, since the platform will reconnect automatically if it drops
Exactly on time, so the virtual waiting room does not fill with early arrivals
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance for getting set up tells patients to pick a spot with plenty of light and not to sit with a window behind them, to keep the camera steady and at eye level showing head and shoulders, to wear loose clothing where skin has to be shown, to find somewhere quiet, to close other applications, and, for a video appointment, to sign on fifteen minutes ahead so there is room to sort out any last-minute trouble.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: What Information is Protected
preguntas.subtema: Security Rule scope · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which information does the HIPAA Security Rule protect, as distinct from the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Only health information that is kept or transmitted in electronic form
Health information in any form, including paper charts and spoken conversations
Only the demographic fields the practice sends in a standard claim transaction
Only information that has already been encrypted or otherwise rendered unreadable
preguntas.explicacion: National standards for one subset of the health information that identifies an individual are what the Security Rule sets: the electronic PHI a regulated entity creates, receives, keeps or transmits. The Privacy and Breach Notification Rules go wider; this one does not reach PHI held on paper or spoken aloud. Its text sits in 45 CFR Part 160 and in Part 164, Subparts A and C.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Choice of gauge
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge and complications · CPT D3 k56 k55 k68 · PBT II.J II.I · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A 16 G needle is used on a small forearm vein and a large hematoma forms. According to WHO Chapter 3, what is the effect of a needle that is too large, and of one that is too small?
opciones: Too large tears the vein and causes bleeding; too small damages the cells and invalidates whole-cell tests
Too large damages the blood cells and invalidates the tests; too small tears the vein and causes a hematoma
Too large slows the draw so the sample clots in the tube; too small lets air into the tubing of the set
Too large causes haemoconcentration of the sample; too small causes the tube to lose its vacuum early
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 says that a needle too large for the vein will tear it and cause bleeding, a hematoma, while a needle too small damages the blood cells as the sample is taken and invalidates tests that need whole cells, hemoglobin or free plasma. It adds that transfusion collection needs a larger gauge than blood drawing, and Table 3.1 reserves 16 to 18 G for blood donation.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, section Home Care
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.B.9.l / 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient faints in a crowded corridor where there is no room to lie down. What is the alternative position?
opciones: Seated forward, with the head between the knees
Seated upright, with the chin lifted and eyes closed
Standing, leaning back against the corridor wall
Seated backwards, with both legs stretched out flat
preguntas.explicacion: The person is normally kept lying down for at least ten to fifteen minutes, ideally somewhere cool and quiet. Where that cannot be arranged, the alternative given is to sit the person forward with the head between the knees; tight clothing round the neck is loosened either way.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Body Mass Index", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · RMA III.E.4.a · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has lost weight quickly without meaning to, and the body mass index has dropped. What may that signal?
opciones: An eating disorder, a malignancy or a disease of malabsorption
A gain in lean mass, which the index reads as a fall in body fat
A measurement error, since the index moves slowly by its nature
Dehydration only, since fluid loss is the one thing that moves it fast
preguntas.explicacion: A sudden unintended fall in the index is a warning sign that can point to an eating disorder, a cancer or a disorder of absorption. The figure is also used in surgical clinics to predict recovery and the risk of soft tissue infection after an operation. The patient is treated, not the number.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: Use the show-me method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4I evaluate understanding · CMA I.A.6.d · 2027 I.A.6.d · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient starting a blood thinner correctly states the dose and the times. What should still be done?
opciones: Use the show-me method and have him demonstrate the dose with the pills
Accept the correct statement, since saying it right proves he can do it
Repeat the same explanation once more and end the teaching there
Have him write the dose and the times down and file the note in the chart
preguntas.explicacion: Research behind the show-me method found that many patients who state the timing and amount of a new or changed medicine correctly still get the dose wrong when asked to demonstrate it. Having the patient show the dose with the actual pills catches what words alone hide.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Unpacking Deliveries
preguntas.subtema: Verifying deliveries · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A shipment of vaccine arrives at the desk. Which check belongs to verifying the contents of that delivery?
opciones: Comparing what is inside against the packing list and looking for damage
Signing the carrier's manifest and moving the sealed box to the storeroom
Recording the arrival in the temperature log kept on the storage unit door
Waiting for the coordinator's shift to start before the box is touched at all
preguntas.explicacion: Unpacking is where verification happens: examine the shipping container and its contents for damage, compare the contents against the packing list, check that the right diluents came in the right quantity, and read the expiration dates. Leaving the box sealed defeats the check and the cold chain at the same time.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Granular Leukocytes and Agranular Leukocytes
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A differential on a patient with a bacterial infection shows 80 percent of one leukocyte type. Which type is normally the most common and rises with bacterial infection?
opciones: Neutrophils, normally 50 to 70 percent of leukocytes
Lymphocytes, normally 20 to 30 percent of leukocytes
Monocytes, normally 2 to 8 percent of leukocytes
Eosinophils, normally 2 to 4 percent of leukocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Neutrophils are the most common leukocyte at 50 to 70 percent of the count; they respond fast to infection, prefer bacteria, and high counts point to bacterial infection or inflammation, as well as burns and stress. Lymphocytes are second at 20 to 30 percent and rise with viral infections; monocytes are 2 to 8 percent and eosinophils 2 to 4 percent, rising with allergies and parasitic worms.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: Media Mail
preguntas.subtema: Media Mail · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An office is shipping loose-leaf medical reference pages and their binders to a satellite clinic on the cheapest eligible service. What must staff know about it?
opciones: Media Mail takes those pages and binders, and every package may be opened for inspection
Media Mail takes any office paper, and the contents of a package are never examined
Ground Advantage takes those pages, and packages of paper are exempt from inspection
Priority Mail takes those pages, and books are the only content it accepts by weight
preguntas.explicacion: Medical loose-leaf pages and binders are on the short list of what qualifies for Media Mail, along with books, printed music, recordings and manuscripts. The trade for the low price is that every Media Mail package may be opened and inspected, and anything ineligible inside means somebody pays the higher postage.

preguntas.subtema: Correction period · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A violation is due to willful neglect. What period does the regulation give for correcting it before the top penalty tier applies?
opciones: Thirty days from the first date the entity knew, or would have known with reasonable diligence
Sixty days from the first date the entity knew, matching the deadline for breach notification
Ten working days from the first date the entity knew, as with new hire vaccination records
Six years from the first date the entity knew, matching the documentation retention period
preguntas.explicacion: Tier three catches willful neglect that gets put right inside a window of 30 days. The clock starts the day the entity, or the business associate acting for it, first knew of the violation, or would have known of it had reasonable diligence been used. Let that window close without correcting and the case drops into the fourth tier, the costliest one.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose screening tests during pregnancy (007562), How the Test will Feel; MedlinePlus, Glucose tolerance test (003466), How the Test will Feel; StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: Tolerance test patient care · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.B patient interaction · CCMA 3E k139 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Twenty minutes after drinking the glucose solution, a pregnant patient says she feels nauseated, sweaty and lightheaded. What is the appropriate response?
opciones: Reassure her: those reactions are known, and serious effects are very uncommon
Stop the test and report it to the provider as a failed glucose screen
Offer her a light snack to settle her stomach before the next blood draw
Have her drink the glucose solution again, since some may not have stayed down
preguntas.explicacion: Most patients come through the glucose tolerance test with no side effects at all; a few turn sweaty, lightheaded or nauseated once the solution is down, and anything serious is very uncommon. The patient stays seated throughout and does not eat while the test runs. What she is asked beforehand is whether blood tests or medical procedures have brought on such symptoms before, which the provider is told; repeating the drink is no part of any of these protocols.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part D (Drug Coverage) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who put off joining a Medicare drug plan asks when a late enrollment penalty starts to apply.
opciones: Once she has gone sixty-three days or more without coverage as good as Part D
Once she has gone thirty days or more without coverage as good as Part D
Once eight months have passed since her job-based health coverage ended
Once her first seven months of Medicare eligibility have run out entirely
preguntas.explicacion: The way to dodge the Part D penalty is to join a drug plan when Part A or Part B first starts, and never to spend sixty-three days or more with no creditable drug coverage, meaning coverage similar in value to Part D. Someone on a limited income and with limited resources who qualifies for Extra Help pays no late enrollment penalty at all.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 5.4, Table 5.4c: Common Metric Conversions in Health Care
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k17 · CMA I.D.2.b(1) · RMA III.G.2.f · NCMA 1.7
preguntas.pregunta: A label reads 0.25 g and the order is written in milligrams. Which equivalence applies?
opciones: 1 gram equals 1000 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 1000 micrograms
1 gram equals 100 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 100 micrograms
1 gram equals 1000 micrograms, and 1 milligram equals 1000 grams
1 gram equals 10 milligrams, and 1 milligram equals 10 micrograms
preguntas.explicacion: The metric system is built on units of ten, so converting is a matter of moving the decimal point. The equivalences to hold in the head are that a gram is 1000 milligrams and a milligram is 1000 micrograms, alongside a liter being 1000 milliliters. Confusing milligrams with micrograms is a thousand-fold error, which is exactly why the microgram symbol is written out as mcg on an order.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Disorders of Clotting; and Plasma Anticoagulants
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74 post-procedural bleeding) · PBT I.C · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on daily low-dose aspirin keeps bleeding at the puncture site longer than expected. What does aspirin do to hemostasis?
opciones: It is an antiplatelet; it inhibits the aggregation of platelets
It is a thrombolytic; it converts plasminogen into plasmin
It inactivates factor X, in the same way antithrombin does
It blocks vitamin K, so the liver makes fewer clotting factors
preguntas.explicacion: Aspirin is an antiplatelet drug that is very effective at inhibiting platelet aggregation, which is why it is given during heart attacks and strokes and sometimes daily at low dose to people at cardiovascular risk. Thrombolytics such as tissue plasminogen activator work on plasminogen instead, and antithrombin works on factor X and on the conversion of prothrombin.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Cortisol Test, section What happens during a cortisol test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k45 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: For a blood cortisol test, when are the samples usually drawn?
opciones: Once in the morning and again around 4 p.m. on the same day
Once at midnight, when cortisol is normally at its peak
Once in the morning only, after a strict 12-hour overnight fast
Every hour for 2 to 3 hours after a sugary glucose drink
preguntas.explicacion: Blood samples are usually taken twice in one day: in the morning, when cortisol is normally highest, and again around 4 p.m., when it is normally much lower, which is why the patient needs two appointments. The physiology matches: peak near awakening, lowest at night. A 12-hour morning fast describes iron, and hourly samples describe the tolerance test.

preguntas.subtema: Dental code set · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A practice adds a dental service line and asks which code set covers it, and who keeps that set up to date. What is the answer?
opciones: The dental procedure code set, kept by the American Dental Association
The dental procedure code set, kept by the federal health department
The procedure coding system for inpatients, kept by the federal health department
The common procedure coding system, kept by the American Medical Association
preguntas.explicacion: For dental services the regulation names the Code on Dental Procedures and Nomenclature. The American Dental Association is the body that maintains it and distributes it. The federal health department keeps the diagnosis set, the inpatient procedure set, and the level of the common procedure system that covers supplies and equipment.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, How to Understand and Use the Nutrition Facts Label: Calories; and The Percent Daily Value
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 food labels · CMA I.A.6.g(4) · 2027 I.A.6.g(4) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: What calorie level are the % Daily Values on the Nutrition Facts label based on?
opciones: 2,000 calories a day, used as general nutrition advice
2,500 calories a day, used as general nutrition advice
1,800 calories a day, the average for adult women
The calorie level the shopper enters in the MyPlate Plan tool
