preguntas.explicacion: The footnote of the panel states that the percentages rest on a 2,000-calorie day, offered as general advice. A given person may need more or fewer calories depending on age, sex, height, weight and activity, which is why the label points readers to a personalized plan for their own estimate.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 7 to 10
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k57 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.J · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's order calls for every tube on the chart. Which one is filled ninth?
opciones: The pale yellow tube used for tissue typing and DNA work
The purple top tube used for hematology and cross-match
The light gray top tube used for glucose determinations
The light green tube used for chemistry panels on plasma
preguntas.explicacion: Position 9 belongs to the pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube, whose listed uses are HLA tissue typing, paternity testing and DNA studies. EDTA is number 8 and the fluoride/oxalate tube number 10, so the ACD tube falls between them; the light green PST comes earlier, at position 7.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC); and Medicare.gov, Federally Qualified Health Center services: Costs
preguntas.subtema: Community resources for care · CCMA 4D k162 · CMAA 2H k30 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient without insurance asks where she can be seen for primary care on a sliding scale based on what she can pay. What fits?
opciones: A federally qualified health center, whose fees slide with the patient's ability to pay
An ambulatory surgical center, where Part B pays the facility fee for an approved surgery
A hospital emergency department, which evaluates a sudden illness that quickly worsens
A skilled nursing facility, where daily skilled nursing or therapy is given short term
preguntas.explicacion: Federally qualified health centers are federally funded nonprofit centers and clinics that serve areas and populations which are medically underserved. They furnish primary care regardless of the patient's ability to pay, and the fee follows a sliding scale tied to that ability. Centers also offer lower fees to people with limited income.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Medicare Advantage (Medicare Part C); and Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What is a Medicare Advantage Plan?
opciones: A private plan under contract with Medicare that delivers Part A and Part B benefits
A private plan sold by insurers that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare
A federal plan that replaces Part A for patients treated in a network of hospitals
A state plan that covers premiums and deductibles for people with low income
preguntas.explicacion: Medicare Advantage, also called Part C, comes from private companies under contract with Medicare to deliver every Part A and Part B benefit, usually with drug coverage on top; the types include health maintenance organizations and preferred provider organizations. Private insurance that pays the patient's share of Original Medicare is Medigap, and help with premiums for people on a low income comes through Medicaid.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, How to Understand and Use the Nutrition Facts Label: Nutrients
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 food labels · CMA I.A.6.g(4) · 2027 I.A.6.g(4) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of nutrients does the Nutrition Facts label flag as ones to get less of?
opciones: Saturated fat, sodium and added sugars
Saturated fat, sodium and dietary fiber
Total fat, total sugars and total carbohydrate
Cholesterol, protein and trans fat
preguntas.explicacion: The label separates the nutrients to get less of, which are saturated fat, sodium and added sugars, from the ones to get more of: calcium, dietary fiber, iron, potassium and vitamin D. Fiber belongs to the second list. Total sugars and trans fat carry no percentage at all, so they are not part of either guide.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 8: Conduct Brown Bag Medicine Reviews
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4F facilitate compliance · CMA I.A.6.d · 2027 I.A.6.d · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to bring everything to a brown bag medicine review. What does that include?
opciones: Prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, supplements and herbals
Prescriptions and over-the-counter drugs, but not vitamins or supplements
Prescriptions only, since the rest are not entered in the medication list
Prescriptions and the pill organizer, but not the original containers
preguntas.explicacion: The review covers every prescription, every over-the-counter product, every vitamin, supplement and herbal medicine, plus topicals, liquids, injections and inhalants, and the pills in both their original bottles and any organizer. Seeing the actual containers is what reveals whether and why medicines are being taken wrong.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 depth by age · PBT II.J lancets · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.5 equipment by age
preguntas.pregunta: A 4-year-old needs a finger-prick. Which puncture depth is recommended for that age?
opciones: 1.5 mm, the depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years
2.4 mm, the depth for a child over 6 months and under 8 years
0.85 mm, the depth for any child who has not reached school age
2.2 mm, the longest lancet, because the finger has no bone risk
preguntas.explicacion: Two finger-prick depths are given for children: 1.5 mm between 6 months and 8 years, and 2.4 mm from 8 years on. The 0.85 mm lancet is the length kept for premature babies, and 2.2 mm is the longest lancet in normal use on an adult finger, since a finger puncture is not to pass 2.4 mm.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Small quantities of capillary blood
preguntas.subtema: Shared glucometers · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k104 · CMA I.B.5 / 2027 I.B.4 · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A glucometer and its lancet platform are used for several inpatients during a round. What does best practice require?
opciones: Dedicate it to one patient, or clean and disinfect it between uses
Change the lancet and wipe the platform with a dry gauze pad
Rinse the platform under running water at the end of the round
Keep it in a clean bag between patients, which avoids contact
preguntas.explicacion: For small quantities of capillary blood the equipment is single-use: a lancet, or a retractable one, and a platform or glucometer either dedicated to a single patient for the whole stay or, between patients, wiped free of every visible trace of dirt and then disinfected with alcohol. The reason is on the record: hepatitis has reached patients where a glucometer or its platform was passed from one person to the next without that reprocessing.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Critical Limits of Laboratory Results for Urgent Clinician Notification" (EJIFCC 2003, PMC6178782), introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5G 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A glucose drawn from the arm carrying a glucose infusion comes back far above the critical limit, and the patient looks well. What clears the picture?
opciones: Testing a second specimen collected properly from another site
Repeating the measurement twice on the same tube and averaging
Reporting the figure and letting the clinician judge the context
Diluting the specimen and correcting for the dilution factor used
preguntas.explicacion: Preanalytical influences are named outright as a frequent source of results that only look critical, and the example given is a glucose drawn through a venous catheter that had been used for a glucose infusion. Cases like that are normally settled by testing another, properly collected specimen; repeating the same contaminated tube only confirms the contamination.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Step 7 and Table 2.3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection"; and WHO Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010) (NBK138665)
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error: haemolysis · CPT D3 k9 k59 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory rejects a sample as hemolyzed. Which collection practices are recognized causes of hemolysis?
opciones: Pressing the syringe plunger, shaking the tube, and a short draw in the gray tube
Leaving the tourniquet on for more than one minute, and drawing the tubes in the wrong sequence
Using a 21 G needle in an adult, and inverting the citrate tube three to six times
Preparing the skin with povidone iodine, and labeling the tubes away from the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Pressing the plunger raises the risk of hemolysis, Table 2.3 warns that a short draw in the fluoride tube may cause hemolysis, and vigorous shaking or overmixing of the tube produces hemolysis. A long tourniquet causes hemoconcentration, the wrong sequence causes additive carry-over, iodine raises potassium, and three to six gentle inversions is the correct handling of the citrate tube.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with COPD asks what those letters mean. Which expansion is correct?
opciones: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a disease of the lungs
Chronic obstructive peptic disorder, a stomach disease
Congenital obstructive pulmonary defect, a lung disease
Chronic occlusive peripheral disease, an artery disease
preguntas.explicacion: COPD is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, the long-standing lung condition that makes breathing hard. The look-alike abbreviations belong elsewhere: PUD is peptic ulcer disease, CHD is congenital heart disease and PAD is peripheral arterial disease, the arteries outside the heart.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Complications and Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Complications: haematoma · CPT D3 3Q 3L k70 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E9 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A hematoma forms at a site where the technique looked correct throughout. Which omission is the likely explanation?
opciones: Pressure was not kept up during and after the needle came out
Pressure was kept up too long after the needle had come out
The tourniquet was released before the needle was withdrawn
The site was cleaned with alcohol rather than povidone iodine
preguntas.explicacion: A hematoma can form when too little pressure is kept up during the draw and after it, which is why the gauze is taped down to give continuous pressure. Releasing the band before the needle comes out is the correct order, and alcohol is the preferred antiseptic for a routine draw.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Oxygen Therapy", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: NCMA 2B.14 · CCMA 3B4 · CMA I.A.6.d
preguntas.pregunta: A nasal cannula is running at 4 L/min. Roughly what oxygen concentration does that deliver?
opciones: Somewhere in the 24% to 40% band that 1 to 6 L/min produces
Somewhere in the 40% to 60% band that 1 to 6 L/min produces
Close to 50%, which is what a face tent reaches at high flow
Between 60% and 80%, the range of a mask with a reservoir bag
preguntas.explicacion: A cannula runs at one to six liters a minute and gives roughly 24% to 40% oxygen; the figure is approximate because how much room air is mixed in depends on the patient's rate and depth of breathing. A simple face mask at 5 to 10 L/min gives about 40% to 60%, a face tent up to 15 L/min about 50%, and a nonrebreather at 10 to 15 L/min more still.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (equipment compatibility and expiration dates)
preguntas.subtema: Equipment quality checks · CPT D3 3B k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A box of evacuated tubes is found to be past its expiration date. What two problems do expired tubes present?
opciones: Reduced ability to draw blood in, and additives that may have degraded
Loss of sterility of the stopper, and a gel that no longer separates serum
A higher risk of hemolysis, and colors that no longer match the order of draw
Cracks in the plastic, and an anticoagulant that turns plasma into serum
preguntas.explicacion: Expiration dates matter because expired vacuum tubes have a decreased capacity to aspirate blood and their additives may be degraded, so even small deviations can affect the results. The other options mix real problems from the tube collection review, such as a missing anticoagulant or a lost vacuum after uncapping, with effects the chapter does not attribute to expiry.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Blood Glucose Test, sections What happens during a blood glucose test, and Will I need to do anything to prepare
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes fasted 14 hours for a hemoglobin A1C 'to be safe'. Which statement is correct?
opciones: Fasting was not needed; the A1C reflects average glucose over about 3 months
Fasting was needed; the A1C requires no caloric intake for at least 8 full hours
Fasting was needed; samples are drawn before and after a sugary drink
Fasting was harmful; the A1C result will now read falsely low
preguntas.explicacion: The hemoglobin A1C test uses one sample, needs no fasting, and reports average blood glucose over the past 3 months. The 8-hour rule with no caloric intake applies to the fasting plasma glucose, and the drink-then-resample sequence is the tolerance test. Fasting is simply not part of the A1C's preparation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Introduction; and Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: What is the relationship between an ethical principle and a patient right?
opciones: A right appears when a body with authority enforces an ethical standard
A right appears when a professional society publishes it in its own code
A right appears when a majority of patients in a survey come to expect it
A right and an ethical principle are the same thing under a different name
preguntas.explicacion: Human rights are the minimum standards for how people can expect to be treated; ethics are the customary standards for how people should treat others. Every patient right rests on one or more ethical principles, and a right exists at the moment an organization with the authority to enforce that ethical standard actually enforces it. As ethics shift over time, so do rights.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: Electronic notice delivery · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice takes its first new patients through an online intake before any in-person visit. What does the notice rule require?
opciones: An electronic notice sent automatically with the first request, and an attempt at a return receipt
A paper notice mailed within thirty days of the electronic request for service being received
An electronic notice posted on the web site only, since online patients can read it there
A telephone call reading the notice aloud, since electronic delivery cannot be acknowledged
preguntas.explicacion: Where the first delivery of service happens over the Internet, by e-mail or in some other electronic way, the notice goes out electronically, automatically and at the same moment as the patient's first request for service, and the provider has to make a good faith effort to get back a return receipt or another response transmission. Any web site describing the entity's services or benefits must carry the notice prominently as well.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Understanding telehealth technology options
preguntas.subtema: Consent before a video visit · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: When does the telehealth guidance say informed consent for a video visit has to be obtained?
opciones: Before the appointment, alongside a platform that meets the privacy requirements
At the start of the appointment, once the clinician has confirmed who the patient is
Only where the session will be recorded or a third party is to be brought into it
After the appointment, when the visit is documented as having been done by video
preguntas.explicacion: Patients may worry about privacy and about data security, both over what they share during a visit and over home devices that collect their health data. Providers are told to deliver telehealth from private locations, to apply safeguards that are reasonable to the protected health information, to use a platform that meets the privacy requirements, and to obtain informed consent from the patient before the telehealth appointment.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, introduction and Section 9
preguntas.subtema: Nothing left blank · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What must a safety data sheet do when its preparer finds no information for a required element?
opciones: Say that no applicable information was found for that element
Leave that element blank, which is read as not applicable
Copy the entry from a sheet for a similar product in the family
Move the element to section 16 with the other information
preguntas.explicacion: Silence is not allowed. Where the preparer finds no relevant information for a required element, the sheet must say outright that nothing applicable was found, and section 9 repeats the rule for the physical and chemical properties: an item that is not relevant, or not available, carries a note saying so for that property. A blank leaves the reader unable to tell an absent hazard from an unresearched one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Geriatric Care Special Needs Assessment", Issues of Concern: Functional Status
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA 2B.2 · CMA I.A.4.g
preguntas.pregunta: A geriatric intake separates basic from instrumental activities of daily living. Which pair is right?
opciones: Bathing and dressing are basic; shopping and handling finances are instrumental
Shopping and cooking are basic; bathing and toileting are instrumental activities
Walking and feeding are basic; grooming and bladder control are instrumental
Driving and using the telephone are basic; dressing and feeding are instrumental
preguntas.explicacion: Basic activities are self-care: bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, feeding oneself, and control of bladder and bowel. Instrumental ones are what independent living needs on top of that: taking medicines, shopping, cooking, transport, finances, housework and the telephone. The Katz index measures the first group and the Lawton scale the second.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule
preguntas.subtema: Identity theft protection · CCMA 5F · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4C k63 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many elements must a written identity theft prevention program contain under the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Four: identify, detect, respond and update
Three: identify, detect and report to the police
Five: identify, detect, respond, update and insure
Two: identify the red flags and train the staff on them
preguntas.explicacion: The program must include reasonable policies for identifying the red flags of identity theft in day-to-day operations, procedures designed to detect the flags it identified, the actions to take when one is detected, and a way of keeping the program current against new threats. A red flag is a suspicious pattern, practice or activity signaling possible identity theft, such as an identification document that does not look genuine.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The note describes a threatened condition that in the end did occur. How is it coded?
opciones: As a confirmed diagnosis, just as if it had been documented outright
As threatened, using the index subentry for that term where it exists
As threatened, since that is the word the provider used in the record
Not at all, because a threatened condition is an uncertain diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: A condition the note calls impending or threatened is coded as a confirmed diagnosis if it did in fact occur. Only when it did not occur does the coder look for a subentry for impending or threatened, and where no such subentry exists the underlying conditions are coded instead of the threatened one.

preguntas.subtema: Medicare Advantage records · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A plan holds a Medicare Advantage contract. For how long must it keep the books and records behind that contract?
opciones: Ten years, so that the accounting and the services can be audited and inspected
Seven years from the date of service, as with orders and certifications in Part B
Five years, as with the medical records a hospital keeps to take part in Medicare
Six years from creation, as with the documentation the privacy standards require
preguntas.explicacion: Every retention period in this area belongs to a different rule, and the trap is borrowing one for another. The Medicare Advantage contract obliges the organization to keep its books, records and other evidence of accounting for ten years, enough for CMS to audit the finances and to inspect the quality and timeliness of the services.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Adult BMI Calculator: BMI Category Ranges
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: An adult has a body mass index of 41.2. How is that classified?
opciones: Class 3 obesity, also called severe obesity, from 40.0 upward
Class 2 obesity, the band that runs from 35.0 to 39.9
Class 1 obesity, the band that runs from 30.0 to 39.9
Obesity without a class, since the classes stop at 40.0
preguntas.explicacion: Obesity is divided into three classes: 30.0 to 34.9, 35.0 to 39.9, and 40.0 or greater, the last of which is also called severe obesity. Naming the class matters because risk climbs with it: high cholesterol, diabetes of type 2, blood pressure that runs high. The index is still a screening measure, not a diagnosis.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Precautionary Statements
preguntas.subtema: Precautionary statements · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What are the four types of precautionary statements found on a Hazard Communication label?
opciones: Prevention, response, storage and disposal
Physical, health, environmental and unclassified
Identification, composition, handling and transport
Danger, warning, caution and notice
preguntas.explicacion: Precautionary statements describe the measures recommended to minimize or prevent harm from exposure, storage or handling, and they come in four types: prevention, to limit exposure; response, for spills, emergencies and first aid; storage; and disposal. Physical, health and environmental are the three hazard groups of the GHS; identification, composition, handling and transport are SDS section titles; and Danger and Warning are the only two signal words, so caution and notice do not exist in this system.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine collection - infants (003417), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: Infant bag collection · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(e) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A mother is sent home to collect urine from her 6-month-old with an adhesive bag. Which instruction is correct?
opciones: Wash the genital area, apply the bag, put a diaper over it, check the baby often and remove the bag once urine collects
Apply the bag over the unwashed skin so the adhesive holds better, and leave it in place until the next diaper change
Wash the genital area, apply the bag without a diaper so it is visible, and leave it on for exactly 24 hours
Wash the genital area with an antiseptic, pass a small catheter into the bladder and drain the urine into the bag
preguntas.explicacion: The area around the urethra is washed with the soap or wipes the provider recommends, the bag is opened and stuck on (the whole penis inside it, or over the labia), a diaper goes on over the bag, and the baby is checked often. Active infants can displace the bag, so extra bags are useful. The urine is emptied into the container without touching its inside and, at home, kept in a plastic bag in the refrigerator. Catheterization is done by a provider.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment; Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.a · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A prenatal clinic wants one body measurement to follow nutritional status. Which one is reported as the measurement of choice in pregnancy?
opciones: Mid-upper arm circumference, taken at the marked midpoint of the arm
Waist circumference, taken over each hip bone at the mid-axillary line
Body mass index, worked out again from height and weight at each visit
Triceps skinfold, taken with calipers just above the midpoint of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Mid-upper arm circumference helps grade how severe malnutrition is, and in the pregnant population one study reports it as the anthropometric measurement to choose. It is taken standing, with the arm hanging freely and the muscles unflexed, the tape snug at the marked midpoint of the arm and not pressed into the skin.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Exclusive Provider Organization (EPO) Plan
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which managed care plan covers services only from doctors, specialists and hospitals in its network, except in an emergency?
opciones: An exclusive provider organization plan
A preferred provider organization plan
A point of service plan with referrals
A fee-for-service indemnity arrangement
preguntas.explicacion: The exclusive provider organization is the managed care plan whose coverage stops at the edge of the network, with the emergency exception. A PPO pays something for outside providers at a higher cost to the patient. A point of service plan also pays less outside the network and adds the referral rule. Fee for service is a payment method, one payment per service delivered, not a network design.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(a)(3), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D4 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A swab reaches the laboratory carrying the patient's name and ID number, but nothing on it says where on the body it came from. Under CLIA's specimen labeling policy element, what is missing?
opciones: The specimen source, which must appear on the label when appropriate
The test requested, which must be written on every specimen container
The collector's signature, which is required on all microbiology specimens
The date of birth, which is mandatory on the label for every specimen
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1242(a)(3) requires the laboratory's labeling procedure to cover the patient's name or unique identifier and, when appropriate, the specimen source; for a swab the site is exactly that appropriate case. The regulation does not put the test name, the collector's signature or the date of birth on the container itself, although the requisition must carry the sex and the age or date of birth.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · RMA III.E.4.c · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: How is an infant under 2 years weighed?
opciones: Undressed and with the diaper off, on a calibrated beam or digital infant scale
In a clean diaper and light clothing, on a calibrated beam or digital infant scale
Held by a parent on a floor scale, with the parent's weight subtracted afterward
Undressed, on the same floor scale used for children older than 24 months
preguntas.explicacion: For children under 2 the weighing is done on an infant scale, digital or a calibrated beam, with the clothes off and the diaper removed, to the nearest 0.01 kg or half an ounce. From 24 months onward a balanced or electronic floor scale is used instead.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(e)(2)(ii)(M), Special practices
preguntas.subtema: The biosafety manual · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C2 k109 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: In a laboratory that works with concentrated HIV or HBV, what does the standard require of the biosafety manual?
opciones: It is reviewed and updated at least yearly, and staff must read and follow it
It is written once at start-up and kept for the duration of employment
It is posted at the door with the name and phone of the laboratory director
It takes the place of the exposure control plan for employees in that area
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e)(2)(ii)(M) asks for a biosafety manual to be prepared or adopted, then reviewed and updated periodically, at least once a year and more often if needed. It also puts a duty on the staff: they are advised of the potential hazards, and they have to read the practices and procedures they are given and then follow them. What goes on the door is the warning sign of (g)(1)(ii)(A). All of this sits on top of the exposure control plan, which paragraph (c) still demands.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Before a sample is accepted, the accessioning clerk checks the two identifiers on the tube. What second check does the emergency laboratory in the rejection study also require?
opciones: That the sample and the requested tests match each other correctly
That the tube was drawn by a phlebotomist rather than by a nurse
That the barcode was printed within the last 30 minutes
That the hemolysis index was measured before the sample was accessioned
preguntas.explicacion: In that laboratory the secretary verifies that the minimum two identification criteria, name and surname plus patient ID, are present, and additionally checks that the sample and the test requests match; with these controls the misidentification rate was 0.3 %. Serum indices are measured after acceptance, and neither the collector's role nor the barcode print time is an acceptance criterion.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, overview
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: How long does a fainting episode usually last, and what is the typical recovery?
opciones: Usually less than a couple of minutes, with quick recovery
Usually 10 to 15 minutes, with gradual recovery over an hour
Usually a few seconds, with confusion for several minutes afterwards
Usually 5 to 10 minutes, with weakness for the rest of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting is a brief loss of consciousness from a drop in blood flow to the brain, most often lasting less than a couple of minutes, with quick recovery; the medical name is syncope. Ten to fifteen minutes is how long the person is kept lying down afterwards, and confusion on waking points to a seizure rather than syncope.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: Blood in an arm vein drains toward the heart against gravity. Which feature of the vein keeps it from running back down?
opciones: One-way valves set inside the lumen of the vein
A thicker muscular coat than the artery beside it
The perforating branches that reach the deep veins
The venae comitantes that travel with the artery
preguntas.explicacion: Veins carry one-way valves in the lumen, and their job is to stop the blood draining backwards on its way up to the heart. The wall holds less muscle than an artery, which is why a vein stretches and acts as a reservoir. Perforating veins link the superficial system to the deep one, and the venae comitantes are the paired veins that run with the forearm arteries.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Body Parts and Disorders; Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A soft fatty lump under the skin is reported as a lipoma. Which two word parts build that term?
opciones: A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning tumor
A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning inflammation
A root meaning muscle plus an ending meaning tumor
A root meaning fat plus an ending meaning enlargement
preguntas.explicacion: Lip- and lipo- name fat, and so does adip-; the ending -oma is a tumor. The endings that crowd around it say something else entirely: -itis is inflammation, -megaly is enlargement and -osis is an abnormal condition. Muscle is my- or myo-, so a tumor built on that root would be a myoma.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CMAA 3B k38 safeguards · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital gives its laboratory technologists access to laboratory records but not to the full medical history. What is that practice called, and does HIPAA allow it?
opciones: Selective, role-based access, which is exactly the way the rule expects internal access to work
Selective, role-based access, which the rule discourages because it slows care coordination
A limited data set, which HIPAA permits only for research, public health or health operations
A hybrid entity designation, which limits the rules to the components that do covered work
preguntas.explicacion: Holding each worker to the part of the record their role requires is exactly what the rule asks: the policies have to name who, or which classes of people, need access, which categories of information they need, and on what conditions. A limited data set is a stripped-down form of information for research and similar uses, and a hybrid entity is an organizational choice, not an access control.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Claim Denial Rate
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations and denials · CMAA 6E, 4G k67 · CCMA 5M k183 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A denial arrives stating that the billed procedure differs from the one authorized. What does the source of that problem suggest for next time?
opciones: Update the authorization before the claim goes out when the procedure changes
Send the claim unchanged, since the payer matches authorizations automatically
Bill the patient for the difference, since the authorization covered part of it
Wait for the appeal decision before asking the payer to change any authorization
preguntas.explicacion: Among the causes of denials, billing a procedure code that differs from the authorized one is listed with its own remedy: update the information before submission or justify the discrepancy clearly. Some payers will change an authorization only up to 14 days past the date of service, after which the denial tends to become permanent, so waiting for an appeal wastes the window. Nothing in that mismatch makes the balance a patient responsibility.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet · CPT D3 k60 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: What does a tourniquet do that makes venipuncture easier?
opciones: It presses on the limb and blocks the venous return for a while, so the veins show up
It stops arterial inflow so that the veins below it empty and become straighter
It disinfects the skin above the site, so the alcohol contact time can be shortened
It keeps the blood from clotting in the tubing of a winged collection set
preguntas.explicacion: The tourniquet puts a passing pressure on the limb and blocks the flow artificially, which helps the phlebotomist find the veins, and cites studies showing the veins dilate and gain surface area right after a tightly placed tourniquet. It must not stop arterial flow, it has no antiseptic role, and it has nothing to do with the air in butterfly tubing.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(g)(1), (g)(3) and (g)(5), Personal representatives
preguntas.subtema: Personal representatives · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.3.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A parent asks for the lab results of their 8-year-old child. How does HIPAA treat the parent?
opciones: As the child's personal representative, acting as the individual for that PHI
As a third party who needs the child's own signed authorization first
As a family member entitled only to a verbal summary at the visit
As a personal representative only after a court has appointed the parent as guardian
preguntas.explicacion: Under section 164.502(g) a personal representative is treated as if they were the individual. For an unemancipated minor that representative is the parent, the guardian or a person acting in loco parentis who holds authority under applicable law to make health care decisions, and it covers the PHI relevant to that role, with no court appointment needed. The exceptions are services the minor may lawfully consent to alone, and situations of abuse or endangerment where the entity may refuse to treat the person as representative; state law can widen or narrow parental access.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Directional Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A report describes one structure as cranial to another. Which directional term is used for that same idea?
opciones: Superior, toward the head end of the body
Inferior, away from the head end of the body
Anterior, toward the front of the body
Posterior, toward the back of the body
preguntas.explicacion: Most directional terms travel in pairs that mean the same thing: superior and cranial point toward the head, inferior and caudal away from it, anterior and ventral name the front, and posterior and dorsal the back. That is why the hand belongs to the superior extremity and the foot to the inferior one.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Germs and Hygiene — How can I protect myself and others from germs?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k169 disease prevention education · CMA I.A.6.c · 2027 I.A.6.c · RMA III.A.1 infection control · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how long she should scrub when washing her hands at home. What is the answer, and when does it matter most?
opciones: At least 20 seconds, including before, during and after preparing food
At least 20 seconds, but only after using the toilet or changing a diaper
At least 10 seconds, including before, during and after preparing food
At least 60 seconds, including before, during and after preparing food
preguntas.explicacion: Hands are scrubbed well and often, for at least 20 seconds. The moments that matter most are the ones where germs are picked up or passed on: before, during and after handling food, before eating, around caring for someone sick or treating a wound, after the toilet or diapers, after coughing or sneezing, and after animals or garbage.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k149 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: In lead V6 the ventricular complex writes a deep downward deflection instead of the usual tall upright wave. What is suggested?
opciones: Record from a position further to the left, out at V7
Record from a position further to the right, back at V1
Drop V6 one intercostal space and run the tracing again
Raise the standardization and run the tracing again
preguntas.explicacion: V6 is expected to write a tall upward wave. When a deep S appears there instead, the guidance is to move out to the left and take V7, hunting for a pattern whose main deflection points up. Moving an electrode down a space is not part of that advice.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.404(a), (b) and (d), Notification to individuals
preguntas.subtema: Breach notification deadline · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3E k33
preguntas.pregunta: A breach of unsecured PHI has just been discovered. How fast must the covered entity notify the individuals affected?
opciones: No more than 60 calendar days after discovery, and without unreasonable delay
Within 30 days after discovery, matching the right-of-access deadline
Within 90 days after discovery, the period a substitute web notice stays posted
By the end of the calendar year, regardless of the number of individuals
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.404 requires notice to every individual whose unsecured PHI was accessed, acquired, used or disclosed, or is reasonably believed to have been. Two limits apply at once: no unreasonable delay, and 60 calendar days from discovery as the outer edge. A breach counts as discovered the first day it is known, or would have been known with reasonable diligence, to any workforce member other than the one who caused it. Written notice travels by first-class mail, or by e-mail if the person agreed to that; where contact details are missing for 10 or more people, a substitute posting on the website or a media notice runs for 90 days.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiii)(B) and (C), specimen containers
preguntas.subtema: Specimens that can puncture · CPT D1 1G k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.6.a / 2027 I.B.5.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A specimen stiff enough to puncture its primary container is being shipped to a reference laboratory. What does the standard add?
opciones: A secondary container that resists puncture as well as leakage, and is labeled
A secondary container that closes and holds fluids, with no puncture requirement
A red bag around the primary container, which substitutes for the outer label
A label stating which portion of the primary container remains contaminated
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiii) builds up in three steps. The specimen goes in a container that will not leak. If the outside of that container becomes contaminated, subparagraph (B) puts it inside a second leakproof container that is labeled or color-coded. And subparagraph (C) adds the extra requirement here: when the specimen itself could puncture the primary container, the secondary one must be puncture-resistant on top of everything else. The label naming the contaminated portion is for equipment being serviced, under (g)(1)(i)(H).

preguntas.subtema: Activity review · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which administrative safeguard makes a practice review, on a regular basis, records of system activity such as the audit logs and the reports on access and on security incidents?
opciones: Information system activity review, part of the security management process
Audit controls, the technical standard that makes the system record the activity
Evaluation, the periodic check of whether the policies still meet the standards
Security reminders, the periodic updates sent to every member of the workforce
preguntas.explicacion: Audit controls make the system capable of recording and examining activity; the duty to actually read what it recorded is a different, required specification of the security management process, called information system activity review. A practice can satisfy one and fail the other.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Issues of Concern: Children
preguntas.subtema: Consent for minors · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: When a parent authorizes a procedure for their 9-year-old, what is that authorization called?
opciones: Informed permission, since consent itself belongs to the patient
Implied consent, because the parent brought the child in for care
Proxy consent, given under a durable power of attorney for the child
Waived consent, the category used when a patient cannot sign for themselves
preguntas.explicacion: Children, typically those under 18, cannot give informed consent, so the parent or legal guardian permits the treatment and the process is named informed permission instead. Implied consent is inferred from the patient's own situation, such as an emergency. A waiver is when the patient voluntarily gives the consent process up, and a power of attorney is a document an adult signs about their own care.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: malpractice
preguntas.subtema: Malpractice · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: How is malpractice defined as a legal term?
opciones: Professional negligence: breaching the duty to follow accepted professional standards
Any error a professional makes while a patient is under that professional's care
An intentional act by a professional that the client did not agree to beforehand
A breach of the written contract between a professional and the paying client
preguntas.explicacion: Malpractice is professional negligence, the tort that arises where a professional breaks the duty owed to a client, and that duty is generally to keep to the professional standards that are generally accepted. Every other element of a negligence tort still has to be shown too: the duty, the breach, both kinds of causation and the damages. Doctors and lawyers are the commonest defendants.

preguntas.pregunta: At what speed does the paper run during a standard recording?
opciones: 25 mm per second, so one large square is 0.2 seconds
50 mm per second, so one large square is 0.2 seconds
25 mm per second, so one large square is 0.4 seconds
10 mm per second, so one large square is 0.5 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: The paper moves at 25 mm per second, with time on the horizontal axis and voltage on the vertical one. At that speed one second is divided into five large squares, so each large square stands for 0.2 seconds. Any other speed changes what every square on the grid is worth.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether every one of her follow-ups can now be booked by video. How does the workflow guidance answer that?
opciones: It can bridge between office visits, but some care needs one
It replaces office visits once the patient is set up on it
It is limited to the first visit for any new problem
It is used only when the patient cannot travel to the office
preguntas.explicacion: Virtual care is put forward as a bridge that sits between visits to the office: part of the care still calls for the patient to be in the room, and it is the mixture of the two that supports care management. Nothing in the guidance limits virtual visits to new problems or to patients who cannot travel.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Flash Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d (2027 I.C.5.b(3)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: Flash (immediate-use) steam sterilization was originally defined with which cycle?
opciones: An unwrapped item at 132 °C for 3 minutes at 27-28 pounds of pressure, gravity displacement
An unwrapped item at 121 °C for 3 minutes at 27-28 pounds of pressure, gravity displacement
A single-wrapped item at 132 °C for 10 minutes at 15-16 pounds of pressure, prevacuum
An unwrapped item at 135 °C for 30 minutes at 27-28 pounds of pressure, prevacuum
preguntas.explicacion: The original definition was an unwrapped object held at 132 °C for three minutes at 27 to 28 pounds of pressure in a gravity displacement machine. The item goes in an open tray or a rigid container designed to let steam in fast. Many facilities now stretch the exposure to four minutes at that temperature so the lethality matches a wrapped load.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 k74 complications · PBT II.I complications · CCMA 3E13 · NCMA 2C.10
preguntas.pregunta: A heel-prick that goes too deep in a neonate can infect which structure?
opciones: The heel bone (calcaneus), causing osteomyelitis
The tibial artery, causing septic arteritis
The plantar fascia, causing chronic fasciitis
The posterior tibial tendon, causing tendinitis
preguntas.explicacion: Osteomyelitis of the heel bone, the calcaneus, is one of the complications of capillary sampling the WHO names. The depth rules exist to avoid it: no heel-prick beyond 2.4 mm, avoid the posterior heel where skin to bone is 2.33 mm in a 3 kg baby, and use the medial or lateral plantar surface where the distance is 3.32 mm. The tibial artery risk is laceration, not infection.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(3) (2027 I.C.5.b(4)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: Which spores are used in the biological indicator for a steam sterilizer, and which for dry heat and ethylene oxide?
opciones: Geobacillus stearothermophilus for steam, and Bacillus atrophaeus for dry heat and ethylene oxide
Bacillus atrophaeus for steam, and Geobacillus stearothermophilus for dry heat and ethylene oxide
Geobacillus stearothermophilus for both, incubated at two different temperatures by method
Bacillus atrophaeus for both, with a longer incubation used for the steam sterilizer strips
preguntas.explicacion: Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores, incubated at 55 to 60 °C, monitor steam, and also gas plasma of hydrogen peroxide and peracetic acid in liquid form; ethylene oxide and dry heat use Bacillus atrophaeus, incubated at 35 to 37 °C. These spores are chosen because they resist the agent more than the bioburden found on the devices themselves.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: assault; and Wex: battery
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(5) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist raises a needle toward a patient who has clearly refused, and the patient recoils. No contact occurs. Which tort fits?
opciones: Assault, since the patient was put in apprehension of imminent contact
Battery, since raising the needle is itself an offensive act toward them
False imprisonment, since the patient was held in the chair by the act
Negligence, since a reasonable phlebotomist would not have done that
preguntas.explicacion: Assault means an intentional act leaving another person in reasonable fear of contact that is imminent and either harmful or offensive. No physical injury has to occur; the actor must have intended the contact and the victim must have been aware it might happen. Battery is the contact itself, so with no contact there is no battery.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3 Step 5 Disinfect the entry site
preguntas.subtema: Skin preparation for cultures · CPT D4 4A k75 · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E k139 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO's venipuncture steps, the routine skin prep is a 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds. Which collection is explicitly excluded from that routine prep?
opciones: A blood culture, which uses a different site preparation
A draw for potassium or uric acid, which uses povidone-iodine
A capillary puncture of the heel in a newborn
A draw from a patient who has an IV line in the other arm
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 of the WHO procedure applies the 70% alcohol swab for 30 seconds, followed by 30 seconds of drying, unless the collector is drawing blood cultures or preparing for a blood collection, which have their own skin preparation. The same step notes that alcohol is preferred over povidone-iodine precisely because iodine contamination can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus and uric acid, so those tests are not an exception.

preguntas.subtema: Order documentation retention · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A physician orders a Part B diagnostic test. How long must documentation of that written order be kept and made available to CMS?
opciones: Seven years from the date of service
Five years from the date of service
Six years from the date of service
Three years from the date of service
preguntas.explicacion: The enrollment regulation puts the duty on both sides. Whoever furnishes the Part A or Part B service that was ordered or certified, referred or prescribed, and the physician or eligible professional who ordered it, must each hold the documentation for seven years from the date of service and give CMS or a Medicare contractor access on request. That documentation includes the NPI of the ordering professional.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Use of Accompanying Adults or Children as Interpreters
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2)(4) / 2027 F.1.d(1)(3) · RMA I.D.1.c · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient who uses sign language comes for a draw without an interpreter. Under the ADA effective-communication rules, what may the clinic NOT do?
opciones: Require the patient to supply her own interpreter, family or friend
Offer video remote interpreting, if the connection meets the standards
Exchange written notes for a short, simple question at the counter
Let a companion interpret when the patient asks and the companion agrees
preguntas.explicacion: The ADA puts the duty of effective communication, interpreters included, on the covered entity, and the entity may not tell a patient to bring somebody along to interpret. VRI is an allowed choice where it works, notes will do for simple exchanges, and a companion may interpret in two situations only: an emergency with an imminent threat, or where the patient asks for it, the adult agrees and it is appropriate.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth: Description
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth modalities · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient describes a non-face-to-face exchange with her doctor that took place through the practice's online portal. What is that called?
opciones: An e-visit, one of the ways of communicating with a provider through telehealth
A virtual check-in, a brief real-time exchange lasting ten minutes or less
Remote patient monitoring, which sends clinical data from a device to the provider
Store-and-forward, where an image is uploaded for a specialist to read later
preguntas.explicacion: Telehealth means medical services taken from a provider elsewhere in the country over audio and video, and in some cases over audio alone. Two of the named routes are e-visits, exchanges that are not face to face and that usually run through the practice's online portal, and virtual check-ins, short live exchanges that usually last ten minutes or less.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A documented condition has no code of its own, and the Alphabetic Index shows the abbreviation NEC. What does that point the coder to?
opciones: The other specified code for that condition in the Tabular List
The unspecified code for that condition, which NOS also stands for
The excluded code above the note, which is never reported alongside
The manifestation code, which is bracketed and sequenced second
preguntas.explicacion: NEC stands for not elsewhere classifiable and, in both the Index and the Tabular List, represents the other specified code: it is used when the record has detail for which no specific code exists. NOS stands for not otherwise specified and is the equivalent of unspecified, which is used when the record does not have enough detail to be more precise.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Body Planes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.f (2027 I.C.6.e) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A radiologist describes a cut made exactly down the middle of the body into equal right and left halves. What is that plane called?
opciones: The midsagittal or median plane
The parasagittal or lateral plane
The frontal or coronal plane
The axial or cross-sectional plane
preguntas.explicacion: Any vertical cut that separates right from left is sagittal. When it runs straight down the midline and leaves equal halves it earns the extra name midsagittal or median; when it leaves unequal sides it is parasagittal. Front from back is the frontal plane, and upper from lower the transverse.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(iii); OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Latex Allergy
preguntas.subtema: Latex allergy and glove alternatives · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist develops hives after wearing the gloves supplied at work. What must the employer provide?
opciones: Glove liners, powderless or hypoallergenic gloves, or a similar alternative, readily accessible
A prescription antihistamine and a return to the same gloves once the hives have settled
A respirator, because latex protein becomes airborne when powdered gloves are removed
A transfer to duties without patient contact until the allergy has been evaluated
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(iii) wants PPE in the right sizes readily accessible, and specifically that a worker allergic to the gloves normally supplied find within reach glove liners, powderless gloves, hypoallergenic gloves or an equivalent alternative. OSHA's latex allergy page warns against assuming those alternatives are latex-free, and among the options it lists gloves that are synthetic, low in protein or free of powder; it also notes that washing the hands once the gloves come off removes powder and latex left on the skin. The glove exception of (d)(3)(ix)(D) belongs to volunteer blood donation centers alone.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k12 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the note means by an upper respiratory infection. Which everyday term matches it?
opciones: The common cold
A stomach bug
A urinary infection
A skin infection
preguntas.explicacion: URI stands for upper respiratory infection, which is another name for the common cold. Translating it out loud is part of the job, because the abbreviations the staff use daily are not the words a patient uses. A urinary tract infection is UTI, one letter away and a completely different problem.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b
preguntas.pregunta: A wound specimen for culture reaches the laboratory in a non-sterile cup that barely covers the bottom. Which two requirements did the collection miss?
opciones: A sterile leak-proof container, and enough material for the full microbiological and serological work
A sterile leak-proof container, and a fixative to hold the organisms until the plates are poured
A tightly lidded transport container, and enough material for the full biochemical work-up
A sterile leak-proof container, and a site chosen away from where the organism is most likely to be
preguntas.explicacion: Specimens for culture belong in sterile, leak-proof containers, and the quantity has to be enough for the whole microbiological and serological examination, not just the first plate. The site is chosen from the clinical picture and from where the causative organism is most likely to be found. A fixative would defeat the purpose, since the organisms have to stay alive.

preguntas.subtema: Stool from a diaper · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) / (2)(e) · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A stool specimen for parasites is needed from a child in diapers. How should the parent collect it?
opciones: Line the diaper with plastic wrap placed so urine and stool stay apart, then move the stool to the container
Scrape the stool directly from the absorbent diaper into the container, avoiding the wet areas
Apply an adhesive collection bag over the perianal area, as is done for infant urine samples
Place plastic wrap loosely over the toilet bowl, held by the seat, as for an older child
preguntas.explicacion: For a child in diapers the diaper is lined with plastic wrap positioned to keep urine and stool from mixing, which gives a better sample; the stool is then transferred to the clean container and returned as directed. Plastic wrap over the toilet bowl is the method for patients who use the toilet, and the adhesive bag is a urine device. The container is labeled with name, date and time.

opciones: On the inner leg, about 4 to 5 cm above the ankle
On the outer leg, about 4 to 5 cm above the ankle
On the inner leg, about 10 to 15 cm above the ankle
On the inner thigh, about 4 to 5 cm above the knee
preguntas.explicacion: The limb electrodes are applied first, starting with the right leg, on the inner surface about 4 to 5 cm above the ankle, with the tab of the electrode pointing up the leg. The left leg is done the same way, and then the two arms.

preguntas.subtema: Covered entities and business associates · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Which of the following is a HIPAA covered entity?
opciones: A health care provider that transmits claims electronically
An outside computer repair company that services the lab's servers
A pharmaceutical sales representative who visits the clinic
An accredited agency that conducts patient satisfaction surveys
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule binds covered entities, which are health plans, health care providers that transmit health information electronically, and clearinghouses, and it binds business associates as regards a covered entity's PHI; a clearinghouse acting as a business associate follows a narrower set of sections. Outside computer repair firms, survey agencies, equipment companies and pharmaceutical representatives are examples of third parties who reach PHI only through business associate arrangements, which require written satisfactory assurances.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, introduction
preguntas.subtema: How the SDS is arranged · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which sections of a safety data sheet are meant to be read first, for quick general information about a chemical?
opciones: Sections 1 through 8, from identification to exposure controls
Sections 9 through 11 and 16, the technical and scientific ones
Sections 12 through 15, the ones OSHA does not enforce at all
Sections 4 and 5 alone, on first aid and on fighting the fire
preguntas.explicacion: The sheet is built in blocks. Sections 1 through 8 carry the general information: identification, the hazards, what is in the product, how it is handled safely, and the emergency control measures such as fire fighting; they are written for someone who needs the answer fast. Sections 9 through 11 and 16 hold the technical and scientific detail, and sections 12 through 15 are there for consistency with the international system, their content left to other agencies.

preguntas.pregunta: What did comparison of dedicated phlebotomy teams with staff who have broader duties show?
opciones: The teams reached lower rates of contamination, even with equal training
The teams reached higher rates of contamination, despite equal training
The two groups performed identically once both had the same training
The teams drew more tubes per hour but hemolyzed more specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratory staff and members of phlebotomy teams reach lower contamination rates than staff whose responsibilities are broader, even where the training received is the same. It is one of the arguments for formal training and supervised practice in this procedure.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Criminal Health Care Fraud Statute
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A group of clinics ran a scheme, knowingly and willfully, to obtain money from a health benefit program. Which law is aimed at exactly that?
opciones: The criminal health care fraud statute, which reaches any such program
The civil False Claims Act, which asks for no specific intent at all
The Anti-Kickback Statute, which reaches payment made for referrals
The exclusion statute, which keeps offenders out of those programs
preguntas.explicacion: The criminal health care fraud statute covers knowingly and willfully carrying out, or trying to carry out, a scheme to defraud a health care benefit program or to obtain its money by false pretenses, and it is punished with fines, imprisonment or both. The other laws named reach false claims, remuneration for referrals and participation itself.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 k77 k79 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E k139 · NCMA 2C.8 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse inoculates a blood culture bottle straight from the syringe used for the draw, then fills the second bottle with 1 mL. Which two points of technique were missed?
opciones: Changing the needle before inoculating the bottle, and inoculating about 10 % of the medium volume (3 mL into 30 mL)
Cleaning the bottle bung with alcohol only after inoculation, and inoculating about 50 % of the medium volume
Warming the bottle to 37 °C before inoculation, and inoculating at most 1 mL so that the medium is not diluted
Drawing the culture after the first antibiotic dose, and inoculating 10 mL into each bottle regardless of medium volume
preguntas.explicacion: For blood cultures the syringe needle is swapped before the bottle is inoculated, so skin flora do not ride in; the rubber bung is wiped with iodine both before the injection and again afterwards; and the volume drawn runs to roughly 10 % of the medium, 3 mL into a 30 mL bottle for instance. Ask the laboratory which media suit the organism suspected, and take the set before antimicrobials start whenever that is possible.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient with hearing loss is being booked for her first video visit. Which planning question does HHS file under meeting patient needs?
opciones: How the practice will support patients with a disability such as hearing or vision loss
How the practice will bill for the extra minutes a supported appointment will take up
How the practice will judge whether the request suits a telehealth appointment at all
How the practice will know that its staff are comfortable using the new technology
preguntas.explicacion: Meeting patient needs takes in how the office will work out what accommodations a patient might need, how and when reminders reach her, how support will be arranged for a patient whose disability is a hearing loss or a loss of vision, and how a caregiver or other helper will be supported through the visit. Judging appropriateness is a scheduling question; comfort with the technology is a staffing one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Height Assessment", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.c · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which instrument gives the most accurate recumbent length in an infant?
opciones: An infantometer, which holds the baby in position while the length is read
A horizontal length scale, the flexible scale laid alongside a small baby
A stadiometer laid on its side, with the head and the feet against it
A nonstretchable tape measure run from the crown of the head to the heel
preguntas.explicacion: Length in a baby who cannot stand is taken lying down, and the instrument matters. The horizontal length scale is a flexible scale for that job; the infantometer does the same with greater accuracy because it holds the infant securely in position. For a child who can stand, the preferred instrument is the stadiometer, upright as it was built to be.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, How Medicare works with other insurance
preguntas.subtema: Coordination of benefits · CMA III.G.3.a (2027 III.G.3.a) · CMAA 5 k75 · CCMA 5B · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: How far does the primary payer go before a claim passes to the secondary payer?
opciones: It pays up to the limits of its own coverage and sends on the rest of the balance
It pays the whole allowed amount and sends on only the patient's own cost sharing
It pays half of the allowed amount and sends on the remaining half of the balance
It pays up to the limits of the secondary plan and sends on the unpaid remainder
preguntas.explicacion: The primary payer covers up to the limit of its own coverage and hands what is left over to the secondary payer. Where the secondary payer does not pick that remainder up, the patient can be left owing it. This ordering of payment is what coordination of benefits means. Where the group health or retiree coverage is the one paying second, it may pay nothing at all until the patient has signed up for Part B.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A colleague asks where to place the stethoscope for a blood pressure reading. Where is the brachial pulse felt?
opciones: Just medial to the biceps tendon
Just lateral to the biceps tendon
Directly over the median cubital vein
Just medial to the pronator teres muscle
preguntas.explicacion: The brachial artery crosses the fossa medial to the biceps tendon, and that is where the pulse is palpated and where the stethoscope goes when blood pressure is measured. Knowing the line matters at the bedside, because the artery lies under the same small triangle used for venipuncture.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Reservoirs and Carriers
preguntas.subtema: Carriers · CPT D1 1K k11 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k94 · CMA I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist skips hand hygiene after a patient with an infection and carries the organism to the next patient without becoming infected herself. In epidemiologic terms she is which of these?
opciones: A passive carrier, contaminated but not infected
An active carrier, infected but without symptoms
A biological vector, in which the pathogen reproduces
A nonliving reservoir, like contaminated water
preguntas.explicacion: A carrier is someone who can pass a pathogen on without showing symptoms. A passive carrier is contaminated and can move the pathogen mechanically to another host without being infected, and the microbiology text uses exactly this example: the health worker who does not wash her hands after seeing an infected patient. An active carrier is infected, symptoms or not, and may transmit during incubation or convalescence. Vectors are animals, usually arthropods, and a reservoir is where a pathogen normally lives.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k9 k63 · D1 1K k31 · PBT II.F VI.G · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What can poor infection control during a draw produce, besides risk to the worker?
opciones: Bacterial infection where the needle went in, and contaminated specimens
Bacterial infection where the needle went in, and a lost tube vacuum
Hemolysis of the specimen, and degradation of the tube additive
A prolonged clotting time, and a falsely low platelet count reported
preguntas.explicacion: Weak infection prevention and control practices can lead to bacterial infection at the site where the needle was inserted and to contamination of the specimens themselves. It is one reason the cleaned site is not touched again and single-use devices are never shared between patients.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System: How We Conduct Case Surveillance
preguntas.subtema: Communicable disease reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.a / 2027 E.5.a · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: Who legally requires a positive result for a notifiable condition to be reported, and to whom?
opciones: State law requires it to the health department; notifying the CDC is voluntary
Federal law requires it to the CDC; notifying the health department is voluntary
State law requires it to the CDC, which then informs the health department
Accreditation standards require it to both, on the same reporting form
preguntas.explicacion: Hospitals, providers and laboratories report positive results or diagnosed cases to the appropriate health department under state disease reporting laws, and that case reporting is mandatory. What the state and local health departments then send on to the CDC is de-identified data about confirmed cases, and that notification is voluntary.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F 2M k43 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Before agreeing, the patient asks when the results will be back. How does that question relate to obtaining consent?
opciones: Answer it; consent follows once all questions, including result timing, are addressed
Decline to answer; discussing results in any form is the physician's role alone
Proceed with the draw and refer the question to the front desk afterwards
Ask the patient to sign first, then answer the question while preparing the tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is obtained after a comprehensive explanation and discussion, once the patient has acknowledged the procedure-related information and all potential inquiries, including the time it will take for results to return, have been fully answered. Signing before answering, or deferring the question to others, reverses that order.

preguntas.fuente: DOL, Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Medical Assistants
preguntas.subtema: Administrative responsibilities · CCMA 1 k2 · CMA II.F.4 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 1 k2 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which duties does the Bureau of Labor Statistics list on the administrative side of a medical assistant's job?
opciones: Answering telephones, scheduling appointments and restocking office supplies
Setting the fee schedule and negotiating the practice's contracts with health plans
Auditing the practice's claims for fraud and reporting findings to the payer
Approving which staff members may open the electronic health record system
preguntas.explicacion: Medical assistants take on both administrative and clinical work, and often specialize in one of the two. On the administrative side the Handbook describes helping patients get to grips with their insurance and obtain coverage: filling out forms, coding the information, ringing the companies about a bill. It also lists keeping medical and office supplies inventoried and restocked, answering the telephone and scheduling appointments.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: Patient instructions · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks the scheduler whether she can take her video visit while she drives to work. What does the patient guidance say?
opciones: She should not, since a telehealth visit is not to be taken while driving or on errands
She may, if she switches to audio only and pulls over whenever an examination is required
She may, provided the car has hands-free equipment and the connection is private
She should not, unless the appointment is a brief exchange of ten minutes or less
preguntas.explicacion: The tips for a successful visit tell the patient to stay on track, which means leaving food and drink alone while the visit lasts, and to stay safe, which means not taking a visit at the wheel or in the middle of errands. She is also told to sign on early so she can message or telephone the office if the video refuses to start, and to be patient when the clinician runs late.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Data Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Processing mail · CCMA 5O · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7D · NCMA 3.6
preguntas.pregunta: Incoming mail includes lab reports for several patients. What does the Privacy Rule require of the way it is handled?
opciones: Reasonable safeguards protecting it against uses the rule does not permit
An accounting entry for each report before it is filed in the record
A business associate agreement with the carrier that delivered the mail
A written authorization from each patient whose report arrived that day
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity has to keep safeguards in place, administrative, technical and physical alike, that protect against uses and disclosures the rule does not permit and that hold incidental ones down. What counts as reasonable shifts with the size of the entity and the nature of its business; the examples given are shredding documents that hold PHI before throwing them out, and keeping records under lock and key or behind a pass code.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.2, Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2N k49 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k127 · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A 3-year-old needs venipuncture and the mother asks whether she should hold him. What does the WHO guidance say?
opciones: Yes, if she wishes; give full instructions on how and where to hold
No; only trained staff may immobilize a child for a blood draw
No; a child must be immobilized with a mechanical restraint device
