opciones: Bacterial conjunctivitis, which gives purulent or mucopurulent discharge
Viral conjunctivitis, which gives purulent or mucopurulent discharge
Allergic conjunctivitis, which gives purulent or mucopurulent discharge
Toxin-induced conjunctivitis, which gives purulent discharge and no redness
preguntas.explicacion: The type of discharge is the most useful clue. Bacterial conjunctivitis produces purulent discharge that reforms after it is removed, or thicker mucopurulent discharge that clings to the lashes. Watery discharge is what the viral and the allergic kinds give, and a swollen node in front of the ear points to the viral one.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which part of the arm is the preferred site for a limb electrode, and why?
opciones: The inside of the lower arm, where the skin is thinner
The outside of the upper arm, where the skin is thinner
The inside of the upper arm, where the muscle is thicker
The back of the forearm, where there is the least hair
preguntas.explicacion: The inner surface of the lower arm is chosen because the skin there is thinner, which gives a better signal. The tab of the electrode points up toward the arm, and the clip connector is attached to the tab once the electrode is pressed down.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, Chapter 2.11: Checklist for Obtaining a Health History
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A1 · NCMA 2A.5
preguntas.pregunta: After finishing an interview at the bedside, which set of checks is made before leaving the room?
opciones: Call light within reach, bed low and locked, side rails secured, table reachable, floor clear
Head of the bed at 45 degrees, side rails down, and the brakes released so it can be moved
Bed raised to a safe working height with the rails lowered and a wheelchair set at 45 degrees
The room lights switched off, the door pulled shut and the privacy curtain drawn round the bed
preguntas.explicacion: Five safety measures close every bedside encounter: the call light in reach, the bed in its lowest position with the brakes on, the side rails secured, the table in reach, and the room scanned so nothing is left to trip over. A raised bed with the rails down and a wheelchair at an angle describes the start of a transfer, not the state a patient is left in.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic's video remote interpreting picture is choppy and grainy. Under the ADA rules, what follows?
opciones: The service falls short of the performance standards set for that method
The service is acceptable, since remote interpreting carries no standards
The patient must accept it, because an on-site interpreter costs far more
The patient must supply a relative to interpret until the link is fixed
preguntas.explicacion: Where video remote interpreting is chosen, a set of performance standards has to be met in full: video and audio in real time and full motion, carried on a dedicated high-speed or wireless connection, with images of quality and no lag, nothing choppy, blurry or grainy; a picture sharp and large enough to show face, arms, hands and fingers; clear audio; and staff trained to set the thing up.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which patients are described as more likely to have a vasovagal faint during a venous procedure?
opciones: Those seated rather than lying, with previous faints or marked anxiety
Those lying rather than seated, with previous faints or marked anxiety
Those seated rather than lying, when more than three tubes are drawn
Those lying rather than seated, when the needle is larger than 21 gauge
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting of this kind is reported more often in people who are sitting up than in those lying down, and in people who have fainted before or who are markedly anxious about blood or needles. Those are exactly the patients who are asked about earlier faints and offered a lying position.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Using a cane — Cane Basics
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.6.b · RMA III.H.3.a.i · CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who had surgery on the right knee is being taught to use a cane. In which hand does it go?
opciones: The left hand, opposite the leg that is weaker or was operated on
The right hand, on the same side as the leg that was operated on
Either hand, as long as the tip lands ahead of the stronger leg
The right hand, changing to the left once the knee bears weight
preguntas.explicacion: The cane is held on the side away from the weak leg. Cane and weak leg then swing forward together and land level with each other, some of the load shifts onto the cane, and the strong leg steps past. Turning is done by pivoting on the strong leg. The tip, or all four prongs, must be flat on the floor before any weight goes onto the cane.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Heat emergencies", Symptoms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.n · 2027 I.B.8.n · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: Which change tells you a patient with heat illness has reached heat stroke?
opciones: A temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) with confusion, and sweating may stop
A temperature above 100 °F (38 °C) with heavy sweating and severe thirst
A temperature below 95 °F (35 °C) with shivering and cool moist skin
A temperature above 102 °F (38.9 °C) with cramps in both of the legs
preguntas.explicacion: Heat stroke is the point where the body can no longer control its temperature and the temperature keeps climbing: fever above 104 °F (40 °C), confusion, irrational behavior, slurred speech, seizures or unconsciousness, and sweating may stop. Death, organ failure, damage to the brain and shock can follow, so the emergency number is called at once.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 15.1 Characteristics of Infectious Disease, Classifications of Disease
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient develops an infection at a surgical site after an operation. Which two labels describe that disease?
opciones: Iatrogenic, caught because of a medical procedure, and nosocomial
Zoonotic, transferred from an animal to a human, and noncommunicable
Congenital, present at or before birth, and degenerative in its course
Idiopathic, of unknown cause, and inherited from parent to offspring
preguntas.explicacion: An iatrogenic disease is one the medical procedure itself brings on: a wound treatment, a catheterization, surgery whose site becomes contaminated. Diseases picked up in a hospital are called nosocomial, and the two labels often describe the same event. A zoonosis, by contrast, passes from an animal to a person.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 5.2 Review, Observations, and Replication
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k147 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.5 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: A strip was cut short and carries only two complete complexes in each lead group. Why does it fail the quality check?
opciones: Four standard complexes have to appear on the tracing
Ten standard complexes have to appear on the tracing
Six standard complexes have to appear on the tracing
Two standard complexes have to appear in every lead
preguntas.explicacion: The acceptance list is short and mechanical: the complexes clearly drawn with the P wave in plain view, the P wave and the QRS upright in lead I, a baseline that does not wander past 5 mm, and four standard complexes on the tracing. A short strip fails on the last one.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Numbers and Amounts
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why one lab result is labeled hyperglycemia and another hypoglycemia. Which pair of prefixes explains the difference?
opciones: Hyper- means above or excessive; hypo- means under or deficient
Hyper- means quick or rapid; hypo- means slow or delayed
Hyper- means large or long; hypo- means small or short
Hyper- means outer or outside; hypo- means within or inner
preguntas.explicacion: These two prefixes sit in the group of numbers and amounts: hyper- is above, beyond or excessive, and hypo- is under or deficient. Attached to the root for sugar and the ending -emia, a blood condition, they name too much and too little glucose in the blood. Fast and slow are tachy- and brady-; large and small are macro- and micro-.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Instructions for Recording Temperatures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: The morning reading shows the sample refrigerator drifted above its acceptable range some time overnight. What is the required sequence?
opciones: Stop testing, ask the person who supervises testing, and document what was done
Move the samples to a second refrigerator and carry on with the day's testing
Repeat the reading in an hour and act only if it is still out of range
Discard every reagent in the unit and record the loss in the maintenance log
preguntas.explicacion: If the temperature strays outside the recommended range for any length of time, testing stops and whoever directs or supervises it is contacted for guidance on what comes next, including whether the affected reagents, kits, controls or samples have to be thrown out and when testing may start again. Every corrective action taken is documented.

preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Disciplinary Actions for Misconduct
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: A candidate is asked by a classmate to describe the questions on the exam he just sat. What is the risk if he does?
opciones: Misconduct, which can void scores, revoke the credential and bar retesting
A written warning, after which the credential continues without change
A delay in scoring, which is lifted once the candidate signs an attestation
A fee for re-registration, which the candidate pays before the next attempt
preguntas.explicacion: Misrepresenting eligibility, giving a false attestation, breaching the rules of conduct for testing, or not following the codes of ethics, all count as misconduct. Anything capable of compromising an exam's security, its validity or its integrity draws discipline, which can run to invalidating scores, revoking the credential and banning the person from that exam or any other one offered.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound", Mechanism
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which Korotkoff phases mark the systolic and the diastolic pressures?
opciones: Phase I marks the systolic and phase V, when all sound goes, marks the diastolic
Phase I marks the systolic and phase IV, the abrupt muffling, marks the diastolic
Phase II marks the systolic and phase V, when all sound goes, marks the diastolic
Phase III marks the systolic and phase IV, the abrupt muffling, marks the diastolic
preguntas.explicacion: Phase I is the clear tapping heard for at least two beats in a row, and that is the systolic pressure. Phase IV is the sudden muffling into a soft blowing sound, and phase V is silence, which is the diastolic. Phases II and III, the swishing and the return of sharper sounds, have no known clinical meaning.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Acknowledgment of the notice · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient takes the notice of privacy practices and politely declines to sign the acknowledgment. What must the front desk do?
opciones: Record what was tried in order to get the acknowledgment, and why it failed
Record the refusal and hold the appointment until a signed acknowledgment is on file
Record the refusal and post a second copy of the notice by certified mail within 60 days
Record the refusal and count the notice as acknowledged once the visit is documented
preguntas.explicacion: A direct treatment provider hands the notice over no later than the date of first service and, emergencies aside, tries in good faith to get a written acknowledgment that it was received. Where no acknowledgment can be had, the file records what was attempted and why it came to nothing. The notice also goes to anybody who asks for it.

preguntas.subtema: Record confidentiality · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Besides limiting who may receive information from a chart, what else must a hospital's confidentiality procedure prevent?
opciones: Unauthorized people gaining access to the records or altering what is in them
Authorized staff consulting a record outside the hours the department is open
Clinicians correcting an entry that they themselves made earlier in the same day
Copies leaving the department without the medical record service's own stamp
preguntas.explicacion: The condition asks for a procedure that keeps the records confidential in two directions: information and copies go only to authorized individuals, and unauthorized individuals must not be able to reach the records or change what they contain. Originals leave the hospital only under federal or state law, a court order or a subpoena.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Termination and the critically ill · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.4.d(2) · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient already served with a termination notice is admitted in a critical condition the week the notice period runs out. What does the practice owe her?
opciones: To hold the termination until she is medically stable again
To end care on the date in the letter and refer the hospital to it
To hold the termination until she signs a fresh consent to treat
To end care on the date in the letter unless she asks for more time
preguntas.explicacion: Staying clear of an abandonment claim means giving notice that is adequate and a fair chance to line up another clinician. Where there is an emergency, or the patient is critically ill, termination has to wait until she is medically stable again. Courts have held that the duty to go on treating someone at a critical stage of illness applies whatever her ability to pay.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: Complications: petechiae · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these findings is an underlying cause of petechiae?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia
Hemoconcentration
Hypoglycemia
Venous fibrosis
preguntas.explicacion: Petechiae have four primary causes: too few platelets, platelets that work badly, coagulation disorders and a loss of vascular integrity. Hemoconcentration is the tourniquet artifact in the phlebotomy chapter, hypoglycemia is a mimic of syncope, and venous fibrosis is a local contraindication to puncture; none is listed as a cause of petechial bleeding.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.4 Postexamination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k150 k152 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: How are the wax pencil marks taken off the chest once the recording is over?
opciones: With gauze and baby oil, after the electrodes are removed
With gauze and alcohol, after the electrodes are removed
With soap and warm water, before the patient gets dressed
They are left in place for the next recording on that patient
preguntas.explicacion: After the tracings are taken from the machine and labeled and the electrodes are peeled off, the cosmetic pencil marks are wiped away with gauze and baby oil, and the patient puts the gown back on. Alcohol has a different job: cleaning the sites beforehand.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anaphylaxis", Treatment / Management: Epinephrine
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k67 k82 · CMA I.B.9 · 2027 I.B.8 · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: By which route and at which site is epinephrine given for anaphylaxis?
opciones: Intramuscularly, into the outer middle part of either thigh
Subcutaneously, into the fatty layer over the back of the arm
Intramuscularly, into the deltoid muscle of the dominant arm
Intravenously, at the concentration used for an intramuscular dose
preguntas.explicacion: Epinephrine goes into muscle, and the thigh is preferred over the deltoid. Intramuscular delivery works faster and gives better outcomes than the subcutaneous or the intravascular route. The intravenous route uses a different, more dilute concentration and carries a much higher risk of cardiovascular complications.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.1, Patient identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 k49 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3E1 k124 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: On a pediatric ward the child's wristband is found clipped to the cot rail rather than on the child. What does the WHO instruct?
opciones: Do not use it; ask the parent or guardian for the child's full name
Use it, because the cot is assigned to that child on the ward admission list
Use the cot number as the second identifier next to the form
Ask the child directly to state the full name and date of birth
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 6 says a wrist or foot band counts only if it is attached to the patient; a band on the bed or cot, and the bed number, are not to be used. Where a parent or legal guardian is present, that person is asked for the child's first and last names, and the laboratory form is then matched to the child: the name on it, the date of birth, the hospital or file number.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Heart Valve Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which heart valve has two cusps, and where is it located?
opciones: The mitral valve, between the left atrium and left ventricle
The tricuspid valve, between the right atrium and right ventricle
The aortic semilunar valve, at the base of the ascending aorta
The pulmonary semilunar valve, at the base of the pulmonary trunk
preguntas.explicacion: The mitral valve, also called bicuspid or left atrioventricular, has two cusps that chordae tendineae tie to a pair of papillary muscles, and it guards the doorway from the left atrium into the left ventricle; in the clinic it is called mitral. The tricuspid carries three flaps, and the pulmonary and aortic semilunar valves have three flaps each and no chordae tendineae.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is preparing the skin. For which collection does the thirty-second alcohol swab instruction not apply?
opciones: A blood culture set
A coagulation panel
A fasting glucose
A cross-match sample
preguntas.explicacion: The alcohol swab for thirty seconds with thirty seconds of drying is written for routine draws, and the exception named is a blood culture, which is prepared differently. Alcohol is preferred over povidone iodine for the routine case, because iodine can raise potassium, phosphorus and urate.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Benefits of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Effect on demand · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Physicians at a practice fear that offering same-day appointments will bring a flood of extra visits. What does the reported experience suggest?
opciones: Demand tends to fall, mostly because patients more often get to see their own clinician
Demand tends to rise sharply, which is why a contingency plan is needed from the first day
Demand stays flat, but the visits shift out of the afternoon and into the morning session
Demand tends to fall, mostly because patients settle more of their problems by telephone
preguntas.explicacion: Against what many physicians anticipate, the demand for appointments goes down, and the reason given is that patients more often manage to see their own clinician. Seeing one's personal physician strengthens continuity of care, which goes with better care and higher satisfaction. Practices also report savings, because fewer no-shows free clinical and staff time.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(5)(i), Sharps injury log; govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430, sec. 3(5)
preguntas.subtema: Sharps injury log · CPT D1 k12 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which three items must the OSHA sharps injury log record for each incident?
opciones: The type and brand of device, the department or work area, and how the incident happened
The injured employee's name, the source patient's status, and the prophylaxis given
The date of the training, the trainer's qualifications, and the attendees' job titles
The route of exposure, the written opinion, and the vaccination dates of the employee
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(5)(i), added by the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, asks the log for three things at minimum: which device was involved, by type and brand; where it happened, meaning the department or the work area; and an explanation of how the incident came about, all of it written so that the injured employee's confidentiality holds. Names, source status and prophylaxis live in the confidential medical record; training details in the training record; and the route of exposure and the written opinion in the post-exposure evaluation file.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 2O k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the median cubital vein the most common choice for a blood draw?
opciones: Its thick walls tolerate the negative pressure of the draw
It is the only vein in the fossa that lacks an accompanying nerve
It is the site of choice when an intravenous line has to be started
It is the most prominent vein without any tourniquet applied
preguntas.explicacion: The median cubital vein is superficial, sits over the bicipital aponeurosis and is the usual choice because its thick walls can withstand the negative pressures used when drawing blood. The dorsum of the hand, not this vein, is described as the preferred site for an IV; and the chapter does not claim the vein is nerve-free or always visible without a tourniquet.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Ready?: Actions for Unexpected QC Results; Figure 1
preguntas.subtema: Control out of range · CPT D1 1F · PBT IV.B.1 / IV.B.3 · CCMA 3D3 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.9.c · RMA III.C.3.d · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: The glucometer's liquid control reads outside the range printed on the bottle. Three patients are waiting. What should the operator do?
opciones: Hold patient results, look for the cause, correct it, repeat the control, then retest the patients
Test the patients now and note on each result that the control was out of range that morning
Repeat the control once; if it is still out, average the two readings and proceed if within range
Switch to a new bottle of control solution and report the patients if the second control passes
preguntas.explicacion: An unexpected control result, internal or external, stops patient reporting until the problem is found and fixed. The checklist: were the instructions followed, are the reagents, kits or controls outdated, were they stored correctly, could caps have been switched and cross-contaminated the vials, and what do the insert's troubleshooting steps say. Only after acceptable repeat QC are patient samples retested and final results reported.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Temperature Log Instructions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3D k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.3.e · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: The morning temperature log for the specimen refrigerator reads 10 °C (50 °F). Why does this reading call for action?
opciones: A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 2 and 8 °C (36 to 46 °F), so 10 °C is above range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 15 and 30 °C (59 to 86 °F), so 10 °C is below range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between −25 and −15 °C (−13 to 5 °F), so 10 °C is far above range
A specimen refrigerator is typically kept between 0 and 4 °C (32 to 39 °F), so 10 °C is above range
preguntas.explicacion: Patient samples are normally refrigerated between 2 and 8 °C (36 to 46 °F); the 15 to 30 °C band is room temperature for testing and storage, and −25 to −15 °C is the usual sample freezer. What fixes the acceptable range for any given unit is the manufacturer's instructions for the reagents, kits, controls and samples inside it, and the temperature is read and logged every day even where an alarm or a data logger is fitted.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Application of PPE; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Proper Donning
preguntas.subtema: Donning sequence · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: In what order does the CDC-recommended sequence put on personal protective equipment?
opciones: Gown, then mask or respirator, then eye protection, then gloves
Gloves, then gown, then mask or respirator, then eye protection
Mask or respirator, then gloves, then gown, then eye protection
Eye protection, then mask or respirator, then gown, then gloves
preguntas.explicacion: The donning order is gown first, covering neck to knees and wrapping the back; then the mask or respirator, with the nose band fitted and a fit check for respirators; then goggles or a face shield; and gloves last, pulled over the cuffs of the gown. Donning takes place outside the patient room. Gloves go on last so that they are the cleanest item when patient contact begins and so that they cover the gown cuffs.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abnormal Respirations", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on a strong opioid is breathing 9 times a minute. Which term and which mechanism fit?
opciones: Bradypnea, which sedatives and opioids cause by depressing the drive to breathe
Bradypnea, which opioids cause by stiffening the chest wall against expansion
Hypoventilation, which in this patient comes from weakness of the breathing muscles
Apnea, which is the term for any rate under 12 breaths per minute in an adult
preguntas.explicacion: Fewer than 12 breaths a minute in an adult is bradypnea, and the usual company it keeps is sedative or opioid use, alcohol intoxication, hypothyroidism and traumatic brain injury. Neuromuscular disease causes hypoventilation through muscle weakness, and apnea means breathing has stopped, not that it has slowed.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth instructions · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: How does the telehealth guidance want the setup steps delivered to a patient who has never used the platform?
opciones: As written step-by-step instructions, or as direct personal support from staff
As a single reminder message sent on the morning the appointment is due to start
As a printed leaflet given to her at the next office visit she attends in person
As a spoken summary during the opening minutes of the video appointment itself
preguntas.explicacion: Skills and comfort vary from patient to patient, and so do their computers, their software versions and their bandwidth, so what needs reviewing is never the same twice. What the guidance asks for is a written set of instructions covering every step of the process from beginning to end, plus a tip: have a coordinator, a nurse, an administrative staff member or a community health worker take the patient through it.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Steam Sterilization: Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d (2027 I.C.5.b(3)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: Which minimum exposure is recognized for wrapped supplies in a gravity displacement steam sterilizer?
opciones: 30 minutes at 121 °C (250 °F)
45 minutes at 132 °C (270 °F)
15 minutes at 132 °C (270 °F)
60 minutes at 121 °C (250 °F)
preguntas.explicacion: Steam works at two temperatures, 121 °C, which is 250 °F, and 132 °C, which is 270 °F, and the recognized minimums for wrapped supplies are 30 minutes at the lower one in a gravity displacement machine and 4 minutes at the higher one in a prevacuum machine. Forty-five minutes at 121 °C is the figure for decontaminating microbiological waste, where trapped air slows the steam.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship", Clinical Significance: Standardized notification
preguntas.subtema: Termination of care · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.d(2)(b) · NCMA 4.9 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: What belongs in a letter terminating care?
opciones: The end date, cover until then, emergency resources and a records release
The end date, the clinical reason, and the name of the replacing clinician
The end date, the balance owed, and the date the account goes to collections
The end date, a copy of the chart, and the patient's signed acknowledgement
preguntas.explicacion: The letter states the date the relationship ends, says the clinician stays available for care and medication refills until then, points toward emergency help such as a local crisis center, and offers to send the records on to a new clinician once the patient authorizes it, with a release form enclosed. Giving a reason is usually optional, and naming specific colleagues is debated.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Shock", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.j · 2027 I.B.8.j · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with heavy bleeding from a leg wound turns pale, cool and clammy and cannot answer questions clearly. How is the patient positioned?
opciones: Flat on the back with the legs raised about 12 inches (30 cm), head not raised
Sitting upright in a chair with the injured leg resting on a low stool
Flat on the back with the head raised about 12 inches (30 cm) on pillows
On the left side with the knees drawn up and the injured leg supported
preguntas.explicacion: The shock position is supine with the legs lifted roughly 12 inches, or 30 centimeters, and the head left down. It is used only when the patient is conscious and has no injury to the head, neck, spine or leg; if raising the legs causes pain or harm, the patient is left flat. The patient is kept warm and tight clothing is loosened.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I 5F · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9.a
preguntas.pregunta: A physician calls asking why no result was issued for a specimen sent that morning. The specimen had been rejected. What does the emergency laboratory do with rejected samples?
opciones: Stores them up to 24 hours at 4 °C and issues an immediate LIS report stating the sample was not processed
Discards them at once as biohazardous waste and telephones the ward within 30 minutes of rejection
Runs the tests anyway and reports the results with a comment noting the reason for rejection
Freezes them at –20 °C for one week in case the physician asks for the analysis to be repeated
preguntas.explicacion: Unsuitable samples are recognized at arrival by visual inspection and serum indices; those rejected are kept for up to 24 hours at 4 °C, and a report goes out immediately through the laboratory information system saying the sample was not processed. That report is how the ordering physician learns that a new specimen is needed; testing a rejected tube or discarding it unrecorded defeats the purpose.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Antigens, Antibodies, and Transfusion Reactions
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.C · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2 EKB 3 · CPT Core k3 k5 (applied D4 4D)
preguntas.pregunta: Blood bank reports may call the surface antigens of red cells by another name. Which term is it?
opciones: Agglutinogens
Agglutinins
Isoantibodies
Immunoglobulins
preguntas.explicacion: With red cells the antigens may be called isoantigens or agglutinogens, and the antibodies isoantibodies or agglutinins, though the plainer words antigen and antibody are more common. Immunoglobulin is another name for antibody. The agglutinogen is the marker on the cell; the agglutinin is the Y-shaped antibody that clumps cells carrying it.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Portal self-scheduling limits · CMAA 4E k56 · CCMA 5U k172 · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient uses the portal at midnight to book a visit for chest pain that started an hour earlier. What is wrong with that use of the portal?
opciones: Portal self-scheduling is offered for non-urgent appointments, which this is not
Portal self-scheduling is offered only to patients seen within the past year
Portal self-scheduling is offered only during the hours the office is open
Portal self-scheduling is offered only for visits with her own primary clinician
preguntas.explicacion: The portal is open at any hour from any internet connection, and beyond reading her own record some portals let a patient send a secure message to the clinician, ask for a refill, look up benefits and coverage, change her contact details, make a payment, download forms and book appointments that are not urgent. That last limit is built into the scheduling feature itself.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Indications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.2
preguntas.pregunta: Why might a tracing be ordered for a patient who already has a pacemaker?
opciones: To check the device is working and pacing as programmed
To decide whether the device should be switched off first
To measure the battery charge left inside the device
To confirm the device is safe before an MRI is done
preguntas.explicacion: One of the listed indications is detecting malfunction of a pacemaker or defibrillator, evaluating how the device is programmed and functioning, checking its reading of arrhythmias and confirming that the pacing is being delivered as it should.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Contact Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Contact Precautions PPE · CPT D1 1I k34 k36 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is sent to draw blood from a patient on Contact Precautions for a multidrug-resistant organism. Which PPE does the CDC call for?
opciones: A gown and gloves, put on when entering the room and discarded before leaving
A surgical mask put on at the door, with gloves only for the venipuncture itself
A fit-tested N95 respirator, with gown and gloves added only if the patient has a draining wound
Gloves alone, since Standard Precautions already cover blood contact during the draw
preguntas.explicacion: For Contact Precautions the CDC recommends a gown and gloves for any interaction that may bring contact with the patient, or with the environment around them, put on as the room is entered and taken off before leaving so the pathogen stays inside. A mask on entry is the Droplet rule, and the fit-tested N95 belongs to Airborne. Standard Precautions still run underneath, so the gloves the phlebotomist would wear anyway are not enough on their own; the gown is added because this pathogen travels by contact with the patient and the surroundings.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(b), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D k112 · NCMA 2C.1 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.9.a
preguntas.pregunta: A physician phones the laboratory to order a test and says the written order will follow. Under CLIA, how long does the laboratory have to obtain the written or electronic authorization?
opciones: 30 days from the oral request
7 days from the oral request
24 hours from the oral request
90 days from the oral request
preguntas.explicacion: Under 42 CFR 493.1241(b) an oral request is acceptable provided the laboratory then solicits authorization in writing or electronically inside 30 days, and keeps either that authorization or a record of its attempts to obtain it. The default is a written or electronic request from an authorized person; the oral route is the exception, and its ceiling is 30 days, not a day, a week or three months.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Clinical Significance and Issues of Concern (damages)
preguntas.subtema: Burden of proof · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: What is the burden of proof in a civil tort case such as a malpractice claim?
opciones: A preponderance of the evidence: more likely than not
Beyond a reasonable doubt, as in criminal cases
Clear and convincing evidence agreed by a unanimous jury
Proof to a certainty, the standard applied to damages
preguntas.explicacion: A tort case is decided on a preponderance of the evidence, meaning more likely than not, better than 50 percent. The criminal yardstick of beyond a reasonable doubt has no place here, and in a number of states the jury need not even be unanimous to hold a tortfeasor responsible. One is liable for a tort rather than guilty of it. Damages are a separate question: they have to be proved to a certainty instead of estimated, and statutes may cap them, but that goes to the amount awarded, not to the burden for establishing liability.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad; and StatPearls, "Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)" (NBK559281)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An imaging report describes hepatomegaly. Which ending carries the meaning of enlargement?
opciones: -megaly, which is added to the root for the organ
-sclerosis, which is added to the root for the organ
-ectasis, which is added to the root for the organ
-trophy, which is added to the root for the organ
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -megaly means enlargement, and hepat- names the liver, so hepatomegaly is an enlarged liver. The near neighbors mean other things: -sclerosis is a hardening, -ectasis an expansion or dilation of a hollow structure, and -trophy is growth in the sense of nourishment, as in atrophy and hypertrophy.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Where is the HIPAA Privacy Rule Applicable; 45 CFR 164.520(b)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Stricter state law · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.a(2) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: State law is stricter than HIPAA about disclosing HIV test results. Which rule governs the disclosure?
opciones: The more stringent rule, in this case the state law
HIPAA, since federal law always preempts state law
Whichever rule the facility's privacy official prefers
Neither; HIV results are excluded from PHI altogether
preguntas.explicacion: Many states have privacy rules stricter than HIPAA, especially for HIV, mental health, genetic and substance-use information, and federal rules on substance use disorder records are stricter as well; where a more stringent rule exists it takes precedence over HIPAA in that jurisdiction, while HIPAA still applies to everything else. The notice of privacy practices must reflect the more stringent law when it limits a use or disclosure. HIV results are ordinary PHI under HIPAA; the extra protection comes from state law, not from an exclusion.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 5: Safety, Near Misses
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 6 k211 · CMA I.B.11.c · 2027 I.B.10.c · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: A dose is drawn up wrong but caught before it reaches the patient. How is that event described?
opciones: A near miss: an error that could have harmed but was intercepted
A sentinel event: an error that reached the patient and caused harm
A reckless act: a deliberate choice to work outside the safe procedure
A latent condition: a flaw in the system that has yet to cause an error
preguntas.explicacion: A near miss is an error with the potential to harm a patient that fails to do so by chance or because someone intercepted it. Near misses are investigated the same way as worse events, because they usually come from poor communication, weak teamwork, memory overload or unstandardized procedures rather than from a careless person.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Complete Blood Count (CBC), What is a complete blood count?; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", Lavender
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A complete blood count is ordered. Which tube is used, and what does the CBC measure?
opciones: A lavender EDTA tube; red cells, white cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and MCV
A light blue citrate tube; the seconds the sample takes to clot and the INR
A gray fluoride tube; plasma glucose and the average glucose of recent months
A gold serum separator tube; electrolytes, kidney waste products and the liver enzymes
preguntas.explicacion: Hematologic assays go in the lavender EDTA tube, and a CBC counts the blood cells: red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, hemoglobin, hematocrit and the mean corpuscular volume. Clotting seconds and the INR belong to the PT/INR in citrate, glucose to the gray tube, and electrolytes, BUN, creatinine and liver enzymes to the metabolic panels run on serum.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", section Clinical Significance, When To Access Capacity
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which behavior is listed as a trigger to look further into a patient's decision-making capacity?
opciones: Blanket acceptance or refusal of the care being offered
Asking several detailed questions about the tests ordered
Requesting that a relative be present during the draw
Preferring one particular arm for the venipuncture
preguntas.explicacion: The triggers listed are these: the patient cannot voice a decision at all; accepts or refuses across the board; asks nothing about the treatment offered; gives reasons for refusing that are excessive or inconsistent; has newly lost the ability to manage daily activities; is agitated or disruptive; has a labile mood; hallucinates; or is clinically intoxicated. Asking questions points the other way.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, symptom and sign
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports nausea and fatigue, and the exam records a fever and a rash. Which entries are symptoms and which are signs?
opciones: Nausea and fatigue are symptoms; fever and rash are signs
Nausea and fatigue are signs; fever and rash are symptoms
All four are symptoms, since the patient came in reporting them
All four are signs, since a provider recorded them in the chart
preguntas.explicacion: A symptom is something the person feels and can only report: pain, nausea, fatigue, anxiety. A sign is something found on the exam or on a test, so anyone can observe it: fever, swelling, a skin rash, a high blood pressure or a high blood glucose. Both matter, but only one of them can be measured.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Shock", Symptoms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.j · 2027 I.B.8.j · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of findings fits a patient who is going into shock?
opciones: Rapid weak pulse, shallow breathing, pale clammy skin and confusion
Slow bounding pulse, deep slow breathing, flushed dry skin and euphoria
Rapid strong pulse, deep rapid breathing, warm dry skin and hunger
Slow weak pulse, noisy breathing, blue lips and a raised temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Shock is circulatory failure, so blood pressure falls very low and the picture is a fast but weak pulse, shallow breathing, skin that is pale, cool and clammy, low or absent urine output, and anxiety, restlessness or confusion. Bluish lips and nails may appear. One in five people who go into shock die of it, so help is called at the first signs.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Treatment Refusal; 42 CFR 482.13(b)(2)
preguntas.subtema: Refusing treatment · CPT D1 1D k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k211 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.2 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with capacity refuses a treatment that the whole team believes would help him. What is the legal position?
opciones: He may refuse, whatever others judge the benefit to be
He may refuse once a second clinician has confirmed it
He may refuse only treatments that are not life-sustaining
He may refuse only after signing a form releasing the team
preguntas.explicacion: Capacity brings with it the right to turn down any treatment on offer, however strongly other people judge that giving it would be an act of beneficence, and a Supreme Court decision stretched that right to measures that decide whether the patient lives or dies. The root of it is autonomy, and it travels with informed consent: capacity is the condition for both, and judging capacity is part of the consent conversation itself.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Platform changes · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: The telehealth platform will be upgraded next month. What does the guidance tell the practice to do about the patients already using it?
opciones: Tell them about the change and what they have to do to be ready for their visit
Wait until one of them reports a problem and walk her through the new version then
Book no video visits at all until every one of them confirms the update is installed
Send the instructions only to the patients whose first video visit is still to come
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance closes on what to do when the platform changes: where the telehealth platform gets updated, the practice tells its existing patients about the change and about anything they must do so as to be ready for the visit. Patients new to the platform are the ones who get the full step-by-step walkthrough, but the existing ones cannot simply be left to find out for themselves.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Exceptions to Informed Consent
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7 · CMAA 3D k40
preguntas.pregunta: Which situation is a recognized exception to the requirement for informed consent?
opciones: A life-threatening emergency with no time to obtain consent
A test the clinician considers clearly in the patient's interest
A patient who speaks a different language from the staff
A patient carrying a psychiatric diagnosis such as schizophrenia
preguntas.explicacion: The recognized exceptions are three: the patient is incapacitated, a life-threatening emergency leaves no time, or the patient voluntarily waives consent. A clinician's view that the test is good for the patient is the paternalism the consent literature warns against; language barriers call for an interpreter; and a psychiatric diagnosis by itself does not remove the right to consent.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.d · NCMA 2B.5
preguntas.pregunta: A reading of 120/80 mm Hg is written in the chart. What else belongs beside it?
opciones: The arm used and the position the patient was in during the measurement
The size of the cuff and the make of the sphygmomanometer that was used
The rate at which the cuff was deflated and the peak pressure it reached
The time since the patient last ate, since food shifts the reading upward
preguntas.explicacion: The pair of numbers alone cannot be compared with the next visit's. Both arms are measured at the first evaluation because the sides can differ, and any position other than the standard one alters the value, so the arm and the position are recorded with the reading. Later comparisons then rest on the same conditions.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, What is therapeutic drug monitoring?; and StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Two patients on the same dose of the same drug show different levels. Which factors are named for that?
opciones: Aging, pregnancy, illness and infection change how a drug is processed
The color of the tube stopper and the order in which the tubes filled
The arm chosen for the draw and how long the tourniquet stayed on
The time of day alone, since every drug level follows a diurnal rhythm
preguntas.explicacion: As soon as a medicine is taken the body begins to process and remove it, so the level in the blood varies over time, and aging, pregnancy, illness and infection all affect how quickly that happens. Levels also differ between individuals on the same dose because of how the drug is absorbed, spread through the body, metabolised and got rid of, and because of diet and the other drugs taken alongside.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Pulse Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b(1) · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A pulse is described as irregularly irregular, with no pattern at all to the spacing. Which rhythm does that describe?
opciones: Atrial fibrillation, whose beats fall without any repeating pattern
Sinus arrhythmia, whose rate changes in step with the breathing cycle
Sinus bradycardia, whose beats are widely spaced but evenly spread
Sinus tachycardia, whose beats are closely spaced but evenly spread
preguntas.explicacion: Rhythm is sorted into three descriptions: regular, regularly irregular, and irregularly irregular. The middle one covers patterns that repeat, such as the mild variation with breathing known as sinus arrhythmia. The last one, with no pattern whatever, is the hallmark of atrial fibrillation and is reported.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Referral
preguntas.subtema: Referrals · CCMA 5P k177 · CMA III.G.5.a · RMA II.B.2.c · CMAA 4G k67 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in an HMO calls to book with a cardiologist and has no order from her primary care doctor. What is missing?
opciones: A referral, the written order from her primary care doctor for the visit
A preauthorization, the plan's decision that the visit is medically necessary
A claim, the request for payment the office sends after the appointment
An accounting of disclosures covering the records the specialist will receive
preguntas.explicacion: A referral is a written order from the primary care doctor sending the patient to a specialist or for certain services. Many health maintenance organizations require that order before care from anyone but the primary care doctor, and without it the plan may refuse to pay. Preauthorization is a different decision, made by the insurer about medical necessity.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Competence in the Care of LGBTQ Patients", sections Patient Versus Provider Use of Slang Terms, and How to Create a Practice That Welcomes Members of the LGBTQ Community
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k18 · CCMA 6 k194 · CMA F.2.b / 2027 F.1.c · RMA I.D.1.e · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: The requisition says 'Robert', but the patient introduces herself as Roberta and uses she/her. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Use the name and pronouns she gives, and note them in the record for next time
Use the legal name on the requisition until the record has been formally amended
Ask the partner who accompanies her which pronouns you should use
Avoid using any name or pronoun for the rest of the visit, to be safe
preguntas.explicacion: Staff are told to call a patient by the name she gives and the pronouns she has chosen, to follow the patient's lead and ask where there is doubt, and to leave a note in the record so that later visits go the same way, editing the electronic record if that is what it takes. Identifying the specimen is a separate step and uses the identifiers on file.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244)
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · CMA III.G.2 · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: What separates fraud from abuse in the Medicare program?
opciones: Fraud involves knowing deception; abuse causes needless program cost without it
Fraud is committed by providers only; abuse is committed by patients and staff
Fraud is billed to a federal program; abuse is billed to a commercial insurer
Fraud is punished by the payer; abuse is punished only by the state licensing board
preguntas.explicacion: Fraud typically means knowingly submitting false claims, misrepresenting facts, or paying or taking remuneration for referrals. Abuse is the label for practices that cause unnecessary program costs, directly or indirectly, or that fall short of professionally recognized standards. Which of the two applies depends on the facts, the intent and the knowledge involved, and either can bring administrative, civil and criminal liability.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Additives and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A smear shows platelets sticking to the white cells rather than to each other. What is that finding called?
opciones: Platelet satellitism
Platelet clumping
Rouleaux formation
Pseudo-polycythaemia
preguntas.explicacion: Platelets adhering to polymorphonuclear cells is known as platelet satellitism, and careful microscopic review of the smear is what picks it up. Clumping of platelets with one another in EDTA is the neighbouring artefact, and rouleaux are stacks of red cells, not platelets.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.508(c)(1)-(4), Core elements and requirements
preguntas.subtema: Authorization elements · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a valid HIPAA authorization contain?
opciones: An expiration date or event, plus the individual's signature and date
A notarized seal and the signature of the treating physician
The patient's Social Security number and insurance identifier
A statement that the authorization cannot be revoked once it has been signed
preguntas.explicacion: The core elements in 164.508(c)(1) are a specific description of the information, the person or class authorized to disclose it, the recipient, the purpose, an expiration date or event, and the individual's signature and date, with the authority of any personal representative described. The required statements then tell the individual of the right to revoke in writing, whether treatment or benefits may be conditioned on signing, and that the recipient may redisclose the information. It must be in plain language and the individual receives a copy. Notarization is not required, and a no-revocation clause would contradict the rule.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: Why are the cable wires pulled as straight as possible when they are attached?
opciones: Loops in them can cause alternating-current interference
Loops in them can shorten the life of the patient cable
Loops in them can slow the paper as it feeds through
Loops in them can reverse the polarity of that lead
preguntas.explicacion: Each wire is picked out of the cable distribution block, plugged into its connector, and then laid out straight. A loop in a lead wire is one of the recognized invitations to interference from the room current, an artifact that can bury the small waves the provider needs to see.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(e)(2)(iii)(A) and (B), Containment equipment
preguntas.subtema: Biosafety cabinet certification · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: How often must a certified biological safety cabinet be recertified in a laboratory working with concentrated HIV or HBV?
opciones: When it is installed, whenever it is moved, and at least once a year
Every three years, the period for which training records are kept
Once at installation, and again only after a spill occurs inside it
Every six months, and after each change of the exhaust air filter
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (e)(2)(iii) requires certified biological safety cabinets, or equivalent containment such as special clothing, sealed rotors, safety cups for the centrifuge or respirators, for any activity that could throw droplets, splashes, spills or aerosols of infectious material. Subparagraph (B) sets the certification schedule: at installation, at every move, and at least once a year. That annual cycle is shared with the biosafety manual review in (e)(2)(ii)(M); three years is the retention period for training records.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Key points for single-dose vials
preguntas.subtema: Single-dose vials · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A single-dose vial of lidocaine contains far more than one patient needs. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: Do not keep the remainder for later or another patient; buy the smallest vial that meets the need
Label it with the date and use it for up to 28 days, as with a multi-dose vial
Pool the leftover contents with other single-dose vials in a clean preparation area
Save the remainder for the same patient's next visit, since it is dedicated to one person
preguntas.explicacion: A single-dose vial is approved for one patient for one case, procedure or injection, typically lacks a preservative, and must never be used for more than one patient. If it holds more than needed, the remainder is not retained for future use even on the same patient, leftover contents are not pooled or stored, and the practical advice is to purchase the smallest vial necessary. The 28-day dating rule applies to opened multi-dose vials, which contain a preservative.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.C Competency Assessment · NCMA 4.12 comply with CLIA
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory replaces its glucose analyzer with a different instrument. Under CLIA, what has to happen before the staff report patient results on it?
opciones: Each individual's performance is reevaluated so the evaluation covers the new instrument
Each individual repeats the six competency procedures within six months of the changeover
The laboratory enrolls in a second approved proficiency testing program for that analyte
The technical consultant attests in writing that the earlier evaluations still apply here
preguntas.explicacion: The annual cycle comes with an interrupt: where the methodology or the instrumentation changes, that person's performance has to be evaluated again over the new method or instrument, and before any patient result is reported. Nobody signs the old evaluation forward, and there is no grace period.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Respiratory Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: What is the normal resting respiratory rate for an adult?
opciones: 12 to 20 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
20 to 30 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
8 to 12 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
30 to 60 breaths per minute, counted with the depth and the pattern
preguntas.explicacion: The adult range is 12 to 20 breaths per minute, and the assessment records rate, depth and pattern rather than the number alone. The 30 to 60 band belongs to infants. Respiration is the vital sign most often left out of the chart, and it is also the one that changes earliest when a patient is deteriorating.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Abdominal Regions and Quadrants
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.f (2027 I.C.6.e) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: How many regions does the detailed regional scheme of the abdomen produce, and how many does the quadrant scheme produce?
opciones: Nine regions and four quadrants
Four regions and nine quadrants
Six regions and three quadrants
Twelve regions and six quadrants
preguntas.explicacion: Providers divide the abdominal cavity either into nine regions or into four quadrants, so that a complaint can be placed precisely. The regional scheme is the more detailed one and comes from two horizontal and two vertical lines; the quadrant scheme is simpler and is the one used more often in medicine.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 4: Perform hand hygiene and put on gloves
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene and gloves · CPT D3 3A · PBT II.F · CCMA 3C4 k100 k101 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Before a routine venipuncture, what does the WHO's Step 4 require for hand hygiene and gloves?
opciones: Soap and water, or 3 ml of alcohol rub if hands are not visibly soiled, then well-fitting non-sterile gloves
Use 3 ml of alcohol rub in every case, even on visibly soiled hands, then put on sterile gloves
Wash with soap and water, dry with a reusable towel, then put on sterile gloves for every patient
Put on well-fitting non-sterile gloves first, then clean the gloved hands with alcohol rub
preguntas.explicacion: Step 4 gives two options: wash the hands with soap and water and dry them with single-use towels, or, if they are not visibly contaminated, rub 3 ml of alcohol rub over palms, fingertips and backs of the hands until dry; only then are well-fitting non-sterile gloves put on. Sterile gloves are reserved for blood cultures. Gloves are never a substitute for hand hygiene.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Fill level and ratios · CPT D3 k59 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with polycythemia has a hematocrit of 60%. What should be considered when collecting a citrate specimen from this patient?
opciones: The high hematocrit raises the citrate effect, so the anticoagulant volume may need adjusting
The high hematocrit lowers the citrate effect, so the tube should be filled only halfway
The tube is collected as usual, since hematocrit affects the EDTA tube and not the citrate tube
A larger 16 to 18 G needle is used so the viscous blood reaches the 9:1 ratio faster
preguntas.explicacion: Inadequate filling or a hematocrit above 55% increases the citrate level in the sample and interferes with the recalcification performed during analysis, and with a high hematocrit the anticoagulant volume may need to be adjusted. Half filling would make the citrate excess worse. The 16 to 18 gauge belongs to blood donation in the WHO needle table, not to coagulation draws, for which 19 to 22 G is suggested.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Cleaning
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k105 · CMA I.C.5.d(1) (2027 I.C.5.b(1)) · RMA III.D.2.n · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: Which order of steps does the guideline require before an instrument can be high-level disinfected or sterilized?
opciones: Clean it thoroughly first, because leftover organic and inorganic matter blocks the process
Soak it in the germicide first, so the softened soil rinses off with less friction afterward
Disinfect at a low level first, so the item is safe for the person who will scrub it later
Rinse it in sterile water first, so tap-water organisms cannot dry onto the working surfaces
preguntas.explicacion: Cleaning always comes first. Material left on the surface interferes with the process in two ways: it reacts chemically with the germicide, using it up, and it shields microbes as a physical barrier. Meticulous cleaning also lowers the bioburden, which shortens the exposure needed. Sterile-water rinsing is what follows high-level disinfection, not what precedes it.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A processor inspects centrifuged serum tubes and sets aside the ones that look pink. Why do current recommendations favor an automated hemolysis index over this visual check?
opciones: Visual detection is inaccurate: serum looks hemolysed only above about 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, whereas the index is reproducible
Visual detection is accurate for serum but not for plasma, so the index is needed only for anticoagulated tubes
Visual detection is reliable above 0.5 g/L, but only the index can detect hemolysis before centrifugation
Visual detection cannot distinguish hemolysis from lipemia, whereas the index reports both as a single value
preguntas.explicacion: Sample quality used to be judged by looking at the tube before and after spinning, but visual detection is inaccurate: after separation, free hemoglobin becomes visible only around 0.2 to 0.3 g/L, while the cut-off for clinically significant interference is 0.5 g/L. Chemistry analyzers measure the serum indices, hemolysis included, with high reproducibility, which is why systematic automated measurement is strongly recommended.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample looks pink after centrifugation. Which result on the chemistry panel should the processor expect the laboratory to question first?
opciones: Potassium
Magnesium
Chloride
Glucose
preguntas.explicacion: Among frequent chemistry tests, the analytes most sensitive to hemolysis are lactate dehydrogenase, creatine kinase and its MB isoenzyme, potassium, conjugated bilirubin, ALT, AST and iron; potassium is the one whose distortion most often changes patient management, which is why one hospital measures the hemolysis index on every potassium sample. Albumin, glucose and other analytes showed biases that stayed within CLIA limits in the study on graded hemolysis, as did magnesium and chloride.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(2)(i), Training Records
preguntas.subtema: Content of training records · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which information must a bloodborne pathogens training record include?
opciones: Dates, a summary of the content, the trainer's name and qualifications, and attendees' names and titles
Dates, the trainer's name, and each attendee's hepatitis B vaccination status and serology
Dates, the content, and the type and brand of any device that caused an injury during the year
Dates, the attendees' names, and a copy of each attendee's signed declination or consent
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(2)(i) lists four items for the training record: the dates of the sessions, the contents or a summary, the names and qualifications of whoever conducted the training, and the names and job titles of everyone who attended. Vaccination status and serology belong to the confidential medical record of (h)(1); the type and brand of a device belong to the sharps injury log of (h)(5); and the signed declination of Appendix A is a separate document required by (f)(2)(iv).

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Glucose screening tests during pregnancy (007562), How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: One-step gestational testing · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k139 fasting · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is booked for one-step gestational testing. What should she be told to expect?
opciones: An 8- to 14-hour fast, a 75 g drink, and about 2 hours in the office
An 8- to 14-hour fast, a 100 g drink, and about 3 hours in the office
No fast at all, a 50 g drink, and about 1 hour in the office
A 3-day carbohydrate diet, a 75 g drink, and about 2 hours in the office
preguntas.explicacion: One-step testing means nothing to eat or drink except sips of water for 8 to 14 hours, a liquid holding 75 g of glucose, and draws before the drink and every 60 minutes for two hours, so at least two hours should be allowed. The 100 g / 3-hour version is the second step of the other pathway, and the 50 g nonfasting drink is its first step. Nothing may be eaten during the test.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Semen analysis (003627), How to Prepare for the Test; and StatPearls, "Semen Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Semen abstinence · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A man scheduled for a semen analysis asks how long he should abstain from ejaculation beforehand. What is the usual instruction?
opciones: From 2 to 3 days, and in no case longer than 5 days before the test
From 2 to 3 hours, and in no case longer than 5 hours before the test
At least 7 days, and preferably 10 days or more before the test
No abstinence at all, since recent activity does not change the count
preguntas.explicacion: To get an adequate sperm count the patient avoids any sexual activity that ends in ejaculation for 2 to 3 days, and the interval should not stretch past 5 days because quality falls off after that. The StatPearls account of the same test sets the window differently, at a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 7 days, so the figure a candidate quotes depends on which reference the laboratory follows.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Biological Hazards, Requirements under 29 CFR 1910.1030 (Universal Precautions); OSHA, Bloodborne Pathogens: Hazard Recognition
preguntas.subtema: Universal vs Standard Precautions · CPT D1 k11 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C1 k99 k100 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: According to OSHA, may a facility apply Standard Precautions instead of Universal Precautions?
opciones: Yes, as an alternative, if the facility follows all other provisions of the standard
No; Universal Precautions is the only approach the standard's definitions recognize
Yes, but only in hospitals holding accreditation from a CMS-approved body
Yes, and doing so exempts the facility from the exposure determination requirement
preguntas.explicacion: The eTool explains that Standard Precautions, like Body Substance Isolation before them, treat every body fluid and body substance as infectious, and that OSHA accepts them as alternatives to Universal Precautions so long as the facility keeps to every other provision of the bloodborne pathogens standard. OSHA's hazard page dates Standard Precautions to 1996 and describes them as broadening Universal Precautions with extra infection prevention elements. The exposure determination of (c)(2) still has to be done, and accreditation is a CLIA matter, not a condition here.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Seating and Wheelchair Evaluation", Technique or Treatment: Seating Systems
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a.ii · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who spends most of the day in a wheelchair asks why a cushion is needed. What is the reason?
opciones: Sitting straight on the seat surface concentrates pressure over the bony pelvis
The cushion raises the seat so the arms can reach the hand rims more easily
The cushion holds the pelvis tilted backward, which keeps the trunk upright
Sitting on the seat surface makes the chair tip forward during a transfer
preguntas.explicacion: Nobody should sit directly on a sling or solid seat. Long hours of sitting, often without protective sensation, load the ischial tuberosities and sacrum until the tissue breaks down. The cushion spreads that pressure, and pressure-relief moves such as leaning forward, leaning to the side or pushing up on the arms are taught alongside it.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), What's Medicare Fraud?
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic sends Medicare claims for appointments its patients never kept. How does CMS class that practice?
opciones: As fraud, since it claims payment for care never given
As abuse, since it adds cost the program need not bear
As waste, since the appointment slot could not be reused
As an error, since the schedule was not kept up to date
preguntas.explicacion: Claiming from Medicare for an appointment the patient never kept sits on the CMS list of fraud examples, alongside billing for services never provided and upcoding. Abuse covers practices that push unnecessary cost onto the program without that knowing deception, which is why the two are told apart by intent and knowledge rather than by the amount.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Ending the relationship · CCMA 5 k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · CMAA 4F k60 · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician wants to drop a patient he finds difficult and demanding. What do the ethical guidelines say?
opciones: Being a challenging patient is not on its own a ground for ending the relationship
Any patient may be dismissed at will, since the relationship rests on mutual consent
Dismissal is allowed once the patient has been rude to a member of the office staff
Only the health plan may end the relationship, by removing the patient from the panel
preguntas.explicacion: The clinician-patient relationship usually begins by mutual consent and is governed by State law. Ethical guidance holds that a clinician may not terminate it merely because someone is a challenging patient, and that irresponsible health behaviors do not release the professional from the duties of the relationship. The expected route is to try to resolve the conflict and, failing that, seek help from a consultant.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Disorders of Platelets; and 18.5 Hemostasis, Disorders of Clotting
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 3C bleeding disorders) · PBT I.C · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's platelet count is far below normal. What is the term for this, and what is the main risk?
opciones: Thrombocytopenia; excessive bleeding even from minor wounds
Thrombocytosis; the formation of unwanted clots or thrombosis
Leukopenia; an inability to ward off infection and disease
Thrombophilia; an inherited or acquired tendency to form thrombi
preguntas.explicacion: An insufficient number of platelets is thrombocytopenia; blood may then fail to clot properly, so excessive bleeding can follow even minor wounds. The opposite, too many platelets, is thrombocytosis and carries a risk of unwanted clots. Leukopenia is too few white cells, and thrombophilia (hypercoagulation) is a tendency to thrombosis that can be genetic or acquired.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(vi)
preguntas.subtema: Removing the gown · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What is the correct way to take off a gown after caring for a patient?
opciones: Release the ties, touch only the inside, and turn it inside out
Release the ties, roll it from the sleeves toward the neckline
Pull it over the head without untying, keeping the front outward
Fold it front to front and hang it for the rest of the shift
preguntas.explicacion: The gown is third in the doffing sequence. Ties or straps are released first; then it comes off touched only on the inside, eased away from neck and shoulders and turned inside out so the contaminated face finishes up enclosed, and it goes straight into the proper container. The bloodborne pathogens standard adds the companion rule: a garment that blood has soaked through comes off immediately, in a way that avoids contact with the outer surface, and a gown is never hung up for a second use.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(ii)(A), Housekeeping
preguntas.subtema: Decontamination of surfaces and spills · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C k97 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b / 2027 I.B.4.b I.B.6.b · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A work surface in the draw room is splashed with blood during a procedure. What does OSHA require?
opciones: Decontaminate it with an appropriate disinfectant immediately or as soon as feasible
Decontaminate it at the end of the work shift, the time the standard sets for possibly contaminated surfaces
Remove and replace the protective covering at the end of the shift, as with plastic wrap over equipment
