Flush it with water immediately, as the standard requires for skin and mucous membranes
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(A) names three moments for decontaminating a work surface with a suitable disinfectant: when a procedure is finished; right away, or as soon as feasible, when the surface is visibly contaminated or blood or OPIM has been spilled on it; and at the end of the shift if it may have been contaminated since the last cleaning. A visible spill falls under the second case and does not wait for the shift to end. Protective coverings, in (d)(4)(ii)(B), are likewise replaced as soon as feasible once overtly contaminated. Flushing with water is the rule for eyes and mucous membranes in (d)(2)(vi), not for surfaces.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule, Notification by a Business Associate
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics · CMAA 3E k44 · NCMA 4.3 disclosure laws
preguntas.pregunta: A billing company discovers that it exposed patient data belonging to one of the clinics it serves. Whom must it notify, and how quickly?
opciones: The clinic, with no unreasonable delay and 60 days after discovering it at the latest
The affected patients, with no unreasonable delay and 60 days after discovery at the latest
The Secretary of HHS, with no unreasonable delay and 60 days after discovery at the latest
The clinic, within 60 days of the end of the calendar year in which it was discovered
preguntas.explicacion: A breach at or by a business associate travels upward: the business associate tells the covered entity, with no unreasonable delay and at the latest 60 days after discovery, and should identify the individuals affected and hand over whatever the covered entity needs for its own notices. Ultimate responsibility for notifying individuals stays with the covered entity, though it may delegate the task.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: Two separate conditions treated at one visit both fall under the very same diagnosis code. How many times is that code reported?
opciones: Once, since a unique code is reported only once for an encounter
Twice, once for each of the two conditions the provider documented
Twice, because the units reported have to match the work done
Once, and only where the two conditions are on the same side
preguntas.explicacion: A unique diagnosis code goes on an encounter a single time. The rule covers bilateral conditions where no distinct codes identify laterality, and it covers two different conditions that are classified to the same code. Units of service belong to procedure reporting, not to the diagnosis list.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(2)(i) and (f)(2)(ii), Hepatitis B Vaccination
preguntas.subtema: No prescreening as a condition · CPT D1 1H k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.b III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic wants to check each new hire's antibody level first and offer the hepatitis B vaccine only to those who are not immune. What does the standard say?
opciones: Screening may not be made a condition of receiving the vaccine that is offered
Screening is required before the first dose, and has to be repeated a year later
Screening replaces the vaccine when the employee signs the declination form
Screening is allowed only within ten working days of the initial assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Two sentences have to be read together. Paragraph (f)(2)(i) has the vaccine offered after training and within ten working days of initial assignment, unless the employee has already completed the series, unless antibody testing has shown the person to be immune, or unless the vaccine is medically contraindicated. Paragraph (f)(2)(ii) then bars the employer from making a worker join a prescreening program as the price of getting vaccinated. So a result that already exists can remove the need for the offer, while nobody may be told to be screened first in order to qualify.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wound Closure Techniques", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.a · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: A contaminated wound with no major tissue loss is irrigated, debrided and watched for several days before it is closed. Which type of healing is that?
opciones: Tertiary intention, also called delayed primary closure
Secondary intention, in which granulation fills the defect
Primary intention, in which the edges are approximated at once
Maturation, the last of the four phases that every wound goes through
preguntas.explicacion: Tertiary intention, or delayed primary closure, is the route for a grossly contaminated wound that has not lost much tissue: it gets explored and irrigated, debrided, then watched for roughly three to seven days before it is closed or grafted. Primary intention is closure at once with sutures, staples or glue; secondary intention leaves the wound open to granulate and contract.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, Home Care
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has fainted in the chair and been eased to the floor. How high should the feet be raised?
opciones: About 12 inches (30 cm) above the level of the heart
About 4 inches (10 cm) above the level of the heart
About 3 feet (90 cm), by resting the legs on the chair seat
Level with the heart, with the head turned to the side
preguntas.explicacion: The immediate steps after a faint are: check airway and breathing, loosen anything tight at the neck, raise the feet above heart level by about 12 inches or 30 centimeters, turn the person on the side if they have vomited, and keep them lying down for at least 10 to 15 minutes. The side position is for vomiting; it does not replace elevating the legs.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient recovers from a faint during a draw. Which finding afterwards is a red flag pointing away from a simple vasovagal episode?
opciones: A bitten tongue, which suggests a seizure
Pallor and sweating during the event itself
A slow pulse and low blood pressure during the event
Generalized weakness for a few minutes after waking
preguntas.explicacion: The patient is usually slow of pulse, hypotensive, pale and sweating during the event and should have an entirely normal examination afterwards; findings such as tongue biting, which points to a seizure, or pallor that carries on, which points to symptomatic anemia, call for a fuller evaluation. The syncope chapter notes that generalized weakness on regaining consciousness is typical.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Table 18.1 Clotting Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3) · PBT I.C · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which clotting factors require vitamin K for their production?
opciones: II, VII, IX and X
I, V, XI and XIII
III, IV, VIII and XII
VIII, IX, XI and XII
preguntas.explicacion: Four factors need vitamin K for their synthesis: prothrombin (II), proconvertin (VII), antihemolytic factor B (IX) and the Stuart-Prower factor (X), all made in the liver. The intrinsic-pathway set VIII, IX, XI and XII is a different grouping, and fibrinogen, proaccelerin, factor XI and the fibrin-stabilizing factor are not vitamin K dependent.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A physician orders blood cultures, a CBC and a fasting glucose on the same venipuncture. Which sequence follows the WHO table?
opciones: Blood culture bottle, purple EDTA tube, light gray fluoride tube
Purple EDTA tube, blood culture bottle, light gray fluoride tube
Light gray fluoride tube first, blood culture bottle, purple EDTA tube
Blood culture bottle, light gray fluoride tube, purple EDTA tube
preguntas.explicacion: In Table 2.3 the blood culture bottle is drawn first (position 1), EDTA sits at position 8 and the oxalate/fluoride glucose tube closes the list at position 10. Any sequence that places the gray tube before EDTA, or the culture bottle anywhere but first, breaks the table. The footnote also reminds the reader that local color codes can differ, so the laboratory's own chart is checked.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 1.1.3 and 1.2
preguntas.subtema: Scope of practice · CPT D3 k54 · D1 1D k26 · PBT II.K · CCMA 3E7 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which two activities does the word phlebotomy cover in this guidance?
opciones: Sampling for laboratory tests, and collecting blood for donation
Sampling for laboratory tests, and inserting intravenous cannulae
Collecting blood for donation, and transfusing blood to a patient
Sampling for laboratory tests, and collecting non-blood specimens
preguntas.explicacion: For the purposes of the guidance the term covers two things: blood sampling for laboratory tests and blood collection for donation. Cannulation, transfusion and non-blood specimens sit outside that definition, as do central line, arterial line, cord blood and stem cell collections.

preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a blood cortisol test asks how many visits it will take that day. What is the answer?
opciones: Two visits on the same day, at different hours
One appointment, with two tubes drawn back to back
Three appointments, spread across the same morning
One appointment, followed by a 24-hour urine jar
preguntas.explicacion: A blood cortisol test needs the patient back twice on the same day, at different hours. Samples are usually taken once in the morning, when the level normally peaks, and again around 4 p.m., by which time it is normally much lower. The 24-hour urine collection is a different form of the test, not an add-on to the blood one.

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wants to keep her worklist on a personal flash drive and check it over the clinic's open wireless network. What is the guidance?
opciones: Avoid storing it on portable media, and use only encrypted networks
Store it on the drive but keep the drive locked in the staff room
Use the open network, since the worklist holds no test results
Store it on the drive after deleting the names, keeping the numbers
preguntas.explicacion: Portable media are a documented source of breaches: laptops and flash drives get stolen, so workers are told not to keep patient data on them, and to encrypt it if it must be kept, or better, to view the data without storing it. Where several computers reach records over a wireless network, the network's encryption has to be switched on, and staff must stop using an unencrypted one because of the risk of interception.

preguntas.pregunta: How is a diploma or certificate verified during credentialing?
opciones: By checking with the primary source that issued the document
By reviewing the original document the applicant brings in person
By having the applicant sign a sworn statement of authenticity
By confirming it with the applicant's two professional references
preguntas.explicacion: A national body sets credentialing standards, and one of its key features is that any certificate, diploma or degree gets verified with the primary source: handing over an original is no longer enough. Cases of workers holding posts on certificates that were bogus and experience that was falsified are exactly what the process exists to catch.

preguntas.pregunta: Minutes after the gloves touched her arm a patient has trouble breathing and cold, clammy skin. What does this suggest?
opciones: A severe allergic reaction, an emergency needing treatment at once
Irritant contact dermatitis, treated by washing and a steroid cream
Latex-fruit syndrome, which shows as an itchy mouth after eating
A delayed type IV reaction, the one behind allergic dermatitis
preguntas.explicacion: A severe reaction usually shows in more than one part of the body: confusion, dizziness or fainting, trouble breathing or swallowing, vomiting, cramps or diarrhea, skin gone pale or red, and shock with shallow breathing and cold, clammy skin. A severe allergic reaction is an emergency and is treated at once.

preguntas.pregunta: An 8-year-old with fever and exudative tonsils has a negative rapid strep test. What does current guidance recommend?
opciones: Send a throat swab for culture, because a negative rapid test in a child or adolescent is backed up by culture
Accept the negative result as final, because the rapid antigen test is highly specific for group A streptococcus
Repeat the rapid test at once with a second swab, and treat only if the second cassette also turns positive
Order a throat culture only if the rapid test had been positive, to identify which streptococcal group is present
preguntas.explicacion: A rapid strep test detects group A streptococcal antigen in 10 to 20 minutes, but a throat culture, which takes 24 to 48 hours, sometimes finds infections the rapid test misses. Culture after a negative rapid test is therefore important in children and teens, who can develop rheumatic fever from untreated strep. High specificity means a positive is trustworthy; it says nothing about the negatives the antigen test misses.

preguntas.explicacion: Identification starts by matching the patient to the laboratory request form, and once the samples are taken, a way of identifying and tracking them is essential so that the specimen is matched correctly to the result and to the patient. For donors the match is to the screening results.

preguntas.subtema: Notice of privacy practices · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient is registering at the front desk. When must the notice of privacy practices be given to her?
opciones: By the date of the first service at the latest, with a good faith effort at written acknowledgment
Within thirty days of the first visit, matching the deadline for responding to an access request
At the second visit, once the office knows the patient intends to keep using the practice
Only if the patient asks for it, since the notice is posted in the reception area anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Where the treatment relationship is a direct one, the provider hands the notice over by the date of the first service at the latest and tries, in good faith, to obtain written acknowledgment of receipt. Where no acknowledgment can be got, the provider documents what was tried and why it did not work. The notice also has to be posted prominently at the site and kept available for people to take away.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Technique or Treatment: Handwashing Technique
preguntas.subtema: Handwashing technique · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: While washing hands at a sink for routine hand hygiene, which technique detail is correct?
opciones: Keep the hands below the elbows and turn off the faucet with a towel
Keep the hands above the elbows, as in the surgical scrub, and rinse toward the fingertips
Turn off the faucet with clean hands so the towel stays dry for drying
Dry the hands on a shared cloth towel and apply lotion before gloving
preguntas.explicacion: Routine handwashing is done with the hands kept below the elbows so water runs from less to more contaminated areas, 3 to 5 mL of soap, at least 15 to 20 seconds of friction over palms, backs, wrists, finger webs, fingertips, thumbs and nails using WHO's six-step pattern, a thorough rinse, drying with a clean or disposable towel, and using a towel to turn off the water so the clean hands are not recontaminated. Hands above the elbows is the surgical scrub position, where the hands are the cleanest area.

preguntas.pregunta: A stock bottle of disinfectant is decanted into a smaller labeled bottle kept at the draw station for the week. What must that bottle show?
opciones: The product identifier and words or symbols giving the general hazards
The full sixteen-section data sheet printed and taped to the bottle
The date it was filled and the initials of the employee who filled it

preguntas.explicacion: A container of a hazardous chemical kept in the workplace has to be labeled, tagged or marked either with everything a shipped container carries, or, more simply, with the product identifier plus words, pictures or symbols that give at least general information about the hazards, working together with the rest of the hazard communication program. The data sheet stays in its binder or on the computer; the biohazard label belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard and marks a different hazard.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)", Recognition and Initial Management of Cardiac Arrest
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1L k38
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant finds an adult unresponsive, not breathing, and with no pulse. In what order are the steps of CPR performed?
opciones: Chest compressions first, then the airway, then rescue breathing
The airway first, then rescue breathing, then chest compressions
Rescue breathing first, then the airway, then chest compressions
The airway and two breaths, then a pulse check, then compressions
preguntas.explicacion: Circulation is handled first: compressions are started before the airway is opened and before any breath is delivered. The older airway-first order was set aside in 2010 after research showed that beginning compressions early gave better results than managing the airway first. A lone rescuer compresses and leaves ventilation for a second responder.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Equipment: Manual Auscultation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Sounds are heard, fade to silence, and then come back as the cuff keeps deflating. What has happened?
opciones: An auscultatory gap: listening continues, and the diastolic is the final silence
A false start: the cuff was underinflated, and the first sounds heard were artifact
A normal phase II, in which the swishing quality always drops below hearing
A leaking valve: the pressure fell too quickly and the sounds were skipped over
preguntas.explicacion: In some patients, particularly those with a wide pulse pressure, the sounds vanish between phase II and phase III and then return. Stopping at that silence underestimates the systolic value or records the diastolic too early. Auscultation carries on, and the diastolic is taken at the last disappearance of sound.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Body Cavities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.d (2027 I.C.6.c) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks which organs lie in the pelvic portion of the ventral cavity. Which answer is right?
opciones: Most of the urogenital system, together with the rectum
Most of the gastrointestinal tract, with the kidneys
The heart and the lungs, with the large blood vessels
The brain in the upper part and the spinal cord below
preguntas.explicacion: The ventral cavity is divided by the diaphragm into the thoracic cavity above, which holds the heart, lungs, trachea, esophagus, large vessels and nerves, and the abdominopelvic cavity below. That lower one splits again: the abdominal portion holds most of the gastrointestinal tract with the kidneys and adrenal glands, the pelvic portion most of the urogenital system and the rectum.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Injection Safety: Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices, Key points for multi-dose vials
preguntas.subtema: Multi-dose vials in patient areas · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C7 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A multi-dose vial is carried into a patient's room for an injection. What does the CDC say about that vial afterwards?
opciones: Dedicate it to that single patient; it may not go back into use for others
Return it to the clean medication room and keep using it for up to 28 days
Discard it immediately, since any vial entering a patient area is contaminated
Wipe the septum with alcohol and continue using it for other patients
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC would rather each multi-dose vial served a single patient. Where one has to cover several, it is kept and drawn from in a clean space set aside for preparing medication, apart from where patients are actually being treated. Taking it into a treatment space instead ends the shared use: an operating or procedure room, an anesthesia or procedure cart, a patient room or bay all count, and from that point the vial belongs to that one patient. Nothing requires binning it on the spot, but it may not go back to anyone else, and the 28-day clock that started at the first puncture keeps running.

preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A blood donor asks how long the red cells she just gave would have lived. What is the lifespan of an erythrocyte, and what removes it?
opciones: About 120 days; macrophages in spleen, liver and marrow remove them
About 10 days, after which macrophages phagocytize them in the spleen
About 4 to 6 weeks, the time the body needs to replace donated cells
A few hours to a few days, like most of the granular leukocytes
preguntas.explicacion: A red cell lasts as long as 120 days in the bloodstream, and the worn-out cells are then taken up by macrophages that sit mostly in the marrow, the liver and the spleen. Ten days is far too short: nothing here puts a red cell's life in days. Four to six weeks is what the body needs to rebuild the cells given in a donation, and hours to days covers most of the white cells.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient's coverage comes through her husband's employer. What kind of plan is that?
opciones: A group health plan, offered by an employer to employees and their families
A group health plan, offered by an insurer directly to individual subscribers
An individual plan bought through the Marketplace with a premium tax credit
A supplemental policy that pays what the primary policy leaves unpaid each year
preguntas.explicacion: A group health plan is coverage an employer or an employee organization offers to its workers and their families, which is exactly the husband's arrangement. Coverage sold straight to one person is an individual policy, and the premium tax credit is tied to buying through the Marketplace. A policy that pays after another one is supplemental coverage, a different product entirely.

It is held just off the frontal bone, never touching the skin at all
It is pressed on the forehead and held still until the display stops changing
It is drawn from the lateral hairline down the neck over the carotid pulse point
preguntas.explicacion: This device is moved slowly from mid-forehead across to the hairline at the side, reading infrared radiation from the skin above the superficial temporal artery and reporting the highest of the many values it samples. The instrument that is held away from the skin without contact is the infrared forehead thermometer.

preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D4 4G hematocrit) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's hematocrit result comes back as 42. What does that number mean?
opciones: That 42% of the blood volume is made up of red blood cells
That 42% of the blood volume is plasma, the liquid portion
That the red blood cell count is 4.2 million per microliter
That 42% of the formed elements are white cells and platelets
preguntas.explicacion: A hematocrit is reported as the percentage of the blood that consists of red cells; the rest of the sample is white cells, platelets and plasma. The usual figure is about 45 percent, with women at 37 to 47 (mean 41) and men at 42 to 52 (mean 47). White cells and platelets together form under 1 percent of a sample, so they are not counted in the hematocrit, and 4.2 million per microliter would be a cell count, not a percentage.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Where open access works · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A fee-for-service practice is told that open access only suits capitated managed care. Is that right?
opciones: No: it is reported to work in fee-for-service settings as well as in managed care
Yes: the model rests on capitation, since a same-day slot is not separately billable
Yes: the model was designed inside managed care and has not been tried outside it
No, but it holds up only where the practice also carries a large managed care panel
preguntas.explicacion: Experts in designing and implementing the model report that it works in fee-for-service settings as much as in managed care. Its logic has nothing to do with how a visit gets paid for: it brings queuing theory and industrial engineering to bear on matching the demand for visits against the supply of clinician time, on the supposition that the trouble is not a shortage of capacity but an imbalance between the two.

preguntas.subtema: Post-vaccination testing · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: When should anti-HBs be tested to document a healthcare worker's response to the hepatitis B vaccine series?
opciones: 1 to 2 months after the final dose
6 months after the final dose
Within 10 working days of the final dose
Every year, at the annual training
preguntas.explicacion: Postvaccination serologic testing for anti-HBs is done 1 to 2 months after the third dose, so that the worker's response status is on record for any future exposure; a level of 10 mIU/mL or more after a documented series is the correlate of protection. For workers who also received HBIG, testing may have to wait until the HBIG antibody has cleared, about 6 months after it was given. Ten working days is the OSHA deadline for offering the vaccine, and annual testing is not recommended for immunocompetent responders.

preguntas.pregunta: After a capillary draw on a 5-year-old, what follow-up care is suggested for the child beyond the requisition?
opciones: A gesture that leaves the child on a positive note, such as praise, a handshake or a fun sticker
A dose of oral sucrose, 0.012 to 0.12 g, which the WHO recommends as analgesia at any age
An explanation of every result the laboratory will report, so the child feels informed
A brief period lying flat, since children faint more often than adults after skin punctures
preguntas.explicacion: Follow-up has two parts, completing the requisition and giving comfort and reassurance; a small gesture is enough to end on a good note, praise out loud, a handshake, a fun sticker, a pat on the back. Asking her to bring printed forms to the nearest office on the morning of the appointment
Asking her to complete the forms with the clinician during the first minutes of the visit

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pregnancy Test, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; What do the results mean?; MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: HCG in urine (003619)
preguntas.subtema: False-negative urine hCG · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.5 · CCMA 3D2 / 3D9 · CMA I.C.10.d.(4) · RMA III.C.4.b.iv · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose period is two days late drank several glasses of water before giving a random urine sample, and the office pregnancy test is negative. How should this result be handled?
opciones: It may be a false negative from dilute urine or early testing; a repeat on first morning urine in about a week is advised
It is reliable, because office cassettes detect hCG from 10 days after conception regardless of urine concentration
It should be repeated immediately with a second cassette from the same kit, since a single negative can never be reported
It confirms that the patient is not pregnant, because urine tests are 97 to 99 % accurate at any point after a missed period
preguntas.explicacion: Drinking large amounts of fluid before collecting the sample can dilute the hCG so that it does not show on the test, and testing too soon after conception may precede detectable hormone levels; both produce false negatives. First morning urine is the most concentrated. Because hCG rises daily in early pregnancy, a negative test is repeated about a week later, and a still-suspected pregnancy is referred to the provider. The 97 to 99 % accuracy figure applies to tests done a week or two after a missed period.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", Considerations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1L k38
preguntas.pregunta: What does an automated external defibrillator do once its pads are on the chest?
opciones: It reads the heart rhythm and shocks only when the rhythm calls for a shock
It delivers a shock as soon as the pads are attached to an unresponsive patient
It paces the heart at 100 to 120 beats a minute while compressions go on
It confirms the pulse and holds compressions until a pulse can be felt
preguntas.explicacion: The device analyzes the rhythm on its own and delivers a shock if, and only if, a shock is what that rhythm needs; the rescuer follows its spoken instructions exactly. When a shock is advised, compressions pause and everyone stands clear; the moment the shock is delivered, or if none is advised, CPR resumes without delay.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k147 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: A conventional 12-lead ECG is being set up. How many wires are attached to the patient?
opciones: Ten: four on the limbs and six across the chest
Twelve: four on the limbs and eight across the chest
Six: two on the limbs and four across the chest
Fourteen: six on the limbs and eight across the chest
preguntas.explicacion: Twelve leads are produced from ten wires. Four limb electrodes generate the six limb leads, and each of the six chest positions has its own wire. The limb leads look at the heart in the vertical plane and the chest leads record it in the horizontal plane, which is why both groups are needed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Specimen Collection (Fecal Samples)
preguntas.subtema: Representative stool portions · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.B.2 / V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: When a stool specimen is collected for the laboratory, which portions should be included?
opciones: Any visible pus, mucus or blood, plus material from the first, middle and last parts of the stool
Only the formed central portion, and never any mucus or blood, which would contaminate the culture badly
The last part of the stool only, since it has been in contact with the rectal mucosa longest
About 1 mL mixed with 9 mL of saline, the preparation used for every stool culture
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen is passed into a clean, dry container with a tight lid and moved on into a labeled transport container. It should deliberately take in anything abnormal the eye can see, blood, mucus or pus, and stand for the first, middle and last parts of the stool. Mixing about 1 mL with 9 mL of buffered saline and freezing the supernatant is the preparation for a suspected viral infection, not a general rule.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.g · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: What is done to the work surface itself before any sterile supply is placed on it?
opciones: It is disinfected and then allowed to dry completely
It is disinfected and covered while still visibly wet
It is wiped with sterile water and dried with a towel
It is covered with a second drape without being wiped
preguntas.explicacion: The surface is disinfected and left to dry all the way through before anything sterile goes down on it. A surface still wet with disinfectant lets moisture wick through the drape, and moisture wicked from an unsterile area contaminates the field within an inch of where it appears. Only sterile supplies are allowed onto the field once it is established.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 12: Use Health Education Material Effectively
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k160 education methods · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant hands a patient a pamphlet about her new diagnosis and moves on. Why is that not enough?
opciones: Material works only inside a teaching plan: review it and check understanding
Material works only if it is written at or below the fourth grade level
Material works only when it is mailed home instead of handed over in person
Material works only when the patient signs that she received the pamphlet
preguntas.explicacion: Handing over a pamphlet or pointing at a website does not by itself produce understanding or a change in behavior. When the information matters, someone in the practice goes through it with the patient and the caregiver, circling or highlighting key points, personalizing it, and confirming with teach-back.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Facilitated virtual visit · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: In a facilitated virtual visit, what is the role of the medical assistant at the patient's site?
opciones: Collecting objective data with equipment and transmitting it to the remote clinician
Interpreting the findings and deciding whether the patient needs an in-person visit
Recording the encounter so the clinician can review the video after the appointment
Waiting outside the room, since a facilitated visit requires the patient to be alone
preguntas.explicacion: This is a synchronous model: the patient travels to a nearby site stocked with diagnostic equipment, usually a clinic, while the clinician joins from somewhere else. On site a telehealth facilitator, described as a medical assistant or a nurse, works the tools (digital stethoscope, thermometer, pulse oximeter), gathers the objective findings and sends them across for the clinician to evaluate.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: What shapes the workflow · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.1 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Two practices adopting telehealth find their workflows end up looking very different. Which factors does the guidance say the changes depend on?
opciones: The vendor chosen, the size and setting of the practice, the patient population and the services given
The vendor chosen, the age of the record system, the state licensing board and the payer mix
The size and setting of the practice, the services given, and the number of exam rooms it keeps
The patient population, the services given, and whether the practice owns its own building
preguntas.explicacion: Telehealth reshapes several processes at once: check-in, triage, consent, scheduling, billing, documentation and the structure of the appointment. How far each one shifts depends on which telehealth vendor was chosen, on the size and the setting of the practice, on its patient population and on the services it provides. The record system is expected to merge easily into whatever workflow comes out.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Timeliness
preguntas.subtema: Right of access · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient submits a written request for a copy of her chart on March 3. By when must the office act on it?
opciones: No later than 30 calendar days from receipt of the request, and sooner where possible
No later than 60 calendar days from receipt, the same period allowed for an amendment
No later than 10 working days, the period set for verifying the requester's identity
No later than 6 years from receipt, matching the accounting of disclosures period
preguntas.explicacion: Access has to be provided within 30 calendar days of receiving the request. OCR treats that as an outer limit and encourages faster responses, noting that a portal or personal health record can make access almost immediate, and that patients reasonably expect speed from an office that uses health information technology every day.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Expert Witness", Introduction: Medical Errors Compared to Medical Negligence
preguntas.subtema: Negligence · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(1) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's condition worsens after appropriate treatment and the family talks about suing. Does the outcome alone show negligence?
opciones: No: an undesirable result can happen even when the care was appropriate
No: a result only counts once the state licensing board has reviewed it
Yes: a worsening condition after treatment is what negligence means
Yes: any deviation from the expected recovery is a compensable injury
preguntas.explicacion: A medical intervention can leave the patient better, worse or unchanged, and all three are possible with entirely appropriate care. Negligence cannot be read off an unexpected result, a failure to cure or a failure to recover. Even an error that fell below the standard may have caused no damages, in which case there is probably nothing to claim.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part A (Hospital Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who never worked long enough to earn premium-free Part A asks what buying it will cost her in 2026.
opciones: Either $311 or $565 a month, depending on how long she or her spouse paid the taxes
A flat $202.90 a month, which is what every enrollee pays for Part A in 2026
A flat $283 a year, payable once the first hospital benefit period has opened
A flat $1,736 a year, the same figure as the inpatient hospital deductible
preguntas.explicacion: Part A costs most people nothing, because Medicare taxes were paid long enough by them or by a spouse, generally ten years' worth. Someone who does not qualify may be able to buy it: in 2026 the amount is either $311 or $565 a month, depending on how long those taxes were paid. Part B has to be taken as well in order to buy Part A.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Sections 1, 7, 8 and 11
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 8 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: Which Safety Data Sheet section tells the reader which gloves and eye protection to use with a chemical and lists its exposure limits?
opciones: Section 8, on exposure controls and personal protection
Section 7, Handling and Storage, with incompatibilities
Section 11, Toxicological Information, with routes of exposure
Section 1, Identification, with the emergency phone number
preguntas.explicacion: Section 8 brings together the OSHA permissible exposure limits and ACGIH threshold limit values, the engineering controls such as local exhaust ventilation, and the personal protective measures, down to the glove material, for example nitrile or PVC, and its breakthrough time. Section 7 gives safe handling and storage conditions and incompatible chemicals; Section 11 describes toxic effects, symptoms and carcinogen listings; Section 1 identifies the product and supplier and gives the emergency telephone number.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Preparing for telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth scheduling decisions · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5B k170 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Before a practice starts booking video visits it is told to settle several scheduling questions. Which one belongs on that list?
opciones: How the office will decide that a particular request suits a telehealth appointment
How the clinician will write the visit up in the record once the video call ends
How the practice will train its current health care team to use the new platform
How the practice will support a caregiver who is helping the patient during the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Under scheduling, the questions are when telehealth appointments will be offered, whether patients will book online or by telephone, how the office will judge whether a telehealth appointment is appropriate, and how and when reminders go out. Training the team is a staffing question, supporting a caregiver falls under meeting patient needs, and documentation comes afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction (Yellow, Pink, and Blue)
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 3N k57 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A blood culture bottle has just been filled. Which anticoagulant does it hold, and how is it mixed?
opciones: Sodium polyanethole sulfonate; the bottle is mixed eight to ten times
Sodium citrate at 3.2 percent; the bottle is inverted three to six times
Sodium fluoride with oxalate; the bottle is inverted three to six times
Lithium heparin with a gel; the bottle is mixed eight to ten times over
preguntas.explicacion: Culture bottles hold sodium polyanethole sulfonate, which works as an anticoagulant and blocks activation of complement, and the bottle is mixed eight to ten times once filled. Three to six inversions is the figure for the citrate tube, and fluoride with oxalate belongs to the glucose tube.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 k147 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: How is the paper of a standard 12-lead recording laid out?
opciones: Six lines of graph, with the leads printed in four groups of three
Three lines of graph, with the leads printed in four groups of three
Six lines of graph, with the leads printed in three groups of four
Twelve lines of graph, with one lead printed on each of them
preguntas.explicacion: The tracing paper is set out in six channels. The twelve leads are written in four groups of three, so the first three channels carry lead I with aVR, V1 and V4, then lead II with aVL, V2 and V5, then lead III with aVF, V3 and V6.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, chapter 3, section 3.3.2.4
preguntas.subtema: Signature requirements · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A provider wants to sign chart notes with a rubber stamp because handwriting is slow. What does CMS say?
opciones: A stamp is not usually acceptable, apart from a disability accommodation
Stamped signatures are acceptable whenever the provider keeps the stamp locked away
Stamped signatures are acceptable if a signature log lists the stamp and its owner
Stamped signatures are acceptable on orders but never on progress notes or reports
preguntas.explicacion: A handwritten signature is a mark made by a person to signify knowledge, approval, acceptance or an obligation. CMS says a stamp is not usually acceptable, and lets one be used only under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, by an author with a physical disability who can show a contractor that the disability prevents signing. A signature log is a different device altogether, for tying initials or an illegible signature to a name.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The record describes the same condition as both acute and chronic, and the Index has separate subentries at the same level. What does the coder do?
opciones: Code both of them, and sequence the acute or subacute code first
Code both of them, and sequence the chronic code first of the two
Code the chronic one alone, since it is the longer-standing problem
Code the acute one alone, since it is what brought her in this time
preguntas.explicacion: Where the same condition is written up as acute or subacute and also as chronic, and the Alphabetic Index carries separate subentries indented to the same level, both codes go on and the acute or subacute one is sequenced first. Signs and symptoms that routinely accompany a disease process are not coded in addition unless the classification says so.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.2; and Section 2.2.3, Step 7
preguntas.subtema: Syringe transfer · CPT D3 3M k54 k59 · D1 1G k30 · PBT II.F VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A tube is being filled by injecting through its rubber stopper. Which precaution applies?
opciones: The tube stands in a sturdy rack and is not held in the other hand
The tube is held in the other hand so the angle can be corrected
The tube is laid flat on the tray so the blood runs down its wall
The tube is held by an assistant while the worker steadies it
preguntas.explicacion: Laboratory sample tubes are placed in a sturdy rack before the needle goes through the stopper, and the paired prohibition is not to inject into a tube while holding it in the other hand. Where a rack is not available, one hand fills the tube or a needle shield protects the other.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare; and What Part B covers
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks which part pays for the doctor visit and the walker ordered today.
opciones: Part B, which covers provider services, outpatient care and durable equipment
Part A, which covers provider services, outpatient care and durable equipment
Part D, which covers provider services and the equipment ordered during them
Medigap, which covers provider services once Part A benefits are exhausted
preguntas.explicacion: Part B is the medical insurance half: services from doctors and other providers, outpatient care, home health, durable medical equipment such as walkers and wheelchairs, and many preventive services. Part A is hospital insurance, Part D pays for prescription drugs, and Medigap is private supplemental insurance that helps with the patient's share of costs in Original Medicare rather than covering new categories.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k152 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why are the chest marks drawn again right after the sites are scrubbed?
opciones: The rubbing takes the marks off and the spots are lost
The alcohol makes the wax pencil marks hard to read
The marks have to be moved a space down after cleaning
The marks are copied onto the log sheet for the record
preguntas.explicacion: Each chest site is briskly rubbed with alcohol and gauze, and the cosmetic pencil marks come off with the oil and dead skin. The recommended habit is to keep an eye on the spot while cleaning it and re-mark it immediately, so the landmark work does not have to be repeated.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: slander; Wex: libel
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(2)-(3) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A staff member repeats a false and damaging claim about a patient out loud in the break room. Which tort is that, and what does it require?
opciones: Slander, and unlike libel the damages have to be proven by the person suing
Slander, and like libel the damages are presumed from the fact of publication
Libel, and the damages have to be proven by the person bringing the lawsuit
Libel, and the damages are presumed once the statement has been repeated
preguntas.explicacion: Defamation is a statement that harms someone's reputation, and it splits in two: libel is generally written or otherwise recorded, slander is generally spoken. With slander, damages are not presumed and the party suing has to prove them. Traditional libel rules go the other way and take the injury as given once the statement was published.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's skin is oily at the electrode sites. How is each site prepared?
opciones: Rub it with alcohol and gauze about ten times
Rub it with alcohol and gauze about three times
Wipe it with dry gauze and then let it air dry
Part the hair and press the electrode down firmly
preguntas.explicacion: Each site is scrubbed vigorously with alcohol and gauze roughly ten times to take off oil, sweat and scaly skin. Applying an electrode to a surface that was not cleaned that way is one of the causes of a drifting baseline. Parting the hair is a separate trick, and it helps the electrode stick.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Ethics", Clinical Significance; and StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity"
preguntas.subtema: Unbiased care · CCMA 7G · CMA E.7 / 2027 E.6 · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient refuses the plan the clinician is convinced is best. What does respect for autonomy require?
opciones: The clinician stops, having explained the reasoning and listened first
The clinician proceeds, since beneficence outranks the patient's refusal
The clinician presses until the patient accepts, then documents consent
The clinician transfers the patient, since the relationship has broken down
preguntas.explicacion: Where the patient does not accept that the clinician's plan is the best available, the clinician stops, and that is respect for autonomy. Restricting a patient's freedom against her will on the argument that she will be better off is paternalism, and pushing someone toward the course the clinician prefers serves neither autonomy nor beneficence.

preguntas.subtema: Research consent · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: What may a research consent form never contain?
opciones: Wording that releases the investigator from liability for negligence
Wording about whom to contact if the subject is injured by the research
Wording that the study may end without the subject's own agreement
Wording that identifiers may be stripped for later, unrelated studies
preguntas.explicacion: Exculpatory language is barred: no consent may make the subject waive, or seem to waive, legal rights, or release the investigator, sponsor or institution from liability for negligence. The other three belong in a form. A contact for research injury is a basic element, and early termination by the investigator and future use of de-identified material are additional elements.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Overview
preguntas.subtema: Which title applies · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Under which part of the disability law is a privately owned medical office covered?
opciones: Title III, which reaches businesses and non-profits that serve the public
Title I, which reaches employers with fifteen or more people on the payroll
Title II, which reaches the services and programs of state and local government
Title IV, which reaches the companies that provide telephone and relay services
preguntas.explicacion: A private hospital or medical office is a place of public accommodation, and doctors' offices and hospitals are named among the businesses that serve the public. A clinic run by a state or a city falls under Title II instead, and Title I is the employment side, which applies to the same office as an employer.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k135 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A citrate tube was drawn to only 67 % of its nominal volume. According to the fill-level study cited in the rejection paper, which coagulation result remains relatively reliable at that fill?
opciones: Prothrombin time
Activated PTT
Fibrinogen level
Factor VIII level
preguntas.explicacion: Lippi and colleagues found a clinically significant bias once tubes fall below 89 % of total fill for aPTT, below 78 % for fibrinogen and below 67 % for factor VIII, whereas prothrombin time and activated protein C resistance stayed relatively reliable even at 67 % of nominal volume. The laboratory still sets its acceptance line at 80 %, so the practical answer is a redraw, but PT is the test least disturbed by the short fill.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: What to expect on connecting · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has been told to connect early asks what she will see while she waits. What does the guidance say to describe for her?
opciones: A virtual waiting room, or hold music, until the clinician joins the appointment
A message telling her to ring the front desk so that she can be let in
A form she has to finish on screen before the video will start at all
A recorded message that reads out the practice's policy on canceling appointments
preguntas.explicacion: Appointment setup guidance tells the office to describe what the patient will meet when she connects early, and names the virtual waiting room and hold music. Connecting fifteen minutes ahead for a video appointment is what leaves room for last-minute troubleshooting, so she needs to know that the wait is expected and not a sign that something has gone wrong.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.2 Basic Concepts Related to Wounds
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.l · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: In what order do the phases of wound healing occur?
opciones: Hemostasis, inflammatory, proliferative, maturation
Inflammatory, hemostasis, maturation, proliferative
Proliferative, hemostasis, inflammatory, maturation
Hemostasis, proliferative, inflammatory, maturation
preguntas.explicacion: Vessels constrict and clotting factors act first, which is hemostasis and lasts up to an hour depending on the injury. Vasodilation then lets white cells in to clean the bed, showing as swelling, redness and exudate. The proliferative phase brings epithelialization, angiogenesis, collagen and contraction, and maturation lays down more collagen for strength.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: What fasting window is recommended before routine morning blood sampling?
opciones: Not less than 12 hours after the last solid meal
Not less than 8 hours after the last alcoholic drink
Not less than 24 hours after alcohol, with no limit on food
Not less than 2 hours after any food or drink
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation is morning sampling in a fasting state of not less than 12 hours since the last solid meal, with water allowed, coffee and energy drinks not allowed that morning, alcohol avoided for 24 hours, non-emergent medicines avoided, and no heavy exertion for 24 hours. The two-hour question comes from the WHO Annex C interview, and 8 hours is the glucose minimum.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Premium; and Glossary: Deductible
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5C · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which term describes the amount a person pays every month for their health insurance, whether or not they use any care?
opciones: Premium
Deductible
Copay
Network
preguntas.explicacion: The premium is the monthly price of the coverage itself, owed whether or not any service is used. HealthCare.gov adds that, on top of it, the patient usually pays other costs when care is actually received: a deductible, copayments and coinsurance. Its glossary describes a copay as a fixed amount per covered service, such as $30. The network is the set of contracted providers, not a payment at all.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medigap basics
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient bought a Medicare SELECT policy and has changed her mind about it. What right does she have?
opciones: Twelve months in which to switch across to a standard Medigap policy instead
Six months in which to switch, matching the Medigap open enrollment period
Thirty days in which to switch, after which the policy holds for the whole year
No right to switch, since every policy with the same letter is the same anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Some states also sell a kind of Medigap policy called Medicare SELECT, and a buyer of one has the right to change her mind within twelve months and move to a standard Medigap policy. That is separate from the six-month Medigap Open Enrollment Period, which governs when a policy can be bought without health questions in the first place.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fiber — Recommendations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(f) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(f) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: How much fiber a day is recommended for older children, adolescents and adults?
opciones: 21 to 38 grams, against an actual average of about 16 grams
21 to 38 grams, against an actual average of about 30 grams
10 to 20 grams, against an actual average of about 16 grams
40 to 60 grams, against an actual average of about 30 grams
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation runs from 21 to 38 grams a day, while people in the United States average around 16 grams, so most patients are short. Younger children cannot eat enough calories to reach that range, but whole grains and fresh fruit still belong in their diet.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Telehealth: Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth-appropriate visits · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5B k170 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks whether her diabetes education can be done by video instead of in the office. What does Medicare list?
opciones: Diabetes self-management training is among the services it covers by telehealth
An annual wellness visit with a physical examination is covered by telehealth
A screening mammogram read at the imaging center is covered by telehealth
A vaccine given at the patient's own home by a nurse is covered by telehealth
preguntas.explicacion: Plenty of services that normally happen face to face can be delivered by telehealth. Medicare names advance care planning, rehabilitation for the heart and the lungs, caregiver training, assessments of cognition, screening for depression, training in diabetes self-management, medical nutrition therapy, outpatient psychotherapy and speech therapy, and warns that the list is not everything it covers.

Toward the midline of the sternum
Toward the patient's left shoulder
Toward the top of the patient's head
preguntas.explicacion: Once the six chest sites have been scrubbed and re-marked, the electrodes go on with their tabs turned toward the cable yoke, and the clip connectors are then attached to those tabs. On the legs the tab is pointed the other way, up toward the upper leg.

preguntas.pregunta: How does the WHO say the alcohol swab should be moved over the venipuncture site?
opciones: From the center outward and downward, covering at least 2 cm
From the outside toward the center, covering at least 2 cm
Back and forth over the vein until the skin looks clean
In one pass along the vein, from the tourniquet toward the hand
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 describes firm but gentle pressure, starting at the center of the site and working downward and outward to cover an area of 2 cm or more, then letting the skin dry. The other patterns are not described. The step also forbids touching the cleaned area afterwards, and if it is touched the disinfection is repeated.

opciones: It is measured in both arms at that first evaluation
It is measured in the dominant arm and only that arm from then on
It is measured in one arm sitting and the other arm lying down
It is measured in the arm and again at the ankle for comparison
preguntas.explicacion: At the first evaluation the pressure is taken in both arms, because a difference between the two sides is itself a finding. After that the arm used is recorded so later readings can be compared with the same conditions, since the position and the limb both influence the number obtained.

The temperature of the tubes and the height of the sharps bin
The number of tubes on the tray and the color of the stoppers
The width of the tourniquet and the brand printed on the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Among the strategies put forward for difficult access are tapping the skin over the vein, a warm compress or a brief soak of the limb, and optimizing the operator's ergonomics, which covers the positioning of the patient and adequate ambient lighting.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says the bladder is very full and asks whether that matters. What is the effect?
opciones: A full bladder adds roughly 10 mm Hg, so the patient empties it before the reading
A full bladder lowers the reading by roughly 10 mm Hg through a vagal reflex
A full bladder has no measurable effect, so the reading proceeds as scheduled
A full bladder matters only in men, in whom the effect can reach 20 mm Hg
preguntas.explicacion: A distended bladder raises the reading by around 10 mm Hg, and figures of 10 to 15 mm Hg on both the systolic and the diastolic have been reported. Emptying the bladder is therefore part of the preparation, alongside no food or drink for 30 minutes and five minutes seated with the back supported.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, First Aid
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications: cold packs · CPT D3 k69 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient calls the next day about a painful bruise at the puncture site. What first-aid advice applies to a bruise?
opciones: Ice wrapped in a towel for up to 15 minutes each hour, never directly on the skin, with the area raised above the heart
Ice placed directly on the skin for 30 minutes at a time, with the arm kept below the level of the heart
A warm compress for 15 minutes each hour and vigorous massage to disperse the pooled blood under the skin
A tight adhesive strip over the bruise for 24 hours, kept on until the color turns greenish-yellow
preguntas.explicacion: Place ice on the bruise to speed healing and reduce swelling, wrapped in a clean towel and never directly on the skin, for up to 15 minutes each hour; to hold the bruised part above heart level where that can be managed; and to rest it. It also describes the color change from pinkish red to bluish to greenish-yellow as the bruise heals. Warm compresses are a measure to raise veins before a puncture.

preguntas.pregunta: A tracing looks like electrical interference, yet the wires lie straight and no equipment is running nearby. What is checked next?
opciones: The hook-up, because reversed leads can imitate that effect
The paper, because a low supply can imitate that effect
The gel, because a dried electrode can imitate that effect
The grid, because a slow paper speed can imitate that effect
preguntas.explicacion: Swapped lead wires sometimes write something that looks like alternating-current interference, so once contact and surroundings are ruled out the wiring is verified. The same reversal of the arm wires turns every complex in lead I upside down.

The OSHA hotline, 1-800-321-6742
FDA MedWatch, for the device involved
The Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System
preguntas.explicacion: A worker with questions about medical treatment after an exposure is told to ring 1-888-448-4911, the Clinicians' Post Exposure Prophylaxis Line, which the National Clinician Consultation Center runs; the CDC's PEP guidance gives that same number with its hours. The OSHA hotline is for reporting severe injuries, fatalities and hospitalizations; MedWatch takes voluntary reports about device problems; and VAERS collects adverse events after vaccination, hepatitis B vaccine included.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Issues of Concern, Hospice and End of Life; StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section When consent is voluntarily waived
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 k217 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: An impaired elderly inpatient cannot communicate about a proposed procedure. In what order should a decision-maker be sought?
opciones: A legally appointed medical power of attorney, then a documented directive, then family
Family members first, then the attending physician, then a court-appointed guardian
The attending physician first, then the hospital ethics committee, then family
A court-appointed guardian first, before consulting any relative or document
preguntas.explicacion: Defer first to anyone legally appointed as medical decision-maker, such as a medical power of attorney; if none exists, to look for a living will or other documented directive; and only then to family, ideally through shared decision-making. A court appoints a guardian only when the state hierarchy fails.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k51 · CMA I.A.1.e · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: What range is normal for oxygen saturation on a pulse oximeter in a healthy adult?
opciones: 95% to 100%, with hypoxemia defined below 90%
90% to 100%, with hypoxemia defined below 85%
85% to 95%, with hypoxemia defined below 80%
92% to 98%, with hypoxemia defined below 88%
preguntas.explicacion: A healthy adult reads 95% to 100%, and a saturation under 90% is hypoxemia. People with a lung disease such as COPD or pneumonia, and people who live at high elevation, may sit somewhat lower and still be acceptable, which is why the reading is judged against the patient rather than against the number alone.
