opciones: The whole penis is placed inside the bag and the adhesive strip is pressed onto the skin around it
Only the tip of the penis is placed inside the bag and the adhesive strip is pressed onto the diaper
The bag is taped across the two skin folds flanking the opening where urine flows out
The bag is laid loose inside the diaper, without adhesive, so that the voided urine drains into it
preguntas.explicacion: For a boy the whole penis goes inside the plastic bag and the sticky strip fixes to the skin; for a girl the bag covers the two skin folds that flank the vaginal opening. Before it goes on, the area round the urethra is washed thoroughly with the soap or wipes the provider supplied. A bag not sealed to the skin, or one holding only the tip, will leak.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient position)
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical factors · CPT D3 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E1 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives at the office laboratory out of breath after climbing several flights of stairs. What is recommended before the draw, and why?
opciones: Have the patient sit for at least 15 minutes, since posture changes alter biochemistry results
Draw immediately, because exertion raises the venous pressure and makes the veins easier to find
Have the patient lie down for two to three minutes and then draw with a butterfly set
Postpone the draw for 24 hours, the interval the chapter sets after physical activity
preguntas.explicacion: Patients in an office setting should stay seated for at least 15 minutes before the procedure, because statistically significant changes in several biochemistry parameters follow a change in position, and any unavoidable change should be recorded. The 24-hour rule in the same chapter concerns avoiding excessive physical activity before the collection, not a postponement.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Issues of Concern, Intoxicated Patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who smells strongly of alcohol refuses his draw and the nurse is unsure how impaired he is. What is directed?
opciones: Carry out the usual capacity assessment, since intoxication varies in degree
Draw anyway, because intoxication always removes the right to refuse care
Accept the refusal with no assessment, since the refusal is his to make
Wait for a court order before any decision about the draw is taken
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohol or drugs on board may leave a patient without capacity, and where the level of intoxication is uncertain the usual capacity assessment is carried out. That impairment is often temporary: sober again, the same patient may decide soundly. Formal guardianship through a court belongs to long-term situations.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Blood Culture Contamination: An Overview for Infection Control and Antibiotic Stewardship Programs (2022), section 2 Proper Skin Antisepsis; and Quality Tool SOP model step 2; and CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination (one-pager, abril 2025)
preguntas.subtema: Skin preparation for cultures · CPT D4 4A k75 · PBT II.G II.F · CCMA 3E k139 · NCMA 2C.8 bacterial culture site
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wipes the antecubital site with a disinfectant that contains alcohol and then, to save time, inserts the needle while the skin is still wet. Why does the CDC object?
opciones: The disinfectant has to dry on the skin before the culture is drawn
Alcohol must be replaced by a water-based iodine prep for cultures
The site should have been re-palpated with a bare finger after cleaning
Alcohol is only for the bottle septum, never for the venipuncture site
preguntas.explicacion: For blood cultures the skin is disinfected with an alcohol-containing product and allowed to dry before the draw; improper antisepsis is a recognized cause of contamination. The alcohol removes the normal skin oils so that a water-based preparation can reach the skin surface, which is why alcohol is part of the prep rather than something to replace. Touching the cleaned site again is prohibited by the WHO's venipuncture steps, and 70% isopropyl alcohol is also the agent for the septum.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview of the Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Body Fluid Samples
preguntas.subtema: Body fluid transport · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.1 / V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k117 · CMA I.C.8.c · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: Pleural, peritoneal and synovial fluids have been aspirated for culture. How should they travel to the laboratory?
opciones: Promptly and at room temperature, which keeps the organisms viable
Promptly and refrigerated, which keeps the organisms viable in transit
Promptly and frozen, since the cell count is read from the thawed fluid
Whenever convenient, provided each container has been sealed and labeled
preguntas.explicacion: Aspiration is aseptic and the container sterile, and what gets recorded is the appearance, the color, the turbidity, the viscosity and any clot. Portions go out for cell count and differential, for protein and glucose, for culture and for cytology. The microbiology portion depends on prompt transport at room temperature to keep the organisms alive, the same principle that governs cerebrospinal fluid.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Other Issues, Human Clinical Studies; and StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", section Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Under which measure was the Institutional Review Board established in the United States?
opciones: The National Research Act, in 1974
The National Research Act, in 1984
The Belmont Report, issued in 1976
The Declaration of Helsinki revisions
preguntas.explicacion: The National Research Act created the board in 1974, bringing regulation to human research after unethical practices such as the Tuskegee syphilis experiments. The Belmont Report names beneficence, justice and respect for persons as its guiding principles, and the Declaration of Helsinki is an ethical statement; neither created the board.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which superficial vein connects the cephalic and basilic veins in the cubital fossa?
opciones: The median cubital vein
The median antebrachial vein
The brachial vein
The dorsal venous arch
preguntas.explicacion: As the cephalic and basilic veins approach the cubital fossa they become joined by the median cubital vein, which has a median cephalic and a median basilic connection. The dorsal venous arch is where both veins begin on the back of the hand, the median antebrachial vein is the dominant vessel only in the type I fossa, and the brachial vein is deep.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Services and Facilities
preguntas.subtema: Barrier removal · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: An older office building has two steps at its entrance. What does the law ask of the practice inside it?
opciones: Remove the barrier where doing so is readily achievable, and otherwise serve by other means
Remove the barrier only when the building is next altered or the lease comes up for renewal
Remove the barrier only if a patient files a written complaint about the entrance first
Leave the entrance as it stands, since buildings raised before the law are not reached by it
preguntas.explicacion: Every building is subject to the requirements for existing facilities, whatever its age. Under Title III architectural barriers are removed where removal is readily achievable, that is, easily accomplishable without much difficulty or expense; where it is not, the services still have to be made available by alternative methods that are readily achievable.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Allowed amount
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMAA 5C k76, 4 k61 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What does the allowed amount of a plan represent?
opciones: The most the plan will pay for a covered service, also called the negotiated rate
The most the patient will pay for a covered service before the plan pays its share
The most the patient will pay in a plan year before coverage of benefits reaches 100%
The total the provider charges for the service before any discount is applied to it
preguntas.explicacion: The allowed amount is the ceiling a plan will pay for a covered service, and the glossary also calls it the eligible expense, the payment allowance or the negotiated rate. What the patient pays first is the deductible; the yearly ceiling on patient spending is the out-of-pocket limit; and the provider's own charge is a separate figure, which is why a charge above the allowed amount can leave a balance.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Low blood sugar", Overview
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.f · 2027 I.B.8.f · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1M k37
preguntas.pregunta: At which blood glucose level is a patient considered to be hypoglycemic?
opciones: Below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L), which can already do harm
Below 100 mg/dL (5.6 mmol/L), the lower end of the fasting range
Below 55 mg/dL (3.1 mmol/L), and never above that figure
Below 40 mg/dL (2.2 mmol/L), when the patient loses consciousness
preguntas.explicacion: A blood sugar under 70 mg/dL, or 3.9 mmol/L, counts as low and can be harmful at or below that level. Symptoms may not appear until the glucose falls below 55 mg/dL, which is why the number matters and not only how the patient looks. Severe low blood sugar that ends in unconsciousness is what is called insulin shock.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Blood pressure measurement
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.d · NCMA 2B.5
preguntas.pregunta: How is a blood pressure of 120 over 80 correctly recorded?
opciones: 120/80 mm Hg, systolic first and the units written after the pair
80/120 mm Hg, diastolic first because it is the resting value of the two
120/80 mm, since the unit of the gauge is millimeters of the column
120 over 80 kPa, the pressure unit used on automated office devices
preguntas.explicacion: The systolic value goes first, then a slash, then the diastolic, and the unit is millimeters of mercury: 120/80 mm Hg. The gauge on the cuff reads in that unit, and the arm used and the patient's position belong in the record beside the numbers, since both change the value.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services: USPS Ground Advantage
preguntas.subtema: Hazardous shipments · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An item classed as hazardous material cannot travel by air. Which domestic service is named as the primary option for it?
opciones: USPS Ground Advantage, the ground service that reaches most places in two to five days
Priority Mail Express, whose network is built around the fastest possible movement
First-Class Mail, whose light pieces travel with ordinary letters and small envelopes
Media Mail, whose slower schedule already allows for surface transport of the contents
preguntas.explicacion: Ground Advantage is described as the low-rate ground service with expected delivery in two to five days and as the primary option for hazardous materials that cannot go by air. Its handling fee for such items is also the only one of the three parcel services set at nothing extra.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields; and StatPearls, "Sterile Technique" (NBK459175)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.g · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: A sterile drape has been opened over a treatment table. Which part of it counts as contaminated from the start?
opciones: The one-inch border running around the edge of the drape
The one-inch border running around the edge, plus the center
The half of the drape furthest from the person who opened it
The four corners where the flaps were folded before opening
preguntas.explicacion: An imaginary border one inch wide along the edges is treated as unsterile, so supplies are never tossed or slid into it. The same one-inch rule applies around any hole, tear or patch of moisture wicked in from an unsterile area. Peel-pack wrappers carry the same border, which is why items are not slid out near the edge of the pouch.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Light Blue; and "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: What concentration of sodium citrate does the light blue coagulation tube contain?
preguntas.explicacion: Both the tube collection review and the prothrombin time chapter give 3.2% sodium citrate as the anticoagulant of the light blue tube. The figure 9 comes from a different rule in the same chapter, the 9 to 1 ratio of blood to citrate that the tube must keep, and the other two numbers are misplacements of the decimal point. The citrate works by chelating calcium.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: When Can Information Be Shared?
preguntas.subtema: Where consults happen · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A clinician takes a telephone consult about a named patient from the phone in the hospital cafeteria. What is wrong with that?
opciones: The talk is allowed, but it has to happen away from the public
The talk is barred, since consults require written authorization
The talk is allowed only if the patient is on the line as well
The talk is barred, because phone lines are never encrypted
preguntas.explicacion: Consulting another provider is a permitted conversation; where it happens is what matters. Such talk belongs in a private room, out of earshot of the public, and a telephone consult taken from a cafeteria line, where anyone nearby can hear, is the example given of how not to do it. Staff may still coordinate verbally at a nurses' station, and providers may discuss a patient's status by telephone.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance; StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Indications
preguntas.subtema: Soap and water vs alcohol rub · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 k102 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: When does the CDC say soap and water must be used rather than alcohol-based hand sanitizer?
opciones: When hands look soiled, after using the restroom, or during a C. difficile outbreak
Before every aseptic task and after any contact with the patient's immediate surroundings
Whenever the sanitizer on hand contains less than 60 percent alcohol by volume
Whenever gloves have been worn for longer than the 20 seconds a hand rub takes
preguntas.explicacion: In most clinical moments the CDC prefers an alcohol-based hand rub, and it sends staff to soap and water in a short list of situations: hands that look soiled, before eating, after a restroom visit, and while caring for patients with known or suspected C. difficile or norovirus during an outbreak. The reason is chemical, since spore formers and non-enveloped organisms survive alcohol and have to be removed mechanically by washing. Aseptic tasks and contact with the patient's surroundings are moments for hand hygiene by either method, not reasons to reach for soap.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Introduction; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding into the skin
preguntas.subtema: Complications: petechiae · CPT D3 3L k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: How is a spot tested to decide whether it is non-blanching?
opciones: Brief pressure is applied, and the spot does not disappear
Brief pressure is applied, and the spot fades then returns
The skin is stretched, and the spot spreads sideways with it
The skin is cooled, and the spot pales under the cold pack
preguntas.explicacion: A non-blanching spot is one that stays visible after brief pressure is put on the area. That single maneuver separates bleeding into the skin, which does not pale, from simple redness of the skin, which does. Both petechiae and purpura are defined as non-blanching.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification; Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.b
preguntas.pregunta: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen from a neurology ICU arrives in a urine cup instead of a sterile CSF tube. How does the emergency laboratory handle it?
opciones: A laboratory medicine specialist decides whether this precious specimen is rejected or accepted
The accessioning clerk rejects it automatically, as with any specimen in an improper container
It is accepted without review, because CSF can never be recollected from the same patient
It is transferred by the clerk into a sterile tube and processed as an ordinary specimen
preguntas.explicacion: Improper container is a standing rejection criterion, and sending CSF in a urine cup is described as a common mistake in the neurology ICU; but for precious specimens such as CSF, bone marrow or aspirates received in unsuitable tubes or under wrong transport conditions, the decision to reject or accept is reserved to the laboratory medicine specialists rather than made automatically at the desk.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Vaccine Administration: During the Visit, Needle Length
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k72 · CMA I.D.2.d(2) · RMA III.G.2.b · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: An adult woman weighing about 250 lb is to receive an intramuscular vaccine in the deltoid. Which needle is chosen?
opciones: A 1.5-inch needle, 22 to 25 gauge, because she weighs more than 200 lb
A 1-inch needle, 22 to 25 gauge, which is the choice below 130 lb
A 5/8-inch needle, 23 to 25 gauge, which is the subcutaneous choice
A 1-inch needle, 18 to 22 gauge, chosen for a thicker vaccine product
preguntas.explicacion: Needle length for an intramuscular vaccine in an adult follows weight. Below 130 lb, and from 130 to 152 lb, an inch is used; men from 153 to 260 lb and women from 153 to 200 lb take 1 to 1.5 inches; men over 260 lb and women over 200 lb take 1.5 inches. The gauge stays 22 to 25 throughout. Five eighths of an inch with 23 to 25 gauge is the row for the subcutaneous route at any age.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A child with Down syndrome is plotted below the usual curves. What does the technique call for?
opciones: A specialized chart for that condition is used in place of the standard one
The standard chart is kept, and the values below the curve are simply noted
The chart is dropped, and only the measurements themselves are recorded
The chart for a younger age group is used, since growth runs behind schedule
preguntas.explicacion: Conditions that change the pattern of growth need their own plots to give a meaningful result, and specialized charts exist for achondroplasia, for cerebral palsy, and for the syndromes of Down, Turner, Williams, Prader-Willi and Rett. Whatever chart is used, it contributes to the picture rather than making a diagnosis by itself.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Hypodermic single-use needle and syringe
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which disadvantage does the WHO device table attach to collecting blood with a hypodermic needle and syringe?
opciones: The blood has to be transferred, adding needle-stick and splash risk
It cannot be used for blood drawing in the pediatric population
It cannot be heparinized, so it is unsuitable for arterial blood samples
It requires more training than an evacuated tube system
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 lists as disadvantages of the syringe that the blood has to be transferred, which adds a risk of needle-stick injuries or blood splashing, that large or multiple samples are difficult, and that a smaller syringe and pediatric tube are needed for children. Its advantages include use in children, heparinization for arterial draws, low cost and no special training.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient position and fasting)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says the only thing taken that morning before a fasting draw was a cup of black coffee, no sugar. Under the guidance on fasting samples, is the specimen acceptable?
opciones: No: during the fasting period water is acceptable, but coffee and other drinks such as energy drinks are not allowed
Yes: black coffee without sugar adds no calories and is treated the same way as plain water during a fast
Yes, provided the coffee was taken more than 2 hours before the draw and the patient then drank plain water
No: coffee is allowed only together with the morning medicines, which this patient did not take
preguntas.explicacion: The recommended set-up is a morning draw after at least 12 hours without solid food. Water during the fast is fine; coffee, energy drinks and any other beverage are off the table that morning, and alcohol is dropped for the preceding 24 hours. A non-fasting sample is accepted only for patients who cannot manage the fast, in emergencies, and for analytes that fasting does not move. Fasting status is confirmed a second time once identity has been verified.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications; and StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Technique
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 k49 · PBT II.D II.I · CCMA 3E1 k128 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's history shows a right radical mastectomy. Which precaution applies when choosing where to draw?
opciones: Avoid drawing from the arm on the side of the mastectomy
Draw from the right arm but use a smaller-gauge needle
Draw from the right hand only, never from the antecubital fossa
Draw from either arm, as long as the tourniquet stays under one minute
preguntas.explicacion: A history of radical mastectomy on the same side is listed among the site contraindications, along with scar tissue from earlier attempts, cellulitis or an abscess, fibrosis of the vein, a hematoma, a vascular graft, and any venous access device such as a port, a central catheter or an IV. Capillary testing repeats the rule: keep off the side of a recent mastectomy or of an ongoing infusion.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Copayment; and Glossary: Coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: Copayment vs coinsurance · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.6.e, III.G.9.c / 2027 III.G.6.c · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What is the difference between a copayment and coinsurance?
opciones: A copayment is a set dollar figure per service and coinsurance is a percentage of it
A copayment is a percentage of the service and coinsurance is a set dollar figure
A copayment is owed before the deductible and coinsurance replaces the deductible
A copayment is owed monthly for coverage and coinsurance is owed at each visit
preguntas.explicacion: A copayment is a fixed amount, $20 for instance, that the patient pays for a covered service. Coinsurance is a share expressed as a percentage of the allowed amount, 20% for instance, so the dollars change with the price of the service. Both are usually owed after the deductible is satisfied. The monthly amount owed for the coverage itself, used or not, is the premium.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(ix)(D), Gloves in volunteer blood donation centers
preguntas.subtema: Donation center gloving policy · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A volunteer blood donation center decides gloves are not routinely needed for every draw. What must the employer still do?
opciones: Reevaluate the policy periodically, keep gloves available, and never discourage their use
Record every draw done without gloves in the sharps injury log kept for the year
Obtain a signed declination from each employee who draws without wearing gloves
Report the policy to the Assistant Secretary before the first donation session
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ix)(D) lets a volunteer blood donation center judge that routine gloving for every phlebotomy is unnecessary, but it attaches four duties: reevaluate that judgment periodically, make gloves available to anyone who wants them, do nothing to discourage their use, and require them when the employee has cuts or breaks in the skin, when hand contamination looks likely, and while the employee is being trained. The declination statement is for the hepatitis B vaccine, and the sharps log records percutaneous injuries, not gloving decisions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Other Issues: Disposing of PHI
preguntas.subtema: Disposal of PHI · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3B k39
preguntas.pregunta: How should paper records and prescription labels that contain PHI be disposed of?
opciones: Shredded or incinerated so that nobody can piece them back together
Placed in a red biohazard bag and treated as regulated waste
Handed to the person in charge of shredding to take home and destroy later
Kept in a locked cabinet indefinitely, since PHI may never be destroyed
preguntas.explicacion: Documents with PHI are shredded or incinerated so that no reconstruction is possible, computers, CDs and drives are completely erased before disposal, and the people assigned to destruction are chosen so that records are in fact destroyed rather than taken home; letting the shredding staff carry records home is exactly what that selection is meant to prevent. A red bag is the container for regulated waste under the bloodborne pathogens standard, which is about infection, not confidentiality, and HIPAA sets a retention period for its own documentation rather than a ban on destroying records.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Language Barriers; and ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2F k16 k43 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 k127 · CMA F.1.c(2) / 2027 F.1.d(3) · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who is deaf and uses sign language needs the informed-consent discussion for a therapeutic phlebotomy. What should be arranged?
opciones: An American Sign Language medical interpreter for the discussion
A written summary handed to the patient in place of the discussion
The patient's hearing spouse to relay the discussion in sign language
A shorter discussion, since the procedure is routine and low risk
preguntas.explicacion: Language barriers and interpreters used badly complicate informed consent, so interpreter services go to patients whose command of the spoken language is limited, and medical interpreters in American Sign Language should be available for patients who are hearing-impaired. Under the ADA a companion may interpret only in narrow circumstances, and a doctor's office discussing a procedure generally needs an interpreter.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A paternity test is requested. Which tube does the WHO order-of-draw table assign to that use?
opciones: The pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube
The light blue tube with sodium citrate
The purple tube with EDTA anticoagulant
The yellow-black striped blood culture bottle
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 lists HLA tissue typing, paternity testing and DNA studies as the uses of the pale yellow tube containing acid-citrate-dextrose (ACD, ACDA or ACDB), whose mode of action is described as complement inactivation. The light blue tube is for coagulation, the purple tube for hematology and cross-match, and the yellow-black bottle for aerobic and anaerobic cultures and fungi.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Non-invasive Techniques)
preguntas.subtema: Volume and labeling · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.D.2 · CCMA 3D4 k113 · CMA I.C.8.a · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: How much urine is needed for an accurate routine urinalysis, and where should the label go?
opciones: About 15 to 30 mL, with the label placed on the container itself and not on the lid
About 15 to 30 mL, with the label placed on the lid so the container stays see-through
The container filled to capacity, with the label placed on the container and not the lid
About 100 to 120 mL, with the label placed across the lid and the container together
preguntas.explicacion: Roughly 15 to 30 mL is enough for an accurate analysis, so patients are told not to fill the cup to the top. The lid and rim are closed carefully to avoid contaminating them, and the specimen is labeled before or immediately after collection, on the container and never on the lid, because a lid can end up on a different cup.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), If an Exposure Occurs; WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Step 1
preguntas.subtema: Needlestick first aid · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After a needlestick, what does the CDC say about squeezing the wound or applying bleach to it?
opciones: Neither has evidence behind it, and caustic agents like bleach are not advised
Squeezing is recommended to expel contaminated blood; bleach is not advised
Bleach at a 1:10 dilution is recommended on the wound; squeezing is not
Both are recommended right away, before the wound is washed with soap and water
preguntas.explicacion: Nothing in the evidence says an antiseptic, or squeezing the wound, lowers the chance of passing on a bloodborne pathogen, and bleach and other caustics are not advised at all. What is recommended is washing the needlestick with soap and water. The WHO annex on occupational exposure says the same: soap and water, no alcohol and no strong disinfectant, let the wound bleed freely, and leave it undressed. The 1:10 bleach dilution belongs to surfaces after a spill, never to skin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Expert Witness", Introduction: Burden of Proof
preguntas.subtema: Civil and criminal acts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4 · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What does the jury have to be convinced of in a civil medical negligence case?
opciones: That the plaintiff's account is more plausible than the defendant's
That the plaintiff's account is proven beyond any reasonable doubt
That the plaintiff's account is supported by two expert witnesses
That the plaintiff's account is admitted by the treating clinician
preguntas.explicacion: Civil cases use a lower bar than criminal ones. The plaintiff has to convince the jury by a preponderance of the evidence, meaning at least 51 percent: the argument and the evidence must look likelier as the proximate cause of the injury alleged than whatever the defense puts up. Proof beyond a reasonable doubt belongs to criminal prosecutions.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination (one-pager, April 2025)
preguntas.subtema: Blood culture procedure · CPT D4 4A · PBT II.C patient identification · CCMA 3E k139 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Before drawing blood cultures, which identification check satisfies the first step of the CDC's model procedure?
opciones: The patient states full name and date of birth, matched to the order
The nurse confirms the patient's name aloud at the door of the room
The room and bed numbers match the numbers printed on the requisition
The name on the wristband matches the name printed on the requisition
preguntas.explicacion: Step 1 is identification with two or more identifiers unique to that patient, the example of good practice given being name and date of birth. A name on its own, whether a nurse says it or a wristband shows it, is one identifier, and room or bed numbers do not belong to the patient. Only once identification is done does the procedure move to disinfecting the site and the bottle septa.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Non-fasting sampling is 'rarely acceptable'. For whom is the exception made?
opciones: Patients who cannot tolerate fasting, emergency cases, and tests not affected by food
Any patient who forgot to fast, provided the omission is written on the requisition
Inpatients only, because their meals are already controlled by the ward
Patients on therapeutic drug monitoring, who must eat together with the dose
preguntas.explicacion: Three situations make a non-fasting sample acceptable: the minority of patients who cannot cope with the strict conditions, an emergency, and those particular parameters that food leaves alone. Merely noting that the fast was broken does not make the sample acceptable; the provider is told and may reschedule.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Public Health Activities
preguntas.subtema: Employer disclosures · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.5 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k37 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: An employer asks the practice for information about an employee's work-related injury. When may that be released without authorization?
opciones: When the employer needs it to comply with an occupational safety requirement
Whenever the employer is the one paying the premium for the employee's plan
Whenever the employee has already told the employer that the injury happened
Only when a court has ordered the practice to produce the medical record
preguntas.explicacion: Among the public health activities, a covered entity may disclose to an employer, at the employer's request and about its own employee, information on an illness or injury that is work- related or on medical surveillance of the workplace, because the employer needs it to satisfy the requirements of OSHA, or those of the Mine Safety and Health Administration, or of a State law that does the same job. Workers' compensation disclosures are a separate national priority purpose.

preguntas.fuente: DEA, Drug Scheduling
preguntas.subtema: Laws and regulations · CCMA 7A k214 (Controlled Substances Act) · CMA E.5.b · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: On what basis are controlled substances placed into their schedules?
opciones: On accepted medical use and the potential for abuse or dependency
On the strength of the dose and the route by which it is given
On the cost to the health plan and the risk of diversion in transit
On the length of time the drug has been approved for sale in the country
preguntas.explicacion: Drugs and substances, and certain chemicals employed in making them, are sorted into five schedules by their accepted medical use and their potential for abuse or dependency, with the abuse rate as the determining factor. Schedule I has a high potential for abuse and no medical use currently accepted; Schedule V has the lowest potential of all and holds limited quantities of certain narcotics.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: R-Wave
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k149 k153 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: A tracing shows no build-up of the R wave across the chest leads. Which technical cause does the assistant check?
opciones: An electrode that was not put where its landmark falls
A paper speed that was set below 25 mm per second
A calibration mark that printed at half its usual height
A lead wire that was left looped across the patient's arm
preguntas.explicacion: The R wave should grow steadily from V1, the smallest, to V5, the largest. When that build-up is missing, the listed causes are an old anteroseptal infarct, hypertrophy of the left ventricle and an electrode that was placed inaccurately, which is the fixable one.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Nervous System: The Peripheral Nervous System; and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 14.1 Sensory Perception (CC BY 4.0)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(3) (2027 I.C.6.f(3)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which division of the nervous system controls the heart, the stomach and the intestines without conscious effort?
opciones: The autonomic division of the peripheral nervous system
The somatic division of the peripheral nervous system
The sensory division of the central nervous system
The reflex division of the central nervous system
preguntas.explicacion: The peripheral system splits in two. The somatic part serves the skin and skeletal muscles and handles conscious activity. The autonomic part connects the center to the visceral organs and works continuously without conscious effort, minding heart rate, breathing rate, blood pressure and body temperature.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Interface inventory · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which list does the contingency guidance tell an organization to keep and review as part of its downtime planning?
opciones: Its system-to-system connections, marking those that must be told of an outage
Its staff members trained on paper charting, marked by the date of their training
Its patients seen during the last outage, marked by the unit that attended them
Its equipment serviced in the past year, marked by the date of the next service
preguntas.explicacion: Interfaces are the part that fails quietly. The organization keeps a comprehensive list of its system-to-system interfaces and reviews it regularly, every six months or yearly, noting which of them raise legal or regulatory duties to warn the other side, such as a state immunization registry or a prescription drug monitoring program.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Capillaries; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Classification & Structure of Blood Vessels, Capillaries
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3 k71) · PBT I.A.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is the wall of a capillary made of, and what is the capillary's job?
opciones: One endothelial layer on a basement membrane; exchange with tissue fluid
Three tunics with a thin muscular media; regulation of blood pressure
Endothelium with a few muscle cells; collecting blood as it leaves the bed
Rings of smooth muscle called sphincters; control of flow into the bed
preguntas.explicacion: A capillary is an endothelial layer wrapped in a basement membrane, and in the narrowest ones a single cell curls round to touch itself; its job is perfusion, the exchange of gases and other substances between blood and interstitial fluid. The three tunics belong to the arteriole, the sphincters to the metarteriole, and endothelium with a few muscle cells and elastic fibers describes the venule that gathers blood leaving the bed.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Directing to a Third Party
preguntas.subtema: Directing PHI to a third party · CCMA 5 k176 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient wants her records sent straight to a research app she uses. What does the Privacy Rule require of her request?
opciones: It must be in writing, signed by her, and name the recipient and where to send the copy
It must be approved by the privacy official, who decides whether the recipient is suitable
It must come with an authorization from the app developer accepting business associate duties
It must be limited to a summary, since only summaries may be directed outside the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Beyond taking copies herself, an individual may direct the covered entity to send her PHI on to another person or entity of her choosing. The request has to be in writing, has to be signed, and has to say plainly who that designated recipient is and the address the information should go to; an electronic copy of a signed request, or one executed electronically through a secure portal, is acceptable. The same fee limits and the same form-and-format rules apply.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Temperature; and StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever" (NBK562334)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's oral temperature is 36.6 °C at 7 am and 37.1 °C at 5 pm on the same day. What accounts for the difference?
opciones: Normal daily variation: the value is lowest early in the morning and peaks late in the afternoon
A change of site: an axillary reading runs about one full degree above an oral one in the same patient
The second half of the menstrual cycle, which lowers the recorded value by about one degree
An early low-grade fever, which is graded from a reading of 37.3 °C upward at any hour
preguntas.explicacion: Body temperature swings by roughly half a degree Celsius over 24 hours: lowest in the early morning, highest late in the day. Both readings sit inside the 36.5 to 37.5 °C band, so neither is a fever. Low-grade fever starts at 37.3 °C, the axilla reads lower than the mouth, and the luteal phase raises the value, it does not lower it.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, Chapter 2.6: Current and Past Medical History
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.A.3.c · CCMA 3A3 · NCMA 2B.4
preguntas.pregunta: During an intake interview, when is a closed or direct question the better tool?
opciones: When one specific detail has to be pinned down, such as whether medicines are taken as prescribed
When the patient is first invited to say, in their own words, exactly what brought them in today
When the patient's cultural background and what matters about it is being explored
When the patient is asked to put into words what the dizziness actually feels like
preguntas.explicacion: Closed questions collect a fact: taken as prescribed or not, allergic or not, pregnant or not. Open-ended ones invite the patient to elaborate and are what the interview opens with, what cultural background and beliefs are explored with, and how a symptom gets described. A closed answer of no or sometimes is then followed up with an open-ended request to tell more.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Orthostatic Hypotension", Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k48 · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which patients are most likely to show orthostatic hypotension?
opciones: Older adults: about 1 in 5 of those aged 60 and over are affected
Older adults: about 1 in 50 of those aged 60 and over are affected
Young adults, in whom the baroreceptor reflex has not yet fully matured
Adults aged 45 to 49, the group in which more than 25% are affected
preguntas.explicacion: Prevalence climbs steeply with age, largely through loss of baroreceptor sensitivity: roughly one in five community-dwelling adults aged 60 or older is affected, and the rate is higher still in long-term care. Population studies put it under 5% at ages 45 to 49 and above 25% at 85 and over.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k9 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Two tubes come back faulty from the same phlebotomist: one is hemolyzed and one holds small clots. What separates the two errors?
opciones: Too much mixing haemolyses the sample; too little leaves small clots
Too little mixing haemolyses the sample; too much leaves small clots
Too much mixing leaves clots; a short draw is what haemolyses a sample
Both faults come from mixing too little, at different points in the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with an anticoagulant are inverted in a figure-of-8 until the blood and additive are properly combined. Push it too far and hemolysis appears; stop too soon and small clots form. Both faults make the specimen unusable, and both are decided at the bedside, not in the laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding, Considerations and First Aid
preguntas.subtema: Bleeding control · CPT D1 1M k37 · CMA I.B.9.a / 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's venipuncture site keeps bleeding through the gauze after the draw. What is the most important first step?
opciones: Apply direct pressure over the site and keep it until the bleeding stops
Apply a tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the site and note the time
Remove the soaked gauze, clean the wound, and apply fresh gauze
Raise the arm above the heart and peek every minute to check
preguntas.explicacion: For bleeding on the outside, nothing matters more than direct pressure, and it stops most of it: press on the wound with a sterile bandage, a clean cloth or, failing those, a hand, and hold the pressure until the bleeding stops, without peeking. Raising the bleeding part can be added where possible, but lifting the dressing every minute disturbs the clot. A soaked dressing stays where it is with another laid on top, and a tourniquet is kept for severe, life-threatening limb bleeding that continuous pressure has not controlled.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 2O k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why are veins preferred over arteries for a routine blood draw?
opciones: Veins run superficially, while arteries have thicker walls and more nerves, so puncturing them hurts more
Veins carry oxygenated blood, which is what most chemistry analysers are calibrated to measure
Arteries collapse under the vacuum of the tube, while veins tolerate the negative pressure
Arterial blood clots too quickly in a citrate tube to allow coagulation testing
preguntas.explicacion: Veins are preferred for efficiency and patient comfort because they run superficially, whereas arteries tend to have thicker walls and more associated nerves, making a puncture more painful; arterial sampling is reserved for arterial blood gases. The chapter says nothing about arteries collapsing or clotting faster, and thick walls are a property it credits to the median cubital vein.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Infection Control in Healthcare Personnel (2019), section 7, Selected federal requirements for exposure and illness management
preguntas.subtema: Notification of emergency responders · CPT D1 k24 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k96 · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: Which federal law requires that emergency responders be notified when they may have been exposed to selected infectious diseases?
opciones: The Ryan White HIV/AIDS Treatment Extension Act
The Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act of 2000
The Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993
The Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended
preguntas.explicacion: Several federal rules bear on exposure and illness management, and the one written for emergency responders is the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Treatment Extension Act of 2009: a responder who may have been exposed to certain infections has to be told, and the CDC keeps the list of which exposures trigger that notice and how it is reported. The Needlestick Act of 2000 amended the OSHA standard instead, on safer devices and the sharps injury log. The FMLA entitles eligible employees to unpaid, job-protected leave while their group health coverage continues. The ADA limits whether and how an employer may ask a worker about illness, and obliges it to offer reasonable accommodation when a work restriction is applied.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Platelets
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What exactly is a platelet?
opciones: A fragment of megakaryocyte cytoplasm wrapped in plasma membrane
A small complete cell with a two-lobed nucleus, 8 to 10 µm wide
An immature erythrocyte that still contains remnants of organelles
A leukocyte that has left the circulation to phagocytize debris
preguntas.explicacion: A platelet is not a cell: it is a piece of the cytoplasm of a large marrow cell, the megakaryocyte, enclosed by a bit of plasma membrane, which is why the older name thrombocyte is misleading. Each megakaryocyte releases 2000 to 3000 platelets. The small two-lobed cell is the basophil, the immature red cell is the reticulocyte, and the emigrated phagocyte is the macrophage.

preguntas.subtema: Media accountability · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A practice writes down which staff member took which laptop out of the building and when it came back. Which specification does that log satisfy?
opciones: Accountability, a record of hardware movements and of the person answering for them
Maintenance records, a record of repairs made to doors, walls and locks in the office
Workstation use, which fixes what may be done at a given class of workstation
Facility security plan, which guards the premises and its equipment against theft
preguntas.explicacion: Accountability sits under device and media controls, and it is the addressable specification calling for a log of where hardware and electronic media go and of who answers for them. Maintenance records look at the building itself, not at equipment that travels.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Patient Data Verification
preguntas.subtema: Insurance verification · CMAA 5B k66, 4 k58 · CCMA 5E · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A patient hands over a new insurance card at check-in. Which step protects the claim best?
opciones: Verifying coverage and benefits with the plan before the visit is billed
Filing the card in the paper chart and billing the plan listed last year
Asking the patient to state the group number aloud instead of copying it
Waiting for the remittance advice to reveal which plan is now primary
preguntas.explicacion: Verification of patient data prevents rejections, delays and denials: insurance eligibility belongs on the list of items to confirm before the claim goes out, along with the name, the age and the billing address. Billing last year's plan invites a denial for coverage that has ended, an oral group number adds an error, and learning it from the remittance advice means the denial already happened.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient identification and tube labeling)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: To save time, a phlebotomist prints and sticks labels on all the tubes at the nursing station before entering the patient's room. What is wrong with this practice?
opciones: Tube identification and labeling must be done in the presence of the patient to avoid misidentification
Labels printed in advance lose their adhesive and can peel off during centrifugation or refrigeration
Tubes must be labeled only after the draw is complete, and the label must be applied later at the accessioning desk
Pre-printed labels are acceptable only when the requisition is placed outside the transport bag
preguntas.explicacion: Both identifying the tube and applying its label are done with the patient present, so that the tube cannot be matched to the wrong person; before the draw the patient's identification data and the tube labels are double-checked against each other. Labeling away from the patient, whether before at the station or later at the accessioning desk, breaks that link. The transport bag pocket is a separate rule about the requisition, not about when to label.

preguntas.subtema: Conditioning an authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.b · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient refuses to sign an authorization sending her records to her employer. May the practice make her appointment conditional on signing it?
opciones: No, treatment may not be conditioned on an authorization outside narrow exceptions
No, unless the practice notes the refusal in the record and offers a later date
Yes, a practice may set the terms on which it accepts a patient for treatment
Yes, where the employer is the source of the coverage that pays for the visit
preguntas.explicacion: Conditioning treatment, payment, enrollment in a plan or eligibility for benefits on the individual signing an authorization is forbidden to a covered entity. The exceptions are narrow: research-related treatment, a plan's own enrollment or underwriting determinations, and care provided solely in order to create information for a third party. The form itself has to state which case applies.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Primary care; and MedlinePlus, Choosing a primary care provider
preguntas.subtema: General vs specialty care · CCMA 1A k7 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks which professionals may serve as her primary care provider. What is accurate?
opciones: Doctors, nurses, physician assistants and also nurse practitioners may serve
Only doctors of medicine and doctors of osteopathic medicine may serve
Only physicians who completed a family practice residency may serve
Any licensed health worker, a pharmacist or a dietitian included, may serve as one
preguntas.explicacion: Doctors, nurses, physician assistants and also nurse practitioners all count as primary care providers. The primary care provider is the one a patient turns to first for checkups and for health problems, and who helps manage her health overall. Family practitioners, pediatricians, geriatricians, internists and obstetrician-gynecologists are among the physician types filling that role.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Setting newborns aside, where inside the hospital did the seven-year study find the highest proportion of hemolysed serum?
opciones: The emergency department, at 6.81 %, ahead of intensive care at 5.93 %
Intensive care, at 6.81 %, ahead of the emergency department at 5.93 % of sera
The inpatient wards, whose draws are done with a straight needle
The outpatient clinics, whose samples travel longest before separation
preguntas.explicacion: Across 1,882,721 serum samples the general patient population sat at 3.33 %, but the two areas where patients are sickest ran higher: 6.81 % in the emergency department, with 1.73 % of tests rejected, and 5.93 % in intensive care, with 0.97 % rejected. The authors read that gap as an argument for training the staff who collect in those areas.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, the PASS rule
preguntas.subtema: PASS · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45
preguntas.pregunta: What does the first S in PASS stand for when operating a portable fire extinguisher?
opciones: Squeeze the trigger, holding the extinguisher upright
Sweep the nozzle from side to side across the flames
Stand back 75 feet, the maximum travel distance
Shut the door behind you before discharging
preguntas.explicacion: PASS sums up how an extinguisher is worked: pull the pin, aim the nozzle at the base of the fire, then, with the extinguisher held upright, squeeze the trigger, and sweep from side to side so the spray covers the fire. Sweeping is the second S. Seventy-five feet is the maximum travel distance to a Class A extinguisher under 29 CFR 1910.157, not a stand-off distance, and shutting the door is the confine step of RACE, done before anyone tries to put the fire out.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Tips for communicating with older patients; and StatPearls, "Therapeutic Communication", Table (Specific Techniques)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B 2D k15 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 · CMA F.1.c(7)(a) / 2027 F.1.d(7)(b) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist greets an 80-year-old with 'Hi sweetie, I'm here for your blood.' What should change in that greeting?
opciones: Use a formal form of address such as Mr. or Ms., and give your own name and role
Use the patient's first name to build rapport, then state your job title
Speak louder and more slowly, because most older adults have hearing loss
Address the accompanying family member first, to save the patient effort
preguntas.explicacion: Formal terms of address are the default with older patients, and familiar words like 'dear' can be read as disrespect; staff may also ask how the patient prefers to be addressed. The technique table pairs that with introducing oneself by first and last name. Raising the voice distorts language sounds and can sound like anger, and remarks should not be aimed only at the companion.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(3)(ii)(A) and (C), Post-exposure Evaluation and Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Source individual testing · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After a needlestick, what does the standard say about testing the source patient's blood?
opciones: Test it as soon as feasible for HBV and HIV once consent is obtained, unless consent is not legally required
Test it only if the exposed employee first agrees to have his or her own baseline blood drawn
Test it without asking, because a patient's blood already drawn belongs to the laboratory
Do not test it; the standard bases follow-up on the employee's serology and vaccination status alone
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(3)(ii) makes identification and documentation of the source individual part of the follow-up unless it is infeasible or barred by state or local law. Under (f)(3)(ii)(A) the source's blood is tested for HBV and HIV infectivity as soon as feasible after consent; if consent is refused, the employer documents that legally required consent could not be obtained, and where the law does not require consent, available blood is tested and the results recorded. Results go to the exposed employee together with the rules on disclosing the source's identity and status.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.1
preguntas.subtema: Warm-site backup · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A large organization that treats patients around the clock keeps a warm-site backup that can run the whole record system. What does the guidance expect of it?
opciones: Current patient data, running within eight hours, and a test at least every quarter
Current patient data, running within eight hours, and a test at least every year
Current patient data, running within one hour, and a test at least every quarter
A weekly copy of patient data, running within eight hours, and a yearly test
preguntas.explicacion: The example given is a remote backup facility, more than fifty miles away and more than twenty miles from the coast, holding current patient data and able to be brought up in less than eight hours, with the backup computer system tested at least quarterly. A single point of failure is what the practice exists to remove.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A light blue sodium citrate tube has just been filled for a PT/INR. How should it be mixed?
opciones: Inverted gently 3 to 6 times immediately after the draw
Inverted gently 8 to 10 times immediately after the draw
Shaken vigorously for a few seconds so the anticoagulant mixes
Left upright for 10 to 15 minutes before any mixing
preguntas.explicacion: Gentle mixing means inverting the citrate tube 3 to 6 times right after the sample enters the tube; vigorous shaking can froth or hemolyse the sample and distort coagulation results. Eight to ten inversions is the figure for blood culture bottles, and the 10 to 15 minute rest is the clotting time for plain red tubes before centrifugation.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, benign
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A pathology report calls a growth benign. What does that tell the patient?
opciones: It may keep growing, but it does not spread to other parts of the body
It has stopped growing, and it does not spread to other parts of the body
It is growing slowly, and it spreads only through the lymph system
It is not growing at all, and it will disappear without any treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Benign means not cancer. A benign tumor can still get larger, and its size may cause trouble by itself, but it does not invade nearby tissue or travel elsewhere. The opposite term is malignant: those cells grow in an uncontrolled way, invade nearby tissue and spread through the blood and lymph system.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - infant", First Aid; and StatPearls, "Breast Examination Techniques" (NBK459179)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: An infant is found unresponsive and not breathing. How are chest compressions delivered?
opciones: With the two thumbs side by side over the sternum, below the nipple line
With the heel of one hand over the lower half of the sternum, as in a child
With two fingers over the upper third of the sternum, above the nipples
With both hands wrapped around the chest, squeezing from front and back
preguntas.explicacion: The rescuer's hands encircle the infant's chest and both thumbs press together on the sternum below the nipple line, to a depth of about 1½ inches (4 cm) at 100 to 120 per minute. Two fingers on the sternum just under the nipple line is the other accepted hand position. The heel of one hand is what a child of 1 year to puberty gets.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Nursing Rights of Medication Administration", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k22 · CMA I.D.2.a · RMA III.G.2.g · NCMA 1.5
preguntas.pregunta: An order says a dose is due at a set hour. How far from that hour should the dose be given?
opciones: Within about half an hour, since a wider gap can alter the drug's bioavailability
Within about six hours, the widest interval an around-the-clock order would use
Within about four hours, the window written into a typical order given as needed
At any point in the shift, as long as the true time is charted in the record
preguntas.explicacion: The right time means administering the medication as close as possible to the hour the prescriber intended, and the guiding principle is not to stray from it by more than about half an hour, because a longer gap can shift bioavailability and other mechanisms. Drugs given by infusion must also run at the ordered rate. Four to six hours is the window inside an as-needed order, not a tolerance for timing.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Mean Arterial Pressure
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: If the mean arterial pressure stays below 60 mm Hg for an extended time, what is the result?
opciones: Ischemia, too little blood flow, usually with hypoxia
Hypervolemia, too much fluid retained by the kidneys
Hypertension, from an excess of endothelin release
Polycythemia, from a rise in the output of EPO
preguntas.explicacion: When MAP falls below 60 mm Hg for long, pressure is no longer enough to push blood through the tissues; the result is ischemia, insufficient blood flow, commonly accompanied by hypoxia, inadequate tissue oxygenation, to which neurons are especially sensitive. Hypervolemia and hypertension are excesses of volume and pressure, and polycythemia is an overproduction of red cells, a different condition.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", sections Structure and Function and Common Pathway
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: The superficial veins of the arm drain the skin and the fascia beneath it, while the deep veins drain the muscles and the bones. Which vessels carry blood from one system into the other?
opciones: The perforating veins, which drain into the deep veins
The venae comitantes, which drain into the dorsal arch
The median cubital vein, which drains into the palmar arch
The cephalic and basilic, which drain into the radial veins
preguntas.explicacion: The two systems are joined by perforating veins, and those run into the deep veins all along the limb. The venae comitantes are the paired veins that accompany the ulnar and radial arteries; the median cubital joins the cephalic to the basilic at the elbow; and those two channels themselves end up higher in the arm, in the axillary or the subclavian.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Out-of-pocket maximum/limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5C · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What is the out-of-pocket maximum of a health plan?
opciones: The yearly cap on what the patient pays for covered in-network care; past it, the plan pays 100%
The most the patient pays per visit for covered services; the plan pays 100% of the rest
The most the patient pays in a plan year including premiums and out-of-network care
The 2026 Marketplace cap, $10,600 per individual, which applies only to premiums
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov describes the out-of-pocket maximum, or limit, as the ceiling on what the patient spends on covered services in a plan year, not per visit. Once her deductible, her copayments and her coinsurance for care inside the network add up to that figure, the plan covers 100% of covered benefits for the rest of the year. The glossary lists what does not count toward it: monthly premiums, out-of-network care, services the plan does not cover, and charges above the allowed amount. The $10,600 figure is the 2026 Marketplace ceiling for an individual, and it caps cost sharing, never premiums.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: Post-visit summary · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient worries she will forget what was said during a video visit. Which step does the patient guidance suggest to her?
opciones: Asking the clinician afterwards to send her a summary or notes of the appointment
Recording the appointment on her own telephone so she can play it back later
Asking the clinician for a direct mobile number she can use with any question later
Asking for the same appointment to be repeated in the office later that week
preguntas.explicacion: Feeling confident in a telehealth visit includes learning how it works, taking her time, choosing a clinician who listens, asking for anything unclear to be explained, and getting a summary: she is told to ask the clinician to send a summary or notes after the visit, which can include answers to the questions she raised. Writing a list beforehand is suggested for the same reason.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "OSHA Fire Safety", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Fire triangle · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which three components must be present for a fire to ignite?
opciones: A fuel, an oxidizer like oxygen, and an ignition source
A fuel, a flammable liquid, and a compressed gas
Heat, smoke, and an electrical current from a wall outlet
Oxygen, nitrous oxide, and an electrocautery device
preguntas.explicacion: Three components are needed: a fuel source such as linens, flammable liquids or tissue; an oxidizer such as oxygen or nitrous oxide, which greatly increases combustibility; and an ignition source such as an open flame, electrostatic discharge, electrocautery, lasers or any energized device. The operating room is a high-risk setting because all three are usually present at once. Oxygen and nitrous oxide are both oxidizers and electrocautery is an ignition source, so that combination lacks a fuel; smoke is a product of fire, not a component.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Gait Belts
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a · CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA 2A.5
preguntas.pregunta: A gait belt is about to be put on a patient who is being helped to stand. How is it applied?
opciones: Around the waist over the clothing or gown, fastened with a buckle
Around the waist against the bare skin, fastened with a buckle
Around the chest over the clothing or gown, fastened with a buckle
Around the hips against the bare skin, tied rather than buckled
preguntas.explicacion: The gait belt is a two-inch-wide belt, with or without handles, that goes around the patient's waist and buckles shut. It is applied on top of clothing or a gown, which protects the patient's skin. Belts of this kind are used for standing, walking and moving from bed to chair.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The note mentions a condition treated years ago that no longer exists but still shapes today's treatment. How is it handled?
opciones: It is not coded as current, and a history code may be added as secondary
It is coded as current, because the note for this visit still mentions it
It is coded first, since it explains the treatment chosen for her today
It is left out entirely, since a condition that has resolved is never coded
preguntas.explicacion: Coders report the conditions that coexist at the time of the visit and that require or affect care. Conditions previously treated that no longer exist are not coded as current. Personal and family history categories may still be used as secondary codes where that history bears on the care given today or steers the treatment.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime paper forms · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: How much paper capacity does the SAFER contingency practice expect each patient care area to hold for a downtime?
opciones: Enough forms to care for its patients for at least eight hours
Enough forms to care for its patients for at least three days
Enough forms to care for its patients for at least thirty days
Enough forms to care for one shift of scheduled visits only
preguntas.explicacion: The recommended practice is to keep paper forms on hand that can stand in for the EHR's key functions while it is down, since clinical and administrative operations have to carry on. The implementation guidance fixes the stock: enough in each patient care area to cover its patients for eight hours at least, forms for entering orders and for documenting medications, laboratory and radiology tests included.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pulse Oximetry
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k51 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient using a home oximeter reads 87%. What is the instruction?
opciones: Seek immediate medical attention: 88% or lower calls for emergency care
Call the provider during office hours, as 92% or lower is the reporting level
Repeat the reading in the morning, since a single value is not acted upon
Change the sensor to the other hand and act only if the value stays under 80%
preguntas.explicacion: Two thresholds are given for home monitoring: at 92% or lower the provider is contacted, and at 88% or lower the patient seeks immediate attention. A reading of 87% is in the second group. Bluish lips or nails, trouble breathing, chest tightness and a fast heart rate are the signs that go with a low value.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A 6-month-old is crying and squirming while you try to count the pulse. Which approach suits the arteries of a child that age?
opciones: Use the pads of two fingers with gentle pressure, and settle the child first
Press until the beat disappears and then ease off slowly to pick it up again
Press hard with a single fingertip, since small arteries sit deep in the tissue
Count during the crying, since crying steadies the rate and makes it easier
preguntas.explicacion: A young child's arteries are smaller and closer to the surface than an adult's, so they compress easily and are harder to find. The pads of the index and middle fingers keep the examiner's own pulse out of the count and apply pressure gentle enough not to close the vessel. Crying and movement change the rate, so a calm child comes before the count.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (gloves and tourniquet)
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet application · CPT D3 3E k60 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Why is it suggested to put on gloves BEFORE applying the tourniquet?
opciones: To avoid prolonging the time the tourniquet stays on
To keep the tourniquet free of MRSA from the phlebotomist's hands
To ensure the site is not touched after disinfection
To make the veins dilate before the tourniquet is placed
preguntas.explicacion: Wearing gloves before the tourniquet goes on may be advised so that the band is not left on too long; gloving afterwards adds seconds while the band is already constricting the arm. MRSA on tourniquets is a separate concern the WHO raises, and not touching the cleaned site is the WHO's Step 5 rule; neither is the reason given for the sequence.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Introduction and Please sit down and make yourself comfortable
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L 2M k40 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k126 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: How does the WHO script close the run of pre-draw questions before the procedure starts?
opciones: By asking how the patient feels now and to report discomfort at once
By asking the patient to sign the laboratory form as a record of consent
By reading out the tests once more and naming the ordering clinician
By checking the wristband a second time against the laboratory form
preguntas.explicacion: After the questions on earlier draws, fear of needles, allergies, fainting and recent food or drink, the script asks how the patient is feeling at that moment. It then closes by proposing to start and asking the patient to say at once if they feel unwell or uncomfortable. The tests and the clinician who ordered them were named in the opening part.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Appointment types · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5B k173 · CMA III.H.1.a-b · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Implementing open access includes simplifying the appointment types. Which three does the improvement guide recommend a practice keep?
opciones: Personal with her own physician, team with another clinician, and unestablished
Routine, urgent and follow-up, each one holding its own block of the morning
New patient, established patient and annual wellness, each of a different length
Short, long and double, where the long one is worth about two of the short ones
preguntas.explicacion: One recommended tactic is to strip out complexity by holding the practice to three types: personal, where the patient sees her own physician; team, where she is seen by another clinician on the team; and unestablished, for patients who do not yet have a physician. Appointment length is handled apart from that, as short or long, a long visit counting for roughly two short ones.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "OSHA Fire Safety", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.c · 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: A small fire starts in a clinic storeroom. Which order do the letters of RACE set out?
opciones: Rescue those at risk, pull the alarm, confine the fire, then extinguish
Pull the alarm, rescue those at risk, extinguish the fire, then confine
Rescue those at risk, confine the fire, extinguish it, then pull the alarm
Confine the fire, pull the alarm, rescue those at risk, then extinguish
preguntas.explicacion: Rescue comes first, above all where patients cannot move on their own; then the alarm is pulled to warn the rest of the building, the fire is confined to one place, and last it is put out. The extinguisher itself is worked by pulling the pin, aiming at the base of the flames, squeezing the handle and sweeping side to side.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has a large bruise with swelling over the median cubital vein from a draw two days ago. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Choose another site; a hematoma contraindicates venipuncture there
Draw through the bruise, since the vein beneath it has already been located
Draw just above the bruise after applying ice for 15 minutes
Draw below the bruise with a 23 G butterfly to reduce trauma
preguntas.explicacion: The presence of a hematoma, the pooling of blood under the skin, is among the local reasons not to puncture a site, together with residual scar tissue and venous fibrosis felt on palpation.
