Ice for up to 15 minutes each hour is first aid for a bruise, not a preparation for drawing through it, and the chapter gives no 'above or below' exception.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Does your provider accept Medicare as full payment?
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A physician has opted out of Medicare and asks the patient to sign a private contract. What follows for her?
opciones: Medicare pays nothing for his services except in emergencies, and he stays out two years
Medicare pays its share as usual once she files her own claim for those services
Medicare pays the approved amount less the fifteen percent limiting charge for him
Medicare pays none of it for one year, after which the physician returns automatically
preguntas.explicacion: Providers who do not want to work with the program may opt out, and Medicare will not pay for what they furnish except in an emergency. Opting out lasts a minimum of two years, and at each two-year point the provider may stay out, become non-participating, or accept assignment. The patient may have to pay up front or agree a payment plan under the private contract.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet time · CPT D3 3E k60 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A PT and PTT are being collected. What is the guidance on tourniquet time for these tests?
opciones: Keep it as short as possible, to avoid artifacts such as hemolysis
Leave it on until the citrate tube is full, so the 9:1 ratio is reached
Apply it for at least one minute, so the vein is engorged before the puncture
Release it before the needle enters, since stasis activates clotting factors
preguntas.explicacion: Coagulation sampling calls for an atraumatic venipuncture performed as soon as possible, with tourniquet time minimized during collection, to avoid artifacts in coagulation results such as hemolysis. The 9:1 ratio depends on the fill volume, not on the tourniquet; no minimum time is prescribed; and releasing it before the needle enters is not what any of the sources describe.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Red
preguntas.subtema: Specimen preparation, serum · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A plain red top tube has just been filled. How long is the blood usually allowed to clot before it is centrifuged?
opciones: About 10 to 15 minutes, though some specimens take up to 60 minutes
About 3 to 6 minutes, the same interval used to invert the citrate tube
About 30 seconds, the time the alcohol needs to dry on the skin
At least two to three hours, so the clot separates from the serum
preguntas.explicacion: A red tube contains no additive; contact with the tube surface activates the coagulation cascade, and the blood is left to clot for 10 to 15 minutes before centrifugation; clotting time varies and can reach almost an hour. Three to six is the number of citrate inversions, 30 seconds is the alcohol drying time, and hours are not mentioned.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomical Terminology, Planes of the Body
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.f (2027 I.C.6.e) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: An imaging study is cut along a plane that separates the body into right and left portions. Which plane is it?
opciones: The sagittal plane, cut vertically from the front through to the back
The coronal plane, cut vertically from one side across to the other
The transverse plane, cut horizontally straight through the body
The oblique plane, cut at an angle across the other three
preguntas.explicacion: There are three planes in common use. Sagittal is vertical and splits right from left; coronal, also called frontal, is vertical and splits front from back; transverse, also called axial, is horizontal and splits upper from lower. The oblique plane crosses the body at an angle to all three.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Risk of Infection After a Needlestick Injury: HBV and Summary
preguntas.subtema: HBV prophylaxis works · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: For a susceptible worker exposed to hepatitis B, how well does immune globulin plus starting the vaccine work?
opciones: More than 90% effective at preventing infection
About 50% effective at preventing the infection
About 60% effective, like a booster dose alone
Around 30% effective, as the vaccine alone is
preguntas.explicacion: Hepatitis B is the most transmissible of the three: for a susceptible worker the reported range is 6 to 30 percent after a single needlestick from an infected patient. It is also the one with the best answer: hepatitis B immune globulin together with the start of the vaccine series is more than 90 percent effective at preventing infection. Workers with antibodies from vaccination or past infection are not at risk in the first place. Neither HCV nor HIV has anything comparable.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When can I sign up for Medicare?; and Medicare costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient signed up for Part B three years after she was first eligible. How long will the late enrollment penalty last?
opciones: For as long as she holds Part B, and the longer the wait the larger it grows
For three years, one year of penalty for each year that she delayed signing up
Until the eight-month special enrollment period that follows her retirement
Until she buys a Medigap policy, which takes the penalty amount over from her
preguntas.explicacion: Someone who does not sign up for Part B when first eligible has to wait to enroll and goes months without coverage, and may pay a monthly penalty for as long as she has Part B, with the penalty rising the longer the delay ran. A similar penalty exists for Part A when it has to be bought and is not taken at the first opportunity.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Limited English Proficiency (LEP), Your Right to Language Assistance Services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 7A k214 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic tells a patient that a telephone interpreter costs $30 unless she brings a relative. Per HHS OCR?
opciones: Not allowed: language access services must be provided free of charge
Allowed, if the fee is listed in the posted notice of nondiscrimination
Allowed, because interpreters are required only in emergency departments
Allowed, if the relative is an adult who agrees to interpret for her
preguntas.explicacion: A program funded by HHS, or covered by the civil rights laws it enforces, has to provide language access services free of charge, and a visit to a doctor is among the examples listed. What Section 1557 requires is a notice saying that language assistance can be had, not a fee schedule, and AHRQ Tool 9 adds that a relative is no acceptable substitute for a qualified interpreter.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, section Considerations
preguntas.subtema: Terminology: haematoma and bruise · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Bruises are described in three types. Which is the most severe and painful?
opciones: The periosteal bruise, which involves the bone
The subcutaneous bruise, which is under the skin
The intramuscular bruise, in the belly of a muscle
The dermal bruise, which sits in the skin itself
preguntas.explicacion: Bruises are grouped as subcutaneous, under the skin; intramuscular, in the belly of the muscle underneath; and periosteal, a bone bruise. The bone bruise is the most severe and the most painful of the three, and bruises in general can last from days to months.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 9
preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist has just finished a draw. At which two moments is the label checked against the request form?
opciones: Right after the draw, and again before the tubes are dispatched
Right after the draw, and again when the results are reported back
Before the needle goes in, and again when the patient has left the room
Only once, when the tubes are put into the transport bag with the form
preguntas.explicacion: The closing steps ask the worker to check the label and the form for accuracy once the sharp has been discarded, and then to look over the labels on the tubes and the forms once more before dispatch. Labeling itself is done with the patient present, so that a tube is never matched to the wrong name.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, What is fasting for a blood test? and Can I drink anything besides water during a fast?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient phones on the morning of a fasting test to ask whether coffee counts. When should that question have been raised?
opciones: At least a full day before the test, so there is time to prepare
At least a week before, when the requisition is first written
On arrival at the draw station, where the instructions are posted
Only if the patient has already broken the fast by mistake
preguntas.explicacion: A patient is handed a copy of the instructions when a fast is ordered, and any question those instructions do not answer goes to the provider a full day ahead at least, leaving time to prepare properly. Coffee is not allowed: juice, soda and other drinks reach the bloodstream and shift the results. Only plain water passes.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth privacy · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 4B k55 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: An upcoming telehealth visit will cover a sensitive topic. What extra step does the guidance suggest?
opciones: Helping the patient find a private spot and agreeing what a companion may hear
Moving the appointment to the office, since sensitive topics rule telehealth out
Recording the visit so that the discussion can be reviewed by a second clinician
Asking the patient to bring a relative, who can confirm what was discussed later
preguntas.explicacion: For appointments touching sensitive subjects the guidance suggests discussing whether the patient can find a private place, and offering tips for one at home, in a car or at a friend's house. It also covers other communication options such as e-mail, text or the platform's chat feature where personal safety may be an issue, and says to establish with an interpreter or caregiver present what the patient is comfortable letting them hear, and whether a release is needed.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, How to Obtain a CLIA Certificate of Waiver (2019): Will my laboratory receive a CMS survey?; CDC, To Test or Not to Test? (2024), Regulatory Requirements
preguntas.subtema: No routine surveys, complaint surveys yes · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1.a.v · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: Is a site that performs only waived tests inspected by CMS or the state agency?
opciones: Not routinely, but it may receive an unannounced survey if a complaint is filed
Yes, on the same two-year survey cycle as Certificate of Compliance laboratories
Never; the Certificate of Waiver exempts the site from any on-site visit
Only during the first year, to verify the manufacturer's instructions are on file
preguntas.explicacion: Certificate of Waiver and PPM sites are not subject to routine surveys; biennial surveys are for COC and COA laboratories. A waived site must still permit announced or unannounced inspections, and CMS does visit when a complaint is received, to check whether the site runs tests its certificate does not permit, when inaccurate testing could harm patients, or to gather information about practices at waived sites.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Fecal Occult Blood Test (FOBT), Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?; and StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: NSAIDs and FOBT · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.2 · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · RMA III.C.4.a.iv · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Why are aspirin and NSAIDs such as ibuprofen listed among the medicines that can interfere with a fecal occult blood test?
opciones: They can irritate the stomach and cause bleeding, giving a positive result not due to a tumor
They reduce the oxidation of the guaiac reagent, giving a false-negative result
They contain plant peroxidases that react with the developer, like horseradish
They color the stool black, which hides the blue reaction on the card
preguntas.explicacion: Aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen, corticosteroids and some other drugs irritate the gastric lining and cause real blood loss, so the card turns positive for a reason unrelated to a colorectal lesion. A patient who takes aspirin for the heart should not stop it without talking to the provider; acetaminophen may be permitted instead. Blocking the oxidation is the vitamin C effect, and plant peroxidases come from raw vegetables.

preguntas.subtema: Media re-use · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: The office wants to hand a set of flash drives that once held claim files to another department. Which Security Rule specification governs that?
opciones: Media re-use, which has the information taken off the drive before it is handed on
Disposal, which governs the final disposition of the hardware once it leaves service
Accountability, which keeps a record of who moved the hardware and where it went
Data backup and storage, which copies the information before equipment is moved
preguntas.explicacion: Device and media controls carry four specifications. Disposal deals with hardware at the end of its life; the one that fits a drive still in service and about to be passed to someone else is media re-use, and like disposal it is required, not addressable. Both aim at the same risk: information left behind on hardware that changes hands.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, section Home Care
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 1L 1M k37 k38 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.B.9.l / 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which check comes first when someone has just fainted in the drawing room?
opciones: The airway and the breathing
The pulse in the punctured arm
The puncture site for bleeding
The label on the tube just filled
preguntas.explicacion: The first of the immediate steps is to check the person's airway and breathing, calling emergency help and starting rescue breathing and resuscitation if they are needed. Loosening tight clothing, raising the feet and keeping the person down come after that.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k87 · PBT III.C · CCMA 3E11 k140 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.d
preguntas.pregunta: A small laboratory without an ultracentrifuge keeps receiving milky sera and cannot send them out. Which alternative does the published evidence support?
opciones: High-speed spinning in a micro-centrifuge, validated for the analytes involved
Diluting the serum with saline before running the affected chemistry analytes
Redrawing after a twelve-hour fast, since lipemia always comes from the meal
Reporting the lipemic figures with a comment, since the bias stays within limits
preguntas.explicacion: Ultracentrifugation clears lipemic interference, but the instrument sits only in highly specialized laboratories. A comparison of high-speed centrifugation in a micro-centrifuge against an ultracentrifuge found the cheaper route suitable, on the analyser tested, for creatinine, sodium, lactate dehydrogenase, urate, total protein, magnesium, cholesterol and triglyceride.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.2 Cardiac Muscle and Electrical Activity, Sinoatrial (SA) Node; Atrioventricular (AV) Node; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Physiology of the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structure is the heart's pacemaker, where is it, and how often does it fire on its own?
opciones: The SA node, in the upper posterior wall of the right atrium; 70 to 80 per minute
The AV node, in the lower right atrium within the septum; 70 to 80 per minute
The SA node, in the upper wall of the left atrium; about 100 per minute
The bundle of His, in the interventricular septum; up to 220 per minute
preguntas.explicacion: The sinoatrial node lies high and toward the back in the wall of the right atrium, close to where the superior vena cava opens, and it is the pacemaker because nothing else depolarizes as fast; left to itself it fires 70 to 80 times a minute. The atrioventricular node sits lower in the right atrium and passes at most about 220 impulses a minute, which fixes the usual ceiling for heart rate.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Decontamination, Sterilize
preguntas.subtema: Decontamination vs sterilization · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.b / 2027 I.B.4.b · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: Under the standard, the term decontamination means which of the following?
opciones: Using physical or chemical means to make a surface safe to handle, use or dispose of
Killing every form of microbial life, endospores of bacteria included
Treating all blood and certain body fluids as if known to be infectious
Altering the way a task is performed so that exposure becomes less likely
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) defines decontamination as treating a surface or an item, physically or chemically, so that the bloodborne pathogens on it are removed, inactivated or destroyed to the point of no longer transmitting infection, leaving the item safe to handle, use or throw away. Killing every form of microbial life, endospores included, is the neighbouring definition of sterilize; handling all blood as infectious is Universal Precautions; and altering the way a task is done is a work practice control.

preguntas.subtema: Signature by a representative · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's son signs the release form as her personal representative. What must the form carry in addition to his signature and the date?
opciones: A description of the authority under which he acts for her
A copy of the identification he presented at the front desk
A statement that she was unable to sign the form for herself
A second signature from a member of the practice's workforce
preguntas.explicacion: The core element covering the signature says that where a personal representative signs, the form must also describe that person's authority to act for the individual. The other core elements do not change: the information, who discloses it, who receives it, the purpose and an expiration date or event all remain.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A blood bank cross-match is ordered. Which two tubes in the WHO table list cross-match among their uses?
opciones: The red clot activator tube and the purple EDTA tube
The serum separator tube and the light green PST
The light blue citrate tube and the light gray fluoride tube
The pale yellow ACD tube and the blood culture bottle
preguntas.explicacion: In Table 2.3, blood bank (cross-match) appears in the uses column of two rows: the red top with clot activator, alongside chemistries, immunology and serology, and the purple EDTA tube, alongside hematology. The serum separator and PST tubes are listed for chemistries, the citrate and fluoride tubes for coagulation and glucose, and the ACD tube for HLA typing, paternity and DNA studies.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Introduction; and StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: What is claimed for double gloving in relation to a sharps injury?
opciones: It lowers the volume of blood transferred, but the puncture risk remains
It lowers the puncture risk, but the volume of blood transferred remains
It removes both the puncture risk and the volume of blood transferred
It changes neither, and is recommended only for surgical procedures
preguntas.explicacion: Wearing two pairs of gloves may reduce the amount of blood passed on during a sharps injury, but it does not stop the needle from puncturing the skin. Gloves are credited with the same limited benefit in a needle-stick: less blood transmitted, not an injury prevented.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Skin preparation
preguntas.subtema: Cotton and alcohol · CPT D1 1K k10 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.B.5 / 2027 I.B.4 · RMA III.A.3.b · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A colleague keeps a jar of cotton balls soaking in alcohol and tears the cotton by hand as she goes. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Cotton pre-torn by bare hands is already contaminated, and bacteria grow in it
Alcohol evaporates from an open jar and is too weak to prepare the skin
Cotton fibers stick to the puncture site and cause the wound to keep oozing
Alcohol stored in an open jar has to be discarded at the end of the shift
preguntas.explicacion: Skin preparation calls for 70 percent alcohol applied with a single-use swab or a clean cotton-wool ball. Cotton torn ahead of time with bare fingers is already contaminated, and bacteria multiply in it as the hours pass, so jars of cotton left soaking in alcohol are not to be kept; the cotton is moistened right at the moment of use, and the main container must not be contaminated while doing it. For a blood donation the recommended preparation is a single step of 2 percent chlorhexidine in 70 percent isopropyl alcohol, left to air dry.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Orthostatic Hypotension", Etiology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k48 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A drop in pressure appears only 6 minutes after the patient has stood up. How is it classified?
opciones: Delayed orthostatic hypotension, which by definition appears after 3 minutes
Classic orthostatic hypotension, which appears within 3 minutes of standing
Initial orthostatic hypotension, which lasts under 15 seconds after standing
Postprandial hypotension, which appears within 2 hours of a large meal
preguntas.explicacion: The types are separated by timing: initial lasts less than 15 seconds after the change of posture, classic appears within three minutes, and delayed appears after three minutes. Postprandial hypotension is a different entity, a systolic fall of at least 20 mm Hg within two hours of eating.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Financial Eligibility
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Whose Medicaid income is worked out by the SSI methodologies rather than by the MAGI rules?
opciones: An applicant who is sixty-five or older, or who is blind or has a disability
An applicant who is pregnant and is applying for coverage for the first time
An applicant who is the parent of a child already enrolled in the program
An applicant who is an adult in a state that widened coverage to low earners
preguntas.explicacion: The Affordable Care Act put Modified Adjusted Gross Income at the center of financial eligibility for Medicaid, for CHIP and for Marketplace help, and it governs most adults, most parents, most pregnant women and most children. Certain people are exempt: eligibility resting on being sixty-five or over, on blindness or on disability is generally decided with the income methods of the SSI program.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xi), Engineering and Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Minimizing splashes · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How does the standard say every procedure involving blood must be carried out?
opciones: In a way that keeps splashes, sprays, spatter and droplets to a minimum
Inside a certified biological safety cabinet, never on the open bench
With a mask and face shield worn for every procedure regardless of splash risk
Behind a protective covering that is replaced at the end of every shift
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xi) requires every procedure with blood or OPIM to be carried out so that splashing, spraying, spatter and the making of droplets are kept to a minimum. Biological safety cabinets become mandatory under (e)(2)(ii)(E) only where HIV or HBV research, or production work with those viruses, is going on. A mask with eye protection is required by (d)(3)(x) when splashes may be generated and facial contamination is anticipated, not for every task, and the protective coverings of (d)(4)(ii)(B) are an option for surfaces, not a way of performing a procedure.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Rh Blood Groups; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia 003345 Blood typing, How the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A blood type is reported as A positive. What does the 'positive' refer to, and what share of Americans share that status?
opciones: The Rh D antigen is on the red cells; about 85 percent
The Rh D antigen is on the red cells; about 50 percent
Anti-D antibodies are in the plasma; about 85 percent
The A antigen is on the red cells; about 15 percent
preguntas.explicacion: The Rh group is separate from ABO, and only one Rh antigen, D, matters clinically; those who carry it, about 85 percent of Americans, are Rh positive, and the word positive or negative is added to the ABO letter. Anti-D antibodies are not preformed; they appear only in Rh negative people after sensitization. The lab reports the result simply as Rh+ or Rh−.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Cuts and puncture wounds", When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k79 · CMA I.B.9.m · 2027 I.B.8.m · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: Which sign in a healing wound points to infection?
opciones: A red streak spreading from the wound, with pus-like drainage and fever
A thin scab that itches and edges that have pulled slightly together
Bruising around the wound that is turning from purple to yellow
Clear fluid on the dressing during the first day, with no odor at all
preguntas.explicacion: Warmth and redness in the area, throbbing pain, swelling, fever, a red streak running away from the wound, or drainage that looks like pus are the signs that send the patient back to the provider. They are what the assistant looks for at a dressing change, along with a wound that is large or deep even when it is no longer bleeding much.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 1
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is stocking the tray for the morning. How should the laboratory sample tubes be kept before use?
opciones: Dry and standing upright in a rack
Damp and lying flat inside the tray
Chilled and upright in a small cooler
Dry and lying flat under the request forms
preguntas.explicacion: The list of equipment assembled before a draw asks for a supply of sample tubes stored dry and upright in a rack. The rack itself stays near the worker and out of the patient's reach, so that it is not knocked over during the procedure.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6: Take blood
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural care · CPT D3 3Q k70 k74 · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E9 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: The needle has just been withdrawn. What does the WHO ask the patient to do, and what must the patient avoid?
opciones: Hold the gauze in place with the arm extended and raised, and not bend the arm
Bend the arm firmly over the gauze and keep it tightly bent for at least five minutes
Lower the arm below the heart so the puncture seals under gravity
Rub the site through the gauze for 30 seconds to disperse any pooled blood
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 says to withdraw the needle gently, apply gentle pressure with clean gauze or cotton wool, and ask the patient to hold it in place with the arm extended and raised; the patient is told not to bend the arm, since bending it brings on a hematoma. Lowering the arm and rubbing the site are not described anywhere in the guideline.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, surgical antisepsis; StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Surgical Hand Antisepsis
preguntas.subtema: Surgical hand antisepsis · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k104 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.b.i · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: A surgical hand scrub with an antimicrobial agent usually lasts how long?
opciones: About 2 to 6 minutes
About 15 to 20 seconds
About 10 to 15 minutes
About 30 to 60 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Surgical antisepsis is a scrub that usually lasts 2 to 6 minutes; the clinical literature adds that scrubs of 10 minutes or more give no extra benefit and irritate the skin. The scrub is done with hands above the elbows, jewelry removed, nails cleaned under running water and a sterile brush or sponge, followed by drying with a sterile towel before sterile gloves. Fifteen to twenty seconds is routine handwashing, not surgical antisepsis.

preguntas.fuente: MyPlate, USDA: Fruits — what counts as a cup
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which amount counts as one cup from the Fruit Group?
opciones: Half a cup of dried fruit
Half a cup of canned fruit
Two cups of 100% fruit juice
Half a cup of frozen fruit
preguntas.explicacion: A cup-equivalent of fruit is one cup of fresh, frozen or canned fruit, one cup of 100% juice, or half a cup of dried fruit, which is concentrated and therefore counts double. The guidance adds that at least half of the fruit eaten should be whole fruit rather than juice.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Besides treatment and surgery, for which of these is informed consent listed as required?
opciones: Blood and medication infusions, and anesthesia
Routine vital signs and a height measurement
Transport of specimens to a reference laboratory
Storage of leftover serum for one further week
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent is required for treatment, for dissemination of patient information, for the discussion of the HIPAA rules, for specific procedures, for surgery, for blood and medication infusions, and for anesthesia. It is a communication process between clinician and patient, not merely a signature on a document.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Exceptions
preguntas.subtema: Breach exceptions · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse opens the wrong chart by accident, in good faith and within her duties, and closes it without using anything. What is this?
opciones: One of the three exceptions to the definition of a breach
A breach that still requires notice to the patient within sixty days
A reportable security incident that must go to the Secretary each year
A disclosure that must go on the accounting of disclosures
preguntas.explicacion: Three situations sit outside the definition. First: an unintentional acquisition, access or use by a member of the workforce who was acting in good faith and inside the authority given to her. Second: an inadvertent disclosure between two people who are both authorized to reach PHI at the same entity or organized arrangement. In both, the information may not then be used or disclosed improperly. Third: a good faith belief that whoever received it would not have been able to retain it.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Pictograms (Figure 1 note)
preguntas.subtema: Required pictograms · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: The GHS uses nine hazard pictograms. How many does OSHA enforce, and which one is optional?
opciones: Eight; only the environmental pictogram is optional
Nine; none is optional under the 2012 revision
Seven; the environmental and the health hazard ones are optional
Eight; the flame pictogram is optional for laboratory reagents
preguntas.explicacion: OSHA adopted the GHS pictograms but enforces eight of the nine: the one for the environment is not required, since environmental hazards fall to other agencies, though a label preparer may add it as supplementary information, so workers may still see it. The health hazard and the flame are among the eight required whenever the classification calls for them. The names of the eight appear in a figure of the OSHA brief; the count and the exception are what the text states.

preguntas.subtema: Patient rights and restraint · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29
preguntas.pregunta: A restraint is ordered for a 14-year-old whose behavior is violent. How long may that order run before renewal?
opciones: Two hours
One hour
Four hours
Eight hours
preguntas.explicacion: Where restraint or seclusion is used to manage behavior that is violent or self-destructive, and unless state law is stricter, each order may be renewed for up to four hours for adults of 18 or more, two hours for children and adolescents from 9 to 17, and one hour for children under 9, for a total of 24 hours. After 24 hours the patient must be seen and assessed before a new order is written.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Common Pathway
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In the common pathway of coagulation, what is the job of thrombin?
opciones: Turns soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin
Turns inactive prothrombin into its active form
Cross-links and stabilizes the fibrin clot
Degrades the fibrin once the vessel has healed
preguntas.explicacion: The common pathway has three moves: once factor X is active, prothrombinase converts prothrombin (factor II) into thrombin; thrombin then converts fibrinogen (factor I) into insoluble fibrin strands; and factor XIII stabilizes the fibrin clot. Activating prothrombin is the job of prothrombinase, not of thrombin, and breaking fibrin down later is the work of plasmin.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.5 Circulatory Pathways, Veins Draining the Lower Limbs and Table 20.16
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53 foot) · PBT I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: On the top of the foot, which venous network collects blood from the digital veins?
opciones: The dorsal venous arch
The plantar venous arch
The great saphenous vein
The small saphenous vein
preguntas.explicacion: On the top of the foot the digital veins gather into the dorsal venous arch, which feeds the anterior and posterior tibial veins; the sole drains instead into the plantar veins and the plantar arch. The great saphenous climbs the inner leg and thigh to the femoral vein, and the small saphenous runs up the outside of the leg to the popliteal.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.2.1, Needle and syringe
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly and sterility · CPT D3 3A 3B k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: When preparing a needle and syringe, from which end does the WHO say each package should be opened?
opciones: The needle from the hub end, kept capped; the syringe from the plunger end, nozzle still protected
The needle from the tip end, with the cap removed; the syringe from the nozzle end, ready to attach
Both from the middle, so the two parts can be joined without touching either end
The needle from the hub end, cap removed; the syringe from the plunger end, nozzle exposed
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.2.1 opens the hypodermic needle from the hub end, the back of the needle, keeping it capped, and the syringe from the plunger end, keeping the nozzle protected in its packaging; the nozzle is then pushed firmly into the exposed hub of the still-capped needle, and the assembly is left in place until needed. Uncapping early or exposing the nozzle defeats the purpose of the sequence.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Assistive Devices
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a · CCMA 3B4 k65 · NCMA 2A.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has some muscle strength but cannot get from sitting to standing alone. Which device is made for that?
opciones: A sit-to-stand lift, for weight-bearing patients who lack the strength
A mechanical lift with a sling, for patients who cannot bear weight
A slider board, for moving a patient lying supine between surfaces
A gait belt with handles, for a patient who cannot bear weight at all
preguntas.explicacion: Sit-to-stand lifts are for patients who bear weight but cannot rise on their own strength; some are mechanized and some are not. The hydraulic lift with a sling is for the patient who cannot bear weight at all, and the slider board moves a patient who is lying flat from one surface to another.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Daily Value on the Nutrition and Supplement Facts Labels: Lows and highs of %DV
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 food labels · CMA I.A.6.g(4) · 2027 I.A.6.g(4) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on a sodium restriction reads 20% Daily Value for sodium on a label. How should he read that number?
opciones: That serving is high in sodium, since 20% or more counts as high
That serving is moderate in sodium, since high starts at 40%
That serving is low in sodium, since low means under 25% DV
That serving supplies a fifth of the sodium he is allowed each week
preguntas.explicacion: The general guide on the label puts 5% of the Daily Value or less at the low end and 20% or more at the high end, for any nutrient. So a serving at 20% is a high-sodium serving, and two servings would take him to 40% of the day's allowance. Daily Values are daily amounts, never weekly ones.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Evacuation Plans and Procedures eTool, Emergency Action Plan: Shelter-in-Place
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.a · 2027 I.B.7.a · CMAA 3 k45 · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: A tank car leaking chlorine derails behind the clinic and the authorities advise staying indoors. What does the office do?
opciones: Shelter in place in an interior room with no windows or few of them
Evacuate by the marked routes and gather at the outside assembly point
Send staff home in their own cars by the route furthest from the tracks
Move everyone to the room nearest the exit and keep the doors propped
preguntas.explicacion: When a chemical, biological or radiological release makes the outside air the greater danger, staying inside is safer than evacuating: an interior room, with no windows or few, is chosen and used as refuge. The signal that tells staff to shelter has to be easy to tell apart from the evacuation alarm, and staff are trained in both.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Wound Irrigation", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which assembly generates the pressure recommended for irrigating a laceration?
opciones: A 35 to 50 mL syringe with a 19-gauge catheter, giving 25 to 40 PSI
A 35 to 50 mL syringe with no catheter, poured gently over the wound
A 10 mL syringe with a 25-gauge needle, giving well above 70 PSI
A bulb syringe held against the skin, giving 25 to 40 PSI of pressure
preguntas.explicacion: A large syringe with a plastic catheter on the end, pushed with both hands, produces about 25 to 40 pounds per square inch, which is enough to lift debris and bacteria out without driving them deeper; above 70 the tissue itself is injured. Normal saline is the usual solution, and roughly 50 mL is used for each centimeter of wound length.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Promoting Interoperability Programs
preguntas.subtema: MACRA and MIPS · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.G.4 (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA 7 k90 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What did MACRA do in 2015 to the incentive program that had paid clinicians for meaningful use of certified EHRs?
opciones: It sunset that program and folded similar requirements into MIPS as one of four categories
It doubled the payments available under that program and extended it through 2027
It replaced that program with a penalty applied to every practice using paper charts
It moved that program from CMS to the Office for Civil Rights for enforcement
preguntas.explicacion: The EHR Incentive Programs were established in 2011 under the HITECH Act. In 2015 the Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act sunset the Medicare program for eligible professionals and built similar requirements into the Merit-based Incentive Payment System as one of its four performance categories, Promoting Interoperability. The hospital program continues; the Medicaid one ended on December 31, 2021.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(a), Standard: Notice of rights; 482.13(h), Patient visitation rights
preguntas.subtema: Notice of patient rights · CPT D1 k14 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA II.E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Medicare Conditions of Participation, 42 CFR 482.13, when must a hospital inform patients of their rights?
opciones: In advance of furnishing or discontinuing care, whenever possible
Within 30 days of admission, in a written notice signed by the patient
Only when the patient or a representative files a formal grievance
At discharge, together with the billing statement and visitation policy
preguntas.explicacion: The first standard of 482.13, notice of rights, has the hospital tell each patient, or the representative where state law allows one, what their rights are before care is given or withdrawn, whenever that can be done. The same standard calls for a grievance process: a clear procedure for grievances written or spoken, time frames for the review, and a written decision naming the contact person, the steps taken and the outcome. Visitation rights are explained along with the rest, not at discharge.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Open access principles · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5C k171 · CMA III.H.1.c · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A front desk moving to open access is told its single rule is to do today's work today. Which habit does that ask the staff to drop?
opciones: Sorting callers by clinical urgency, since demand is now sorted by clinician instead
Booking the follow-up visits a clinician asked for, since those slots are needed today
Offering a caller a later day, since under this model nobody may decline the same-day slot
Tracking the calls patients make, since demand is read from the count of past appointments
preguntas.explicacion: The model breaks with the traditional split between urgent and routine, which is what pushes routine care back. Instead of triaging callers by urgency, reception simply sorts the demand by clinician. Clinically necessary follow-ups are still booked ahead, patients may still choose a later day, and the practice has to measure both supply and demand as precisely as it can.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, FAQ: What is a patient portal?
preguntas.subtema: Portal functions · CMAA 4E k56 · CCMA 5U k172 · CMA III.H.3.a (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.B.6.c · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks whether she has to telephone the office to settle her balance and confirm what her plan covers. What does ONC say some portals allow?
opciones: Checking benefits and coverage and making payments through the portal itself
Filing the claim with her insurer once the appointment has been completed
Reading the explanation of benefits her insurer prepared for the last visit
Setting the allowed amount her plan will pay for the appointment she booked
preguntas.explicacion: On top of secure messaging, refill requests and booking non-urgent appointments, some portals let the patient look up her benefits and coverage, correct her contact details, pay what she owes, pull down forms and fill them in, and read educational material. Filing the claim and setting an allowed amount are done by the practice and the plan, not by the patient at her portal.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Mandatory & Optional Medicaid Benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A mother asks whether her child's Medicaid covers a screening and whatever the screening turns up. What does the mandatory benefit list say?
opciones: The early and periodic screening benefit, with diagnosis and treatment, is mandatory
Screening is mandatory in every state, but the treatment it leads to is left optional
Screening for children is one of the optional benefits a state may add if it chooses
Screening is mandatory only in the states that widened Medicaid to low-income adults
preguntas.explicacion: The early and periodic screening benefit, taking in diagnosis and treatment, appears on the federal list of mandatory Medicaid state plan benefits that every state must provide, and it is named as one benefit rather than split between the screening and what follows. The optional list is where a state chooses what to add through its state plan.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(i) and (b), Definitions: Personal Protective Equipment
preguntas.subtema: What makes PPE appropriate · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Under the bloodborne pathogens standard, protective equipment counts as appropriate only when it does what?
opciones: Keeps blood from reaching work clothes, skin, eyes or mouth for as long as it is worn
Carries the manufacturer's label with the biohazard symbol printed in orange-red
Is picked by the employee from the sizes the supplier keeps in stock at the site
Is worn over the uniform, which the standard also counts as protective clothing
preguntas.explicacion: The definition of appropriate in paragraph (d)(3)(i) is a performance test, not a brand or a label: under normal conditions of use, and for the whole time it will be worn, the item must not let blood, or any other potentially infectious material, through to work or street clothes, to undergarments, or to the skin, eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes. Paragraph (d)(3)(iii) is what puts the right sizes within reach; and the definitions in (b) exclude ordinary uniforms, pants and shirts from being protective equipment at all.

preguntas.fuente: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, Guideline 4: Limits
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks about added sugars. In the 2020-2025 Dietary Guidelines, what is the limit for anyone age 2 and older?
opciones: Less than 10 percent of the calories eaten in a day
Less than 20 percent of the calories eaten in a day
Less than 15 percent of the calories eaten in a day
Less than 5 percent of the calories eaten in a day
preguntas.explicacion: The fourth guideline of that edition caps added sugars below a tenth of daily calories from age 2 on, and tells caregivers to keep added sugars out of the diet entirely before that age. The 15 percent figure is what is left over after food group needs are met; 5 and 20 percent are the label's low and high marks for a nutrient, not a sugar limit. Note that the 2025-2030 edition drops the percentage ceiling and instead recommends no added sugars at all, with none at all for children age 4 and under.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Osteoarthritis", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(2) (2027 I.C.6.g(2)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A 60-year-old reports knee pain that worsens with activity and eases with rest, plus morning stiffness that clears in about twenty minutes. Which diagnosis fits?
opciones: Osteoarthritis, the most common form of arthritis
Osteoporosis, the most common form of arthritis
Rheumatoid arthritis, the most common form of arthritis
Osteomalacia, the most common form of arthritis
preguntas.explicacion: Osteoarthritis is a clinical diagnosis, and the picture is consistent: activity makes the pain worse and rest relieves it, age is over 45, morning stiffness clears inside thirty minutes, the joint is bony and enlarged, and range of motion is limited. Osteoporosis is loss of bone mass, not a joint disease, and it usually causes no symptoms until something breaks.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Section 5, Device Design; and eCFR 21 CFR 862.1675
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 k54 k66 · D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Into which regulatory class do needle-safety devices of this kind typically fall?
opciones: Class II, and subject to the quality system design controls
Class I, and exempt from any quality system requirement
Class III, and subject to premarket approval before any sale
Class II, and exempt from design controls once cleared once
preguntas.explicacion: These devices are typically class II and fall under the quality system regulation, which includes design controls: a set of checks built into development so that gaps between the requirements and the design surface early. A blood specimen collection device is likewise a class II device.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Responding to HBV Exposures in Health Care Settings, Vaccinated clinicians with low anti-HBs levels and Table 1
preguntas.subtema: Vaccine non-responders · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A worker who never reached a protective anti-HBs level after two complete vaccine series is exposed to an HBsAg-positive source. Per the CDC table, what is given?
opciones: Two doses of HBIG, the first right away and the second one month later
One dose of HBIG plus the start of a third complete vaccine series
A single vaccine booster, then anti-HBs testing 1 to 2 months later
No further treatment, since two series show the worker is a documented responder
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's guidance for vaccinated clinicians with anti-HBs below 10 mIU/mL after two complete series says that if the source is HBsAg-positive or unknown, the clinician receives two doses of HBIG, the first as soon as possible and the second 1 month later, and that further vaccine is not recommended because two series have already failed. If the source is HBsAg-negative, neither HBIG nor vaccine is needed. WHO's Table D.1 groups known non-responders with the unvaccinated for HBIG, but the CDC table is the more specific source here.

preguntas.subtema: Required specifications · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice argues that its risk analysis found little need for an emergency access procedure, so it will not build one. Is that allowed?
opciones: No, that specification is required, so it has to be implemented as the rule states
Yes, if the reason is documented and an equivalent alternative measure is put in place
Yes, provided the automatic logoff is shortened to make up for the missing measure
No, but a small practice may write a note in the contingency plan in place of it
preguntas.explicacion: The document-and-substitute route belongs to addressable specifications only. The emergency access procedure, which lets staff obtain the information they need during an emergency, is marked required, and a required specification must be implemented whatever the size of the practice.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7: Fill the laboratory sample tubes
preguntas.subtema: Syringe transfer and haemolysis · CPT D3 k54 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: While transferring blood from a syringe, a phlebotomist pushes the plunger to speed up filling of a slow tube. What does the WHO say about this?
opciones: Do not press the plunger; the extra pressure raises the risk of hemolysis
Press the plunger only for tubes with additives, which need a full draw
Press the plunger gently once the stopper has been removed from the tube
Pressing is acceptable for the last tube, once the tourniquet has been released
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 instructs the phlebotomist to pierce the stopper from directly above with slow, steady pressure and not to press the syringe plunger, because the extra pressure raises the risk of hemolysis; for tubes without a rubber stopper it asks for an extremely slow injection for the same reason. There is no exception for additive tubes, for the last tube, or after removing the stopper.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Responding to HBV Exposures in Health Care Settings, Unvaccinated clinicians and Table 1; CDC, Exposure to Blood (2003)
preguntas.subtema: HBV PEP for unvaccinated workers · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: An unvaccinated phlebotomist is stuck by a needle used on an HBsAg-positive patient. According to the CDC, what is given and when?
opciones: HBIG and the first vaccine dose, as soon as possible and preferably within 24 hours, at separate sites
The vaccine series only, started within 7 days, since HBIG is reserved for known non-responders
HBIG only, repeated one month later, since starting the vaccine after exposure is too late
A 28-day antiviral course started within 72 hours, followed by the vaccine series
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's table covers a clinician never vaccinated, or one who never finished the series, exposed to a source that is HBsAg-positive or unknown: one dose of HBIG plus hepatitis B vaccine, as soon as possible, injected at a different anatomical site such as the other limb, the series then completed on schedule and anti-HBs measured 1 to 2 months after the last dose. The older brochure puts the start preferably inside 24 hours and no later than 7 days. Two doses of HBIG a month apart are for non-responders after two series, and the 28-day antiviral course is HIV PEP.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Administrative Requirements, Privacy Personnel; 45 CFR 164.530(a)
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA personnel designations · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which two roles must a practice name to satisfy the personnel designations of the Privacy Rule?
opciones: A privacy official who builds and runs the policies, and a contact who takes in complaints
A privacy official who builds and runs the policies, and a records custodian who releases charts
A compliance officer who audits the billing, and a contact who takes in privacy complaints
A privacy official who builds and runs the policies, and a trainer for every new workforce member
preguntas.explicacion: Two names go on the wall, not one. The privacy official owns the policies and procedures: writing them and putting them to work. The contact person, or a contact office, is the door for the public — complaints arrive there, and so do questions about how the practice handles information, which is why the notice has to say who that is and add that a complaint may also go to the Secretary of HHS. Training, sanctions and mitigation are separate administrative duties of the same section, and they do not have to be handed to a designated person.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Radiologic PPE
preguntas.subtema: Radiologic PPE · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.3 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.8.a / 2027 I.B.7.a · RMA III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.3
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is called to draw blood in the fluoroscopy suite while imaging is under way. Which protection is meant for that setting?
opciones: A lead apron, leaded glasses and cap, and a thyroid collar
A fluid-resistant gown, a face shield and two pairs of gloves
An N95 respirator with eye protection, as for airborne cases
A chemical-resistant suit with a self-contained air supply
preguntas.explicacion: Where x-ray and gamma radiation are in use, above all in fluoroscopy and the other procedures guided by imaging, the protective equipment is leaded: an apron or vest, leaded glasses, a leaded cap and a protective collar, each of which cuts the dose received. A personal dosimeter is required for workers who enter a high radiation or restricted area, or who take in more than a quarter of the occupational limit within a calendar quarter.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Unpacking Deliveries
preguntas.subtema: Cold chain monitor · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A cold chain monitor is included in the shipping container. What does the receiving staff member do with it?
opciones: Read it for any excursion during transit and then discard it, since it is single use
Read it for any excursion during transit and place it inside the storage unit
File it with the packing list as the record of the temperature during transit
Return it to the distributor with the shipping container for its next journey
preguntas.explicacion: The monitor's job ends when the box is opened: it is checked for a temperature excursion during transit and then thrown away, because it is made for one trip only. It is not the storage unit's monitoring device, which is a continuous digital data logger that stays with the unit.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions: Laboratory
preguntas.subtema: CLIA scope · CPT D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1 · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which facility falls outside the CLIA definition of a laboratory?
opciones: A draw station that only collects and prepares specimens, with no testing
A physician office that performs only waived tests on its own patients
A hospital laboratory accredited by a CMS-approved organization
A mobile unit that performs hematology testing on human specimens
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA calls a laboratory a facility that examines materials taken from the human body, by chemical, hematological, microbiological, serological or similar methods, to give information for diagnosis, prevention, treatment or the assessment of health, and it says that a facility only collecting or preparing specimens, or only acting as a mailing service, without doing any testing, is not a laboratory. An office running waived tests and a mobile unit running hematology both perform examinations and so need a certificate; a pure collection site does not.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Vaginal Instillations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B5 k69 · CMA I.D.2.c(8) · RMA III.G.4.d(iv) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: In which forms is medication supplied for the vaginal route?
opciones: Foams, creams, tablets and suppositories that melt with the heat of the body
Foams, creams and coated tablets that are swallowed with a full glass of water
Powders for reconstitution and metered aerosols delivered through a spacer device
Ointments and skin patches that are pressed firmly in place for about ten seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Vaginal instillation is used mostly for hormone therapy and antifungal treatment, and the medication comes as foam, cream, tablet, or a suppository that melts at body heat. The patient is asked to void first and is positioned on the back with the knees flexed; perineal care is done, gloves are changed, and the applicator is filled and inserted. Privacy is part of the procedure, not an extra.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(ii) and (b), Definitions: Engineering controls
preguntas.subtema: Maintaining engineering controls · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What does the standard require of the safety devices and sharps containers a draw station uses every day?
opciones: They are inspected on a regular schedule, then maintained or replaced
They are examined only after an exposure incident has been reported and logged
They are replaced every three years, the period set for keeping training records
They are checked by the manufacturer at installation and then left in service
preguntas.explicacion: Engineering controls are the devices that take the hazard away from the worker: self-sheathing needles, needleless systems, sharps disposal containers. Paragraph (d)(2)(ii) says that on a regular schedule they are examined, and then maintained or replaced, so that they still do what they were bought to do. Waiting for an injury reverses that logic, and the three-year figure is the retention period for training records in (h)(2)(ii), not a replacement interval.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hypoglycemia", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k82 · CMA I.B.8.b · 2027 I.B.7.b · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes is too drowsy to swallow and the glucose meter reads 42 mg/dL. Which emergency medicine is indicated?
opciones: Glucagon, given into the muscle or by the newer intranasal form
Glucose tablets, placed under the tongue until they dissolve there
Epinephrine, injected into the outer part of the thigh right away
Insulin, given subcutaneously to move the glucose into the cells
preguntas.explicacion: A conscious patient who can swallow gets a readily absorbed carbohydrate such as fruit juice; when the patient cannot take anything by mouth, glucagon is the answer, given intramuscularly or by the newer intranasal preparations. A complex carbohydrate follows as soon as the patient wakes, and the glucose is rechecked more often.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Technique or Treatment and Complications; and StatPearls, "StatPearls (NBK482331) — Petechiae" (NBK482331)
preguntas.subtema: Complications: hematoma · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: What is a hematoma, and which two technique errors cause it?
opciones: Blood pooled under the skin; a needle pushed beyond the vein lumen, or too little pressure during and after the draw
Pinpoint bleeding into the dermis; leaving the tourniquet on too long, or using a needle that is too small
Pooling of blood under the skin; shaking the tube after filling, or drawing the tubes out of sequence
Bleeding into the skin larger than 2 mm; drawing from the basilic vein, or using povidone iodine
preguntas.explicacion: A hematoma is the pooling of blood under the skin, and two errors are linked to it: pushing the needle in past the lumen of the vein, and not applying enough pressure during and after the draw. The WHO adds a third, letting the patient bend the arm. Pinpoint dermal bleeding is petechiae, and spots larger than 2 mm are purpura in the petechiae chapter.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - young child (age 1 year to onset of puberty)", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: Two medical assistants are giving CPR to a 4-year-old child. Which compression-to-ventilation ratio do they use?
opciones: 15 compressions to 2 breaths, because two rescuers are working
30 compressions to 2 breaths, the ratio for a single rescuer
5 compressions to 1 breath, trading places after every cycle
10 compressions to 2 breaths, with 1 breath every 6 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: A child or infant worked by one rescuer gets 2 breaths after every 30 compressions; when two rescuers are present that changes to 2 breaths after every 15 compressions. The rate stays at 100 to 120 per minute either way. One breath every 6 seconds is the rate for rescue breathing in a patient who still has a pulse, not a compression ratio.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.5
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k56 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E7 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is named among the factors that shape the quality of a laboratory sample?
opciones: The gauge of needle chosen for the puncture
The color of the gloves worn for the draw
The brand of alcohol rub kept on the trolley
The height of the rack the tubes stand in
preguntas.explicacion: The factors named as shaping the quality of a laboratory sample are the knowledge of the staff, use of the correct gauge of needle so the sample is not hemolyzed or otherwise abnormal, the anatomical site chosen, the recommended tubes, matching patient to sample, transport conditions and interpretation.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.2, Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2N k49 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k127 · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: The flow into the tube is slow during a child's draw. Which measure does the WHO offer for the parent to do?
opciones: Tighten and release the child's wrist rhythmically to help the flow
Lower the child's arm below the level of the table for a minute
Press firmly above the elbow until the vein stands out clearly
Rub the puncture site briskly with dry gauze between the tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Where venipuncture proves difficult, the parent may be asked to tighten and release the child's wrist rhythmically so there is adequate blood flow, the child may be kept warm, warm cloths may be laid over the puncture area to dilate the vessels, and a transilluminator or pocket pen light may be used to show the dorsal hand veins and those of the antecubital fossa.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT VI.B · CCMA 3D9 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: The laboratory notifies a phlebotomist that a specimen was rejected for a critically ill patient. Why must the recollection be arranged without delay?
opciones: Rejection forces a new sample request, prolongs turnaround and can delay diagnosis and treatment
Rejected specimens are discarded after 30 minutes, after which the original order is canceled
The laboratory cannot issue any report for the patient until the replacement sample is received
A second rejection from the same unit automatically triggers an accreditation incident report
preguntas.explicacion: Sample rejection stops the analysis and generates a new request, which lengthens turnaround time and delays diagnosis and treatment of critical patients, with adverse outcomes described in the literature; that is the reason the task of contacting the patient or unit for recollection matters. Rejected tubes are actually kept 24 hours at 4 °C, other reports are not blocked, and accreditation bodies ask for monitoring, not automatic incidents.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Pathophysiology
preguntas.subtema: Complications: petechiae · CPT D3 3L k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which four mechanisms are given as the primary causes of petechiae and purpura?
opciones: Low platelets, platelet dysfunction, clotting disorders, loss of vascular integrity
Low platelets, high hematocrit, iron deficiency, loss of vascular integrity
High platelets, platelet dysfunction, clotting disorders, raised blood pressure
Low platelets, platelet dysfunction, dehydration, prolonged tourniquet pressure
preguntas.explicacion: These rashes come from hemorrhage into the dermis, and the underlying mechanisms named are a low platelet count, platelets that do not work, disordered coagulation and vascular integrity that has given way. Some clinical pictures produce the spots through a combination of more than one of them.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, HITECH Act Enforcement Interim Final Rule
preguntas.subtema: HIPAA penalties · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: How many culpability categories does the civil money penalty scheme for HIPAA violations use?
opciones: Four, running from not knowing up to willful neglect that was never corrected
Three, running from an honest mistake up to a deliberate sale of patient records
Two, one for covered entities and a separate one for their business associates
Six, one for each of the circumstances in which records may go to law enforcement
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH set four categories of violation reflecting rising culpability, matched by four tiers of penalty. In order: the entity did not know and would not have known with reasonable diligence; there was reasonable cause but no willful neglect; there was willful neglect but the violation was corrected inside 30 days; and there was willful neglect and no correction.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: The R waves on a strip are spaced unevenly, so the square method will not work. What is done instead?
opciones: Count the beats in a 10-second strip and multiply by 6
Count the beats in a 10-second strip and multiply by 4
Count the beats in a 10-second strip and multiply by 10
Count the small squares between two R waves and use 300
preguntas.explicacion: The square methods assume the beats are evenly spaced. When they are not, the count is taken over the whole ten-second strip and multiplied by six to reach a rate per minute. Dividing 300 by small squares mixes up the two grids and gives a figure far off the real rate.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: When may a three-character code be reported on a claim?
opciones: Only when that category is not subdivided any further
Only when the record supports no more specific code
Only when its index entry ends with a dash after it
Only when the index lists it as the default for the term
preguntas.explicacion: All categories in the tabular list are three characters, and a three-character category with nothing subdivided under it is itself a code. A three-character code is therefore used only when it is not subdivided; where fourth, fifth or sixth characters exist, a code that stops short of them is invalid, and so is one missing an applicable seventh character. A dash at the end of an index entry says the opposite of what the answer offers: that more characters are still required.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Pathophysiology
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.B.9.l / 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Why does laying a patient flat bring them round after a faint?
opciones: Blood returns from the legs and the heart no longer pumps uphill
Blood leaves the legs and pools where the tourniquet had been
The vagus nerve is compressed and the heart rate rises at once
The cool, quiet space raises the blood pressure by itself
preguntas.explicacion: When the patient falls or is laid supine, circulating volume returns from the lower limbs and the heart no longer has to deliver blood against gravity, so consciousness comes back quickly. That is also why the person is asked to sit or lie down promptly as soon as the warning symptoms appear.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: The forearm a patient offers shows a hot, red area diagnosed as cellulitis. Why is that site excluded for venipuncture?
opciones: Cellulitis or an abscess raises the risk of bacteria entering the blood directly
The redness blanches under pressure, so it is erythema and not bleeding into the skin
The swelling dilutes the specimen with tissue fluid, just as squeezing a finger does
Alcohol cannot be used on inflamed skin, so the site cannot be disinfected
preguntas.explicacion: A condition such as cellulitis or an abscess raises the risk of bacteria getting straight into the blood, so another site is chosen. Blanching is the feature that tells erythema from bleeding into the skin, tissue fluid dilution is the WHO's capillary warning about squeezing, and nothing in the material forbids alcohol on inflamed skin.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Storage
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(2) (2027 I.C.5.b(2)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA EKB 5
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic uses event-related shelf life for its sterile packs. What does that mean in practice?
opciones: A pack stays sterile until something compromises it, such as a tear, wetness or a broken seal
A pack stays sterile for thirty days from the cycle date, after which it is reprocessed
A pack stays sterile until the next biological indicator is run, regardless of its cycle date
A pack stays sterile only while it sits in a closed cabinet, and is reprocessed once moved
preguntas.explicacion: Event-related practice recognizes that contamination is caused by an event, not by the calendar: a tear in the packaging, packaging that gets wet, a broken seal. Handling is itself the risk, since the probability of contamination climbs with the amount of it. Facilities that still date every product are using the older time-related practice instead.

preguntas.fuente: NIA, Talking With Your Older Patients, Families and caregivers as part of the health care team
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · CCMA 7B k216 k218 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.D.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: The son says, 'I'll sign the consent, she's forgetful.' No proxy or power-of-attorney paperwork exists. Who decides?
opciones: The patient remains responsible for her own choices; set clear boundaries with the family
The son may sign, because adult children are the default decision-makers for parents
A clinic staff member signs on the patient's behalf as a neutral third party
The draw is deferred until a court appoints a guardian for the patient
preguntas.explicacion: It is above all the adult children who want to take over for a parent whose cognition is failing. Only a family member named as health care agent or proxy holds, in some circumstances, the legal authority to decide about care; without that authority the patient stays responsible for her own choices, and the clinician sets clear boundaries with the family. Where there is no proxy and no advance directive at all, the short-term decision falls to the team or to an ethics committee, and a court assigns formal guardianship only when the need is long term.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, preparation steps
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant takes a refrigerated control and a refrigerated patient sample straight from the fridge to the bench and starts the run. What step was skipped?
opciones: Letting the refrigerated material come up to room temperature first
Recording the refrigerator temperature at the moment of removal
Checking that the kit lot matches the lot of the control material
Writing the date of opening on the outside of the reagent vial
preguntas.explicacion: The preparation checklist for waived testing puts several steps before the run: check vials and reagents for contamination, discoloration or damage; prepare them the way the current instructions say; write the opening date on a vial or kit just opened; let refrigerated reagents and samples warm to room temperature; and then run quality control as the instructions recommend.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Contact Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Dedicated equipment · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k96 · CMA I.B.5.c / 2027 I.B.4.c · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: Under Contact Precautions, what does the CDC recommend for a blood pressure cuff and similar patient-care equipment?
opciones: Disposable or dedicated equipment; if sharing is unavoidable, clean and disinfect it before the next patient
Shared equipment may be used freely, since the pathogen spreads by contact with the patient, not with objects
Wrap shared equipment in a protective cover that is changed at the end of the shift
Autoclave the equipment after each use, since disinfection does not reach contact pathogens
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's Contact Precautions recommendations use blood pressure cuffs as the example: equipment for patient care should be disposable, or else dedicated to that one patient, and where sharing between patients cannot be avoided it is cleaned and disinfected before the next one. The reason is that contact transmission takes in the patient's environment and the objects in it, not only skin. The same page asks that these patients' rooms be cleaned and disinfected often, at least daily, or before another patient uses the space in outpatient settings, with attention to high-touch surfaces.
