preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2 Prepare the skin
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 puncture technique · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: How should the puncture stroke itself be made in capillary sampling?
opciones: A single quick, firm, deliberate stroke, for good flow and no second stick
Two short strokes in the same track, so that the second one opens the bed fully
A slow stroke that stops as soon as the first drop of blood appears
A rocking stroke across the print lines, to widen it without going deeper
preguntas.explicacion: One stroke, quick and carried through, is what brings a flow good enough to avoid a second attempt. Going in again would mean either a used lancet or a used hole, and both are barred because they invite bacteria and infection. Depth is a matter of lancet length, not of rocking the device.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Restraint and Seclusion", sections Removal of Restraints and Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k49 · CCMA 3E1 k127 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: An agitated inpatient calms down 20 minutes into a 4-hour restraint order. What should happen?
opciones: Remove the restraints immediately; he is no longer a danger to anyone
Keep the restraints on until the 4-hour order expires, as written
Keep the restraints on until the next scheduled face-to-face evaluation
Loosen one limb every 15 minutes until the order runs out
preguntas.explicacion: The moment the patient stops being a danger, to himself or to anyone else, the restraints come off; the time limit on the order is a ceiling, not a duration to be served. Restraint and seclusion are interventions of last resort, required to be the least restrictive measure available, with no evidence that they are therapeutic or that they reduce aggression, and staff observe the patient regularly throughout.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(1)(ii) and (f)(1)(iii), Hepatitis B Vaccination and Post-exposure Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: Terms of the medical follow-up · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: How must the hepatitis B vaccination and any post-exposure follow-up be made available to an exposed employee?
opciones: Free, at a reasonable time and place, and under a licensed healthcare professional
Free, but only at the occupational health service the employer has contracted
At the employee's expense, reimbursed once the written opinion has arrived
Free, and only during the first ten working days of the initial assignment
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(1)(ii) puts four conditions on every medical evaluation and procedure the standard requires, prophylaxis included: no cost to the employee, a reasonable time and place, work carried out by a licensed physician or by any other licensed healthcare professional, or under their supervision, and agreement with the Public Health Service recommendations current at that moment. Paragraph (f)(1)(iii) adds that laboratory tests go to an accredited laboratory, also free. The ten working days are the deadline for offering the vaccine, not a window that closes on follow-up.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1; and StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which change in practice is credited with markedly reducing needle-stick injuries?
opciones: Dropping recapping and putting the sharp straight into a safety container
Recapping every needle carefully with the cap held in the other hand
Storing used needles on the tray until the end of the drawing session
Rinsing the used needle before it goes into the puncture-resistant bin
preguntas.explicacion: Eliminating needle recapping and disposing of the sharp immediately into a puncture-resistant container is described as markedly reducing these injuries. Routine recapping is no longer recommended precisely because handling a used needle is what creates the chance of a puncture.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, section Causes
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · D2 2L k48 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Besides fear and pain, which everyday events are listed as bringing on a faint?
opciones: Coughing hard, straining at stool, standing still too long, passing urine
Eating a light meal, reading in poor light, walking upstairs, yawning
Drinking water, sitting down slowly, wearing loose clothing, resting
Breathing slowly, lying flat for an hour, raising the legs, whistling
preguntas.explicacion: Faints are described as happening during or just after coughing very hard, having a bowel movement with straining, standing in one place too long, or passing urine, especially at night. Emotional distress, fear and severe pain sit on the same list, and all of them can appear in a drawing room.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Hand Hygiene in Healthcare Settings, Clinical Safety guidance for healthcare providers, moments for hand hygiene
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene after gloves · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist wearing gloves finishes a draw and removes them. Which CDC moment for hand hygiene applies?
opciones: Immediately after glove removal, before anything else
Only if the gloves were visibly soiled with blood
Before touching the next patient, which covers this case
At the end of the shift, because gloves replace hand hygiene
preguntas.explicacion: Immediately after glove removal is one of the CDC's moments for hand hygiene. The others: before an aseptic task, immediately before touching a patient, when moving from a soiled site to a clean one, after touching the patient or their surroundings, and after contact with blood or a contaminated surface. The same page states that gloves do not substitute for hand hygiene. Waiting for the next patient skips the glove-removal moment, and visible soiling changes only the method, soap and water rather than alcohol rub, not whether hygiene happens.

preguntas.subtema: Scope of practice · RMA I.C.6 · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: As a general rule, what level of supervision does auxiliary personnel need for services billed as incident to?
opciones: Direct supervision from the physician, or from whoever bills the service
General supervision, with the physician's overall direction only
Personal supervision, with the physician inside the treatment room
No supervision, provided the state license allows the task itself
preguntas.explicacion: Auxiliary personnel are individuals acting under the supervision of a physician or other practitioner, whether employed, leased or contracted, who are not excluded from federal health programs and who meet any state licensure requirements for the service. The general rule is direct supervision, which for some services may be met through real-time audio and video presence, never audio alone. Two named groups drop to general supervision: designated care management services and behavioral health services.

preguntas.subtema: Equipment quality · CPT D3 3A 3B k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.2 · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why is a service expected to keep enough laboratory tubes in stock at all times?
opciones: So blood is never decanted from one tube into another to reuse tubes
So the tubes on the tray can be replaced before their expiry each month
So a second tube of every color is always drawn as a spare specimen
So the same manufacturer supplies the needles and holders in the tray
preguntas.explicacion: Management is asked to make enough sample tubes available precisely to keep dangerous shortcuts out of the room, and the example given is decanting blood so that tubes can be recycled. The single-manufacturer rule is a separate point about components fitting one another.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 4
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene and gloves · CPT D3 3A · D1 1K k35 · PBT II.F VI.G · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finishes cleaning a spill and her hands are visibly soiled. Which form of hand hygiene is required before the next draw?
opciones: Soap and water, dried with single-use towels
Alcohol rub, worked in until the hands are dry
Alcohol rub, followed by a second pair of gloves
Soap and water, dried with a shared cloth towel
preguntas.explicacion: Hand hygiene before a draw can be done two ways: washing with soap and water and drying on single-use towels, or rubbing with alcohol when the hands are not visibly contaminated. Visible soiling therefore rules the rub out. Well-fitting non-sterile gloves go on once the hands are dry.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antiepileptic Drug Monitoring", section Other Issues, Trough Versus Free Levels
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: What does a 'trough level' represent in antiepileptic drug monitoring?
opciones: The lowest drug concentration, typically just before the next dose is due
The highest drug concentration, shortly after the dose has been taken
The unbound, pharmacologically active fraction of the drug in blood
The average concentration across the whole dosing interval
preguntas.explicacion: The trough catches the drug at its floor, which usually falls just ahead of the next dose, and it matters most for a drug with a short half-life because it shows the minimum kept up between doses. Free levels are the unbound, active fraction, measured where protein binding may be altered. The peak and the average across the interval are different quantities.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advance Directives", Issues of Concern: POLST
preguntas.subtema: Medical directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.a-b / 2027 E.7 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: What makes a POLST or MOLST form different from a living will?
opciones: It records the wishes as medical orders that carry across care settings
It records the wishes as a sworn statement filed with the state registry
It records the wishes of the family rather than those of the patient
It records the wishes only for the hospital where it was first signed
preguntas.explicacion: On a POLST or MOLST the patient's preferences are written as medical orders, and in states that recognize the form those orders travel with the patient across health care settings, including the prehospital one. A surrogate may complete it. In some states the form is void if it contradicts an existing living will; in others it replaces the living will, because it is easier to adjust.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN: NPI - What You Need to Know
preguntas.subtema: NPI entity types · CCMA 5 k183 · CMA III.H.2 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 6 k89 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A group practice and each of its physicians are enrolling. Which NPI entity types apply?
opciones: Type 2 for the organization and Type 1 for each individual provider
Type 1 for the organization and Type 2 for each individual provider
Type 2 for both, since everyone in a group enrolls under the group number
Type 1 for both, since the number always belongs to a licensed human being
preguntas.explicacion: There are two enumeration categories. Entity Type 1 covers individual health care providers, sole proprietors included, and a sole proprietor applies with a Social Security Number rather than an employer identification number even if one exists. Entity Type 2 covers organizations. Students, interns and residents are eligible and must apply. Billing services, clearinghouses and health plans may not obtain one at all.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Code Sets Overview; and MLN Booklet MLN006976, Procedure Coding
