preguntas.pregunta: Blood soaks through the gauze being held on a bleeding wound. What should be done?
opciones: Lay another cloth over the first one and keep up the pressure
Lift the gauze to look at the wound and then press again harder
Replace the soaked gauze with dry gauze and press on the artery
Loosen the pressure for a moment so that a clot can start to form
preguntas.explicacion: A soaked dressing is not taken off: another one is placed on top and pressure continues until bleeding stops, and then the dressing is wrapped firmly in place. Peeking disturbs the wound and makes control harder. Bleeding that keeps seeping through calls for medical attention right away.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Designated Record Set
preguntas.subtema: Designated record set · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which category of information is expressly excluded from the individual's right of access?
opciones: Psychotherapy notes kept separate from the rest of the patient's medical record
Laboratory results, which the patient obtains from the testing laboratory instead
Billing and payment records, which belong to the revenue cycle rather than the chart
Medical images such as X-rays, because they are not readily producible on paper
preguntas.explicacion: Two categories are excluded outright: psychotherapy notes, meaning a mental health provider's own notes on a counseling session kept apart from the record, and information gathered because a legal proceeding is expected or under way. Otherwise the right of access is broad; it expressly reaches insurance information, billing and payment records, laboratory results, and medical images like X-rays.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Materials and methods, Sample identification; Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 k146 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A barcode scanner at the accessioning desk misreads a patient identification label. What did the emergency laboratory identify as the cause of such misreads?
opciones: A mismatch between the scanner settings and the print area size or symbology of the barcode on the wristband
Barcodes printed more than 30 minutes before collection, which fade beyond the reading threshold of the scanner
Labels printed with more than two identifiers, which overload the nine-digit internal code the scanner expects
Heat from the centrifuge, which distorts the code 39 bars so that the digits no longer match the record
preguntas.explicacion: Barcoding carries an evidence-based recommendation behind it, since it cuts identification errors in specimens and in testing, yet this laboratory still saw scanners misread patient barcodes when the symbology or the print area on a wristband or specimen label did not match the scanner's settings. Its own nine-digit code 39 barcode carries name, sex, age, tube and sample type, print and collection times, collection site, the tests, the ordering doctor and the phlebotomist.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Business Associate Defined
preguntas.subtema: Business associates · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k33 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The practice hires an outside company to process its claims. Under the Privacy Rule, what is that company?
opciones: A business associate, because it performs a function for the practice that uses patient information
A member of the practice workforce, because it handles the same records the front desk handles
A health care clearinghouse, because any outside company that touches claims fits that definition
An ordinary supplier outside the rule, since only entities that treat patients are regulated
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate is a person or an organization outside the workforce that performs functions or supplies services for a covered entity where the work involves using or disclosing health information that identifies an individual. Processing claims, analyzing data, reviewing utilization and doing the billing are the functions named. Someone whose work never touches PHI is not one.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 5: "Chunk and Check"
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4I evaluate understanding · CMA F.3.a · 2027 F.1.h · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: An assistant has a lot of ground to cover with a patient. When should teach-back be used during the visit?
opciones: In chunks through the visit, checking each segment before the next
Once at the very end, so the whole plan can be repeated together
Once at the start, to find out what the patient already knows
Only when the patient looks confused during the explanation
preguntas.explicacion: The habit is called chunk and check: information is broken into small segments and each one is taught back before the next is started, rather than saving it all for the end. Used consistently it becomes routine and does not make the visit longer.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex E, One-hand scoop technique
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A used needle really has to come off its syringe. How is the one-hand scoop performed?
opciones: Leave the cap on a surface, guide the tip in with one hand, then secure it
Hold the cap in one hand and push the needle into it with the other hand
Pinch the cap between two fingers and twist the syringe until it is covered
Hold the cap with forceps and press the needle down onto a firm surface
preguntas.explicacion: The cap is left resting on a surface, or propped against something firm and upright with the opening towards the worker, and the used tip is guided into it with one hand only. The needle and syringe are then lifted vertically and the other hand fixes the cap once the tip is covered.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, U.S. Preventive Services Task Force: A and B Recommendations — Colorectal Cancer: Screening
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4C screening timelines · CMA I.A.5.a · 2027 I.A.5.a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A 47-year-old with no risk factors asks whether colorectal screening applies to him yet. What is the recommendation?
opciones: Yes; screening is recommended from age 45, and carries an A grade from 50 to 75
No; screening is recommended only from age 50, and runs through age 75
Yes; screening is recommended from age 40, and carries an A grade from 45 to 75
No; screening starts at 45 only for adults who have a family history
preguntas.explicacion: Colorectal cancer screening is recommended for adults from 45 to 49 with a B grade and for all adults from 50 through 75 with an A grade, so a 47-year-old is inside the window. Grade B means the recommendation rests on somewhat less certainty of benefit than grade A, not that it is optional.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: COBRA
preguntas.subtema: Coverage continuation · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's job ended last month and he kept his employer coverage under COBRA. What changed for him?
opciones: He now pays the full premium, including the employer's old share, plus a small fee
He now pays the same share of the premium he paid while he was still employed
He now pays no premium, and the plan bills the former employer for the coverage
He now pays a premium set by the Marketplace, based on his household income
preguntas.explicacion: COBRA is the federal law that lets a person keep employer coverage for a time after the job ends, after losing dependent status, or after another qualifying event. Whoever elects it pays 100% of the premium, the portion the employer used to cover included, plus a small administrative charge. Nothing shifts the cost back to the employer, and income-based premiums belong to Marketplace coverage instead.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urea Breath Test", Procedures (Urea Breath Test)
preguntas.subtema: UBT medication holds · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.C.3 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient on omeprazole and a recent course of antibiotics is booked for a urea breath test. What has to happen first?
opciones: Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 4 weeks and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 2 weeks
Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 2 weeks and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 4 full weeks
Stop antibiotics and bismuth for at least 4 days and the proton pump inhibitor for at least 2 days
Only the antibiotic has to stop, for 4 weeks; acid suppressants do not interfere
preguntas.explicacion: Antibiotics and bismuth compounds are stopped at least 4 weeks ahead, and proton pump inhibitors and sucralfate at least 2 weeks ahead, because all of them suppress the urease activity the test measures and produce a false negative. Histamine-2 blockers are ideally held 24 to 48 hours beforehand. Plain antacids are allowed and do not interfere.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Rapid shallow breathing
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: An adult arrives with fast, shallow breathing and no history of anxiety. How is this handled?
opciones: It is treated as an emergency rather than something to be managed at home
It is observed at home for 24 hours, since the pattern often settles on its own
It is managed with an inhaler alone, which settles the breathing once the dose is taken
It is recorded as hyperventilation, which is the term for fast and shallow breathing
preguntas.explicacion: Unless anxiety is the whole story, fast shallow breathing is handled as an emergency: asthma, a clot in the lung, pneumonia, heart failure and chronic lung disease all present this way. Hyperventilation is the term for breathing that is rapid and deep, which is why the depth is charted along with the rate.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Dietary Fats — Summary
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(b) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(b) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient trying to lose weight asks why fat is watched so closely when some fat is necessary. What is true of dietary fat?
opciones: Gram for gram it carries twice the calories of protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries half the calories of protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries the same calories as protein or carbohydrate
Gram for gram it carries twice the calories that alcohol carries
preguntas.explicacion: Some fat belongs in the diet: it supplies energy, it helps the body absorb certain vitamins, and it shapes cholesterol levels. What makes it easy to overdo is density, since fat holds twice the calories that protein or carbohydrate holds for the same weight, so extra fat puts on weight quickly.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5: Disinfect the entry site
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G k63 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: After cleaning the site, a phlebotomist palpates the vein once more with a gloved finger to confirm its position. What does the WHO require now?
opciones: Repeat the disinfection, because the cleaned site was touched
Proceed at once, since the glove was clean and the alcohol has dried
Wipe the fingerprint with dry gauze and proceed without delay
Apply povidone iodine over the alcohol before inserting the needle
preguntas.explicacion: Step 5 says not to touch the cleaned site and, in particular, not to place a finger over the vein to guide the exposed needle; if the site is touched, the disinfection is repeated. A clean glove does not change the rule. The same step prefers alcohol to povidone iodine, which can falsely raise potassium, phosphorus or uric acid results.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Pictograms; and OSHA, 29 CFR 1910.1030 (texto oficial en osha.gov)
preguntas.subtema: Pictogram design · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How is a GHS hazard pictogram drawn on a shipped chemical label?
opciones: A black symbol on a white background inside a red square frame set on a point
A black symbol on a fluorescent orange background with the legend BIOHAZARD
A red symbol on a white background inside a black diamond used for transport
A black symbol inside a red square frame that may be left empty as a design element
preguntas.explicacion: A pictogram on a shipped container is a red square frame standing on one point, with a black symbol for the hazard set on white inside it, drawn wide enough to be seen clearly. A red frame left empty, with no symbol in it, is not a pictogram and has no place on the label. The fluorescent orange label carrying the BIOHAZARD legend belongs to the bloodborne pathogens standard, and the diamond-shaped transport labels are what the Department of Transportation requires for shipping, which the OSHA pictograms do not replace.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling; and "Prothrombin Time", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A new phlebotomist shakes a filled citrate tube hard to be sure the blood mixes. What is the consequence?
opciones: Frothing or hemolysis that makes the coagulation results inaccurate
Small clots in the tube, the result the review links to under-mixing
A rise in the citrate-to-blood ratio, as happens with a short draw
Loss of the vacuum, so the next tube in the sequence will not fill
preguntas.explicacion: Both the coagulopathies review and the prothrombin time chapter say the citrate tube is inverted gently and never shaken, because vigorous agitation causes frothing or hemolysis and the coagulation results become unreliable. Small clots are the opposite problem, inefficient mixing, in the tube collection review; the citrate ratio changes with underfilling, not with shaking.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(iv)(A) and (d)(3)(iv), Laundry and PPE
preguntas.subtema: Contaminated laundry · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.6.a / 2027 I.B.5.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A lab coat is soaked with blood after a difficult draw. How do the standard's laundry rules apply?
opciones: Bag it where it was used, without sorting or rinsing, in a container that prevents soak-through
Rinse it in the nearest sink first, then bag it, so the laundry service is not exposed
Take it home to wash separately, since the employer is not responsible for laundering
Sort it with other soiled coats at the laundry, where staff wear gloves and gowns
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(iv)(A) requires contaminated laundry to be handled as little as possible and with minimal agitation, bagged or containerized at the location of use, and never sorted or rinsed there; when it is wet enough to soak through, the bag or container must prevent leakage to the outside. The employer, not the employee, cleans and launders required PPE at no cost under (d)(3)(iv), so taking the coat home is not an option, and the gloves worn by laundry staff under (d)(4)(iv)(B) do not permit sorting at the point of use.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: Patient-initiated ending · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient writes that she is leaving the practice for a clinician nearer her home. Does the office owe her a termination notice?
opciones: No, though a letter confirming her decision is wise and cuts the risk of a later claim
Yes, and the same thirty days of care and medication refills still have to be offered
Yes, and it has to travel by certified mail with a return receipt like any other notice
No, and no letter should go out either, since the record closes with her last visit
preguntas.explicacion: When it is the patient who has ended the relationship, no termination notice is owed by the physician. Putting her decision on paper in a short letter is still the prudent move: it removes the ambiguity and lowers the exposure to a legal claim. The thirty days that are usually deemed reasonable, and the certified mail, attach to a termination the practice itself starts.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Pulse
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which two arteries are normally used to palpate a pulse?
opciones: The radial artery at the wrist and the common carotid in the neck
The brachial artery in the upper arm and the femoral in the thigh
The median cubital vein at the elbow and the cephalic along the arm
The dorsalis pedis on the foot and the popliteal behind the knee
preguntas.explicacion: A pulse is the expansion and recoil of an artery, and it is normally taken at the wrist over the radial artery or in the neck over the common carotid, though any artery near the surface will serve: the temporal, facial, brachial, femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis are the other listed spots. The median cubital and the cephalic are veins, and only arteries pulse.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Preventing falls — Home Setup
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A1 · CMA I.A.6.b · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient is being taught how to make the home safer after a near fall. Which change is advised?
opciones: Take up the loose throw rugs and secure any cords crossing the walking routes
Keep a low stepladder in the kitchen so high shelves stay within easy reach
Choose smooth leather soles, which slide less on carpet than rubber ones do
Move the bedroom upstairs so that the daily climb builds strength in the legs
preguntas.explicacion: Tripping hazards come out first: loose rugs, trailing cords, uneven flooring in doorways. Light the path from the bedroom to the bathroom, put rails by the tub and toilet and a non-slip mat inside. Shoes should be low-heeled with rubber soles, not leather. Standing on chairs or stepladders is out, and daily life is arranged to avoid stairs altogether.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: living will
preguntas.subtema: Advance directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.b / 2027 E.7.a · RMA I.C.7 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: Life-sustaining treatment is given to a patient whose living will refused it. What claim may follow, and what defeats it?
opciones: Medical battery; the claim fails if the provider did not know of the living will
Medical battery; the claim fails only if a relative asked for the treatment
Negligence; the claim fails if the treatment turned out to help the patient
Breach of contract; the claim fails if the document was signed years earlier
preguntas.explicacion: A living will is an advance directive listing what the person wants if they can no longer give informed consent or refusal, commonly which life-sustaining measures may be used when there is no reasonable expectation of recovery. Administering life-sustaining treatment against it can expose the provider to a medical battery suit, but a provider unaware of the living will will not lose such a claim.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Compliance Programs for Small Entities
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A two-physician practice cannot support a compliance officer even part-time. What does the OIG guidance suggest?
opciones: Naming a compliance contact, kept clear of billing and coding
Naming the office manager who runs the billing and the coding
Hiring an outside auditor to act as the compliance officer
Leaving the seven elements aside until the practice grows
preguntas.explicacion: A small entity still works through the seven elements, scaled to what it can carry. Where no compliance officer is possible, one person is designated as the compliance contact and made responsible for seeing the compliance work done; that person should be kept out of legal services and, wherever possible, out of billing, coding and claim submission.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1 and Section 7.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 lancet placement · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: How should the lancet be oriented on the fingertip in a capillary puncture?
opciones: On the side of the finger pad, crossing the fingerprint lines at a right angle
On the center of the fingertip pad, running along the fingerprint lines
On the side of the finger pad, running along the fingerprint lines instead
Over the very tip of the finger next to the nail, at a right angle to the nail bed
preguntas.explicacion: A finger puncture is made on the side of the pad, with the lancet crossing the print lines instead of following them; on the heel the spot is the medial or lateral plantar surface. One quick, firm stroke carried through gives a flow good enough that the patient need not be stuck again.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, Access to Medical Care for Individuals with Mobility Disabilities: Services and Facilities
preguntas.subtema: Reasonable modifications · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1 · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 7 k98 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for a change in how the office usually does things so that she can be seen. What is the limit on that duty?
opciones: The change is made unless it would alter the essential nature of the service
The change is made unless another patient objects to the way it affects his visit
The change is made unless it costs the practice more than a routine visit is paid
The change is made unless the practice has already made one for her this year
preguntas.explicacion: Providers owe full and equal access, and along with it modifications to policies, to practices and to procedures that are reasonable, whenever such a change is what makes the service fully available to a person with a disability. The single boundary written into the duty is a change that would alter the essential nature of what the practice does.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Location of the Heart; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Structure of the Heart
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the heart sit in the body?
opciones: In the mediastinum between the lungs, with the apex pointing to the left
In the mediastinum, with two thirds of its mass to the right of the midline
In the left pleural cavity behind the sternum, with the apex pointing right
In the pericardial cavity below the diaphragm, at the level of the third rib
preguntas.explicacion: The heart lies in the chest between the two lungs, in the space called the mediastinum, wrapped in its own pericardial sac; the base reaches the level of the third costal cartilage and the apex points a little to the left of the sternum, between the fourth and fifth ribs, with roughly two thirds of the mass left of the midline. That position decides where the stethoscope goes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: The superficial veins on the back of the hand arise from which structure, and where do they drain?
opciones: From the dorsal venous arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the dorsal venous arch, into the radial and ulnar deep veins
From the deep palmar arch, into the cephalic and basilic veins
From the median cubital vein, into the dorsal venous arch below it
preguntas.explicacion: On the dorsum of the hand the superficial veins spring from the dorsal venous arch, which drains into the cephalic and the basilic, the two main superficial channels of the limb. The palmar arches belong to the deep system and drain into the ulnar and radial veins instead.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · D2 2E k41 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: Beyond first and last name and date of birth, which further identifier is described as accepted for matching a patient to a specimen?
opciones: The social security number or the patient's address
The name of the insurance plan covering the visit
The color of the identification bracelet in use
The number of the room where the draw took place
preguntas.explicacion: Identification is built on the patient's first and last name and date of birth plus one further general identifier, and the examples given are the social security number or the address. Extra data of that kind lowers the risk of preventable error, which is why more than one item is used.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3, footnote b
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k57 k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic decides that stopper color alone will tell staff in what sequence to fill tubes. What problem remains?
opciones: The sequence still has to be followed; color by itself does not enforce it
Stopper colors are identical between manufacturers, so the risk is covered
Color tells the phlebotomist how many inversions each tube will need
Color identifies the additive, so carry-over between tubes cannot happen
preguntas.explicacion: Color coding makes the tubes easy to tell apart, but an incorrect collection still follows when the sequence is not respected, which is why training matters. Color codes can also differ from one laboratory to another, so they should be checked locally rather than assumed.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(xii), Personal Protective Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Caps and shoe covers · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Surgical caps or hoods and shoe covers are required by the standard in which situation?
opciones: Where gross contamination is reasonably anticipated, autopsies for instance
When a patient is uncooperative and may pull away during the venipuncture
Whenever blood may splash onto the face during a routine venipuncture
Whenever a patient is on Contact Precautions for a resistant organism
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(xii) reserves caps, hoods, shoe covers and boots for situations where gross contamination is reasonably anticipated, and gives autopsies and orthopedic surgery as the examples. An uncooperative patient is the example the standard uses in (d)(3)(ix)(D)(4)(ii) for when a blood donation center must require gloves; splashes to the face trigger masks and eye protection under (d)(3)(x); and Contact Precautions call for gown and gloves under the CDC recommendations, not for head or shoe covering.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 8: Draw samples in the correct order
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee asks why the tubes cannot simply be filled in whatever order is convenient. What reason does the WHO give in Step 8 for a fixed order of draw?
opciones: It prevents the additive in one tube from being carried over into the next tube
It ensures the tubes that need a full draw are filled while the tourniquet is still on
It gives the serum tubes 10 to 15 minutes to clot before the last tube is filled
It minimizes platelet clumping, which is the reason given for the capillary sequence
preguntas.explicacion: Step 8 states the purpose in one line: draw the tubes in the right order so that additives are not carried across from one tube to the next. The clotting time of 10 to 15 minutes is a processing detail for red tubes, not a reason for the order; and platelet clumping is the reason Chapter 7 gives for the reversed skin-puncture order, not for venipuncture.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: The same hospital had earlier published rejection figures for its routine core laboratory rather than the emergency one. Which reason topped that list?
opciones: Clotted specimens, followed by inadequate volume
Hemolysed specimens, followed by clotted ones
Misidentified specimens, followed by lipemic ones
Improper containers, followed by delayed transport
preguntas.explicacion: In the core laboratory clotted specimens accounted for 55.8 % of all rejections and inadequate volume for 29.3 %, a pattern the authors read as much like what the emergency laboratory saw. Most of those clotted tubes came from adult inpatient services, 54.3 %, and then from pediatric inpatient services, 26.8 %, which aims the training effort at the wards rather than at the laboratory.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Does Pneumatic Tube System Transport Contribute to Hemolysis in ED Blood Samples?" (West J Emerg Med 2016, PMC5017839), Introduction and Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: An emergency department reports that 15 % of its blood samples are hemolysed. How does that compare with published figures?
opciones: It sits inside the 6 to 30 % range reported for emergency departments, far above the 2 % ASCP benchmark
It is below the 20 % benchmark set by the ASCP for samples drawn during intravenous placement
It is unusually high, since emergency departments typically report hemolysis in fewer than 3 % of samples
It matches the 13 to 14 % rate expected for any sample sent through a pneumatic tube system
preguntas.explicacion: The American Society for Clinical Pathology sets 2 % as the benchmark, yet blood drawn in the emergency department hemolyses at 6 to 30 %; in the pneumatic tube study the ED figure was about 13.5 % against roughly 3 % elsewhere in the hospital, a gap the authors trace to blood taken during IV placement instead of by straight stick. The 13 to 14 % figure was that hospital's rate, not something the tube system caused.

preguntas.fuente: plainlanguage.gov, Federal plain language guidelines
preguntas.subtema: Plain language · CCMA 6 k206 · CMA II.F.2 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k95 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which federal statute requires that content written for the public be written for its specific audience?
opciones: The Plain Writing Act of 2010
The 21st Century Cures Act of 2016
The HITECH Act of 2009, part of ARRA
The Privacy Rule, published in 2000
preguntas.explicacion: Plain language means content that is clear and easy to grasp; the guidance presents it as more efficient and more effective, and as a legal duty besides. It was the Plain Writing Act of 2010 that laid down the requirement: whatever is written for the public has to be written for the particular audience it addresses. That is why pinning down the audience comes before drafting the letter or the handout.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 lancet depth · PBT II.J lancets · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.5 equipment for the test ordered
preguntas.pregunta: When preparing a lancing device for a fingerstick glucose test, what depth setting is advised?
opciones: No deeper than 2.0 mm, so the tip cannot reach and injure bone
No deeper than 3.0 mm, so the tip cannot reach and injure bone
At least 2.4 mm, to guarantee a drop large enough for the strip
The deepest setting on the first finger, then shallower on repeats
preguntas.explicacion: For a capillary glucose reading the device is set no deeper than 2.0 mm, which keeps the tip clear of bone; newer lancing devices also hurt less than the older systems. A modern meter runs on 0.3 to 1 microlitre, so there is nothing to gain from a deep stick. For finger punctures in general the ceiling is 2.4 mm.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Atrial Fibrillation", Differential Diagnosis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which strip is described as irregularly irregular?
opciones: One where the spacing between beats follows no pattern
One where the spacing changes in a repeating pattern
One where the spacing is even but the rate is above 100
One where the spacing is even but the QRS is over 120 ms
preguntas.explicacion: Sorting a strip into regular or irregular comes before naming anything. Even spacing is a regular rhythm whatever the rate or the width of the complexes; spacing that repeats a pattern is called regularly irregular, as in flutter; and spacing with no pattern at all is irregularly irregular, as in fibrillation.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(1)(ii) and (h)(1)(iv), Medical Records
preguntas.subtema: Employee medical record retention · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: How long must an employer keep the medical record it maintains for a phlebotomist with occupational exposure?
opciones: For the duration of employment plus 30 years
For 3 years from the date of the last entry
For 6 years from the date of the last entry
For the duration of employment plus 5 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(1)(iv) requires the records of paragraph (h) to be kept at least for the length of employment plus 30 years, following 29 CFR 1910.1020. The record itself holds the employee's name, hepatitis B vaccination status and dates, results of examinations and follow-up, the employer's copy of the written opinion and the information sent to the healthcare professional. Three years is the retention of training records in (h)(2)(ii); six years is the HIPAA documentation period in 45 CFR 164.530(j), a different regulation.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: An excluded provider's period of exclusion has now run its course. What happens to her standing with the federal programs?
opciones: Reinstatement is not automatic; she has to apply for it once the period ends
Reinstatement is automatic on the day the stated period of exclusion runs out
Reinstatement follows as soon as a state Medicaid agency enrolls her once more
Reinstatement follows as soon as a practice checks the list and cannot find her
preguntas.explicacion: The exclusions program is explicit that an excluded individual or entity does not get reinstated automatically when the specified period runs out; an application has to be made. That is why the list gets checked month by month rather than counted forward: a period that has expired does not by itself put anyone back into the federal programs.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia", section Evaluation (peripheral smear and pseudothrombocytopenia)
preguntas.subtema: Additives and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k57 k9 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A CBC drawn in EDTA reports a very low platelet count, but the smear shows the platelets stuck together in clumps. What is this called, and what causes it?
opciones: Pseudothrombocytopenia, from in vitro platelet clumping caused by EDTA-dependent agglutinins
True thrombocytopenia, from platelet destruction that had already begun before the blood was drawn
Hemoconcentration, from a tourniquet left in place for more than one minute
Platelet satellitism, from the sodium fluoride in a gray tube drawn before the EDTA
preguntas.explicacion: Platelet clumping can occur when EDTA is the anticoagulant, producing pseudothrombocytopenia, a falsely low count due to in vitro aggregation from EDTA-dependent agglutinins. It is an artifact of the tube, not a disease of the patient. Platelet satellitism is a different smear finding, and hemoconcentration is the tourniquet effect described in the phlebotomy chapter.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 6.2.2 and 7.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D4 4B assisting with pediatric collection · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 k130 wrapping · NCMA 2C.10
preguntas.pregunta: Blood is flowing poorly from a heel-prick in a cold, fussy infant. Which measure improves flow?
opciones: Keep the child warm and swaddled, with only the sampling limb bare; warmth can raise flow sevenfold
Lower the heel well below the level of the heart for two minutes so gravity fills the capillary bed
Squeeze the heel rhythmically at the puncture itself until a steady stream of blood appears there
Switch to a 25-gauge butterfly on the dorsal hand, which the WHO prefers when a heel-prick fails
preguntas.explicacion: The baby is kept warm: as few clothes off as possible, wrapped in a blanket, held by a parent with only the limb being sampled left out, and warm cloths on the site. Warmth can multiply the flow by as much as seven. Squeezing hemolyses the sample, and needles of 25 gauge or finer are the ones to keep away from.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Breast self-exam — Information
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B3 k64 · CMA I.A.5.a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: When in the month should a menstruating patient do a breast self-exam?
opciones: About three to five days after her period starts, at the same time each month
About three to five days before her period starts, at the same time each month
On the first day of her period, when the tissue is at its most tender
Halfway between two periods, which is when the tissue is most nodular
preguntas.explicacion: Three to five days after the period begins the breasts are least tender and least lumpy, which makes changes easier to notice; the point is to repeat it on the same schedule every month. After menopause, the same day of each month is used instead. Experts do not agree on whether the practice finds cancers or saves lives.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, footnote d
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist is worried that tissue fluid from a difficult puncture could contaminate a coagulation specimen. What does the WHO table allow in that situation?
opciones: Collecting a non-additive tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the light blue tube first and then a second one for the test
Collecting a purple EDTA tube before the light blue citrate tube
Collecting the citrate tube last, after all the additive tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Footnote d of Table 2.3 addresses this exact worry: if tissue fluid or thromboplastin could contaminate the specimen, a tube without additive can be drawn ahead of the additive tube. That keeps the sequence of the table intact, because the plain tube is position 2 and citrate is position 3. EDTA is far down the list at position 8, and citrate never moves to the end.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2 and section 5
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A sputum specimen for molecular bacterial testing is too thick to pipette and cannot be run today. Which pair of handling points applies?
opciones: Thin it with acetylcysteine or dithiothreitol; hold it at 4 to 8 °C for up to a week
Thin it with sterile saline; hold it at room temperature for up to a week
Thin it with acetylcysteine or dithiothreitol; freeze it at −20 °C the same day
Thin it with buffered glycerol; hold it at 4 to 8 °C for up to three days
preguntas.explicacion: Sputum is one of the viscous specimen types that jam automated pipetting, and the additives named for it are N-acetyl l-cysteine and dithiothreitol; homogenisation with inert beads in sterile buffer is the physical alternative. For storage the general guideline is 4 to 8 °C for up to seven days, with below −70 °C reserved for keeping it as long as twelve months.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Table 20.2 Comparison of Arteries and Veins; and 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 k7 (applied D3 k61 palpation, k62) · PBT I.A.2 I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: While palpating for a venipuncture site you feel a vessel that pulses. Which set of features identifies an artery rather than a vein?
opciones: Thick wall, small rounded lumen, high pressure, no valves
Thin wall, large flattened lumen, low pressure, valves in the limbs
Thin wall, large lumen, high pressure, valves present in the limbs
Thick wall, small lumen, low pressure, valves present in the limbs
preguntas.explicacion: Arteries have thick walls, a rounded appearance, high pressure and no valves; veins have thin walls, irregular often collapsed lumens, low pressure and valves, mostly in the limbs and below the heart. The pulse itself is the expansion and recoil of an artery as blood is ejected from the heart, so a pulsing vessel is an artery.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Examples of Safety Device Designs
preguntas.subtema: Self-blunting needles · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: How does a self-blunting phlebotomy needle protect the person drawing the blood?
opciones: A blunt cannula inside it is pushed past the tip before the needle leaves the vein
A spring pulls the needle back into the tube holder once the vein has been entered
A hinged shield snaps over the tip as the tube is pushed onto the holder
A blunt cap is screwed onto the tip once the needle has left the vein
preguntas.explicacion: In a self-blunting phlebotomy or winged-steel needle, a blunt cannula sits inside the needle and is pushed past the tip while the needle is still in the vein, so what finally leaves the patient is no longer sharp. Retracting needles and hinged or sliding shields are separate designs on the same list, and each works at a different moment; the blunting one is the only one that acts while the needle is still in the vein.

preguntas.subtema: Security incident · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: The firewall blocks a log-in attempt from outside the practice that never reached any record. Does the Security Rule count that as a security incident?
opciones: Yes, the definition takes in attempted as well as successful unauthorized access
No, an incident starts only once information has actually been reached or altered
No, unless the attempt is later shown to have exposed unsecured information
Yes, but only where the attempt interferes with how the information system runs
preguntas.explicacion: The wording is deliberately wide. It reaches unauthorized access, use, modification, disclosure or destruction of information whether the attempt succeeded or not, and it reaches interference with the way the system operates as well. Interference is one branch of the definition, not the whole of it, and the practice has to identify these events, respond to them, mitigate them and write them down.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: When Can Information Be Shared?; Issues of Concern: Selective Access
preguntas.subtema: How much to tell a colleague · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks a phlebotomist to place an IV line for a patient's chemotherapy. How much of the history should the request carry?
opciones: Only what the task needs; the reason for the therapy is not required
The full oncology history, so the phlebotomist can judge the vein
The diagnosis and the stage, since both work for the same employer
No history at all, since treatment details may not be shared
preguntas.explicacion: Providers are not restricted from talking to one another about treatment, and a patient's care would stall if they were. The caution is about how much: asking someone to place a line does not require telling them why the therapy was prescribed. That is the same minimum necessary thinking behind selective access to records, where a laboratory worker needs the laboratory record and not the whole medical history.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Sample Collection and Handling
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the light blue coagulation tube fall in relation to the serum tubes and the other additive tubes?
opciones: Ahead of all of them: before the clot activator, separator, heparin and EDTA tubes
After the serum tubes, but still ahead of the heparin and EDTA tubes
Last of all, because it is one of the tubes that requires a full draw
Immediately before the fluoride tube, since both of them require a full draw
preguntas.explicacion: The numbered table gives the citrate tube position 3, the clot activator 4, the serum separator 5, the heparin tubes 6 and 7, EDTA 8, ACD 9 and the fluoride/oxalate tube 10. The four-group summary used in the coagulopathy review says the same thing in fewer words: sterile containers first, coagulation tubes next, plain and gel tubes after them, and the remaining additive tubes last. Both put the coagulation tube ahead of every serum and additive tube, and the full-draw requirement, which the citrate, EDTA and fluoride tubes share, says nothing about position.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Time Pressures
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to sign for a procedure while already medicated in the holding area. Why is that criticised?
opciones: Consent should be a two-way talk with time to ask questions and reflect
Consent signed outside a clinic has to be witnessed by a second nurse
Consent is not valid unless the same clinician performs the procedure
Consent in writing takes the place of discussing risks and benefits
preguntas.explicacion: The improper methods singled out are these: discussing the procedure shortly before it happens; taking consent in the holding area just before surgery; and taking it while the patient is medicated or on the point of falling asleep. What is called for instead is a structured two-way dialogue in a clinic or an office, leaving the patient time to ask questions and to think.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations, inspection · NCMA 4.12 · RMA III.C.1 CLIA '88
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic holding a certificate of waiver gets an unannounced visit from a surveyor after a complaint from the public. Is that allowed?
opciones: Yes, waived sites escape routine biennial inspection but can still be inspected for cause
No, a waived site may be inspected only when it applies to change its certificate type
Yes, because waived sites are inspected on the same biennial schedule as everyone else
No, a waived site answers to its accreditation organization instead of to the surveyor
preguntas.explicacion: Waiver and provider-performed microscopy certificates are not subject to biennial inspection, but an inspection may happen at any time during operating hours to check for an imminent and serious risk, to evaluate a public complaint, to see whether testing has gone beyond the certificate, or to gather information on the waived list. Refusing an inspection can cost the certificate.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Indications: Five Moments for Hand Hygiene
preguntas.subtema: Moments for hand hygiene · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist has greeted the patient and is about to clean the skin for the puncture. Which moment for hand hygiene is that?
opciones: Before a clean or aseptic procedure
After contact with the patient nearby
After exposure to any body fluid
After leaving the patient's own room
preguntas.explicacion: There are five moments, two of them before and three of them after. The two before are touching a patient and beginning a clean or aseptic procedure; the three after cover body fluid exposure or glove removal, patient contact, and contact with the patient's immediate surroundings. Cleaning the skin for a puncture is the aseptic procedure itself, so hands are done again right before it and not only on arrival.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", sections Introduction and History (1973)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k14 · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA E.1.d (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which organization created the first patient bill of rights, in 1973?
opciones: The American Hospital Association (AHA)
The American Medical Association (AMA)
The American Cancer Society (ACS)
The Joint Commission (TJC)
preguntas.explicacion: The American Hospital Association produced the first patient bill of rights in 1973, a document about relationships between patients, professionals and organizations that carried little enforceability. The American Cancer Society also produced one in the same decade, and the AMA did not publish a list of patient rights until 2017. Such bills remain non-enforceable.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: false imprisonment
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: When is a person falsely imprisoned?
opciones: When they are confined in an area bounded in every direction, without consent
When they are asked to remain in a room until the paperwork has been finished
When they are told they may face a lawsuit if they leave the building early
When they are kept waiting far longer than the appointment time they were given
preguntas.explicacion: False imprisonment is intentionally restraining someone inside a bounded area without their consent or legal authority, and an area counts as bounded only if movement is blocked in every direction; a reasonable and safe way out means it is not. Restraint can come from a locked door, force, failure to release or misuse of authority. A threat of future legal trouble is not enough.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, section When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 k69 k74 · D1 1M k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports extreme pressure and severe pain in a large bruised area of the forearm. Why does that need urgent care?
opciones: It may be compartment syndrome, which can threaten the limb and life
It may be a periosteal bruise, which heals only after several months
It may be thrombophlebitis, which resolves once the arm is elevated
It may be simple swelling, which settles with ice applied every hour
preguntas.explicacion: A feeling of extreme pressure in a bruised part, especially when the area is large or very painful, can mean compartment syndrome, in which rising pressure cuts the blood and oxygen supply to the tissues. It is described as life-threatening and needing emergency care, sometimes surgery.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT VI.A · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Having measured an overall specimen rejection rate of 6 %, a laboratory sets itself a target below 2 %. Which two measures did it adopt to get there?
opciones: Monthly documentation of rejected samples and training where rejection is worst
Automatic acceptance of borderline samples and a monthly report to the medical director
A separate set of rejection criteria for the night shift and longer storage of rejects
Weekly rotation of the accessioning secretaries and a stricter barcode reading policy
preguntas.explicacion: The plan to bring 6 % down below 2 % rested on two things: enhanced documentation of every rejected sample, reviewed monthly, and periodic training organized for the departments with the highest rejection rates. Identifying and documenting the problem is described as the first step in improving quality; loosening the criteria would only move the error further down the line.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms, entry Preauthorization; and CMS, Medicare Program Integrity Manual, Chapter 3 (documentación, enmiendas y correcciones del registro)
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations · CMAA 4G k67, 6E · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: The plan approved the preauthorization for a scheduled procedure. What has the office actually obtained?
opciones: A decision that the service is medically necessary, with payment still not promised
A decision that the service is medically necessary, and a guarantee it will be paid
A decision that the patient has met the deductible for the plan year in question
A decision that the provider may bill the patient if the plan denies the claim
preguntas.explicacion: Preauthorization is the plan's finding that a service, a treatment plan, a drug or an item of durable medical equipment counts as medically necessary. The glossary is explicit that it is no promise the plan will cover the cost, since eligibility, benefits and coding still come into play when the claim is adjudicated. It says nothing about the deductible, and shifting liability to the patient is what an advance written notice of non-coverage does in Medicare.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Cerebrospinal Fluid Samples)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: A lumbar puncture yields three numbered sterile tubes. Which tube is routinely designated for microbiological culture and sensitivity?
opciones: Tube 2, with tube 1 going to chemistry and serology and tube 3 to cytology
Tube 1, with tube 2 going to chemistry and serology and tube 3 to cytology
Tube 3, with tube 1 going to chemistry and serology and tube 2 to cytology
Tube 1, with tube 2 going to cytology and tube 3 to chemistry and serology
preguntas.explicacion: Cerebrospinal fluid collected under strict asepsis, usually between L3-L4 or L4-L5, is distributed into three sterile tubes: the first for chemistry and serology, the second for culture and sensitivity, and the third for cytological examination. Processing has to be immediate, because delay degrades the cells and shifts the biochemical values, glucose in particular, so a mis-sent tube costs time the specimen does not have.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), What is a comprehensive metabolic panel?; and Lab Tests: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP), What is a basic metabolic panel?
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: An order is changed from a basic metabolic panel to a comprehensive one. Which measurements does the comprehensive panel add to the eight of the basic?
opciones: Albumin, total protein, ALP, ALT, AST and bilirubin
Phosphate, uric acid, lactate and blood ammonia
Cholesterol, triglycerides and the calcitonin level
Hemoglobin, hematocrit, platelets and the white count
preguntas.explicacion: The basic panel reports eight substances: glucose, calcium, the four electrolytes, and the two waste products BUN and creatinine. The comprehensive panel reports fourteen, adding albumin and total protein, the enzymes ALP, ALT and AST, and bilirubin, which is what lets it speak for the liver as well as the kidneys. Lipids and blood counts are ordered as separate tests.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.5
preguntas.subtema: Downtime registration · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient walks in while the record system is down. What does the contingency guidance expect the practice to have arranged?
opciones: Temporary record numbers to assign now and reconcile once the system returns
A paper chart opened under the patient's name and filed as a permanent record
A wait until the system returns, since a record cannot be opened without it
Registration in the read-only backup system, which accepts new patients too
preguntas.explicacion: Patient identification is one of the required practices for downtimes. There has to be a way to register a new patient while the system is unavailable, including assigning unique temporary record numbers, plus a process for reconciling those identifiers once the record system comes back. A read-only system, by definition, cannot take a new registration.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(1)(i)(A), (F), (G) and (I), Labels
preguntas.subtema: Labeling exemptions · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which container is exempt from the biohazard labeling requirement of the standard?
opciones: A unit of blood labeled as to contents and released for transfusion
A refrigerator that stores specimens of blood awaiting testing
A sharps container that is only one-quarter full
A bag of regulated waste that is going to an off-site incinerator
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(1)(i)(F) lets a unit go unlabeled when its container already states what is inside and it has been released for transfusion, or for another clinical use; (g)(1)(i)(G) does the same for individual containers placed inside a labeled one, and (g)(1)(i)(I) for waste that has been decontaminated. Refrigerators holding blood and containers of regulated waste are named in (g)(1)(i)(A) as needing the label, and a sharps container carries a label or color coding from the moment it goes into service under (d)(4)(iii)(A)(1)(iv), whatever its fill level.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how soon a urine culture will tell which organism is growing. What is the usual answer?
opciones: In 24 to 48 hours, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
In 2 to 4 hours, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
In 48 to 72 hours, the incubation time the plates need before any organism can be identified
In about a week, the incubation time the plates need before organisms can be identified
preguntas.explicacion: Urine is plated with a calibrated loop on media such as blood agar and MacConkey agar, held at 35 to 37 degrees Celsius, and read after 24 to 48 hours; that is also how long the laboratory tells the patient the culture takes. Susceptibility testing follows from the isolated colonies. A few unusual organisms, such as Oligella urolytica, need longer than 48 hours, which is the exception rather than the routine.

preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant realizes she charted a blood pressure in the wrong patient's record. How is the correction made?
opciones: The change is clearly and permanently marked, with its date and author identifiable
The wrong reading is erased or covered so that the record shows only accurate data
The entry is deleted from the system and re-entered under the correct patient name
The entry stays as it is, and a note about it goes into the practice incident log
preguntas.explicacion: CMS expects services to be documented when they are rendered, and accepts that entries sometimes have to be amended, corrected or added late. The date and the author of any amendment, correction or delayed entry must be identifiable, and the change or addendum must be clearly and permanently denoted. Reviewers examine such entries against the signature requirements of the same chapter.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion; PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337), Preanalytical phase studies recently published

preguntas.pregunta: A preterm infant on oxygen has a moderately hemolysed serum sample with an LDH ordered for monitoring. What approach did the neonatal laboratory and the surveyed neonatologists favor?
opciones: Report the approximate LDH with a comment that moderate hemolysis affects it, rather than rejecting it outright
Reject the LDH and every other analyte on the sample, since LDH is the analyte most sensitive to hemolysis
Correct the LDH with a formula based on the hemolysis index and report the adjusted value without a comment
Report the LDH only after a repeat heel sample, since a moderate index in a newborn always means in vivo hemolysis
preguntas.explicacion: LDH is a basic monitoring test in premature babies receiving supplementary oxygen and is very sensitive to hemolysis, so the laboratory may be slightly more permissive in them: raise the hemolysis borderline a little and report the approximate LDH with a note that moderate hemolysis affects it. That matches a survey in which neonatologists preferred receiving the result with a qualitative comment on the interference over having the LDH rejected. Correction formulas, by contrast, have been shown to be unreliable.

opciones: Bordetella pertussis, the cause of whooping cough
Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the cause of tuberculosis
Escherichia coli, the commonest cause of urinary infection
Streptococcus agalactiae, the group B strep of pregnancy
preguntas.explicacion: The nasopharyngeal culture samples the secretions of the throat at its very top, behind the nose, and serves for Bordetella pertussis, Neisseria meningitidis, Staphylococcus aureus including the methicillin-resistant strain, and for viruses: SARS-CoV-2, now the commonest reason for the test, plus respiratory syncytial virus and influenza. Tuberculosis is looked for in sputum, group B strep in a vaginal-rectal swab.

preguntas.explicacion: The 2025 SAFER guides come in eight titles across three groups, and each one names its own subject. Contingency Planning covers the safety practices tied to planned or unplanned EHR unavailability, meaning any time clinicians or other users cannot reach all or part of the system. The other three guides listed cover patient identification, test result follow-up and communication among clinicians and patients.

preguntas.pregunta: When a safety feature has to be activated by the user rather than working on its own, how should that be done?

With both hands, so the shield is seated squarely over the used needle
After the needle is in the container, where the tip can hurt no one
By the coworker who receives the device, before the tube is removed
preguntas.explicacion: A passive feature, one that needs nothing from the user, is preferred. Where the user does have to activate it, the recommendation is a single-handed technique that keeps both hands behind the exposed sharp, and a feature the user can plainly see has engaged. Waiting until the device is inside the container defeats the purpose, since injuries also happen during disposal, and passing an unprotected device to another worker adds a second person to the risk.

preguntas.pregunta: Which devices placed for venous access rule out a site for a routine draw?
opciones: A venous port, a central catheter or an intravenous catheter
A venous port only, since catheters can be drawn through safely
An intravenous catheter only, when fluids are actually running
A central catheter only, when the line was placed within a week
preguntas.explicacion: The contraindication is written broadly: any device used for venous access, and the three examples given are a venous port, a central catheter and an intravenous catheter. Blood taken from an existing peripheral access can be hemolyzed, contaminated, or diluted by fluid and medication.

preguntas.pregunta: A provider asks the medical assistant to chart that a patient "has capacity to consent." What should the assistant do?
opciones: Decline: the assessment belongs to a physician, PA or nurse practitioner
Chart it once the patient has answered the teach-back questions correctly
Chart it, since any licensed staff member is allowed to record it
Ask the unit nurse to perform the assessment and to chart it instead
preguntas.explicacion: Because of licensure, determining capacity falls outside the role of a nurse, a nursing assistant, a technician or other support staff; it is performed and documented by a licensed physician, a nurse practitioner or a physician assistant. Teach-back checks comprehension during the consent conversation, which is a different task, and psychiatry can be consulted for the hard cases.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A blood count report uses the word leukopenia. What does the ending of that term indicate?
opciones: A deficiency or lack of the cells named by the root
A blood condition involving the cells named by the root
An enlargement of the structure named by the root
An abnormal softening of the tissue named by the root
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -penia means a deficiency or lack, so leukopenia is too few white cells. The endings around it name other things: -emia is a blood condition, -megaly an enlargement, and -malacia a softening. Leukocytosis, with -osis for an abnormal condition, points the other way.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Characteristics of Leukocytes
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A CBC report lists white cells at 7,000 per microliter. How do leukocytes differ from the other formed elements?
opciones: They are complete cells with a nucleus, some 5,000 to 10,000 per µL
They are anucleate biconcave discs, numbering about 5 million per µL
They are cell fragments only 2 to 4 µm across, made in the marrow
They are complete cells that never leave the vessels, unlike erythrocytes
preguntas.explicacion: Among the formed elements only the white cells are complete cells, with a nucleus and organelles, and there are far fewer of them than red cells, about 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter, so 7,000 is in range. Red cells stay inside the vessels, while white cells cross the wall to work in the tissues. The anucleate discs are the red cells, and the fragments 2 to 4 micrometers across are the platelets.

preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a video visit has no working camera and asks whether the appointment is off. What do the categories of telehealth allow?
opciones: An audio-only call still counts as synchronous care when a video visit is not an option
An audio-only call counts as asynchronous care, since no picture is shared between them
The visit must be rebooked in person, because synchronous care requires live video
The visit must become a secure message exchange, which is the audio-only equivalent
preguntas.explicacion: Synchronous care means provider and patient interacting live, with a caregiver joining where that makes sense. The video call is the familiar shape of it, but audio-only calls are listed as synchronous as well, for occasions when a video visit is not possible, and so is secure text messaging used to answer a patient's questions.

preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.2 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which plasma protein is the most abundant and contributes most to the osmotic pressure of blood?
opciones: Albumin, about 54 percent of plasma protein
Fibrinogen, about 7 percent of plasma protein
Gamma globulin, the antibody fraction
Alpha globulin, which carries iron and lipids
preguntas.explicacion: There are three groups of plasma proteins. Albumin, made by the liver, is the largest share at about 54 percent (3.5 to 5.0 g/dL); it binds fatty acids and steroid hormones and is the main protein holding water inside the vessels, which helps keep blood volume and pressure. Globulins are second at about 38 percent, and the gamma fraction is the antibodies. Fibrinogen is about 7 percent and is needed for clotting.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, in situ
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A biopsy report reads carcinoma in situ. What do those last two words add?
opciones: The abnormal cells are still only where they first formed
The abnormal cells have reached one nearby lymph node only
The abnormal cells have already settled in a second organ
The abnormal cells are not cancer and will not spread at all
preguntas.explicacion: In situ means in its original place, so in a carcinoma in situ the abnormal cells are found only where they first formed and have not spread. That is a different statement from benign, which means the growth is not cancer, and from metastasis, where cells break away and start a new tumor somewhere else.

preguntas.pregunta: How long is the sharps injury log kept, and what happens when someone asks for a copy of it?

Three years after the training it documents, with the trainer's name removed
Thirty years after the employee leaves, with the device brand taken out
Five years, and copies go only to the Assistant Secretary who asks for them
preguntas.explicacion: The standard sends the log's retention to 29 CFR 1904.33, and the model plan spells out what that comes to: five years at minimum, counted from the close of the calendar year the log covers. The model adds that any copy handed out has the personal identifiers stripped, which matches the demand in (h)(5)(i) that the record keep the injured worker's identity confidential. Three years is the training record; employment plus thirty years is the medical record.

preguntas.pregunta: A clinic receives far more appointment requests every single day than its clinicians could ever see. What can open access do for it?
opciones: Nothing lasting, because no scheduling system works if demand always exceeds capacity
Solve it, because the model assumes the trouble is never a real shortage of capacity
Solve it, once the backlog has been worked down over six to eight weeks of longer days
Solve it, by going back to triaging the callers whose problems sound the most urgent
preguntas.explicacion: The model rests on the supposition that the problem is usually an imbalance between supply and demand rather than a shortage of capacity, and it can absorb excess demand on a given day. But the guide states the limit plainly: where demand is permanently greater than capacity, no scheduling system works. Clearing a backlog does not change that.

preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.2 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What proportion of blood plasma is water?
opciones: About 92 percent
About 55 percent
About 45 percent
About 7 percent
preguntas.explicacion: Plasma is about 92 percent water. Nearly all the rest, about 7 percent, is protein, and the electrolytes, gases, nutrients and wastes together add up to roughly 1 percent. The other figures belong to different measures: about 45 percent of whole blood is red cells (the hematocrit), and plasma is a little over half of whole blood, which is where a 55 percent figure comes from.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: An office has used the same automated blood pressure monitor daily for three years and has never had it serviced. What does accurate measurement require of the device?
opciones: That it be validated for use and calibrated again at intervals
That it be retired for a mercury column, the only exact gauge
That it be checked only when a reading looks wrong to the operator
That it be calibrated once, on the day it is first put into service
preguntas.explicacion: Accuracy is not technique alone; it is equipment too. An oscillometric monitor has to be validated as appropriate for use, and it has to be recalibrated from time to time, with the organization keeping up routine maintenance alongside standardized protocols and competency assessment. A device left to drift adds a systematic error that careful positioning cannot undo.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Arrhythmia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: What is sinus arrhythmia?
opciones: Variation in rate, with the R-R interval changing over 0.12 s
Variation in rate, with the R-R interval changing under 0.04 s
A run of early beats from a focus outside the sinus node
A rate that climbs above 100 and then falls back below 60
preguntas.explicacion: It is a variation of ordinary sinus rhythm: the spacing between beats shifts by more than 0.12 seconds while the P waves keep one shape and the pattern of activation from the sinus node. Vagus nerve activity during breathing produces it, and its presence usually points to good cardiovascular health.

Under ten seconds

preguntas.pregunta: A worker is stuck by another person's used needle. What are the first two actions?
opciones: Wash the area with soap and water or antiseptic, then seek medical care
Squeeze the wound to bleed it, then report the incident at end of shift
Cover the wound with a dressing, then wait for the source result to arrive

preguntas.explicacion: The exposed area is washed straight away with water and soap, or cleaned with a skin antiseptic, rubbing alcohol or hand sanitizer, and medical attention is sought at once. The same instructions apply to blood reaching the eyes, nose, mouth or skin, and prophylaxis is not delayed.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Shock", DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.j · 2027 I.B.8.j · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient waiting for the ambulance with signs of shock asks for a glass of water. What is the correct answer?
opciones: Nothing is given by mouth, not food and not fluids, while shock is suspected
Small sips of water are allowed as long as the patient can sit up alone
Water is allowed but food is not, since the stomach must stay empty
A sugary drink is offered, which raises the pressure while help is coming
preguntas.explicacion: Nothing is given by mouth to a patient in shock, neither food nor drink. The assistant calls for emergency help, checks airway, breathing and circulation, rechecks the breathing rate at least every 5 minutes, and keeps the patient warm. If the patient vomits or drools, the head is turned to one side to prevent choking.

preguntas.pregunta: On an acceptable tracing, what does an upright P wave and QRS complex in lead I tell the technician?
opciones: That the limb electrodes were applied the way they should be
That the chest electrodes were applied the way they should be
That the paper speed was set the way the standard asks for
That the calibration mark came out the height it should be
preguntas.explicacion: The standards ask that both the P wave and, except in rare cases, the QRS complex point upward in lead I, and that is read as a sign that the limb electrodes went on correctly. The opposite picture, everything inverted in lead I, points to swapped arm wires.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Skilled nursing facility (SNF) care: Coverage details and Who's eligible
preguntas.subtema: Transition of care to a SNF · CCMA 4H · CMAA 1 k1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A hospitalized patient will need daily physical therapy after discharge. What must have happened for Part A to cover a skilled nursing facility stay?
opciones: An inpatient hospital stay, medically necessary, of at least 3 days running beforehand
An inpatient hospital stay, medically necessary, of at least 7 days running beforehand
A face-to-face assessment by a nurse practitioner within 30 days after the discharge
A certification by two doctors that the patient's life expectancy is 6 months or less
preguntas.explicacion: Coverage in a skilled nursing facility rests on a qualifying inpatient hospital stay: at least three days in a row, counted from the day of admission as an inpatient but not the day of discharge. The patient must also enter the facility generally within 30 days of leaving and need daily skilled care. The face-to-face visit belongs to home health, the six-month prognosis to hospice.
