preguntas.subtema: Common tests and collection · CPT D3 k55 k57 · D2 k47 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A PT/INR is ordered for a patient with almost no usable arm veins. Which sample does the test also accept?
opciones: A sample taken from a fingertip
A sample taken from an ear lobe
A sample taken from a saliva swab
A sample taken from a urine specimen
preguntas.explicacion: This test may be run on blood from a vein or on blood from a fingertip, which is why point-of-care devices for it exist at all. A venous draw still takes under five minutes and the usual risks are no more than slight pain or bruising where the needle went in.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Latex Allergies - for Hospital Patients, Hospital Items That Contain Latex
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D II.J · CCMA 3E1 k128 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a latex allergy. Which items in a phlebotomy tray may contain latex?
opciones: Exam gloves, tourniquets and elastic bandages
Alcohol swabs, gauze pads and paper towels
Needles, tube holders and vacuum tubes
Glucometers, lancets and test strips
preguntas.explicacion: Latex turns up in hospital items such as surgical and exam gloves, in catheters and tubing, in tourniquets and medicine vials, and in elastic bandages and wraps; sticky tape and electrode pads are now often latex-free but should be checked. The patient should be given vinyl or silicone alternatives, and latex items removed from the room.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Measurement of Blood Pressure; and StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Cubital Fossa" (2023), section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1 · CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53)
preguntas.pregunta: When taking a manual blood pressure, where is the stethoscope placed, and which artery is being heard?
opciones: In the antecubital fossa, listening over the brachial artery
At the wrist, listening over the radial artery
At the neck, listening over the common carotid artery
In the antecubital fossa, listening over the median cubital vein
preguntas.explicacion: The cuff goes around the arm at heart level, and the stethoscope is placed on the antecubital region while the cuff deflates, to hear the Korotkoff sounds as blood returns through the brachial artery; the first sound marks the systolic pressure and the last the diastolic. The radial and carotid arteries are pulse sites, not where the cuff is read.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.9 Checklist for Wound Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.n · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: A wound culture is being taken. From where in the wound is the swab taken?
opciones: From a square centimeter of viable tissue at or near the center, never from pus or slough
From the thickest pocket of pus, where the organisms are present in the largest numbers
From the eschar at the edge, where the oldest tissue holds the longest-standing organisms
From the skin just outside the margin, where exudate collects and dries against the dressing
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen has to come from the cleanest tissue available, so a square centimeter of viable tissue at or near the center of the wound is chosen, and pus, slough, eschar and necrotic material are avoided; exudate is never collected from the skin. The swab is rotated over that area for five seconds with enough pressure to express fluid, and moistened with saline first if the bed is dry.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.a · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: What is the standing of skinfold thickness measurements in the clinic?
opciones: They vary widely between measurers and have had limited clinical use
They are the reference standard against which body mass index is judged
They have replaced waist circumference as the measure of central fat
They are taken with a tape rather than calipers at eight standard sites
preguntas.explicacion: Skinfolds are read with calipers at sites that include the chest and the abdomen, the subscapular area, the calf and the thigh, the iliac crest, the triceps and the biceps, pinching the skin about 2 cm from the point being measured. Even with a standard technique the readings vary a great deal, and their use in the clinical setting has so far been limited.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Muscular System: Muscle Types
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(2) (2027 I.C.6.f(2)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which three types of muscle tissue does the body contain, and which of them is both striated and involuntary?
opciones: Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; cardiac is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; smooth is striated and involuntary
Skeletal, smooth and cardiac; skeletal is striated and involuntary
Striated, spindle and rectangular; spindle is striated and involuntary
preguntas.explicacion: Skeletal muscle attaches to bone, is striated and is under voluntary control. Smooth muscle lines the hollow organs, is not striated and works involuntarily under the autonomic nervous system. Cardiac muscle sits in the heart wall and takes one feature from each: striated like skeletal, involuntary like smooth.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Burns", Considerations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 · CMA I.B.9.b · 2027 I.B.8.b · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A burn on a patient's forearm is red and painful and has raised blisters. How is that depth classified?
opciones: Partial thickness, the depth once called a second-degree burn
Superficial, the depth once called a first-degree burn
Full thickness, the depth once called a third-degree burn
Superficial with inhalation injury, since blisters mean smoke
preguntas.explicacion: Blisters mark the partial-thickness level, which reaches the outer layer and the layer beneath it and is painful, red and swollen. A superficial burn touches only the outer layer and gives pain, redness and swelling with no blisters. A full-thickness burn reaches the deep layers, looks white or charred, and the skin there may be numb.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Growth chart; and StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement" (NBK537315)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.c · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: How is height measured in a child under 3 years old at a well-child visit?
opciones: Lying down, as recumbent length, with the head and feet against the boards
Standing at a wall-mounted stadiometer, with the child's shoes taken off
Standing, but with a parent holding the child upright against the device
Lying down, with a tape run along the child from the crown to the knees
preguntas.explicacion: Under the age of 3 the measurement is taken lying down and is called recumbent length; from 3 years on it is taken standing. The head goes against the headboard with the body supine and the footboard brought against the soles, and a second person keeps the body and legs straight.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Grapefruit Juice and Some Drugs Don't Mix
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition and medications · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking simvastatin mentions the grapefruit juice he drinks every morning. What is the concern?
opciones: Grapefruit interacts with some statins, and the drug label may warn against it
Grapefruit cancels the statin's effect, so the dose has to be doubled
Grapefruit interacts with every drug taken by mouth, without exception
Grapefruit is only a problem when it is eaten whole, not as juice
preguntas.explicacion: Grapefruit and its juice can change how certain medicines work, and the FDA has required warnings on some of them. Statins such as simvastatin and atorvastatin are on the list, along with some blood pressure, transplant, anti-anxiety, corticosteroid, antiarrhythmic and antihistamine drugs. Not every drug in those classes is affected.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, opening paragraph; and Fibrinolysis
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In what order do the three steps of hemostasis occur after a vessel is punctured?
opciones: Vascular spasm, platelet plug, coagulation
Platelet plug, vascular spasm, coagulation
Coagulation, fibrinolysis, platelet plug
Vascular spasm, coagulation, fibrinolysis
preguntas.explicacion: Hemostasis is the sealing of a ruptured vessel, in three steps: first the smooth muscle of the vessel wall contracts (vascular spasm), then platelets stick to the exposed collagen and to each other (platelet plug), and finally a fibrin clot forms (coagulation). Fibrinolysis is not one of the three; it is the later breakdown of the clot as the vessel heals. Failure of any step leads to hemorrhage.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Where is the stethoscope placed for a manual reading?
opciones: Over the medial antecubital fossa, at the usual course of the brachial artery
Over the lateral antecubital fossa, where the radial artery begins its course
Over the middle of the cuff, so the sound reaches it through the inflated bladder
Over the wrist at the radial artery, where the pulse was palpated before inflating
preguntas.explicacion: The bell or the diaphragm goes on the inner side of the crease of the elbow, where the brachial artery runs, which is why the cuff leaves that space free. Positioning matters: shifting the stethoscope makes the sounds appear earlier or later and moves the recorded pressure with them.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Nosebleed", Home Care
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 · CMA I.B.9.a · 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room starts a nosebleed. How is it managed?
opciones: Sitting up and leaning forward, pinching the soft part for 10 full minutes
Sitting up and tilting the head back, pinching the bridge for 5 minutes
Lying down flat with a cold pack on the neck and the nostrils packed
Sitting up and blowing the nose gently every minute to clear the clots
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits, leans forward so blood is not swallowed, breathes through the mouth, and squeezes the soft part of the nose shut between thumb and finger for a full 10 minutes without checking early. Cold across the bridge of the nose may help; lying down is not advised, the inside of the nose is not packed, and sniffing or blowing waits.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: The dorsum of the hand is the preferred location for what?
opciones: Establishing an intravenous site
Routine venous blood sampling in adults
Arterial blood gas sampling
Capillary sampling in infants
preguntas.explicacion: The median cubital vein is the common site for drawing blood; the dorsum of the hand, by contrast, is the site of choice for starting an IV line. Arterial sampling is indicated for blood gases and is done on arteries, and the capillary site the chapter names for infants is the lateral plantar surface of the heel.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 2O k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: The only clearly visible vein in a patient's antecubital fossa forks into two branches right at the point that would be easiest to reach. What does the WHO's Step 3 say about that spot?
opciones: Do not insert the needle where veins diverge, because it raises the chance of a hematoma
Insert the needle at the fork, because two branches give the best blood flow
Insert the needle just below the fork only if the tourniquet has been on for less than a minute
Use the fork, since the biceps aponeurosis beneath it prevents hematoma formation
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 instructs the phlebotomist not to put the needle in where the veins divide, precisely because that raises the chance of a hematoma, and to look for a vein of decent calibre, plainly visible, straight and unobstructed. The protective role of the biceps aponeurosis applies to the median cubital vein in general, not as a license to puncture a branching point.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Respiratory Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k50 · CMA I.A.1.f · RMA III.E.3 Respiration c · NCMA 2B.5
preguntas.pregunta: What is recorded when the respiratory assessment is charted?
opciones: The rate, the depth of the breaths and the pattern they follow
The rate alone, since depth and pattern are subjective judgments
The rate and the oxygen saturation, which stands in for the depth
The rate and the position the patient was in during the counting
preguntas.explicacion: A respiratory rate on its own leaves out what the breathing looked like. The assessment characterizes rate, depth and pattern, because the pattern carries the diagnosis: deep and regular, cycling with pauses, or paradoxical chest movement each point somewhere different. Substituting an oximeter reading for a count is a known documentation problem.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Atrial Fibrillation", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which pattern is the hallmark of atrial fibrillation?
opciones: Irregularly irregular narrow complexes with no clear P waves
Regularly irregular narrow complexes with no clear P waves
Irregularly irregular wide complexes with clear P waves
Regular narrow complexes with a P wave before each of them
preguntas.explicacion: Atrial activity is so fast that no real P waves survive on the tracing, and only some impulses get through to the ventricles, which is what makes the spacing irregularly irregular. The pulse is irregular too, and the ventricular rate usually falls somewhere between 80 and 180 per minute.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Diabetes Diet, Eating, & Physical Activity — Plate method
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(b) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(b) · RMA I.D.1.c communication methods · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A newly diagnosed patient with diabetes is taught the plate method. How is the 9-inch plate divided?
opciones: Half nonstarchy vegetables, one quarter carb foods, one quarter protein foods
Half carb foods, one quarter nonstarchy vegetables, one quarter protein foods
One third each of nonstarchy vegetables, carb foods and protein foods
Half protein foods, one quarter nonstarchy vegetables, one quarter carb foods
preguntas.explicacion: The plate method controls portions without weighing or counting. Half the plate goes to nonstarchy vegetables, leafy greens, carrots, peppers or green beans for instance; a quarter to carb foods high in fiber, brown rice, whole grains, beans or fruit; and the last quarter to lean meats, fish, dairy or soy.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: How should V4, V5 and V6 look once all six chest electrodes are on?
opciones: Lined up horizontally along the fifth intercostal space
Lined up vertically down the left mid-clavicular line
Lined up horizontally along the fourth intercostal space
Lined up diagonally from the sternum toward the axilla
preguntas.explicacion: The last three chest electrodes share one level, the fifth intercostal space, so they should form a straight horizontal row from the mid-clavicular line out to the mid-axillary line. Checking that row before recording catches an electrode that has crept up or down a space.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Disorders of Clotting
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 3C bleeding disorders) · PBT I.C · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: A male patient bleeds into his joints after exercise and lacks functional factor VIII. Which disorder is this, and how common is it among hemophilias?
opciones: Hemophilia A, roughly 80 percent of cases
Hemophilia B, roughly 20 percent of cases
Hemophilia C, the rare autosomal form
Thrombocytopenia, a shortage of platelets
preguntas.explicacion: Hemophilia is a group of inherited disorders in which one or more clotting factors are not produced in functional amounts. Hemophilia A, a deficiency of factor VIII, accounts for about 80 percent of cases; hemophilia B, a deficiency of factor IX, about 20 percent. Both are X-linked and typically passed from carrier mothers to sons. Hemophilia C is a rare autosomal defect of factor XI.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex G, Antiretroviral drugs for PEP; CDC, Clinical Guidance for PEP, Exposure to HIV is a medical emergency
preguntas.subtema: Starting PEP before results · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: The rapid HIV test on the source patient will not be back for hours. What do the WHO and CDC guidance say about starting PEP?
opciones: Start it without waiting for results; stop it later if the source proves negative
Wait for the result, since PEP is only prescribed once the source is confirmed positive
Start it only if the worker's own baseline test is negative and the 72-hour window has closed
Skip it and rely on follow-up testing at 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months
preguntas.explicacion: A health worker should not wait for test results before taking or giving PEP, and the prophylaxis can be stopped if the source turns out negative. The CDC says the same about the exposed person's own rapid test: when it has not come back and prophylaxis is indicated, the first dose goes in immediately, to be stopped later if the person has HIV or the source proves not to. The 72-hour window is the deadline for starting, not a period to wait out, and follow-up testing complements PEP rather than replacing it.

preguntas.subtema: Rescinding an authorization · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.2.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient revokes his consent to share his substance use disorder records. What about what was already sent?
opciones: The revocation does not undo disclosures already acted on in reliance
The revocation obliges the recipient to return or destroy the records
The revocation is only valid if it is given before the expiration event
The revocation must be approved by the program before it takes effect
preguntas.explicacion: The consent form has to tell the patient how to revoke it in writing, and that the right to revoke does not reach back over what the program or another lawful holder has already done in reliance on the consent. The program does not get to approve or refuse the revocation, and revoking is not tied to the expiration date the form carries.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A main term in the alphabetic index carries a see instruction. What does the coder do with it?
opciones: Go to the term the note names, since that is where the code is
Use the code beside the main term and read the other term later
Look at the other term only if the first gives no useful code
Verify the main term in the tabular list without looking further
preguntas.explicacion: A see note after a main term means the coder has to go to the term it points at in order to find the right code. That is different from a see also note, which offers another main term that may hold useful entries but need not be followed when the original main term already gives the code that is needed.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 5.4: Metric Equivalencies
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k17 · CMA I.D.2.b(1) · RMA III.G.2.f · NCMA 1.7
preguntas.pregunta: Within the metric system, which way does the decimal point move when a larger unit is converted into a smaller one?
opciones: To the right, because the unit is getting smaller
To the left, because the unit is getting smaller
It stays put, since only the unit's name changes
It moves both ways, depending on the drug ordered
preguntas.explicacion: The metric system is organized in units of ten, so a conversion inside it only moves the decimal point: to the right when going to a smaller unit, and to the left when going to a larger one. Grams to milligrams is a move to the right by three places; milligrams to grams is the same move to the left. The prefixes run kilo, hecto, deca, the base unit, deci, centi and milli.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient treated for pneumonia has the cough and fever that illness routinely brings. Are those coded as well?
opciones: No, symptoms routinely tied to a disease process are not coded on their own
Yes, every symptom the provider documents is coded along with the disease
Yes, but only as secondary codes placed after the code for the disease
No, unless the provider states in the note that they are unrelated to it
preguntas.explicacion: Signs and symptoms that go with a disease process as a matter of course are not assigned as additional codes, unless the classification instructs otherwise. Additional signs and symptoms that are not routinely associated with the disease are coded when they are present. So the test is whether the finding is part of the illness or beyond it.

preguntas.fuente: DailyMed, GLUMETZA (metformin hydrochloride) extended-release tablets, Boxed Warning
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k24 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.e · NCMA 1.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which risk does the boxed warning of an extended-release metformin product describe?
opciones: Lactic acidosis, with malaise, myalgia, breathing trouble, drowsiness and belly pain
Hypoglycemia deep enough to bring on seizures, coma and death if a meal is missed
Fetal toxicity, so that the drug has to stop as soon as a pregnancy is detected
Anaphylactic reactions, occasionally fatal, of the kind seen with beta-lactam drugs
preguntas.explicacion: The box on this label describes metformin-associated lactic acidosis reported after marketing: cases have ended in death, and in hypothermia, hypotension and bradyarrhythmias that resist treatment. It names the risk factors, kidney impairment, age 65 or over, contrast studies, surgery and heavy alcohol use among them, and it directs that the drug be stopped and hemodialysis started promptly when acidosis is suspected.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.3 A-C Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: What can cause alternating-current interference on a tracing?
opciones: Loops in the lead wires, or poor electrode contact
A cold patient, or a nerve disorder of the arms and legs
A pillow under the head, or crossed legs on the table
Scaly skin, or an electrode placed over breast tissue
preguntas.explicacion: Interference from the current in the walls is common in clinics and hospitals, and it traces back either to poor contact at an electrode or to equipment near the room. Wires are pulled straight when they are attached because a loop in a lead wire also invites it.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.2 Pre-examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is on the table for a 12-lead. How is the examination gown handled?
opciones: A man's gown top comes off; a woman's stays draped over her chest
A woman's gown top comes off; a man's stays draped over his chest
Both gowns come off, and a sheet is drawn up over the shoulders
Both gowns stay closed, and the electrodes go on top of them
preguntas.explicacion: A male patient takes the top of the gown off so the chest is exposed. A female patient slips her arms out but keeps the gown over her chest, and after the chest electrodes are on, the gown is carefully re-draped over her while the tracing is recorded.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: For Notification and Other Purposes
preguntas.subtema: Family involvement · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's adult daughter is helping with his care and asks about the medication list. What does the Privacy Rule permit?
opciones: Sharing what is directly relevant to her involvement in his care, on his informal permission
Sharing the entire record with her, since a relative helping with care stands in for the patient
Withholding the list unless she is appointed as his personal representative by a court
Sharing only after she signs an authorization form on the patient's behalf at the front desk
preguntas.explicacion: On informal permission a covered entity may give family, relatives, friends or anyone else the patient names whatever bears directly on that person's part in the care or in paying for it. That is narrower than a personal representative, who stands in the patient's shoes for every purpose. The same provision lets a pharmacist hand filled prescriptions to somebody acting for the patient.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Asynchronous Telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Asynchronous telehealth · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A primary care clinician sends a focused question to a specialist and receives the answer two days later. Which telehealth service is that?
opciones: An electronic consultation, which is one of the asynchronous arrangements
A facilitated virtual visit, where an assistant gathers the objective data
A teletriage visit, used to sort symptoms quickly in an urgent setting
A remote critical care consultation, which guides a team at the bedside
preguntas.explicacion: The asynchronous, store-and-forward route collects history, images and diagnostic data and passes them to a specialist who reads them later. An e-consult, in which the primary care clinician puts a focused question to a specialist, sits in that group, together with portal messaging, teledermatology, off-site reading of images and digital intake questionnaires.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5, Note
preguntas.subtema: Antiseptic agents and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 3G k63 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A basic metabolic panel was drawn after the skin was prepared with povidone iodine. Which results does the WHO warn may be falsely raised?
opciones: Potassium, phosphorus and uric acid
Sodium, chloride and bicarbonate
Glucose, BUN and creatinine
Albumin, bilirubin and total protein
preguntas.explicacion: The note to Step 5 explains why alcohol is preferred over povidone iodine: blood contaminated with iodine may show falsely increased potassium, phosphorus or uric acid. The other groups are real components of the metabolic panels (electrolytes, kidney waste products, liver proteins), but the WHO does not link them to iodine contamination.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Vacuum extraction systems
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which two mechanisms does the WHO describe in some vacuum-tube systems for dealing with the used needle?
opciones: One retracts the needle into the barrel and snaps shut; another releases it into the sharps container
One shears the needle from the hub with a small blade; another bends it so it cannot be used a second time
One recaps the needle automatically; another sterilizes it in place for reuse on the same patient
One dissolves the needle in disinfectant; another seals it inside the last tube that was filled
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 says some systems have a mechanism that, once the needle has been used, retracts it into the barrel and snaps it shut, while others have a quick-release mechanism that dislodges the used needle straight into the sharps container. Shearing a contaminated needle, or breaking it, is forbidden by OSHA, and no source describes automatic recapping, dissolving or sealing a needle in a tube.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.10 Checklist for Intermittent Suture Removal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m · NCMA 2B.16
preguntas.pregunta: Which sutures are taken out first when an incision line is being cleared?
opciones: Every second one, with the wound reassessed before any of the rest come out
Every one at once, since leaving some in place delays the closure of the skin
The two at the ends first, since they carry the most tension along the line
The ones nearest any redness first, since those are the ones most likely to infect
preguntas.explicacion: Alternate sutures are removed first, then the wound is judged again: if the edges are well approximated the rest can follow, and if there is doubt the remainder wait several days. Removing them all too early risks dehiscence. Steri-Strips may be applied before removal to lower that risk, and the line is watched for separation throughout.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, About Body Mass Index (BMI)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: From what age is body mass index calculated in children, and how often?
opciones: From the age of 2, and once a year as part of the growth assessment
From the age of 5, and once a year as part of the growth assessment
From birth, and at every well-child visit alongside length and weight
From the age of 2, but only when the weight has crossed a percentile line
preguntas.explicacion: The index can be worked out from the age of 2, once height and weight are both being measured in the usual way, and an annual assessment using the growth charts is recommended from that age. Tracking it over time is what makes it useful, for monitoring growth and development and for dosing medicines.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Yearly "Wellness" visits, Coverage details
preguntas.subtema: Pre-appointment screening · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a yearly Wellness visit asks what the questionnaire the office sent her ahead of the appointment is for. What is it?
opciones: A Health Risk Assessment, which feeds her prevention plan
A financial responsibility form, which sets her share of the cost
A notice of privacy practices, which records her acknowledgement
An advance directive, which records her wishes about treatment
preguntas.explicacion: Part of the visit is a questionnaire the provider hands out, the Health Risk Assessment, whose answers are used to build or update the personalised prevention plan for that patient. Advance directives do come up at that visit, but as an offer to talk about them, and they are a different document altogether.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Definition of Breach
preguntas.subtema: Breach presumption · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A staff member e-mails a lab result to the wrong patient. How does the Breach Notification Rule treat that event at the outset?
opciones: As a breach, unless a risk assessment shows a low probability that the information was compromised
As a breach only after the Office for Civil Rights investigates and reaches that conclusion
As an incidental disclosure, since a misdirected message cannot reasonably be prevented
As a security incident rather than a breach, because e-mail systems are technical safeguards
preguntas.explicacion: Any use or disclosure that the Privacy Rule does not permit is presumed to be a breach. The presumption only falls where the covered entity or business associate demonstrates, through a risk assessment, a low probability that the PHI was compromised. An entity may also skip the assessment entirely and simply notify.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.5.2 Lead Patterns
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.5 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: Every complex in lead I comes out inverted. What is checked first?
opciones: The arm electrodes, which are almost certainly reversed
The leg electrodes, which are almost certainly reversed
The chest electrodes, which are almost certainly reversed
The clip connectors, which are almost certainly loose
preguntas.explicacion: Inverted complexes throughout lead I point to the two arm wires having been swapped, a common error that the technician does not always catch. Reversed leads can even produce something that looks like electrical interference, so the hook-up is verified before blaming the room or the machine.

preguntas.fuente: NHA Candidate Handbook (2026), Code of Ethics; and Maintaining your Certification
preguntas.subtema: Professional development · CPT D1 k26 · CCMA 7C · RMA I.C.4.e · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: What does that code say about a certified professional's knowledge over time?
opciones: That learning continues and that the person keeps up with current research
That the original training is sufficient until the credential is renewed
That new techniques are learned only through the employer's own program
That research is followed only when the employer pays for the coursework
preguntas.explicacion: One of the six duties is to keep learning, applying and advancing knowledge and skills, practical and scientific alike, and to stay current with the latest research and how it is used in practice. Nothing ties that duty to who pays or who provides the course, and the very purpose of renewing the credential is to show that the holder stays current.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Lavender; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Table 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: By what mechanism does the EDTA in a purple top tube keep the blood from clotting?
opciones: It binds the calcium in the sample so the coagulation cascade cannot proceed
It inhibits the formation of thrombin, as the heparin in a green tube does
It activates clotting on contact so the cells can be spun away from the serum
It blocks the breakdown of glucose, which also keeps the cells from clumping
preguntas.explicacion: EDTA works by chelating the calcium ions in the blood, and the WHO table describes the same action as forming calcium salts to remove calcium. Because the blood never clots, the liquid left after spinning is plasma. Thrombin inhibition is how heparin works, contact activation is the plain red tube, and blocking glycolysis is the sodium fluoride of the gray tube.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Business Associate Notice
preguntas.subtema: Business associate breach · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: The practice's billing vendor suffers a breach of unsecured PHI. What does the vendor owe the practice?
opciones: Notice straight away, and in any event within 60 days of the vendor discovering it
Notice within 30 days, together with the individual notices already mailed on its own
No more than its yearly report to the Secretary, which the practice can look up
Notice only once the practice asks, since the duty to notify patients rests with the practice
preguntas.explicacion: A business associate that suffers a breach has to tell the covered entity straight away, and in any event within 60 days of discovery; it should also identify each affected individual and hand over what the entity needs to write its own notices. Responsibility for notifying the individuals stays with the covered entity, though it may delegate the job to the business associate where that makes more sense.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.1 Baseline Drift
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k148 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: The tracing shows a wandering baseline in leads I and II. Which correction comes first?
opciones: Clean the sites again with alcohol and dry them with gauze
Straighten the lead wires so that no loops are left in them
Ask the patient to hold a breath while the strip is recorded
Switch the machine off and on so the self test runs again
preguntas.explicacion: Leads I and II both take their signal from the arm electrodes, so the sites those leads share are the place to look. Poor skin preparation heads the list of causes, and the remedy given for it is more alcohol to clean and gauze to dry before the electrode goes back on.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 2.2 Description of Equipment and Supplies
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k152 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: The room is set up before the patient comes in. Which set of supplies is laid out?
opciones: Silver chloride electrodes, alcohol, gauze and paper tape
Silver chloride electrodes, iodine, cotton and cloth tape
Carbon electrodes, alcohol, gauze and adhesive bandages
Silver chloride electrodes, saline, gauze and elastic wrap
preguntas.explicacion: The tray holds silver chloride electrodes with their clip connectors, alcohol and gauze for the skin, table paper, paper tape, a wax cosmetic pencil for the chest marks and scissors. Iodine and saline belong to other procedures and do not go into this one.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Max packing · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5C k171 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: While a practice works down its backlog it is told to apply max packing. What does that mean in the appointment book?
opciones: Handling any upcoming preventive or screening need at whatever visit brings the patient in
Booking the patient's next preventive and screening visits before she leaves the office
Replacing one-to-one visits for a chronic condition with a single group visit
Using the telephone and e-mail for concerns that do not really need a visit at all
preguntas.explicacion: Max packing reduces the demand for future visits by dealing with preventive and screening needs whenever the patient is already there, whatever the reason for that visit. Group visits for patients who share a chronic condition, and using phone and e-mail for concerns that need no visit, are two other tactics the same section lists for reducing demand.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: Asking for accommodations · CMAA 4H k62 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient is being booked for her first video visit. Should she tell the practice about her need for captioning before the day of the visit?
opciones: Yes: she should tell the provider if she needs support such as closed captioning or a screen reader
Yes, but only where the platform the practice uses has no captioning already built into it
No: accommodations are arranged by the clinician once the visit begins and the need is plain
No: a video visit will not suit her, and an office appointment should be booked in its place
preguntas.explicacion: The preparation list for patients includes asking for help where it is needed: the provider is to be told if the patient needs support such as a screen reader, closed captioning or anything else. The same list has her check the visit details in the reminder she is sent, find a quiet place with good internet access, and test the device she will use, with help from the team if she wants it.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Chemical burn or reaction", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.t · 2027 I.B.8.t · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A chemical splashes into a patient's eye at the front desk. What is done?
opciones: Flush the eye with running water for at least 15 minutes and get help
Cover both eyes with a dry pad and send the patient to the hospital
Rinse the eye for 30 seconds and then check the vision with a chart
Hold the eyelid open and wipe the chemical away with sterile gauze
preguntas.explicacion: A chemical in the eye is flushed with water immediately and the irrigation keeps going for at least 15 minutes under running water, and medical help is sought right away. Household remedies, ointments and salves are not put on a chemical burn, and a blister or dead skin is left alone.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth barriers · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k55 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her video appointments freeze constantly. Which barrier does HHS name as the biggest one for telehealth?
opciones: No access to an internet service fast enough to carry video reliably
Lack of a telephone line at the address where the patient normally lives
Lack of a signed consent form covering the use of video technology
Lack of a printer at home for the visit summary the clinician sends
preguntas.explicacion: The barrier named as the biggest of all is having no access to an internet service fast enough to carry video. The suggestions offered are that the patient may qualify for federal help through the Lifeline program, that plenty of fast food restaurants push free Wi-Fi out into the parking lot, and that most public libraries offer high-speed internet and often a private room.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Cardiovascular System: Arteriosclerosis; and 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Heart Defects
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1
preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes atherosclerosis from arteriosclerosis?
opciones: Atherosclerosis is plaque in the wall, one specific type of arteriosclerosis
Arteriosclerosis is the plaque buildup; atherosclerosis is generalized loss of compliance
Atherosclerosis affects the veins of the legs; arteriosclerosis affects the arteries
Arteriosclerosis is a congenital narrowing of the aorta; atherosclerosis is acquired
preguntas.explicacion: Arteriosclerosis is the general loss of arterial compliance, the hardening of the arteries, which raises pressure and resistance and drives hypertension and coronary disease. Atherosclerosis is the more specific buildup of plaque, triglycerides, cholesterol, leukocytes and calcium trapped in a damaged wall, and is one type of arteriosclerosis. A congenital narrowing of the aorta is coarctation.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Exposure to Blood: What Healthcare Personnel Need to Know (2003), Risk of Infection After Exposure: HBV
preguntas.subtema: HBV transmission risk · CPT D1 k31 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k97 k123 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: For a susceptible worker, the CDC puts the risk of HBV infection from a single needlestick with HBV-positive blood at which figure?
opciones: 6 to 30 percent, depending on the source's HBeAg status
0.3 percent, the same figure the CDC gives for HIV
About 1.8 percent, the same as for hepatitis C
Under 0.1 percent, since most workers are vaccinated
preguntas.explicacion: A susceptible person stuck or cut with HBV-infected blood faces a 6 to 30 percent chance of infection, and where in that range depends on the source's hepatitis B e antigen status: HBsAg-positive individuals who are also HBeAg-positive carry more virus and transmit more readily. Workers who were vaccinated and developed immunity are at virtually no risk, which is why the question specifies a susceptible worker. There is no known risk from intact skin. The 0.3 and 1.8 percent figures are for HIV and HCV.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peak Flow Rate Measurement", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(13)(c)· NCMA 2B.14
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's peak flow reading falls at 65% of her personal best. Which zone is that?
opciones: The yellow zone, which runs from 50% to 80% of personal best
The green zone, which runs from 50% to 80% of personal best
The yellow zone, which runs from 30% to 50% of personal best
The green zone, which runs from 65% to 100% of personal best
preguntas.explicacion: The meter is marked in three zones after a traffic light. Green covers 80% to 100% of personal best, and with no symptoms the patient carries on as before. Yellow runs from 50% to 80% and is where the written action plan starts, beginning with the bronchodilator. The zones only work alongside the symptoms, not instead of them.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k135 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: A lavender EDTA tube for a CBC arrives with a visible red-cell clot. Which handling error is the most likely cause according to the rejection study?
opciones: Poor mixing after collection and leaving the tube lying horizontally instead of upright
Centrifuging the tube too soon, before the anticoagulant had time to dissolve
Transporting the tube in a padded holder, which stops the additive from circulating
Filling the tube above its nominal volume so that the EDTA was diluted by excess blood
preguntas.explicacion: Visible clots in anticoagulated tubes, whether red-cell clots in whole blood or fibrin in plasma, are attributed mainly to poor mixing after the draw and to tubes left horizontal rather than vertical; manufacturers and CLSI ask for gentle inversion several times to bring blood and additive into contact. Anticoagulated tubes are not centrifuged for a CBC, and racks or padded holders are the recommended way to carry tubes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Interpretation of Vital Signs
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k55 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.1.a · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: Over four hours a patient's pulse and respiratory rate climb steadily, though every value is still inside the usual range. How is that read?
opciones: As possible early deterioration, since the trend carries more than one value
As normal, since a value inside the reference range is by definition normal
As measurement error, since real change would cross the range boundaries
As anxiety, the usual reason for a rise while the readings stay in range
preguntas.explicacion: Vital signs are compared with the patient's own earlier values, not only with a reference range. Trends over time carry more meaning than isolated measurements in evolving infection, bleeding, respiratory failure or shock, and even modest progressive change can be early physiologic deterioration while every reading still sits inside the traditional range.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(g)(6)(i) and (g)(6)(iii), Safety data sheets
preguntas.subtema: A shipment with no SDS · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A shipment of a hazardous disinfectant arrives at a laboratory with a label but no safety data sheet. What must the employer do?
opciones: Obtain one as soon as possible from the manufacturer or the importer
Return the shipment unopened, since the sheet travels with the label
Write one from the label, which carries the same hazard information
Wait for the next shipment, which must include the updated sheet
preguntas.explicacion: Manufacturers and importers have to provide a safety data sheet with the first shipment and with the first shipment after the sheet is updated, either with the containers or beforehand. When a shipment labeled as a hazardous chemical turns up without one, the duty falls on the distributor or the employer to get one from whoever made or imported the chemical, as fast as they can, and those parties must also supply a sheet on request. A label alone is no substitute: it carries a fraction of what the sheet holds.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient identification and labeling)
preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · NCMA 2C.14 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist collects three patients' tubes and labels them all at the desk afterwards. When and where should tubes be labeled?
opciones: Tube identification and labeling are done in the presence of the patient to avoid misidentification
Labeling at the desk is acceptable if the tubes were kept in separate racks per patient
Labels are applied before the draw, at the desk, so that the tubes are ready when the patient arrives
Labeling may wait until the laboratory receives the tubes with the matching requisitions
preguntas.explicacion: Identifying the tube and labeling it are both done with the patient present, so that a tube is far less likely to be misidentified, and identification data and labeling are double-checked before the blood is withdrawn. Its complications section adds that identifying the patient and labeling the tube are where the likeliest errors of the job happen.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 4, 8 and 9
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · D2 k47 · PBT II.J II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: Tissue typing, a paternity study and a DNA study are requested on the same patient. How many different tube types does the table assign?
opciones: One, because all three are listed against the same pale yellow tube
Two, because paternity work is listed against the purple EDTA tube
Three, because each of the three studies has its own tube and color
Two, because DNA studies are listed against the red clot activator tube
preguntas.explicacion: The pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube carries all three uses in one row: HLA tissue typing, paternity testing and DNA studies. EDTA is listed for hematology and cross-match, and the red clot activator tube for chemistries, immunology, serology and cross-match, so neither takes those studies.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.4, Availability of appropriate supplies
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic in a low-resource setting cannot afford safety-engineered devices. What does the guidance accept?
opciones: A needle and syringe used with skill is accepted in that situation
Draws should be postponed until safety devices can be purchased
Needles may be reused between patients if they are sterilized first
Only capillary sampling should be offered until devices arrive
preguntas.explicacion: Cost drives what a low-resource service can buy, and where safety-engineered devices cannot be had, a needle and syringe used with skill is accepted. What is not negotiable is that every patient gets a sterile needle and syringe, which is why enough supplies have to be stocked.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E7 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: An ESR rack sits on a shelf that leans a few degrees away from vertical. How much can that change the result?
opciones: Three degrees off vertical can raise the value by as much as thirty percent
Three degrees off vertical can lower the value by as much as thirty percent
Thirty degrees off vertical can raise the value by as much as three percent
Tilt has no measurable effect once the tube has been standing for an hour
preguntas.explicacion: Tube orientation is one of the technical factors that alters this measurement: tilt and vibration both push the value up, and an angle of three degrees from vertical can raise it by up to thirty per cent. Elevated room temperature and direct sunlight also raise the reading.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, TeamSTEPPS 3.0, Tool: Two-Challenge Rule
preguntas.subtema: Escalation · CCMA 6K k210 · CMAA 2B k25 · NCMA EKB 22
preguntas.pregunta: The safety problem is still unresolved after the concern has been voiced twice. What comes next?
opciones: A stronger course: bring in others and go up the chain
A repeat of the same concern in exactly the same words
A note in the chart that the concern was not accepted
A pause until the next shift takes over the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Where the outcome is still unacceptable, a stronger course falls to the challenger: bring in other team members, then go to the supervisor and up the chain of command. Once the chain is invoked it is essential to tell the whole team that additional input has been sought.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Evacuation Plans and Procedures eTool, Emergency Action Plan: Minimum Requirements [29 CFR 1910.38(c)]
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.a · 2027 I.B.7.a · CMAA 3 k45 · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: Under OSHA's emergency action plan rule, which element must the plan contain?
opciones: A way to account for all employees once the evacuation is finished
A list of the medicines kept in the office emergency supplies
A copy of the safety data sheet for every product in the building
A record of the annual training given to each employee by name
preguntas.explicacion: The rule sets a floor of six elements: a way to report fires and other emergencies, the evacuation procedures with escape routes assigned, procedures for employees who stay to run critical operations, accounting for everyone after the evacuation, rescue and medical duties for those who perform them, and names or job titles to contact.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Elbow Cubital Fossa", sections Introduction and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D3 3F k61 k62 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: In which layer of the cubital fossa does the median cubital vein actually lie?
opciones: In the roof, superficial to the tendon sheet that reinforces it
In the floor, deep to the brachialis and supinator muscles below
Beside the brachial artery, between the two heads of pronator teres
Under the biceps tendon, which shields it from the skin above it
preguntas.explicacion: The roof of the fossa is skin and fascia reinforced by the bicipital aponeurosis, and the median cubital vein runs within that roof, which is why it can be reached with a short needle. The floor is formed by brachialis above and supinator below, well away from any superficial vein.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k135 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c)
preguntas.pregunta: A light blue citrate tube for PT and aPTT arrives filled to about two-thirds of its nominal volume. Applying the acceptance criteria of the emergency laboratory, what is done?
opciones: It is rejected: under-filled citrate tubes below 80 % of target volume fail acceptance because the blood-to-anticoagulant ratio is wrong
It is accepted for both tests, because prothrombin time remains reliable at 67 % fill and aPTT is only slightly affected
It is accepted for the prothrombin time only, and the aPTT is canceled with a note asking for a properly filled tube
It is topped up with blood from the lavender tube of the same patient to restore the nominal volume before testing
preguntas.explicacion: Insufficient volume gives an inadequate blood-to-anticoagulant ratio, and in citrate tubes that lengthens PT, aPTT and thrombin time and lowers fibrinogen; a clinically significant bias appears below 89 % of fill for aPTT and 78 % for fibrinogen, so the laboratory rejects any citrate tube under 80 % of target. Prothrombin time alone stays fairly reliable down to 67 %, but that does not rescue a tube ordered for both tests, and blood is never moved between tubes.

preguntas.subtema: Charting standards · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which five attributes must every patient medical record entry carry under the Medicare conditions of participation?
opciones: Dated, timed, legible, complete and authenticated by the person responsible
Typed, countersigned, numbered, indexed and filed by the medical record service
Dated, timed, legible, complete and witnessed by a second member of the staff
Handwritten, dated, timed, initialed and stamped with the practice identifier
preguntas.explicacion: Every entry has to be authenticated, dated and timed, and it must be legible and complete; the person who provided or evaluated the service is the one who signs it, on paper or electronically, in line with the facility's own policies. The same condition of participation asks the hospital to run a system that identifies authors and keeps records so that the authentication stays trustworthy and every entry stays secure.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Challenges of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Measuring demand · CMAA 4A k49 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice plans to estimate how many same-day slots it will need from last year's appointment counts. What is wrong with that?
opciones: Past appointments reflect the clinical time that was on offer more than the demand there was
Past appointments reflect the demand there was, though not the urgency behind any of it
Past appointments cannot be used because the practice has since changed its appointment types
Past appointments reflect demand well, but the count has to be adjusted for the no-show rate
preguntas.explicacion: The model needs accurate figures for the size of each doctor's panel, for the level of demand and for the slots free each day. Demand is hard to read backwards: how many appointments were held in the past says more about the clinical time on offer than about what patients wanted. It has to be gathered going forward, by tracking the calls patients make and the follow-ups clinicians ask for.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: How to make a splint — First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.2.d · NCMA 2B.13 · RMA III.H.3.a.iv
preguntas.pregunta: How far should a splint extend along the injured limb?
opciones: Past the injury, taking in the joint above and the joint below it
Past the injury, taking in the joint above it but leaving the one below
Only over the injury itself, so the joints can still be moved and checked
From the injury to the nearest bony prominence, whichever way that falls
preguntas.explicacion: The splint reaches beyond the injured area and includes the joint on each side of it, which is what stops the part from moving and eases the pain. The limb is splinted in the position it was found, well padded, with ties above and below that are not knotted over the injury and not tight enough to cut off circulation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Complications and errors · CPT D3 k74 3R k22 · PBT II.I III.B · CCMA 3E12 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: Which two problems have studies found to be the most likely errors in phlebotomy?
opciones: Getting the patient wrong and labeling the tube badly
Nerve injury and increased pain from poor technique
Hematoma formation and prolonged tourniquet time
Contamination between tubes and short draws in citrate tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Nerve injury and increased pain can result from improper technique and hematoma from inadequate pressure, but other studies found identifying the patient and labeling the tube to be where the likeliest errors sit, which is why the chapter insists on identifying the patient and labeling the tubes in the patient's presence. The other options are real risks, not the ones the chapter ranks first.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (fasting)
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical factors · CPT D3 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E1 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for fasting morning blood work says she had only black coffee and water since dinner 13 hours ago. Is the fasting acceptable?
opciones: No; water is allowed during the fast, but coffee is not permitted that morning
Yes; black coffee has no calories, and 13 hours exceeds the 12-hour minimum fast
No; the fast must be at least 24 hours, the same interval set for alcohol
Yes, provided she also avoided physical activity for the previous 24 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Morning sampling should follow a fast of not less than 12 hours after the last solid meal; water is acceptable during the fast, but other drinks, energy drinks and coffee among them, are not allowed on the morning of the draw. Alcohol is avoided for 24 hours, and outpatients should avoid excessive physical activity for 24 hours; neither turns coffee into an acceptable drink.

preguntas.subtema: Inpatient procedure code set · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital reports the operations it performed on its own inpatients. Which standard code set does the regulation adopt for those procedures?
opciones: The tenth revision procedure coding system for hospital inpatients
The tenth revision clinical modification used for the conditions treated
The combination of the common procedure system and the physician code set
The common procedure coding system used for supplies and equipment
preguntas.explicacion: For procedures and other actions taken on hospital inpatients and reported by hospitals, the standard is the tenth revision procedure coding system, covering prevention, diagnosis, treatment and management. The clinical modification of the same revision is the standard for diseases, injuries, impairments and their causes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Drug Labeling", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k24 · RMA III.G.4.e · NCMA 1.6
preguntas.pregunta: A provider asks you to check the approved indications and the contraindications of a prescription drug. Where is that information found?
opciones: In the approved prescribing information, published as the label on DailyMed
In the Drug Facts panel, which every prescription product carries by law
In the Medication Guide, which lists every indication the FDA has approved
In the immunization information system, which stores approved product data
preguntas.explicacion: The prescribing information is the FDA-regulated labeling written for health professionals, and it moves heading by heading: what the drug is approved to treat, how it is dosed, the forms and strengths on the market, when it must not be used, the warnings with their precautions, the reactions reported, the interactions with other drugs, and how it behaves in specific populations. The Drug Facts panel is the over-the-counter format, and a Medication Guide is patient labeling.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient identification and labeling)
preguntas.subtema: Identification and labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · NCMA 2C.14 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: The date of birth on the requisition does not match what the patient states. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: Defer the blood sampling until the discrepancy is resolved
Draw the blood and note the discrepancy on the tube label
Use the date of birth on the requisition, since it comes from the record
Use the date the patient states, since the patient is the primary source
preguntas.explicacion: If there is any discrepancy in the identification data, any blood sampling should be deferred until the issue is resolved, and identification and labeling are double-checked before the draw. Drawing first and sorting it out later is the pattern behind the misidentification errors the chapter describes as the most likely mistakes in phlebotomy.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Testing Procedures; MedlinePlus, Glucose tolerance test (003466), How to Prepare for the Test
preguntas.subtema: OGTT fasting · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.D patient preparation · CCMA 3E k139 fasting · RMA III.C.4.e patient preparation · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions
preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient arrives at 8 a.m. for a diagnostic OGTT and mentions eating a sandwich at 3 a.m. What should you do?
opciones: Reschedule; the test needs a 10- to 16-hour fast, and at least 8 hours
Proceed; five hours is enough because the glucose load resets the baseline
Proceed, but skip the fasting sample and draw only at 2 hours
Proceed with a 100-g load instead, to compensate for the meal
preguntas.explicacion: The diagnostic OGTT is done in the morning after an overnight fast: StatPearls gives 10 to 16 hours for ambulatory outpatients and MedlinePlus at least 8 hours with nothing to eat or drink. Five hours meets neither, so the test is rescheduled. The fasting sample cannot be skipped because the 2-hour value is read against it, and the load for a nonpregnant adult stays at 75 g regardless of what was eaten.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.1 and Table 7.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 site by age and weight · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: A 14-month-old who already walks and weighs 12 kg needs a skin-puncture sample. Which site is indicated, and why?
opciones: A finger: over 6 months and above 10 kg the finger is indicated, and a walking child's feet may have calluses
The heel: the plantar surface remains the site of choice until the child weighs more than 15 kg
The heel: finger punctures in children under 2 years carry the nerve damage the WHO describes
An ear lobe: the WHO reserves finger-pricks for adults and heel-pricks for neonates and infants
preguntas.explicacion: In a pediatric patient the heel or finger is selected by age and weight: the finger-prick applies over 6 months and above 10 kg. Once a child is walking, the feet may have calluses that hinder blood flow. Nerve damage is listed as a complication of puncturing the fingers of neonates, not of toddlers, and ear lobes are used only rarely, in mass screening or research.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: One note in a chart says dysphagia and another says dysphasia. Which contrast between the two endings is correct?
opciones: The first is about swallowing and the second is about speech
The first is about speech and the second is about swallowing
The first is about breathing and the second is about swallowing
The first is about swallowing and the second is about breathing
preguntas.explicacion: A single letter separates them. The part -phagia, also written -phagy, is eating or swallowing, and -phasia is speech; dys- in front of either means difficult or abnormal. Breathing is -pnea, which is the ending in apnea and in dyspnea, so it belongs to neither of these two words.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.1 Structure and Function of Blood Vessels, Table 20.1 Comparison of Tunics in Arteries and Veins; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Classification & Structure of Blood Vessels
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3 k62) · PBT I.A.2 I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Both arteries and veins have three tunics. Which tunic is normally the thickest in an artery, and which in a vein?
opciones: Tunica media in arteries; tunica externa in veins
Tunica externa in arteries; tunica media in veins
Tunica intima in arteries; tunica media in veins
Tunica media in both, since both carry blood under pressure
preguntas.explicacion: The layers from inside out are tunica intima, tunica media and tunica externa. The media, rich in smooth muscle and elastic fibers, is normally the thickest layer in arteries, while in veins the media is thinner than the externa, which is the thickest layer there. Veins have less smooth muscle and connective tissue overall, which is why their walls are thinner than those of arteries.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Granular Leukocytes
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which leukocyte releases histamine and heparin from its granules?
opciones: Basophil
Eosinophil
Neutrophil
Monocyte
preguntas.explicacion: Basophils, the least common leukocyte at under one percent, have large granules that release histamine, which promotes inflammation, and heparin, which opposes clotting. Eosinophil granules carry antihistamines and toxins for parasitic worms; neutrophil granules carry lysozyme, oxidants and defensins; and monocytes become the phagocytic macrophages.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: power of attorney; and Wex: durable power of attorney
preguntas.subtema: Power of attorney · CCMA k218 · CMA E.8.c / 2027 E.7.b · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: When does an ordinary power of attorney stop working?
opciones: When the principal is no longer competent to make their own decisions
When the principal is admitted to a hospital for more than one night
When the agent moves out of the state where the document was signed
When the principal signs any later document naming a different agent
preguntas.explicacion: A power of attorney normally holds good only while the principal is still alive and still competent to decide. Without a durability provision it ends the moment the principal becomes incapacitated. A durable one, whose durability has to be stated in the document, stays valid through incapacity and typically runs until the principal dies or the document is revoked.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157(d)(2), (4), (5) and (6), Selection and distribution; OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety
preguntas.subtema: Extinguisher placement · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: How far may a worker have to travel to reach an extinguisher for Class A hazards, and for Class B hazards, under 29 CFR 1910.157?
opciones: 75 feet for Class A; 50 feet for Class B
50 feet for Class A; 75 feet for Class B
75 feet for both classes
25 feet for Class A; 50 feet for Class B
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d) of 29 CFR 1910.157 distributes extinguishers by class of fire: for Class A fires the travel distance to any extinguisher is 75 feet, 22.9 meters, or less; for Class B the distance from the hazard area is 50 feet, 15.2 meters, or less; Class C units follow the pattern of the Class A or B hazard present; and Class D agents are within 75 feet of combustible metal working areas. OSHA's laboratory guidance repeats the 75 and 50 foot figures and notes that solvents and compressed gases make Class B the high-risk category in laboratories.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medigap (Medicare Supplement Insurance)
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient enrolled in a Medicare Advantage Plan asks the office to help her buy a Medigap policy. What is the obstacle?
opciones: Medigap is sold only to people who have Original Medicare, both Part A and Part B
Medigap is sold only during the Medicare Open Enrollment Period held every year
Medigap is sold only to people who also carry a separate Part D drug plan
Medigap is sold only to people who paid Medicare taxes for at least ten years
preguntas.explicacion: Medigap is extra insurance bought from a private company to help with the enrollee's share of costs in Original Medicare, such as copayments, coinsurance and deductibles. It can only be bought by someone who has Original Medicare, which generally means signing up for Part A and Part B before a Medigap policy can be purchased at all.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Vascular Spasm; Extrinsic Pathway; Intrinsic Pathway; Disorders of Clotting
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: How long does the vascular spasm that follows a vessel injury usually last, and what triggers it?
opciones: Up to 30 minutes, at times hours; triggered by endothelins
A matter of seconds, the time the extrinsic pathway needs
A few minutes, the time the intrinsic pathway needs
About 3 hours, until bradykinin dilates the vessel again
preguntas.explicacion: When a vessel is injured the smooth muscle in its wall contracts sharply; the response is thought to be set off by endothelins released by the lining cells and by pain receptors, and it typically lasts up to 30 minutes but can go on for hours. Seconds and minutes are the completion times of the extrinsic and intrinsic pathways, and 3 hours is the window for thrombolytic drugs after a stroke.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (gloves and hand hygiene)
preguntas.subtema: Hand hygiene and gloves · CPT D3 3A · PBT II.F · CCMA 3C4 k100 k101 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Blood cultures are ordered along with routine tubes. What is the glove requirement for this draw?
opciones: Sterile gloves are mandatory when blood cultures are being obtained
Non-sterile gloves are sufficient, as the culture bottle is sealed
Gloves may be omitted if the hands were washed with soap and water
Double gloving is required for cultures to reduce blood transfer in a needlestick
preguntas.explicacion: A new, unused pair of gloves with careful hand washing before and after each patient is recommended for every draw, and wearing sterile gloves is mandatory when planning to obtain blood cultures. Double gloving is mentioned in the needlestick chapter as a way to reduce the volume of blood transmitted in an injury, not as a culture requirement.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations
preguntas.subtema: Health care operations · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which activity is a health care operation under the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Reviewing the competence and qualifications of health care professionals
Sending a chart to the specialist who will see the patient next month
Submitting a claim to the health plan for the visit performed yesterday
Releasing records to a life insurer weighing an application for a policy
preguntas.explicacion: Health care operations are the administrative, legal, financial and quality-improvement work that keeps the business running and supports treatment and payment. The list takes in quality assessment and improvement; care coordination and case management; reviews of how competent and how qualified the professionals are and how they perform; training; accreditation, licensing and credentialing; medical review and auditing; fraud detection; and compliance programs.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Poisoning first aid", DO NOT
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.h · 2027 I.B.8.h · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A parent calls to say a toddler swallowed a cleaning product a minute ago and looks fine. What is the correct instruction?
opciones: Call the emergency number or the poison center, without waiting for symptoms
Watch the child for an hour and call back if any symptom shows up
Give a glass of milk to coat the stomach and then come to the office
Make the child throw up before the product can be absorbed further
preguntas.explicacion: Symptoms of a poisoning may take time to appear, so nobody waits for them: the emergency number or the poison center is called at once. Vomiting is not induced unless poison control or a provider says to, because a poison that burned going down burns again coming back up, and the poison is not neutralized with vinegar or lemon juice either.

preguntas.fuente: DEA, Drug Scheduling (Schedule III)
preguntas.subtema: Laws and regulations · CCMA 7A k214 (Controlled Substances Act) · CMA E.5.b · NCMA 4.13
preguntas.pregunta: Where does Schedule III sit compared with the schedules on either side of it?
opciones: Below Schedules I and II in abuse potential, and above Schedule IV
Above Schedules I and II in abuse potential, and below Schedule IV
Level with Schedule II, because both have accepted medical uses
Level with Schedule V, because both are dispensed without limits
preguntas.explicacion: Schedule III holds drugs whose potential for dependence, physical and psychological, is moderate to low: more abuse potential than Schedule IV, less than Schedules I and II. Products with under 90 milligrams of codeine per dosage unit, ketamine, anabolic steroids and testosterone are the examples given. Schedule IV is low potential, and Schedule V lower still.
