preguntas.pregunta: The explanation is done and the patient has agreed. Before the tourniquet, what does the preparation guidance say to ask?
opciones: Which collection sites they would like to see prioritised
Which tube colors the last phlebotomist ended up using
Whether they would rather have a capillary sample instead
Whether they want the results sent to a second clinician
preguntas.explicacion: Informed consent without patient resistance is obtained after the full explanation, and only once every question, including when the results will come back, has been answered. The patient is also asked which collection sites have been convenient before, so those can be prioritised, and at the same point those afraid of testing or with a vagal history are identified.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Characteristics of Leukocytes; and 18.2 Production of the Formed Elements
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k3 (applied D3) · PBT I.C · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2 EKB 3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4))
preguntas.pregunta: The process by which leukocytes squeeze between the cells of a vessel wall to enter the tissues is called what?
opciones: Diapedesis
Chemotaxis
Phagocytosis
Hemopoiesis
preguntas.explicacion: The exit of white cells through the wall of capillaries and other small vessels is called emigration or diapedesis, from roots meaning to leap through. Chemotaxis is the movement of leukocytes toward chemical signals once they are in the tissue; phagocytosis is the engulfing of pathogens or debris; and hemopoiesis is the production of the formed elements in the marrow.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.524(b)(1) and (b)(2), Requests for access and timely action
preguntas.subtema: Right of access deadline · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for a copy of her lab results. Under HIPAA, how long does the covered entity have to act on the request?
opciones: No later than 30 days after receipt, with one possible 30-day extension explained in writing
No later than 60 days after receipt, the same limit as breach notification
No later than 15 days after receipt, the same limit as the OSHA written opinion after exposure
No later than 10 working days, with unlimited extensions if the record is large or on paper
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.524(b)(2) requires action on an access request no later than 30 days after receipt, either granting access or giving a written denial; if the entity cannot act in time it may take one extension of no more than 30 days, provided it tells the individual in writing, within the original period, the reason and the date it will finish. The entity may require requests in writing if it says so. Sixty days is the breach notification limit and 15 days the OSHA written opinion; neither governs access.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(g)(8) and (g)(9), Safety data sheets
preguntas.subtema: SDS for staff on the road · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A mobile phlebotomy team works at several sites during one shift. Where may the safety data sheets for its chemicals be kept?
opciones: At the primary facility, if the worker can get the information at once
Only in the vehicle, where a paper copy has to travel with the team
At the site being visited, with a copy left behind after each visit
In the state office, which sends the sheet within one working day
preguntas.explicacion: The general rule is that the employer keeps the sheets in the workplace and makes them readily accessible during each work shift while employees are in their work areas; electronic access is fine as long as it puts no barrier in the way. For employees whose work takes them to more than one geographical location during a shift, the sheets may stay at the primary workplace, on the condition that the worker can immediately obtain the information in an emergency.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Variability of Vital Signs in Older Adults
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k55 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Temperature d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: An 82-year-old with a urinary infection has a temperature of 37.2 °C (99 °F). Why is that value not reassuring?
opciones: Thermoregulation blunts with age, so a serious infection may raise the value only slightly
Older adults run a higher baseline, so 37.2 °C means the temperature has actually dropped
Urinary infections are the one group of infections that never raise body temperature
The reading is only reassuring once a second value taken an hour later agrees with it
preguntas.explicacion: Baseline core temperature tends to fall with age and the response to infection is blunted, so an older adult may never mount a high fever even when seriously ill. A modest rise above that person's own baseline can be clinically important, which is why the other vital signs and the clinical picture are weighed alongside it.

preguntas.subtema: Sanction policy · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A receptionist is found opening a neighbour's chart out of curiosity. Which required specification should already have been in place for that?
opciones: A sanction policy for workforce members who break the security policies
A termination procedure that ends access when a person leaves the practice
A workforce clearance procedure that decides whether the access was proper
A log-in monitoring procedure that watches attempts and reports differences
preguntas.explicacion: The security management process calls for sanctions, appropriate to the case, against any member of the workforce who does not follow the security policies and procedures. Clearance, termination and log-in monitoring are addressable specifications that decide on access or watch it; only the sanction policy answers what happens to the person afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: MyPlate, USDA: Protein Foods — ounce-equivalents; and Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 14: Protein Group
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A vegetarian patient asks what counts as a single ounce-equivalent inside the Protein Foods Group. Which of these does?
opciones: One tablespoon of peanut butter
One tablespoon of sunflower seeds
One cup of cooked beans or lentils
One cup of tofu cut into cubes
preguntas.explicacion: An ounce-equivalent of protein is an ounce of lean meat, poultry or seafood, one egg, a quarter cup of cooked beans, or a tablespoon of peanut butter. Beans, peas and lentils count either here or in the vegetable group. A whole cup of beans is four ounce-equivalents, not one.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: How much of the percutaneous injury burden can safety-engineered devices avoid, and what undoes that gain?
opciones: Up to seventy-five percent; disassembly, recapping, or not activating the feature
Up to twenty-five percent; disassembly, recapping, or not activating the feature
Up to seventy-five percent; using them on pediatric rather than adult patients
Up to ninety-nine percent; storing them in a tray rather than in the packaging
preguntas.explicacion: Replacing conventional devices with engineered ones can avoid as much as seventy-five percent of percutaneous injuries. The gain is lost when the device is taken apart, when the needle is recapped by hand, or when the safety feature is simply never activated, and exposure to blood then follows.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E k135 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A coagulation test (prothrombin time) is ordered. Which tube does it require, and what is the additive?
opciones: A light blue top tube with sodium citrate, always filled completely
A purple top tube with EDTA, which also removes calcium, filled completely
A red top clot activator tube, spun so the serum can be tested
A light gray fluoride/oxalate tube, which also requires a full draw
preguntas.explicacion: The WHO table lists the light blue coagulation tube for tests such as protime and prothrombin time. Its additive is sodium citrate, which binds calcium as calcium salts and so keeps the blood from clotting, and the table marks it as one of the tubes that needs a full draw. EDTA works the same way on calcium, but the table assigns it to hematology and cross-match, not coagulation; the red top carries a clot activator and gives serum, which a clotting test cannot use; and the gray fluoride/oxalate tube, which also needs a full draw, is the glucose tube.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: First morning urine · CPT D4 4G · PBT IV.A.1 · CCMA 3D2 · CMA I.C.10.a.(1) · RMA III.C.4.b.v · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: A provider orders a routine urinalysis for a patient coming in tomorrow. Which specimen should the medical assistant ask the patient to bring, and why?
opciones: The first void of the morning, because urine that collected overnight is more concentrated
A random specimen collected two hours after breakfast, because food raises the analyte levels
A 24-hour collection, because a single void cannot be dipped reliably for protein or glucose
A specimen collected after drinking a liter of water, because dilute urine is easier to read
preguntas.explicacion: First-void or morning urine is considered the best specimen for routine testing: the urine that accumulates in the bladder overnight is more concentrated, which reflects the kidneys' ability to concentrate and lets the strip detect trace substances that a dilute sample would miss. Random, postprandial and 24-hour collections exist, but each is ordered for a specific purpose, not for the routine dipstick.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Use of Accompanying Adults or Children as Interpreters
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · PBT II.B · CCMA 6D k195 · CMA F.1.c(2)(4) / 2027 F.1.d(1)(3) · RMA I.D.1.c · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: The deaf patient's 11-year-old daughter offers to interpret the pre-draw questions. Under the ADA guidance?
opciones: Not permitted; a minor may interpret only in an imminent-threat emergency
Permitted, provided the patient requests it and the child agrees to help out
Permitted, because the pre-draw questions are short and simple
Permitted, as long as a staff member witnesses the exchange
preguntas.explicacion: Using people's children as interpreters has proved particularly problematic. The ADA's two exceptions differ by age: where an emergency involves a threat that is imminent, an adult or a minor child may be relied on if no qualified interpreter is at hand; outside an emergency only an accompanying adult may, and only where the patient asks, the adult agrees and it is appropriate.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(c)(3), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D k112 · NCMA 2C.1 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A requisition lists the patient's name and the tests ordered but nothing else about the patient. Which of these does CLIA require the requisition to solicit?
opciones: The patient's sex and age or date of birth
The patient's address and insurance number
The patient's weight and current medications
The patient's room number and attending nurse
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1241(c) lists what the test requisition must ask for: the authorized person requesting the test with a contact for alert values, the patient's name or unique identifier, the sex and the age or date of birth, the tests to be performed, the specimen source when appropriate, the date and, if appropriate, the time of collection, and any further information needed for accurate testing. Insurance data, weight and location are not on that list.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Cost sharing
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which costs are included in the term cost sharing?
opciones: Deductibles, copayments and coinsurance for the services a plan covers
Premiums, deductibles and the charges for services a plan does not cover
Premiums and any amount a non-network provider bills above the allowed rate
Only the copayment collected at the desk on the day of the covered service
preguntas.explicacion: Cost sharing is the part of covered costs the patient pays personally, and the glossary names deductibles, coinsurance and copayments as the examples. It leaves out premiums, amounts balance billed by providers outside the network, and services the plan does not cover. Medicaid and CHIP are the exception where premiums are counted as cost sharing. The copayment alone is only one piece of it.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) General Information
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMA III.G.1.c (2027 III.G.1.c) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A supplier wants a new HCPCS Level II code created for a product it sells. Who is allowed to ask for it?
opciones: Anyone may ask CMS to change the national code set
Only the manufacturer that holds the product license
Only a Medicare contractor may put the request in
Only the association that maintains Level I may do it
preguntas.explicacion: CMS decides on additions, revisions and deletions to HCPCS Level II, and anyone may submit a request to modify the national code set through its electronic application system. Drug and biological applications are due at the start of each quarter, and applications for other items twice a year.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b · RMA III.E.3 Pulse d · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which other bedside findings are read alongside a peripheral pulse to judge how well the blood is circulating?
opciones: The color and the temperature of the skin, and capillary refill
The strength of the grip, the turgor of the skin and breath sounds
The oral temperature, the pain score and the pattern of breathing
The last recorded weight, the fluid intake and the urine output
preguntas.explicacion: A pulse is one strand of the circulatory picture. It is read next to the color and temperature of the skin and to capillary refill, which together help tell a local vessel problem from a systemic one such as shock. Read on its own, a single pulse finding says little; read with those signs and the clinical context, it says a great deal.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which drawbacks have users reported with safety cannulae compared with standard ones?
opciones: Slower flashback, more friction, and harder threading of the line
Faster flashback, less friction, and a lower price for each device
Slower flashback, less friction, and no possibility of blood splatter
Faster flashback, more friction, and a needle that cannot be shielded
preguntas.explicacion: Users report feeling safer with these devices, but they cost more and can make insertion harder: the flashback appears more slowly, there is greater friction as the cannula is advanced, and threading it into the vein is more difficult. Firing the mechanism may also raise blood splatter.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A chart note lists tonsillitis as the reason for the visit. What does the ending of that term tell you?
opciones: That the structure named by the root is inflamed
That the structure named by the root has been removed
That the structure named by the root has been cut into
That the structure named by the root is drooping down
preguntas.explicacion: The ending -itis means inflammation, so tonsillitis is inflamed tonsils. The endings that get mixed up with it point elsewhere: -ectomy is cutting a part out, -otomy is an incision, and -ptosis is a falling or drooping. Reading the ending first tells you what is happening to whatever the root names.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, ABO Transfusion Protocols
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k5 (applied D4 4D) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: An emergency patient is typed AB positive. Which blood types could he theoretically receive, and why?
opciones: Any type, since his plasma carries neither anti-A nor anti-B
Only AB+, since both antigens must match the donor exactly
Only O−, since that is the type of the universal donor
Any Rh− type, since Rh+ cells would sensitize the patient
preguntas.explicacion: The AB positive patient is the universal recipient: with both A and B antigens on his own cells he makes neither anti-A nor anti-B, and as an Rh positive person he can take Rh positive or Rh negative blood. Matched blood is still preferred, because the donor's plasma brings its own antibodies. An Rh positive recipient is not sensitized by Rh positive cells; that risk belongs to Rh negative people.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Prothrombin Time", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 3N k9 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which single fault explains both an unreliable clotting result and the loss of the specimen that produced it?
opciones: A clot in the tube, which uses up the very factors being measured
A tube filled to its line, which leaves the anticoagulant in excess
A tube inverted six times, which shears the fibrin strands apart
A tube kept at room temperature, which activates factor VII early
preguntas.explicacion: When a specimen clots, the clotting factors are consumed inside the tube and whatever the analyser then measures cannot be trusted. Clots follow a traumatic puncture, activation inside the device or poor mixing. Room temperature is the correct storage; it is refrigeration that activates factor VII.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Pre-appointment screening · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4H k62 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A first-time telehealth patient is being screened before her appointment. Which question belongs in that screening?
opciones: Whether she has a device with a camera and microphone that works with the platform
Whether she prefers the practice to bill her insurer before or after the appointment
Whether she would rather receive her visit summary by letter or by facsimile
Whether she agrees to have the encounter recorded for the practice training file
preguntas.explicacion: The checklist for learning about a patient's technology asks whether she has a camera and a microphone on a computer, a tablet or a mobile device, and whether those work with the platform; whether her internet connection carries enough bandwidth for video; whether she has a secure place with internet from which to take the appointment; and whether she needs a hand setting up an e-mail account where the platform requires one.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A chemistry panel is ordered in a plain red clot activator tube and a serology test in a gold serum separator tube. Which is filled first according to the WHO table?
opciones: The red clot activator tube, then the gold serum separator tube
The gold serum separator tube, then the red clot activator tube
Either one, since both yield serum and share the same position
The gold tube first, because its gel must be reached by more blood
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 separates the two serum tubes: the red top with clot activator is position 4 and the serum separator tube, red-gray tiger or gold, is position 5. Both produce serum after centrifugation, but the table does not merge them into one position, and it gives no rule about gel volume. The red tube is drawn before the gold one.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: General Provision
preguntas.subtema: Incidental disclosures · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A visitor in the waiting room glimpses another patient's name on the sign-in sheet. Is that a violation?
opciones: No, it is an incidental disclosure, permitted where safeguards and minimum necessary are in place
No, because sign-in sheets are excluded from the definition of protected health information
Yes, because the rule requires that every risk of an unintended disclosure be eliminated first
Yes, unless each patient signed an authorization allowing the office to use a sign-in sheet
preguntas.explicacion: OCR treats the glimpse of a sign-in sheet, or a conversation overheard at a nursing station, as an incidental disclosure: a secondary one that no reasonable step could have prevented, that is limited in nature, and that flows from something the rule already allows. It is permitted as long as reasonable safeguards and the minimum necessary policies are applied to the underlying use.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Abdominal thrusts", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.d · 2027 I.B.8.d · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: An adult who choked on food cannot speak or breathe but is still conscious. What does the rescuer do?
opciones: Cycles of five back blows and then five abdominal thrusts, until it comes out
Cycles of five back blows and then five chest thrusts, until the object is out
Thirty chest compressions and two breaths, repeated until the ambulance arrives
Five finger sweeps of the mouth and then five slow breaths into the airway
preguntas.explicacion: For a conscious adult with a blocked airway the rescuer works in cycles, 5 blows to the back and then 5 thrusts to the abdomen, over and over until the object is out or the person goes limp. Back blows plus chest thrusts is the infant sequence. Compressions belong to the unconscious victim: abdominal thrusts are for the conscious one.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 16: Other Information
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 16 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k106 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic wants to know whether the safety data sheet in its binder is the current version. Which section settles that?
opciones: Section 16, which gives the date of preparation or of the last revision
Section 1, which gives the product identifier and the supplier's address
Section 15, which gives the regulations in force for that product
Section 3, which gives the composition and the concentration ranges
preguntas.explicacion: Section 16 is where the sheet says when it was prepared or last revised, and it may also point out where the changes were made compared with the previous version; the supplier can be asked to explain them. Any other useful information goes here as well. Section 15, the regulatory section, is one of the four that OSHA does not enforce, and neither the identification nor the composition section carries a revision date.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Issues of Concern: Exceptions to Informed Consent
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA II.E.3 · RMA III.D.2.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient booked for a minor office procedure cannot make the decision himself and never named anyone to decide for him. What settles who consents?
opciones: The order of decision-makers fixed by that state's law, and a court-appointed guardian if that fails
The closest blood relative, since the legal surrogate decision-maker is set by federal law
The physician doing the procedure, who may consent for a patient with no surrogate on record
The order fixed by that state's law, and the treating physician's own choice if no relative answers
preguntas.explicacion: Losing the ability to decide does not hand the decision to the team. With no advance directive and nobody named as proxy, who may speak for the patient is settled by the law of the state, and that order is what has to be worked through. If nobody in it can be found or qualifies, the matter goes before a court and a guardian is appointed. Where the doubt is about capacity itself rather than about who decides, a psychiatric evaluation of competency may be requested first. What does not happen is the clinician stepping into the gap on his own account.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Information to provide beforehand · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A video visit is booked to review a patient's medicines. Which item does the guidance tell the office to ask her to have ready?
opciones: The bottles themselves or a list of them, plus the pharmacy's contact details
The claim forms the pharmacy sent after the last two prescriptions were filled
The plan's drug list, so the tier of each medicine can be checked on screen
The explanation of benefits the insurer mailed after her last prescription
preguntas.explicacion: Depending on the nature of the appointment, the office may ask the patient to prepare a list of her current medicines or gather the actual bottles, her medical history, the symptoms and questions she wants to raise, her pharmacy's contact information, measurements such as weight and temperature, and a flashlight or phone light if her throat will be examined.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Clean catch urine sample (007487), After Collecting the Sample; and PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Transport and preservation
preguntas.subtema: Home clean-catch storage · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 / V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient collected a clean-catch specimen at home at 7 a.m. and cannot bring it to the office until noon. What should she have been told to do with it?
opciones: Screw the lid on tightly, put the cup in a plastic bag and keep it in the refrigerator until she brings it in
Leave the cup capped on the kitchen counter at room temperature, since refrigeration would alter the cells
Keep the cup in an inside coat pocket so the specimen stays at body temperature during transport
Freeze the specimen at home and let the office thaw it later, since freezing preserves it better than cold
preguntas.explicacion: After collecting, the patient closes the lid tightly without touching the inside of the cup or lid; when the sample is collected at home it goes into a plastic bag in the refrigerator until it can be delivered. Room temperature lets bacteria multiply, freezing is not an accepted substitute for refrigeration in urine preservation, and body-temperature transport in a coat pocket is the instruction for a semen sample, not urine.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(4)(ii), Information Provided to the Healthcare Professional
preguntas.subtema: What the evaluator receives · CPT D1 1H k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k109 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: After a needlestick, which information must the employer send to the healthcare professional who evaluates the exposed employee?
opciones: The employee's duties in the incident, the route and circumstances, and the source results
The employee's job title, the brand of the device, and the department where it happened
A summary of the annual training and the names and qualifications of the trainer
The signed declination form and the dates of the employee's last three exposures
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(4)(ii) lists five things the evaluating professional receives: a copy of the regulation, a description of what the employee was doing when the exposure happened, documentation of the route and the circumstances, the source individual's blood results if they exist, and the medical records the employer keeps that matter for treatment, vaccination status included. The device brand and the work area are what the sharps injury log records under (h)(5)(i); training content and trainer qualifications belong to the training record in (h)(2)(i).

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, How to Understand Your Lab Results, section What can affect my results
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which of the following is a common factor that can affect the accuracy of test results?
opciones: Exercising hard before the test
Sitting for 15 minutes before the draw
Drinking plain water during the fast
Having the draw done in the morning
preguntas.explicacion: The common confounders are eating or drinking certain things, certain medicines and supplements, hard exercise shortly before the test, being on a menstrual period, and whether the preparation instructions, fasting among them, were actually followed. Sitting beforehand, plain water and a morning appointment are all things the other sources recommend, not confounders.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Abandonment", Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Abandonment · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.a(4) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.9 · CMAA 3A k31
preguntas.pregunta: What is patient abandonment?
opciones: Ending the relationship one-sidedly without notice enough to find other care
Ending the relationship after the patient has missed several appointments
Refusing to treat a person who has never been seen at the practice before
Transferring a patient to a specialist without telling the primary clinician
preguntas.explicacion: Abandonment is a breach of duty: the clinician terminates the relationship one-sidedly and without giving the patient adequate notice to arrange substitute medical care. It presupposes that a clinician-patient relationship existed, which starts when the clinician acts on the patient's diagnosis or treatment, or agrees to. Someone never seen at the practice is not yet in that relationship.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Choosing a primary care provider: Information
preguntas.subtema: Referral coordination · CCMA 4E · CMA II.F.4.a / 2027 II.F.2.a · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is unsure how urgent her symptom is. Which role does her primary care provider fill?
opciones: Assessing how urgent the problem is and directing her to the best place for care
Deciding which services the health plan will agree to pay for that month
Arranging the hospital admission and writing the discharge summary later
Confirming that the specialist she has picked belongs to the plan network
preguntas.explicacion: The primary care provider is the patient's main provider in situations that are not emergencies. The role is to deliver preventive care and to teach healthy lifestyle choices, to spot and treat the common medical conditions, to judge how urgent a problem is and steer the patient to the right place for that care, and to refer on to medical or surgical specialists when they are needed.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Bloodborne Infectious Disease Risk Factors (Feb. 13, 2025), Prevention: Reporting
preguntas.subtema: Information to report · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which information does NIOSH say to collect when reporting a needlestick?
opciones: Date and time, the procedure, the device with brand and model, and the department
The source patient's diagnosis and insurance, and the worker's vaccination card
The lot number of the gloves worn and the brand of disinfectant on the counter
The names of all patients drawn that shift and the time each was seen
preguntas.explicacion: NIOSH lists what to gather: the date and time of the exposure, the procedure or action being performed, specific details such as profession, department or unit, shift and whether the injured person was the device user, and the specific type of device with brand and model when known. These details feed the sharps injury log, which records the device type and brand, the work area and how the incident occurred, including depth of injury and whether a safety feature was activated. Patient insurance and glove lot numbers are not on the list.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Drug Information: How to Use Eyedrops (a601171)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k70 · CMA I.D.2.c(6) · RMA III.G.4.d(viii) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: An eye drop has just been instilled. What is the patient told to do next?
opciones: Close the eye two to three minutes and tip the head down, without blinking hard
Blink several times quickly so that the drop spreads over the surface of the eye
Close the eye ten to fifteen minutes, the time an emergency eye flush station runs
Keep the eye open and look up for five minutes, as is done after an ear instillation
preguntas.explicacion: The lower lid is pulled down to form a pocket, and the drop is released into it with the dropper held close but touching nothing. The eye then stays closed for two to three minutes with the head tipped down as if looking at the floor, without blinking or squeezing; gentle pressure over the tear duct helps, and any excess is wiped away. The fifteen minutes belong to an eye flush and the five minutes to ear drops.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Recommendations, section 5. Cleaning and Disinfecting Environmental Surfaces in Healthcare Facilities
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C5 k105 · CMA I.B.5.c (2027 I.B.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.i · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient bleeds about 5 mL onto a countertop. Which hypochlorite dilution does the guideline give for decontaminating that surface?
opciones: 1:100, which delivers roughly 525 to 615 ppm of available chlorine
1:10, which delivers roughly 5,250 to 6,150 ppm of available chlorine
1:50, which delivers roughly 1,000 ppm of available chlorine at day zero
1:5, which delivers the concentration used against Clostridioides difficile spores
preguntas.explicacion: For a small spill, under about 10 mL, of blood or of any other material that might be infectious, a 1:100 dilution of 5.25 to 6.15 percent sodium hypochlorite is used on the nonporous surface, which works out to 525 to 615 ppm of available chlorine. The stronger 1:10 dilution is reserved for large spills and for units with high rates of C. difficile.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 2.4.2 Care of the Paper
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k152 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: How is the thermal recording paper stored?
opciones: Cool, dry and dark, below 80 °F and 40 to 65% humidity
Cool, dry and dark, below 60 °F and 20 to 30% humidity
Warm, dry and dark, below 80 °F and 40 to 65% humidity
Cool, dry and lit, below 80 °F and 40 to 65% humidity
preguntas.explicacion: The paper is kept in a cool, dry, dark place, under 27.6 °C or 80 °F, with relative humidity between 40 and 65 percent. Bright light and ultraviolet sources such as sunlight or fluorescent lamps yellow the paper and fade the tracings, and cleaning solvents must not touch it.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A k87 · PBT III.C · CCMA 3E11 k136 · NCMA 2C.6 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d)
preguntas.pregunta: An emergency department keeps sending serum samples that reach the laboratory with fibrin after a very short wait. Which tube change did the study laboratory plan to make?
opciones: Switch to rapid serum tubes, which speed up clotting and shorten processing while improving serum quality
Switch to heparin plasma tubes, which contain no clot activator and so cannot form any fibrin at all
Switch to serum separator tubes with gel, which trap the fibrin below the barrier during centrifugation
Switch to citrate tubes filled completely, which keep the fibrinogen in solution until testing
preguntas.explicacion: To prevent fibrin formation the laboratory planned to use rapid serum tubes, described as tubes that accelerate coagulation, reduce processing time and increase serum quality, a fit for emergency departments and intensive care units. Gel separator tubes do not solve early spinning and are refused for therapeutic drug monitoring; heparin and citrate tubes give plasma, which is a different specimen.

preguntas.subtema: Advance directive information · CCMA 5D · CMA I.A.5 · RMA I.C.1.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital admits an adult patient. What does the advance directive regulation require the facility to do?
opciones: Give written information about the patient's rights to make care decisions
Require the patient to sign an advance directive before treatment can begin
Contact the patient's next of kin to obtain an advance directive on her behalf
File a copy of any directive with the State agency within ninety days of admission
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation reaches hospitals, critical access hospitals, skilled nursing and nursing facilities, home health agencies, hospices, and those religious institutions providing nonmedical health care alike: each keeps written policies on advance directives for every adult in its care, and each hands the adult written information about the rights State law gives her over decisions about her care, the right to accept or refuse treatment included, and about drawing up a directive should she wish to.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Revenue Cycle Management: The Art and the Science", Days to Pay
preguntas.subtema: Tracking unpaid claims · CMA III.G.3.b(5) (2027 III.G.3.b) · CMAA 6 k81 · CCMA 5 k181 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Two weeks after a batch of claims went out, nothing has come back from the payer. What does the guidance on tracking submitted claims advise?
opciones: Set a reminder to check on every claim within twenty-one days of submission
Wait for the remittance advice, which every payer owes within thirty days
Send the whole batch again on paper so the payer cannot say it never arrived
Write the balances off and bill the patients once ninety days have gone by
preguntas.explicacion: Among the remedies for slow payment are gathering demographic data accurately, billing accurately, cross-checking entries before submission, confirming that the claims sent were actually received and processed, and setting reminders to follow up on every claim within twenty-one days of submission. Paper is the opposite of a remedy: it always takes longer and hands the payer the excuse that the claim never arrived or is still being processed.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.b · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: From what distance are sterile items dropped onto an established sterile field?
opciones: About six inches away from the field
About one inch away from the field
About eighteen inches away from the field
Directly against the surface of the field
preguntas.explicacion: Items are released about six inches from the field, the same distance used when pouring a sterile solution. The gap keeps the outer packaging, and the hand holding it, from touching what is sterile. Once the wrapper is open the item must not brush any part of it, the former package seal included, and the arm never passes over the field.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Individual Notice
preguntas.subtema: Individual breach notice · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A breach of unsecured PHI is discovered on June 1. When and how must the affected patients be told?
opciones: Without unreasonable delay and within sixty days, in writing by first-class mail
Without unreasonable delay and within thirty days, by telephone call to each patient
Within sixty days of the end of the calendar year, in a single written summary
Within ten working days, by a notice posted at the front desk of the practice
preguntas.explicacion: Individual notice has to go without unreasonable delay, and 60 days after the discovery of the breach is the outer limit. It has to be written and sent by first-class mail, or by e-mail where the person agreed to electronic notices. It describes the breach, the kinds of information involved, the steps the person ought to take, what the entity is doing about it, and how to get in touch.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Airborne Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Airborne Precautions in transport · CPT D1 1I k34 k36 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis must be taken to radiology. What does the CDC say about the escort's respiratory protection during transport?
opciones: No respirator is needed in transport if the patient wears a mask and infectious lesions are covered
A fit-tested N95 is always required for the escort, whether or not the patient is masked
A surgical mask on the escort is sufficient, because the patient is out of the isolation room
Transport is prohibited; imaging must be done inside the airborne infection isolation room
preguntas.explicacion: Inside the room, Airborne Precautions require a fit-tested, NIOSH-approved N95 or higher respirator for personnel. For transport, which the CDC limits to medically necessary purposes, the patient wears a surgical mask if possible and observes cough etiquette, and the CDC states that staff transporting such a patient do not need a mask or respirator during the move when the patient is masked and any infectious skin lesions are covered. The rule is specific to transport; it does not replace the respirator at the bedside.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C 2M k42 · PBT II.A II.B · CCMA 3E1 3E2 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Before the draw, which points does the phlebotomist double-check and then share with the patient?
opciones: Identity, the purpose of the draw, the tests to be run, and the exact volume to be taken
Identity, the expected results, and the reference ranges for each test ordered
Identity, the tube colors needed, and the order of draw that will be followed
Identity, the diagnosis code, and the physician's working differential diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: The patient's identification, the purpose of the procedure, whether diagnostic sampling or therapeutic phlebotomy, the specific tests to be run and the exact amount of blood are all double-checked; telling the patient each of those makes them more comfortable and sets a professional tone. Results and diagnoses are not the phlebotomist's to discuss.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings, Oral Glucose Tolerance Test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Before an oral glucose tolerance test a patient asks about the old advice to load up on carbohydrate for three days. What is the current position?
opciones: Updated evidence suggests it may not be needed for every patient
It stands as a firm requirement of 150 g daily for three days
It was replaced by a 24-hour fast in place of the eight-hour one
It applies now only to patients who are already taking insulin
preguntas.explicacion: Individuals were traditionally told to take at least 150 g of carbohydrate a day for three days beforehand, to avoid a false-positive result. Newer evidence indicates that eating carbohydrate freely in the days before makes no significant difference to the outcome in most clinical situations, so that preparation may not be needed for everyone. The eight-hour fast stands.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Mandatory & Optional Medicaid Benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicaid patient says she has no way of getting to her appointment. What does the federal list of state plan benefits say about that?
opciones: Transportation to medical care is a benefit every state Medicaid program must cover
Dental services are a benefit that every state Medicaid program is obliged to cover
Physical therapy is a benefit that every state Medicaid program is obliged to cover
Private duty nursing is a benefit every state Medicaid program is obliged to cover
preguntas.explicacion: Federal law obliges states to provide the mandatory state plan benefits, and transportation to medical care is one of them, alongside hospital services inpatient and outpatient, laboratory and X-ray, physician services, nursing facility care, home health and family planning. Dental care, physical therapy and private duty nursing sit on the optional list instead.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Nasopharyngeal Swab; and StatPearls, "Overview of the Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", Throat and Nasal Swabs
preguntas.subtema: Transport medium · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k113 · CMA I.C.8.c · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: After a nasopharyngeal swab is withdrawn, what happens to it?
opciones: Its tip goes into a tube of viral transport medium and the applicator stick is snapped off
Its tip goes into a dry sterile tube and the applicator stick is left long for handling
Its tip is rolled onto a glass slide, air dried, and sent with the applicator attached
Its tip goes into a tube of normal saline and the applicator stick is snapped off
preguntas.explicacion: The swab tip is placed into a sterile tube holding 1 to 3 mL of viral transport medium and the applicator stick is snapped or cut off so the cap can seal. Rolling a specimen onto slides for smears is what is done with the nasal swab collected for direct microscopic examination, and plain saline is what is instilled during a nasal wash, not the medium the swab travels in.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Telehealth Systems, Function
preguntas.subtema: Synchronous telehealth · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k54 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which service is an example of synchronous telehealth?
opciones: A live video visit between a patient at home and a clinician elsewhere
A digital intake questionnaire the patient completes before the appointment
A continuous glucose monitor transmitting readings to the clinician's dashboard
A secure portal message asking for a refill that the office answers next week
preguntas.explicacion: Synchronous telehealth delivers health information in real time, patient and clinician talking live. The forms listed are video visits direct to the consumer at home from a smartphone or a computer, consultations run clinic-to-clinic and clinician-to-clinician, teletriage in urgent settings, behavioral health encounters by live video, and remote critical care consultations.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, opening paragraph and Shape and Structure of Erythrocytes
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A CBC on a man reports 5.4 million red cells per microliter. How does that compare with the reference values?
opciones: It matches the typical male value; women average about 4.8 million
It is high; men average about 4.8 million and women about 5.4 million
It is high; the reference count is 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter
It is normal only if reticulocytes are under 25 percent of the count
preguntas.explicacion: A man averages roughly 5.4 million red cells in every microliter and a woman about 4.8 million, so this result is ordinary for him. A count of 5,000 to 10,000 per microliter belongs to the white cells instead. Reticulocytes run 1 to 2 percent of the red cells; the 25 percent figure is the share of all the body's cells that are red cells, not a ceiling for reticulocytes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Oral Antidiabetic Medications", Mechanism of Action
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.b · RMA III.G.4.c · NCMA 1.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking metformin alone asks whether the tablets can drop the blood sugar too low. What is correct?
opciones: They do not, because metformin does not make the pancreas secrete extra insulin
They do, because metformin shuts the potassium channels of the pancreatic beta cells
They do, because metformin drives glucose and potassium into the cells like insulin
They do, but only once the daily dose passes 2000 mg taken in divided doses
preguntas.explicacion: Metformin works on the liver and the muscle: it activates hepatic AMP-activated protein kinase, damps gluconeogenesis and lipogenesis, and improves the uptake of glucose driven by insulin. Because it never asks the beta cell for more insulin, monotherapy does not produce hypoglycemia. Closing the beta cell's potassium channels is how a sulfonylurea works, and that is the class where hypoglycemia is the main worry.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.508(b)(4), Prohibition on conditioning of authorizations; 164.508(a)(3)
preguntas.subtema: Conditioning treatment on authorization · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: May a clinic refuse to draw a patient's blood unless she signs an authorization releasing her results to a marketing company?
opciones: No: treatment may not be conditioned on an authorization, with narrow exceptions
Yes: a covered entity may set any condition it discloses in its notice
Yes, if the marketing company has signed a business associate agreement
No, unless the patient pays out of pocket and in full, which removes the restriction
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.508(b)(4) forbids making treatment, payment, enrollment or the eligibility for benefits hang on the individual signing an authorization. The exceptions are narrow: research-related treatment conditioned on a research authorization, a health plan's enrollment or underwriting authorization sought before enrollment, and care given solely to create PHI for a third party. Marketing needs an authorization of its own under 164.508(a)(3), and a business associate agreement covers services performed for the covered entity, not marketing by an outside company.

preguntas.subtema: Electronic summary notice · CMAA 5 k78 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.3.b(3) · RMA II.A.2 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with Original Medicare would rather not wait for her summary notice to arrive by post. What does Medicare offer her?
opciones: An e-mail with a link to the notice for any month in which a claim was processed
An e-mail with a link to the notice on the same schedule as the posted version
An e-mail with the notice attached, sent each time a provider submits a claim
An e-mail alert whenever the claim total for the period passes her deductible
preguntas.explicacion: Electronic delivery is an option: choosing it brings an e-mail carrying a link to the notice for any month in which a claim has been processed, without waiting for paper. The posted version arrives at least twice a year, every six months, and only for a period in which services or supplies were actually received.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Case Study of a Successful Comprehensive Prevention Program

preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomy service cut its needlestick rate from 1.5 to 0.2 per 10,000 venipunctures. What was behind that drop?
opciones: Training, changed work practices, safety devices, and encouraging reporting
Fewer draws per shift, and a bonus for each month without an injury
Double gloving for every draw, and a second worker at each bedside
Replacing every vacuum tube holder with a syringe and transfer device
preguntas.explicacion: In the reported case the service brought its rate down over three years, against a national median of about 0.94 per 10,000 venipunctures, through a bundle rather than a single change: worker education, changes in work practices, devices with safety features, and active encouragement of injury reporting, on top of the published guidelines and the bloodborne pathogens standard. The authors credited a thorough understanding of the injuries their own staff were having.

preguntas.subtema: Order of draw and tube colours · CPT D3 3J k57 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.J · CCMA 3E6 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic switches to a tube manufacturer whose stopper colors do not match the chart on the wall. What does the WHO advise about color codes and additives?
opciones: Verify the recommendations with the local laboratory, since codes can differ
Follow the colors of the previous manufacturer, since the additive sequence is standard
Draw the coagulation tube first in every case, because it needs a full draw
Apply the WHO table as printed, because it fixes the color for every manufacturer
preguntas.explicacion: Step 8 says color coding and tube additives may vary and tells the reader to check the recommendations with the local laboratory; footnote b of Table 2.3 repeats it for local color codes. The table is offered for illustration, not as a universal color standard. The coagulation tube keeps its place ahead of the serum and additive tubes whatever color its stopper is.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Introduction; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding into the skin
preguntas.subtema: Complications: petechiae · CPT D3 3L k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: After the tourniquet is released, a patient's forearm shows a scatter of red dots about 1 mm across that do not fade when pressed. What are they called?
opciones: Petechiae
Purpura
Ecchymosis
Erythema
preguntas.explicacion: Petechiae are pinpoint non-blanching spots under 2 mm affecting skin and mucous membranes, caused by bleeding into the dermis; a non-blanching spot over 2 mm is purpura. A very large bruised area is an ecchymosis, and erythema, unlike bleeding into the skin, does blanch when pressed. Thrombocytopenia, platelet dysfunction, coagulation disorders and loss of vascular integrity are the underlying causes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Clinical Significance and section Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: How is the weight of the patient's signature in informed consent described today?
opciones: Its value as proof of understanding is questioned, and communication is favored
It is the single element the accreditation body checks when it reviews a record
It is needed only for procedures that carry a risk of serious bleeding
It moves responsibility for a bad outcome from the clinician to the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Adequate informed consent counts as a patient safety issue, and leaning on a signature as proof that the patient understood is increasingly doubted; the process is moving toward communication and away from signatures. The elements still have to be documented, whether on a form, in progress notes or elsewhere in the record.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peak Flow Rate Measurement", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(13)(c)· NCMA 2B.14
preguntas.pregunta: How does a patient establish a personal best peak flow?
opciones: Recording readings 2 to 4 times a day for 2 weeks while feeling well
Recording readings 2 to 4 times a day for 2 weeks during an exacerbation
Taking the highest of three readings on the day the meter is handed over
Using the value predicted for the patient's height, age and sex instead
preguntas.explicacion: The personal best is the highest value recorded in a diary over two weeks of readings taken two to four times a day, ideally while the patient feels well; it can come out above or below the predicted value. It anchors the written action plan, and it is re-established yearly to allow for growth in children and for disease progression.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: In a neonatal unit many samples are icteric. Why does this make visual screening for hemolysis even less dependable?
opciones: The high bilirubin colors the serum and leads to underestimation of hemolysis by eye
Bilirubin binds free hemoglobin, so the hemolysis index reads falsely low on the analyzer
Icteric serum cannot be centrifuged fully, so the red cells stay suspended in the sample
Bilirubin makes the serum turbid, which is mistaken for lipemia rather than hemolysis
preguntas.explicacion: Neonatal samples usually carry a high bilirubin, and that biases the eye further towards missing hemolysis when the judgment is visual; it is one more argument for assessing hemolysis, icterus and lipemia automatically and objectively. The index itself is a spectrophotometric measurement the paper treats as the reliable reference, and turbidity marks lipemia, not bilirubin.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Nasopharyngeal Swab and Deep Nasal Swab
preguntas.subtema: NP swab depth · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(c) · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: How far should a nasopharyngeal swab be inserted?
opciones: To a depth equal to the distance from the nostril to the outer opening of the ear
To a depth of less than one inch, until resistance is felt at the turbinates
To a depth equal to the distance from the nostril to the outer corner of the eyelid
To a depth of about two inches, or until the patient begins to cough or gag
preguntas.explicacion: The head is tilted back 70 degrees, the swab goes in until it has reached a depth equal to the distance from the nostril to the outer opening of the ear, and it is left several seconds to soak up secretions before being withdrawn slowly while rotating. Less than one inch, to the turbinates, is the deep nasal swab instead. Both nostrils are done with the same swab.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Water in diet — Recommendations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 nutrients · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(g) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(g) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: What is the Dietary Reference Intake for water in adults?
opciones: 91 to 125 fluid ounces (2.7 to 3.7 liters) a day, from food and drink together
91 to 125 fluid ounces (2.7 to 3.7 liters) a day, from drinking water alone
64 fluid ounces (about 1.9 liters) a day, from food and drink together
40 to 60 fluid ounces (1.2 to 1.8 liters) a day, from drinking water alone
preguntas.explicacion: The reference intake for adults falls between 91 and 125 fluid ounces, that is 2.7 to 3.7 liters, and it counts everything taken in from both food and beverages, not glasses of plain water. No separate figure is set for drinking water. Needs shift with sex, weight, age, activity and medical conditions.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Safely Using Sharps (Needles and Syringes) at Home, at Work and on Travel, How to Dispose of Sharps
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: What features does the FDA describe for a cleared sharps disposal container?
opciones: Puncture-resistant plastic, leak-resistant sides and bottom, and a tight puncture-resistant lid
Transparent flexible plastic with a wide open top so the fill level is always visible
A lined cardboard box marked with the biohazard symbol, emptied by hand when three-quarters full
Any closable metal can, provided it is labeled and kept away from the patient
preguntas.explicacion: FDA-cleared sharps containers are built of plastic a needle cannot pierce, with sides and a base that do not leak and a tight lid that a needle cannot go through, and used sharps go into them immediately. When no cleared container is available, a stout plastic household container, a laundry detergent bottle for instance, is the alternative given; an open top, a cardboard box or hand emptying contradict those features.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Does Pneumatic Tube System Transport Contribute to Hemolysis in ED Blood Samples?" (West J Emerg Med 2016, PMC5017839), Results and Conclusion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.D.4 · CCMA 3E k144 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital compared hemolysis in 15,851 ED specimens sent by pneumatic tube with 92 hand-carried during system downtime. What did it find, and what did the authors advise?
opciones: No significant difference (13.6 % vs 13.1 %); each system is unique, so every facility should examine its own
A large increase with the tube system (13.6 % vs 3.3 %); hospitals should hand-carry all ED specimens
Less hemolysis with the tube system (10.3 % vs 13.1 %); faster delivery protects the red cells
No difference, which proves that pneumatic tube systems can never contribute to hemolysis anywhere
preguntas.explicacion: The proportions of hemolysed specimens were 13.6 % by pneumatic tube and 13.1 % hand-carried, with no statistical difference, and the result held for gross and mild hemolysis separately. Because other hospitals have seen large increases after installing a system, and features such as speed, distance and packing differ, the authors encourage each facility to consider whether its own transport method contributes to hemolysis rather than generalising.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 1.1
preguntas.subtema: Quality of collection · CPT D3 k9 · D1 1B 1D k25 · PBT VI.A.1 · CCMA 3E7 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: In which respects does phlebotomy practice differ most between countries and institutions?
opciones: Technique, training, safety devices, disposal, device reuse and hepatitis B vaccine
Technique, tube color codes, room lighting, chair design and staffing levels
Training, laboratory opening hours, courier routes and analyser brands used
Safety devices, billing codes, appointment systems and record retention rules
preguntas.explicacion: Drawing blood is one of the commonest invasive procedures in health care, yet practice varies widely from country to country, and between institutions and individuals inside one of them. The differences named are technique, training, use of safety devices, disposal, reuse of devices and hepatitis B vaccine.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Free Samples
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A drug company leaves free samples at the practice. What may the office do with them?
opciones: Give them to patients free of charge, but never sell them
Sell them at cost to patients who cannot afford the drug
Bill the plan for them at the price a pharmacy charges
Bill Medicare for them once the patient takes the first dose
preguntas.explicacion: Handing free samples to patients at no charge is lawful; selling them is not, and physicians have been prosecuted for billing Medicare for samples they were given. A practice that keeps samples should store them safely and apart from the stock it has bought.

preguntas.fuente: USPS, Compare Mail Services
preguntas.subtema: Mail classes · CCMA 5O · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.3.f · CMAA 7G k96 · NCMA 3.6
preguntas.pregunta: Records must reach a hospital across the country by the fastest domestic service the Postal Service offers. Which is it?
opciones: Priority Mail Express, delivered seven days a week
Priority Mail, delivered in two to three days
USPS Ground Advantage, delivered in two to five days
First-Class Mail, the service used for ordinary letters
preguntas.explicacion: Priority Mail Express is described as the fastest domestic shipping service; it runs every day of the week and every day of the year, with limited exceptions, and reaches most United States addresses and post office boxes in one to three days under a money-back guarantee. Priority Mail arrives in two to three days and Ground Advantage in two to five.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, Information Blocking
preguntas.subtema: Information blocking · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 7 k90 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A practice delays sending records to a competing clinic in the hope of keeping the patient. What is that practice at risk of being?
opciones: Information blocking, a practice likely to interfere with the use of electronic health information
A breach of unsecured PHI that obliges the practice to give notice inside sixty days
A minimum necessary violation, since the records were not limited to what was needed
An impermissible marketing communication, since the aim was to keep the patient enrolled
preguntas.explicacion: Information blocking names a practice by an actor that would probably get in the way of accessing, exchanging or using electronic health information, unless the law demands it or one of the exceptions covers it. The actors reached are health care providers, health information networks and exchanges, and the developers of certified health IT. For a provider the test is whether it knows the practice is unreasonable and likely to interfere.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Hazardous Chemicals, health hazard and physical hazard classifications
preguntas.subtema: Health vs physical hazards · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Hazard Communication standard, which of these is classified as a health hazard rather than a physical hazard?
opciones: Skin corrosion or irritation
A flammable liquid such as a solvent
A gas under pressure in a cylinder
An oxidizing liquid or solid
preguntas.explicacion: The eTool splits the classifications into two families. On the health side: acute toxicity; corrosion or irritation of the skin; serious eye damage or eye irritation; sensitization of the airways or of the skin; germ cell mutagenicity; carcinogenicity; toxicity to reproduction; target organ toxicity; and aspiration hazard. On the physical side: explosives; gases under pressure; flammables and oxidizers; substances that are self-reactive, pyrophoric or self-heating; organic peroxides; anything corrosive to metal; and substances that release flammable gas on contact with water.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Formation of the Platelet Plug
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k74) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Bleeding from a small puncture stops within minutes, before any fibrin has formed. Which step of hemostasis is doing the work, and which plasma glycoprotein stabilizes it?
opciones: The platelet plug, stabilized by von Willebrand factor
The fibrin mesh, which factor XIII cross-links and stabilizes
The vascular spasm, which serotonin from platelets maintains
Fibrinolysis, which plasmin made from plasminogen carries out
preguntas.explicacion: In the second step of hemostasis, platelets meet the exposed collagen, become spiked and sticky and clump together, helped by a plasma glycoprotein called von Willebrand factor that stabilizes the growing plug. The plug can temporarily seal a small opening and buys time for coagulation. Factor XIII stabilizes fibrin, serotonin keeps the vessel constricted, and plasmin dissolves the finished clot.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Measuring Your Blood Pressure: How to measure your blood pressure at home
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B14 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is being taught to monitor blood pressure at home. Which instruction is given?
opciones: Take two or more readings a minute or two apart, at the same time each day
Take one reading a day, at the hour the patient happens to be free that day
Take at least two readings 10 minutes apart, at a different hour each day
Take a reading only on days the patient feels unwell, and log those values
preguntas.explicacion: Self-measured monitoring works best with a routine: the same hour every day, at least two readings a minute or two apart, and every value written in a log. One common plan is a reading before breakfast and before dinner for five days, which gives the provider at least ten values to work from.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Capacity · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia signed a consent form last month. What does that tell the team about today's decision?
opciones: Nothing by itself; capacity is judged for the decision at hand, on the day
It stands until a court holds a hearing and rules the patient incapacitated
It stands as long as the same clinician is the one obtaining consent today
It stands, because a dementia diagnosis makes the finding permanent anyway
preguntas.explicacion: A capacity assessment is valid only for the time, place and situation in which it was made: it is a snapshot, not a status. The same patient may be lucid and deciding well one day and disoriented two weeks later, and an intoxicated patient may decide soundly once sober. The court hearing settles competence, which is the separate legal question.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A problem list records a TIA two years before the CVA the patient was admitted with. What separates those two entries?
opciones: A TIA is a small stroke, and a CVA is the stroke itself
A TIA is a small stroke, and a CVA is a clot in a deep vein
A TIA is a heart attack, and a CVA is a stroke of the brain
A TIA is a brief seizure, and a CVA is a stroke of the brain
preguntas.explicacion: TIA stands for transient ischemic attack, listed as a small stroke, while CVA is a cerebrovascular accident, the stroke or brain attack itself. The abbreviations that get swapped in belong to other organs: AMI and MI are the heart attack, and DVT is the clot in a deep vein.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", sections Issues of Concern and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 k9 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist fills the light gray fluoride tube before the purple EDTA tube. What is the main risk?
opciones: Additive carried from one tube into the next, giving unreliable results
Loss of the vacuum in the purple tube as soon as it is pushed on
A short draw in the gray tube, which can haemolyse that specimen
Clotting in the purple tube, because its additive was left unmixed
preguntas.explicacion: A fixed sequence exists so that the additive of one tube is not carried into the tube filled next, and falsely raised or lowered values can follow in chemistry, hematology, serology and microbiology. A short draw and unmixed additive are real faults, but they come from filling and mixing, not order.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Systolic and Diastolic Pressures; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Physiology of Circulation, Pulse and Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.2 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's blood pressure is recorded as 120/80. What does each number represent?
opciones: 120 is systolic, during ventricular contraction; 80 is diastolic, during relaxation
120 is diastolic, during ventricular relaxation; 80 is systolic, during contraction
120 is the pulse pressure in the aorta; 80 is the mean arterial pressure in the arteries
120 is the pressure inside the aorta; 80 is the pressure inside the venae cavae
preguntas.explicacion: A blood pressure of 120/80 is a normal adult value written as systolic over diastolic: the higher number, around 120 mm Hg, is the arterial pressure produced by ventricular contraction, and the lower, about 80 mm Hg, is the pressure during ventricular relaxation. Pulse pressure is their difference (40 mm Hg here) and mean arterial pressure is a separate calculated value.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fever
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A5 k56 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A caregiver reports a child's temperature as 38 °C. Which Fahrenheit value is recorded, and what does it mean by the rectal route?
opciones: 100.4 °F, which is exactly the rectal threshold for fever in a child
101.4 °F, which is above the rectal threshold for fever in a child
99.5 °F, which is the oral rather than the rectal threshold in a child
98.6 °F, which is the average adult value and not a fever at any site
preguntas.explicacion: The two scales are recorded as a pair in clinical sources: 38 °C is 100.4 °F, and that is the exact point at which a rectal reading counts as fever in a child. The oral threshold is 99.5 °F (37.5 °C) and the average adult value is 98.6 °F (37 °C), which is why the route is always written beside the number.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which tube in the WHO order of draw is filled immediately before the purple EDTA tube when a full set is collected?
opciones: The light green PST with lithium heparin and gel
The dark green sodium heparin tube
The pale yellow acid-citrate-dextrose tube
The red-gray tiger top or gold serum separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: EDTA is position 8 in Table 2.3, and position 7 is the light green plasma separator tube with lithium heparin and a gel separator. The dark green sodium heparin tube is position 6, the serum separator tube position 5, and the pale yellow ACD tube comes after EDTA at position 9. Reading the table by neighbours is the surest way to reconstruct the whole sequence.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7
preguntas.subtema: Syringe transfer · CPT D3 k54 k9 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Blood from a syringe has to go into a sample tube that has no rubber stopper. How is it transferred?
opciones: Injected extremely slowly, keeping pressure and speed to a minimum
Injected as briskly as possible so the tube fills before it can clot
Poured down the inner wall of the tube after the needle is removed
Injected only after the needle has been recapped for the transfer
preguntas.explicacion: Where there is no rubber stopper to pierce, the blood is injected extremely slowly, because keeping the pressure and the velocity of the transfer low is what limits hemolysis. The instruction that closes that step is not to recap and remove the needle afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Yellow, Pink, and Blue

preguntas.pregunta: After a blood culture bottle is filled, how many times should it be mixed?
opciones: 8 to 10 times
3 to 6 times
1 or 2 times
15 to 20 times
preguntas.explicacion: A culture bottle is mixed 8 to 10 times after the blood is added so that the contents combine properly. The 3 to 6 inversions belong to the light blue citrate tube in the coagulopathies review, done immediately after the draw. One or two turns is the kind of under-mixing the review links to small clots, and 15 to 20 is not a figure given for any tube.

preguntas.pregunta: Which team member manages oxygen therapy, draws arterial blood gases and runs mechanical ventilators?
opciones: The respiratory therapist, who also gives inhalers and nebulizer medicines
The physical therapist, who also teaches patients to use walkers and canes safely
The occupational therapist, who also assesses the home for safety needs
The clinical laboratory technologist, who also performs blood bank testing
preguntas.explicacion: Respiratory therapists treat respiratory conditions: drawing arterial blood gases, managing oxygen therapy, running mechanical ventilators and CPAP or BiPAP machines, giving inhalers and nebulizer medicines, intubating, assisting with bronchoscopy, performing chest physiotherapy, and taking a central part during cardiac and respiratory arrests.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A referral is addressed to a nephrologist. Which organ does the root of that specialty name?
opciones: The kidney, which is also named by the root ren-
The liver, which is also named by the root hepat-
The bladder, which is also named by the root cyst-
The stomach, which is also named by the root gastr-
preguntas.explicacion: Nephr- and ren- both name the kidney, which is why the same organ gives us nephrology and renal failure. The other roots belong to their own organs: hepat- the liver, cyst- a bladder or sac, gastr- the stomach. Two roots for one organ is common in this vocabulary, one from Greek and one from Latin.
