Cognitive dysfunction, the commonest reaction and a reason to change agents
preguntas.explicacion: Statins are generally well tolerated; the reactions seen most are myopathy, hepatotoxicity and new diabetes. Myopathy is dose dependent and shows as diffuse myalgias or otherwise unexplained tenderness or weakness that reverses when the drug is stopped. Rhabdomyolysis is the gravest complication but is rare, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy persists for months, and cognitive change is rare.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Does Pneumatic Tube System Transport Contribute to Hemolysis in ED Blood Samples?" (West J Emerg Med 2016, PMC5017839), Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A ward asks why the laboratory presses so hard on hemolysis when redrawing a tube takes two minutes. What consequences does the literature attach to it?
opciones: Delayed decisions, a longer stay in the department, and extra needle sticks
Loss of the quality control run and a forced recalibration of the analyser
A mandatory report of the quality failure to the accrediting organization
A penalty against the laboratory's proficiency testing performance that year
preguntas.explicacion: A hemolysed sample usually means drawing and testing a second one. Repeats hold up treatment and the clinical decisions that depend on it, stretch the patient's stay in the emergency department, and leave the patient unhappy at having been stuck more than once. The cost lands on the patient, not on the analyser, which is why the collection step gets the attention.

preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: A patient files a written grievance about the quality of care. What must the hospital give back?
opciones: Written notice naming the contact person, the steps taken, the result and the date
Written notice that the complaint was received and then forwarded to the state agency
Verbal notice from the department manager once the review has been completed
Written notice of the outcome only if the grievance is found to have merit
preguntas.explicacion: A hospital must run a process for resolving grievances promptly and tell each patient whom to contact in order to file one. Resolving it means giving the patient written notice of the decision, naming the hospital's contact person, describing the steps taken to investigate, the results, and the date the process closed. The governing body owns the process.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: The chest electrodes are being placed on a patient. Where does V1 go?
opciones: At the fourth intercostal space, right of the sternal border
At the fifth intercostal space, right of the sternal border
At the fourth intercostal space, left of the sternal border
At the fifth intercostal space, in the mid-clavicular line
preguntas.explicacion: V1 sits in the fourth intercostal space just to the right of the sternum, and V2 goes in the same space on the left side. The two spots are found by walking the fingers down from the sternal angle, and they are marked before the skin is cleaned so the location is not lost.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Blood cultures, a prothrombin time and a complete blood count are ordered on one venipuncture. Which specimen is collected third?
opciones: The purple EDTA tube for the complete blood count
The light blue citrate tube for the prothrombin time
The blood culture bottle for the microbiology order
A non-additive tube drawn ahead of the citrate tube
preguntas.explicacion: Of the three, the culture bottle sits at position 1, the citrate tube at position 3 and EDTA at position 8, so the EDTA tube is the third one filled. A non-additive tube does hold position 2, but the footnote reserves it for when tissue fluid or thromboplastin contamination is a concern.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Neomycin, Polymyxin, and Hydrocortisone Otic: To use the eardrops
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k70 · CMA I.D.2.c(6) · RMA III.G.4.d(viii) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has been prescribed eardrops. Which set of instructions is correct?
opciones: Warm the bottle in the hand a minute or two, lie with that ear up, stay five minutes
Warm the bottle under hot tap water, lie with that ear down, stay for two minutes
Use the drops cold from the refrigerator, sit upright, and stay still for ten minutes
Warm the bottle in the hand, lie with that ear up, and get up as soon as it is done
preguntas.explicacion: The bottle is held in the hand for one or two minutes to warm the solution, a suspension is shaken, and the ear canal is cleaned and dried with a sterile applicator first. The patient lies with the affected ear uppermost, the ordered number of drops goes in without the dropper touching anything, and that position is kept for five minutes. A cotton wick may be used and is replaced at least every 24 hours.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · RMA III.E.3 Pulse b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which peripheral pulse is described as the hardest to palpate, especially for a less experienced clinician?
opciones: The posterior tibial, found immediately behind the medial malleolus
The popliteal, found a little lateral to the midline in the popliteal fossa
The femoral, found just below the inguinal ligament toward the pubic symphysis
The brachial, found between the medial epicondyle and the tendon of the biceps
preguntas.explicacion: The posterior tibial pulse sits just behind the bony bump on the inner ankle and is considered the most difficult of the peripheral pulses to feel. The popliteal is also sought less often, but the one singled out for difficulty is the posterior tibial, which matters when its absence is being used as a finding.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 3.2 The Cytoplasm and Cellular Organelles, Organelles for Energy Production
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k35 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A neuron may hold more than a thousand of one organelle, while a bone cell holds only a couple hundred. Which organelle is it, and why the difference?
opciones: The mitochondrion, because a neuron needs far more ATP than a bone cell
The lysosome, because a neuron digests far more debris than a bone cell
The nucleus, because a neuron stores far more genetic material than a bone cell
The Golgi apparatus, because a neuron exports far more protein than a bone cell
preguntas.explicacion: Mitochondria convert the energy held in nutrients such as glucose into ATP, along an inner membrane folded into cristae. Cells that spend a lot of energy carry a lot of them: muscle cells are packed with them for contraction and neurons need them to run their sodium and potassium pumps, while a bone cell is far less active.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Authorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorization elements · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a-b · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which feature must appear on a valid HIPAA authorization form?
opciones: An expiration and a statement of the right to revoke it in writing, all in plain language
A witness signature from a workforce member who watched the patient sign the document
A cost estimate of the copies, since the fee has to be agreed before the release is signed
A clause making treatment conditional on the patient granting the authorization requested
preguntas.explicacion: An authorization has to be written in specific terms and in plain language, and it has to state what information is involved, who is disclosing it, who is receiving it, when it runs out, and that it can be revoked in writing. Conditioning treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits on the patient signing one is forbidden to a covered entity, save in the limited circumstances the rule spells out.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Overweight & Obesity — Definition & Facts, BMI of adults ages 20 and older
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k26 weight control · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(a) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(a) · RMA XI vital signs and measurements · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which body mass index range is classified as overweight in adults aged 20 and older?
opciones: 25 to 29.9, with obesity beginning at 30
25 to 29.9, with obesity beginning at 35
24 to 28.9, with obesity beginning at 29
27 to 31.9, with obesity beginning at 32
preguntas.explicacion: The adult table runs 18.5 to 24.9 for healthy weight, 25 to 29.9 for overweight, and 30 or higher for obesity, with 40 and above marked as severe obesity. Body mass index estimates overweight and obesity from weight and height together; it is not a direct measurement of body fat.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, EMR vs EHR - What is the Difference?
preguntas.subtema: EHR versus EMR · CCMA 5 k172 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.c · CMAA k3 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes an electronic health record from an electronic medical record?
opciones: The EHR is built to be shared with other organizations involved in the patient's care
The EHR is the version the patient keeps at home, while the EMR belongs to the practice
The EHR holds only billing and demographic data, while the EMR holds the clinical notes
The EHR is a scanned copy of the paper chart, while the EMR is entered directly by staff
preguntas.explicacion: An EMR is the digital version of the paper chart in one clinician's office: it tracks data over time, flags who is due for screening and supports quality work inside that practice, but the information does not travel easily beyond it. An EHR is designed to reach past the organization that collected the data, so the record follows the patient to the specialist, the hospital or the next state.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urine Culture", Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and PMC, PMC4771218 LaRocco et al., Effectiveness of Preanalytic Practices on Urine Cultures (2016), Summary of findings
preguntas.subtema: Urine culture delay · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k117 · CMA I.C.8.c · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: A clean-catch urine for culture cannot reach the microbiology laboratory for about 6 hours. What keeps the culture result valid?
opciones: Refrigerating it or placing it in a boric acid preservative tube, either of which holds it for up to 24 hours
Keeping it at room temperature, which is acceptable for up to 24 hours as long as the cup stays capped
Freezing it, since freezing stops bacterial growth more completely than refrigeration does
Adding a formaldehyde preservative, the additive that best protects bacteria for later culture
preguntas.explicacion: Urine for culture must be plated within 2 hours unless it is refrigerated or placed in a preservative; both boric acid and refrigeration hold the specimen adequately for up to 24 hours. Urine left at room temperature for more than 4 hours shows overgrowth of both pathogens and contaminants. Formaldehyde is used to preserve cells and causes false-positive strip reactions, and freezing is not an accepted substitute for refrigeration.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Doses/Measurement Units
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A handwritten order reads QD. Which misreading put that abbreviation on the Do Not Use list?
opciones: It is read as QID, four times daily, instead of every day
It is read as QOD, every other day, instead of every day
It is read as QHS, nightly at bedtime, instead of every day
It is read as PRN, only as needed, instead of every day
preguntas.explicacion: QD means every day, but a handwritten q that trails off, or the period that follows it, gets taken for the letter i, and the order turns into QID, four doses a day. Write daily instead. QOD has its own entry on the list, where the badly written o is the problem.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Network; and Glossary: Out-of-pocket maximum/limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.e (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 4 k61 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: What does a health plan's "network" consist of?
opciones: The providers, facilities and suppliers under contract with the insurer
The list of prescription drugs the plan covers, also called its drug list
The providers the patient may see without a referral from the primary care doctor
The services that count toward the out-of-pocket limit, including out-of-network care
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines the network as the set of facilities, providers and suppliers that have a contract with the insurer or plan to deliver health care services. Being in the network is a matter of contract, not of whether a referral is needed: in many HMOs even in-network specialists require one. The glossary's entry on the out-of-pocket limit shows the other side of the coin: care received out of network does not count toward that limit. The list of covered drugs is the formulary, a separate entry.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature e · NCMA 2B.5
preguntas.pregunta: A temperature is charted as 38.2 °C with no other detail. What is missing?
opciones: The route used, since each site carries its own average and its own fever cut-off
The thermometer model, since each manufacturer calibrates its device differently
The room temperature, since a warm room lifts every reading by a fixed amount
The patient's baseline, since a value has no meaning until a baseline is on file
preguntas.explicacion: The same patient reads differently at the armpit, the mouth, the ear and the rectum, and the thresholds for calling a value a fever follow the site. A number without its route cannot be graded or compared with the last one, which is why the route is written beside the value and the hour it was taken.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Plasma Anticoagulants
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k57 heparin tubes) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which natural anticoagulant is released by basophils, opposes prothrombin, and is also given as a drug to surgical patients at risk of clots?
opciones: Heparin
Protein C
Thrombin
Plasmin
preguntas.explicacion: Several plasma anticoagulants keep clotting confined to the injury: the protein C system, TFPI, antithrombin and heparin. Heparin comes from basophils, is short-acting, opposes prothrombin and also sits on the cells lining the vessels; a pharmaceutical form is given, for example, to surgical patients at risk of clots. Thrombin builds fibrin and plasmin dissolves it; neither is an anticoagulant.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: CPR - adult and child after onset of puberty, First Aid and When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: Lone rescuer sequence · CPT D1 1L k38 · CMA I.B.9.c / 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist working alone finds an unresponsive adult who is not breathing. What is the first step?
opciones: Call 911 (or the local emergency number), get an AED if one is known to be nearby, then start CPR
Give 2 rescue breaths, then check the pulse for 10 seconds before calling
Start compressions for 2 minutes, then leave to look for an AED anywhere in the building
Place the person in the recovery position and monitor breathing until help arrives
preguntas.explicacion: After checking responsiveness by tapping and shouting, a lone rescuer calls 911 or the local emergency number as soon as the person is found unresponsive, retrieves an AED only if one is known to be nearby, and then begins CPR with 30 compressions and 2 breaths; the rescuer should not leave the person to search for an AED whose location is unknown. With help available, one person calls while another starts CPR. The recovery position is for a person who has started breathing again, and pulse checks are left to health professionals.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advance Directives", Clinical Significance; and Issues of Concern: Living Will
preguntas.subtema: Health care proxy · CCMA k218 · CMA E.8.c / 2027 E.7.b · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: How much authority does an appointed health care proxy have?
opciones: The same authority to request or refuse care the patient would have had
Authority limited to the treatments the living will names one by one
Authority limited to comfort care and to consenting for routine tests
Authority to demand any treatment at all, since the patient cannot speak now
preguntas.explicacion: The proxy or surrogate holds the same power to request or refuse treatment the patient would have held if they could still decide and speak. That authority is not confined to whatever the living will happened to list, and it is not narrowed to comfort measures. What it does not include is demanding care that is not medically indicated: the right to refuse is broader than the right to demand.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Latex Allergies - for Hospital Patients, How to Avoid Exposure to Latex in the Hospital
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient with a known latex allergy is admitted for several days of blood work. Which measure applies?
opciones: Post a sign on the door, note the allergy in the chart, and remove latex items from the room
Use powdered latex gloves, which release fewer allergenic proteins onto the skin
Keep the latex gloves in the room but double-glove with vinyl over them
Notify only the surgical team, since gloves matter most in the operating room
preguntas.explicacion: Hospital patients with latex allergy should ask for a sign on the door and notes in the chart, for latex gloves and other latex items to be removed from the room, and for pharmacy and dietary staff to be told so they do not handle medicines or food with latex gloves. Cornstarch powder on latex gloves is a leading source of inhaled allergen, the opposite of a safeguard.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Design Recommendations
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Under the FDA's design advice for needle-safety features, what must be true once the feature has fired?
opciones: It cannot be deactivated and stays protective through disposal
It can be reset once so the device can be used on the same patient
It stays protective until the device reaches the sharps container
It may be released by a second single-handed action if needed
preguntas.explicacion: Table 1 of the FDA guidance lists, for all feature types, that the user should be able to tell easily whether the feature is activated, and that once activated it cannot be undone and should keep protecting right through disposal. Resetting or releasing the feature is the opposite of that recommendation, and protection that ended at the container would not cover the disposal step.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning", Structure and Function: Supine Position
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b(7) · RMA III.F.2.b.i · NCMA 2B.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is placed supine with the arms out on boards. How far may the arms be abducted?
opciones: Less than 90 degrees, which keeps the humerus from pressing on the axilla
Up to 120 degrees, as long as a pad is placed underneath each elbow
As far as the boards reach, provided the palms are turned toward the floor
Exactly 90 degrees, the angle at which the ulnar nerve is under least strain
preguntas.explicacion: Abduction is held under 90 degrees so that the humerus does not press into the axilla and injure the brachial plexus. The forearms rest neutral or supinated, palms toward the body, which keeps pressure off the ulnar nerve; malpositioning of the arm in this position is the commonest source of ulnar injury. A draw sheet tucked under the torso holds an adducted arm.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fiber — Side Effects; and Recommendations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(f) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(f) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who doubled his fiber in one week complains of gas, bloating and cramps. What should he be told?
opciones: Build fiber up slowly over a few weeks and drink plenty of fluid
Build fiber up slowly over a few weeks and cut back on fluid
Stop the fiber, since these symptoms mean he cannot tolerate it
Switch entirely to fiber supplements, which do not cause symptoms
preguntas.explicacion: A large jump in fiber over a short time brings gas, bloating and abdominal cramps, and the complaint usually settles once the gut bacteria adjust. Adding fiber gradually rather than all at once reduces the gas and diarrhea, and fluid is what carries fiber through the digestive tract, so about eight glasses a day are advised.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", section Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A seated patient becomes pale and sweaty and says he is about to faint. What should happen right away?
opciones: He should sit or lie down quickly with the legs elevated, and stay horizontal afterwards
He should stand up and walk slowly to a couch, since the movement restores the venous return
He should be given a sugary drink, since hypoglycemia is the most common cause
He should keep still and upright while the last tube finishes filling
preguntas.explicacion: Patients are told to sit or lie down at once during an acute episode, legs raised, to help recovery from reflex postural hypotension, and should be kept horizontal afterwards and prevented from standing too soon; any injury from a fall needs immediate attention. Standing up is the opposite of the advice, and hypoglycemia is listed as a mimic of syncope, not its usual cause.

preguntas.subtema: Verbal orders · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A provider gives a verbal order during a procedure. What does the record have to show afterwards?
opciones: That the order was dated, timed and authenticated promptly by a responsible practitioner
That the order was witnessed by two members of staff before it was carried out
That the order was entered as a standing order approved by the medical staff earlier
That the order was repeated back and then filed in the practice correspondence log
preguntas.explicacion: Orders of every kind, spoken ones included, have to carry a date, a time and prompt authentication from the practitioner who gave the order, or from another practitioner who is responsible for the patient where State scope-of-practice law, the facility's policy and the medical staff rules permit it. Preprinted and electronic standing orders run on a separate mechanism, with their own approval and review requirements.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 5.4, Table 5.4a: Common Household Conversions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k17 · CMA I.D.2.b(2) · RMA III.G.2.f · NCMA 1.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is asked to record intake in milliliters and reports drinking one cup of water. What is recorded?
opciones: 240 mL, since a cup is 8 ounces and an ounce is 30 mL
180 mL, since a cup is 6 ounces and an ounce is 30 mL
480 mL, since a cup is 8 ounces and an ounce is 60 mL
120 mL, since a cup is 8 ounces and an ounce is 15 mL
preguntas.explicacion: One ounce is 30 mL and one cup is 8 ounces, so a cup comes to 240 mL. The rest of the household ladder follows from there: a pound is 16 ounces, a pint is 2 cups, a quart is 4 cups and a gallon is 4 quarts. Intake and output conversions are one of the routine calculations, and they are recorded in metric units even when the patient reports them in household ones.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 1.3 Types of Microorganisms, Prokaryotic Microorganisms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structural feature separates bacteria from the fungi and protozoa?
opciones: Bacteria are prokaryotes, so their genetic material has no true nucleus
Bacteria are eukaryotes, so their genetic material has no true nucleus
Bacteria are acellular, so their genetic material sits outside any cell
Bacteria are multicellular, so their genetic material is shared between cells
preguntas.explicacion: Bacteria and archaea are prokaryotes: their DNA is not housed in a true nucleus, and most bacterial cell walls contain peptidoglycan. Fungi and protozoa belong to the eukaryotes, whose defining feature is that the cell does have a nucleus. Viruses are in neither camp, because they are not made of cells at all.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.3 Aseptic Technique, Table 4.3
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.B.5.a (2027 I.B.4.a) · RMA III.A.3.a(i) · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: When must soap and water be used for hand hygiene rather than an alcohol-based rub?
opciones: When the hands are visibly soiled, and when the patient has Clostridioides difficile
When the hands are visibly soiled, and when the patient is on droplet precautions
When gloves are about to be worn, and when the patient has Clostridioides difficile
When entering a room, and when the previous patient was on contact precautions
preguntas.explicacion: Alcohol-based rub is used until dry for most moments of hand hygiene, but two situations send the practitioner to the sink: hands that are visibly soiled and a patient with C. difficile. Hand hygiene is also one of the infection control measures planned before a procedure, alongside environmental control, the choice of gloves, the aseptic field and sequencing from clean to dirty.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A · D2 2N · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: What is placed under the patient's arm before the draw begins?
opciones: A clean paper or towel
A warm compress pack
A rolled cloth tourniquet
A sterile drape with a window
preguntas.explicacion: Preparing the patient includes making the person comfortable, supine where that is possible, and laying a clean paper or towel under the arm that is going to be used. Warming the limb is a measure kept for veins that are hard to find, not a routine part of setting the patient up.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, CLIA Test Complexities: Test complexity categorization; Nonwaived testing; Related terms
preguntas.subtema: Three CLIA complexity categories · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F / VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.1 · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: Under CLIA, laboratory tests are sorted into how many complexity categories, and which are they?
opciones: Three: high complexity, moderate complexity and waived
Two: waived and nonwaived, with no further split
Four: waived, PPM, moderate and high complexity
Three: home use, point-of-care and laboratory
preguntas.explicacion: The regulation grades every test system as waived, moderate complexity or high complexity, from the least to the most demanding. Moderate and high together are called nonwaived testing. Provider-performed microscopy is a subcategory inside moderate complexity, not a fourth category, and point-of-care describes where a test is run, not how it is classified.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Other Issues, Human Clinical Studies
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which three elements must valid informed consent for a research study include?
opciones: Disclosure of information, competency to decide, and a voluntary decision
Disclosure of information, a witness signature, and an approved study budget
Competency to decide, a voluntary decision, and payment for participation
Competency to decide, a signed waiver, and a copy filed with the sponsor
preguntas.explicacion: Valid research consent stands on three elements: the information has to be disclosed; the patient, or the surrogate deciding for them, has to be competent to make that decision; and the decision has to be voluntary. Ethical standards in the design of a study are watched over by an Institutional Review Board, which may waive the consent requirement only where the risk to participants is minimal.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6; and StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Anchoring the vein · CPT D3 3H k64 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: A trainee steadies the vein by pressing a thumb on the skin just ABOVE the intended puncture point. What is the correct anchoring technique?
opciones: Place the thumb below the site and pull the skin down and slightly away, making it taut
Place the thumb above the site but press down harder, so that the vein cannot roll sideways
Use the index finger over the vein itself to guide the shaft of the needle
Skip anchoring; ask the patient to make a fist, which fixes the vein in place
preguntas.explicacion: Step 6 of the WHO procedure anchors the vein by holding the arm and placing a thumb below the venipuncture site; the free hand then uses the thumb to draw the skin downward and a little away from the site until it is taut. A finger over the vein is what Step 5 explicitly forbids after disinfection, and the fist is an addition that makes the veins prominent, not a replacement for anchoring.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Urgent care; and Glossary: Emergency services
preguntas.subtema: Urgent care vs emergency · CCMA 1A k4 · CMAA 1 k1 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A caller with no regular provider has a painful ear infection that began last night. Where should the front desk steer her first?
opciones: To an urgent care center, since the problem needs prompt care but is not emergency severe
To the hospital emergency department, where a sudden illness is always evaluated first
To an ambulatory surgical center, the outpatient site that handles same-day procedures
To a skilled nursing facility, where licensed nurses treat and observe a condition daily
preguntas.explicacion: Urgent care is meant for a problem serious enough that a person would want care without delay, yet not so severe that the emergency room is required. Emergency services mean evaluating an emergency condition and treating it so it does not worsen. For someone with no primary care provider, urgent care usually saves time and money over the emergency room.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Statin Medications", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k16 · CMA I.D.1.d · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking a statin has just learned she is pregnant. What does the drug information say about continuing?
opciones: Statins are stopped for most pregnant patients, and are also ruled out in lactation
Statins may run at half the usual dose to the end of the first trimester and stop
Statins are safe throughout pregnancy but are stopped during lactation for the infant
Statins are ruled out in pregnancy but may be resumed as soon as lactation begins
preguntas.explicacion: Statins are stopped for most patients who become pregnant. The FDA asks the clinician to weigh the need only where cardiovascular risk is extreme: the homozygous form of familial hypercholesterolemia, or heart and vessel disease already established. Breastfeeding rules them out as well, because the infant needs cholesterol for steroid synthesis and cell membranes. Active liver disease is the remaining contraindication.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Definition of Breach
preguntas.subtema: Breach risk assessment · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which factor is part of the risk assessment used to decide whether an impermissible disclosure is a breach?
opciones: The identity of the unauthorized person who used or received the information
The number of years the practice has operated without a previous incident
Whether the workforce member involved had completed the yearly privacy training
Whether the patient complained to the practice about the disclosure afterwards
preguntas.explicacion: At least four things go into the assessment: what PHI was involved and how much of it, taking in which identifiers appear and how likely re-identification would be; who the unauthorized person using or receiving it was; whether the PHI was in fact acquired or viewed; and how far the risk has been mitigated. Training records and complaints do not figure.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Hospital-wide Hazards: Recordkeeping, 29 CFR Part 1904; govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, sec. 2(9)
preguntas.subtema: OSHA 300, 301 and 300A · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.11.c / 2027 I.B.10.c · RMA II.B.7.e · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: Under OSHA's recordkeeping rule, 29 CFR part 1904, which forms record work-related injuries and illnesses?
opciones: The OSHA 300 log, the 301 incident report and the 300A summary posted each year
The sharps injury log, the training record and the employee medical record
The OSHA 200 log, which the Needlestick Act found sufficient for exposure tracking
The exposure determination, the written opinion and the Appendix A declination
preguntas.explicacion: Covered employers record each recordable injury and illness on the OSHA Form 300 log, prepare a Form 301 incident report with details of each case, and at the end of the year prepare the Form 300A summary and post it in a visible place. The sharps injury log, training records and medical records are kept under the bloodborne pathogens standard; the exposure determination, written opinion and declination are other documents of that same standard. Congress found the old OSHA 200 log insufficient, which is why the sharps log was added.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.4
preguntas.subtema: Read-only backup · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: What is a read-only backup record system able to do for a practice during an outage?
opciones: Show and print the information already recorded, from a copy refreshed often
Accept new orders and notes that are merged into the record after the outage
Run the scheduling module so that the day's appointments can still be moved
Send the claims already prepared, since billing does not alter clinical data
preguntas.explicacion: A read-only backup is a copy of what is already in the record system, kept up to date as often as possible, optimally hourly, and tested regularly. Users can look things up and print from it, but nothing new goes in, which is why paper forms and temporary record numbers are still needed for what happens during the outage.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, CLIA Test Complexities: Related terms ("Point-of-care testing"); and CDC, MMWR Recommendations and Reports 2005;54(RR-13), Good Laboratory Practices for Waived Testing Sites
preguntas.subtema: POCT is a location, not a category · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k111 · RMA III.C.2.a · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: A coworker says a rapid test "must be waived because we run it at the point of care." What is the correct reading of the term point-of-care testing under CLIA?
opciones: It describes where testing is done and says nothing about the test's complexity
It is a synonym for waived testing when the operator is not a laboratorian
It is the category for tests cleared by the FDA for home use
It refers to a laboratory licensed by a state whose rules are stricter than CLIA
preguntas.explicacion: Point-of-care is a location: the bedside or near the site of care. Some point-of-care tests are waived, but faster technology also lets nonwaived tests be run near the patient, so a test cannot be assumed waived just because of where it is performed. Home-use clearance is one route to waived status, and the state-licensed laboratory description is the meaning of CLIA-exempt.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(iv), Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.subtema: Exposure Control Plan · CPT D1 1H k31 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: How often does OSHA require an employer's written Exposure Control Plan to be reviewed and updated?
opciones: At least once a year, and whenever the tasks, procedures or positions with occupational exposure change
Within 10 working days of each new hire with occupational exposure, and otherwise every three years
Once a year together with the annual employee training, and at no other time even if tasks change
Every time an exposure incident is reported, and kept for the duration of employment plus 30 years
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(iv) sets two triggers: a review at least every year, plus a review whenever new or changed tasks, procedures or job positions alter who is exposed and how. The same review has to take in new technology that cuts exposure and document, each year, which safer medical devices were considered and adopted. The other periods belong to other rules of the same standard: 10 working days is the deadline for offering the hepatitis B vaccine, three years is how long training records are kept, and employment plus 30 years is the retention of medical records. An exposure incident triggers follow-up for the employee, not a rewrite of the plan.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", section Clinical Significance, When To Access Capacity
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 k49 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with dementia was found to lack capacity two weeks ago. What does that finding mean today?
opciones: Nothing by itself: the finding held for that time and that situation
It carries over until a judge rules that the patient has recovered
It carries over for the whole admission, once it is in the record
It removes the need to explain the draw, but not to ask permission
preguntas.explicacion: A capacity assessment holds good only for the moment, the place and the circumstances in which it was made; it is a snapshot, and it cannot be carried over to another occasion. A history of dementia does not by itself mean the person lacks capacity, and the same patient may be clear enough today to take part in the conversation. Competence is a court's decision.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1241(c)(6), Standard: Test request
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5F · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D k112 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: Which item on the test requisition allows the laboratory to judge later whether a specimen was transported within an acceptable time?
opciones: The date and, when appropriate, the time of specimen collection
The date the requisition was printed by the ordering office
The time the specimen was logged into the laboratory information system
The expected turnaround time promised to the ordering provider
preguntas.explicacion: CLIA requires the requisition to solicit the date and, if appropriate, the time of collection; combined with the receipt date and time the laboratory must document, this gives the transport interval that decides acceptability for time-sensitive tests. The printing date of the form and the promised turnaround say nothing about when blood left the patient, and the log-in time is the second half of the interval, not the first.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A stool specimen for a gastrointestinal molecular panel has to travel from a rural clinic. Which transport and storage plan matches the general guidelines?
opciones: Room temperature in stabilising media, or on ice; then 2 to 8 °C for four to seven days
Room temperature without media, or frozen; then 2 to 8 °C for up to twenty-four hours
On ice only, never at room temperature; then at −20 °C from the moment it arrives
Room temperature in stabilising media only; then at room temperature until extraction
preguntas.explicacion: For stool the variables listed are time, transport and storage temperature, stabilisation media and the patient's medications. Transport is either at room temperature when a stabilising medium is used or on ice, and storage runs four to seven days, at 2 to 8 °C or at room temperature if stabilised. Freezing on arrival is not part of that general scheme.

preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.c · 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: How far may an employee have to travel to reach an extinguisher for a Class A fire?
opciones: 75 feet (22.9 m) or less from anywhere employees may need one
50 feet (15.2 m) or less, the same as for a Class B hazard area
100 feet (30.5 m) or less, measured from the nearest exit door
25 feet (7.6 m) or less, measured from any combustible material
preguntas.explicacion: For Class A fires the travel distance to an extinguisher is 75 feet or less, and the same 75 feet applies to the distance from a combustible metal working area to a Class D agent. For Class B hazard areas the distance is 50 feet or less, and Class C units are spread on the pattern of the Class A or Class B hazards already there.

preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: On what is the WHO's illustrative order of draw for vacuum tubes based?
opciones: A 2003 consensus of the US national committee that then set clinical laboratory standards
The 2008 CDC guideline on disinfecting and sterilizing in health-care settings, with its annexes
The FDA classification of blood specimen collection devices in 21 CFR 862.1675
The OSHA standard on bloodborne pathogens, 29 CFR 1910.1030, at paragraph (d)(2)
preguntas.explicacion: Step 8 and the source line of Table 2.3 credit the sequence to the US committee on clinical laboratory standards and to its 2003 consensus, presented as a revised and simplified order for vacuum tubes or syringe and needle. The CDC disinfection guideline, the FDA device classification and the OSHA standard are real documents in the same study material, but none of them sets tube order.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with diabetes has a pulse that is very hard to locate in one leg. What may this suggest?
opciones: A blockage in the artery, which the provider may follow up with a Doppler study
Dehydration, which empties the vessel and flattens the wave that reaches the leg
A bounding circulation, which spreads the wave and makes any single beat harder to feel
An irregular rhythm, in which the beats are too widely spaced for the fingers to catch
preguntas.explicacion: A pulse that is hard to find can mean the artery is blocked, and such blockage is common where there is diabetes, or arteries hardened by high cholesterol. The provider may order a Doppler study to look. A fast pulse is what suggests infection or dehydration, and a bounding pulse that lasts is checked for its own reasons.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", section Clinical Significance; and "Phlebotomy", Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which structure lies beneath the median cubital vein and protects it, helping to prevent hematoma formation?
opciones: The bicipital aponeurosis
The medial cutaneous nerve
The brachial artery
The dorsal venous arch
preguntas.explicacion: The biceps aponeurosis shields the median cubital vein and keeps hematomas from forming, and the phlebotomy chapter describes the vein as superficial and lying over the bicipital aponeurosis of the fossa. The nerve and the artery are the structures that make the basilic vein risky, and the dorsal venous arch is in the hand.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: One draw yields a filled culture bottle and a filled citrate tube. How many mixing movements does each receive?
opciones: Eight to ten for the culture bottle and three to six for the citrate tube
Three to six for the culture bottle and eight to ten for the citrate tube
Eight to ten for both containers, since both hold an anticoagulant
Three to six for both containers, since both are drawn before serum tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Once filled, the culture bottle is mixed eight to ten times, while the citrate tube is inverted three to six times straight after the blood goes in. Vigorous shaking is avoided in both cases, since it can froth or haemolyse the sample and spoil the clotting results.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI - How to Enroll, Enrollment Information for Providers and After You Enroll
preguntas.subtema: Medicare eligibility verification · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: The clearinghouse reports that Medicare eligibility checks for one of the practice's providers are coming back rejected. What is the likeliest cause?
opciones: That provider's NPI has no active HETS EDI enrollment on file, which is now required
That provider's NPI has no active claims EDI enrollment, which is checked in its place
The clearinghouse has not linked its unique identifier to the beneficiary's Medicare number
The beneficiary's Medicare card was issued before the current numbering system took effect
preguntas.explicacion: Providers and suppliers check Medicare beneficiary eligibility through HETS, and since 11 May 2026 every National Provider Identifier submitted for eligibility verification has to have a valid HETS EDI enrollment on file. Where that enrollment is not active, the eligibility request is rejected. The electronic claims enrollment is a separate thing, verified by the contractor before it approves HETS access.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Technology support · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.2.a · CMAA 4B k55 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: What does the telehealth guidance recommend a practice do with a patient before the first virtual appointment?
opciones: Walk her through the platform, or run a brief practice appointment with her
Ask her to install the software without help, to test whether she can manage
Send her the login details only, since written instructions overwhelm most patients
Have her come to the office once so that staff can configure her own device there
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance asks for written instructions that take the patient step by step through the whole process, and it says frustration and time lost to troubleshooting both drop when a telehealth coordinator, a nurse, an administrative staff member or a community health worker walks the patient through it directly. Where it can be arranged, someone on the team should run a short practice appointment so the patient rehearses every step.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1; and Annex E
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the WHO say the sharps container must be during a blood draw?
opciones: Within arm's reach and clearly visible
Outside the room, away from the patient
On the floor beside the chair
Behind the phlebotomist, by the waste bag
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 ends its description of vacuum systems with the rule that the sharps container has to be within arm's reach and in plain sight, so that sharps can be disposed of safely; Annex E says the needle is discarded immediately and the disassembly is done close to the container. A container that is far away, out of sight or behind the operator invites the delay that leads to injuries.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, Home Care; and StatPearls, "Syncope", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 k37 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: After fainting, a patient wakes up within a minute and wants to get up and leave. What is the correct advice?
opciones: Keep them lying flat for ten to fifteen minutes at least, ideally somewhere cool and quiet
Let the person stand as soon as consciousness returns, since the episode is over
Seat the person upright at once and offer a hot drink to raise the blood pressure
Keep the person lying down for at least an hour before allowing any movement
preguntas.explicacion: Keep the person flat for ten to fifteen minutes at least, ideally in a cool, quiet space, and, if lying down is impossible, to sit the person forward with the head between the knees. Patients should likewise be kept horizontal after the event and prevented from standing up too soon. No source calls for an hour on the floor.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 2.4 Care and Maintenance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F7 k152 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: How are the lead wires cared for as part of the routine?
opciones: The plug at the end of each wire is rubbed with alcohol and gauze
The plug at the end of each wire is soaked in a disinfectant
The whole patient cable is wiped with a mild detergent solution
The clip connectors are swapped for a fresh set at each visit
preguntas.explicacion: Tarnish on the metal plug at the end of a lead wire spoils the connection, so each plug is rubbed clean with alcohol and gauze. The mild detergent solution is for the examination table, which is wiped with it at the start of each session and covered with fresh paper between patients.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Who Decides Which Aid or Service Is Needed? and Use of Accompanying Adults or Children as Interpreters
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 7A k214 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient arrives without warning and asks for an interpreter. What may the clinic require under the ADA rules?
opciones: Reasonable advance notice, though walk-in requests are honored where possible
Two working days of written notice for any auxiliary aid or service at all
That the patient book a later appointment, since no notice at all was given
That the patient pay the interpreter fee whenever notice was not given
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may ask for reasonable notice in advance when someone requests an aid or a service, gauged by how long it takes to arrange one, but it may not impose excessive notice requirements, and a walk-in request is honored so far as that is possible. Responsibility for effective communication sits directly on the entity, which cannot make the patient bring an interpreter.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, sections What is fasting for a blood test, and How long do I have to fast; MedlinePlus, How to Prepare for a Lab Test, section How do I prepare for a lab test
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a fasting lipid panel and mentions having chewed sugar-free gum and smoked a cigarette that morning, but eaten nothing. Does the fast hold?
opciones: No: while fasting for a blood test the patient should also not chew gum, smoke or exercise, so the provider is told
Yes: only food and caloric drinks break a fast; sugar-free gum and tobacco are permitted before a lipid panel
Yes, provided the gum and the cigarette were more than two hours before the draw and the patient drank plain water
No: smoking breaks the fast but chewing gum does not, so only the cigarette needs to be reported to the provider
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting for a blood test means taking nothing by mouth but plain water in the hours before the draw, usually 8 to 12 of them, and the patient is also asked to leave off gum, tobacco and exercise while the fast runs. Where the instructions were not followed to the letter the patient says so to the provider or to the laboratory professional, because even a small deviation can move the result and the test may have to be booked again.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.3 Erythrocytes, Hemoglobin; and MedlinePlus, Hematocrit Test, What do the results mean?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1 · PBT I.B.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who moved to a high-altitude city three months ago now has a hematocrit above the sea-level reference range. Which mechanism explains it?
opciones: Kidney cells sensed low oxygen and secreted EPO, raising red cell output
The liver secreted thrombopoietin, raising platelet and red cell output
The spleen released its stored third of the platelets and red cells
Reticulocytes were held in the marrow, so more mature cells circulated
preguntas.explicacion: Interstitial fibroblasts in the kidney secrete erythropoietin when oxygen is low, which steps up erythrocyte production until oxygen delivery is restored; people living at high elevations therefore keep a higher hematocrit than those at sea level, and altitude is a recognized cause of a high hematocrit. Thrombopoietin drives platelets, and the spleen stores platelets, not the answer here.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Throat swab culture (003746), How the Test is Performed; and CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Combined Nasal and Throat Swab
preguntas.subtema: Throat swab technique · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.C.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.iii · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: How is a throat swab culture collected?
opciones: The head is tilted back, the mouth held wide open, and the swab rubbed at the back of the throat near the tonsils
The head is tilted forward, the tongue depressed, and the swab rolled along the inner surface of both cheeks
The head is tilted back, the mouth held wide open, and the swab rubbed over the tongue and under it
The head is tilted back 70 degrees and the swab passed through a nostril until it reaches the throat
preguntas.explicacion: The patient tilts the head back and opens wide while the sterile swab is rubbed along the back of the throat near the tonsils, and the provider may scrape several times to raise the chance of catching the organism. Gagging is expected and the patient has to resist closing the mouth. The tongue is deliberately avoided, the cheek is where a buccal swab goes, and the nostril route is the nasopharyngeal swab.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: A regular strip has 15 small squares between two R waves. What is the rate?
opciones: 100 per minute, from 1500 divided by the small squares
75 per minute, from 1500 divided by the small squares
100 per minute, from 300 divided by the small squares
20 per minute, from 300 divided by the small squares
preguntas.explicacion: The finer grid gives the same answer: divide 1500 by how many small squares lie between one R wave and the next. Fifteen of them come to 100 beats a minute, which is also three large squares, and 300 divided by three gives the same answer.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Hospitals eTool, Laboratory: Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders, Hazard; OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Ergonomic Hazards
preguntas.subtema: Ergonomic risk factors · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G · CMA I.B.9 / 2027 I.B.8 · NCMA 2A.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which ergonomic risk factors does OSHA identify for laboratory employees?
opciones: Static postures, repetition, forceful exertion, awkward postures and contact stress
Noise, ionizing radiation, chemical vapors and aerosols from biological specimens
Long shifts, night work, understaffing and fatigue from emergency procedures
Latex exposure, glove powder, hand lotions and frequent handwashing
preguntas.explicacion: The risk factors named are static posture from sitting or standing a long while, repetition when samples are sorted or the computer is used, exertion of force, postures that take a joint out of neutral, and contact stress; back pain, tendonitis, tenosynovitis and carpal tunnel syndrome are the disorders that follow. Pipetting, microscope work and keyboarding are the typical tasks. Noise and radiation are separate physical hazards and latex is an allergy hazard, each with its own OSHA guidance.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: In-network coinsurance; and Glossary: Out-of-network coinsurance
preguntas.subtema: In-network and out-of-network coverage · CMAA 4 k61 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A plan lists in-network coinsurance of 20% and out-of-network coinsurance of 40%. What does that tell the patient?
opciones: Her share of the allowed amount doubles when she uses a provider without a contract
Her share of the allowed amount doubles once she has used up the plan's yearly limit
The provider without a contract is paid twice as much by the plan for the same service
The provider without a contract must accept the plan's allowed amount as full payment
preguntas.explicacion: In-network coinsurance is the percentage owed when the provider has a contract with the plan, and it is normally lower than the out-of-network percentage; here the patient's share rises from a fifth to two fifths of the allowed amount. The figures describe what the patient owes, not extra payment to the provider, and a provider without a contract has agreed to nothing, which is why balance billing shows up outside the network.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Hand Hygiene in Clinical Practice", Handwashing Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.B.5.a (2027 I.B.4.a) · RMA III.A.3.a(i) · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: How long should routine handwashing with soap and water last, and how much soap is used?
opciones: At least 15 to 20 seconds of friction, with about 3 to 5 mL of soap
At least 15 to 20 seconds of friction, with about 10 to 15 mL of soap
At least 5 to 10 seconds of friction, with about 3 to 5 mL of soap
At least 60 seconds of friction, with about 3 to 5 mL of soap
preguntas.explicacion: Roughly 3 to 5 mL of soap is spread into a lather and worked with vigorous friction for a minimum of 15 to 20 seconds over palms, backs of the hands, wrists, the spaces between the fingers, fingertips, thumbs, cuticles and under the nails. Hands stay below the elbows so water runs from the less contaminated area toward the more contaminated one.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, NIDDK: Diabetes Diet, Eating, & Physical Activity — Carb counting
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k26 diabetes · CMA I.A.6.g(3)(b) · 2027 I.A.6.g(3)(b) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which patients with diabetes most need to count carbohydrates rather than only use the plate method?
opciones: Those who take insulin, since the count guides the insulin dose
Those who take insulin, since carbohydrate must be kept under 50 grams
Those with a recent diagnosis, for their first three months only
Those who are also managing high blood pressure at the same time
preguntas.explicacion: Carb counting means planning and tracking the carbohydrate in every meal and snack. Not everyone with diabetes needs it, but for a patient on insulin it is what shows how much insulin to take. Someone not using insulin can often work with the plate method and skip the counting altogether.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Helping patients prepare for their telehealth appointment
preguntas.subtema: Setting up the picture · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how to sit for her video appointment so the clinician can see her properly. What does the setup guidance tell her?
opciones: Plenty of light in front, camera steady at eye level, head and shoulders in the frame
Plenty of light behind her, camera steady at chest level, the whole room in the frame
Plenty of light in front, camera held in the hand, and the face filling the whole frame
Plenty of light behind her, camera steady at eye level, head and shoulders in the frame
preguntas.explicacion: The patient is told to choose a spot with plenty of light and to avoid sitting with her back to a window, which makes her face harder to see. The camera should be steady, at eye level, and framed so that head and shoulders are in view. She is also asked to find a quiet place and to close other applications so they do not slow the connection or distract her.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, Chapter 2.2: Subjective Versus Objective Data
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 k44 · RMA III.F.1.a · NCMA 2B.4
preguntas.pregunta: A confused patient's daughter supplies most of the history. What must the record show?
opciones: That the information came from someone other than the patient, and from whom
Only what the patient answered for himself, leaving the daughter's account out of it
The daughter's account as objective data, since she observed him at home
The daughter's account with no source, since it is now part of the record
preguntas.explicacion: The patient is the primary source of subjective data; charts, family members and other team members are secondary sources. When the history comes from a care partner, where it came from is documented. Care partners are worth including rather than excluding: with altered mental status, the caretaker is often the only route to the relevant history.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: How is the radial pulse located at the wrist?
opciones: Two fingers are laid on the underside of the wrist, below the base of the thumb
Two fingers are laid on the underside of the wrist, below the base of the little finger
The thumb is laid over the front of the wrist, in line with the middle finger tendon
Two fingers are laid on the back of the wrist, between the two prominent tendons
preguntas.explicacion: The index and middle fingers go on the palm side of the wrist, just below the base of the thumb, and press with the pads flat until the beat comes up. The vessel runs on the thumb side of the anterior wrist, just above the base of the thumb, so a hand placed on the little-finger side or on the back of the wrist finds nothing.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(2)(iv), Hepatitis B Vaccination, and Appendix A
preguntas.subtema: Hepatitis B vaccine declination · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: An employee with occupational exposure refuses the hepatitis B vaccine. Which document does the standard require?
opciones: The declination statement in Appendix A of the standard, signed by the employee
A written opinion from the evaluating healthcare professional, kept for 15 days
An entry in the sharps injury log noting the department and the employee's reason
A note in the training record, retained three years, that the vaccine was explained
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(2)(iv) requires the employer to make sure that anyone who turns down the vaccine signs the statement printed in Appendix A. The other documents exist in the standard but serve other purposes: the written opinion of (f)(5) follows a vaccination or an exposure evaluation; the sharps injury log of (h)(5) records injuries from contaminated sharps that pierce the skin; and the training record of (h)(2) lists dates, content, trainer and attendees. None of them documents a refusal.

preguntas.fuente: eCFR, 21 CFR 862.1675(a), Blood specimen collection device
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 k54 k57 · D1 1B k25 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which items fall inside the regulatory definition of a blood specimen collection device?
opciones: Tubes, vials, whole systems, serum separators, trays and vacuum tubes
Collection tubes and vacuum tubes only, since trays hold no specimen at all
Serum separators and centrifuges, since both act on the separated serum
Needles, lancets and tourniquets, since all three touch the patient's skin
preguntas.explicacion: The definition covers devices meant to collect and handle blood specimens, and to part the serum from the cellular components before testing, and the generic type is written broadly enough to take in tubes, vials, whole systems, serum separators, collection trays and vacuum sample tubes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Reasons for Termination
preguntas.subtema: What follows a dismissal · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A committee asks what becomes of patients after a practice dismisses them. What did the review of 536 terminations find?
opciones: Of those who re-established care in the same network, only a quarter were seen within six months
Of those who re-established care in the same network, three quarters were seen within one month
Of those who re-established care in the same network, nearly all were seen within six months
Of those who re-established care in the same network, only a quarter were seen within two years
preguntas.explicacion: Of the patients who left and later re-established care inside that same network, only a quarter, 25%, obtained a primary care appointment in the six months that followed, which the authors raise as a possible discontinuity of care. The same study found race, age and employment status to be independent predictors of who ends up dismissed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Organ Systems Involved
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k55 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.1.a · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which pair of vital signs is expected to rise together with a fever?
opciones: Heart rate and respiratory rate, because the febrile state raises oxygen demand
Heart rate and blood pressure, because the vessels constrict to conserve body heat
Respiratory rate and oxygen saturation, because ventilation clears the extra heat
Blood pressure and oxygen saturation, because cardiac output rises with the fever
preguntas.explicacion: Producing a fever is expensive: a rise of one degree Celsius takes 10% to 12.5% more metabolic work. Oxygen demand climbs, and heart rate and respiratory rate climb with it. That is why a fast pulse in a febrile patient is expected rather than surprising, and why a fast pulse may also signal infection or dehydration.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D3) · PBT I.B.2 · CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A blood gas report shows a pH of 7.40. Where does this fall relative to the normal range for blood?
opciones: Right at the average; normal is 7.35 to 7.45
Slightly acidic; normal is 7.45 to 7.55
At the low end; normal runs 7.40 to 7.50
Slightly alkaline; normal is 7.0, like pure water
preguntas.explicacion: Blood pH averages about 7.4, with a healthy range of 7.35 to 7.45, so a reading of 7.40 sits in the middle of normal. Blood is somewhat more alkaline than pure water, whose pH is 7.0, and it carries many buffers that keep the value steady. A range starting at 7.45 or 7.40 would wrongly turn a normal reading into a low one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Premature Ventricular Complex", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: What defines a premature ventricular complex on the tracing?
opciones: An early QRS over 120 ms, usually with no P wave before it
An early QRS under 120 ms, usually with no P wave before it
An early QRS over 120 ms, always with a P wave before it
A late QRS over 120 ms, usually with two P waves before it
preguntas.explicacion: The beat arises in the ventricles, so it comes early, its shape is abnormal and it lasts longer than 120 ms. A large T wave of the opposite polarity typically follows it, and no P wave precedes it, because the impulse did not travel down from the atria.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 482.13(e)(8), (e)(9) and (e)(12), Standard: Restraint or seclusion
preguntas.subtema: Restraint time limits · CPT D1 k14 · CCMA 7A k215 · CMA II.E.1.d · RMA I.C.1.e · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: For violent or self-destructive behavior, how long may a single restraint order last for an adult before it must be renewed?
opciones: 4 hours for adults 18 and older
2 hours for adults 18 and older
1 hour for adults 18 and older
8 hours for adults 18 and older
preguntas.explicacion: Unless state law is stricter, an order aimed at violent or self-destructive behavior may be renewed only within these limits, to a total of 24 hours: 4 hours for adults 18 or older, 2 hours for children and adolescents from 9 to 17, and 1 hour for children under 9. Past 24 hours a physician or other authorized practitioner has to see and assess the patient before a new order, and the patient is seen face to face within 1 hour of the intervention starting. Restraint for non-violent patients may be renewed as hospital policy allows.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS): Surveillance Case Definitions for Current and Historical Conditions
preguntas.subtema: Communicable disease reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.a / 2027 E.5.a · NCMA 4.10
preguntas.pregunta: Which conditions have to be reported by a practice?
opciones: The ones on that state's list, which is not the same in every state
The ones on a single national list that applies in the same way everywhere
The ones the practice's laboratory contract names in its service agreement
The ones the accrediting body includes in its yearly safety goals
preguntas.explicacion: Which conditions are reportable varies from state to state. What harmonizes them is a recommendation from the council of the state and territorial epidemiologists, which proposes which diseases state health departments should report on to the national surveillance system, and the case definitions behind that list are updated every year so cases are counted the same way across jurisdictions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Clinical Significance: Temperature
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature b(ii) · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Where is an oral thermometer probe placed so that the reading is most reliable?
opciones: In the posterior sublingual pocket, with the lips closed around the instrument
In the buccal space between the cheek and the lower molars, with lips parted
On the middle of the tongue, held down by the patient with gentle pressure
Under the tip of the tongue, kept away from the frenulum and the lower teeth
preguntas.explicacion: The mouth is the most widely used site, but only one spot in it is dependable: the pocket under the back of the tongue, with the lips shut around the probe. Readings taken elsewhere in the mouth drift, and the patient must not have smoked or taken hot or cold food or drink shortly before the measurement.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", What healthcare information is protected; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Introduction and Definition of PHI
preguntas.subtema: What counts as PHI · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: What makes a laboratory result protected health information under HIPAA?
opciones: Any identifier tying the result to one patient: name, phone number or email
Only the patient's Social Security number or medical record number, not the name
Only the result itself, regardless of whether a name is attached
Only electronic storage; a printed result with a name attached is not PHI under the rule
preguntas.explicacion: Health information turns into protected health information once it carries an identifier tying it to one particular patient: a name, a telephone or email address, a street address, a Social Security number. The Privacy Rule lists 18 such elements, and information about relatives, employers or the people who share a patient's household is covered as well. PHI may be written, spoken, on paper or electronic, of any size, inside the facility or outside it. Strip every identifier under the de-identification standard and what is left is no longer PHI.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Exclusion: Reinstatement
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: OIG turns down an excluded provider's application for reinstatement. When may she apply again?
opciones: After a year, which is the wait a refusal opens up
After five years, the floor for a mandatory exclusion
After sixty days, the deadline that runs on overpayments
At any moment, since a refusal sets no waiting time
preguntas.explicacion: Reinstatement is not automatic when the exclusion period ends: the excluded party has to apply and receive written notice from OIG granting it. Where OIG denies the application, the party may re-apply after one year. The five-year figure is the minimum length of a mandatory exclusion, not a waiting time after a refusal.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Other Issues: Criminal violations; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Criminal Violation of HIPAA Rules
preguntas.subtema: Criminal penalties · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: Which HIPAA violation carries a criminal penalty of up to $100,000 and up to 5 years in prison?
opciones: Obtaining or disclosing identifiable health information under false pretenses
Knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable health information
Selling identifiable health information for gain or to cause malicious harm
Failing to correct a violation due to willful neglect within the required period
preguntas.explicacion: The criminal side has three tiers. Knowingly obtaining identifiable health information, or disclosing it, reaches $50,000 and 1 year. Doing so under false pretenses reaches $100,000 and 5 years. Doing so while intending to sell, transfer or use the information for commercial advantage, for personal gain, or to do malicious harm reaches $250,000 and 10 years. These cases belong to the Department of Justice, and they can land on nurses, secretaries, telephone operators and other employees, not only on institutions. Willful neglect left uncorrected is the highest civil tier, not a criminal one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A febrile patient in early septic shock has pulses that feel unusually strong and full. How does that fit the picture?
opciones: Distributive shock can give bounding pulses early, from widened vessels
Bounding pulses rule shock out, since every form of shock weakens them
Bounding pulses with fever come from fluid moving out into the tissues
Bounding pulses point to hypovolemia, where vessels clamp down early
preguntas.explicacion: Pulse quality helps separate the kinds of shock. Hypovolemic shock gives weak or absent peripheral pulses, because there is little volume and the vessels constrict to compensate. Distributive shock, of which septic shock is the example, may give bounding pulses early on from peripheral vasodilation, so a full pulse does not rule the diagnosis out.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Grey (closing paragraph on mixing)
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A purple EDTA tube arrives in the laboratory with several small clots inside. Which collection error is associated with this finding?
opciones: The tube was not mixed enough after it was filled
The tube was inverted too many times in the figure-of-8 pattern
The tube was filled after the gray fluoride tube
The tube was drawn through a butterfly without a discard
preguntas.explicacion: Tubes with anticoagulants need adequate mixing, for instance by inverting them in a figure-of-8 pattern, and inefficient mixing can leave small clots. Overmixing is the other extreme and leads to hemolysis, not clots. Drawing out of order risks additive carry-over, and the butterfly discard concerns air in the tubing, not clotting.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation; and MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, What is fasting for a blood test?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 k128 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient ran a half marathon yesterday and is booked for a draw this morning. Which instruction was missed?
opciones: Outpatients should avoid heavy physical activity in the 24 hours before
Outpatients should avoid heavy physical activity in the hour before
Outpatients should rest lying down for 15 minutes before the first tube
Outpatients should avoid heavy physical activity for the whole week
preguntas.explicacion: An outpatient is to be kept away from heavy exercise in the 24 hours before the blood is drawn, and exercise is one of the things ruled out during a fast. Exercising hard before a test also appears among the common factors that spoil accuracy. Fifteen minutes is the rule for holding a seated posture, not for exercise.
