preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.3
preguntas.subtema: Warm-site activation · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: An unplanned outage has lasted an hour and a half with no end in sight. What does the downtime policy ideally say about the backup site?
opciones: The warm-site process should be started before two hours of unavailability pass
The warm-site process should be started once eight hours of records pile up
The warm-site process waits until the vendor confirms the outage is unplanned
The warm-site process is reserved for outages announced ahead of time by IT
preguntas.explicacion: The policy is expected to say when the warm-site backup process gets activated, and the guidance puts that trigger ideally before two hours of unplanned unavailability have gone by. The eight hours elsewhere in the same guide belong to a different practice: the stock of paper forms each care area keeps.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Non-Financial Eligibility
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient meets her state's Medicaid income limit but has just moved in from another state. Which non-financial rule applies to her?
opciones: She must be a resident of the state whose Medicaid program is paying for her care
She must have lived in the state for a full year before an application is accepted
She must apply first in the state she came from and ask for the file to be moved
She must be enrolled in a Marketplace plan while the new application is decided
preguntas.explicacion: Alongside the financial rules, Medicaid applicants have to satisfy non-financial criteria: a beneficiary must generally live in the state whose program covers her, and must be a citizen of the United States or a qualified non-citizen of certain kinds, a lawful permanent resident for example. Some eligibility groups narrow further by age, or by pregnancy or parenting status.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Code Sets Overview
preguntas.subtema: Code sets · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · CMA III.G.1 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which code sets did HIPAA adopt for use in standard health care transactions?
opciones: ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT, dental procedure codes and national drug codes
ICD-10 and CPT only, since the other sets are used inside each practice
ICD-10, HCPCS and the place of service codes each contractor publishes
ICD-10, HCPCS and the adjustment reason codes payers use on remittances
preguntas.explicacion: The code sets named in the HIPAA regulations classify diagnoses, procedures, tests, treatments, equipment and supplies, and they are ICD-10, HCPCS, CPT, the code on dental procedures, and the national drug codes. Place of service codes identify where care happened, and adjustment reason codes explain payment decisions; neither is a medical data code set.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Reduction and Prevention", Function: Medical Error
preguntas.subtema: Incident reporting · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is transferred without the gurney being stabilized first. What kind of error is that?
opciones: An error of omission, an adverse event caused by an action not taken
An error of commission, an adverse event caused by a direct action
A latent error, since the equipment itself was never checked properly
A never event, since a fall from a gurney should be impossible anyway
preguntas.explicacion: Medical errors split into omission and commission. Errors of omission cause harm through something not done — not strapping a patient into a wheelchair, not stabilizing a gurney before a transfer — while errors of commission follow from a direct act by a team member. The term never event is reserved for errors that should never happen at all, such as wrong-site surgery or pressure ulcers.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Issues of Concern: Relevant Definitions
preguntas.subtema: Competency vs capacity · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A coworker says a patient with dementia "is not competent to sign." What is accurate about that word?
opciones: Competence is a legal finding a judge makes; the bedside call is capacity
Competence is the bedside finding; capacity is what a court declares later
Competence and capacity are one finding, made by any licensed staff member
Competence is presumed lost once a dementia diagnosis appears in the chart
preguntas.explicacion: Competence is about being able to take part in legal proceedings. It is presumed, and disproving it takes a hearing with evidence before a judge; clinicians never make that call. What the clinical team assesses is capacity: whether this patient can make this decision, now, in this situation. A dementia diagnosis does not by itself remove capacity.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Vacuum-tube systems and Manually retractable evacuated tube systems
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 k55 3D · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A vacuum-tube system is being used on a small child. What adjustment does the WHO device table call for, and why?
opciones: A smaller tube with reduced vacuum (1 to 5 ml), to reduce hemolysis
A larger tube with full vacuum, so the sample is collected before the vein collapses
A butterfly set with a discard tube, to remove the air from the tubing
A 16 to 18 G needle, so the tube fills before the tourniquet limit is reached
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 says that with vacuum systems a smaller tube whose vacuum is lower is what a pediatric patient gets, and for retractable evacuated systems specifies a 1 to 5 ml tube with lower vacuum to reduce hemolysis. The discard tube is the butterfly rule for air in the tubing, and 16 to 18 G is the blood donation gauge in Table 3.1, far too large for a child.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, BMI Frequently Asked Questions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A 7-year-old girl's body mass index is at the 88th percentile for her age and sex. How is that read?
opciones: Overweight: the band runs from the 85th to below the 95th percentile
Obesity: the band starts once the 85th percentile has been reached
Healthy weight: the band runs from the 5th to below the 95th percentile
Overweight: the band runs from the 75th to below the 90th percentile
preguntas.explicacion: Children from 2 through 19 are compared with others of the same age and sex rather than with fixed adult numbers. A percentile of 88 means the value equals or exceeds that of 88% of the reference group, and the overweight band runs from the 85th to below the 95th. Obesity starts at the 95th percentile.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Recommendations: Selecting and Evaluating Needle Devices with Safety Features
preguntas.subtema: Evaluating a new device · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Before a hospital adopts a new safety needle across its draw stations, what must the product evaluation show?
opciones: That the feature works reliably, staff accept it, and patient care does not suffer
That the device costs no more than the one it replaces over a full year
That the manufacturer has registered and listed it with the federal agency
That the injury rate has already fallen in the department that will use it
preguntas.explicacion: Three points settle whether a device with a safety feature is adopted: does the feature work reliably and effectively, will the worker who has to use it accept it, and does patient care come to no harm. The recommended process adds training in the new device, clear written criteria, on-site follow-up for informal feedback, and monitoring after implementation. Registration and listing are what the manufacturer owes the device regulator, not what the evaluation measures.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.1 Eligibility Criteria
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F1 k150 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.1 2D.2
preguntas.pregunta: Is a resting tracing recorded on a patient with cognitive impairment?
opciones: Yes: nobody is automatically excluded from the test
No: the patient cannot follow the instructions given
Yes, but only if a relative holds the arms still for it
No, unless a provider stays in the room during the run
preguntas.explicacion: The eligibility rules say plainly that there are no automatic exclusions and that patients with cognitive impairment should have the recording done. What is asked of every patient still applies: relax, breathe normally and stay still without talking.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Thrombocytopenia" (2025), sections Continuing Education Activity and Introduction; and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.4 Leukocytes and Platelets, Platelets
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's platelet count is 155,000 per microliter. Below what count would this be called thrombocytopenia, and where is about a third of the body's platelets kept?
opciones: Below 150,000 per µL; about one third is stored in the spleen
Below 150,000 per µL; about one third is stored in the liver
Below 100,000 per µL; about one third is stored in the spleen
Below 50,000 per µL; about one third stays in the red marrow
preguntas.explicacion: In adults the line for thrombocytopenia is drawn at a count under 150,000 per microliter, so 155,000 sits just above it; mild cases run from 100,000 up to that line, moderate from 50,000 to 100,000, and severe below 50,000. Once platelets reach the circulation, roughly a third of them move to the spleen, which keeps them until a vessel tears. The liver and the red marrow are not that store.

preguntas.subtema: Compound authorizations · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice wants one signed form to release both a patient's psychotherapy notes and the rest of her chart. What does the compound authorization rule allow?
opciones: Nothing of the sort: notes of that kind travel only with an authorization of their own
One form, as long as the two kinds of record are listed under separate headings
One form, as long as the patient initials the psychotherapy section separately
One form, as long as neither release is a condition of her continuing treatment
preguntas.explicacion: An authorization may not be combined with another document to make a compound authorization except in the cases the rule sets out. One of them is narrow: an authorization for psychotherapy notes may be combined only with another authorization for psychotherapy notes. Research permissions are the other main exception.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, sections Can I drink anything besides water, and What if I make a mistake
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient scheduled for a fasting glucose says he skipped breakfast but had a coffee with sugar an hour ago. What should the phlebotomist do?
opciones: He has broken the fast; tell the provider, since the test may need rescheduling
Coffee does not count as food, so the draw may proceed as a fasting sample
Proceed and mark the sample 'non-fasting' only if he also ate solid food
Wait one more hour so the sugar clears, then draw it as a fasting sample
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting means no food or drink except plain water; juice, coffee, soda and other beverages get into the bloodstream and affect results, and a patient who eats or drinks before the test should tell the provider because the test may have to be rescheduled. A fasting glucose needs at least 8 hours without caloric intake, not one more hour.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Why might a clinician palpate a peripheral pulse and listen to the heart at the same moment?
opciones: To see whether every ventricular contraction produces a beat that can be felt
To confirm that the stethoscope and the palpating fingers agree on the rhythm term
To measure the delay between the heart sound and the wave arriving at the wrist
To decide which of the two sides of the body carries the stronger pulse volume
preguntas.explicacion: Doing both at once answers a specific question: does each contraction of the ventricle reach the periphery as a palpable beat? Contractions that do not produce a felt beat will be missed by counting at the wrist alone, which is why the two are compared when the finding is in doubt.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, footnote c
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k9 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A chemistry panel gives results the clinician cannot explain, and the tube was set down without being inverted. What does the table warn about?
opciones: Blood not thoroughly mixed with its additive can give erroneous results
Blood not mixed with its additive loses the vacuum it was drawn under
Blood left unmixed separates into serum before it reaches the laboratory
Blood left unmixed cools too quickly and the additive stops working at all
preguntas.explicacion: The footnote to the order-of-draw table asks for additive tubes to be inverted gently and warns that erroneous results may follow if blood and additive are not properly combined. The movement described elsewhere is a figure-of-8, and it is done as soon as the tube comes off the needle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Issues of Concern (recapping and disposal); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 3.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Sharps disposal · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: The sharps container in a drawing station is full to the top, so a phlebotomist sets the used needle on the tray to dispose of it later. Which risks are being ignored?
opciones: Injuries happen when sharps containers are overfilled and when used needles are not placed in them immediately
The needle should have been recapped with two hands and left on the tray until a container was available
The needle should have gone into the regulated-waste bag, since bags are acceptable whenever containers are full
There is no added risk once the safety feature is activated, so the delay is acceptable
preguntas.explicacion: Used needles go straight into an approved sharps container kept close to the point of use; injuries also happen when a needle ends up in an ordinary waste bag, or when a container is filled past the line or handled badly. Recapping as a routine is no longer advised, because handling a used needle is what raises the risk of a puncture, and the WHO requires the container to be within arm's reach and clearly visible.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anthropometric Measurement", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.b · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A child arrives with one leg in a cast and the parent asks for the usual growth measurements. What does the technique call for?
opciones: The numbers taken now may mislead, so they are not forced in this state
The numbers are taken anyway and the weight of the cast subtracted later
The numbers are contraindicated in any child with a limb deformity
The numbers are taken and plotted on a chart drawn for injured children
preguntas.explicacion: Body measurements are noninvasive and carry no true contraindication, but there are states in which the figure will not mean what it appears to mean: acute illness, a limb deformity, a cast. A height or a weight taken then can be falsely reassuring or falsely alarming, so the measurement is better postponed than plotted.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7: Fill the laboratory sample tubes
preguntas.subtema: Collection methods · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.F II.J · CCMA 3E7 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Several tubes are needed from one venipuncture. Which system does the WHO's Step 7 say to use, and what if it is not available?
opciones: Vacuum tubes with a needle and a tube holder; failing that, a syringe or a winged set
A syringe, because it lets the phlebotomist control the pressure; otherwise evacuated tubes
A winged needle set attached to a syringe; otherwise a hypodermic needle and syringe
Evacuated tubes only; if they are not available the draw is postponed
preguntas.explicacion: Step 7 says that when several tubes are needed, vacuum tubes with a needle and a tube holder are used because the tubes fill directly, and that a syringe or winged needle set is the alternative when that system is unavailable. Chapter 3 gives the reasons: closed vacuum systems reduce direct exposure to blood and make multiple samples from one puncture easier.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Asthma", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.C.6.h(5) (2027 I.C.6.g(5)) · RMA I.A.2.a · CMAA 1 k10 · NCMA 1.10
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has intermittent cough, wheezing and shortness of breath that come and go with allergens and colds. Which test confirms the suspected diagnosis?
opciones: Spirometry showing variable expiratory airflow obstruction
Spirometry showing a fixed and irreversible airflow obstruction
A chest radiograph showing a lobar area of consolidation
A sputum culture growing a typical respiratory pathogen
preguntas.explicacion: Cough, wheezing and shortness of breath are the hallmark symptoms of asthma, but on their own they are too nonspecific, so the diagnosis needs the symptoms to fit and spirometry to document expiratory airflow obstruction that varies. Obstruction that does not vary points toward COPD, and consolidation or a positive culture toward pneumonia.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Sprains", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.o · 2027 I.B.8.o · RMA III.H.1.b III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.13 EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: How is ice applied to a freshly sprained ankle?
opciones: Wrapped in cloth, never placed straight onto the skin, with the joint raised
Placed straight onto the skin so that the cold reaches the joint faster
Alternated with a hot pack every few minutes to keep the tissue warm
Held under an elastic wrap tight enough to stop the swelling completely
preguntas.explicacion: Ice goes on right away to hold down swelling, always wrapped in cloth and never directly against the skin. The area is then wrapped firmly but not tightly to limit movement, and the swollen joint is kept raised above the level of the heart, even during sleep, with the joint rested for several days.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E10 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A serum specimen for a serology test will be examined later the same day, once the afternoon run is set up. Where does the published guidance have it kept in the meantime?
opciones: In the refrigerator at 2 to 8 °C, the condition given for serum awaiting prompt serological testing
In the freezer at −20 °C or lower, the condition given for delayed transport or long-term storage
At room temperature on the bench, since the blood has to clot before it can be processed at all
On wet ice in a transport cooler, the condition given for a bronchoalveolar lavage in transit
preguntas.explicacion: Blood for serology is allowed to clot before processing, and in transit it is protected from extremes of temperature. Serum that will be examined promptly is held at 2 to 8 °C until it is tested. Freezing at −20 °C or lower is the instruction for long-term storage or delayed transport, which is a different situation from a specimen due to run in a few hours.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: guardian
preguntas.subtema: Legal guardianship · CCMA k218 · CMA E.3.c · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: What obligation does a court-appointed guardian owe the ward?
opciones: A fiduciary duty to act in the ward's best interests, not to follow their wishes
A fiduciary duty to follow the ward's stated wishes on every personal decision
A duty to consult the ward's relatives before any medical decision is taken
A duty to seek court approval before consenting to any routine medical care
preguntas.explicacion: A guardian is a legal representative a court appoints for someone who cannot care for themselves, and the person they act for is the ward. They owe a fiduciary duty to act in the ward's best interests, and they have no duty to respect the ward's wishes. They control finances, property and care, and they need court authorization for large or extraordinary expenditures.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.2
preguntas.subtema: Quality assurance · CPT D3 k9 · D1 1E k28 · D2 2C k42 · PBT VI.A.1 · CCMA 3E7 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: How should the reasons for taking a blood sample be recorded in a service?
opciones: Set out in a written protocol, or in instructions kept on file
Agreed verbally between the phlebotomist and the ordering clinician
Written on the tube label at the moment the specimen is collected
Left to the judgment of whoever is drawing blood on that shift
preguntas.explicacion: The guidance asks that the indications for blood sampling be set out clearly, either in a written protocol or in written instructions such as a laboratory form. Written standard operating procedures for each step also appear among the elements of quality assurance.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 1
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A k54 k57 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which containers does the equipment list accept for collecting the blood itself?
opciones: Glass or plastic tubes with rubber caps, vacuum tubes, or screw-capped glass
Vacuum tubes only, since caps of any other kind cannot hold a vacuum
Glass tubes with screw caps only, because plastic reacts with additives
Plastic tubes with rubber caps only, since glass may break in transport
preguntas.explicacion: Blood may go into sterile tubes of glass or plastic with rubber caps, into vacuum-extraction tubes, or into glass tubes with screw caps, and which of them is used depends on what has been agreed with the laboratory. Large volumes call instead for a sterile glass or collapsible pack.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Worker Rights and Protections
preguntas.subtema: Reportable violations · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: A worker is transferred to a worse shift a week after complaining to OSHA. What can she do, and by when?
opciones: A whistleblower complaint to OSHA, filed within 30 days of the retaliation
A whistleblower complaint to OSHA, filed within 30 days of the original hazard
A whistleblower complaint to OSHA, filed within 180 days of the retaliation
A grievance with the employer, which OSHA then reviews on appeal
preguntas.explicacion: An employer may not lawfully fire a worker, demote her, transfer her or retaliate in any other way because she complained to the agency. A worker who believes that has happened may lodge a whistleblower complaint inside 30 days of the retaliation: the clock runs from the retaliation itself, not from the hazard that prompted the original complaint, which can be reported confidentially.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Standard Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Standard precautions · CPT D1 1J k11 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C1 k100 · CMA I.B.4 / 2027 I.B.3 · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which practices make up standard precautions, the framework applied at every patient encounter?
opciones: Hand hygiene, protective equipment, cough etiquette, placement and safe sharps
Isolation rooms, contact tracing, daily temperature checks and visitor logs
Sterile gloves, sterile fields, surgical scrub and sterile drapes for each draw
Testing every patient on admission and treating those who test positive
preguntas.explicacion: Standard precautions are the baseline for every encounter, before anything is known about the patient: hand hygiene whether or not gloves were worn, both before and after contact with a patient or with body fluids; appropriate protective equipment, including gown, gloves and eye protection where fluid exposure is possible; respiratory and cough etiquette; patient placement that takes single rooms and routes of transmission into account; and safe handling of needles and instruments.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Therapeutic drug levels (003430), How to Prepare for the Test; MedlinePlus, Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, Will I need to do anything to prepare for the test?
preguntas.subtema: Drug level preparation · CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.D patient preparation · CCMA 3E k139 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions
preguntas.pregunta: A patient due for a drug level asks whether to skip the morning dose so the result comes out low. What is the right answer?
opciones: No: doses are not stopped or changed without talking to the provider first
Yes: the dose is always held on the morning of a therapeutic drug level
Yes, if the level is a trough, since a trough must be drawn off therapy
No, but the dose may be delayed two hours without a new order
preguntas.explicacion: Patients must not stop or change their medicines before a drug level without speaking to the provider; the provider is the one who says whether the times of any doses need to change. Depending on the drug, the test is scheduled before or after the regular dose, which is exactly why an unannounced skipped dose ruins the result. A trough is drawn on therapy, just before the next dose.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 1.3
preguntas.subtema: Downtime recovery · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: The system comes back after a six-hour outage. What does the contingency guidance expect next?
opciones: A process that gets what was written on paper entered and reconciled into the record
A fresh risk analysis of the whole practice before any user logs back into the system
A breach report to the Secretary describing the outage and the paper forms used
Destruction of the paper forms, so that two versions of the visit never coexist
preguntas.explicacion: Along with stocking the paper forms, the guidance calls for a process that gets whatever was written on paper while the system was down keyed into the EHR and reconciled once it is back: orders entered as coded data, for instance, and documents scanned where their contents are not typed in some other way. Training and testing staff on downtime and recovery are separate practices.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 3.2 The Cytoplasm and Cellular Organelles, The Endoplasmic Reticulum
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k35 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which organelle is the site where the cell builds its proteins?
opciones: The ribosome, which reads messenger RNA to assemble a protein
The lysosome, which reads messenger RNA to assemble a protein
The peroxisome, which reads messenger RNA to assemble a protein
The centrosome, which reads messenger RNA to assemble a protein
preguntas.explicacion: A ribosome is the organelle where proteins are made: two ribosomal RNA subunits wrap around messenger RNA and translation begins. Ribosomes stud the rough endoplasmic reticulum, which is what makes it look bumpy. Lysosomes and peroxisomes are enzyme-filled sacs that break things down rather than build them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Patients with Impaired Decision-Making Capacity; and StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Issues of Concern, Psychiatric Patients
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: An inpatient carries a schizophrenia diagnosis and is being asked to agree to a draw. What follows?
opciones: The diagnosis by itself does not remove the right to give informed consent
A surrogate signs for any patient who carries a psychiatric diagnosis
Consent is waived, because the admission paperwork already covers draws
The nearest relative decides once a psychiatric diagnosis is on the record
preguntas.explicacion: Neither cognitive impairment, nor mental illness, nor a severe medical condition strips away by itself the right to give informed consent, so long as the person can understand, weigh and communicate a decision. Research shows that carrying a diagnosis such as schizophrenia does not preclude capacity, so each patient gets a full assessment.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Nitroglycerin Sublingual: How should this medicine be used?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B5 k69 · CMA I.D.2.c(3) · RMA III.G.4.d(v) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how to take a sublingual nitroglycerin tablet when an angina attack begins. What do you tell them?
opciones: Sit down, put it under the tongue and let it dissolve; do not chew, crush or swallow it
Sit down, chew the tablet well and swallow it with water so that it starts working faster
Lie down, crush the tablet between the teeth and hold the powder against the inner cheek
Sit down and swallow the tablet whole, then take a second one after ten minutes have passed
preguntas.explicacion: The instruction is to sit down and take one dose as the attack starts. The tablet goes under the tongue, or between cheek and gum, and is left to dissolve; it is never chewed, crushed or swallowed. Burning or tingling is normal and says nothing about whether it is working. If the pain does not ease, emergency help is called, and further doses come five minutes apart when the prescriber has ordered them.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, the RACE rule; StatPearls, "OSHA Fire Safety", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: RACE · CPT D1 1A 1L k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 · CMAA 3A k45
preguntas.pregunta: Smoke starts pouring from a centrifuge in the processing room while two patients sit in the waiting area. Under the RACE sequence, what is the first action?
opciones: Rescue or remove everyone in immediate danger
Activate the alarm system and call the operator
Confine the fire by closing the doors
Extinguish it with the nearest CO2 unit
preguntas.explicacion: RACE orders the response to a fire: R, rescue or remove all occupants from danger; A, activate the alarm system; C, confine the fire by closing doors; E, evacuate or extinguish. In healthcare the first step matters most because patients may be unable to move on their own. Extinguishing comes last and only for a fire that can be handled with a portable unit; the PASS rule, pull, aim, squeeze, sweep, governs how the extinguisher is used once that point is reached.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)", Recognition and Initial Management of Cardiac Arrest
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: Two staff members are running a resuscitation in the office. How often should they trade the compressor role?
opciones: Every 2 minutes, or sooner if the one compressing gets tired
Every 10 minutes, or when the monitor shows a shockable rhythm
Every 30 seconds, after each set of 30 compressions and 2 breaths
Only when the defibrillator announces that everyone must stand clear
preguntas.explicacion: Compressors rotate every 2 minutes, or earlier if fatigue sets in, because tired hands lose rate and depth. Two minutes is also about five cycles of 30 compressions and 2 breaths. Rotation is one of the quality items of a high-performance team, along with proper depth, full recoil and avoiding excessive ventilation.

preguntas.subtema: Sharing information · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.4.c(1) · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A prosecutor subpoenas a patient's substance use disorder records for a case against that patient. What is needed?
opciones: A court order, and the subpoena as well, before anything is released
The subpoena on its own, since a court has already signed the document
The program director's approval, recorded in the disclosure log
Written notice to the patient, after which the records may be sent
preguntas.explicacion: Records, or testimony relaying what they contain, may not be used against the patient in proceedings, whether civil or criminal, administrative or legislative, without specific written consent or a court order. That order only comes once notice has been given and a chance to be heard allowed, and it has to arrive with a subpoena, or a similar legal mandate that compels disclosure, before anything is released.

preguntas.subtema: Release of records · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Under the medical record condition of participation, when may an original medical record leave the hospital?
opciones: Only in accordance with Federal or State law, a court order or a subpoena
Whenever another treating facility asks for it to continue the patient's care
Whenever the patient signs the practice release form at the records window
Whenever the medical record service keeps a photocopy of the file it releases
preguntas.explicacion: The confidentiality standard asks for a procedure that keeps records confidential, lets information or copies go out only to individuals who are authorized, and puts the facility under a duty to stop unauthorized people reaching or altering them. Releasing the original record is tighter still: it happens only where Federal or State law, a court order or a subpoena calls for it.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Form and Format
preguntas.subtema: Form and format · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose record is kept in the EHR asks for an electronic copy. What does the Privacy Rule require?
opciones: An electronic copy in the form asked for if readily producible, or an agreed readable format
A paper printout, since hard copy is always an acceptable substitute for an electronic request
New software purchased by the practice so that every requested file format can be produced
An electronic copy only when the patient accepts the security risk of unencrypted transfer
preguntas.explicacion: Where PHI is kept electronically and the individual asks for electronic access, the entity must provide it in the requested form and format if readily producible, and otherwise in an agreed alternative readable electronic format. No entity has to buy new software for every possible request, but each must be able to produce some electronic copy. Only if the individual turns down every electronic format offered may the request be satisfied with a readable hard copy.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (equipment compatibility); and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex C, Table C.1
preguntas.subtema: Equipment selection · CPT D3 3A 3B k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic buys needles from one company, tube holders from another and tubes from a third. What is the guidance on mixing brands like that?
opciones: Needle, holder and tubes should come from the same manufacturer, since mixing brands can cause problems in use
Mixing brands is acceptable as long as every component is within its expiration date and sterile
Only the needle and the holder must match; the tubes are interchangeable across manufacturers
Mixing brands is acceptable for adults but not for pediatric tubes with reduced vacuum
preguntas.explicacion: Needle, tube holder and tubes are chosen from the same manufacturer to ensure compatibility; otherwise the volume aspirated, the gel stability and the additives can be affected. The WHO device table lists parts from different makers mixed together as a disadvantage of vacuum systems that can create a problem during use. Neither text limits the rule to adults or to two of the three parts.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Ready? Set? Test! (2024), Appendix B, Temperature Log Instructions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic stores some test kits and patient samples on an open shelf rather than in the refrigerator. Which range is typically kept for a room used for testing and storage?
opciones: 15 to 30 °C, that is 59 to 86 °F
2 to 8 °C, that is 36 to 46 °F
18 to 22 °C, that is 64 to 72 °F
10 to 25 °C, that is 50 to 77 °F
preguntas.explicacion: Rooms used for testing and for storing reagents, kits, controls and patient samples are typically held between 15 and 30 °C, or 59 to 86 °F. The colder band, 2 to 8 °C, belongs to the refrigerator and −25 to −15 °C to the freezer. Whatever the room reads, the manufacturer's instructions decide which condition a given product may be stored in.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy, Chambers and Circulation through the Heart; Layers; Left Ventricle
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which chamber pumps blood into the systemic circuit, and why is its wall so much thicker than its counterpart's?
opciones: The left ventricle; it must overcome the high resistance of the long systemic circuit
The right ventricle; it must push blood through the dense capillary beds of both lungs
The left atrium; it receives oxygen-rich blood from all four of the pulmonary veins
The right atrium; it receives blood from both venae cavae and from the coronary sinus
preguntas.explicacion: The ventricles are the primary pumping chambers, and the left ventricle is the major pump for the systemic circuit, ejecting blood into the aorta. Although both ventricles move the same volume per beat, the left wall is much thicker because it must generate far more pressure to overcome the resistance of the long systemic circuit; the pulmonary circuit is shorter and offers less resistance.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A code carries a code also note. What does that instruct the coder to do?
opciones: Report two codes if needed, letting the circumstances of the encounter set the order
Report two codes, with the underlying condition sequenced first in every case
Report a secondary code if it is known, after the code that carries the note
Report only one of the two codes, since they are independent of one another
preguntas.explicacion: A code also note says two codes may be needed to describe a condition fully, but it gives no direction on sequencing, so which comes first turns on the circumstances of the encounter. That is what separates it from a code first note, which puts the underlying condition first, and from a use additional code note, which adds a secondary code where it is known.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k82 k83 · CMA I.B.8.b · 2027 I.B.7.b · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: An unresponsive patient is not breathing and an opioid overdose is suspected. How does naloxone fit into the response?
opciones: It is given if available, without letting it interrupt the CPR going on
It is given first, and compressions wait until the patient responds
It is given only after the ambulance crew has taken over the airway
It is given instead of rescue breaths while compressions continue
preguntas.explicacion: When opioid poisoning is suspected in a patient who is not breathing, naloxone is given if it is at hand, and it must not interfere with the CPR already under way. In a patient who still has a pulse but is breathing abnormally, rescue breathing runs at 1 breath every 6 seconds and naloxone follows the protocol in force, with the pulse rechecked.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A faint during a blood draw is usually vasovagal. Which other forms of reflex syncope are described alongside it?
opciones: Situational syncope, such as cough or micturition, and the carotid sinus form
Cardiac arrhythmia and orthostatic syncope, such as rising from a lying position
Hypoglycaemic syncope and febrile syncope, such as a faint during an infection
Carotid sinus syncope and cardiac syncope, such as a faint from a heart block
preguntas.explicacion: Reflex syncope covers episodes in which the control of blood pressure fails and brain perfusion drops. The vasovagal form is the commonest of them, and the other members of the group are situational syncope and the carotid sinus form, the kind brought on by coughing or passing urine.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Conventional devices
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: For which two situations is a needle and syringe listed as the easier choice?
opciones: Small or difficult veins, and arterial sampling with a heparinized syringe
Small or difficult veins, and drawing many tubes from one single puncture
Prominent forearm veins, and arterial sampling with a heparinized syringe
Prominent forearm veins, and drawing many tubes from one single puncture
preguntas.explicacion: For a patient with small or difficult veins, drawing with a syringe can be easier than with an evacuated tube system, and a heparinized syringe can also be used for arterial blood. Collecting large or multiple samples is where the syringe is described as difficult, not where it shines.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Petechiae", section Introduction; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bleeding into the skin
preguntas.subtema: Terminology: petechiae and purpura · CPT D3 3L k68 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A non-blanching spot at the puncture site measures about four millimeters. What is it called?
opciones: Purpura, because it is larger than two millimeters
Petechia, because it is smaller than ten millimeters
Erythema, because it sits over an inflamed puncture
Ecchymosis, because it is smaller than ten millimeters
preguntas.explicacion: The dividing line is two millimeters: a non-blanching spot below that size is a petechia and one above it is purpura. A very large bruised area of bleeding under the skin is called an ecchymosis, and redness that fades under pressure is erythema, not bleeding at all.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(d), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k92 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E14 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A reference laboratory accepts specimens from outside clinics. What must it make available to those clients according to CLIA?
opciones: Written instructions on patient preparation, collection, labeling, storage, transport, processing and acceptability
A copy of its CLIA certificate and the qualifications of its laboratory director and testing personnel
A monthly report of the number and condition of specimens rejected from each client's collection site
A price list for each test together with the turnaround time expected from receipt to final report
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1242(d) obliges a laboratory that takes referral work to keep written instructions available to its clients covering, as applicable, the same ground its own policies must cover: how the patient is prepared, how the specimen is collected and labeled, how it is stored, preserved and transported, how it is processed, and when it is accepted or rejected. Certificates, rejection statistics and price lists are not in the standard.

preguntas.fuente: ISMP, List of Error-Prone Abbreviations, Symbols, and Dose Designations (2024), Dose Designations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k10 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k8 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A dose is written as 1.0 mg on a paper order. Which error does that invite, and how should it be written?
opciones: It can be read as 10 mg, so a whole number carries no trailing zero
It can be read as 0.1 mg, so a whole number carries no trailing zero
It can be read as 100 mg, so a whole number carries a leading zero
It can be read as 1 mL, so the unit is changed from mg to mL
preguntas.explicacion: A zero written after the decimal point disappears if the point itself is not seen, and 1.0 mg becomes 10 mg, ten times the dose. Whole-number doses are therefore written without that trailing zero. The mirror-image rule covers doses under one unit: they always get a leading zero, so .5 mg is written 0.5 mg.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(3)(iv), application to laboratories
preguntas.subtema: A laboratory that ships · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital laboratory ships a hazardous chemical to another employer. How does the Hazard Communication standard treat it then?
opciones: As a manufacturer or distributor: it must label and send the sheet
As a laboratory still: only the incoming label rules apply to it
As a transporter: only the shipping name and number are needed
As an exempt employer, since the chemical is used in patient care
preguntas.explicacion: The reduced set of duties for laboratories has a limit. Where a laboratory employer ships hazardous chemicals, the rule counts it as a manufacturer of chemicals or as a distributor, so containers leaving the laboratory carry the label paragraph (f) requires of shipped containers, and a safety data sheet goes to distributors and to other employers. Inside the laboratory the short list applies; on the way out, the full labeling rules do.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k9 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.b) · RMA I.B.3.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks why a PPD was placed in the skin of the forearm. What is that test looking for?
opciones: Tuberculosis, which that skin test screens for
Prostate disease, which the PSA test screens for
Inflammation, which the CRP test screens for
Thyroid disease, which the TSH test screens for
preguntas.explicacion: PPD stands for purified protein derivative, and it is placed as a skin test for tuberculosis, which the abbreviation TB names. The other three are blood tests on the same list: PSA for prostate disease, CRP for inflammation or heart problems, and TSH for thyroid disease. All three are real abbreviations, but none of them is a test placed in the skin.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3.1 Recording the ECG
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 3F7 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.7 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: While the machine is acquiring data, the display shows a bad-lead message. What happens next?
opciones: The faulty lead is corrected and the unit acquires the data again
The recording is allowed to finish and the lead is fixed afterwards
The unit leaves that lead blank and prints the other eleven of them
The unit stops working until the biomedical engineer resets the error
preguntas.explicacion: A bad-lead message in the lower corner of the display is not something to record through: the faulty lead has to be put right, and once it is, the machine goes back and acquires the data by itself. Only a display free of error messages lets the run continue.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Winged steel needles (butterfly)
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 k55 k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A 3-year-old with small, difficult veins needs one tube of blood. Which device does the WHO device table favor, and what advantage does it list?
opciones: A winged (butterfly) needle, which allows better precision than a hypodermic or evacuated tube needle
A vacuum-tube system, which eliminates blood transfer and allows numerous samples from a single puncture
An auto-disable syringe, which prevents reuse and reduces the risk of needle-sticks
A 21 G straight needle with a syringe, which is the most common means of blood sampling
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 describes winged steel needles as good for drawing blood from pediatric patients or from patients with small or difficult veins, allowing better precision than a hypodermic or evacuated tube needle, at higher cost and with the air-in-the-tubing caveat. Auto-disable syringes are explicitly not recommended for phlebotomy, and Table 3.1 gives no 21 G option for children.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 3N k9 k59 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: An ESR specimen that was poorly mixed reaches the laboratory with a clot in it. How does the clot affect the reading?
opciones: It disrupts the stacking of red cells and lowers the value obtained
It disrupts the stacking of red cells and raises the value obtained
It leaves the value unchanged, since only the plasma column is read
It raises the value, in the same way that a tilted tube raises it
preguntas.explicacion: Clotted blood breaks up the rouleaux, the coin-like stacks of red cells whose settling is being measured, so the value comes out lower than the patient's true one. The faults that raise the value are physical ones: a tilted tube, vibration, warmth and an inadequate fill.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Grandfathered health plan
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about a grandfathered health plan is correct?
opciones: It is an individual policy bought on or before March 23, 2010, with fewer protections
It is an individual policy bought on or before March 23, 2010, sold by the Marketplace
It is a job-based policy that keeps its status even after benefits are cut sharply
It is a policy that must disclose the ten categories of benefits it leaves uncovered
preguntas.explicacion: A grandfathered plan is an individual policy bought on 23 March 2010 or earlier, sold by an insurer, an agent or a broker rather than through the Marketplace, and it may lack some of the rights the health care law added. The status can be lost when significant changes cut benefits or push costs up. What a plan must disclose is whether it regards itself as grandfathered.

preguntas.subtema: Workstation defined · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.a · CMAA 7A k97 · NCMA 3.4
preguntas.pregunta: Under the Security Rule's own definitions, what does the word workstation take in?
opciones: A laptop, a desktop or a device doing the same work, plus the media beside it
Only the desktop computers the practice owns and keeps inside its own building
Any device that holds records, the telephone system and the fax machine included
The whole room in which a computer that reaches the records has been installed
preguntas.explicacion: Workstation is defined as an electronic computing device, such as a laptop or a desktop, or any other device performing similar functions, together with the electronic media in its immediate environment. That is why a laptop taken home falls under workstation security and not only under device and media controls.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Complications
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K 3L k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Bright red blood pulses back into the hub during an attempted venous access. What is done?
opciones: The device is removed at once and direct pressure applied
The device is advanced further until the flow settles down
The device is left in place and the tourniquet reapplied
The device is withdrawn slightly and the tubes are filled
preguntas.explicacion: An artery entered by accident calls for prompt removal of the line and direct pressure over the site to control the bleeding. Arterial injury sits among the local complications of this kind of procedure, alongside nerve injury, hematoma, bleeding and simple failure of the attempt.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · RMA III.E.3 Temperature c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient insists there is a fever because the forehead feels warm to the hand. How reliable is that judgment?
opciones: Unreliable: judging fever by touch is wrong in up to 40% of people, so a reading is taken
Reliable in adults but not in children, whose skin loses heat faster to the room air
Reliable when the hand is placed on the neck instead, where the skin is better perfused
Unreliable only when the room is cold, which chills the skin and hides a real fever
preguntas.explicacion: Deciding whether someone is febrile by feeling the skin is inaccurate in as many as 40% of people, in either direction. When fever is suspected, an instrument reading is obtained and documented with the route used. The patient's own baseline matters too: some people habitually run warmer or cooler than the average.

preguntas.subtema: Reports to authorities · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA II.E.6 · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k37
preguntas.pregunta: Which disclosure may be made to a public authority without the patient's authorization?
opciones: A report of a communicable disease or of suspected child abuse, as authorized by law
A report of the patient's employer and insurance details for a workplace injury claim
A report of the patient's diagnosis to a school for enrollment, beyond proof of immunization
A report of psychotherapy notes to a family member concerned about the patient
preguntas.explicacion: Public health disclosures in 164.512(b) include reporting disease and injury to a public health authority and reporting child abuse or neglect to an authority authorized to receive it; disclosures to a school are limited to proof of immunization required by law, with the parent's or adult's documented agreement. Disclosures to an employer are confined to workplace medical surveillance and work-related illness findings with written notice to the worker. Psychotherapy notes need an authorization in almost every case, and a concerned relative is not a public authority.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: Where does muscle tremor on a tracing come from, and when does it appear?
opciones: From the arm and leg muscles, when the patient is tense or cold
From the chest muscles, when the patient breathes too deeply
From the arm and leg muscles, when the electrodes have dried
From the heart muscle itself, when the rate climbs above 100
preguntas.explicacion: Tremor is a signal thrown off by the patient's own arm and leg muscles. It shows up when the person is tense, cold, or affected by a muscle or nerve disorder, which is why calming and warming the patient is the first thing tried when the baseline is fuzzy rather than wandering.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Adult Immunization Schedule by Age: Influenza
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4C immunizations · CMA I.A.5 · 2027 I.A.5 · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: How often does the adult immunization schedule call for influenza vaccine?
opciones: One dose annually for adults
One dose every two years
One dose every five years
Two doses annually for adults
preguntas.explicacion: Influenza vaccine is given as a single dose each year for adults, with certain formulations preferred in older adults. The schedule is organized by age and then by medical condition, which is why a transplant recipient or a pregnant patient may see a different row for the same vaccine.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026, Section I.B.10
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is seen for the contracture left by a burn she suffered twelve years ago. What do the guidelines say about coding it?
opciones: There is no time limit, and the acute burn code is not used now
There is a limit of seven years on coding a residual effect
The acute burn is coded first and the residual one after it
Only the acute burn is coded, since it caused the problem
preguntas.explicacion: A sequela is what an illness or an injury leaves behind once its acute phase is over, and no time limit governs the use of a sequela code: the residual may show up early or years later. Two codes are normally needed, the residual condition first and the sequela code second, and the code for the acute phase is never used with them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Power of Attorney", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Durable power of attorney · CCMA k218 · CMA E.8.c / 2027 E.7.b · RMA I.C.1.f · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: What does the word "durable" add to a power of attorney for health care?
opciones: It keeps the agent's authority alive after the person loses capacity
It keeps the agent's authority alive after the person has died
It lets the agent decide about the finances as well as the medical care
It lets the agent be replaced by a backup without a new document
preguntas.explicacion: The durable proviso is what protects the appointment if the person loses the functional capacity to decide for themselves, which is exactly the moment the document is needed, so the form is usually headed as a durable power of attorney covering health care. A synonym is health care proxy. Naming a backup agent is a separate choice made when the document is written.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Blood Plasma; and 18.5 Hemostasis, Fibrinolysis; and MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia 003423 Venipuncture, Why the Test is Performed
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5 k87) · PBT I.B.3 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A red-top tube is left to clot and then centrifuged. What is the fluid above the clot called, and how does it differ from plasma?
opciones: Serum; it is plasma from which the clotting factors have been removed
Plasma; it still contains fibrinogen and the other clotting factors
Buffy coat; the pale layer of leukocytes and platelets above the cells
Whole blood; the formed elements are suspended in the fluid again
preguntas.explicacion: Serum is plasma after the clotting factors have been removed: in a clotted tube it is the fluid squeezed out of the clot as it retracts. Plasma is the fluid part of circulating blood, still carrying fibrinogen and the other factors; serum is what remains liquid after the blood clots in a tube. The buffy coat is the layer of white cells and platelets in a spun, unclotted sample, and whole blood has all the formed elements suspended.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Utilize standardized notification procedures
preguntas.subtema: Termination letter · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.3.f · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which element belongs in the letter that ends a clinician-patient relationship?
opciones: The date care ends, and an offer to send the records on once the patient authorizes it
The reason for the dismissal, set out plainly so that the patient is able to dispute it
The names of three colleagues who have already agreed to take the patient on
A statement of the balance owed, since unpaid accounts are a lawful ground to dismiss
preguntas.explicacion: The letter states the date the relationship ends, confirms that care and medication refills run until that date, steers the patient toward emergency help such as a local crisis center, and offers to forward the record to the next clinician the moment a signed release comes back, with the release form in the envelope. Giving a reason is usually not obligatory, and authors are split on whether to name particular colleagues.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Please sit down and make yourself comfortable; and StatPearls, "Vancomycin" (NBK459263)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K 2L k46 k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k125 · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: Besides fainting and allergies, which time-bound question does the WHO pre-draw interview include?
opciones: Whether anything has been eaten or drunk in the last two hours
Whether the patient has fasted for the past twelve hours or more
Whether the patient took any medicine in the past 24 hours
Whether the patient exercised hard in the past 30 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: Annex C asks whether the patient has had blood taken before, is scared of needles, is allergic to anything, has ever fainted while blood was being drawn, whether anything has been eaten or drunk in the last two hours, and how they feel at that moment. Twelve hours is the fasting recommendation for morning sampling, 24 hours the alcohol window, and 30 minutes the vancomycin trough window.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 3186, Model Exposure Control Plan, Procedures for Evaluating the Circumstances Surrounding an Exposure Incident; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Reviewing an exposure incident · CPT D1 1H 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic reviews a needlestick that happened while a phlebotomist recapped a butterfly needle. Which findings does that review put on record?
opciones: The engineering controls in use, the device brand, the PPE worn and the employee's training
The anti-HBs level of the employee and the hepatitis B status of the source patient
The dates of the last two annual sessions and the names of everyone who attended
The disinfectant used on the surface and the schedule for cleaning that work area
preguntas.explicacion: The written plan has to contain a procedure for looking into the circumstances of every exposure incident, and the model plan spells out what that review determines: which engineering controls were in use, which work practices were followed, the type and brand of the device, the protective clothing worn, where it happened, what procedure was under way, and what training the employee had. Serology results belong to the confidential medical evaluation, not to this review, and training dates and attendance are the separate training record.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Reducing visit demand · CMAA 4A k52 · CCMA 5C k171 · CMA III.H.1.c · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: Part of making open access work is cutting the demand for one-to-one visits. Which measures does the improvement guide name for that?
opciones: Dropping visits kept alive by outdated protocols, running group visits, and using phone and e-mail
Dropping visits kept alive by outdated protocols, running group visits, and charging for same-day slots
Shortening every appointment, opening an evening clinic, and using phone and e-mail for some concerns
Dropping visits kept alive by outdated protocols, hiring locum cover, and stretching follow-up intervals
preguntas.explicacion: Three tactics are named. Some visits survive only because an old clinical protocol demands them, such as routine follow-up for a urinary tract infection or an annual Pap smear, and those sources are identified and addressed. Group visits handle patients who share a chronic condition. And the telephone and e-mail settle concerns that do not need a visit at all.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 7: Investigations of Violations
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: An internal investigation into a compliance report is under way at a practice. What does the OIG guidance ask it to keep?
opciones: A record built as it goes: the allegation, the steps, the outcome
A summary written up once the investigation has been closed
A copy of the report alone, until any discipline is decided
A log of the witnesses only, kept by the compliance officer
preguntas.explicacion: Whatever the size or the gravity of the matter, the investigation is recorded as it happens: the alleged violation, a description of how it was investigated, interview notes and key documents, a log of witnesses and documents reviewed, the result, and any discipline or corrective action that followed. Evidence has to be preserved as well.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Line Placement", section Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes · CPT D3 k55 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A supply list gives the size of some catheters in gauge and of others in French. What does the French figure describe?
opciones: Three times the outer diameter in millimeters
One third of the outer diameter in millimeters
Three times the inner diameter in millimeters
One third of the usable length in millimeters
preguntas.explicacion: French sizing takes the outer diameter of the catheter in millimeters and multiplies it by three, so a device measuring six millimeters across is an 18F. It is kept for larger devices and specialized catheters: peripheral lines are not sized that way but by gauge, where the lower number is the wider device and the range stocked runs from fourteen to twenty-six.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Physical Examination Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with obesity has a pulse that cannot be found with light fingertip pressure. What is the next step at the bedside?
opciones: Palpate more deeply or reposition the limb, since a light touch can miss a pulse
Press as hard as possible, because heavy pressure brings a deep pulse to the surface
Record the pulse as absent, because a pulse that light pressure misses is not present
Move to the opposite limb, because a pulse missed on one side is always felt on the other
preguntas.explicacion: Pressure has to be judged: too much flattens a weak pulse and too little misses a subtle one. Where there is obesity or edema, deeper palpation or moving the limb may be what finds it. When no pulse can be felt at all, Doppler ultrasound is the noninvasive tool used next rather than a chart entry of absent.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Patient Abandonment, Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Abandonment and scheduling · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.4.d(2) · RMA I.C.1.c · CMAA 4F k60 · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A scheduling error leaves a patient without the coverage her clinician had arranged. How is that treated?
opciones: As inadvertent abandonment, for which the provider may be liable in damages
As a breach of unsecured PHI that triggers individual notice to the patient
As an information blocking practice, since care was interfered with electronically
As a minimum necessary failure, since the schedule reached the wrong people
preguntas.explicacion: Abandonment means ending the relationship one-sidedly, without notice enough for the patient to line up substitute care, and it counts as a breach of duty. It comes in two forms: intentional, such as refusing to see someone who has not paid, and inadvertent, for which the examples given are a misunderstanding about call coverage and negligence arising from errors in the scheduling system. When that happens, damages may fall on the provider who was covering as well as on the primary one.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, HETS EDI - How to Enroll, Enrollment Information for Vendors & Clearinghouses
preguntas.subtema: Who enrols for eligibility checks · CMAA 4C k58 · CCMA 5 k181 · CMA III.G.3 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: A vendor offers to complete the practice's HETS enrollment on its behalf so that nobody at the office has to deal with it. What does CMS say?
opciones: The provider itself must acknowledge the rules of behavior and name its relationship with the vendor
The vendor may enroll the provider once it holds a signed trading partner agreement on file
The provider must enroll separately with each contractor whose jurisdiction it bills into
The vendor may enroll the provider, but only for the jurisdiction where the practice sits
preguntas.explicacion: Vendors and clearinghouses are asked to support enrollment, encouraging providers to enroll and sharing their unique identifier, but they are told not to enroll providers themselves. It is the provider who has to read the HETS Rules of Behavior, acknowledge them, and state what its relationship with the vendor is. Enrolling once with a single contractor is enough; there is no need to repeat it with each one.

preguntas.fuente: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2020-2025, Guideline 4: Limits
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: What daily saturated fat limit do the 2020-2025 Dietary Guidelines set for people age 2 and older?
opciones: Under 10 percent of the day's calories
Under 10 grams for the whole day
Under 20 percent of the day's calories
Under 30 percent of the day's calories
preguntas.explicacion: Saturated fat gets the same ceiling as added sugars: below a tenth of the calories eaten that day, starting at age 2. The limit is written as a share of calories, not as a fixed weight, so it moves with the person's calorie needs. The label's own Daily Value for saturated fat is 20 grams on a 2,000-calorie diet.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), At a glance
preguntas.subtema: Two tiers of precautions · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How do Transmission-Based Precautions relate to Standard Precautions, according to the CDC?
opciones: A second tier added to Standard Precautions for patients with certain known or suspected infections
A replacement for Standard Precautions once a pathogen has been confirmed by the laboratory
The first tier, applied to every patient until an infection has been ruled out
A set that covers bloodborne pathogens only, while Standard Precautions cover respiratory ones
preguntas.explicacion: Transmission-Based Precautions form the second tier of basic infection control: they are layered on top of Standard Precautions whenever a patient may carry, or be colonized by, an agent that calls for extra measures. They never take the first tier's place, and what triggers them is a known or suspected infection rather than a blanket rule for everyone. Contact, Droplet and Airborne are the three categories, chosen by the route of transmission; bloodborne exposure is handled by Standard Precautions and by the OSHA standard.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions: CLIA certificate (1)-(5); 42 CFR 493.15(c)
preguntas.subtema: CLIA certificates · CPT D1 1B k25 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · RMA III.C.1 · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic performs only fingerstick glucose and other tests on the CLIA waived list. Which CLIA certificate does it need?
opciones: A certificate of waiver from CMS
A certificate of compliance
A certificate of accreditation
A certificate for PPM procedures
preguntas.explicacion: A certificate of waiver is issued to a laboratory that restricts itself to the waived tests listed in 42 CFR 493.15(c) and no others. A certificate of compliance follows an inspection finding compliance with all condition-level requirements; a certificate of accreditation rests on accreditation by an organization approved by CMS; and a certificate for PPM procedures covers a physician, a dentist or a midlevel practitioner doing only provider-performed microscopy plus, if desired, waived tests. A registration certificate lets an entity do moderate or high complexity testing until surveyed.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Breach Notification Rule: Notice to the Secretary
preguntas.subtema: Notice to the Secretary · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3E k34 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: A breach affects 40 patients. When must the Secretary be notified?
opciones: Annually, within 60 days of the close of the calendar year in which it was discovered
Straight away, and in any event within 60 days of discovering the breach
Annually, within 90 days of the close of the calendar year in which it was discovered
Only if the affected patients ask the practice in writing to make the report
preguntas.explicacion: Notice to the Secretary travels through a breach report form filed electronically on the HHS site. When 500 or more individuals are affected the report goes in straight away and in any event within 60 days of the breach. Where fewer than 500 are affected the practice may report annually, and those reports fall due within 60 days of the close of the calendar year in which the breaches were discovered.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A dark green sodium heparin tube and a light green PST are both ordered. Which comes first in the WHO sequence?
opciones: The dark green sodium heparin tube, then the light green PST
The light green PST, then the dark green sodium heparin tube
Either one, because both contain heparin and share position 6
The light green PST, because gel tubes precede plain heparin tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 lists the dark green sodium heparin tube at position 6 and the light green plasma separator tube, with lithium heparin and a gel separator, at position 7. They are two separate rows, not a shared position, and the gel tube comes after the plain heparin tube. Footnote d confirms that the PST, if used, is drawn in the position shown.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 570: E-mail with patients
preguntas.subtema: E-mail with patients · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 7H k97 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: May a practice discuss treatment with a patient by ordinary e-mail?
opciones: Yes, provided the practice applies reasonable safeguards when it does so
No, unencrypted e-mail is forbidden for messages that touch on treatment
Yes, but only after the patient signs an authorization for each message
No, unless the practice first files a security incident report with the Secretary
preguntas.explicacion: The Privacy Rule lets covered providers communicate electronically with patients so long as reasonable safeguards go with it. The precautions given as examples are verifying that the address is right before anything is sent, and sending an alert first to confirm it. Unencrypted e-mail is not forbidden for treatment-related messages, though other safeguards should be used, such as limiting how much the message carries.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Blood pressure measurement
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the lower edge of the cuff sit on the arm?
opciones: About 1 inch (2.5 cm) above the crease at the bend of the elbow
About 3 inches (7.6 cm) above the crease at the bend of the elbow
Directly on the crease at the elbow, so the bladder covers the artery
About 1 inch (2.5 cm) below the shoulder, over the thickest part of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: The cuff is wrapped snugly around the upper arm with its lower edge about an inch (2.5 cm) above the crease of the elbow, leaving room for the stethoscope. The arm is bare and supported so the upper arm is at heart level, and a bunched sleeve is removed rather than pushed up.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Security safeguards · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Into which three categories does the Security Rule sort the safeguards a practice must put in place?
opciones: Administrative, physical and technical
Preventive, detective and corrective controls
Required, addressable and optional measures
Confidentiality, integrity and availability
preguntas.explicacion: Regulated entities have to put in place safeguards that are reasonable and appropriate, and the rule sorts them into three families: administrative, physical and technical, which is the skeleton of the rule itself. Confidentiality, integrity and availability are the goals those safeguards serve, not the families; required and addressable describe how each implementation specification inside a standard is designated.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 heel anatomy · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: A colleague suggests puncturing the back (posterior curve) of a newborn's heel. Why is that spot avoided?
opciones: In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is only 2.33 mm, so the lancet may hit bone
In a 3 kg baby the skin-to-bone distance there is 3.32 mm, too deep for a lancet to reach blood
The posterior heel is where the tibial artery runs closest to the skin surface
The posterior heel is the site the WHO reserves for premature neonates with a 0.85 mm lancet
