The lavender EDTA tube is the hematology tube, the green heparin tube is used for stat chemistry, and the light blue citrate tube is reserved for coagulation studies.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Influenza Specimen Collection guide (2024), Packing
preguntas.subtema: Labeling the transport tube · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.3 · CCMA 3D4 k113 · CMA I.C.8.a · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: What does the CDC say about writing the label on a viral transport tube?
opciones: Use a barcode or a permanent marker, because pencil and pen rub off or smear
Use a pencil, because permanent marker dissolves in the transport medium
Use a pen and cover the writing with clear tape so the ink cannot smear
Label the outer shipping bag instead, so that the tube itself stays easy to read
preguntas.explicacion: The label goes on the transport tube itself, written with a barcode or a permanent marker, since pencil and pen can rub off or smear in transit; the cap is then checked to be tightly sealed and the paperwork completed to state health department requirements. A frozen cold pack goes in with the specimen, and packing follows the transport regulations for biological substances.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 15.2: Drug Name; StatPearls, "Nursing Rights of Medication Administration", Right drug
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k19 · CMA 2027 I.D.1.f · RMA III.G.4.c · NCMA 1.4
preguntas.pregunta: Why is the generic name considered the safer one to write on a medication order?
opciones: It lets the pharmacist substitute among brands, and full names are written out
It is shorter than the brand name, so less of it can be misread on the order
It is the only name the pharmacy software will accept when an order is entered
It carries the strength inside the name, so the dose cannot be transcribed wrong
preguntas.explicacion: A drug may be ordered by generic or by brand name, and the generic is regarded as the safest choice because it allows the pharmacist to substitute among the various brand products. Names that look or sound alike are a real hazard, since two similar names can belong to drugs with entirely different mechanisms and uses, so writing full generic names out is the evidence-based practice recommended for prescribers.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Special Enrollment Period; and Glossary: Open Enrollment Period
preguntas.subtema: Coverage enrollment · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A caller wants to buy a Marketplace plan in March, outside the yearly enrollment window. When can she enroll?
opciones: When a qualifying life event, such as marriage or a birth, opens a special period
When she agrees to a higher premium for the months already gone by this year
When her employer confirms in writing that it offers her no coverage at all
When the yearly window reopens on November 1 and closes on December 15
preguntas.explicacion: Open enrollment for the Marketplace runs from November 1 to January 15. Outside it, a person may still sign up if a qualifying life event applies, such as getting married, having a baby, moving, or losing other coverage, and the special period usually allows 60 days before or after the event. Back premiums buy nothing, lack of a job offer is not by itself an event, and the December 15 date is not when the yearly window closes.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.1 Baseline Drift
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k149 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these produces a wandering baseline?
opciones: An electrode that was not firmly stuck to the skin
A loop left in one of the patient cable wires
A metal watch left on the patient's wrist
A machine switched on without its self test
preguntas.explicacion: The listed causes of unstable contact are poor skin preparation, failure to attach the electrode or the connector securely, patient movement, tension on the lead wires, a faulty connection between electrode and wire, and dried-out electrodes. A loop in a wire is a different artifact: it invites interference from the current in the room.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337), Preanalytical phase studies published in this issue
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5B · PBT III.A.3 · CCMA 3E10 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A physician asks to add a test to a serum sample collected the previous day and kept refrigerated. What decides whether the laboratory can honor the add-on?
opciones: Whether the analyte is documented as stable for that storage time and temperature in that tube type
Whether the request reaches the laboratory within 30 days of the original oral order for the panel
Whether the original requisition already listed the panel to which the new test belongs
Whether the tube carried a gel barrier, since only gel tubes may be retested after storage
preguntas.explicacion: Add-on acceptability rests on stability data: the study that measured common biochemical analytes in serum separator tubes under various storage conditions exists precisely to define the time and temperature within which a stored sample can be retested. The 30-day rule concerns written authorization of oral orders, the original panel does not fix what may be added, and that same study covered tubes both with and without a gel barrier, so the gel is not what settles the question.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.3 Cardiac Cycle, Heart Sounds; and SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Physiology of the Heart, Heart Sounds
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k6 (applied D3) · PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse auscultating a patient hears the 'lub' and then the 'dub'. What produces the second heart sound, S2?
opciones: The semilunar valves snapping shut as the ventricles relax
The atrioventricular valves shutting as the ventricles contract
The semilunar valves opening as the ventricles eject blood
The atria pushing blood into a stiff, hypertrophied ventricle
preguntas.explicacion: A healthy heart gives two sounds: S1, the lub, when the atrioventricular valves shut as the ventricles contract, and S2, the dub, when the semilunar valves shut as the ventricles relax. Both sounds are vibrations set off by valves closing, and abnormal ones are called murmurs. The atrial push into a stiff ventricle is S4, seldom heard and a sign the left ventricle is failing.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.520(c)(2), Specific requirements for certain covered health care providers; 164.520(c)(1)(v)(B)
preguntas.subtema: Notice of privacy practices · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient arrives at a clinic that treats patients directly. When must the clinic hand over its notice of privacy practices?
opciones: No later than the first service delivery, with a good-faith effort to obtain acknowledgment
Within 60 days of the first visit, by mail to the patient's home address
Only when the patient asks for it, since posting the notice in the office is sufficient by itself
At the first visit, and the patient must sign it before any care may be provided
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.520(c)(2) has a covered provider that treats patients directly hand over the notice no later than the day of the first service delivery, electronic service included, or as soon as practicable after an emergency; it must then try in good faith to get the patient's written acknowledgment that the notice arrived, and where that fails, document the attempt and the reason; and it must keep the notice available on site and posted prominently. The acknowledgment is sought, never made a condition of care. Sixty days is the window a health plan without a website has to distribute a materially revised notice.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 10: Stability and Reactivity
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 10 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which safety data sheet section states whether a chemical is stable in storage and which conditions could set off a hazardous reaction?
opciones: Section 10, which also names the hazardous decomposition products
Section 3, which also names the ingredients and their percentages
Section 5, which also names the extinguishing agents to be used
Section 12, which also names the effects on fish and other species
preguntas.explicacion: Section 10 has three parts: reactivity test data, chemical stability under ordinary temperature and handling conditions, and the rest, which covers whether the chemical could react or polymerize and release heat or pressure, the conditions to avoid such as static discharge, shock or vibration, the classes of materials it is incompatible with, and the hazardous decomposition products it may give off. Combustion products also appear in section 5, because a fire is where they matter.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 lancet for premature neonate · PBT II.J lancets · NCMA 2C.5 equipment by age
preguntas.pregunta: Which lancet length is made specifically for premature neonates?
opciones: 1.5 mm
2.2 mm
2.4 mm
preguntas.explicacion: Makers offer lancets from 0.85 mm, the neonatal size, up to 2.2 mm, and the 0.85 mm one is the length kept for a premature baby. Of the other figures, 1.5 mm is the finger depth between 6 months and 8 years, 2.2 mm is the longest lancet in normal adult use, and 2.4 mm is the ceiling for both the finger and the heel.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Risk Analysis and Management
preguntas.subtema: Risk analysis · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which step does the Security Rule expect a practice to take BEFORE deciding which security measures are reasonable for it?
opciones: An accurate and thorough assessment of the risks and vulnerabilities to its ePHI
An encryption project covering every workstation, laptop and portable drive it owns
A signed acknowledgment from each patient that electronic records carry some risk
A written designation of the practice as a hybrid entity with health care components
preguntas.explicacion: The administrative safeguards begin with the security management process, and its first requirement is a risk analysis: assessing, accurately and thoroughly, what could threaten the confidentiality, the integrity and the availability of the ePHI the entity holds, and how exposed it is. Everything else is built on that analysis, because the measures a practice adopts have to be the ones that bring the risks it found down to a reasonable and appropriate level.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.3 Wound Assessment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.c (2027 I.C.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.l · NCMA 2B.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which findings together point to a localized wound infection?
opciones: Erythema, induration, pain, edema, purulent exudate and odor at the wound
Erythema, pink moist granulation, mild pain and clear serous drainage at the wound
Blanching redness, cool skin, numbness and dry crusting at the edge of the wound
Scant serous drainage, itching, flat pale scar tissue and tightness across the wound
preguntas.explicacion: Localized infection shows as redness, an area of hardened tissue, pain, swelling, yellow or green purulent exudate and odor, and new signs go to the provider with a wound culture expected. Pink, moist, painless granulation that may look bumpy is the healthy picture; dark red granulation that bleeds easily is the unhealthy one and often means infection.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Directional Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: An intravenous line is documented as sitting proximal to the wrist. Where on the arm is it?
opciones: Nearer the trunk than the wrist, up toward the elbow
Farther from the trunk than the wrist, out toward the fingers
On the palm side of the wrist rather than the back of it
On the thumb side of the wrist rather than the other side
preguntas.explicacion: Proximal describes a position in a limb nearer to the point of attachment or to the trunk, and distal one farther from it: the upper arm is proximal to the forearm, and the part of the leg below the knee is distal to the thigh. Front and back are anterior and posterior, and the two side terms are medial and lateral.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix A: Word Parts and What They Mean, Good and Bad
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k11 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.a) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k9 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A nosebleed is charted as rhinorrhagia and a runny nose as rhinorrhea. Which contrast between the two endings is correct?
opciones: -rrhage is bleeding, while -rrhea is a flow or discharge
-rrhage is a suture, while -rrhea is a surgical binding
-rrhage is a bursting, while -rrhea is a narrowing or block
-rrhage is a swelling, while -rrhea is a falling or dropping
preguntas.explicacion: Both endings start the same way and are easy to swap. The pair -rrhage and -rrhagic means bleeding, while -rrhea means a flow or discharge of any kind. A third one, -rrhaphy, is a suture. Narrowing is steno-, and drooping is -ptosis, as in the eyelid that will not stay open.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(2)(vii)(N) and (g)(2)(viii), Information and Training
preguntas.subtema: Interactive training · CPT D1 1A k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.e III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic's annual bloodborne pathogens training is a video played at the workstation, with nobody available afterwards. What is missing?
opciones: The chance to ask questions of the person conducting the session, which is required
A written test at the end, which the standard says is kept for three years
A copy of the hepatitis B declination form for each attendee to sign
A separate session for each job title named in the exposure determination
preguntas.explicacion: The training program carries a minimum content list in paragraph (g)(2)(vii), and the last item on it is a chance to put questions to whoever gives the session and get answers back; (g)(2)(viii) adds that this person must know the subject as it applies to that workplace. A video with nobody around fails on both counts. The standard never asks for a written test, the declination form belongs to the vaccine under (f)(2)(iv), and a single session may cover several job classifications.

preguntas.subtema: Record service staffing · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 7A k90 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: Charts routinely take two days to reach the clinicians who ask for them. Which requirement of the medical record condition of participation is at stake?
opciones: Employing enough personnel to complete, file and retrieve records promptly
Keeping every record in its original or legally reproduced form for five years
Using an author identification system that protects the security of the entries
Releasing information from a record only to individuals authorized to have it
preguntas.explicacion: The condition opens on organization and staffing: the medical record service has to be sized to the scope and the complexity of the work, and the hospital has to employ enough personnel for records to be completed, filed and retrieved promptly. The other three duties in the same section deal with form, authorship and confidentiality, not with staffing.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Definition of PHI and HIPAA and Communication With Patients; StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Questions to Consider
preguntas.subtema: Oral disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: Two phlebotomists discuss a named patient's HIV result in a crowded elevator. Under HIPAA this conversation is which of these?
opciones: A violation: oral disclosure of identifiable health information is PHI
Permitted, since both are workforce members of the same covered entity
Permitted, since spoken information is not covered, only written or electronic
A violation only if a patient's relative happens to be in the elevator
preguntas.explicacion: PHI covers written, paper, spoken and electronic information, and the elevator conversation about an identifiable patient is the very example used to illustrate an oral violation; discussions of patient information do not belong in public places, hallways, cafeterias or shared phone lines. Being workforce members does not help, because the disclosure reaches people not involved in the patient's care and exceeds the minimum necessary. State law may add stricter rules for HIV results, and the violation does not depend on who happens to overhear.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Pre-existing condition
preguntas.subtema: Affordable Care Act protections · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the Affordable Care Act did about pre-existing conditions.
opciones: Insurers may not refuse to cover the condition or charge the patient more for it
Insurers may cover the condition after a waiting period set by each state law
Insurers may charge more for the condition only inside the Marketplace plans
Insurers must cover the condition when the patient buys a supplemental policy
preguntas.explicacion: A pre-existing condition is a health problem, such as asthma, diabetes or cancer, that the person had before the new coverage started. Under the health care law, insurance companies can neither refuse to cover treatment for it nor charge extra because of it. There is no waiting period left to serve, the protection is not limited to Marketplace plans, and it does not depend on buying anything additional.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Issues of Concern: Infection Prevention
preguntas.subtema: Signs at the door · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C2 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.3
preguntas.pregunta: What should tell a phlebotomist arriving at a patient's room which protective equipment that patient requires?
opciones: An easily visible sign posted outside the room or contact zone
The color of the wristband the patient was given at admission
The order in the chart, which names the equipment to be worn
The container by the door, whose contents indicate what to wear
preguntas.explicacion: A sign that is easy to see hangs outside the room, or outside the contact zone, and it names the protective equipment that encounter calls for; that is how a worker arriving from elsewhere gears up correctly before crossing the threshold. It fits the rest of the system, since donning is done outside the room and the precautions in force decide which items are needed: not every component is required for every patient.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug plan coverage rules: Quantity limits
preguntas.subtema: Medication authorization · CMA III.G.5.a(2) (2027 III.G.5.a(2)) · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5H k183 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A drug plan pays for only thirty tablets a month and the prescriber wants a larger dose. What is that rule, and what is the way round it?
opciones: A quantity limit, and the prescriber may ask the plan for an exception on medical grounds
Step therapy, and the patient must first try the cheaper drug that sits on the plan's list
Prior authorization, and the plan has to approve the drug before it will be covered at all
A transition fill, and the plan covers one thirty-day supply while the matter is settled
preguntas.explicacion: Plans may cap how much of a drug they cover over a period, for safety and for cost, and the example given is thirty tablets a month. The patient or the prescriber may contact the plan for an exception where the prescriber believes the limit is not medically appropriate for her condition, for instance because she needs a higher dose.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule
preguntas.subtema: Who must comply · CCMA 5F · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 4C k63 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice makes a medical office a creditor for purposes of the Red Flags Rule?
opciones: Regularly reporting delinquent patient balances to a credit reporting company
Regularly deferring payment for services or billing patients afterwards
Regularly accepting payment cards at the front desk for the balance due
Regularly submitting claims to a health plan on the patient's behalf
preguntas.explicacion: The test has two steps, and only the second one decides. Billing patients afterwards answers the first step yes, but the guidance answers the professional who bills at the end of the month plainly: deferring payment on its own is not enough. The second step asks whether the office regularly uses consumer reports in a credit transaction, gives information to credit reporting companies, or advances funds to be repaid; reporting delinquent balances is that second kind, so it is what makes the office a creditor. Taking payment cards does not make anyone a creditor either, and billing a health plan is not credit extended to the patient.

preguntas.subtema: Visitor control · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A drug representative signs in at the desk and is escorted to the back office. Which physical safeguard specification covers that arrangement?
opciones: Access control and validation, which ties entry to a person's role and covers visitors
Workstation security, which restricts the machines that reach records to their users
Facility security plan, which protects the building and its equipment from intrusion
Contingency operations, which open the facility so lost information can be restored
preguntas.explicacion: Facility access controls carry a specification for procedures that control and validate a person's entry by role or function, and visitor control is named inside it, together with controlling who may reach software programs in order to test or revise them.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: invasion of privacy
preguntas.subtema: Torts · CCMA k221, 7E · CMA E.4.a · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which claim belongs under invasion of privacy?
opciones: Public disclosure of private facts about the person concerned
Publication of a written falsehood that damages a reputation
Repetition of a spoken falsehood in front of other employees
Retention of a record for longer than the policy allows for
preguntas.explicacion: Invasion of privacy covers a family of claims: appropriation, false light, public disclosure of private facts and intrusion on seclusion. They range from physically encroaching on private property to wrongfully disclosing confidential information or images, and what they share is an unwelcome or unauthorized intrusion into a person's private life. Libel and slander are defamation instead.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Spirometry", Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.C.10.d(13)(b) · NCMA 2B.14
preguntas.pregunta: How is a patient prepared for spirometry?
opciones: Sitting upright with the back supported, legs uncrossed, height and weight recorded
Sitting upright leaning forward, legs crossed, with the height taken afterward
Lying supine with the head of the bed raised, height and weight recorded first
Standing throughout, since a seated position limits how far the chest expands
preguntas.explicacion: The patient sits upright against a backrest, not leaning forward, without crossing the legs, in light clothing; weight and height are recorded barefoot and the age noted. Smoking and exercise are avoided in the hours before and bronchodilator therapy is stopped. Dentures come out if they get in the way, and the meter's calibration is checked that day.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Introduction to the Endocrine System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(9) (2027 I.C.6.f(9)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What distinguishes an endocrine gland from an exocrine gland?
opciones: An endocrine gland has no duct and releases hormones into the blood
An endocrine gland has a duct and releases hormones into the blood
An endocrine gland has no duct and releases enzymes onto a surface
An endocrine gland has a duct and releases enzymes onto a surface
preguntas.explicacion: Exocrine glands have ducts that carry their product to a surface, which is how sweat, sebaceous and mammary glands and the digestive enzyme glands work. Endocrine glands are ductless: their hormones go straight into the blood and travel everywhere, but they act only on the cells that carry a receptor for them.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Required and Addressable Specifications
preguntas.subtema: Required vs addressable · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice concludes that one addressable specification does not suit an office of its size. What must it do?
opciones: Adopt an alternative that meets the purpose of the standard, and document why it did so
Skip it, since addressable means the specification is offered to entities as an option
Adopt it anyway, since addressable and required specifications carry identical obligations
Ask OCR for a written waiver before the standard containing it can be treated as met
preguntas.explicacion: Every standard has to be met, but the specifications inside them come labeled required or addressable. Addressable is not optional: the entity decides whether the specification counts as reasonable and appropriate in its case, and where it does, the entity adopts it. Where it does not, the entity may put in place some other measure that serves the same purpose the standard serves, and it must document why the original did not fit.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(k), Standard: Test report
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5H k94 · PBT VI.F (CLIA) · CCMA 3E15 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: After a report has gone to the ordering physician, the laboratory discovers a transcription error in one result. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Promptly notify the ordering person, issue a corrected report promptly, and keep duplicates of the original and the corrected report
Issue a corrected report within 30 days and destroy the original so that only the corrected version remains on file
Correct the value in the LIS and rely on the next routine report to carry the corrected result to the physician
Notify the ordering person by telephone with read-back, which replaces the need for a corrected written report
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1291(k) has three parts when a reported result is found to be wrong: the laboratory promptly notifies the authorized person who ordered the test, and whoever uses the result, of the reporting error; it issues a corrected report promptly; and it maintains duplicates of both the original and the corrected report. The original is never discarded, a silent LIS edit notifies nobody, and the read-back procedure belongs to critical results, not to corrections.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "CPR - adult and child 9 years and older", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k83 · CMA I.B.9.c · 2027 I.B.8.c · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15 · CPT 1L k38
preguntas.pregunta: What compression rate is kept during adult CPR?
opciones: 100 to 120 per minute, letting the chest rise fully between compressions
80 to 100 per minute, starting the next push before the chest rises
60 to 80 per minute, matched to the normal resting adult pulse rate
140 to 160 per minute, matched to the resting pulse rate of an infant
preguntas.explicacion: Compressions are fast and hard, in the band of 100 to 120 per minute, and the chest is allowed to come all the way back up after each one. Full recoil between compressions is what maintains coronary artery perfusion pressure, so leaning on the chest defeats the compression that follows. The counted set of 30 is done without pausing.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 2e, 13.2 Basic Concepts: Mechanical Lifts
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.H.3.a · NCMA 2A.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which patient is a hydraulic lift with a sling meant for?
opciones: One who cannot bear weight or is not allowed to stand or help
One who bears weight but cannot rise from a chair unaided
One who is lying supine and has to cross from stretcher to bed
One who walks a short way but tires before reaching the door
preguntas.explicacion: A mechanical lift means a sling slung from a hydraulic frame, and it is for the patient who cannot take weight on their legs or whose condition forbids standing or helping with the move. It may be portable or fixed to the ceiling. The patient who bears weight but cannot rise is the one for the sit-to-stand lift.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Safety-engineered devices
preguntas.subtema: Lancets and safety devices · CPT D3 k54 k66 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.5
preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO classification of safety-engineered devices, how are retractable lancets categorized, and what is their listed advantage?
opciones: Passive devices; they retract and prevent needle-stick injuries
Active devices; the user must slide a sleeve forward over the blade
Passive devices; they prevent reuse but do not reduce needle-sticks
Active devices; the mechanism can trigger during probing and require a new puncture
preguntas.explicacion: Table C.1 places lancets under passive safety-engineered devices with the advantage that they are retractable and prevent needle-stick injuries. The sleeve that slides forward describes the active self re-sheathing needles, and the two remaining descriptions belong to auto-disable syringes, the other passive device, which prevents reuse but offers no needle-stick protection and can trigger while probing.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.4 Complications
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 k74 post-procedural complications · PBT II.I complications · CCMA 3E13 complications · NCMA 2C.10
preguntas.pregunta: Which vascular injury is associated with puncturing the medial aspect of a newborn's heel?
opciones: Laceration of the tibial artery, with collapse of veins
Rupture of the plantar vein, with a spreading hematoma
Thrombosis of the calcaneal branch, with local necrosis
Puncture of the tibial nerve, with loss of the venous branch used
preguntas.explicacion: Heading the list of complications is the collapse of veins that follows when the tibial artery is cut by a puncture on the inner side of the heel. The same list carries osteomyelitis of the calcaneus, nerve injury from sticking a newborn's fingers, hematoma with the venous branch lost, scarring, and necrosis, local or general, as a late effect.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 570: E-mail with patients
preguntas.subtema: Alternative means · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient tells the office that unencrypted e-mail is unacceptable to her. What should the office do?
opciones: Offer another channel, such as a more secure electronic method, mail or telephone
Explain that e-mail is the only channel the Privacy Rule permits for results
Continue using e-mail but omit her name from the subject line of each message
Close her portal account, since electronic access would raise the same problem
preguntas.explicacion: An individual may ask a covered provider to communicate through some other means, or at some other location, where the request is reasonable. The example given is accommodating a request for appointment reminders by e-mail instead of on a postcard. The principle runs the other way too: where unencrypted e-mail will not do for a patient asking for confidential communications, other means should be offered, more secure electronic methods, mail, or the telephone.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: power of attorney
preguntas.subtema: Power of attorney · CCMA k218 · CMA E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: Who can serve as the attorney in fact under a power of attorney?
opciones: A person or an organization; being a lawyer is not required
A licensed attorney at law admitted in the principal's state
A relative of the principal, once the court has approved them
A person named in the principal's will as the estate executor
preguntas.explicacion: A power of attorney is an agreement between a principal and an attorney in fact, and the attorney in fact does not have to be a lawyer. It gives that agent the right to act in the principal's place, and the agent is a fiduciary of the principal. Powers may be general, limited or special, and are usually written, though some jurisdictions allow oral ones.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Clinical Significance: Clergy and Other Religious Figures
preguntas.subtema: Clergy and the patient list · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k213 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital chaplain asks for the names of admitted patients of his denomination. What does the privacy rule allow?
opciones: Telling him, provided the patient was informed and did not object
Telling him, since clergy are workforce members of the hospital
Refusing, unless each patient signed a written authorization first
Refusing, because religious affiliation is never disclosed at all
preguntas.explicacion: Clergy and religious figures may be told which patients belong to their denomination, on the condition that the patient was informed first and raised no objection. That is why these preferences, along with who may visit and who should be notified, are asked at admission and put in writing. Disclosure can still happen in an emergency or when an incapacitated patient could not consent, if it is consistent with that person's best interest and the reasoning is documented.

preguntas.fuente: ADA.gov, ADA Requirements: Effective Communication, Auxiliary Aids and Services (VRI)
preguntas.pregunta: A deaf patient with low vision cannot make out the video remote interpreting screen. Under the ADA guidance?
opciones: VRI is not effective for him; an on-site interpreter may be required
VRI is sufficient as long as it meets the four performance standards
Written notes replace the interpreter, since VRI was properly offered
The patient must now bring his own interpreter, because VRI failed
preguntas.explicacion: The ADA allows VRI where it would be effective, but VRI is not effective in every case, for example for a person who has difficulty seeing the screen because of vision loss or positioning; then an on-site interpreter may be required. Meeting the technical standards does not cure that, and the entity may never shift the duty to the patient.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Winged steel needles
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A 3B k54 k58 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which confusion does the device table warn about when winged steel needles are stocked?
opciones: Winged sets for evacuated tubes look like winged infusion sets
Winged sets for evacuated tubes look like retractable lancet devices
Winged sets with a safety feature look like auto-disable syringes
Winged sets for pediatric use look like adult hypodermic needles
preguntas.explicacion: The disadvantages listed against winged steel needles include the difference between the ones made for evacuated tubes and winged infusion sets, which can create confusion at the tray. The other two entries are the air in the tubing and the higher cost of the device.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Care Transfer Techniques", Clinical Significance: Bed to Wheelchair
preguntas.subtema: NCMA 2A.5 · CCMA 3B4 k65 · RMA III.H.3.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: A patient whose left side is weak is being helped from the bed into a wheelchair. Where does the chair go?
opciones: On his stronger right side, at a 45-degree angle to the bed and with the brakes on
On his weaker left side, at a 45-degree angle to the bed and with the brakes on
Squarely facing the bed at the patient's feet, with the brakes left off for now
On his stronger right side, parallel to the bed, with the footplates left down
preguntas.explicacion: The chair is set at about 45 degrees to the bed with the brakes applied, and when one side is weaker it goes on the healthier side so the patient pivots toward strength. Shoes go on first, the patient sits with feet flat on the floor, and a gait belt is applied if it is needed. Coming back, the footplates are raised and the leg rests swung out of the way.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Patient Instructions: Breast self-exam — Information
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B3 k64 · CMA I.A.5.a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: Which instruction belongs in the teaching for a breast self-exam?
opciones: Lie down with one hand behind the head, then examine the armpit as well
Stand throughout, because lying down flattens tissue and hides the lumps
Press only over the nipple, where discharge would first become visible
Look in the mirror only with the arms raised over the head, not lowered
preguntas.explicacion: Lying down spreads the tissue and makes the whole breast easier to cover, with one hand behind the head and the flat of the middle fingers of the other hand pressing in small circles. Breast tissue runs into the armpit, so that is felt too, sitting or standing. The mirror check is done both with arms at the sides and with arms raised.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: Two conditions are linked by the word with in the Alphabetic Index, and the note never says one caused the other. How are they coded?
opciones: As related, since the classification presumes a causal link between the two
As unrelated, unless the provider has explicitly documented a link between them
As related only where the two conditions sit inside the same chapter of the book
As related, but with the order of the two codes on the claim reversed for it
preguntas.explicacion: The words with and in are read as associated with or due to wherever they turn up in a code title, in the Index or in an instructional note, and a causal relationship between the conditions they link is presumed by the classification. They are coded as related even where nothing in the record says so, unless the record states they are unrelated or a guideline demands the link be explicit.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Lymphatic System: Components of the Lymphatic System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027 I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Where does lymph come from, and what happens if it is not returned to the blood?
opciones: From interstitial fluid; without return there is edema and a falling blood volume
From arterial blood; without return there is edema and a rising blood volume
From the bone marrow; without return there is anemia and a falling blood volume
From the digestive tract; without return there is edema and a rising blood volume
preguntas.explicacion: Lymph is close in composition to blood plasma and comes from the fluid that leaves the capillaries into the tissues. Once that interstitial fluid enters a lymph capillary it is called lymph, and returning it to the blood is what keeps edema away and holds blood volume and pressure where they belong.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: res ipsa loquitur
preguntas.subtema: Legal doctrines · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What must a plaintiff show to rely on res ipsa loquitur?
opciones: That such harm needs negligence, that the thing was controlled, and that they did not contribute
That the defendant admitted the error, that it was documented, and that a witness saw it
That a statute was breached, that the breach was reported, and that the harm was foreseeable
That the injury was severe, that it was permanent, and that another clinician would agree
preguntas.explicacion: The Latin means the thing speaks for itself, and it lets the plaintiff carry the burden on what amounts to circumstantial evidence. Three things have to be proved: that an incident of this type does not usually happen unless there was negligence; that it was caused by an instrumentality under the defendant's sole control; and that nothing the plaintiff did contributed to the cause.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, All features
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which design feature does the FDA recommend for every type of sharps injury prevention feature, regardless of mechanism?
opciones: The user should be able to tell easily whether the feature is activated
The feature should retract the sharp fully within the housing of the device
The feature should activate passively, without any action by the user
The feature should be reversible so that a jammed device can be cleared
preguntas.explicacion: The two recommendations FDA Table 1 applies to all features are that the user can easily tell whether the feature is activated, and that once activated it cannot be deactivated and stays protective through disposal. Full retraction is the recommendation for retractable sharps only, passive operation is one of two acceptable mechanisms rather than a requirement, and reversibility contradicts the table.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 3: Select the site
preguntas.subtema: Site selection · CPT D2 2O k53 · D3 3F · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: What characteristics does the WHO ask the phlebotomist to look for when choosing a vein?
opciones: A vein of decent calibre, plainly visible, straight and unobstructed
The vein closest to the surface, even if it curves or branches
The largest vein, even if it can only be felt with the tourniquet on
A vein on the back of the hand, which the WHO prefers for adults
preguntas.explicacion: Step 3 tells the phlebotomist to extend the arm, inspect the antecubital fossa or forearm, and find a vein of decent calibre, plainly visible, straight and unobstructed, adding that it should be visible before the tourniquet goes on. The back of the hand is the preferred site for an IV, and a vein found only under the tourniquet fails the WHO's visibility criterion.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Growth Charts; and Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025 (USDA/HHS), resumen ejecutivo y capítulo 1 (págs. 1-40)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which growth charts are used for a 14-month-old and which for a 6-year-old?
opciones: WHO standards from birth to 2 years, then CDC charts from 2 years onward
CDC charts from birth to 2 years, then WHO standards from 2 years onward
WHO standards for both, since they cover birth through 19 years of age
CDC charts for both, with the WHO standards kept for children born preterm
preguntas.explicacion: The recommendation splits at the second birthday: the World Health Organization standards for infants and children from birth to 2 years, and the national charts for children of 2 and older. A separate extended set of charts exists for children with severe obesity.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Unique User Identification and Electronic Health Records
preguntas.subtema: HITECH · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k38
preguntas.pregunta: What did the HITECH Act add for covered entities that use electronic health records?
opciones: An audit trail accounting for disclosures, tracking who accesses records and when
A requirement to keep paper copies of every electronic record for 6 years
An exemption from breach notification for encrypted records affecting under 500 patients
A rule allowing shared passwords within a department to speed access
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH pushed providers toward taking up electronic records and using them meaningfully, and it tightened HIPAA along the way. A covered entity running an EHR has to produce an audit trail accounting for disclosures; the system logs who signed on and off, at what time, and what data was viewed or downloaded. Patients may ask for electronic copies of what the record holds, and one who pays out of pocket in full may ask that the information stay away from the health plan. Unique user names and passwords nobody shares are what make that tracking work; a shared password destroys it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · NCMA EKB 22
preguntas.pregunta: How early in a visit can de-escalation be used?
opciones: As early as triage, before any confrontation has started
Once the patient has raised his voice at a staff member
Once the aggression management team has been called in
Only after chemical and physical restraint were refused
preguntas.explicacion: Triage is named as the point where de-escalation can already begin. Managing the workplace turns on prevention and on de-escalation, keeping fight or flight in reserve, with physical restraint used to back up chemical restraint only as a last resort. Waiting for shouting, or for a team to arrive, throws away the early chances to defuse tension.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Latex Allergy", section History and Physical and section Differential Diagnosis
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k128 · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse gets red, irritated hands from her gloves but has no itching and no hives. What does that suggest?
opciones: Irritant contact dermatitis, which is not a true latex allergy
A type I hypersensitivity, the reaction behind a true latex allergy
Allergic contact dermatitis, which adds pruritus and urticaria
Latex-fruit syndrome, in which foods and gloves both provoke it
preguntas.explicacion: Irritant contact dermatitis produces erythema of the skin and comes from friction or contact with chemicals; it is a non-immunologic reaction, so the person does not have a true latex allergy and may need only a protective barrier for the skin. Allergic contact dermatitis is the delayed type IV reaction and brings pruritus and urticaria after exposure.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Urinary System: Components of the Urinary System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(7) (2027 I.C.6.f(7)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Name the four components of the urinary system in the order urine travels through them.
opciones: Kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, urethra
Kidneys, urethra, urinary bladder, ureters
Ureters, kidneys, urethra, urinary bladder
Urinary bladder, kidneys, ureters, urethra
preguntas.explicacion: The kidneys form the urine. The ureters carry it away from them down to the bladder, which holds it only temporarily, and the urethra carries it from the bladder to the outside. Reversing ureter and urethra is the classic slip, and the two words differ by very little in writing.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 1 and section 4.3 Light exposure
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.2 · CCMA 3E k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A courier leaves a box of specimens on the dashboard of a parked car in direct sunlight for an hour. Beyond the heat, what does prolonged light exposure do to the samples?
opciones: UV irradiation can oxidatively degrade nucleic acids, so samples are covered to shield them from unnecessary light
Visible light fades the bar codes, so samples are relabelled on arrival before they can be accessioned
UV irradiation sterilises the specimen surface, so samples intended for culture are treated as contaminated
Light activates clotting in anticoagulated tubes, so samples are inverted again before they are centrifuged
preguntas.explicacion: Light brings two problems at once: the temperature swings that come with sitting in the sun, and UV, whose long exposure oxidises and breaks down the polymers of the nucleic acid. The example given for this variable is a sample left in direct sunlight, and the countermeasure is plain, cover specimens so they take no light they do not need. Keeping transport time short protects them best of all.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.A.2 III.D.3 · CCMA 3E11 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A sedimentation rate is set up from a tube that turns out to hold a small clot, and a second one from an icteric patient. What happens to each reading?
opciones: The clotted one reads low; the icteric one is hard to read at the interface
The clotted one reads high; the icteric one is hard to read at the interface
The clotted one reads low; the icteric one reads high from the extra pigment
Both read high, since neither plasma settles at the expected sedimentation rate
preguntas.explicacion: Clotted blood breaks up the rouleaux the test depends on, so the figure comes out lower than the truth. In liver disease the plasma is icteric, a deep yellow that the eye struggles to separate from the settled red cells, and a hemolysed sample reddens the plasma for the same practical reason: the boundary the reading is taken from stops being sharp.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Bruise, sections Symptoms and When to Contact a Medical Professional
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural complications · CPT D3 k69 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient phones a week after a draw to say the bruise has turned greenish-yellow. What does that indicate?
opciones: The normal sequence of healing, which ends at the usual skin color
An infection developing under the skin at the site of the puncture
A deep periosteal bruise that will need a radiograph of the elbow
Fresh bleeding into the same area from the original puncture wound
preguntas.explicacion: A bruise starts pinkish red and tender, turns bluish, then greenish-yellow, and finally comes back to the usual skin color as it heals, over days to months. What would prompt a call to a clinician is streaks of redness, pus or fever, which point to infection, or extreme pressure in the area.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 1: Assemble equipment
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the WHO's Step 1 say the rack holding the sample tubes should be placed during a draw?
opciones: Near the phlebotomist and out of the patient's reach, so it cannot be knocked over
On the patient's lap, so the phlebotomist can reach the tubes without turning
On the far side of the patient, so the sharps container stays nearest the phlebotomist
Inside the sharps container tray, so used and unused items stay together
preguntas.explicacion: Step 1 ends with the instruction to keep the rack of sample tubes near the worker and out of the patient's reach, so that it cannot be knocked over by accident. The same step lists the tray contents, including gauze, labels, forms, leak-proof transport bags and a puncture-resistant sharps container, which Chapter 3 says has to be within arm's reach and in plain sight.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions Overview
preguntas.subtema: Insurance eligibility verification · CMAA 4 k58 · CCMA 5E · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: Which electronic transaction does an office use to ask a health plan whether a patient's coverage is active?
opciones: The eligibility transaction, one of the standard transactions adopted under HIPAA
The claim status transaction, one of the standard transactions adopted under HIPAA
The remittance advice transaction, which reports the plan's payment decisions
The enrollment transaction, which adds or removes members from a health plan
preguntas.explicacion: Eligibility is one of the standard transactions HIPAA adopted, sitting alongside claim status; coordination of benefits; enrollment and disenrollment; claims and encounter information; referrals and authorizations; and payment with remittance advice. Claim status asks what became of a claim already sent, remittance advice explains how a claim was paid, and enrollment moves members into a plan or out of it.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Disorders of Clotting; and 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, Cardiovascular System: Arteriosclerosis
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k3 (applied D3) · PBT I.C · RMA I.B.2.a · NCMA 1.2 EKB 3 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4))
preguntas.pregunta: A piece of clot breaks free from the vessel wall and travels in the bloodstream. What is the traveling piece called?
opciones: An embolus
A thrombus
A hematoma
A plaque
preguntas.explicacion: A thrombus is a clot that forms within an intact or slightly damaged vessel and stays attached; when part of it breaks loose and moves with the blood it is called an embolus, and once it lodges it is an embolism, which in the heart, brain or lungs is an emergency. A plaque is the fatty buildup of atherosclerosis in an artery wall; neither term names a clot that has broken loose.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Needlestick", section Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k66 · D1 1G 1H k30 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which working conditions are listed as increasing the chance of a blood exposure?
opciones: Devices without safety features, and sharps containers that are overfilled
Devices with passive safety features, and containers emptied twice a shift
Single-use devices, and containers sealed with a tamper-proof lid on top
Devices used on a single patient, and containers kept within arm's reach
preguntas.explicacion: The factors raising exposure risk include failing to follow standard precautions and safety protocols, doing procedures where blood exposure is expected, using devices with no safety features, and needles discarded badly or containers filled past the line.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 10: Prepare samples for transportation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5D k89 · PBT III.D · CCMA 3D5 3E14 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist packs three tubes and the paper requisition together inside the same plastic transport bag. What does WHO best practice say?
opciones: Use a leak-proof bag whose separate outer pocket carries the request form, keeping the paper clean
Use a leak-proof bag and fold the form around the tubes, so the two travel together as one unit
Use a leak-proof bag and staple the form to the outside, so the courier can read the destination
Use a leak-proof bag and place the form in a second bag, so it can be discarded on arrival
preguntas.explicacion: Packing for transport is step 10: the tubes go into a sealed plastic bag that cannot leak, and the request form rides in a pocket on the outside of it, which is exactly what keeps the paperwork off the specimen. Several tubes traveling together are held in a rack or a padded carrier so nothing breaks on the way, and tube labels are matched against the forms one last time before the bag leaves.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sutures and Needles", Function
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.1.b · NCMA 2B.16
preguntas.pregunta: How does suture numbering work?
opciones: Thick sutures run 0 to 10, with 10 the largest; thin ones run 1-0 to 12-0, with 12-0 the smallest
Thick sutures run 0 to 10, with 0 the largest; thin ones run 1-0 to 12-0, with 1-0 the smallest
All sutures run 1-0 to 12-0, and the more zeroes a suture carries the larger its diameter is
All sutures run 0 to 12, and the number gives the breaking strength in newtons, not the width
preguntas.explicacion: Size is given relative to diameter, and the scale runs in two directions. Thick sutures are numbered 0 through 10, with number 10 the largest; thin ones carry zeroes, from 1-0 down to 12-0, and 12-0 has the least breaking strength of all. Between one size and the next there is roughly 0.01 to 0.05 mm of difference in diameter.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Pulse
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A resting adult has a pulse of 108 beats per minute. How is that value classified?
opciones: Tachycardia, since anything above 100 beats per minute is above the adult range
Within range, because the adult range reaches 110 beats per minute while seated
Bradycardia is ruled out, but no term applies until the rate passes 120 per minute
Within range for an adult over 65, whose upper limit rises with arterial stiffening
preguntas.explicacion: The resting adult range is 60 to 100 beats per minute. Above 100 the term is tachycardia and below 60 it is bradycardia, and neither limit shifts with age: the same 60 to 100 band covers everyone from 10 years old upward, including seniors. A fast pulse may point to infection or dehydration, so it is reported.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Pulse Oximetry
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k51 · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: How close is a pulse oximeter reading to the true arterial oxygen saturation?
opciones: It may run 2% to 4% above or below the true value, so an arterial blood gas can confirm it
It matches the true value exactly, which is why it replaced arterial blood gas testing
It runs about 10% below the true value, and the reading is corrected upward for that
It is exact from 95% upward and unusable below that, where a blood gas is required
preguntas.explicacion: The device gives an estimate: results can be 2% to 4% higher or lower than the real figure, and an arterial blood gas is the test used when an exact value is needed. Oximeters are calibrated over a range of 70% to 100%, so readings below 70% should not be compared with the invasive measurement.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Table 18.1 Clotting Factors; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3 k57 additives) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which clotting factor is calcium, and why does that matter for citrate and EDTA collection tubes?
opciones: Factor IV; removing calcium from a sample keeps it from clotting
Factor I; it is converted into fibrin at the end of the cascade
Factor III; damaged cells release it to start the extrinsic path
Factor XIII; it stabilizes the fibrin mesh once it has formed
preguntas.explicacion: Calcium ions are factor IV, drawn from diet, platelets and bone, and needed for the entire clotting process. Sodium citrate and EDTA both act by forming calcium salts that remove calcium from the sample, which is how those tubes keep blood from clotting. Fibrinogen is factor I, tissue factor is III, and the fibrin-stabilizing factor is XIII.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Bleeding", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 k78 · CMA I.B.9.a · 2027 I.B.8.a · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives with a piece of metal embedded in the thigh and bleeding around it. What is done?
opciones: Pad and bandage around the object and tape it where it sits
Pull the object straight out and then press hard on the wound
Rock the object gently loose and pack the opening with gauze
Press directly down on the object to close the vessel beneath it
preguntas.explicacion: An embedded knife, stick or piece of metal is left where it is: pulling it out or probing the wound usually causes more bleeding and more damage. Pads and bandages are built up around the object and it is taped in place. Loose dirt or debris that can be seen is removed, and organs showing through a wound are never pushed back in.

preguntas.subtema: Research consent · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A subject who reads little English is being enrolled in a study. What does the federal consent rule require?
opciones: Information in language the subject or their representative understands
A translated form filed with the review board ten days after enrollment
A relative of the subject to sign the English-language form as a witness
The review board to waive consent whenever a language barrier is present
preguntas.explicacion: The rule states that whatever reaches the subject, or the representative legally authorized for them, has to be in language they understand, and that they must receive the information a reasonable person would want in order to decide, with a chance to discuss it. A board may waive consent only on narrow findings, such as minimal risk, never because translating is inconvenient.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: HITECH Act
preguntas.subtema: HITECH and business associates · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k34 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: What did the HITECH Act change about the position of business associates?
opciones: It made them directly liable, civilly and criminally, for Security Rule violations
It removed the need for a covered entity to sign an agreement with them at all
It made covered entities solely responsible for the acts of a business associate
It limited their obligations to the Privacy Rule and left the Security Rule aside
preguntas.explicacion: HITECH section 13401 extends the Security Rule to business associates: its administrative safeguards, its physical ones and its technical ones, plus its policy, procedure and documentation requirements, now bind them the way they bind covered entities, and violations make them liable both civilly and criminally. Before that the rule touched them only at one remove, through the agreements covered entities had to sign.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Strep A Test, What do the results mean?; MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Streptococcal screen (003745), Normal Results; Considerations
preguntas.subtema: Positive rapid strep · PBT IV.A.5 · CCMA 3D3 · CMA I.C.10.d.(2) · RMA III.C.4.a.iii · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: A rapid strep test on a 30-year-old shows a clear test line and a control line. What does the result mean for further testing?
opciones: Group A streptococcal antigen is present; no confirmatory culture is needed
Group A antigen is present, but a culture must confirm it before antibiotics start
A streptococcus of some group is present, so a culture is needed to identify the group
The patient carries antibodies from a past infection rather than a current infection
preguntas.explicacion: When the rapid test is positive, the patient has strep throat or another group A strep infection and no further testing is needed. The kit detects antigens of group A streptococcus only, not other causes of sore throat and not antibodies. Culture is the backup for negative rapid tests, mainly in children and adolescents. A rapid screen can occasionally be positive without disease, which is called a false positive.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Anti-Kickback Statute
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: What do the safe harbor regulations do under the Anti-Kickback Statute?
opciones: They describe payment practices not treated as offenses
They set the fine that applies to each kind of kickback
They list the referrals a physician may never make at all
They exempt an arrangement from the self-referral law too
preguntas.explicacion: Safe harbor regulations set out payment and business practices that would otherwise raise a kickback question but are not treated as offenses when they meet the requirements written into the regulation. Meeting a safe harbor does not release anyone from the other laws that govern the same arrangement, the self-referral law included.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", section Issues of Concern, Relevant Definitions
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which distinction between capacity and competence is correct?
opciones: Capacity is a clinical call for one decision; competence is a legal finding by a judge
Capacity is decided by a judge; competence is assessed by the treating clinician
Both are legal findings that differ only in the standard of evidence required
Capacity is permanent once established; competence is specific to one situation
preguntas.explicacion: Capacity is a functional judgment: can this person make this particular medical decision, measured against their own baseline and against the situation and what is at stake. Competence is the ability to take part in legal proceedings, presumed until it is disproved at a hearing, and settled by a judge, never by medical providers.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Testing Procedures; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 site preparation · PBT II.F · CCMA k130 cleansing · NCMA 2C.8 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: A patient arrives for a fingerstick glucose test with cold hands. How is the site prepared?
opciones: Wash and dry the site with warm water; alcohol is optional, but it must dry fully first
Swab with alcohol and puncture while still damp, since warm water would dilute it
Warm the hand with a cloth for 10 minutes, then clean with povidone iodine and let it dry
Rub the fingertip briskly until it reddens, then puncture without any cleaning step
preguntas.explicacion: The site is washed and dried well, and warm water is used because it brings the blood along. An alcohol swab is not required for this test; when one is used, the skin has to be dry before the lancet goes in, or the drop ends up diluted or hemolysed. Povidone iodine has no place in a child's skin puncture.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Appendix B: Some Common Abbreviations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k12 · CMA I.A.2.a (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k6 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says a relative had a heart attack. Which term will appear in the record?
opciones: Myocardial infarction, abbreviated MI
Congestive heart failure, abbreviated CHF
Coronary artery disease, abbreviated CAD
Atrial fibrillation, abbreviated AFIB
preguntas.explicacion: What people call a heart attack is charted as a myocardial infarction, written MI or AMI. The distractors are neighbors on the same problem list but different things: CHF is a heart that cannot pump enough blood, CAD is disease of the coronary arteries, and AFIB is a rhythm disturbance.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Does Pneumatic Tube System Transport Contribute to Hemolysis in ED Blood Samples?" (West J Emerg Med 2016, PMC5017839), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: In a hospital where emergency samples hemolyse at 13.5 % and the rest at about 3 %, what did the authors point to as the difference?
opciones: Emergency blood is usually drawn while the catheter is being placed
Emergency blood is usually hand carried instead of going by pneumatic tube
Emergency blood is usually collected into tubes that have no separator gel
Emergency blood is usually drawn by staff who work without a tourniquet
preguntas.explicacion: Hemolysis in the non-emergency samples of that facility ran near 3 %, against 13.5 % in the emergency department. Emergency blood is routinely taken during intravenous line placement, whereas inpatients and outpatients get a straight stick, and drawing through a catheter is known to hemolyse more. Transport was ruled out: hand carried and tube-sent samples hemolysed alike.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 9: Address Language Differences, Let patients know about language access services; and HHS OCR, Section 1557 of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, Resources for Providers
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 7A k214 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: How are patients told that free interpreter services exist at the practice?
opciones: Interpretive services posters displayed in waiting and reception areas
A line printed on the appointment reminder card handed at check-out
A notice read aloud by the clinician at the start of every encounter
A leaflet mailed to every household in the languages of the county
preguntas.explicacion: Practices list in their directories the languages their qualified bilingual clinicians speak, and hang interpretive services posters in the waiting and reception areas so that patients learn free interpreter services exist. Section 1557 adds a duty of its own: the covered entity posts a notice saying it does not discriminate, and another saying language help can be had.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Respiratory Rate", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: An 84-year-old is breathing 24 times a minute. How is that read against the range used for older adults?
opciones: Above the adult ceiling but under the 28 per minute used to call an older adult tachypneic
Inside the adult range, because the upper limit rises to 28 per minute after age 65
Below the threshold that matters, since no term applies to an older adult under 35
Above the adult ceiling, and the same 20 per minute threshold applies at every age
preguntas.explicacion: The general adult range stays at 12 to 20, but in the elderly the figure quoted for calling a patient tachypneic is more than 28 breaths a minute. A count of 24 is therefore above the general ceiling without reaching that mark, and it is charted and compared with the patient's own earlier values.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(ii), Personal Protective Equipment: Use
preguntas.subtema: Declining PPE in an emergency · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: In a rare emergency a phlebotomist judges that stopping to put on a gown would delay care, and draws without it. What does the standard require afterwards?
opciones: The circumstances are investigated and documented, to see whether a change can prevent it
No record is needed, since the judgment of the exposed employee settles the matter
The employee signs the hepatitis B declination form that is kept with the plan
The incident goes in the sharps injury log with the type and brand of the device
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(3)(ii) makes the employer ensure the protective equipment is used, and allows one narrow exception: the employee declined it, briefly and for that moment only, in rare and extraordinary circumstances, on the professional judgment that using it would have kept care from being delivered or would have raised the danger to someone. Even then the standard does not stop there: the circumstances are investigated and documented so the employer can see whether something can be changed. The declination form belongs to the hepatitis B vaccine under (f)(2)(iv), and the sharps log records percutaneous injuries.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Fainting, section Home Care
preguntas.subtema: Responses to complications · CPT D3 3K k69 · D1 1M k37 k38 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.B.9.l / 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who has fainted vomits while still on the floor. What should be done?
opciones: Turn the person onto their side, so choking is prevented
Sit the person upright at once and offer sips of cold water
Raise both legs higher and keep the person face upwards
Place a rolled towel behind the neck and keep the head back
preguntas.explicacion: The immediate steps for a person who has fainted are to check the airway and breathing, loosen tight clothing at the neck and raise the feet above heart level. If the person has vomited, they are turned onto the side to stop them choking, and kept lying down for ten to fifteen minutes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Types of PPE and Infection Prevention; CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions, Airborne Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Respirators and fit testing · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which statement about N95 respirators for healthcare workers is correct?
opciones: Workers required to use them must be fit tested; a PAPR is an option if fit testing fails
Any worker may use them without fit testing, as with a surgical mask
They protect against droplets only and are replaced by a surgical mask for airborne pathogens
They require fit testing only when used against chemical vapors under Level C
preguntas.explicacion: Protection runs on a scale, with loosely woven cloth masks at the bottom and NIOSH-approved respirators at the top, and fit is a large part of what makes a respirator work. Every worker who is required to wear one, N95 included, has to be fit tested; when the fit test cannot be completed, a powered air-purifying respirator carrying NIOSH approval may be considered instead. Airborne Precautions call for a fit-tested N95 or better, so a surgical mask is no substitute. Level C is a HAZMAT category built around air-purifying respirators.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, BMI Frequently Asked Questions; and NIST, Office of Weights and Measures: Approximate Conversions from U.S. Customary Measures to Metric
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.a · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which formula gives body mass index from measurements in metric units?
opciones: Weight in kilograms over the height in meters squared
Weight in kilograms over the height in meters, not squared
Weight in kilograms over the height in centimeters squared
Weight in pounds over the height in inches squared, times 703
preguntas.explicacion: In metric units the index is kilograms over meters squared. An alternative metric form divides by the height in centimeters twice and multiplies by 10,000, which comes to the same thing. Pounds over inches squared, times 703, is the customary formula used when height is in inches and weight in pounds.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Application and Removal of PPE; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(3)(vii)
preguntas.subtema: Where to don and doff · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: Where should personal protective equipment be put on, and where should it be taken off?
opciones: Both outside the patient room, with the respirator removed after exiting
Both inside the patient room, so the corridor stays free of contamination
Put on inside the room and taken off outside, next to the waste container
Put on outside the room and taken off inside, before the door is opened
preguntas.explicacion: Donning takes place outside the patient room, and so does doffing, with one exception spelled out in the sequence: a respirator is not removed until after leaving the room, because the air inside is the hazard it was worn against. The rest of the equipment comes off in order, gloves first, then eye protection, then gown, then mask or respirator, each dropped into the right container. The bloodborne pathogens standard says the same thing in its own words: all protective equipment is removed before leaving the work area.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Point-of-Care Testing", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5G · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A point-of-care coordinator lists the preanalytical errors her operators are most likely to make. Which pair belongs on that list?
opciones: Containers not properly secured before transport, and concentration shifts while aliquoting
Reagent lots recorded in the wrong column, and controls run at the wrong time of day
Results transcribed into the chart late, and duplicate orders entered by two clinicians
Analyser maintenance skipped for a week, and a calibration accepted outside its limits
preguntas.explicacion: Preanalytical error at the bedside belongs to the same family as in the main laboratory: the patient or the specimen misidentified, and whatever goes wrong while the sample is taken, handled, processed, moved or stored. The examples named run to clotting and hemolysis, a container under-filled or over-filled, containers not secured before transport, a tourniquet left on too long, and shifts introduced while aliquoting.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 5: Enforcing Standards
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Two employees at very different levels of the practice commit the same offense. What does the OIG guidance expect?
opciones: The same consequences for both, applied consistently
A lighter consequence for the more senior of the two
A consequence only for the one who supervises the other
Retraining for both, since discipline is not a tool here
preguntas.explicacion: OIG holds that all levels of employees should face the same consequences for similar offenses, and that the commitment reaches contractors and medical staff as well. Officers, managers and supervisors are accountable both for their own failures and for those of the people they supervise. Consequences may be remedial, punitive or both.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Dietary Fats — Summary
