opciones: A 22 G needle of 1 inch, or a 23 G winged set of 0.5 inch
A 21 G needle of 1 to 1.5 inch, or a 22 G needle of 1 inch
A 16 to 18 G needle, so the fragile vein is entered in one pass
A 19 to 20 G needle of 1 inch, the size for small veins
preguntas.explicacion: The column for pediatric, elderly and small-vein patients in Table 3.1 contains two entries: a 22 G needle of 1 inch (2.54 cm) and a 23 G winged butterfly set of 0.5 inch (0.75 cm). The 21 G needle is adult-only, 16 to 18 G is for blood donation, and 19 to 20 G is marked not applicable. Section 3.1.1 adds that a needle too large for the vein tears it and causes a hematoma.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Security Rule: Technical Safeguards
preguntas.subtema: Audit controls · CCMA 5 k189 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.6.d · CMAA 7 k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: A supervisor wants to find out who opened a particular chart last Tuesday. Which technical safeguard makes that possible?
opciones: Audit controls, the mechanisms that record and examine system activity
Authentication, the procedure that verifies who is seeking the access
Integrity controls, the measures confirming ePHI was not altered
Transmission security, the measures guarding data crossing a network
preguntas.explicacion: Audit controls are mechanisms, in hardware, in software or in procedure, that capture and review what happens inside information systems holding or using ePHI. Authentication is the separate standard for confirming that whoever seeks access is who they claim to be; integrity controls establish that no ePHI was altered or destroyed improperly; transmission security guards data on the move across a network.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Epidemiology
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: In patients under forty, what share of fainting episodes is vasovagal in origin?
opciones: More than eighty-five percent of them
Roughly twenty-five percent of them all
Fewer than ten percent of all of them
Almost exactly fifty percent of them all
preguntas.explicacion: More than eighty-five percent of syncopal events in people younger than forty are vasovagal, and even among older patients the figure stays above half. It is the commonest form of syncope in adults, and the lifetime chance of having at least one episode is more than a third.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Droplet Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Droplet Precautions · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k96 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: For a patient on Droplet Precautions, what does the CDC recommend for staff entering the room and for the patient?
opciones: Staff don a mask on entry; the patient wears a mask as source control and when transported
Staff don a fit-tested respirator; the patient goes to an airborne infection isolation room
Staff don gown and gloves; the patient's room is disinfected at least daily
Staff need no mask if the patient is masked; the door must remain closed at all times
preguntas.explicacion: Droplet Precautions apply to pathogens carried in respiratory droplets produced by coughing, sneezing or talking. The CDC asks for source control by masking the patient, a single room if possible, a mask donned by staff on entering the room or patient space, and a mask on the patient plus cough etiquette whenever transport is medically necessary. The respirator and the AIIR are Airborne Precautions; gown and gloves are Contact Precautions; and the masked-patient exemption for escorts applies to transport under Airborne Precautions, not to staff entering a Droplet room.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Introduction to the Digestive System
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(6) (2027 I.C.6.f(6)) · RMA I.A.1 · CMAA 1 k12 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which organs form the digestive tract itself, and which are the major accessory organs?
opciones: Mouth to large intestine form the tract; liver, pancreas, gallbladder and salivary glands assist
Mouth to large intestine form the tract; kidneys, spleen, thymus and appendix assist
Liver, gallbladder and pancreas form the tract; mouth, stomach and intestines assist
Stomach and intestines alone form the tract; mouth, pharynx and esophagus assist
preguntas.explicacion: The digestive tract, or alimentary canal, is one continuous tube from mouth to anus: after the mouth come the pharynx and the esophagus, then the stomach, then the small intestine and the large one. The salivary glands and the liver, the gallbladder and the pancreas are the major accessory organs; they pour fluids into that tube without being part of it.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Administrative Simplification: Transactions Overview
preguntas.subtema: Authorizations · CMAA 4G k67, 6C k87 · CCMA 5H k183 · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which HIPAA standard transaction covers the request a provider sends a plan for a referral or an authorization?
opciones: The referrals and authorizations transaction adopted by HHS under the law
The claims and encounter information transaction adopted by HHS under the law
The premium payment transaction, used between the employer and the plan
The coordination of benefits transaction, used between two health plans
preguntas.explicacion: Referrals and authorizations is one of the electronic transactions HHS adopted under HIPAA, and covered entities that conduct it electronically must use the adopted standard. Claims and encounter information carries the bill for services already given, premium payment moves money for coverage between the employer and the plan, and coordination of benefits exchanges the data payers need to decide who pays first.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(4)(ii)(B) and (C), Housekeeping
preguntas.subtema: Reusable bins and pails · CPT D1 1G k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k108 · CMA I.B.5 / 2027 I.B.4 · RMA III.A.4 III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: The plastic bins that hold used racks in the draw room have dried blood on the bottom. What does the standard require?
opciones: Clean and decontaminate them as soon as feasible, on top of the routine schedule
Discard them as regulated waste, since a soiled reusable bin cannot be cleaned
Line them with plastic wrap, which is then replaced at the end of the work shift
Clean them at the next scheduled inspection, which the standard sets once a year
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(C) covers bins, pails, cans and similar reusable receptacles likely to be contaminated, and it asks two things at once: a regular schedule on which they are inspected and decontaminated, and immediate cleaning, or as soon as feasible, whenever contamination becomes visible. Protective coverings such as plastic wrap belong to (d)(4)(ii)(B) and go over equipment and surfaces; no annual inspection appears here, and a bin that can be cleaned is not regulated waste.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Height Assessment", Equipment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · RMA III.E.4.b · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which instrument is preferred for measuring height, and to what precision?
opciones: A stadiometer, calibrated to read down to one-eighth of an inch
A tape measure held against the wall, read to the nearest half inch
The patient's wingspan, converted to height with a standard equation
An osteometric board, which measures long bones to the nearest millimeter
preguntas.explicacion: The stadiometer is the preferred equipment and the gold standard for this measurement, and it should be calibrated to an eighth of an inch. Estimating from wingspan or measuring with a tape gives less accurate results, and the osteometric board is for measuring the length of long bones.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve", section Clinical Significance; and "Phlebotomy", Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Nerve injury · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A patient reports a sharp, shooting pain and tingling down the forearm the moment the needle enters near the basilic vein. What does this indicate?
opciones: Probable injury to the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve, which runs near the basilic vein
Normal discomfort of a basilic puncture, which resolves as soon as the tourniquet is released
An arterial puncture, since arteries have more nerves and produce tingling
A vasovagal prodrome, which typically begins with tingling in the puncture arm
preguntas.explicacion: The basilic vein runs with the artery and nerve, and cutting the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve there costs the patient sensation over the medial forearm; the nerve chapter adds that damage during a venipuncture brings painful tingling, altered sensation and numbness. The vasovagal prodrome is lightheadedness, warmth, nausea and sweating, not arm tingling.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Power Dynamics and Perceived Authority
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which group is singled out as needing special care over consent because their choices are limited?
opciones: People who are incarcerated
People with private insurance
People living in rural counties
People with high health literacy
preguntas.explicacion: Under power dynamics and perceived authority, the unequal relationship can leave patients feeling pressed to agree, and the vulnerable groups named are older individuals, those with disabilities and those facing acute conditions. Incarcerated individuals are called out separately as a population whose limited choices demand meticulous attention.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L 2N k48 k52 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k126 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic is buying new chairs for its draw station. Why do the armrests need to be adjustable?
opciones: So the phlebotomist can act if the patient has a vasovagal attack
So the tourniquet can be anchored to the rest during the draw
So the arm stays above heart level while the tubes are filling
So the patient can be held in one posture for a full 15 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: The outpatient setting is asked to be clean, private, convenient and well laid out, with a comfortable chair for the patient and one for the provider. The armrests on the patient's chair are set where they suit, and so that the phlebotomist can act appropriately should the patient have a vasovagal mishap. Fifteen minutes seated is a separate rule about posture.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Medicare costs: Part B (Medical Insurance) costs
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74, 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A Medicare patient asks what she will owe for the covered blood work her physician ordered at the office.
opciones: Nothing, because covered clinical laboratory services carry no charge under Part B
Twenty percent of the approved amount, as with most other services under Part B
The yearly deductible first, and twenty percent of the approved amount after that
Five percent of the approved amount, the share that inpatient respite care carries
preguntas.explicacion: The Part B cost table puts covered clinical laboratory services at nothing for the patient, alongside covered home health care services. The twenty percent coinsurance applies to most other Part B services and items once the yearly deductible is met, and durable medical equipment such as a wheelchair or walker carries that same twenty percent.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Skin Antiseptics", Mechanism of Action
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.3.d (2027 I.C.3.d) · RMA III.D.2.d · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: What is the practical advantage of chlorhexidine over povidone-iodine as a surgical skin prep?
opciones: Excellent sustained residual activity, which persists after it is wiped off the field
Excellent sporicidal activity, which is what povidone-iodine has never been shown to have
Excellent activity in the presence of blood, which inactivates chlorhexidine far less
Excellent tolerance around the eye and the ear, where iodine solutions must be avoided
preguntas.explicacion: Chlorhexidine binds to the stratum corneum, so its activity carries on after the prep is wiped away; that residual effect, plus broad coverage and a fast onset, is what distinguishes it. Povidone-iodine also acts quickly but leaves almost no residual activity. The eye and conchal bowl are where chlorhexidine must be avoided, not iodine.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.5 Homeostasis, Negative Feedback
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which three components make up a negative feedback system?
opciones: A sensor, a control center and an effector
A stimulus, a set point and a normal range
A receptor, a hormone and a target organ
A sensor, a normal range and a stimulus
preguntas.explicacion: Negative feedback runs on three parts. The sensor, also called a receptor, watches a physiological value and reports it; the control center compares that value with the normal range; and if it has strayed too far from the set point, the control center turns on an effector, which acts to push the value back.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Steps 1 and 10
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J III.C · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which container is assembled beforehand so specimens can leave the room safely?
opciones: Leak-proof bags and containers for transport
Open wire baskets that let the tubes be counted
A puncture-resistant sharps container
Paper envelopes holding one tube and one form each
preguntas.explicacion: The equipment gathered before a draw takes in leak-proof bags and containers for transport, alongside the tubes, gloves, sampling devices, tourniquet, alcohol rub, swabs, gauze, labels, forms and a puncture-resistant sharps container. Several tubes travel in a rack or padded holder.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Standard Precautions for All Patient Care, Recommendation details
preguntas.subtema: Standard Precautions elements · CPT D1 1J k11 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C1 k100 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of practices does the CDC list as Standard Precautions for all patient care?
opciones: Hand hygiene, risk-based PPE, respiratory hygiene, patient placement, equipment cleaning and safe injections
Gown and gloves on room entry, dedicated equipment and daily room disinfection, for every patient
A fit-tested N95 respirator and an airborne infection isolation room, for every patient
Treating only blood and the listed body fluids as infectious, regardless of patient diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: Standard Precautions apply to all patient care, rest on a risk assessment, and consist of hand hygiene, PPE whenever exposure to infectious material is expected, respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette, appropriate patient placement, handling and disinfection of equipment and the environment, careful handling of textiles, safe injection practices and a surgical mask for lumbar punctures. Gown and gloves on entry describe Contact Precautions, the N95 and AIIR describe Airborne Precautions, and treating only blood and listed fluids as infectious is Universal Precautions, the older approach.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Abandonment, Nursing, Allied Health, and Interprofessional Team Interventions
preguntas.subtema: Notice period · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who keeps missing visits is being dismissed, and the nearest other clinician is sixty miles away. How does that affect the notice?
opciones: It can stretch the usual thirty days, since ninety may be needed where care is far away
It shortens the usual thirty days, since distance is not something the guidance weighs
It leaves the period alone, because the patient's insurer is the one that sets it
It removes the notice, because the practice cannot name a replacement within reach
preguntas.explicacion: Thirty days between the notice and the end of care is often treated as reasonable, but the time that counts as reasonable can be longer where replacement care is hard to reach, and up to ninety days may be needed when no other clinician is within reasonable driving distance. Rural patients are the example given. State rules on the number of days come first.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(5)(ii) and (f)(5)(iii), Healthcare Professional's Written Opinion
preguntas.subtema: Confidentiality of the written opinion · CPT D1 k33 k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After an exposure incident, what may the evaluating professional put in the written opinion the employer receives?
opciones: That the employee was informed of the results and told of any conditions needing further evaluation
The source individual's test results and the diagnosis, so that the employer can plan work restrictions
All findings and diagnoses from the evaluation, so the employer can complete the sharps injury log
The dates of hepatitis B vaccination and the employee's serologic status for the medical record
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (f)(5)(ii) limits the post-exposure opinion to two statements: that the employee has been informed of the evaluation results, and that the employee has been told about any conditions from the exposure that need further evaluation or treatment. Paragraph (f)(5)(iii) adds that every other finding or diagnosis stays confidential and is left out of the report. The employer is not entitled to diagnoses or source results through this document; vaccination dates live in the medical record of (h)(1), not in the opinion.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting started with telehealth, Types of telehealth
preguntas.subtema: Store and forward · CMAA 4B k54 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A scheduler is asked which everyday exchanges count as store-and-forward telehealth. Which set is listed under that heading?
opciones: Messages carrying follow-up instructions, images forwarded for review, results and vitals
Messages carrying follow-up instructions, live video visits, and triage by telephone
Images sent for review, results and vitals, and a live call with an interpreter on the line
Messages with appointment reminders, a live video visit, and a wearable reporting continuously
preguntas.explicacion: Store and forward, the asynchronous kind, covers what providers, patients and caregivers send one another at different moments rather than at the same time. The examples listed are images forwarded for review, laboratory results and vital statistics, and messaging that carries follow-up instructions or confirmations.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 7: Improve your telephone system
preguntas.subtema: Telephone etiquette · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2A k27 · NCMA F.23
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is recording the message that plays once the office has closed. What has to be in it?
opciones: To call 911 in an emergency, and the covering clinician's number
The hours the office closes for lunch on each day of the week
The address of the nearest emergency department and its entrance
A request to use secure email rather than wait for a call back
preguntas.explicacion: An after-hours message, or a service covering the phones, has to tell callers to dial 911 in an emergency and give a number for the clinician on call, said twice and slowly so it can be written down. A separate message covers the hours the office is closed for lunch.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.2 Production of the Formed Elements, Differentiation of Formed Elements from Stem Cells
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which formed element is the only one that arises from the lymphoid stem cell line rather than the myeloid line?
opciones: Lymphocytes
Neutrophils
Eosinophils
Monocytes
preguntas.explicacion: The hematopoietic stem cell gives rise to two lines: lymphoid stem cells, which produce only the lymphocytes (T cells, B cells and natural killer cells), and myeloid stem cells, which produce everything else, including erythrocytes, the megakaryocytes that shed platelets, monocytes and the three granular leukocytes. Lymphocytes finish much of their development in lymphatic tissue.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.15(b); CDC, CLIA Test Complexities: Waived testing; Related terms
preguntas.subtema: Definition of a waived test · CPT D1 k29 · PBT VI.F · CCMA 3D k114 · CMA I.C.9 · RMA III.C.1.a.v · NCMA 4.12
preguntas.pregunta: What makes a test "waived" under CLIA?
opciones: It is a simple procedure whose risk of giving an erroneous result is insignificant
It is performed at the bedside or in an exam room rather than in a laboratory
It has been cleared by the FDA as substantially equivalent to a marketed test
It is a moderately complex procedure done by a physician during the visit
preguntas.explicacion: The regulatory criteria are simplicity and low risk: the test is cleared for home use, or its method is so simple and accurate that user error is negligible, or a wrong result would pose no reasonable risk of harm. Location does not qualify a test; FDA clearance applies to waived, moderate and high tests alike; and a moderate microscopy test done by the physician is PPM, a subcategory inside moderate complexity and not a category of its own.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.1.1 Skin Variations
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.6
preguntas.pregunta: A technician using the same technique all day still gets a mix of clean and poor tracings. Why?
opciones: Skin chemistry varies, so some skin needs extra care
The machine loses its calibration as the day goes on
The room current varies through the day and interferes
The alcohol evaporates, so later sites get less of it
preguntas.explicacion: Skin resistance is not the same from one patient to the next: some skin is sweatier and some scalier, and each condition calls for a different level of care when the electrode goes on. Good technique compensates even for the most difficult skin, which is why the preparation step is never rushed.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Health Maintenance Organization (HMO)
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.e (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient enrolled in an HMO asks whether her plan will pay for a specialist in another state who does not belong to the plan. What is the correct answer?
opciones: It generally pays nothing for that visit, because the care is outside the network
It pays a smaller share of that visit, because the specialist is outside the network
It pays the visit in full once her primary care doctor signs a written referral
It pays the visit in full once she has met the yearly deductible of her plan
preguntas.explicacion: An HMO usually restricts coverage to physicians employed by the plan or under contract with it, and it will not pay for care outside that group except in an emergency. Paying a reduced share for outside providers is what a PPO does. A referral changes which specialist she may see inside the network, and the deductible changes how much she owes, not whether an outside provider is covered at all.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 6.2.2 and Annex C, Table C.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3D k55 device selection, D4 4B · PBT II.J tubes · CCMA 3E3 supplies · NCMA 2C.4 equipment by age
preguntas.pregunta: When an evacuated tube is used for a pediatric venipuncture, which tube is chosen?
opciones: A small-volume tube, 1 mL or 5 mL, with a low vacuum, to avoid collapsing the vein
A standard 10 mL tube, since a partial fill still keeps the correct blood-to-additive ratio
A 1 mL or 5 mL tube with a high vacuum, so that the small needle fills it quickly
A non-additive tube only, because additive tubes cannot be filled through a butterfly
preguntas.explicacion: In a child the evacuated tube picked is a small one, 1 or 5 mL, and of low vacuum: that way the vein is less likely to collapse and there tends to be less hemolysis. The device annex says the same, a smaller tube at reduced vacuum for pediatric patients. The note about the first tube through a butterfly is about air in the tubing, not about additives.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Individuals Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information: Timeliness
preguntas.subtema: Access extension · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: The records the patient asked for are archived offsite and cannot be pulled in time. What may the office do?
opciones: Take one extension of up to 30 more days, telling her in writing why and when she will get them
Take as many extensions as the retrieval needs, so long as each one is documented internally
Take one extension of up to 60 more days, the period the rule gives for amendment requests
Deny the request outright, since information that is not readily accessible falls outside access
preguntas.explicacion: Where the entity cannot make the 30 days, OCR's own example is this very situation: information archived offsite and not readily reachable. One extension is possible, of 30 further days at most, and inside the original 30 the individual has to be told in writing why it is late and on what date access will come. Only one extension per request is allowed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Issues of Concern; StatPearls, "Medical Malpractice", Referrals
preguntas.subtema: Respondeat superior · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.c · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: Under which doctrine is a supervising physician or employer held liable for the acts of an employee working within the scope of employment?
opciones: Respondeat superior, a form of vicarious liability
Strict liability, applied to inherently dangerous activities
Proportional liability, apportioned by degree of fault
Sovereign immunity, which limits awards against governments
preguntas.explicacion: Vicarious liability makes an employer answer for torts its employees commit inside the scope of their work, on the reasoning that the employer is better placed to absorb the loss. That is why a suit against a midlevel provider practicing under a physician's license is aimed at the supervising physician, and respondeat superior is the doctrine that puts it there. Proportional liability instead trims an award by the claimant's own share of fault, strict liability covers dangerous activities and defective drugs or devices, and sovereign immunity caps what can be recovered from governmental bodies.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(f)(3)(ii)(B) and (f)(3)(iv), Post-exposure Evaluation and Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Known source status · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: The source patient of a splash exposure is already documented as HIV-positive. What does the standard say about testing that source?
opciones: Testing for the already known HIV status does not have to be repeated
Testing must be repeated to confirm the status before any prophylaxis is offered
Testing must be repeated within 72 hours and recorded in the sharps injury log
Testing is replaced by a second baseline sample from the exposed employee
preguntas.explicacion: Under (f)(3)(ii)(B), a source already on record as infected with HBV or with HIV does not have to be tested again for what is already known. The employee still has the right, under (f)(3)(ii)(C), to be told the source's results and the laws governing disclosure. Prophylaxis under (f)(3)(iv) follows Public Health Service recommendations when it is medically indicated, not a confirmatory retest, and the sharps injury log holds injuries rather than test results.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Anticoagulated specimens from a neonatal unit clot at 6.67 %, against 0.36 % elsewhere in the same hospital. Which explanation fits the published data?
opciones: Drawn-out, difficult venipuncture and failure to mix the tube afterwards
Excess anticoagulant in the microtubes chosen for very small blood volumes
Transport of the microtubes upright in a rack instead of a padded holder
The longer wait before newborn serum is separated from the cells
preguntas.explicacion: Clotting inside a tube that contains an anticoagulant is attributed to two things: a challenging or prolonged venipuncture, and a tube that was not mixed properly once filled. Newborn draws are hard, which is why their clotting ratio ran roughly eighteen times the hospital average. Published median figures for clotted samples elsewhere sit between 0.05 % and 0.21 %.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, footnote c; and Section 2.2.3, Step 7
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: What does the WHO order-of-draw table say about tubes that contain an additive once they have been filled?
opciones: Invert them gently to mix; poorly mixed blood can give erroneous results
Leave them standing upright until the additive has dissolved on its own
Invert them only if the local laboratory has not already specified otherwise
Shake them firmly for a few seconds so the additive reaches all the blood
preguntas.explicacion: Footnote c of Table 2.3 instructs the phlebotomist to gently invert additive tubes to mix them well, and warns that test results can be wrong when blood and additive are not mixed thoroughly. Step 7 adds that the number of inversions is the one the local laboratory specifies, which is a detail of how many, not a license to skip mixing. Shaking is exactly what to avoid.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex E, Use of a removal device
preguntas.subtema: Sharps handling · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which devices are described for taking a used needle off a barrel or syringe without touching it?
opciones: Needle pliers, and a mushroom-shaped needle guard
Needle pliers, and a spring-loaded recapping block
A blunt cannula, and a mushroom-shaped needle guard
A magnetic tray, and a slotted needle removal rack
preguntas.explicacion: Two removal devices are set out: pliers or artery forceps, which hold the needle while it is unscrewed or pulled off, and a mushroom-type guard, in which the cap is seated and the tip turned firmly into it with one hand. In both cases the needle goes straight into the sharps container.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1232, Standard: Specimen identification and integrity
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k145 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory is writing its specimen identification policy. Under CLIA, over what span must positive identification and integrity of a patient's specimen be assured?
opciones: From collection or receipt of the specimen until testing is complete and results are reported
From the moment the specimen is accessioned until the analyzer finishes the run
From collection until the specimen is centrifuged and the aliquots are labeled
From receipt in the laboratory until the specimen is discarded at the end of its retention period
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1232 asks for written policies that keep the specimen positively identified and in optimum condition across the whole chain: it starts when the specimen is collected or received and ends only when testing is finished and the result has been reported. Stopping at accessioning, at centrifugation or at the analyzer leaves later steps, such as aliquoting and reporting, outside the policy.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 3.3 The Nucleus and DNA Replication, Organization of the Nucleus
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k35 · CMA I.C.6.c (2027 I.C.6.b) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: What is stored in the threads of chromatin inside the nucleus, and what does the nucleolus produce?
opciones: Chromatin holds DNA; the nucleolus makes the RNA for ribosomes
Chromatin holds RNA; the nucleolus makes the DNA for chromosomes
Chromatin holds enzymes; the nucleolus makes the lipids for membranes
Chromatin holds histones; the nucleolus makes the ATP for the cell
preguntas.explicacion: The nucleus is the control center, and the chromatin inside it is DNA wound around histone proteins. When the cell divides, that chromatin condenses into chromosomes. The nucleolus is a dense region within the nucleus that turns out the ribosomal RNA, and the new ribosome subunits leave through the nuclear pores.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(f), Standard: Deceased individuals; 164.502(g)(4)
preguntas.subtema: PHI of deceased individuals · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k219 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.4 · CMAA 3B k39
preguntas.pregunta: How long after a patient's death does HIPAA continue to protect their health information?
opciones: For 50 years after death
For 6 years after death
For 30 years after death
Indefinitely, with no time limit
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(f) requires a covered entity to comply with the Privacy Rule for the PHI of a deceased individual for 50 years following the death; the 2013 Omnibus Rule changed the protection from indefinite to this fixed period. During that time an executor, administrator or other person with authority over the estate is treated as the personal representative. Six years is the retention period for HIPAA documentation, and employment plus 30 years is the OSHA rule for employee medical records.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1291(f) and (l), Standard: Test report
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5H k94 · PBT VI.E VI.F · CCMA 3E15 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.1.a
preguntas.pregunta: A relative phones the laboratory asking for a patient's test results and supplies the patient's full name and date of birth. To whom may CLIA-regulated results be released?
opciones: To authorized persons, to those responsible for using the results, to the requesting laboratory, and to the patient on request
To the ordering provider only; the patient must obtain the results through that provider's office
To any caller who can supply two patient identifiers, since positive identification is what the regulation requires
To the ordering provider and to any physician or relative who states that they are involved in the patient's care
preguntas.explicacion: 42 CFR 493.1291(f) confines the release of results to authorized persons, to those responsible for using them and, where it applies, to the laboratory that first requested the test; paragraph (l) adds that the patient, or someone acting as their personal representative, may have completed reports on request once the laboratory's authentication process shows who they are. Two identifiers over the phone, or a claim of being involved in the case, do not amount to authorization.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow, Conducting telehealth visits
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth intake · CCMA 5R k190 · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5 k80 · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A video visit has just been confirmed and the intake step begins. Which information does the workflow guidance have a staff member review and collect there?
opciones: Identity, symptoms, medical history and, where it fits, the patient's vital signs
Identity, symptoms, medical history and the reading of the consent to the visit
Insurance, symptoms, medical history and the patient's preferred pharmacy details
Identity, symptoms, the reason for the visit and the feedback on the last session
preguntas.explicacion: The visit opens with confirmation, which pins down who the patient is and why she has come. Intake follows, and there a staff member goes over and gathers what is needed: verification of identity, the symptoms, the medical history and, where it fits, the vital signs. Consent and the online forms sit among the steps taken before the appointment; evaluation comes after it.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(c)(1)(v) and (c)(1)(vi), Exposure Control Plan
preguntas.subtema: Employee input on safer devices · CPT D1 k12 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital is selecting a new safety needle. Whose input does the Exposure Control Plan have to document?
opciones: Non-managerial employees who give direct patient care and could be injured by contaminated sharps
The evaluating healthcare professional who provides the written opinions after exposure incidents
The laboratory director or whichever responsible person is named on the biohazard warning signs
The Assistant Secretary and the Director, who may examine and copy the plan on request
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (c)(1)(v), added after the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, tells the employer to ask the workers who give direct patient care and are not managers, the ones exposed to sharps injuries, what they think when engineering and work practice controls are identified, evaluated and chosen, and to leave that consultation documented in the plan. The evaluating professional writes opinions under (f)(5); the responsible person appears on the (g)(1)(ii) signs for HIV and HBV laboratories; and the Assistant Secretary and the Director get access under (c)(1)(vi), which is not a say in choosing a device.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet time and pre-analytical error · CPT D3 3E k9 k60 · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A supervisor tells a trainee that a long tourniquet application causes hemoconcentration. What does that word describe?
opciones: Falsely elevated laboratory results after prolonged constriction of the veins
Falsely lowered laboratory results after prolonged constriction of the veins
Clotting inside the tube after the anticoagulant has failed to mix properly
Dilution of the sample by intravenous fluid running above the puncture site
preguntas.explicacion: Constricting the veins for too long produces hemoconcentration, which shows up as laboratory results that read falsely high. It is the reason the band is released early and the reason illumination devices are preferred when several tubes are needed and the veins are not obvious.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(h)(3)(i) to (h)(3)(iv), Employee information and training
preguntas.subtema: What the training covers · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.iii III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which subject must hazard communication training cover, beyond the hazards of the chemicals themselves?
opciones: Ways to detect that a hazardous chemical is present or being released
The disposal contractor's route and the landfill that receives the waste
The chemical formula of each product and its molecular weight
The purchase price of each product and the budget for replacing it
preguntas.explicacion: Training covers at least four things: the methods and observations that reveal a hazardous chemical is present in the area or is escaping into it, such as monitoring carried out by the employer, devices that monitor continuously, or the look or smell of the chemical as it gets out; the physical and health hazards, asphyxiation, combustible dust, pyrophoric gas and hazards not otherwise classified among them; what an employee can do to stay protected; and the details of the program, of the labels and of the data sheet, the order of its information included.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Semen Analysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure
preguntas.subtema: Incomplete semen sample · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.D.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A man says part of his semen sample spilled outside the container. What should he be told?
opciones: Report the loss to the laboratory, because every fraction of the ejaculate is meant to be collected
Keep it to himself, because the laboratory reports concentration per milliliter and volume does not count
Top the container up with sterile saline to the mark the instructions on the lid show him
Bring a second sample later the same day, since two samples are added together for the count
preguntas.explicacion: Clear instructions are given beforehand precisely so that all fractions of the ejaculate end up in the container, and any loss has to be reported when the sample is handed in. Volume itself is one of the measurements made. Because composition varies from one occasion to another, collecting 2 or 3 separate samples gives more accurate data, but each one needs its own 3-to-7-day abstinence interval.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.5 Hemostasis, Clotting Factors Involved in Coagulation; Extrinsic Pathway
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k8 (applied D3) · PBT I.C · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which coagulation pathway is set off by trauma to the tissues around a vessel and is completed within seconds?
opciones: The extrinsic pathway, started by factor III
The intrinsic pathway, started by factor XII
The common pathway, started by factor X
The fibrinolytic pathway, started by plasmin
preguntas.explicacion: The extrinsic, or tissue factor, pathway is the quicker and more direct of the two: cells damaged outside the vessel put out factor III, thromboplastin, which together with calcium and factor VII activates factor X, and the whole sequence takes seconds. The intrinsic pathway starts inside the blood when factor XII meets a damaged wall or a foreign surface, and takes minutes. Both feed the common pathway.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F.2 Specimen collection · CPT D1 1B k25 operational standards · NCMA 4.12 · CCMA 7A k214
preguntas.pregunta: A tube reaches the laboratory with no label on it, and the courier says he knows which patient it came from. What does the CLIA specimen identification standard require?
opciones: Reject it, because positive identification has to hold from collection through to reporting
Accept it and label it from the requisition, since the courier can confirm where it came from
Accept it and note the discrepancy on the report as an unacceptable specimen condition found
Accept it when the order is stat, and label it once the ordering provider confirms the source
preguntas.explicacion: Those written policies have to guarantee that the patient's specimen is positively identified and kept in the best condition possible, from collection or receipt until testing and reporting are done, so a tube nobody can tie to a patient breaks the chain at its first link. A third party's recollection is not identification. Noting specimen condition on the report belongs to specimens the laboratory did accept.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "ACE Inhibitors", Adverse Effects
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k67 · CMA I.D.1.c · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient taking an ACE inhibitor arrives with swelling of the lips and face. Why is this reaction treated as an emergency?
opciones: The swelling can reach the upper airway, and intubation may be needed to secure it
The swelling is the first stage of the dry cough that most treated patients develop
The swelling means potassium has risen, which is the commonest reaction to the class
The swelling marks the sulfonamide allergy shared with the thiazide in the tablet
preguntas.explicacion: Angioedema is rare with ACE inhibitors but can kill: the face, lips and upper airway swell in episodes, and the airway may have to be secured with an endotracheal tube. Treatment starts with stopping the drug, and the class is avoided in anyone with hereditary angioedema or a previous episode. Hyperkalemia is a separate reaction, reported in 2% to 6%, and it does not swell the face.

preguntas.subtema: Maintenance records · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.5.b · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: After a break-in the practice replaces the back door and its lock. Which addressable specification asks for that work to be documented?
opciones: Maintenance records, for repairs and changes to the parts of the building tied to security
Facility security plan, for keeping the premises and the equipment safe from tampering
Contingency operations, for reaching the building when information has to be restored
Access control and validation, for checking entry by role and for controlling visitors
preguntas.explicacion: Facility access controls carry four addressable specifications. Three of them plan access; the fourth, maintenance records, is about paperwork: policies to document repairs and modifications to physical components related to security, such as hardware, walls, doors and locks.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 7; and StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: Tube inversions · CPT D3 3N k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A new tube brand asks for ten inversions on its insert while the poster on the wall says eight. What settles the number?
opciones: The number the local laboratory specifies for the tubes it has in use
The larger of the two numbers, since extra mixing carries no penalty
The smaller of the two numbers, since extra mixing produces hemolysis
The number printed on the poster, which follows the published sequence
preguntas.explicacion: Before tubes are sent, those holding an additive are inverted the number of times the local laboratory specifies, which is what the guidance points to when brands disagree. Neither extreme is safe on its own: overmixing can haemolyse the sample and too little mixing leaves small clots.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.9 Checklist for Wound Specimen Collection
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.a (2027 I.C.4.a) · RMA III.D.2.i · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: What has to accompany a wound culture specimen when it goes to the laboratory?
opciones: A label made at the bedside and a request form noting any current antibiotic therapy
A label made at the nurses' station and a request form noting the last dressing change
A label made at the bedside and a request form noting the wound's measured dimensions
A label made in the laboratory and a request form noting the patient's temperature trend
preguntas.explicacion: The specimen is labeled in the presence of the patient, with details such as name, date, time, wound location and the site and source, precisely so it cannot be mislabeled. Current or recent antibiotic therapy is noted on the request form because it can alter the result, and where possible the culture is taken before antimicrobials are started. It travels in a biohazard transport bag.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Tort in Healthcare", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Assault vs battery · CPT D1 1D · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7A k221 · CMA II.E.4.a · RMA I.C.1.c · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k31
preguntas.pregunta: A patient raises a fist at the front-desk staff but does not strike. In tort terms this may be which of the following?
opciones: Assault: an intentional act creating apprehension of imminent harmful contact
Battery: harmful or offensive contact that actually occurs
Negligence: an unintentional failure to act as a reasonable person would
Strict liability: harm during a known dangerous activity, regardless of fault
preguntas.explicacion: An assault is complete without any touching: it is an intentional act that makes another person reasonably expect harmful or offensive contact is about to happen. A fist raised at the front desk is the illustration used, and if the blow lands, battery is added to the assault. Reasonableness matters, since someone standing several meters away would not yet create that expectation. Negligence, by contrast, is unintentional, and strict liability attaches to inherently dangerous activities and to defective products without regard to fault.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Personal Protective Equipment", Suggested Sequence for Removal of PPE; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Removing PPE
preguntas.subtema: Mask removal · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.d · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: How does the CDC sequence describe removing a mask at the end of doffing?
opciones: By the ties or straps behind the head, never by the front
By the front panel, pulling it down under the chin first
By the nose bridge, lifting it up and over the head
By the ear loops after untying the gown, keeping gloves on
preguntas.explicacion: The front or mouth area of the mask or respirator is never touched; it is removed by releasing the ties or straps around the back of the head, bottom ties first and then the top, lifting it away from the face, and discarded in the proper container. The front is considered contaminated, which is also why eye protection is lifted from behind the head. Gloves are the first item off, so they are already gone by the time the mask is removed.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 3: Training and Education
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Under the OIG's seven elements, who has to receive compliance training and how often?
opciones: Officers, board members, contractors, employees and medical staff, at least yearly
Only the employees who handle claims and coding, at least once every three years
Only the compliance committee and the compliance officer, twice in each year
Everyone in the entity, but only after an audit or an investigation has found a fault
preguntas.explicacion: Training and education is the third element. Officers, board members, contractors, employees and medical staff should all be trained at least once a year on the entity's compliance program and on its compliance risks, with the applicable fraud and abuse laws reviewed in that training. The compliance officer draws up an annual plan taking in whatever the audits and investigations turned up.

preguntas.subtema: PSDA · CCMA 7D k217, k219 · CMA E.8.d / 2027 E.7.c · NCMA 4.2 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: What must the provider record about an adult patient's advance directive?
opciones: Whether or not one exists, in a prominent part of the current record
Whether or not one exists, in the billing file kept with the claim
The full text of the directive, scanned into the record within 90 days
The name of the agent, sent to the state survey and certification agency
preguntas.explicacion: The rule is that the provider documents, in a prominent part of the patient's current medical record, whether an advance directive has been executed by that individual. The state survey and certification agency is where complaints about these requirements are filed, not where agents are registered, and the 90-day clock belongs to updating information after a change in state law.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(vii) and (b), Definitions: Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Sharps safety and needlestick prevention · CPT D1 k30 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist finishes a draw and, out of habit, starts to push the cap back onto the used needle with both hands. Which OSHA rule does this break?
opciones: Contaminated needles are not recapped, bent or removed unless no alternative is feasible or a procedure requires it
Contaminated needles may be recapped with a one-handed technique whenever the phlebotomist finds it convenient
Contaminated needles may be sheared or broken with a mechanical device, but they may never be bent by hand
Recapping is permitted whenever the employer documents that it is faster than reaching the sharps container
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(vii) forbids recapping, bending or removing a contaminated needle, and forbids shearing or breaking one outright, mechanical device or not. The only way around it is for the employer to show that there is no feasible alternative or that a specific medical or dental procedure demands it, and even then the job has to be done with a mechanical device or with one hand. Convenience and speed are not exceptions, and the one-handed technique is the method for the exception, not a general permission. The standard's own definition of a work practice control gives this very example: banning two-handed recapping.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Managing the pre- and post-analytical phases of the total testing process" (Ann Lab Med 2012, PMC3255486), section 3, "1) Joint Commission International", IPSG 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Why do accreditation bodies treat a mislabeled blood specimen as one of the most dangerous laboratory errors?
opciones: Mislabeling can lead to a hemolytic transfusion reaction from incompatible blood
Mislabeling always causes hemolysis of the specimen during centrifugation
Mislabeling invalidates the CLIA certificate of the laboratory that reports the result
Mislabeling is the most common reason a specimen clots before it is tested
preguntas.explicacion: Identification errors can lead to inappropriate treatment, and a mislabeled blood specimen may end in a hemolytic transfusion reaction from incompatible blood; up to half of transfusion-related deaths trace back to identification error, and as many as 1 in 18 identification errors produce an adverse outcome. The error is about the patient, not about the specimen clotting or hemolyzing, and it does not by itself void a certificate.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Attempt conflict management techniques before termination
preguntas.subtema: Documenting a conflict · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: After a heated exchange at the front desk, the clinician apologises for the way the conversation went. What does the guidance say about the record?
opciones: The conflict goes briefly into the clinical notes, and the apology goes in with it
The conflict goes into an incident report kept apart from the clinical notes
Neither goes in, since an apology in the chart can be read as admitting an error
The conflict goes in only once the practice decides to end the relationship
preguntas.explicacion: An apology offered sincerely for perceived rudeness can take the heat out of a disagreement that has escalated, and it is confined to the way the clinician conducted the exchange so that nobody can read it as an admission of a medical error. Record-keeping that is accurate and complete means the conflict goes briefly into the clinical notes, apology and all, leaving a written account that refreshes the clinician's memory before the next encounter.

preguntas.fuente: FTC, Fighting Identity Theft with the Red Flags Rule: Identify Relevant Red Flags
preguntas.subtema: Suspicious documents · CCMA 5F k190 · CMA III.H.2.b · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A k66 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: The photograph on the card a new patient hands over does not look like the person standing at the desk. Which category of red flag is that?
opciones: A suspicious document presented
Suspicious activity on the account
A notice arriving from elsewhere
An alert from a credit agency
preguntas.explicacion: Suspicious documents form one of the listed categories: a bearer who does not match the photograph or the description of physical appearance, details on the card that clash with what the person is saying, or an application that looks altered, forged, or reassembled after being torn up. Account activity and third-party notices are separate categories.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Personnel
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 3F4 k147 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: Where does the medical assistant's part in electrocardiography end?
opciones: At obtaining the tracing: the clinician reads and diagnoses
At reading the rate and rhythm: the clinician reads the rest
At flagging an abnormal wave for the patient to ask about
At writing a preliminary reading beneath the machine's own
preguntas.explicacion: In clinics and hospitals the recording is usually made by trained technicians and interpreted by clinicians, often confirmed by a cardiologist. Technicians are not expected to interpret, but they are expected to watch the tracing come out with a trained eye so lead problems are caught and fixed.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k117 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: Among the preanalytical quality indicators tracked by that emergency laboratory, which one affected the largest share of samples?
opciones: An inadequate blood-to-anticoagulant ratio, near 35 %
The presence of a fibrin clot inside the tube, near 28 %
An insufficient volume of specimen, near 22 %
Visible or measured hemolysis of the serum, near 2 %
preguntas.explicacion: Ranked against the indicator set of the IFCC working group on laboratory errors, the sample-to-anticoagulant ratio was the worst at 34.9 %, followed by fibrin clots at 27.9 % and insufficient volume at 22 %. Hemolysis and contamination from an intravenous infusion sat at 2.2 % each and lipemia at 0.1 %. Under-filling is what drives the first three together.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (pH)
preguntas.subtema: Alkaline stale urine · CPT D4 4G · PBT V.D.2 / V.A · CCMA 3D k117 · CMA I.C.10.a.(2) · RMA III.C.4.b · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen was left out overnight and the strip now reads a pH of 8.5. What is the most likely explanation?
opciones: The specimen is stale and bacteria have split its urea, releasing ammonia
The specimen is stale and bacteria have consumed all the glucose it contained
The patient has been drinking cranberry juice, which pushes the pH upward
The patient is on a high-protein diet, which pushes the pH upward as well
preguntas.explicacion: Urine pH normally falls between 4.5 and 8, most often 5.5 to 6.5, running slightly acid because of what metabolism produces. The commonest reason for an alkaline reading is an old specimen where bacteria have grown and broken urea down to ammonia. Bacteria metabolising glucose drive the pH down rather than up, and cranberry juice and a high-protein diet are both listed among the causes of acid urine.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4
preguntas.pregunta: Where does V5 go?
opciones: Directly between V4 and V6, in line with both
Directly between V3 and V6, in line with both
Directly between V2 and V4, in line with both
In the mid-axillary line, one space lower down
preguntas.explicacion: V5 is placed straight between V4 and V6, and the three should be linear. The mid-axillary line belongs to V6, and the gap between V2 and V4 is where V3 goes, so mixing the two rules up shifts several electrodes at once and changes the pattern the provider sees.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Issues of Concern: Electronic Health Records
preguntas.subtema: Paying out of pocket · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k35
preguntas.pregunta: A patient pays the full price of a test himself and asks that it not be reported to his health plan. What must the provider do?
opciones: Honor the request, since the care was paid out of pocket in full
Bill the plan anyway, because contracts require every claim
Honor it only if the privacy officer approves the exception
Ask the plan for permission before withholding the claim
preguntas.explicacion: Among the additions that came with the health information technology legislation, covered entities must acknowledge and fulfill a request that information not be shared with a health insurance plan when the individual has paid for that care out of pocket and in full. The same legislation requires an audit trail accounting for disclosures where electronic records are used, and gives patients an electronic copy of what those records hold.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.11 Checklist for Staple Removal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m · NCMA 2B.16
preguntas.pregunta: How is a staple extractor used on a surgical staple?
opciones: Slide the lower tip under the staple, close the handle without lifting, then rock it free
Slide the lower tip under the staple, lift as the handle closes, then pull it straight out
Grip the crown of the staple in the jaws, twist the wrist, then draw the staple upward
Grip both ends of the staple with forceps, squeeze them inward, then lift the staple away
preguntas.explicacion: The lower tip goes beneath the staple, and the handle is closed without pulling up and without changing the angle of the wrist or hand. Closing it presses the middle of the staple down so both ends bend outward and lift free of the skin; only when both ends show is the extractor moved away and the staple released onto sterile gauze.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Other Potentially Infectious Materials; StatPearls, "Universal Precautions", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: OPIM definition · CPT D1 k11 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.b · CCMA 3C1 k99 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.d · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which specimen counts as other potentially infectious material under the standard even when no blood is visible?
opciones: Cerebrospinal fluid from a lumbar puncture
Urine from a routine clean-catch collection
Sweat wiped from a feverish patient's brow
Tears from a patient with conjunctivitis
preguntas.explicacion: The definition of other potentially infectious materials in paragraph (b) names semen, vaginal secretions, cerebrospinal, synovial, pleural, pericardial, peritoneal and amniotic fluids, saliva in dental procedures, any fluid with blood visible in it, and every fluid whose type cannot be distinguished from those, plus unfixed tissue and HIV or HBV cultures. Spinal fluid is on that list outright. Sweat, tears and urine are not, and neither are feces, vomit, sputum or nasal discharge; they count as OPIM only once blood can be seen in them.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Deductible
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.6.e · RMA II.A.1 · CMAA 5C · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's plan has a $2,000 deductible. What does that number mean for the patient?
opciones: The patient pays the first $2,000 of covered services before the plan starts to pay anything
The plan pays the first $2,000 of covered services and the patient pays the coinsurance on the rest
The patient's monthly premium for the coverage is $2,000, whether or not any services are used
The most the patient will pay in the plan year for covered services, after which the plan pays 100%
preguntas.explicacion: HealthCare.gov defines the deductible as what the patient pays for covered care before the plan begins paying, and uses this very figure as its example: with a $2,000 deductible, the first $2,000 of covered services comes out of the patient's pocket, not the plan's. Once it is met, the patient usually still owes a copayment or coinsurance. The monthly payment owed whether or not care is used is the premium, and the yearly ceiling after which the plan pays 100% is the out-of-pocket maximum: two other glossary entries, two different numbers.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Eligibility, Medically Needy
preguntas.subtema: Financial eligibility · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 6 k83 · CCMA 5E k178 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's income is above her state's Medicaid limit, but her medical bills are enormous. Which route may her state offer her?
opciones: A medically needy program, where the expenses she incurs spend her income down
A premium tax credit, which lowers what she pays for a plan on the Marketplace
A sliding fee discount, which lowers what a health center charges her directly
The Medicare Savings Programs, which pay premiums and cost sharing for her
preguntas.explicacion: States may set up a medically needy program for people whose health needs are significant but whose income sits above the other eligibility groups. Such a person becomes eligible by spending down: she incurs expenses for medical and remedial care she has no insurance for, and once those exceed the gap between her income and the state's standard, Medicaid picks up what is above it.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Abdominal thrusts", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.d · 2027 I.B.8.d · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A choking adult loses consciousness while back blows and abdominal thrusts are being given. What comes next?
opciones: Lower the patient to the floor, start CPR, and look in the mouth first
Keep giving abdominal thrusts, now with the patient lying flat on the back
Raise the legs about 12 inches (30 cm) and wait for the ambulance to arrive
Give two rescue breaths and then check the pulse for up to 10 seconds
preguntas.explicacion: Abdominal thrusts are for the conscious victim; the moment consciousness is lost, chest compressions take over. The patient goes onto a firm flat surface, CPR is started, and the mouth is inspected for the object before each set of breaths, taking out only what can be seen.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 3.1.1, Vacuum extraction systems
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: In a vacuum extraction system, what is the role of the barrel, also called the tube holder?
opciones: It holds the tube steady and keeps the worker's hands away from the blood
It creates the vacuum that pulls the blood into the tube once the needle is in the vein
It retracts the used needle automatically in every model once the last tube is filled
It mixes the additive with the blood by rotating the tube as it fills
preguntas.explicacion: Section 3.1.1 describes a double-ended needle whose rubber-cuffed end screws into the barrel (the tube holder, also called an evacuated tube needle holder or a bulldog); the barrel holds the sample tube in place and keeps the worker out of direct contact with the blood. The vacuum is inside the tube itself, retraction into the barrel exists only in some systems, and mixing is done by inverting the tube afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Do Not Resuscitate", Function; and StatPearls, "Advance Directives"
preguntas.subtema: Medical directives · CCMA 7D k217 · CMA E.8.b / 2027 E.7.a · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: A family worries that signing a DNR means their mother will stop being treated. What is accurate?
opciones: Comfort care and pain management continue; the standard of care is not lowered
Only nursing care continues; medications and tests are stopped at that point
Care continues, but the patient must be moved to a hospice unit within a day
Care continues only while the attending physician renews the order each shift
preguntas.explicacion: The idea that a DNR means do not treat is a common misunderstanding. Choosing a DNR or comfort-measures-only status does not reject the rest of medical care, and a DNR order does not lower the standard of care: comfort and pain management go on, and easing suffering is always appropriate. Patients can also name which resuscitative procedures they accept and which they refuse.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Drug plan rules, Prior authorization
preguntas.subtema: Medication authorization · CMAA 4G k67 · CCMA 5H k183 · CMA III.G.5.a(2) · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A drug plan denies a medicine because it requires prior authorization. What does the prescriber need to send for an exception?
opciones: A supporting statement explaining why the drug is medically necessary for this patient
A supporting statement listing the other drugs the patient took over the past year
A copy of the plan's drug list with the requested medication marked on the page
A new prescription written for a drug from the lowest cost-sharing tier instead
preguntas.explicacion: An exception is the plan's decision to cover a drug that is off its list or to waive a coverage rule. The patient or the prescriber must request it, and the prescriber has to supply a statement supporting the request: that the drug is medically necessary for this patient despite the rule, that another drug would harm the patient, or that another drug would be less effective. Sending a copy of the list or simply switching drugs is not an exception request.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Premature Atrial Contraction", Evaluation
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: What marks a premature atrial contraction on the tracing?
opciones: An early P wave of odd shape with a normal QRS after it
An early P wave of odd shape with a wide QRS after it
An early wide QRS with no P wave in front of it at all
A missing P wave with the QRS arriving on time as usual
preguntas.explicacion: These beats start in atrial muscle outside the sinus node, so the P wave comes early and its shape and axis differ from the sinus P waves; it may be inverted or biphasic. The QRS is usually normal, and the PR interval can be shorter, longer or the same as in sinus beats.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Height Assessment", Equipment: Growth Chart Correction for Prematurity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.c · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A baby born at 30 weeks of gestation is now 6 months old by the calendar. How are the growth parameters plotted?
opciones: By corrected age, taking off the weeks born early, and so on until age 2
By corrected age, taking off the weeks born early, and so on until age 1
By calendar age, accepting that the first points will sit low on the curve
By calendar age, on a separate chart drawn for babies born before 32 weeks
preguntas.explicacion: Growth parameters are corrected for gestational age by subtracting the number of weeks the baby was born preterm from the age since birth. For a baby born before 32 weeks that correction runs until 2 years of age; for one born between 32 and 36 weeks it runs at least until 12 months. Corrected age is what places the child at the right point on the curve.

preguntas.fuente: AAMA, Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Standards for CMAs (AAMA), Procedures for Adjudicating Alleged Violations
preguntas.subtema: Unethical conduct · CCMA 7C · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: What is the certificant entitled to when a disciplinary complaint is opened?
opciones: Written notice of the basis, a chance to submit evidence, and an appeal
Written notice of the basis and a hearing before a panel of three peers
Written notice of the basis and the identity of the person who complained
Written notice of the basis, after which the sanction takes effect at once
preguntas.explicacion: The procedure gives the certificant or applicant written notice of the basis for discipline or for denial of eligibility, a chance to submit written evidence about the alleged violations, a decision taken by the certification director, and the chance to appeal that decision to a panel of appeals the certifying board has established. Cooperating with the investigation is itself required.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.4, Complications (adhesive strips)
preguntas.subtema: Bandaging and skin types · CPT D3 k73 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E9 k137 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.13
preguntas.pregunta: A frail 88-year-old has thin, fragile skin. What does the WHO say about adhesive strips in such patients, and how is the problem avoided?
opciones: Repeated strips can break down the skin in the very young and very old; use enough pressure and observe the site
Adhesive strips are mandatory for the elderly because their bleeding time is longer; apply two overlapping strips
Adhesive strips are avoided only in neonates; in the elderly a strip is applied and left for 24 hours
Adhesive strips are replaced by a pressure bandage wrapped around the arm for at least one hour
preguntas.explicacion: Chapter 7, in its list of complications, names skin that breaks down where adhesive strips are used again and again, above all in the very young and the very old, and says it can be headed off by pressing hard enough and by looking at the puncture site once the draw is over. Taped gauze or a bandaid over the gauze is the standard, not a wrapped pressure bandage.

preguntas.subtema: Documentation updates · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A practice rewrites its password policy after moving to a hosted record system. What else does the documentation standard ask of it?
opciones: Reviewing the documentation periodically and updating it as operations change
Keeping the version it replaced for ten years counted from the day of the change
Obtaining a written acknowledgment from each patient that the policy has changed
Filing an amended notice of privacy practices with the Secretary within 60 days
preguntas.explicacion: Security Rule documentation carries three required specifications: hold it for six years from when it was created or from the day it was last in effect, whichever is later; make it available to whoever has to carry the procedures out; and review it and bring it up to date whenever the environment or the operation changes. A newly hosted system is exactly such a change.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3514, Hazard Communication Standard: Safety Data Sheets, Section 11: Toxicological Information
preguntas.subtema: SDS section 11 · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A staff member asks whether a fixative used in the laboratory is a suspected carcinogen. Which section of its safety data sheet answers that?
opciones: Section 11, which reports the listings and the toxicity figures
Section 8, which reports the exposure limits and the protection
Section 2, which reports the classification and the signal word
Section 15, which reports the regulations that apply to the product
preguntas.explicacion: Section 11 gathers what is known about toxicology and health effects: the likely routes of exposure, the immediate, delayed and chronic effects of short and long term exposure, numerical measures of toxicity such as the LD50, the symptoms from the mildest exposure to the most severe, and whether the chemical appears in the National Toxicology Program report on carcinogens, in the IARC monographs, or has been found by OSHA to be a potential carcinogen.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(j)(1) and (j)(2), Disclosures by whistleblowers and workforce member crime victims
preguntas.subtema: Whistleblower disclosures · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7F k214 · CMA II.E.6 · RMA I.C.1.b · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k37
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist reports to the state health oversight agency that her employer is reusing single-use devices, and her report includes patient information. How does HIPAA treat this?
opciones: It is protected when made in good faith to a health oversight agency about unlawful conduct
It is a breach of unsecured PHI that the employer must report to HHS within 60 days of discovery
It is permitted only if the patients signed authorizations first
It is permitted only if made to the news media, which is exempt from the Privacy Rule
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(j)(1) shields whistleblowers: the rule is not broken when a workforce member or a business associate, believing in good faith that the entity has acted unlawfully, breached professional standards or put patients, workers or the public in danger, passes PHI to a health oversight agency, to a public health authority, to an accrediting organization, or to an attorney consulted about it. The same section covers a workforce member who is the victim of a crime and reports limited information about the perpetrator. The media are not on the list of protected recipients.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Broken bone", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k77 k78 · CMA I.B.9.g · 2027 I.B.8.g · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.13 EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: A patient falls in the parking lot and the forearm is deformed and very painful. How is it immobilized?
opciones: With a splint or sling that holds the area above and below the injury
With a splint that presses on the deformity to bring the bone in line
With an elastic wrap around the wrist alone, tight enough to stop movement
With the arm strapped to the chest after the bone is straightened first
preguntas.explicacion: A broken bone is splinted as it lies, and the splint has to reach past the break on both sides, above it and below it; a rolled newspaper or strips of wood will serve. Nobody without the training lines up a fracture or tries to straighten a bone. Ice packs and elevation reduce pain and swelling while the patient waits.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "SOAP Notes", Function: Subjective — Chief concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A3 · CMA I.A.4.a · RMA III.F.1.a · NCMA 2B.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient lists three reasons for the visit. How is the chief concern handled?
opciones: In the patient's own words, inviting them to state all of the concerns so the pressing one shows
As the single diagnosis that the assistant believes best explains the symptoms being reported
As the first symptom mentioned, because the opening statement is always the most significant
