As a summary written afterward, once the examination confirms which finding is abnormal
preguntas.explicacion: The reason for the visit is recorded the way the patient says it, and it may be a symptom, a condition or a previous diagnosis. The first thing mentioned is not necessarily the most important one, so the patient is encouraged to name every concern while the interviewer watches for the detail that reveals the compelling problem. A diagnosis is not a concern.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Korotkoff Sound", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · RMA III.E.2.c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: The Korotkoff sounds are very faint in a thin older patient. Which maneuver is described to bring them out?
opciones: Raise the arm overhead for 30 seconds, opening and closing the hand, then inflate
Raise the arm overhead for 5 minutes, keeping the hand relaxed, then inflate
Lower the arm below the heart for 30 seconds so the vessels fill before inflating
Press the stethoscope harder into the antecubital fossa while the cuff deflates
preguntas.explicacion: Holding the arm above the head for about half a minute while the patient opens and closes the hand five to ten times sharpens the systolic sounds without changing the measured pressure; the arm is then brought back down and the reading proceeds normally. Pressing hard on the diaphragm is listed instead as a source of error.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Glucose Tolerance Test", section Testing Procedures
preguntas.subtema: OGTT timing · CPT D4 4H (and D2 k45 time of day) · PBT II.G II.D · CCMA 3E k139 timed specimens · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: At what time of day should a diagnostic oral glucose tolerance test begin?
opciones: Between 7:00 and 9:00 a.m., after the overnight fast
Any time of day, as long as the 8-hour fast is complete
Between 12:00 and 2:00 p.m., two hours after lunch
Between 4:00 and 6:00 a.m., before the patient's breakfast
preguntas.explicacion: The OGTT is a morning test that must begin between 7:00 and 9:00 a.m.: the fasting sample is drawn, the 75 g load is taken over about five minutes, and the second sample follows two hours later. The starting time is one of the listed conditions, together with the overnight fast, the three-day unrestricted diet, staying seated and not smoking. A fast alone does not make an afternoon OGTT valid.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments, About and Responsibilities
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations · CPT D5 k90 laboratory requirements · NCMA 4.12 · RMA III.C.1 CLIA '88
preguntas.pregunta: Which three federal agencies share responsibility for the CLIA program?
opciones: CMS, the FDA and the CDC, each holding a different part of the program
CMS, the FDA and OSHA, each holding a different part of the program
CMS, the CDC and the DOT, each holding a different part of the program
CMS, the CDC and The Joint Commission, each with a different part of it
preguntas.explicacion: CDC works in partnership with CMS and FDA. CDC supplies analysis and technical assistance, writes technical standards and practice guidelines, monitors proficiency testing practices and runs the advisory committee; CMS issues the regulations in 42 CFR part 493 and certifies laboratories; FDA categorizes tests by complexity. The Joint Commission is a private accreditor, not a federal agency.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Distal (Medical Encyclopedia 002346)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A chart reads: the lesion is distal to the elbow. Where on the arm should you look?
opciones: Farther from the trunk than the elbow, toward the hand
Nearer to the trunk than the elbow, toward the shoulder
On the back of the arm at the level of the elbow itself
Deeper than the elbow joint, under the muscles of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: Distal describes a position in a limb farther from the point of attachment or from the trunk, and proximal is its opposite. The hand is distal to the forearm; the upper arm is proximal to the forearm. A lesion distal to the elbow therefore sits somewhere between the elbow and the fingers.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Nasal Swab, What happens during a nasal swab?
preguntas.subtema: Anterior nares self-collection · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.C.2 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(5)(c) · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is collecting her own anterior nares swab. Which mistake would spoil the specimen?
opciones: Holding the swab still in one spot of a single nostril for the whole collection
Rotating the swab in sweeping circles for 10 to 15 seconds in each nostril
Using the same swab in the second nostril with the same rotating technique
Sealing the swab in a sterile tube and then in the bag the provider supplied
preguntas.explicacion: For an anterior nares specimen the swab is rotated in four or five sweeping circles for 10 to 15 seconds, then moved to the second nostril and rotated the same way. Swabbing only one nostril, failing to rotate, or keeping the swab in a single spot all risk an inadequate sample. Afterward the swab goes into a sterile tube, which is closed and sealed in the bag provided.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Specimen Requirements and Procedure (Blood Specimens)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 · CCMA 3E14 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c(1)
preguntas.pregunta: A swab for viral culture must be shipped to a distant laboratory. At what temperature is it transported to preserve the virus until inoculation or molecular testing?
opciones: Frozen at −70 °C
Frozen at −20 °C
Refrigerated at 4 °C
At room temperature
preguntas.explicacion: Viral culture specimens travel frozen at −70 °C so that viral integrity survives until the culture is inoculated or molecular testing is done. The −20 °C figure is the freezer threshold for serum held for delayed serology, 2 to 8 °C is for serum awaiting prompt testing and for tissue sent to microbiology, and room temperature is reserved for CSF and body fluids whose organisms must stay viable for culture.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Orthostatic Hypotension", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k48 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient stands up and the systolic pressure drops 22 mm Hg within two minutes. What does that meet?
opciones: The definition of orthostatic hypotension: a systolic fall of 20 mm Hg or more
The definition of orthostatic hypotension: a systolic fall of 30 mm Hg or more
No definition, since only a fall in the diastolic value is counted on standing
The definition of a hypertensive response, which is a change of 20 mm Hg either way
preguntas.explicacion: Orthostatic hypotension is a sustained fall of at least 20 mm Hg systolic, or at least 10 mm Hg diastolic, within three minutes of standing after lying down. More than 95% of cases are identified on the systolic figure alone, which is why it is the value most often reported.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine collection - infants (003417), How the Test is Performed and Risks
preguntas.subtema: Infant cleansing direction · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(2)(e) · NCMA 2B.18
preguntas.pregunta: Before applying a urine collection bag, how should the infant's genital area be cleaned?
opciones: Front to back on a female infant, and downward from the penis tip on a male infant
Back to front on a female infant, and from the base of the penis upward on a male infant who is uncircumcised
With an antiseptic solution on both, as is done before passing a catheter
With two sterile wipes on the labia and one on the glans, as in the adult clean-catch
preguntas.explicacion: The area around the urethra is washed thoroughly: from front to back on a girl and from the tip of the penis downward on a boy. Antiseptic cleansing is the preparation for a sterile catheterized sample, which a provider collects when a urinary tract infection has to be ruled out, and the two-wipe routine is the adult instruction. The only common risk of the bag is a mild rash from the adhesive.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 16.2: Inhaled Medications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B5 k69 · CMA I.D.2.c(5) · RMA III.G.4.d(vii) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: A patient uses a dry powder inhaler that contains a corticosteroid. What should they do after each dose?
opciones: Hold the breath about ten seconds, then gargle and rinse the mouth with tap water
Hold the breath about ten seconds, then take the next puff with no pause between them
Breathe out into the device at once, then rinse the mouthpiece under hot running water
Wait five minutes without breathing deeply so the powder can settle in the airway
preguntas.explicacion: With a dry powder inhaler the patient exhales, seals the lips around the mouthpiece and inhales strongly and deeply, then holds the breath about ten seconds or as long as is comfortable and breathes out through pursed lips. Puffs are spaced one to five minutes apart. When the powder contains a corticosteroid, gargling and rinsing with tap water lowers the risk of a fungal infection in the mouth.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth documentation · CCMA 5 k190 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 5E · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: What must the record show after a visit conducted by video, according to the telehealth workflow?
opciones: That the encounter was a telehealth visit, with the matching billing code or modifier
That the patient waived her right to an in-person appointment for the same complaint
That the video was retained by the platform for the period the practice specifies
That the clinician held a license in every State where the practice has patients
preguntas.explicacion: Documentation appears among the steps of the visit itself: the encounter is written up as a telehealth visit, and when the claim goes in it carries either a billing code specific to telehealth or a modifier on the ordinary code. Evaluation comes next, collecting the patient's experience and her suggestions for making future visits better.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "SOAP Notes", Function: Plan
preguntas.subtema: RMA III.F.1.c · CMA I.A.4.i · NCMA 2B.5
preguntas.pregunta: Which content belongs in the Plan section of a SOAP note?
opciones: The testing needed and why, the therapy, the referrals and the patient education
The problem list in order of importance, with the reasoning behind each one
The vital signs, the laboratory data and the imaging gathered at the visit
The chief concern and the present illness set out in the patient's own words
preguntas.explicacion: The Plan is written problem by problem: which test is being ordered and what its result would change, which medication is needed, which specialist is being consulted, and what counseling or teaching the patient receives. The ordered problem list belongs to Assessment, the vitals and results to Objective, and the concern in the patient's words to Subjective.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Introduction and Beneficence (conflicts with respect for patient autonomy)
preguntas.subtema: Autonomy · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7C · CMA II.E.7 · RMA I.C.4.a · NCMA 4.6 · CMAA 3G k47
preguntas.pregunta: A competent adult refuses a blood draw and the phlebotomist does not proceed. Which ethical principle is being honored?
opciones: Autonomy, respecting the patient's right to decide about their own care
Beneficence, doing what is in the patient's medical best interest
Justice, spreading a limited supply fairly among the patients
Nonmaleficence, avoiding actions known to expose the patient to harm
preguntas.explicacion: Patient rights rest on a small set of ethical principles: valuing the patient's dignity, acting with goodwill to preserve life and autonomy, avoiding known harm, and distributing resources fairly. Respect for autonomy is the principle at work when a patient with capacity decides against advice; the clinician should still explain the reasons for the recommendation at the level a reasonable person would need, and document capacity, but the decision belongs to the patient. Beneficence is the principle that most often conflicts with it.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins", Structure and Function; and "Phlebotomy", Anatomy and Physiology
preguntas.subtema: Antecubital anatomy · CPT D2 k53 · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: Of the two main superficial veins of the arm, which one runs along the medial side, where it travels with an artery and a nerve?
opciones: The basilic vein of the arm
The cephalic vein of the arm
The median cubital vein
The brachial vein of the arm
preguntas.explicacion: The cephalic vein drains mainly the radial side of the limb and the basilic vein the medial side, and the phlebotomy chapter stresses the need to tell the median cubital vein from the basilic, which runs medially along the arm, because the basilic runs with the artery and nerve and a puncture there can be very painful. The WHO's Step 3 says the same of the basilic vein; the brachial vein is a deep vessel, not a superficial one.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Point of Service (POS) Plans
preguntas.subtema: Commercial plan types and referrals · CMAA 4G k67, 4 k61 · CCMA 5H k183 · RMA II.A.4 · NCMA 3.9
preguntas.pregunta: A new patient's card says POS. Before booking him with a cardiologist, what does the office need?
opciones: A referral from his primary care doctor, which this type of plan requires
A written waiver of liability, which this type of plan requires up front
A signed assignment of benefits form, which this type of plan renews each year
A copy of the drug list, since this type of plan ties tiers to specialists
preguntas.explicacion: Point of service plans charge the patient less inside the network and, like an HMO, require the primary care doctor to refer the patient before a specialist visit. A waiver of liability is the Medicare advance notice used when denial is expected, not a scheduling step. Assignment of benefits is an intake form that lets the plan pay the office directly, and the drug list sorts covered medicines into tiers.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026

preguntas.pregunta: A term in the Alphabetic Index sits inside parentheses. What does the coder take from that?
opciones: It is a nonessential modifier and may be present or absent without changing the code
It is a manifestation code and is always to be sequenced after the etiology code
It is a synonym or alternative wording offered to explain the title of the code
It is an incomplete term needing one of the modifiers that follow it to be assignable
preguntas.explicacion: Words set inside parentheses are supplementary: they may appear in a statement of the disease or not appear at all, and either way the code assigned is the same. Those are the nonessential modifiers. Brackets do two other jobs: in the Tabular List they carry synonyms and explanatory phrases, and in the Index they mark manifestation codes. A colon follows an incomplete term.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(g)(2)(v), Information and Training
preguntas.subtema: Training after task changes · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k109 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic introduces a new safety-engineered butterfly needle mid-year. The annual training was held four months ago. What does OSHA require?
opciones: Additional training covering the new exposure created, before the annual session comes around
No new training until the next annual session, because training is required only once a year
A full repeat of the annual training program, including the epidemiology of bloodborne diseases
A revision of the Exposure Control Plan in place of training, documented in the sharps injury log
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (g)(2)(v) calls for extra training whenever a change, a new task or a modified procedure, alters the occupational exposure an employee faces, and it lets that training be confined to the new exposures. A new device changes how the task is done, so the clinic cannot sit and wait for the next annual date, and it need not repeat the whole program either. The plan review of (c)(1)(iv) is a separate duty that also bites here, and the sharps injury log records injuries, not plan revisions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Monitoring; and eCFR, 42 CFR 493 Subpart I, Proficiency Testing Programs for Nonwaived Testing (eCFR vigente 2026-09-04)
preguntas.subtema: Trough timing · CPT D2 k45 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E k139 medication levels · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: An intravenous vancomycin trough is ordered for a patient at steady state. What is the correct collection window?
opciones: Within the 30 minutes before the next dose is given
Within the 30 minutes after the infusion has finished
Within the 2 hours before the next dose is given
Within the 12 hours after the previous dose was given
preguntas.explicacion: Serum trough concentrations should be obtained within 30 minutes before a dose is administered, with the patient at steady state, which is usually reached after the third dose. The target trough varies with the indication and commonly runs from 10 to 20 mcg/mL. Drawing after the infusion gives a peak instead, and the 12-hour rule belongs to lithium and to the transplant drugs.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B10 k78 · CMA I.B.9.m · 2027 I.B.8.m · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2B.12 EKB 14
preguntas.pregunta: A patient stepped on a nail this morning. Which detail decides whether a tetanus booster is raised with the provider?
opciones: Whether the last tetanus shot was more than 10 years ago
Whether the wound goes deeper than a quarter inch (0.64 cm)
Whether the puncture was rinsed within 5 minutes of the injury
Whether the wound bled freely or barely bled at all afterward
preguntas.explicacion: A puncture wound bleeds little but carries a higher risk of infection, and the provider is contacted if the patient has had no tetanus shot in the last 10 years; the vaccine is generally repeated every 10 years. Depth over a quarter inch, wounds on the face and wounds reaching bone are what raise the question of stitches instead.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Protected Health Information
preguntas.subtema: What counts as PHI · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.2 · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k35 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these, held by a medical office, is protected health information under HIPAA?
opciones: A patient's e-mail address stored with the record of a visit the office billed last month
The personnel file the office keeps on a receptionist in its role as her employer
A student immunization list held by a school district under the education records law
A journal article on hypertension saved in the practice's shared clinical reference folder
preguntas.explicacion: PHI means health information that identifies an individual and that a covered entity holds or transmits, in any medium; demographic data counts when it travels alongside information about care or payment. Among the common identifiers the rule names name, address, birth date and Social Security number. Two things are carved out expressly: employment records the covered entity keeps in its role as employer, and education records covered by FERPA.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Syncope", section Introduction; and "Vasovagal Episode", section History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Halfway through a draw the patient says, 'I feel hot and dizzy, and everything is going dim.' What do these symptoms represent?
opciones: The prodrome of syncope
The onset of a seizure
A povidone iodine reaction
Tourniquet hemoconcentration
preguntas.explicacion: Fainting may be preceded by dizziness, lightheadedness, sweating, nausea and disturbed vision, and the vasovagal chapter adds warmth, tunnel vision, ringing in the ears and profuse sweating. These warning signs call for the patient to sit or lie down quickly with the legs raised. Hemoconcentration alters laboratory values and produces no symptoms; iodine affects results, not the patient's vision.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Rhythm
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: A strip shows narrow complexes with no P waves and gaps between beats that follow no pattern at all. How is the rhythm described?
opciones: Irregularly irregular, the hallmark of atrial fibrillation
Regularly irregular, the hallmark of atrial fibrillation
Irregularly irregular, the hallmark of a first-degree block
Regular but slow, the hallmark of a junctional escape rhythm
preguntas.explicacion: Sorting the spacing comes before naming anything: gaps with no pattern are irregularly irregular. Together with narrow complexes and no discrete P waves, that is what identifies atrial fibrillation, because only some of the atrial impulses get through.

preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes and lengths · CPT D3 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4

opciones: Nineteen to twenty
Sixteen to eighteen
Twenty-one only
Twenty-three only
preguntas.explicacion: The row for nineteen to twenty gauge carries no entry for adults, for pediatric, elderly or small veins, or for neonates. Sixteen to eighteen is the donation row, twenty-one the routine adult choice, and twenty-three the row that brings in the winged set for the smallest patients.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 3, 5, 8 and 10
preguntas.subtema: Fill level · CPT D3 k51 k57 k59 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's order needs a citrate tube, a gold separator tube and a light gray fluoride tube. Which must be filled to their stated volume?
opciones: The citrate tube and the light gray fluoride tube
The gold separator tube and the citrate tube only
The gold separator tube and the light gray fluoride tube
All three, since every additive works at a fixed ratio
preguntas.explicacion: The requirement for a full draw is attached to three rows of the table: the citrate tube, the EDTA tube and the fluoride/oxalate tube, with a warning that a short draw in the last of these can haemolyse it. The separator tube carries no additive of that kind, only a gel.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", Specimen Requirements and Procedure; and PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Transport and preservation
preguntas.subtema: Urinalysis age limit · CPT D4 4F k84 · PBT V.D.2 / V.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k117 · CMA I.C.8.c.(1) · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2C.15
preguntas.pregunta: A routine urinalysis specimen was collected 30 hours ago and has been refrigerated the whole time. Can it still be tested?
opciones: No: past 24 hours a urine is no good for urinalysis, refrigerated or not
Yes: refrigeration at 4 °C preserves urine for urinalysis for up to 72 hours
Yes, for the chemical strip only; particles must be examined within 1 hour of voiding
No: refrigerated urine must be tested within 4 hours, the limit for leukocyte assessment
preguntas.explicacion: Urine changes as soon as it is voided, so it should ideally be examined within the first hour; if that is impossible it is refrigerated at 4 °C for at most 24 hours, and a specimen older than that is not acceptable for urinalysis. European guidance sets particle examination at under 1 hour at room temperature or under 4 hours refrigerated, which is where the 4-hour figure comes from, but it does not extend the 24-hour ceiling to 72.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Characteristics of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D3 k51 volume) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: How much blood does an adult male typically have, and what share of adult body weight is blood?
opciones: 5 to 6 liters; about 8 percent of body weight
4 to 5 liters; about 8 percent of body weight
5 to 6 liters; about 5 percent of body weight
8 to 10 liters; about 10 percent of body weight
preguntas.explicacion: Blood is roughly 8 percent of adult body weight; adult men average about 5 to 6 liters and women 4 to 5 liters. The 4 to 5 liter figure is therefore the female value, not the male one. A 10 percent figure does exist in this material, but as the share of the blood volume that sits in the systemic arteries at any moment, not as a share of body weight.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern; and 42 CFR 482.13
preguntas.subtema: Patient rights · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29 · CMAA 3D k32
preguntas.pregunta: What weight does a bill of rights published by a health care organization carry?
opciones: It is not enforceable on its own, unlike a right written into regulation
It is enforceable once the organization publishes it and posts it publicly
It is enforceable in the states that have adopted it into their own statutes
It replaces the federal patient rights whenever the organization is accredited
preguntas.explicacion: Various American health care organizations wrote their own bills of rights starting in the 1970s, and those documents are not enforceable in themselves. What makes a right enforceable is a body with the authority to enforce it doing so: the rights a hospital must honor come from regulation, such as the federal conditions on notice, decision-making, privacy and grievances.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Manually retractable syringes
preguntas.subtema: Safety-engineered devices · CPT D3 3M k54 k66 · PBT II.J VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: When can the safety mechanism of a manually retractable syringe NOT be used?
opciones: While the syringe holds blood and during the transfer into tubes
While the needle is still inside the vein and blood is flowing in
While the syringe is empty and before the venepuncture is started
While the device is held in one hand rather than in both hands
preguntas.explicacion: The mechanism draws the needle back into the syringe, which lowers the danger of a stick and stops the device being reused, but it cannot be activated while the syringe is full of blood or during the transfer of that blood. Self re-sheathing devices carry the same limitation.

preguntas.subtema: Notification recipients · CCMA 5 k179 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 7 k90 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Who is a hospital expected to reach with the electronic notifications it sends when a patient arrives at or leaves its emergency department?
opciones: The primary care practitioner the patient has, or the practice he names
Every provider who has treated the patient during the previous twelve months
The patient's health plan, which coordinates the rest of the care from there
The state health department, which forwards the message to the care team
preguntas.explicacion: Notifications go out when the patient registers in the emergency department, when he is admitted, and when he is discharged or transferred, and the hospital has to make a reasonable effort to send them to the applicable post-acute care providers and to the primary care practitioner or practice the patient is established with, or whichever clinician he names as primarily responsible.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Preventing Needlestick Injuries in Health Care Settings, Activities Associated with Needlestick Injuries and Figure 2
preguntas.subtema: When injuries happen · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Hospital surveillance data show that percutaneous injuries cluster in which two moments of the work?
opciones: About 38% happen during use of the device and 42% after use, before disposal
About 62% happen while the container is being replaced by housekeeping
Nearly all happen during disposal, once the device is inside the container
About one quarter happen during use and the rest while recapping needles
preguntas.explicacion: Injuries do not wait for the sharps container. Surveillance in participating hospitals puts roughly 38 percent of percutaneous injuries during the use of the device and 42 percent in the gap between finishing with it and getting rid of it. That is why safe handling has to be planned before the procedure starts. Among hollow-bore needle injuries the largest single cause is manipulating the needle in the patient, at 27 percent, with disposal-related causes at 12 percent and recapping down to 5 percent.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Your Rights Under HIPAA, Who Must Follow These Laws
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.E Professional Ethics, confidentiality · CPT D1 1C k13 · CCMA 7A k214 · RMA I.C.5 comply with HIPAA · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these organizations has to follow the HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules as a covered entity?
opciones: A clinic that bills insurers electronically for the laboratory tests it collects
A life insurer that keeps the results of the physicals it required of applicants
An employer that stores the pre-employment drug screens run on its new drivers
A school district that keeps immunization records on file for every student
preguntas.explicacion: Covered entities are health care clearinghouses, health plans, and health care providers who transmit health information electronically in connection with a standard transaction such as a claim. Employers, life insurers, carriers of workers compensation, most schools and most law enforcement agencies all hold health information about people, and none of them is covered by these two rules.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Elder Abuse", Introduction; and Treatment/Management
preguntas.subtema: Signs of abuse · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: An older patient arrives underweight and unwashed, with medications that were never refilled. Which category fits, and what follows?
opciones: Neglect, and the case is reported even though it is only suspected
Neglect, and the case is reported once the findings are confirmed
Financial abuse, and the case is referred to the hospital's legal team
Psychological abuse, and the case is handled by the social work team
preguntas.explicacion: Neglect is the caregiver's failure to meet obligations to the older adult: withholding food, water, clothing, medication refills or assistive devices. It shows up as being underweight or dehydrated, poor hygiene, dirty clothing and overgrown nails. Reporting is done even when the abuse is only suspected and not proven, so that Adult Protective Services can investigate.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Credentialing", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: Credentialing · RMA I.C.2.a · NCMA 4.1 · CMAA 3F k48
preguntas.pregunta: Which professionals have to go through credentialing at a health care institution?
opciones: Licensed independent practitioners who may provide care without supervision
Every employee of the institution who has any contact with patients at all
Only physicians and surgeons who intend to admit patients to the hospital
Only staff whose salary is billed to Medicare, Medicaid or a private insurer
preguntas.explicacion: Credentialing is required of any licensed, independent professional whom law and a licensing body permit to provide services without supervision, within the scope of that license. Holding a license does not mean a person may do any service they like. It used to be a hospital process; today ambulatory centers, long-term care institutions and urgent care clinics do it too.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Refusal of Care", section Definition/Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2F 2G k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c (both outlines) · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient refuses a blood draw. Which list gives the four components used to assess decision-making capacity?
opciones: Understanding, a clear and consistent choice, appreciation, and reasoning
Disclosure of information, competency, voluntariness, and full documentation
Orientation, short-term memory, attention span, and language fluency
Understanding, a signed refusal form, a witness, and a stable diagnosis
preguntas.explicacion: The four, in order: the patient shows understanding of the situation and the decision; expresses a clear, consistent choice; shows appreciation, that is, applies the facts to their own case; and reasons, inferring consequences and explaining the refusal. Forms and witnesses are not components, and disclosure and voluntariness are elements of research consent.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Evaluation of Coagulopathies", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 · PBT II.J III.A · CCMA 3E7 k135 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: A coagulation specimen reaches the bench looking cloudy and pink. Which appearances lead the laboratory to ask for another draw?
opciones: Marked hemolysis, lipaemia or icterus in the separated plasma
Marked hemolysis only, since fat and pigment do not interfere
A pale plasma layer, a small gel plug or a warm collection tube
A specimen that reached the bench in under two hours of the draw
preguntas.explicacion: Guidance for clotting assays is to discard specimens showing excess hemolysis, lipaemia or icterus, because all three interfere with clot formation or with the light the analyser reads. Most such errors start before analysis, which is why an abnormal result is repeated on a fresh sample.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 6.2.2, Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2N k49 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k127 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: How much may keeping an infant warm raise the rate of blood flow, according to the WHO?
opciones: By as much as sevenfold
By as much as twofold
By about one quarter
By as much as tenfold
preguntas.explicacion: Keeping the child warm can raise the flow of blood as much as sevenfold, which is why as few clothes as possible come off, an infant is swaddled in a blanket, and the parent or carer holds the baby with only the limb for the puncture left bare. Warm cloths laid over the puncture area help dilate the vessels as well.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: subpoena
preguntas.subtema: Legal terms · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c(1) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What happens if a subpoena to appear is ignored?
opciones: It may be punished as contempt, unless the material is privileged
It may be punished as a misdemeanor after a second notice is served
It is dismissed, because compliance is voluntary for medical staff
It is referred to the licensing board, which decides on the sanction
preguntas.explicacion: A subpoena is a written order compelling a person to give testimony on a subject at a stated time and place, or to produce documents or other tangible things, whether for a deposition, a trial, a congressional inquiry or another hearing. Failing to comply can be punished as contempt. If the testimony or the documents are privileged, the person is not required to comply.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 5
preguntas.subtema: Site preparation · CPT D3 3G 3H k63 k64 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E5 k130 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.8
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist has cleaned the site and is about to insert the needle. What is expressly forbidden at that moment?
opciones: Resting a finger on the vein to line the needle up
Asking the patient to make a fist so that the vein stands out more
Anchoring the skin with the thumb placed below the puncture
Waiting for the alcohol to dry before the needle goes in
preguntas.explicacion: After disinfection the site is not touched, and the example spelled out is placing a finger over the vein to steer the exposed needle. If the site is touched, the disinfection is repeated. Making a fist and anchoring below the site are both part of the correct technique.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Please sit down and make yourself comfortable
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k40 k48 · PBT II.B II.D · CCMA 3E1 k126 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which opening question does the WHO interview script use before it asks about fear of needles?
opciones: Have you ever had blood taken before, and how did it feel?
Have you had any food or drink within the last two hours?
Are you allergic to latex, to povidone iodine or to tape?
Have you ever fainted when your blood was being drawn?
preguntas.explicacion: The script seats the patient and then runs through a short set of questions: whether they have had blood taken before and, if so, how it felt and how long ago; whether they are scared of needles; allergies, with latex, povidone iodine and tape named; whether they have ever fainted during a draw; and whether they have eaten or drunk in the past two hours.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, FAQ 580: Medical record retention
preguntas.subtema: Record retention · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.e · CMAA 7A k39 · NCMA 4.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how long the practice must keep her chart under HIPAA. What is the accurate answer?
opciones: HIPAA sets no retention period for medical records; State law generally governs that
HIPAA sets six years, the same period it applies to its own policies and notices
HIPAA sets seven years from the date of the last service the patient received
HIPAA sets five years, the period Medicare applies to hospital medical records
preguntas.explicacion: OCR answers the question head on: the Privacy Rule lays down no retention period for medical records, and how long they are kept is generally a matter of State law. What the rule does demand is that safeguards of the administrative, technical and physical kinds protect the privacy of the records for as long as the entity holds them, disposal included. Six, seven and five years come from other rules.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(h)(2)(ii), Training Records
preguntas.subtema: Training record retention · CPT D1 1N k39 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k110 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.e · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: How long does the bloodborne pathogens standard require training records to be kept?
opciones: Three years from the date the training took place
One year after the last entry, like the extinguisher record
Thirty years beyond the end of the worker's employment
Six years from the date the record was last in effect
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (h)(2)(ii) fixes the period at 3 years counted from the date of the training session. The other numbers are real but belong to other rules: one year after the last entry is the retention of the annual maintenance record for portable fire extinguishers in 29 CFR 1910.157(e)(3); employment plus 30 years is the employee medical record in (h)(1)(iv); and six years is the HIPAA retention for policies and documentation in 45 CFR 164.530(j)(2).

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.4 Sterile Fields
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B2 k59 · CMA I.C.3.c (2027 I.C.3.c) · RMA III.D.2.b · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: In what order are the four flaps of a wrapped sterile kit opened?
opciones: The flap away from the body first, then each side flap, then the one nearest the body
The flap nearest the body first, then each side flap, then the one away from the body
Both side flaps first, then the flap away from the body, then the one nearest the body
The flap away from the body first, then the one nearest the body, then both side flaps
preguntas.explicacion: The far flap is opened first, touching only its very edge, then each side flap one at a time using one hand, and the flap closest to the body last. Opening the near flap last keeps the practitioner from leaning across what is already exposed, and already-opened corners are held so they cannot spring back into the sterile area.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.9 The Endocrine Pancreas, Cells and Secretions
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(9) (2027 I.C.6.f(9)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Within the pancreatic islets, which cells make insulin and which make glucagon?
opciones: Beta cells make insulin; alpha cells make glucagon
Alpha cells make insulin; beta cells make glucagon
Delta cells make insulin; beta cells make glucagon
Beta cells make insulin; delta cells make glucagon
preguntas.explicacion: The pancreas is mostly an exocrine gland, but its islets are endocrine. Beta cells, about 75 percent of each islet, release insulin when blood glucose climbs; alpha cells, about 20 percent, release glucagon when it falls. Delta cells make somatostatin, which holds both of the others back.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, When can I eat and drink normally again? and Can I drink anything besides water during a fast?
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2K 2M k46 · PBT II.B · CCMA 3E1 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A fasting outpatient asks what she should bring to her early appointment. What is suggested?
opciones: A snack, since feeling light-headed after a fasting draw is common
A sugary drink, to be taken half an hour before the first tube
A list of the tests, because the form is not sent to the station
No food at all, because eating waits until the results come back
preguntas.explicacion: Patients may eat as soon as the test is over, and because feeling light-headed after a fasting draw is common they may want to bring something to eat straight away. A sugary drink beforehand would break the fast: only plain water is allowed, and even flavoured carbonated water is ruled out because it may hold sugars or sweeteners.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Pulse Oximetry", Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k51 · RMA III.E.3 Blood Oxygen Saturation · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: An oximeter reading does not match the rest of the clinical picture. What quick step is described for checking the device?
opciones: Place the probe on the clinician's own finger to confirm the equipment is working
Restart the device, since the calibration is reset only when the power cycles
Change the probe to the opposite hand, because the reading always differs by side
Cover the whole limb, since ambient light reaching the skin is the usual culprit
preguntas.explicacion: When a value looks wrong, the probe can be put on the clinician's own finger to see whether the device itself is at fault. Ambient light does interfere, and the answer to that is to cover the probe or the site, not the whole limb. Readings should be followed as trends and acted on when they clash with the findings.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Sections 3.1.1 and 3.1.2
preguntas.subtema: Blood collection devices · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which devices make up the open systems of blood sampling?
opciones: Needles with syringes, and winged steel needles joined to a syringe
Needles with syringes, and winged steel needles joined to vacuum tubes
Vacuum tubes with a holder, and winged steel needles joined to a syringe
Vacuum tubes with a holder, and retractable lancets used on the fingertip
preguntas.explicacion: Open systems are the hypodermic needle with a syringe and the winged steel needle attached to a syringe. Closed systems, which are preferred because they have proved safer, are the ones where the blood goes straight into the tube without being transferred by hand.

preguntas.fuente: Cornell Law School LII, Wex: statute of limitations
preguntas.subtema: Legal terms · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4 · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas.pregunta: What does a statute of limitations do to a claim?
opciones: It bars the claim once a set period has passed after the injury
It caps the money a court may award once the claim is proven
It moves the claim from a state court to a federal court instead
It suspends the claim while the defendant's license is reviewed
preguntas.explicacion: A statute of limitations is any law that shuts the door on claims after a certain period has passed since an injury, and the length of that period depends on the jurisdiction and on the type of claim. The clock may start when the injury happened, when it was discovered, or when reasonable effort would have discovered it. Civil and criminal actions both have them.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337), Preanalytical phase studies recently published
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A serum sample shows no visible hemolysis, yet its plasma hemoglobin is just under 0.5 g/L. According to the study by Koseoglu and colleagues, which results can already be clinically altered?
opciones: LDH, AST, potassium and total bilirubin
Albumin, chloride, glucose and total protein
Amylase, alkaline phosphatase and uric acid
Triglycerides, magnesium and HDL-cholesterol
preguntas.explicacion: That study showed clinically significant differences from visually undetectable to moderate hemolysis for LD and AST, potassium and total bilirubin. Albumin, alkaline phosphatase, amylase, chloride, HDL-cholesterol, glucose, magnesium, CK, triglycerides, total protein, UIBC and uric acid also moved in statistical terms, but their bias stayed inside the conventional CLIA limits, which is where the three distractors come from.

preguntas.fuente: The Joint Commission, National Patient Safety Goals for the Laboratory Program (January 2026), NPSG.01.01.01, Rationale and EP 1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2E k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3A2 k43 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: An outpatient with no wristband arrives at the draw station. Which pair satisfies the two-identifier requirement?
opciones: The full name the patient states and the telephone number held on file
The full name the patient states and the number of the chair she uses
The assigned identification number, read twice off the requisition form
The full name on the requisition and the tests printed underneath it
preguntas.explicacion: The goal accepts a name, an assigned identification number, a telephone number or another person-specific identifier, and asks for at least two of them whenever specimens are collected for clinical testing. A physical location is expressly excluded, one identifier read twice is still one identifier, and the tests ordered are not among the identifiers the goal names.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Incidental Uses and Disclosures: General Provision
preguntas.subtema: Telephone messages · CCMA 6 k204 · CMA II.F.3 · RMA II.B.3.a · CMAA 7F k94 · NCMA 3.2
preguntas.pregunta: Staff leave a message on a patient's home answering machine about a lab result. What governs how much may be said?
opciones: The minimum necessary standard and the reasonable safeguards the rule requires
The accounting of disclosures, which must list the message before it is left
The patient's written authorization, needed before any message may be left
The rule on marketing communications, which limits unsolicited contacts
preguntas.explicacion: Messages left where somebody else may overhear them are the classic incidental disclosure: permitted as a by-product of a use the rule allows, so long as reasonable safeguards and the minimum necessary policies have been applied by the entity to the underlying disclosure. An incidental disclosure that follows from failing to apply either one is not permitted.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Lab Tests: Hemoglobin A1C (HbA1C) Test, What is a hemoglobin A1C test?; and StatPearls, "Blood Glucose Monitoring", section Diagnostic Tests
preguntas.subtema: Common tests · CPT D3 k57 D2 k47 · PBT II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks how one tube of blood can report her average sugar over months. What explains it?
opciones: Sugar binds to hemoglobin and stays put while the cell lives
Sugar is held in the plasma and stays there while the cell lives
The tube additive keeps the sugar steady for about three months
The laboratory averages every glucose result of the past year
preguntas.explicacion: Glucose in the blood attaches to the hemoglobin inside the red cells, and the higher the level the more of that hemoglobin ends up coated. A red cell lives about three months, so the coated percentage reports the average of the last two to three months instead of the level at the moment of the draw. A lifespan near 120 days is what both open sources give.

preguntas.subtema: Patient rights and restraint · CCMA k215 · NCMA EKB 29
preguntas.pregunta: What is never permitted when a restraint is ordered?
opciones: Writing it as a standing order, or on an as-needed (PRN) basis
Writing it as a modification to the patient's plan of care
Writing it by a licensed practitioner other than the attending
Writing it after less restrictive measures have been tried
preguntas.explicacion: Orders for restraint or seclusion may never be written as standing orders or PRN. They do go into a written modification of the plan of care, and they may come from a physician or another licensed practitioner responsible for the patient and authorized by hospital policy, with the attending consulted as soon as possible. They are only used after less restrictive interventions have failed.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results and Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's serum shows a very high hemolysis index and the CRP is rejected; a repeat heel sample two hours later has a low index and a reportable CRP. What does this pattern indicate?
opciones: The first hemolysis was in vitro, produced during a difficult collection, not by disease in the patient
The newborn has intravascular hemolysis that resolved spontaneously between the two collections
The first sample was contaminated by intravenous fluid, which diluted the C-reactive protein
The analyzer's hemolysis index was miscalibrated on the first run and corrected on the second
preguntas.explicacion: In the newborn series the hemolysis indices ran far above what is seen where a severe intravascular hemolysis has been documented, which pointed to in vitro damage from a difficult collection; every CRP rejected for severe hemolysis came back reliable on a repeat sample. A genuine in vivo process would not disappear in two hours, and the index is an automated measurement, not the part that failed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Cubital Fossa" (2023), section Physiologic Variants; and StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins" (2023), section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53) · PBT I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: No vein crosses the antecubital area at an angle; instead a prominent vein runs up the midline of the forearm and meets the basilic and the cephalic inside the fossa. Which recognized variant is this?
opciones: A dominant median antebrachial vein joining the basilic and cephalic
No communication at all between the cephalic and the basilic veins
A median cubital vein present, with the cephalic absent in the upper arm
Venae comitantes, the paired deep veins that travel with the arteries
preguntas.explicacion: Several patterns of the median cubital vein are recognized: the usual one, in which it links basilic and cephalic; one in which a large median antebrachial vein of the forearm is what meets those two inside the fossa; one in which the median cubital is present but the cephalic never develops in the upper arm; and one with no link at all between cephalic and basilic. Venae comitantes are the paired deep veins that flank the arteries.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Specimen rejection in laboratory medicine: Necessary for patient safety?" (Biochem Med 2015, PMC4622196), Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E k129 k139 · NCMA 2C.6 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d)
preguntas.pregunta: A cyclosporine level is ordered on a transplant patient. Which specimen does the laboratory accept for that test?
opciones: Whole blood collected in EDTA
Serum from a tube without gel
Heparinized plasma kept on ice
Serum separated and frozen at –20 °C
preguntas.explicacion: For cyclosporine monitoring only whole blood in EDTA is accepted. Serum without gel is what the source recommends for drugs such as phenytoin, ice and darkness are the methotrexate rule, and frozen serum is the storage advice for delayed serological testing, so each distractor is a correct instruction for another specimen. Specimen type is the first acceptability criterion a processor checks.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Issues of Concern; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 8
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k54 k59 · PBT II.H.1 II.F · CCMA 3E6 k132 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: Blood drawn into a syringe is being transferred into several tubes. Why does the sequence of tubes still matter?
opciones: Additive left on the needle can be carried into the tube filled next
The vacuum of each tube is spent in the sequence printed on its label
The plunger has to be pressed harder for every tube after the first
Serum tubes clot faster whenever they are filled after additive tubes
preguntas.explicacion: One route of contamination described for tube collection is anticoagulant sticking to the needle and passing into the next tube, so a transfer from a syringe is not exempt from the sequence. The order published by the WHO is given for vacuum tubes and for syringe and needle alike.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, ch. 18.5: Description of Procedure, and ch. 18.3: Needles
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B k73 · RMA III.G.2.j · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: An injection has just been given. What happens to the needle and syringe?
opciones: The safety shield goes on and the unit goes into a sharps container, uncapped
The cap goes back on with one hand and the unit goes into a sharps container
The needle is snapped off and the syringe goes into the ordinary waste bin
The unit is set on the tray until the visit is over and then carried to disposal
preguntas.explicacion: The needle is not recapped, because recapping is how people puncture themselves. The safety shield attached to the needle is applied instead, and the syringe and needle go into a sharps container. Gloves come off afterwards and hand hygiene follows. Many needles carry these shields precisely to prevent needlestick injuries, and prefilled syringes cut the same risk further back in the process.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", section Issues of Concern, Cultural Differences; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A 2F k17 k43 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a (both outlines) · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who says she has no immigration papers hesitates at the consent form. What does the guidance note here?
opciones: Fear of deportation can make patients hesitate to sign consent forms
Consent from a patient without papers must be witnessed by two staff
A verbal consent will not stand for a patient who declines to sign
The form is set aside and the draw is recorded in the chart as refused
preguntas.explicacion: Among the cultural differences that complicate consent, the text notes that someone without immigration papers may hold back from signing a consent form for fear of deportation. Consent is a process of communication rather than a signature, the WHO takes verbal consent for a routine draw, and hesitating over a form is not the same as refusing the test.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 one lancet, one puncture · PBT II.F technique · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: A first heel-prick yields too little blood. The phlebotomist wants to reuse the same lancet on the same spot. What is the rule?
opciones: Do not puncture more than once with the same lancet or reuse a site: it can cause bacterial contamination and infection
A second puncture with the same lancet is acceptable if the site is cleaned again with alcohol and allowed to dry
The same lancet may be reused once on the other heel, since the blade has touched only that patient's skin
Reusing the site is preferred, because a fresh puncture nearby raises the risk of osteomyelitis of the calcaneus
preguntas.explicacion: Two things are forbidden with a lancet: sticking the skin twice with the same one, and opening the same hole again. Either route invites bacteria and infection. A surgical blade is never used for a dermal puncture. Osteomyelitis of the calcaneus is a complication of the procedure, not an argument for reusing a site.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Informed Consent", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA II.E.3 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which practice is named as an improper way to obtain consent for a procedure?
opciones: Taking it while the patient is medicated or in the preoperative holding area
Taking it in the office days ahead, with time for the patient to ask questions
Taking it with an interpreter present when the patient's language differs
Taking it with the teach-back method used to check what the patient understood
preguntas.explicacion: Consent obtained shortly before the procedure, in the preoperative holding area, or from a patient who is medicated or nearly asleep is named as improper. The recommended setting is a clinic or office with time to ask questions and process emotions. Interpreters, including sign language interpreters, and the teach-back method are what make the process sound.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 7.1
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3O k71 finger selection · PBT II.E · CCMA 3E8 · NCMA 2C.10 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: For an adult finger-prick, which fingers are recommended, and which are avoided?
opciones: The middle and ring fingers; the thumb and index have calluses and the little finger has thin tissue
The index and middle fingers; the ring and little fingers are too close to the ulnar nerve branch
The thumb and index finger; the middle and ring fingers have the thinnest tissue over the bone
Any finger except the thumb; the little finger is preferred because it is the least sensitive
preguntas.explicacion: The table names the second and third fingers, that is the middle and the ring, as the ones to use. Thumb and index are left alone because callused skin gets in the way, and the little finger because there is too little tissue over the bone. The lancet enters the side of the finger pad, crossing the print lines rather than following them; in an adult the finger is the usual capillary site.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Recommendations: Selecting and Evaluating Needle Devices with Safety Features, step 2
preguntas.subtema: Setting priorities · CPT D1 1A k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which devices should a facility replace first when it plans which safety products to bring in?
opciones: Hollow-bore needles that enter a vein or artery
Solid suture needles used in the operating room
Glass capillary tubes used at the patient's side
Lancets used for finger and heel sticks in clinic
preguntas.explicacion: Priorities come out of data: how injuries are happening in that institution, which devices are in use there, and what local and national figures say about injury and disease transmission. First place goes to the devices that would do most to prevent infection at work, and those are the hollow-bore needles that enter veins and arteries, the ones carrying blood. The team deciding is multidisciplinary and includes the workers who handle the devices.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, Recommended order of draw
preguntas.subtema: Order of draw · CPT D3 3J k59 · PBT II.H.1 · CCMA 3E6 k132 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.7
preguntas.pregunta: A requisition asks for a CBC (EDTA), a prothrombin time (citrate) and a basic metabolic panel (serum separator tube). Using the WHO order of draw, in what sequence are the three tubes filled?
opciones: Light blue citrate, then the serum separator tube, then purple EDTA
Purple EDTA first, then the serum separator tube, then light blue citrate
Serum separator tube, then light blue citrate, then purple EDTA
Light blue citrate, then purple EDTA, then the serum separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Table 2.3 numbers the tubes from 1 to 10. The coagulation tube is number 3, the serum separator tube (red-gray tiger or gold) is number 5, and EDTA is number 8, so citrate comes first, the SST second and EDTA last among these three. Step 8 gives the reason for a fixed sequence: it prevents the additive of one tube from contaminating the next.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Workplace Violence", Treatment / Management
preguntas.subtema: De-escalation · CCMA 6I k208 · CMAA 2B k26 · NCMA EKB 22 · CMA F.1.f / 2027 F.1.f
preguntas.pregunta: Where do prevention and de-escalation sit in managing a patient who may turn violent?
opciones: First, with restraints held back as a last resort
Last, once a security team has already come in
First, but only after a supervisor authorizes it
Last, and only after chemical restraint is given
preguntas.explicacion: Management centers on prevention and de-escalation, with the fight-or-flight reaction as the last resort. Triage is early enough for de-escalation to begin, staff should be trained in it, and physical restraints used alongside chemical ones are likewise a last resort rather than a first move.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Permissive Exclusions; and OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A provider's license was revoked over her professional competence. What kind of exclusion may follow?
opciones: A permissive one, which OIG may impose and whose length varies
A mandatory one, which runs for a minimum of five years
A mandatory one, which lasts as long as the license is gone
None at all, since no criminal conviction has been entered
preguntas.explicacion: Losing a health care license for reasons of professional competence, performance or financial integrity is one of the grounds on which OIG may exclude, and permissive exclusions vary in length. The mandatory exclusions, with their floor of five years, follow convictions such as program fraud or patient abuse.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Advance Written Notices of Non-coverage (MLN006266)
preguntas.subtema: Advance Beneficiary Notice · CMAA 5 k77, 6 k85 · CCMA 5 k186 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: An office is clearing out old files. How long must a signed advance written notice of non-coverage be kept?
opciones: 5 years from the date the care was delivered, where no state rule demands longer
3 years from the date the care was delivered, where no state rule demands longer
5 years from the date the claim for that care was finally paid or denied
Until the claim is paid, after which the signed copy may be discarded safely
preguntas.explicacion: Notices are held for 5 years from the date care was delivered where no state-law requirement says otherwise, and every record is held, including those where the patient turned care down, refused an option or would not sign. The clock starts on the date of service, not on payment of the claim, and the record is not thrown out once the claim closes.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Maintenance of Homeostasis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k38 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1 · PBT I.B.4
preguntas.pregunta: A patient is exercising on a hot day. How does the blood help keep the core temperature from rising?
opciones: More blood is routed to the skin, where heat is lost to the surroundings
Blood is diverted away from the skin so the core keeps its heat
Plasma proteins act as buffers that hold the blood pH near 7.4
The kidneys release erythropoietin so more red cells carry the heat
preguntas.explicacion: Temperature control works as a negative-feedback loop: when the core warms up, more blood is sent to the cooler periphery, heat escapes through the skin vessels and the returning blood is cooler. On a cold day the opposite happens and blood is kept away from the skin to keep the core warm. Buffering pH is a separate homeostatic role of blood, and erythropoietin responds to low oxygen, not to heat.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary of Health Coverage and Medical Terms, entry Out-of-pocket Limit
preguntas.subtema: Insurance terminology · CMAA 5C k76 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient lists what she has paid this year and asks what counts toward her out-of-pocket limit. Which one does?
opciones: The coinsurance the patient paid for covered care given inside the network
The monthly premiums the patient paid to keep the coverage in force this year
The balance billed by a provider who charged above the plan's allowed amount
The cost of a service the plan lists among the benefits it does not cover
preguntas.explicacion: The out-of-pocket limit totals the patient's own share of covered services: what she paid as deductible, as copayments and as coinsurance on care inside the network. Once it is reached the plan usually pays the whole allowed amount for the rest of the year. Three things stay outside that tally by definition: premiums, amounts balance billed above the allowed amount, and care the plan does not cover at all.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 4.3 Aseptic Technique
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C7 k104 · CMA I.C.3.a (2027 I.C.3.a) · RMA III.A.1 · NCMA 2A.7
preguntas.pregunta: How do medical asepsis and surgical asepsis differ in what they set out to do?
opciones: Medical asepsis reduces pathogens as a barrier; surgical asepsis attacks every microorganism
Medical asepsis attacks every microorganism; surgical asepsis reduces pathogens as a barrier
Medical asepsis applies in the operating room; surgical asepsis applies at the bedside only
Medical asepsis covers hand hygiene alone; surgical asepsis covers every use of any glove
preguntas.explicacion: Aseptic technique, or medical asepsis, is the deliberate reduction of pathogens so they are not carried from one person or object to another, a protective barrier. Sterile technique, or surgical asepsis, goes further and aims to eliminate every microorganism in and around the field. It is the standard for surgery, for the care of a central line, and for wound management that goes below the skin.

preguntas.fuente: 42 CFR 493.1242(a), Standard: Specimen submission, handling, and referral
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5A 5D · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A new clinic laboratory is writing the manual for everything that happens before testing. Which item needs a written policy under the specimen submission and handling standard?
opciones: Specimen acceptability and rejection criteria
Calibration verification of the analyser
Competency assessment of the testing staff
Enrollment in an approved proficiency testing program
preguntas.explicacion: That standard sets out eight written policies, where each applies: preparing the patient, collecting the specimen, labeling it, storing and preserving it, the conditions of transport, processing, acceptability and rejection, and referral. Calibration verification belongs to the analytic systems, competency assessment to the general laboratory systems, and proficiency testing to a subpart of its own.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, section What types of blood tests require fasting; MedlinePlus, What You Need to Know About Blood Testing, section What are the different types of blood tests
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D II.G · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: A requisition lists a complete blood count, a lipid panel, a coagulation panel and a troponin. For which of these tests is fasting usually required?
opciones: The lipid panel
The blood count
The clotting panel
The troponin test
preguntas.explicacion: Fasting is usually required for a blood glucose, for cholesterol or lipid panels and for the basic metabolic panel, with liver function tests and the renal function panel sometimes added; triglycerides and calcitonin also appear among the tests that need it. A CBC, coagulation tests and cardiac enzymes such as troponin are not on that list, and no special preparation at all is needed for most blood tests.

preguntas.subtema: Reusable sharps · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: How must contaminated reusable sharps be stored while they wait for reprocessing?
opciones: So that no employee has to reach into the container by hand to retrieve them
Immersed in a 1:10 bleach dilution for at least 10 minutes in an open pan
In a red bag closed before removal, like other regulated waste
In a labeled container that is emptied by hand only when three-quarters full
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(4)(ii)(E) forbids storing or processing contaminated reusable sharps in any manner that would oblige an employee to put a hand inside the container holding them, and (d)(2)(viii) wants that container puncture resistant, leakproof on sides and bottom, and labeled or color-coded. Paragraph (d)(4)(iii)(A)(4) adds that reusable containers are never opened, emptied or cleaned by hand. A red bag is for soft regulated waste, and the 1:10 hypochlorite dilution is WHO's spill disinfectant, not a way of storing sharps.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Stroke", Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.k · 2027 I.B.8.k · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in the waiting room suddenly has a drooping face on one side, a weak right arm and slurred speech. What is done?
opciones: Call the emergency number at once and note the time symptoms began
Give aspirin and water and drive the patient to the clinic next door
Lay the patient flat with the feet raised and recheck in 15 minutes
Take a full set of vital signs first and then call the provider in
preguntas.explicacion: A stroke is a medical emergency and the single most important action is to call for emergency help right away, at the first signs. Muscle weakness of face, arm or leg on one side, numbness on one side, and trouble speaking or understanding speech are typical and they usually start suddenly and without warning.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vital Sign Assessment", Variability of Vital Signs in Older Adults
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k48 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: How is the patient positioned and timed for orthostatic blood pressures?
opciones: Supine for about 5 minutes, then measured again within 1 to 3 minutes of standing
Seated for about 5 minutes, then measured again 10 minutes after standing up
Supine for about 1 minute, then measured again immediately on standing up
Standing for about 5 minutes, then measured again after lying down for 3 minutes
preguntas.explicacion: The patient lies down for roughly five minutes and the pressure is taken again within one to three minutes of standing. The measurement is called for in older adults being evaluated for dizziness, fainting, falls or suspected loss of fluid volume, where the reflexes that defend pressure on standing are often impaired.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Limited English Proficiency (LEP), Your Right to Language Assistance Services
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2B k16 · CCMA 7A k214 · CMA F.1.c(3) / 2027 F.1.d(4) · RMA I.D.1.d · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Under which two federal laws does HHS OCR say HHS-funded programs must provide language access services free of charge?
opciones: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 1557 of the ACA
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act together with the ADA
HIPAA and the Americans with Disabilities Act Amendments Act (ADAAA)
EMTALA and Title X of the Public Health Service Act (family planning)
preguntas.explicacion: Two federal laws require language access services at no charge in programs receiving HHS funds: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act, each with implementing regulations. Title VII and the ADA are anti-discrimination laws cited elsewhere; EMTALA and Title X govern emergencies and minors.

preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.F Laboratory Regulations · CPT D1 1C k13 · CCMA 7E k220 release of information · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: A patient's husband telephones the laboratory for her results, saying he will pass them along to her. What does CLIA require?
opciones: Release results only to authorized persons and to those responsible for using them
Release results to any adult of the household once his identity has been confirmed
Release results to him if the patient named him in the notice of privacy practices
Release results to him, because a spouse counts as the patient's personal representative
preguntas.explicacion: Test results go only to authorized persons, that is, to whoever state law lets order a test or take its results, plus whoever is responsible for using them and the laboratory that requested the test. The one widening is the patient's own access: on request, a laboratory may hand the completed reports it can authenticate as hers to the patient herself, or to her personal representative.

preguntas.fuente: Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect (May 2023), Professionals Required To Report; and Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect - State Statutes
preguntas.subtema: Mandatory reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · CMA E.6.c / 2027 E.5.b · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: Are health care workers mandatory reporters of suspected child maltreatment?
opciones: Yes, in every state except the four that instead require everyone to report
Yes, but only in the states that also require training for those reporters
No, unless the child is a patient of that clinician's own practice already
No, the duty falls on the head of the facility, who files on their behalf
preguntas.explicacion: Physicians, nurses and other health care workers are named as mandated reporters in 46 states plus the District of Columbia and several territories. The four missing ones, Wyoming, North Carolina, New Jersey and Indiana, do not list professions at all, because they require every person to report. Training requirements exist in some states and change nothing about who must report.

preguntas.fuente: NIH, Office of Dietary Supplements: Vitamin B12 — Consumer
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 4 k161 nutrition education · CMA I.A.6.g(1)(e) · 2027 I.A.6.g(1)(e) · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who eats a strict vegan diet asks which vitamin she is most likely to fall short on. Which one, and why?
opciones: Vitamin B12, because only animal foods carry it naturally
Vitamin B12, because plant foods block its absorption in the gut
Folate, because only animal foods carry it naturally
Vitamin C, because cooked plant foods lose almost all of it
preguntas.explicacion: Vitamin B12 sits in a wide range of animal foods; plant foods hold none unless they have been fortified, so people who eat little or no animal food may fall short, and so may their infants when they are pregnant or breastfeeding. The adult recommended amount is 2.4 micrograms a day.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse (MLN4649244), Open Payments Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which program makes drug and device manufacturers report publicly what they pay physicians and teaching hospitals?
opciones: Open Payments, whose data goes up by the end of June each year
The exclusion list, which OIG refreshes at the start of a month
The compliance guidance, which the industry follows voluntarily
The designated health services code list, kept for the Stark law
preguntas.explicacion: The Open Payments program requires manufacturers of drugs, devices and biologics to report nearly every payment or transfer of value made to physicians, to certain practitioners who are not physicians and to teaching hospitals, together with ownership interests, and CMS posts the data by 30 June each year. Covered recipients are encouraged, not required, to review their entries.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200(f)(7), Workplace labeling
preguntas.subtema: Signs instead of labels · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: May an employer use a sign or a placard instead of putting a label on a fixed process container?
opciones: Yes, if it names the containers it covers and is available each shift
Yes, if the container is emptied and refilled at least once a week
No, every container of a hazardous chemical must carry its own label
No, unless the safety data sheet is posted beside the container
preguntas.explicacion: For an individual stationary process container the employer may post a sign or a placard, or lean on batch tickets, process sheets, operating procedures and similar written material, rather than affixing a label. Two conditions ride along: the alternative has to say which containers it applies to and carry the same information a workplace label would, and that written material has to stay within the employees' reach in their work area throughout every shift.

preguntas.subtema: Research consent · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.a · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Under the federal rule on research consent, what must a subject be told about withdrawing?
opciones: That leaving at any point costs no benefit they were entitled to
