That leaving is allowed once the study's enrollment period has closed
That leaving requires the review board to approve the request first
That leaving forfeits any compensation paid for visits already made
preguntas.explicacion: Among the basic elements of research consent is a statement that taking part is voluntary, that refusing carries no penalty or loss of benefits the subject was otherwise entitled to, and that they may stop at any time on the same terms. Nothing in the rule makes withdrawal wait for board approval or tie it to the enrollment calendar.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: Implementation of This Model
preguntas.subtema: Appointment lengths · CMAA 4A k51 k52 · CCMA 5B k173 · CMA III.H.1.a-b · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A practice simplifying its appointment book asks how many different appointment lengths it should keep. What does the improvement guide suggest?
opciones: Two, short and long, with a long appointment worth roughly two short ones
Three, short, standard and long, one for each of the three appointment types
One, since the guide asks that every appointment be made exactly the same length
Four, one for each appointment type plus a longer slot reserved for new patients
preguntas.explicacion: The advice is to cut the number of appointment types down to three — personal, team and unestablished — so as to minimize complexity, and to make them all roughly the same length. Length itself is then reduced to two options, short and long, where a long appointment is about the equivalent of two short ones.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: An entry in the alphabetic index ends with a dash. What is the coder being told?
opciones: More characters are needed, and only the tabular list has them
The entry is a manifestation code that has to be sequenced second
The code is invalid and another main term has to be looked up
The entry carries an excludes note over in the tabular list
preguntas.explicacion: The index does not always give the full code. A dash at the end of an index entry says that more characters are required, and laterality or an applicable seventh character can only be picked up in the tabular list. Even where no dash appears, the tabular list still has to be checked to see whether a seventh character is required.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cryotherapy in Dermatology", Continuing Education Activity
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B13 k80 · CMA I.C.4.c (2027 I.C.4.c) · RMA III.D.2.a · NCMA 2B.11
preguntas.pregunta: A patient treated with liquid nitrogen asks what the treated spot will do over the next days. What is expected?
opciones: Redness, blistering and crusting, with healing over several weeks
Redness and swelling only, with healing complete within about two days
Immediate blanching that fades in an hour, with no visible change afterward
A firm painless nodule that grows for a week and then resolves on its own
preguntas.explicacion: Erythema, blistering and crusting are the expected responses after cryotherapy, and healing usually takes several weeks by secondary intention. The complications worth counseling about are loss of pigment, scarring, nerve injury and recurrence, which is why undertreating a benign lesion is preferred: what persists can be treated at another visit.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Preanalytical phase - a continuous challenge for laboratory professionals" (Biochem Med 2012, PMC4062337), Preanalytical phase studies recently published
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3E k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A laboratory proposes to keep reporting potassium on hemolysed samples by applying a correction formula based on the hemolysis index. What did the follow-up study on this idea conclude?
opciones: Corrective formulas are unreliable and misleading, because cell contents are not released uniformly
Corrective formulas are reliable for potassium and LDH but not for AST and total bilirubin
Corrective formulas work only when the hemolysis is visually undetectable, below 0.5 g/L
Corrective formulas are acceptable if the corrected result is flagged as an estimate in the report
preguntas.explicacion: Following the study that graded hemolysis, Lippi and colleagues showed that formulas meant to adjust results for the degree of hemolysis are unreliable and potentially misleading, because the mechanical injury of blood cells and the release of their contents into serum or plasma do not happen homogeneously. The answer to a hemolysed potassium is a new sample, not an arithmetic correction, flagged or not.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(ix) and (d)(2)(x), Engineering and Work Practice Controls
preguntas.subtema: Work practice controls at the bench · CPT D1 k31 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist keeps a water bottle at the draw station and applies lip balm between patients. Which rule applies?
opciones: Eating, drinking and applying lip balm are all prohibited where exposure is reasonably likely
Drinking is allowed from a closed container, but cosmetics and lip balm are prohibited
Both are allowed if the counter is decontaminated with disinfectant at the end of the shift
Both are allowed as long as the water is not stored in a refrigerator with specimens
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(ix) bans eating and drinking, smoking, handling contact lenses, and applying cosmetics or lip balm, anywhere occupational exposure can reasonably be expected. A closed bottle is not an exception the standard grants. The end-of-shift decontamination in (d)(4)(ii)(A) is a housekeeping duty and licenses nothing at the bench, and (d)(2)(x), which keeps food and drink out of refrigerators and off countertops where blood is kept, is a second and separate prohibition.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", sections Preparation and Technique or Treatment; and WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 6
preguntas.subtema: Tourniquet time · CPT D3 3E k60 k67 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.11
preguntas.pregunta: Ninety seconds have passed with the tourniquet on and the phlebotomist still cannot find a vein. What should happen next?
opciones: Release the band before two minutes and look again with a vein illuminator
Keep the band on until a vein appears, then draw all the tubes without pause
Tighten the band further until the radial pulse disappears at the wrist
Release the band and draw from the peripheral access line already in place
preguntas.explicacion: One guideline asks for the band to come off within a minute of placement and another sets the ceiling at two minutes, so at ninety seconds it is released. Illumination devices are recommended in place of a long application for veins that are hard to see, especially when two or more tubes are due.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations
preguntas.subtema: Consent versus authorization · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.3 · RMA I.C.1.a · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A practice asks new patients to sign a consent for use of their information in treatment, payment and operations. What is the status of that form?
opciones: Voluntary, and it does not substitute for an authorization where one is required
Mandatory, since the rule requires written consent before any treatment begins
Mandatory, and it doubles as the acknowledgment of the notice of privacy practices
Voluntary, but once signed it permits every disclosure the practice may wish to make
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity may choose to obtain consent for treatment, for payment and for health care operations, but nothing obliges it to, and one that does has complete discretion over how the process runs. A consent document is not valid permission where the rule demands an authorization instead, nor where the rule attaches other conditions to the use or disclosure.

preguntas.subtema: Record completion · CCMA 5 k174 · CMA III.H.3.a · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 7A · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Within what period after discharge must the hospital medical record be completed with a final diagnosis?
opciones: Thirty days following discharge
Twenty-four hours following discharge
Ninety days following discharge
Five years following discharge
preguntas.explicacion: The content standard closes with the final diagnosis and completion of the medical record within 30 days following discharge. The 24 hour figure belongs to the history and physical, which must be in the record within a day of admission and before anesthesia; five years is the minimum retention period for the record once it is complete.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship, Ethical Duties Relevant to Termination of the Therapeutic Relationship
preguntas.subtema: Mediation before dismissal · CMAA 4F k60 · CCMA 5A k170 · CMA III.H.1.e · RMA II.B.2.b · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: Attempts to repair the relationship with a patient who keeps missing appointments have come to nothing. Which step does the guidance place before termination?
opciones: Formal mediation by an ombudsperson, a professional mediator or a hospital ethics committee
Formal review by the state medical board, which rules on whether a dismissal is justified
A written warning setting out how many further missed visits will end the relationship
Notice to the insurer, which decides whether the patient may be dropped from the panel
preguntas.explicacion: Conflict resolution is expected to start by exploring the reasons underneath the disagreement and setting reasonable, clear expectations for the relationship going forward. Where those efforts fail, the step to consider is formal mediation by an ombudsperson, a professional mediator or a hospital ethics committee. Only where the conflict proves intractable does the standard notification procedure begin.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: Preventing syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · D2 2N · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Why are the armrests of the patient's chair adjusted before an outpatient draw?
opciones: So the worker can act quickly if the patient has a vasovagal reaction
So the tourniquet can be anchored on the rest instead of the arm
So the tray of tubes can be balanced within the patient's reach
So the arm stays below heart level throughout the whole procedure
preguntas.explicacion: The chair is expected to be comfortable for both people, with the armrests set to a convenient position that also allows appropriate action if the patient has a vasovagal episode. Preparedness of that kind matters most in the patients who admit to fainting during earlier tests.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, CAHPS Ambulatory Care Improvement Guide, Strategy 6A: The Intervention
preguntas.subtema: Open access scheduling · CMAA 4A k51 · CCMA 5A k172 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a.i · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A caller with a routine problem is told the next opening is six weeks away, and the practice is considering open access. What does that model do?
opciones: It offers every caller a slot on the day of the call, almost always with her own physician
It sorts callers by how urgent the problem sounds and books routine ones into a later week
It reserves about half of each day for the follow-up visits clinicians asked for in advance
It lets plan members go straight to a specialist, since the gatekeeper has been removed
preguntas.explicacion: Open access, also called advanced access or same-day scheduling, gives patients a slot the day they call, usually with their own clinician. Roughly half the day is left open; the rest holds clinically necessary follow-ups and the patients who preferred another day, normally no more than a quarter. The same words also name the removal of HMO gatekeepers, which is a different idea.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, row 10
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and additives · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.J II.G · CCMA 3E3 k136 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A glucose specimen will not reach the laboratory for two days. What does the additive in the gray top tube provide?
opciones: It is antiglycolytic and preserves the glucose for up to five days
It is antiglycolytic and preserves the glucose for up to twelve hours
It activates clotting so the glucose stays with the separated serum
It inactivates thrombin so the glucose stays with the plasma fraction
preguntas.explicacion: The light gray tube holds sodium fluoride with potassium oxalate. The oxalate binds calcium and stops clotting, and the fluoride is the antiglycolytic agent credited with preserving glucose for as much as five days. Clot activation belongs to the red tube and thrombin inactivation to the heparin tubes.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sinus Bradycardia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: A strip is regular at 48 per minute with a P wave ahead of every QRS. What does that fit?
opciones: Sinus bradycardia, since the pace still starts at the sinus node
Sinus arrhythmia, since the pace still starts at the sinus node
A first-degree block, since a P wave precedes every QRS
Atrial fibrillation, since the ventricular rate is slow
preguntas.explicacion: Every feature of sinus rhythm is present except the rate, which sits below 60, and that is what sinus bradycardia means. A first-degree block is defined by a PR interval past 200 ms rather than by the rate, and atrial fibrillation has no identifiable P waves at all.

preguntas.fuente: Child Welfare Information Gateway, Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse and Neglect (May 2023), Institutional Responsibility To Report
preguntas.subtema: Mandatory reporting · CCMA 7F k222 · NCMA 4.10 · CMAA 3E k43
preguntas.pregunta: A hospital policy says staff must tell the department head, who then calls child protective services. Does that policy discharge the staff member's duty?
opciones: In many states no: internal policy does not relieve the reporter
Yes, once the notification to the department head is documented
Yes, because institutional reporting replaces individual reporting
Yes, in the nine states where the institution's head files the report
preguntas.explicacion: States handle institutional reporting differently: in some the staff member notifies the head of the institution, in some the head then files, and in others the person reports to the child protection authority first and tells the institution afterwards. What 17 states and two other jurisdictions make explicit is that whatever the organization's policy says, the mandatory reporter is not relieved of the duty.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medical Error Reduction and Prevention", Function: Analyzing Root Causes and Sentinel Events
preguntas.subtema: Incident reporting · CCMA 7F · NCMA 4.8 · CMAA 3E k44
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is a sentinel event?
opciones: A surgical instrument left inside the patient and found afterwards
A near miss intercepted by the pharmacist before the dose was given
A latent equipment fault found during preventive maintenance rounds
An adverse drug reaction that the patient's chart already warned about
preguntas.explicacion: A sentinel event is an occurrence, unexpected, that involves death or serious injury of body or mind, or the risk of one. The published list runs to an object left inside a patient once the operation is over, procedures on the wrong patient or the wrong site, abduction, a child discharged to the wrong family, and a hemolytic transfusion reaction. Each triggers an immediate investigation.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.2.2 Prepare the skin
preguntas.subtema: CPT D3 3G 3O k71 antiseptic for dermal puncture · PBT II.F technique · CCMA k130 cleansing · NCMA 2C.8 site preparation · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(e)
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse hands you povidone iodine to prepare a 2-year-old's finger for a capillary puncture. What is the correct action?
opciones: Do not use povidone iodine for capillary punctures in children; apply alcohol and let it air dry
Use povidone iodine, since alcohol is not effective against skin flora on a child's finger
Use povidone iodine only on the heel; on the finger either antiseptic is acceptable
Use chlorhexidine instead, which the WHO prefers over alcohol for children under 2 months
preguntas.explicacion: Povidone iodine has no place in a dermal puncture on a child or a newborn; the skin is cleaned with alcohol and left to dry, exactly as in an adult. Chlorhexidine is the antiseptic ruled out under 2 months of age, and that rule belongs to venepuncture rather than to the lancet.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(i); OSHA, Bloodborne Pathogens and Needlestick Prevention: Evaluating and Controlling Exposure
preguntas.subtema: Order of controls · CPT D1 k31 k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C1 k97 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas.pregunta: According to paragraph (d)(2)(i) of the standard, when is personal protective equipment required?
opciones: When occupational exposure remains after engineering and work practice controls are in place
Instead of engineering controls, when the employer documents that safer devices cost more
Only when an exposure incident has already occurred and follow-up is under way
Before engineering controls are considered, as the first line of protection
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(i) sets the order: engineering and work practice controls come first, to remove exposure or cut it down, and PPE is added where exposure survives them. OSHA's page on evaluating and controlling exposure reads that to mean the employer has to look at an effective control fit for the clinical setting, a safety-engineered sharp for instance, and put it in place; the text grants no exemption for cost. PPE is preventive, not something that begins after an incident.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Supraventricular Tachycardia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which features describe a supraventricular tachycardia?
opciones: A narrow QRS under 120 ms with a rate above 100 a minute
A wide QRS over 120 ms with a rate above 100 a minute
A narrow QRS under 120 ms with a rate below 60 a minute
A narrow QRS under 120 ms arising below the His bundle
preguntas.explicacion: The term covers the fast rhythms that start at or above the atrioventricular node. The narrow complex is the giveaway: it means the ventricles were activated through the normal pathway from above the His bundle. Rates in adults run over 100 and often between 150 and 220.

preguntas.fuente: HealthIT.gov, SAFER Guide: Contingency Planning, Recommended Practice 2.1
preguntas.subtema: Downtime drills · CCMA 5 k191 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.6.b · CMAA 7 k101 · NCMA 3.5
preguntas.pregunta: Staff have never worked a shift on paper. Which training practice does the contingency guidance recommend to fix that?
opciones: Unannounced downtime drills held at least once a year for the whole staff
A yearly written test on the downtime policy graded by the security official
A refresher whenever the record system is upgraded by its own developer
A briefing given to every new hire during the first week of employment
preguntas.explicacion: At any moment an organization is likely to have staff who have never worked in a paper-based environment. The guidance answers that with training requirements, paper-based ordering and charting practice, and downtime drills held without warning at least once a year, so people meet the situation before it is real.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Medication Routes of Administration", Indications: Sublingual and Buccal Routes
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k20 · CMA I.D.2.c(3) · RMA III.G.4.d(v) · NCMA 1.9
preguntas.pregunta: Nitroglycerin for angina is placed under the tongue instead of being swallowed. What is the reason?
opciones: More than 90% of a swallowed dose is cleared in a single pass through the liver
A swallowed tablet would irritate the lining of the stomach and the small intestine
Sublingual tissue absorbs slowly, which stretches out the effect of every dose
Swallowed nitroglycerin is destroyed by acid before it reaches the small intestine
preguntas.explicacion: Sublingual and buccal drugs diffuse into the venous blood of the mouth, which drains into the superior vena cava rather than the hepatic portal vein, so the first-pass effect is avoided. Nitroglycerin is the standard example: more than 90% of it is cleared in one pass through the liver, so a swallowed tablet would leave almost nothing. The permeable mucosa also makes the onset fast, and the tablet can be removed if needed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Electrocardiogram", Clinical Significance: Rate
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k155 k156 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: Counting between two R waves on a regular strip gives four large squares. What rate does that work out to?
opciones: 75 per minute, from 300 divided by the large squares
60 per minute, from 300 divided by the large squares
80 per minute, from 400 divided by the large squares
100 per minute, from 400 divided by the large squares
preguntas.explicacion: On a regular rhythm the rate is 300 divided by the number of large squares between two R waves, so four large squares give 75 beats per minute. That value sits inside the normal band of 60 to 100, so it is neither bradycardia nor tachycardia.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, MMWR Recommendations and Reports 54(RR-13), Good Laboratory Practices for Waived Testing Sites, Personnel and Training
preguntas.subtema: PBT VI.C Competency Assessment · NCMA 4.12 comply with CLIA
preguntas.pregunta: In a site that holds only a certificate of waiver, what does CLIA require of the education and training of the director and the testing personnel?
opciones: It sets no education or training requirement for either the director or the testing personnel
It asks for a high school diploma plus documented training before patient specimens are analyzed
It asks for the same competency evaluation, twice in year one and yearly after, as elsewhere
It asks whoever is named director to hold an associate degree in some laboratory science
preguntas.explicacion: Waived sites are the gap in the personnel rules: CLIA imposes no education or training requirement on the director or on the people running the tests there. Surveys of those sites found physicians directing most of them and nurses and medical assistants doing most of the testing, with trained laboratorians a small minority. The diploma-plus-training floor starts at moderate complexity.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Antihistamines", Indications and Mechanism of Action
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.a · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which condition is treated with an H2 receptor antagonist rather than with an H1 antagonist?
opciones: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
Allergic rhinitis with sneezing
Chronic urticaria with hives
Pruritus from histamine release
preguntas.explicacion: The two receptor subtypes are treated by two different groups of drugs. H1 antagonists cover allergic disease, whether IgE mediated or not: allergic rhinitis, chronic urticaria, and the itching, vasodilation and swelling that histamine produces. H2 antagonists cut gastric acid secretion, which is why they are used in reflux and in functional dyspepsia, and why they are combined with a proton pump inhibitor for tighter control.

preguntas.fuente: NIOSH, Alert 2000-108, Devices Associated with Needlestick Injuries and Figure 1
preguntas.subtema: Devices behind the injuries · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k123 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which devices account for most of the percutaneous injuries hospitals report to national surveillance?
opciones: Hollow-bore needles, above all hypodermic and winged-steel needles
Suture needles, followed by the scalpel blades used in minor surgery
Glass items, above all broken capillary tubes and specimen slides
Retractable lancets used for the finger and heel sticks of the day
preguntas.explicacion: Surveillance over four years collected close to 5,000 percutaneous injuries, and hollow-bore needles were involved in 62 percent of them: hypodermic needles on disposable syringes took 29 percent and winged-steel needles 13 percent. Glass followed at 17 percent and suture needles at 15 percent, with phlebotomy needles themselves at 4 percent. Hollow-bore needles weigh most because they carry a measurable volume of blood, which is why devices that enter a vein or an artery get the highest priority for replacement with safer ones.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "HIPAA Compliance", Other Issues: Violations of HIPAA; StatPearls, "Patient Confidentiality", Civil and Criminal Violations
preguntas.subtema: Penalty tiers · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k34
preguntas.pregunta: Among the HIPAA civil penalty tiers, which category carries the highest penalty per violation?
opciones: Willful neglect that is not corrected
Willful neglect corrected within the period
Reasonable cause, not willful neglect
A violation the person did not know about
preguntas.explicacion: The four civil tiers climb with culpability: not knowing of the violation, reasonable cause short of willful neglect, willful neglect put right inside the required period, and willful neglect left uncorrected, which tops the scale at $50,000 per violation. Criminal liability is a separate ladder, starting with knowingly obtaining or disclosing identifiable information, rising when it is done under false pretenses, and rising again when it is done for commercial advantage, for personal gain, or to do malicious harm. The civil side is enforced by the Office for Civil Rights.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, When can I sign up for Medicare?
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.b (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A patient who kept working past sixty-five retires in March. How long does she then have to sign up for Part B?
opciones: Eight months from the day she or her spouse stops working, COBRA notwithstanding
Eight months from the day the job-based coverage itself ends, COBRA included
Seven months around her sixty-fifth birthday, a period that has already passed
Sixty-three days, the gap allowed before a drug coverage penalty begins to run
preguntas.explicacion: The eight-month Special Enrollment Period for Part B starts when the person or the spouse stops working, even if COBRA or some other non-Medicare coverage is taken up in the meantime. Someone who loses job-based coverage before that date has eight months from then. Missing the period means a wait, a gap and a monthly penalty for as long as Part B is held.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Managed Care, Summary
preguntas.subtema: Managed care · CMAA 5 k73 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.e (exam through June 2027) · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which three plan designs are usually grouped together as managed care?
opciones: Health maintenance, preferred provider and point of service plans
Health maintenance, preferred provider and prescription drug plans
Health savings, flexible spending and high deductible health plans
Hospital insurance, medical insurance and supplemental policies
preguntas.explicacion: Managed care plans contract with providers and facilities to care for members at reduced cost, and the three types described are the health maintenance organization, the preferred provider organization and the point of service plan, which lets the patient choose between the two approaches at each visit. Savings and spending accounts are ways to pay costs, not plan designs, and hospital plus medical insurance describes the two parts of Original Medicare.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.5.2 Muscle Tremor Interference
preguntas.subtema: CCMA k148 k149 k151 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.2 2D.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which move is suggested to quiet muscle tremor coming from the limbs?
opciones: Move the limb electrodes up to the arms and the thighs
Move the chest electrodes down one intercostal space
Move the limb electrodes down to the wrists and ankles
Move the patient from the table to a seated position
preguntas.explicacion: After reassuring the patient, the limb electrodes may be shifted onto the upper arms and the thighs to get away from the muscles that are generating the signal. Other steps in the same list are moving or removing the pillow, tucking the hands under the buttocks and raising the knees on a pillow.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.5 Circulatory Pathways, Veins Draining the Upper Limbs; and StatPearls, "Anatomy, Shoulder and Upper Limb, Veins" (2023), section Structure and Function
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k7 (applied D2 k53) · PBT I.A.3 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which veins join to form the brachial vein, and is the brachial vein superficial or deep?
opciones: The radial and ulnar veins; it is a deep vein
The cephalic and basilic veins; it is superficial
The median cubital and cephalic veins; it is superficial
The axillary and subclavian veins; it is a deep vein
preguntas.explicacion: The radial and the ulnar veins run alongside the bones of the forearm and come together to form the brachial vein, a deep vessel that carries on into the axillary vein; in the forearm those deep veins travel in pairs beside the arteries as venae comitantes and merge at the cubital fossa. Cephalic and basilic are the superficial pair, and the axillary and subclavian lie further along.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals, Chapter 13: Repositioning Patients — Semi-Fowler's Position; and StatPearls, "Anatomy, Patient Positioning" (NBK513320)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B4 k61 · CMA I.C.1.b(2) · RMA III.F.2.a.i · NCMA 2B.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which angle of the head of the bed defines the semi-Fowler position?
opciones: 30 to 45 degrees, and it is better tolerated over long stretches of time
45 to 90 degrees, which is the range of the Fowler position itself
60 to 90 degrees, the range used while a nasogastric tube is placed
0 to 15 degrees, with the head raised only slightly off the flat bed
preguntas.explicacion: Semi-Fowler keeps the head of the bed between 30 and 45 degrees, with the hips flexed or not, and it serves the same purposes as Fowler while being easier to hold for hours. Fowler itself runs from 45 degrees upward, and the high or full variant, at 60 to 90 degrees, is what lowers the risk of aspiration while an orogastric or nasogastric tube goes down.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Falls and Fall Prevention in Older Adults", Evaluation: Screening Tools
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A1 · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: What is true about the tools available for screening older adults for fall risk?
opciones: No single tool combines high sensitivity with high specificity for that risk
The Tinetti tool has been shown to predict falls accurately in most patients
A one-legged stance held for ten seconds rules out the risk of falling
Screening is reserved for patients who have already fallen at least twice
preguntas.explicacion: Screening for falls yearly is recommended for everyone past 65, but the instruments are weak: a review of dozens of studies and tools found none that is both sensitive and specific. Balance tools such as Tinetti and the one-legged or tandem stance are poor predictors on their own, so the history and the physical examination carry the weight.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Composition of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5 k87) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In a spun hematocrit tube, what makes up the thin pale layer between the packed red cells and the plasma?
opciones: Leukocytes and platelets, normally under 1 percent of the sample
Reticulocytes, normally 1 to 2 percent of the red cell count
Plasma proteins, roughly 7 percent of the plasma volume
Fibrin strands with trapped platelets from a forming clot
preguntas.explicacion: That pale band is the buffy coat. It holds the formed elements that are not red cells, the white cells and the platelets, and normally amounts to less than 1 percent of the sample. Reticulocytes are immature red cells, not a separate layer; the plasma proteins are dissolved in the plasma above; and fibrin only appears if the sample has been allowed to clot, which an anticoagulated hematocrit tube has not.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), section 2.2.3, Step 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2D 2E k41 · PBT II.C · CCMA 3E1 · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which opening request follows WHO step 2, 'Identify and prepare the patient', for a conscious adult?
opciones: 'Please tell me your full name.'
'You are Mr. Johnson, correct?'
'Is this bed 7, the CBC for Dr. Ruiz?'
'Which tests are you here for today?'
preguntas.explicacion: Step 2 tells the health worker to introduce themselves and to ask the patient to state their full name, then to check that the laboratory form matches that identity. Feeding the patient a name to agree with, or identifying by bed number, is not what the step describes; asking which tests are ordered hands the patient a job that belongs to the form.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.6 Blood Typing, Rh Blood Groups
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.h(4) (2027: I.C.6.g(4)) · RMA I.A.2.a · NCMA 1.1 EKB 1 · CPT Core k5
preguntas.pregunta: When is RhoGAM (Rh immune globulin) normally given to an Rh negative pregnant patient?
opciones: In weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 72 hours after the birth
In weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 3 hours after the birth
In weeks 12 to 14 of pregnancy and within 72 hours after the birth
Only within 72 hours after the birth of a second Rh positive baby
preguntas.explicacion: RhoGAM temporarily prevents the Rh negative parent from forming anti-Rh antibodies by destroying any fetal Rh positive cells that cross the placenta, and it is normally given during weeks 26 to 28 of pregnancy and within 72 hours of birth. Since its introduction in 1968 the incidence of hemolytic disease of the newborn in such pregnancies fell from about 13 to 14 percent to about 0.1 percent.

preguntas.subtema: Consent in the record · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.a · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which item does the medical record condition of participation expect to find in the chart before a procedure the medical staff has designated?
opciones: An informed consent form, properly executed, for that procedure or treatment
A copy of the notice of privacy practices signed by the patient at check-in
An advance beneficiary notice explaining what the health plan may not pay for
A statement from the patient describing why the procedure is being requested
preguntas.explicacion: The record must document, as appropriate, informed consent forms properly executed for whichever procedures and treatments the medical staff, or Federal or State law, has specified as needing written consent. The same list runs to consultative evaluations, complications and infections acquired in hospital, every practitioner order and the nursing notes, records of treatment and of medication, reports from radiology and from the laboratory, and the vital signs.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.2 Production of the Formed Elements, Sites of Hemopoiesis
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: In an adult, where does most hemopoiesis take place?
opciones: Red marrow of the skull, pelvis, vertebrae, sternum and upper femur
Red marrow in the medullary cavity of the long bones, as in children
The liver and spleen, which take over from the marrow after birth
The yolk sac, then the fetal liver, spleen and lymphatic tissue
preguntas.explicacion: After birth the red marrow does nearly all of it, and in an adult the work is limited to the bones of the skull and pelvis, the vertebrae, the breastbone and the near ends of the femur and humerus. A child also makes blood in the marrow cavity of the long bones. Liver and spleen keep the ability, called extramedullary hemopoiesis, but step in only when the marrow fails.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, How to Understand and Use the Nutrition Facts Label: Serving Information
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 food labels · CMA I.A.6.g(4) · 2027 I.A.6.g(4) · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: A patient points at the serving size on a package and asks whether that is how much he is supposed to eat. What is the correct explanation?
opciones: It reflects how much people usually eat, not how much he should eat
It reflects how much he should eat to stay within his calorie needs
It is set by each manufacturer to match its own package sizes
It is the amount that supplies 100% of the Daily Value for the day
preguntas.explicacion: The serving size is standardized so similar products can be compared, and it is drawn from the amount people typically consume. It is a reference point, not a target. Every number on the panel, calories included, is tied to it, so eating two servings doubles the calories, the nutrient grams and the percentages.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Transmission-Based Precautions (April 3, 2024), Airborne Precautions
preguntas.subtema: Susceptible staff and airborne pathogens · CPT D1 1I k34 · PBT VI.G.4.c · CCMA 3C2 k96 · CMA I.B.4.a / 2027 I.B.3.a · RMA III.A.2.b · NCMA 2A.3
preguntas.pregunta: A phlebotomist who has never had chickenpox or the vaccine is assigned to a patient with varicella on Airborne Precautions. What does the CDC recommend?
opciones: Restrict her from the room if immune personnel are available to do the draw
Let her draw with an N95, since the respirator makes immunity irrelevant
Let her draw with a surgical mask, since varicella spreads by droplets
Restrict her permanently from all patients on Transmission-Based Precautions
preguntas.explicacion: The CDC's airborne recommendations keep susceptible staff out of the room of a patient who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox, measles, smallpox or disseminated zoster, provided immune colleagues are on hand to do the work, and they ask that susceptible people be immunized as soon as possible after an unprotected contact with a vaccine-preventable infection. Whoever does go in wears the respirator, but that does not cancel the preference for immune staff. Varicella belongs on the airborne list, not the droplet one, and the restriction attaches to this patient rather than to every isolation room.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 2.3, rows 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · D2 k47 · PBT II.J II.G · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(c) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: A serology test is ordered. Which two tubes list immunology and serology among their uses?
opciones: The red clot activator tube and the gold serum separator tube
The red clot activator tube and the purple top EDTA tube
The gold serum separator tube and the light green PST tube
The pale yellow ACD tube and the gold serum separator tube
preguntas.explicacion: Immunology and serology appear against two rows of the table: the red clot activator tube at position 4 and the separator tube at position 5, both of which give serum. EDTA is assigned to hematology and cross-match, the PST to chemistries, and the ACD tube to tissue typing and DNA work.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex A, Table B.1: Personal protection and hygiene
preguntas.subtema: Between procedures · CPT D1 1K k35 · PBT VI.G.4.f · CCMA 3C4 k101 · CMA I.B.4.c / 2027 I.B.3.c · RMA III.A.3.a.i · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: How often should hand hygiene be performed when two different samples are collected from the same patient?
opciones: Before and after the contact, and also between the procedures
Once before the first procedure and once after the last one
Only after the second procedure, when the gloves come off
Only if the gloves tore or blood reached the skin underneath
preguntas.explicacion: The best-practice table sets hand hygiene before and after each patient contact and also between procedures on the same patient, because the point is to reduce cross-contamination, which can happen within one encounter as well as between two patients. The gloves follow the same logic, one clean pair per patient or per procedure. Waiting for a torn glove or visible blood is a different rule, the one that forces washing after contact with blood.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Needle Shield
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: After activating the shield on a safety needle, the phlebotomist notices the tip is still visible at the end of the shield. Against which FDA design recommendation does this fall short?
opciones: The shield must fully enclose the needle and block finger access
The sharp should end up drawn right back inside the body of the device
The housing of a fixed recessed needle should extend beyond the sharp
Color should be used for a clear, specific purpose
preguntas.explicacion: FDA Table 1 gives one recommendation per feature type: a needle shield should enclose the needle completely and keep fingers away once activated; a retractable sharp should end up drawn right back inside the housing; and a fixed recessed needle should have a housing that extends beyond and fully covers the sharp. A shield that leaves the tip exposed fails the first of these; the retraction rule applies to a different design.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2L k48 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E1 k126 · NCMA 2C.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which simple step may significantly decrease a patient's anxiety just before the needle goes in?
opciones: Counting down with the patient
Applying the tourniquet early on
Dimming the room lighting
Offering a sugary drink first
preguntas.explicacion: A simple countdown may significantly reduce anxiety and optimize the conditions for venipuncture. Applying the tourniquet early works against the patient, since it should be released within one minute to avoid hemoconcentration; a sugary drink breaks a fast; and adequate lighting, not dim light, is what the guidance for older patients calls for.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Table 3.1, Recommended needle gauge, length and device; and CDC, NIOSH Alert: Preventing Needlestick Injuries in Health Care Settings, DHHS (NIOSH) Publication No. 2000-108 (Nov. 1999), PDF de CDC Stacks
preguntas.subtema: Needle gauge sizes and lengths · CPT D3 k56 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: For a routine venipuncture on an adult with ordinary veins, which needle does WHO Table 3.1 list with a length of 1 to 1.5 inches?
preguntas.explicacion: Table 3.1 gives the adult 21 G needle a length of 1 to 1.5 inch (2.54 cm), and the adult 22 G needle 1 inch. The 23 G appears for adults at 1 to 1.5 inch as a straight needle, but for children and neonates only as a 0.5 inch winged set. Sixteen to eighteen gauge is reserved for blood donation, and 19 to 20 G is marked not applicable for every age group.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Peripheral Pulse", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b · RMA III.E.3 Pulse e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: Both pedal pulses are easily felt in a patient being screened for peripheral arterial disease. What does that finding allow?
opciones: Leaving the ankle-brachial index aside, since disease is unlikely at that point
Leaving the ankle-brachial index aside only if the patient has no diabetes
Calling the screen negative once the femoral pulses are found to match them
Repeating the palpation in a month in place of ordering any other test
preguntas.explicacion: Palpating the pulses of both feet is a cheap screen. When they are present on both sides the chance of peripheral arterial disease falls below 3.5%, low enough to skip the ankle-brachial index, which compares ankle with arm systolic pressure and costs time, equipment and training. No extra condition is attached to that finding.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 7.1.2, Selecting the length of lancet
preguntas.subtema: Lancets · CPT D3 k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.5
preguntas.pregunta: When choosing a lancet for an adult finger-prick, why does the WHO advise one slightly shorter than the depth that seems necessary?
opciones: Pressure compresses the skin, so the puncture ends up slightly deeper than the lancet length
Shorter lancets give more blood, because the capillary bed lies in the upper dermis
The finger-prick must never exceed 1.5 mm, and most lancets are longer than that
Thinner and shorter lancets are the only ones that retract to prevent needle-sticks
preguntas.explicacion: Section 7.1.2 explains that the lancet picked is a little shorter than the depth estimated because the pressure applied compresses the skin, making the actual puncture a little deeper than the lancet length; pain rises with penetration depth, though blood volume rises with it too. Lengths run from 0.85 mm to 2.2 mm, and an adult finger-prick should not exceed 2.4 mm, not 1.5 mm.

preguntas.fuente: govinfo, Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, Pub. L. 106-430, sec. 3(2) and 3(3); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b)
preguntas.subtema: Definitions added by the Act · CPT D1 k12 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C k97 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which two terms did the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act add to the definitions in the bloodborne pathogens standard?
opciones: Sharps with engineered protections, and needleless systems
Universal Precautions, and the definition of an exposure incident
Regulated waste, and the definition of a contaminated sharp
Occupational exposure, and the definition of regulated waste
preguntas.explicacion: The Act put two definitions into 29 CFR 1910.1030(b). One covers sharps that carry engineered sharps injury protections: a needle or non-needle sharp used to draw fluids, reach a vein or artery, or give medication, built with a feature that lowers the risk of exposure. The other covers needleless systems, devices that take fluids out once access is established, deliver medication, or handle other tasks carrying percutaneous risk, all without a needle. Universal Precautions, exposure incident, occupational exposure, regulated waste and contaminated sharps were already defined in the 1991 standard.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: What should I know before my telehealth visit?
preguntas.subtema: What to ask before booking · CMAA 4E k59 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient about to book her first video visit says she has no health insurance and is worried about the bill. What does the patient guidance tell her to do?
opciones: Ask beforehand what the visit will cost, since her provider may know of local resources
Book the visit anyway, since a visit taken by video is free of charge to the patient
Ask her plan for a preauthorization, which will fix in advance what she is going to owe
Wait for an in-person appointment instead, since a price is quoted only for those visits
preguntas.explicacion: Before a telehealth visit the patient is told to know the costs and to ask what the visit will come to. If she cannot afford it or has no health insurance, her provider may have local resources. The same list asks her to say if she needs help such as a screen reader or closed captioning, to check the details in the reminder she is sent, to find a quiet spot with good internet, and to test her device beforehand.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Annex C, Table C.1, Conventional devices
preguntas.subtema: Device selection · CPT D3 3D k54 k55 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 3E4 k134 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: A syringe draw is planned for a small child. Which adjustment does the device table call for?
opciones: A smaller syringe together with a pediatric laboratory tube
A larger syringe together with a standard adult laboratory tube
A smaller syringe together with a standard adult laboratory tube
A larger syringe together with two pediatric laboratory tubes
preguntas.explicacion: Where a needle and syringe is used on a pediatric patient, the table asks for a smaller syringe and a pediatric laboratory tube. The parallel adjustment for the evacuated system is a smaller tube with a reduced vacuum, which is there to keep the specimen from haemolysing.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Fundamentals 1.4: Unlicensed Assistive Personnel
preguntas.subtema: Allied health roles · CCMA 1A k2 · NCMA 3.1
preguntas.pregunta: A certified nursing assistant records vital signs on a hospital floor. Under what authority is that task performed?
opciones: As a task delegated by the nurse, who stays accountable that it is done
Under the assistant's own license, granted by the state board of nursing
Under standing orders that a provider writes for the nursing unit each shift
Under the supervision of the physician who admitted the patient that day
preguntas.explicacion: Unlicensed assistive personnel are unlicensed people, of any title, who perform tasks a nurse delegates: certified nursing aides and assistants, patient care assistants, patient care technicians and certified medication aides among them. They help patients bathe, dress, eat and toilet, and may collect vital signs, weight and intake and output as delegated. The registered nurse remains accountable.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, Exclusions Program
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A nurse practitioner on the exclusion list writes an order that the practice then acts on. What does exclusion mean for payment?
opciones: No federal program pays for anything she furnishes, orders or prescribes
No federal program pays her directly, though her employer may still bill for it
No federal program pays her until the exclusion period ends and lapses by itself
No federal program pays for what she furnishes, but her written orders are payable
preguntas.explicacion: An excluded person can be paid nothing by federal health care programs for any item or service she furnishes, orders or prescribes, and that bites on every program whose health benefits the United States funds, directly or indirectly, with the Federal Employees Health Benefits Plan as the one carve-out. The order itself is caught, not only the hands-on service.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Personal Representatives: General Provisions
preguntas.subtema: Personal representatives · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A man holds a limited health care power of attorney covering only his mother's life support decisions. What may he access?
opciones: Only the protected health information relevant to the decision his authority actually covers
The complete designated record set, because any power of attorney makes him her representative
No information, since a power of attorney is not a document the Privacy Rule recognizes
Only the billing records, because clinical information stays with the patient in every case
preguntas.explicacion: A personal representative must generally be treated as the individual, but the scope of that authority comes from the underlying law. Where it is broad, as with a parent of a minor or the guardian of an incompetent adult, the representative is treated as the individual for all purposes; where it is limited to particular decisions, the representative is treated as the individual only for information relevant to that representation.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Laboratory Tube Collection", section Definition/Introduction, Green and Red
preguntas.subtema: Tubes and tests · CPT D3 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E3 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: The emergency department wants immediate chemistry results. Which tube is commonly used for stat chemistry, and what type of sample does it produce?
opciones: A green heparin tube, which yields plasma rather than serum
A red tube with no additive, which yields serum after clotting
A lavender EDTA tube, which yields plasma for hematology
A gray oxalate tube, which yields plasma for glucose and lactate
preguntas.explicacion: Green heparin tubes are often used when stat or immediate chemistry results are requested for emergency cases, and unlike red tubes the sample they give is plasma, not serum. The red tube has to clot first, typically 10 to 15 minutes, before centrifugation. The lavender tube is for hematologic assays and the gray tube for glucose and lactic acid.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Microbiology, 16.3 Modes of Disease Transmission, Contact Transmission and Vehicle Transmission
preguntas.subtema: Fomites and indirect contact · CPT D1 1K k11 · PBT VI.G.4.a · CCMA 3C k94 · CMA I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.2.a · NCMA 2A.1
preguntas.pregunta: A doorknob contaminated by an infected person's hands is an example of which element of disease transmission?
opciones: A fomite, in indirect contact transmission
A vehicle, like contaminated food or water
A mechanical vector, like a fly carrying bacteria
A droplet nucleus, the residue of an evaporated droplet
preguntas.explicacion: Indirect contact transmission works through fomites, inanimate objects that pick up pathogens from an infected person or reservoir and pass them to a new host who touches them and then a portal of entry; doorknobs, towels and tablecloths are the everyday examples, and improperly sterilized syringes, needles and catheters are the clinical ones behind many healthcare-associated infections. Vehicle transmission is through water, food or air; a mechanical vector is an animal carrying the pathogen on its body; and a droplet nucleus is what remains when a droplet desiccates in the air.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.404(c), Content of notification
preguntas.subtema: Breach notice content · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.1.b · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3E k33
preguntas.pregunta: Which element must a breach notification letter to an individual include?
opciones: Steps the individual can take to protect against potential harm
The name of the workforce member who caused the breach
A copy of the covered entity's complete privacy policies and procedures
The civil penalty amount the covered entity expects to pay to HHS
preguntas.explicacion: In plain language, and as far as it can, the letter describes what happened, with the date of the breach and the date it was discovered; which types of unsecured PHI were involved, such as a name, a Social Security number, a date of birth or a diagnosis; what individuals should do to protect themselves; what the entity is doing to investigate, to limit the harm and to stop it happening again; and how to make contact, by toll-free number, e-mail, website or postal address. Naming the employee, attaching the policies and estimating penalties are no part of the required content.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section History and Physical
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 3K k68 k69 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Ten minutes after a faint the patient is awake but still noticeably pale. What does that persisting pallor suggest?
opciones: Symptomatic anemia, which calls for a fuller evaluation
A normal recovery, since pallor lingers after every faint
A seizure rather than a faint, as the tongue was not bitten
Hemoconcentration from the tourniquet used during the draw
preguntas.explicacion: After a simple vasovagal event the examination should be entirely normal. Pallor that carries on suggests symptomatic anemia and, like a bitten tongue or an atypical story, prompts a search for another cause rather than a comfortable label.

preguntas.subtema: Security official · CCMA 7 k214 · CMA II.E.1.e · RMA I.C.5 · CMAA 7A k100 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Which Security Rule standard does a practice meet by naming one person to develop and run its security policies?
opciones: Assigned security responsibility, which asks for an identified security official
Security management process, which is met by writing out the policies themselves
Workforce security, which settles which staff members may reach the information
Evaluation, which reviews whether the safeguards still fit how the practice works
preguntas.explicacion: Assigned security responsibility is a standard in its own right: name the security official who will develop the policies the subpart requires and put them into effect. It is the security counterpart of the privacy official the Privacy Rule asks for, and one person may hold both roles.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: De-Identified Health Information
preguntas.subtema: De-identification · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3B k35 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A quality committee wants a data file with no restrictions on its later use. Which step achieves that under the Privacy Rule?
opciones: Stripping the listed identifiers of the patient, relatives, employers and household members
Removing only the names and leaving birth dates, addresses and account numbers in place
Replacing each patient name with the medical record number used inside the practice
Having the privacy official sign a statement that the file is for internal use only
preguntas.explicacion: De-identified information carries no restrictions on use or disclosure, and two routes lead to it. One is a qualified statistician making a formal determination; the other is stripping out the identifiers specified for the individual herself and for her relatives, household members and employers, which counts only where the entity has no actual knowledge that what remains could still identify somebody. Medical record numbers, account numbers and full-face photographs are on the safe harbor list.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Sutures and Needles", Suture Removal
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k75 · CMA I.C.2.c (2027 I.C.2.c) · RMA III.D.2.m · NCMA 2B.16
preguntas.pregunta: Where is a suture cut during removal, and why there?
opciones: Immediately under the knot, so the least contaminated surface is dragged through the tissue
Immediately above the knot, so the whole knot lifts out without pulling on the wound edges
At both ends of the knot, so the strand comes free without any tension on the skin at all
At the midpoint between two stitches, so each half slides out on the side where it entered
preguntas.explicacion: The cut goes immediately under the knot, as close to the skin as possible at the far end of the knot, so that the portion which has been lying on the skin surface is not pulled down through the tissue. Both ends of the knot must never be snipped, because then nothing is left to grasp and the strand below the surface cannot be retrieved.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Height Assessment", Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k57 · CMA I.A.1.c · RMA III.E.4.b · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient in a wheelchair cannot stand for a height measurement. Which alternatives are described?
opciones: Estimates from arm span, lower leg, foot length or recumbent length are used
The last recorded standing height is carried forward until the patient can stand
Height is left blank, because no measurement is valid unless the patient stands
Height is estimated from the seated shoulder width, which tracks stature closely
preguntas.explicacion: Where standing height cannot be obtained, regression equations based on arm span, the lower leg, foot length, shoeprint length or recumbent length are used as indicators of stature, and imaging of long bones has also been used. Where cerebral palsy is severe, measuring the child directly while supine is the most reliable way.

preguntas.fuente: 45 CFR 164.502(b)(1) and (b)(2), Standard: Minimum necessary
preguntas.subtema: Minimum necessary exceptions · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: To which disclosure does the HIPAA minimum necessary standard NOT apply?
opciones: A disclosure to a health care provider for treatment
A disclosure to a health plan for payment
A disclosure to a business associate for operations
A disclosure to a researcher under a privacy board waiver
preguntas.explicacion: A covered entity using, disclosing or requesting PHI must make reasonable efforts to keep it to the minimum necessary for the purpose. Section 164.502(b)(2) sets out where that does not apply: a provider disclosing for treatment or asking for what treatment needs; uses and disclosures to the individual; anything done under an authorization; disclosures to the Secretary for compliance; and uses required by law or by the rule itself. Payment, operations and research disclosures all stay under the minimum necessary limit.

preguntas.subtema: Business associate agreements · CPT D1 1C k13 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k214 · CMA II.E.2.c · RMA I.C.5 · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3B k33
preguntas.pregunta: An outside company will digitize the clinic's paper charts. What does HIPAA require before it receives the PHI?
opciones: Satisfactory assurances in a written business associate contract that it will safeguard the PHI
A signed authorization from every patient whose chart will be digitized by the company
Only the notice of privacy practices, since scanning counts as a health care operation
A certificate of accreditation for the company from a CMS-approved organization, renewed yearly
preguntas.explicacion: Section 164.502(e) lets a covered entity disclose PHI to a business associate, and let it create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on its behalf, if it first secures satisfactory assurances that the associate will safeguard the information, documented in a written contract or arrangement meeting 164.504(e); the associate may then use the PHI only as its contract or the law permits, and must secure the same assurances from any subcontractor. Patient authorizations are not needed for this kind of operational service, and accreditation is a CLIA concept.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, About Body Mass Index (BMI)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A6 k58 · CMA I.A.1.h · RMA III.E.4.e · NCMA 2B.3
preguntas.pregunta: How is obesity defined in children and teenagers?
opciones: A body mass index at or above the 95th percentile for that sex and age
A body mass index at or above the 85th percentile for that sex and age
A body mass index of 30.0 or more, the same threshold as in adults
A body mass index at or above the 90th percentile for that sex and age
preguntas.explicacion: For children and teenagers of 2 through 19 the threshold is the 95th percentile of the index for sex and age. Fixed adult categories do not apply, because children are still growing. Severe obesity in that group is defined at 120% of the 95th percentile or an index of 35 or more.

preguntas.subtema: Amendment of the record · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA III.H.3 · RMA II.B.4.g · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.5
preguntas.pregunta: A patient says her chart lists an allergy she does not have and asks the office to fix it. How long does the practice have to act?
opciones: Sixty days, with one thirty day extension if the patient is told the reason in writing
Thirty days, the same period the rule gives for responding to a request for access
Ten working days, after which the entry must be deleted from the electronic record
Six years, the period the rule sets for keeping its privacy policies and procedures
preguntas.explicacion: The amendment right lets an individual ask a covered entity to correct PHI in the designated record set that is inaccurate or incomplete. The regulation gives 60 days to act on the request, with a single 30 day extension. If the amendment is accepted, the entity must make reasonable efforts to pass it on to those the individual names and to those it knows may rely on the old information to her detriment.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.D.3 · CCMA 3D k117 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.b.iii
preguntas.pregunta: An EDTA tube for an erythrocyte sedimentation rate sat in a rack for four hours before the test was set up. What effect is expected?
opciones: A falsely low ESR, because delayed red cells lose their biconcave shape; testing should start within 2 hours
A falsely high ESR, because delayed red cells aggregate faster; testing should start within 2 hours
A falsely low ESR, because the anticoagulant loses activity; testing should start within 4 hours
A falsely high ESR, because plasma viscosity falls on standing; testing should start within 6 hours
preguntas.explicacion: Delays in processing make red cells lose their biconcave shape, which reduces the ESR, so the test should be started within 2 hours of collection; clotted blood also lowers it by disturbing rouleaux formation. The factors that raise the value are different: a warm room, direct sunlight, tube tilt (3° from vertical can add up to 30 %), vibration, and air bubbles from an under-filled tube.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Authorization
preguntas.subtema: Authorization to release · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A life insurance company asks the office for a patient's records to decide on a policy. What does the office need?
opciones: The patient's written authorization, since this purpose is outside treatment, payment or operations
No document at all, since disclosures to insurers count as payment activities of a plan
A note in the accounting of disclosures, which by itself makes the release permissible
The good faith acknowledgment the patient signed for the notice of privacy practices
preguntas.explicacion: Written authorization is required for any use or disclosure that falls outside treatment, outside payment and outside health care operations, and that is not otherwise permitted or required. The examples OCR gives are a disclosure to a life insurer weighing coverage, a pre- employment physical result going to an employer, and information going to a drug company for its own marketing. The payment definition reaches the patient's health plan, not a life insurer.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Loop Diuretics", Mechanism of Action and Indications; and StatPearls, "Antihypertensive Medications" (NBK554579)
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1C k14 · CMA I.D.1.b · RMA III.G.4.b · NCMA 1.3
preguntas.pregunta: Furosemide is ordered for a patient admitted with fluid overload from heart failure. Where does this class act?
opciones: On the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter of the loop of Henle's thick ascending limb
On the sodium-chloride channel of the distal convoluted tubule of the nephron
On the beta-1 receptors that make the juxtaglomerular cells release their renin
On the enzyme that converts angiotensin I into the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II
preguntas.explicacion: A loop diuretic competes with chloride for the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter of the thick ascending limb and blocks it, so sodium and chloride are not reabsorbed, the interstitium loses its tonicity and free water leaves in the urine. The distal convoluted tubule is where thiazides work; renin release and the angiotensin-converting enzyme belong to beta blockers and ACE inhibitors.

preguntas.fuente: Medicare.gov, Parts of Medicare
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · CMA III.G.4.b / 2027 III.G.4 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: Which services does Medicare Part A help cover?
opciones: Inpatient hospital stays, skilled nursing facility care, hospice and home health
Inpatient hospital stays, doctors' services in the office and durable equipment
Outpatient care, preventive screenings and yearly wellness visits with a doctor
Prescription drugs bought at the pharmacy and many recommended vaccines
preguntas.explicacion: Part A is the hospital insurance half of Original Medicare: inpatient hospital care, care in a skilled nursing facility, hospice, and some home health care. Doctors' services, outpatient care, durable medical equipment and preventive services sit under Part B, and drugs bought at the pharmacy come through Part D, either as a standalone plan or built into a Medicare Advantage plan.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Fainting", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.l · 2027 I.B.8.l · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: A patient faints in the hallway and comes round within seconds. What is the immediate care?
opciones: Check breathing, loosen the collar and raise the feet above heart level
Sit the patient in a chair and offer a sweet drink and a cold compress
Roll the patient face down with the head turned so the airway drains
Stand the patient up slowly with support to restore normal circulation
preguntas.explicacion: Airway and breathing are checked first, tight clothing at the neck is loosened, and the feet are raised above the level of the heart, about 12 inches (30 cm). If the patient vomited, they are turned onto one side. They stay lying down 10 to 15 minutes in a cool quiet place; if that is impossible, they sit forward with the head between the knees.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, Medicaid.gov: Mandatory & Optional Medicaid Benefits
preguntas.subtema: Government plans · CMA III.G.4.c (2027 III.G.4) · CMAA 5 k74 · CCMA 5 k182 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas.pregunta: A family moving out of state asks whether their new state's Medicaid has to cover the child's dental care. What is the accurate answer?
opciones: Dental care is optional, so a state adds it only through the state plan process
Dental care is mandatory, in the same way family planning services are mandatory
Dental care is mandatory, in the same way nurse midwife services are mandatory
Dental care is mandatory, as federally qualified health center services are
preguntas.explicacion: The federal list separates the benefits every state has to provide from those a state may add through the state plan process. Family planning, nurse midwife services and federally qualified health center services are mandatory; dental services, clinic services, physical therapy, private duty nursing and other licensed practitioner services are optional.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Torts and consent · CCMA 7B k216, k221 · CMA E.4.a(5)-(6) · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: A combative patient in the emergency department refuses an IV. Staff place it before any capacity assessment is made. What has occurred?
opciones: Battery, since contact was made with no consent and no documented assessment
False imprisonment, since the patient was held in a bounded area unwillingly
Implied consent, because the emergency exception covers a refused procedure
Negligence, because the standard of care for agitation was not followed first
preguntas.explicacion: Until a capacity assessment has been done and documented, treating a refusing patient is the tort of battery: harmful or offensive contact without consent. Putting the same patient on a hold would add false imprisonment, and restraining or sedating would be both. The way out is the assessment: once lack of capacity is documented, sedation, restraint, venipuncture and testing may go ahead.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Notice of Privacy Practices for Protected Health Information: Providing the Notice
preguntas.subtema: Availability of the notice · CCMA 5 k175 · CMA II.E.1.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 5D k64 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: Besides handing the notice of privacy practices to new patients, where must a treatment provider keep it available?
opciones: Posted at the facility, with copies to take away, and on a website describing its services
Posted at the facility, with copies to take away, and filed with the state licensing board
Posted in the staff area, with copies to take away, and sent to each health plan it bills
Posted at the facility, with copies on request, and read aloud before the first appointment
preguntas.explicacion: The latest version, the one reflecting any change in privacy policies, has to be available at the office for people to ask for and take with them, and posted where it can be seen clearly. Any website the entity keeps that describes its customer services or benefits must carry the notice prominently, and anyone who asks for a copy gets one.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vasovagal Episode", section Introduction; and "Syncope", section Etiology
preguntas.subtema: Complications: syncope · CPT D3 k68 · PBT II.I · CCMA 3E13 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which form of syncope is the most common, and which of its triggers matter in a phlebotomy setting?
opciones: Vasovagal syncope, triggered among other things by pain or emotional upset, with bradycardia and hypotension
Carotid sinus syncope, triggered by pressure on the neck, with tachycardia and high blood pressure
Situational syncope, triggered by coughing or urination, with normal heart rate and pressure
Cardiac syncope, triggered by exertion, with ventricular tachycardia and pallor
preguntas.explicacion: The vasovagal episode is the most common form of reflex syncope and can be set off by pain or by emotional upset, though often no trigger is found; it accounts for nearly half of all cases, with severe pain and stress among its situations, leading to vasodilation and bradycardia. During the event the patient is typically slow of pulse, hypotensive, pale and sweating.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3.1 Recording the ECG
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F3 3F7 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(ii) · RMA III.F.6.a.ii · NCMA 2D.7 2D.9
preguntas.pregunta: The first tracing prints and its quality is poor. What is done before any extra copies are made?
opciones: Stop the machine, fix the problem and run a new tracing
Ask for the extra copies and mark the poor quality on them
Stop the machine and send the poor tracing to the provider
Ask for the extra copies and repeat it only if requested
preguntas.explicacion: The routine has the technician read the first printed tracing for errors before anything else. If the quality is not good, the run is stopped, the problem is resolved and a fresh recording is taken; the number of extra copies is only entered once the strip is good.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Preparation (patient identification and tube labeling)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 k89 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E k145 · NCMA 2C.14 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.a
preguntas.pregunta: A tube arrives in the laboratory bearing only the patient's full name. Which element is missing that is normally required on a labeled specimen?
opciones: The date and time of collection and the identity of the person who collected it
The diagnosis code and the name of the insurance carrier that covers the requested test
The room number and the bed number where the specimen was collected
The color of the stopper and the lot number of the evacuated tube used
preguntas.explicacion: A complete label carries, beside the patient's names and date of birth, the exact date and time of collection and the collector's identification, according to each center's policy; the requesting provider and the specimen's own identifying details may also be included. Diagnosis codes belong on the requisition, not the tube; room or bed numbers cannot serve as identifiers; stopper color and lot are not label content.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Contaminated, Contaminated Sharps, Regulated Waste
preguntas.subtema: Contaminated sharps definition · CPT D1 1G k30 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which item meets the standard's definition of a contaminated sharp?
opciones: A broken capillary tube with dried blood on it
A sealed tube of blood in a transport rack
A dressing soaked with liquid blood that would drip if squeezed
An unused lancet still in its sterile package
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (b) calls a contaminated sharp any contaminated object capable of penetrating the skin, and its examples run from needles and scalpels to broken glass, broken capillary tubes and the exposed ends of dental wires. Two conditions have to hold at once: the object can pierce skin, and blood or OPIM is on it or is reasonably anticipated to be. A sealed tube pierces nothing; a gauze pad that would drip is regulated waste of the liquid kind rather than a sharp; and an unused lancet can pierce but carries nothing, so it is not a contaminated sharp yet.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Exposure Incident; and (f)(3), Post-exposure Evaluation and Follow-up
preguntas.subtema: Exposure incidents and post-exposure follow-up · CPT D1 k33 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.11
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these events meets OSHA's definition of an "exposure incident"?
opciones: Blood splashes into a technician's eye while a tube is being uncapped
A drop of blood lands on the intact skin of a gloved hand
A technician is assigned to a job where contact with blood is reasonably anticipated
A contaminated needle is found in a regulated waste bag, without any parenteral contact
preguntas.explicacion: The definition names the routes that count: the eye, the mouth or another mucous membrane, skin that is not intact, or a parenteral route such as a needlestick, with the contact coming from the employee's duties. A splash to the eye is mucous-membrane contact and qualifies. Intact gloved skin is not a listed route. A job where contact is reasonably anticipated is Occupational Exposure, the neighbouring definition, not an incident.
