A contaminated needle in a waste bag is regulated waste in the wrong container, but without parenteral contact there is no exposure incident. The label matters because reporting an exposure incident is what obliges the employer to make the post-exposure evaluation and follow-up available at once.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Post-procedural care and bandaging · CPT D3 3Q k73 k74 · PBT II.F II.I · CCMA 3E9 k137 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.13
preguntas.pregunta: How is pressure maintained on the site after the needle is removed?
opciones: Gauze pressed over the site as the needle comes out, then taped in place, or a bandaid applied over it
The patient bends the elbow over the gauze, which keeps pressure on the vein without tape
An ice pack wrapped in a towel is held on the site for 15 minutes to prevent a hematoma
The tourniquet is reapplied loosely over the gauze for one minute to compress the vein
preguntas.explicacion: Once the draw is done, clean gauze is used to apply pressure as the needle is swiftly removed, pressure is continued, and the gauze is taped in place to provide continuous pressure against a hematoma; alternatively a bandaid goes over the gauze. Bending the arm is what the WHO forbids, and ice is first aid for a bruise that has already formed.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Cultural Religious Competence in Clinical Practice", sections Religion and Healthcare, and Islam (Clinical Significance)
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2A k17 · CCMA 6 k193 · CMA F.2.a / 2027 F.1.d(8) · RMA I.D.1.d · NCMA 2B.2
preguntas.pregunta: A Muslim woman asks for a female phlebotomist. What is the culturally competent response?
opciones: Find a same-sex practitioner unless the situation is an acute emergency
Explain that staff assignments cannot be changed for religious reasons alone
Proceed with the male phlebotomist if her husband gives his agreement
Ask her to sign a waiver acknowledging the delay before rescheduling
preguntas.explicacion: Religion can shape a patient's preference for the gender of their health provider, along with diet, medicines from animal products and modesty, and the clinical note for Islam reads: find a same-sex practitioner if it is not an acute emergency. Health professionals are asked to accommodate such needs rather than refuse them or route the decision through a relative.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Fasting for a Blood Test, sections Why do I need to fast, and What if I make a mistake; StatPearls, "Overview on Ordering and Evaluation of Laboratory Tests", section Diagnostic Tests in Diabetes Mellitus
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 k46 · PBT II.D · CCMA 3E k125 · NCMA 2C.2 · RMA III.C.4.e · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a)
preguntas.pregunta: During check-in a patient admits to having eaten a pastry two hours before a fasting glucose. What is the correct action?
opciones: Report it to the provider; the test may need to be rescheduled for a day when the patient can fast
Draw the sample anyway and write the time of the pastry on the tube so the laboratory can adjust the result
Have the patient wait in the lobby for six more hours and then draw, since 8 hours will have passed by then
Draw the sample and order a random glucose instead, since the two tests share the same normal value
preguntas.explicacion: If the patient eats or drinks anything other than water during the fast, the instruction is to tell the provider, who may reschedule the test for another time when the patient can fast, because nutrients absorbed from food change the levels of substances in the blood and an inaccurate result gives an inaccurate picture of health. Fasting and random glucose have different normal values, and no note on the tube converts one into the other.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Technique or Treatment
preguntas.subtema: Angle of insertion · CPT D3 3I k65 · PBT II.F · CCMA 3E7 k133 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.9
preguntas.pregunta: At what angle to the surface of the arm is the phlebotomy needle inserted?
opciones: Between 15 and 30 degrees
Between 30 and 45 degrees
Less than 45 degrees
Between 5 and 10 degrees
preguntas.explicacion: The needle goes in slowly at an angle of 15 to 30 degrees to the surface of the arm, after the skin has been pulled taut with the thumb. The WHO gives 30 degrees or less, which is consistent. The 'less than 45 degrees until a flash of blood appears' figure belongs to the peripheral line placement chapter and describes an IV cannula, not a phlebotomy needle.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Contraindications
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A patient has had a mastectomy on the left side. Which arm is used for the cuff?
opciones: The right: a mastectomy on that side is an absolute reason to avoid the left arm
Either arm, provided the cuff is inflated more slowly on the operated side
The left, because the readings on the two sides have to be kept comparable
The right, but only during the first year after the operation was carried out
preguntas.explicacion: A history of mastectomy on that side is listed among the absolute reasons not to put a cuff on that limb, along with a dialysis fistula or shunt and recent surgical wounds. Lymphedema, paralysis or weakness of the limb, and indwelling lines are relative reasons. In each case the other limb or another site is used.

preguntas.fuente: Open RN, Nursing Skills 2e, 20.12 Checklist for Wound Cleansing, Irrigation, and Packing
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B8 k79 · CMA I.C.4.b (2027 I.C.4.b) · RMA III.D.2.k · NCMA 2B.20
preguntas.pregunta: A wound healing by secondary intention is being irrigated. How is it done?
opciones: A 35-mL syringe with a needleless cannula, held an inch above, flushing until the return runs clear
A 35-mL syringe with a needleless cannula, held against the bed, flushing for a fixed thirty seconds
A 10-mL syringe with a fine needle attached, held an inch above, flushing until the return runs clear
A bulb syringe with warmed tap water, held an inch above, flushing until the periwound skin is wet
preguntas.explicacion: Irrigation uses a 35-mL syringe of sterile saline with a needleless cannula, held about an inch above the wound and flushed gently with continuous pressure until the fluid coming back is clear. The runoff drains into a basin, since it is a medium for bacterial growth. The edges are then dried with sterile gauze so the surrounding tissue does not macerate.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Taking a step back from testing: Preanalytical considerations in molecular infectious disease diagnostics" (Clin Biochem 2023, PMC9729171), Table 2
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B k89 · PBT III.D.1 III.D.3 · CCMA 3D5 k121 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A dry cervical swab collected for a molecular sexually transmitted infection panel cannot be couriered until the next day. Which storage condition matches the general guideline?
opciones: Dried, at or below room temperature, for as long as seventy-two hours
Dried, at or below room temperature, for no longer than twelve hours
In viral transport medium at 2 to 8 °C, for as long as seventy-two hours
Frozen at −20 °C from collection, because the targets are unstable
preguntas.explicacion: Urethral, vaginal and cervical swabs are taken for organisms such as Trichomonas vaginalis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, herpes simplex virus and Chlamydia trachomatis, and what governs them is time, temperature and transport medium. The general storage guidance for this family of swabs is dried, at room temperature or below, for up to seventy-two hours.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Blood Pressure Measurement", Equipment: Automated Office Blood Pressure
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.b · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic installs a device that takes several blood pressure readings on its own while the patient waits alone in the room. Which problem is that meant to solve?
opciones: Readings pushed up or down by the presence of the person measuring
Cuffs of the wrong width that squeeze a large arm far too tightly
Readings started before the patient has sat quietly for five minutes
Monitors that drift out of calibration between one service and the next
preguntas.explicacion: Pressure moves when a clinician is in the room: it climbs in white-coat hypertension and hides in masked hypertension. Automated office monitoring records several readings over a few minutes with nobody present, and the values land closer to awake ambulatory pressure. Cuff size, resting time and calibration are separate matters, handled by technique.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: Cataract surgery was done on the right eye last month and the left eye is treated today, with the right one now resolved. Which code fits today's visit?
opciones: The unilateral code for the eye that still has the condition
The bilateral code, since both eyes had the condition this year
The unspecified side code, because only one side is treated now
Two codes, one for each of the eyes that have been treated so far
preguntas.explicacion: The bilateral code is assigned while the condition exists on both sides, including at the encounter that treats the first side. At the second encounter, once treatment has resolved the condition on the side already done, the appropriate unilateral code is used for the side that still has it. If the first treatment did not resolve it, the bilateral code still fits.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Dialysis Fistula", section Enhancing Healthcare Team Outcomes
preguntas.subtema: Contraindications · CPT D3 k62 · PBT II.E II.I · CCMA 3E4 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii · NCMA 2C.3
preguntas.pregunta: A dialysis patient has an arteriovenous fistula in the left forearm. What should be avoided on that side?
opciones: Peripheral venous access, blood draws and blood pressure measurements
Blood draws only; blood pressure cuffs are safe if inflated briefly
Blood pressure measurements only; draws are permitted below the fistula
Only the puncture of the fistula itself; draws above it are permitted
preguntas.explicacion: Nurses help save the veins by keeping peripheral lines, blood draws and pressure cuffs OFF the side of the fistula or of planned fistula creation, and they should know how to assess the thrill and recognize its loss. Checking the thrill is part of monitoring the access, not a clearance to puncture that arm.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Fraud & Abuse: Prevent, Detect, Report (MLN4649244), Physician Self-Referral Law
preguntas.subtema: Fraud and abuse · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: A group bills for a designated health service, unaware that the referral behind it broke the self-referral law. What is the position?
opciones: Filing the claim is prohibited anyway, since intent is not needed
Filing the claim is allowed, because the group did not know of it
Filing is allowed if the referral is put right after the payment
Filing is prohibited only where the referral was made on purpose
preguntas.explicacion: The self-referral law stops the entity from billing at all for a designated health service that came from an improper referral, and it does so whether or not the entity knew of the problem or meant to claim for it. If Medicare pays such a claim the entity holds an overpayment, which has to be reported and returned within 60 days of being identified.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Getting patients set up with telehealth technology
preguntas.subtema: Access barriers · CMAA 4B k55 · CCMA 5V k192 · CMA III.H.1 · RMA II.B.2.a · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient books her first video visit and says she has no internet at home. Which option does HHS suggest the office raise with her?
opciones: A public library, which usually offers high-speed internet and often a private room
A relative's telephone, which she can borrow for the length of the appointment
The clinic waiting room, where she can join the call on the practice's own tablet
A paper questionnaire she can post back instead of attending the appointment
preguntas.explicacion: Having no internet service with the bandwidth for video is named as one of the biggest barriers keeping patients away from telehealth. The suggestions offered are that the patient might be eligible for federal help under the Lifeline program, that plenty of fast food restaurants throw free Wi-Fi as far as the parking lot, and that most public libraries provide high-speed internet and often a private room.

preguntas.fuente: FDA, Medical Devices with Sharps Injury Prevention Features, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff (2005), Table 1, Colored Feature or Component
preguntas.subtema: Needle safety devices · CPT D3 3M k66 · PBT VI.G.4.h · CCMA 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.4.e / 2027 I.B.3.e · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: When a sharps safety device uses color on a component, what is expected of that color?
opciones: It should serve a purpose and follow conventions users know already
It should be red, so the used device is visible in the sharps bin
It should differ between hospitals, so devices are not mixed up
It should change once the safety feature has been activated once
preguntas.explicacion: Color is expected to achieve a specific purpose, such as distinguishing models or sizes, and to fit conventions the user already recognizes, the example given being the orange hubs and needle covers of insulin syringes. Whether the feature has fired is judged by design, not by a color change.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Laboratory Safety Guidance (OSHA 3404), Fire safety, classes of fire and extinguisher types; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157(d)
preguntas.subtema: Classes of fire · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.2 · CMA I.B.8.c / 2027 I.B.7.c · RMA II.B.7.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: Which fuels define a Class B fire?
opciones: Flammable liquids and gases, such as organic solvents
Ordinary combustibles that leave ash, such as paper
Combustible metal powders, flakes or shavings
Energized electrical equipment such as a centrifuge motor
preguntas.explicacion: Class A fires involve ordinary combustibles, fuels that burn and leave ash, and Class B flammable liquids and gases; many organic solvents and compressed gases in a laboratory are Class B hazards. Combustible metals are Class D, handled with a specialized dry powder extinguisher, and 29 CFR 1910.157 treats electrical equipment as Class C, distributing those units by the pattern of the A or B hazards present. The most common laboratory extinguishers are dry chemical BC or ABC and carbon dioxide.

preguntas.fuente: HHS, telehealth.hhs.gov: Planning your telehealth workflow
preguntas.subtema: Telehealth check-in · CCMA 5R · CMA III.H.2.a · RMA II.B.1 · CMAA 5A · NCMA 3.3
preguntas.pregunta: A video visit is about to begin. Which step belongs to the start of the encounter?
opciones: Confirming who the patient is and why she has come to the visit
Submitting the claim with the telehealth modifier already attached
Collecting the patient's feedback on how the technology performed
Sending the appointment reminder with the link to the platform
preguntas.explicacion: The workflow lists the steps in order. Ahead of the visit come the reminder, guidance on using the technology, the online paperwork, a walk-through of the equipment, troubleshooting information, consent and a request that the patient find somewhere quiet and private. The visit itself opens with confirmation, establishing who the patient is and what has brought her, and intake follows. Billing and evaluation come afterwards.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, chapter 5: Scheduling and Receiving Deliveries
preguntas.subtema: Receiving deliveries · CCMA 5T · RMA II.B.5.a · CMAA 7D k99 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: What does the storage and handling guidance say about when a delivery of temperature-sensitive stock may be scheduled?
opciones: Only on days and at hours when staff will be there, and it is never left unattended
On any weekday, provided the carrier leaves the container in a shaded doorway
Only on the first working day of the week, so the count matches the month's order
On any day, provided the container is opened within four hours of its arrival
preguntas.explicacion: Delivery dates and times are chosen so that somebody is there to receive them, and the container is never left standing alone. The coordinator or the alternate is told the moment it arrives, and the contents are unpacked and put into the storage unit straight away rather than left in the shipping box.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, Guideline for Disinfection and Sterilization (2008), Cleaning
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3C6 k103 · CMA I.C.5.d(1) (2027 I.C.5.b(1)) · RMA III.A.4 · NCMA 2A.2
preguntas.pregunta: What are the two essential components of manual instrument cleaning?
opciones: Friction, meaning scrubbing the soiled area, and fluidics, meaning fluid under pressure
Cavitation, meaning imploding bubbles, and sonication, meaning waves of acoustic energy
Agitation, meaning steam passing through the bath, and a short terminal steam cycle
Circulation, meaning water driven by spray arms, and a heat step held near ninety degrees
preguntas.explicacion: Cleaning by hand rests on friction and fluidics. Friction is the old dependable one, a brush rubbed over the soiled area; fluidics is fluid under pressure, used to flush internal channels after brushing or where no brush will pass. Cavitation belongs to the ultrasonic cleaner, and the steam bath and spray arms to washer-sterilizers and washer-disinfectors.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Advance Directives", Issues of Concern: DNR; and Other Issues
preguntas.subtema: Medical directives · CCMA 7D k217 · NCMA 4.2
preguntas.pregunta: Which advance care document is the one that emergency medical services are usually bound to honor?
opciones: A written DNR order signed by the patient's health care provider
A living will kept in the patient's file at the primary care office
A durable power of attorney naming the patient's oldest daughter
A note in the patient portal describing the patient's own wishes
preguntas.explicacion: A DNR is a written document usually signed by the patient's health care provider, and in most states written orders of that kind are the only advance directives that providers of emergency medical services are legally obliged to consider. Some states require EMS to resuscitate unless a state-approved document is produced, which is why an out-of-hospital form exists.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.d (2027 I.C.6.c) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: Which structure separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominopelvic cavity?
opciones: The diaphragm, a dome-shaped muscle used in breathing
The mediastinum, the space that holds the heart
The peritoneum, the membrane around the abdominal organs
The pleura, the membrane that wraps around each lung
preguntas.explicacion: The ventral cavity is split in two by the diaphragm, the dome-shaped respiratory muscle that forms the floor of the chest. Above it lie the heart and lungs, below it the digestive organs, kidneys and adrenal glands. The mediastinum, peritoneum and pleura are structures inside those cavities, not the wall between them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Fecal Occult Blood Test", Specimen Collection (Immunological methods) and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: FIT versus gFOBT · PBT V.B.2 / V.E · CCMA 3D1 k113 · CMA I.C.7.a.(3) · RMA III.C.4.a.iv · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: How does the fecal immunochemical test (FIT) differ from the guaiac test in patient preparation?
opciones: FIT needs no dietary restrictions, because its antibodies detect human globin rather than peroxidase activity
FIT needs a stricter diet, because it detects heme from any animal source as well as human blood
FIT needs the same 3-day diet, but vitamin C may be continued because it targets porphyrins
FIT needs no dietary restrictions, because it detects heme-derived porphyrins by spectrofluorimetry
preguntas.explicacion: Immunochemical kits use antibodies against the globin chain of human hemoglobin, so animal heme and plant peroxidases do not react and no diet is required, which improves adherence; they mainly pick up lower gastrointestinal bleeding and are more specific than guaiac. Guaiac relies on the pseudoperoxidase activity of heme, and the heme-porphyrin method is a separate laboratory assay using spectrofluorimetry.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Competency and Capacity", Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Capacity · CCMA 7B k216 · CMA E.3.c · RMA I.C.1.a · NCMA 4.7
preguntas.pregunta: In a capacity assessment, what must the patient demonstrate?
opciones: Grasp of the facts, weighing of options, a clear choice and steady logic
Correct orientation to person, place and time throughout the interview
Agreement with the plan the clinician has recommended for the problem
A mental status exam with no hallucinations, agitation or pressured speech
preguntas.explicacion: Capacity is shown when the patient understands what is relevant to this decision, can weigh the risks, benefits and alternatives, can tell the team what they have decided, and keeps that reasoning consistent through the encounter. Hallucinations, agitation and disorganized speech are triggers to look harder, not the test itself, and capacity never means agreeing with the clinician's recommendation.

preguntas.fuente: CDC, NHANES III Electrocardiogram Procedure Manual, Section 3.3 Examination Procedures
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F2 k153 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(i) · RMA III.F.6.a.i · NCMA 2D.4 2D.5
preguntas.pregunta: Once the four limb wires are attached, what is double-checked?
opciones: That the right-side wires are on the right and the left ones on the left
That the chest wires are hanging clear of the patient's arms
That the four electrodes are all at the same height on the limbs
That the tabs of the electrodes all point down toward the feet
preguntas.explicacion: Before moving on to the chest, the right arm and right leg wires are confirmed on the patient's right and the left arm and left leg wires on the left, each on its matching limb. That single check is what prevents the reversal that turns every complex in lead I upside down.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA, Evacuation Plans and Procedures eTool, Emergency Action Plan: Minimum Requirements [29 CFR 1910.38(b)]
preguntas.subtema: CMA I.B.8.a · 2027 I.B.7.a · CMAA 3 k45 · RMA II.7.c · NCMA 2A.9 EKB 8
preguntas.pregunta: A clinic with 8 employees asks whether its emergency action plan has to be in writing. What is the answer?
opciones: No: with 10 or fewer employees the plan may be communicated orally
No: any employer may keep the plan oral if the staff are trained yearly
Yes: the plan is written whenever the workplace has any employees at all
Yes: only a plan of 25 or fewer employees may be communicated orally
preguntas.explicacion: The plan is normally written down and held at the workplace where employees can consult it; the exception is an employer of 10 employees or fewer, who may pass it on by word of mouth. That is the only exception in the rule; the six minimum elements still have to be covered, and everyone still has to know how to respond.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 18.1 An Overview of Blood, Composition of Blood
preguntas.subtema: CPT Core k4 (applied D5 k87 centrifuging) · PBT I.B.4 · CCMA 3E k122 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A whole-blood sample is spun in a centrifuge. Which component settles at the very bottom of the tube?
opciones: The erythrocytes, the heaviest formed elements
The buffy coat of leukocytes and platelets
The straw-colored plasma, over half the sample
The serum, once the clotting factors are gone
preguntas.explicacion: In a spun sample the heaviest formed elements, the red cells, pack at the bottom; above them sits a thin pale layer of white cells and platelets, the buffy coat; and the plasma, a pale straw-colored liquid, floats on top as the lightest component and makes up more than half of the sample. Serum is not a layer of whole blood: it is plasma minus its clotting factors, obtained only after the blood has clotted.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Phlebotomy", section Equipment
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A k54 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(b) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which of these belongs on the organized collection tray prepared before a venous draw?
opciones: A stirrer for tubes and waterproof transport bags
A centrifuge rotor and a rack of reagent cartridges
A capillary microtube warmer and a slide staining kit
A pair of sterile scissors and a suture removal blade
preguntas.explicacion: The tray is set out with a utility cart, gloves, a collection apparatus with safety measures, a complete series of unexpired tubes in various volumes, a tourniquet, antiseptic, dressings and gauze pads, a waste bin, a stirrer for tubes and waterproof transport bags.

preguntas.fuente: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms, prognosis
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2B k39 · CMA I.A.2.b (2027 I.A.2.d) · RMA I.B.2.a · CMAA 1 k5 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks what the doctor meant by prognosis. Which answer is accurate?
opciones: The likely course of the disease and the chance of recovery or recurrence
The name given to the disease after the exam and the tests are reviewed
The extent of the disease within the body at the moment it is discovered
The cause or origin of the disease that brought the patient to the visit
preguntas.explicacion: A prognosis is what the disease is expected to do: how it will probably run, and what chance there is of recovery or of a return. The distractors are the terms that sit next to it: diagnosis is identifying the disease from its signs and symptoms, staging measures how far it has spread, and etiology is its cause or origin.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Marketing
preguntas.subtema: Marketing and PHI · CCMA 7 k220 · CMA II.E.2.a · RMA I.C.1.b · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A vendor offers to pay the practice for its patient list so it can promote a product. What does the Privacy Rule require?
opciones: An authorization from each patient, and it must reveal the payment involved
A business associate agreement, after which no authorization is needed
A notice in the accounting of disclosures listing the names that were sold
Removal of the diagnoses from the list, after which it may be sold freely
preguntas.explicacion: Marketing means any communication that talks up a product or a service so as to encourage buying or using it, and it also reaches an arrangement where a covered entity discloses PHI for payment, direct or indirect, so that another entity can push its own products. Authorization is required, save for face-to-face marketing between the entity and the individual and for promotional gifts of nominal value; where a third party is paying, the authorization has to say so.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, "Hypothermia", First Aid
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3B11 k81 · CMA I.B.9.n · 2027 I.B.8.n · RMA III.I.1.b · NCMA 2A.10 EKB 15
preguntas.pregunta: How is a patient with hypothermia warmed while help is on the way?
opciones: With warm compresses on neck, chest wall and groin, out of the cold
With a heating pad on the arms and the legs, set to its lowest level
With a hot water bottle on the feet, wrapped in a towel first
With a heat lamp aimed at the chest from a safe distance away
preguntas.explicacion: The patient is moved out of the cold and warmed gently, with warm compresses on the neck, chest wall and groin and the rescuer's own body heat if needed; warm sweetened nonalcoholic fluids can be given if the patient is alert and swallows easily. Heat applied directly is not used, whether from a heat lamp, a heating pad or hot water, and no alcohol.

preguntas.fuente: AHRQ, Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 7: Improve Telephone Access
preguntas.subtema: Telephone etiquette · CCMA 6C k196 · CMAA 2A k27 · NCMA F.23
preguntas.pregunta: A practice is rebuilding the automated menu callers hear. How many options should that menu offer at most?
opciones: No more than five
No more than three
No more than eight
No more than twelve
preguntas.explicacion: A patient-friendly automated system keeps the menu to five choices at most, offers the languages patients commonly speak, and always leaves a way to reach a person, because some callers are intimidated by machines. A confusing system or a long wait makes some patients simply hang up.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Ventricular Tachycardia", Introduction
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3F4 k155 · CMA I.C.10.d(9)(a)(iii) · RMA III.F.6.c.i · NCMA 2D.8
preguntas.pregunta: How is ventricular tachycardia defined on the tracing?
opciones: Three or more consecutive wide beats faster than 100 a minute
Three or more consecutive narrow beats faster than 100 a minute
Two or more consecutive wide beats slower than 100 a minute
Any single wide beat arriving faster than 100 a minute
preguntas.explicacion: It is a wide complex tachycardia of at least three beats in a row above 100 per minute, arising below the atrioventricular bundle. A single early wide beat is an ectopic complex, not a tachycardia, and a narrow complex points instead to a rhythm coming from above the ventricles.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, MLN Booklet: Medicare Billing: CMS-1500 & 837P (MLN006976), Procedure Coding; and CMS, ICD-10 Codes
preguntas.subtema: Procedural coding · CMA III.G.1.c (2027 III.G.1.c) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.7
preguntas.pregunta: Which code set reports the procedures on an inpatient hospital claim to Medicare Part A?
opciones: The procedure coding system of ICD-10, which CMS keeps
ICD-10-CM, which reports the reason for the admission
HCPCS Level II, which names supplies and equipment
HCPCS Level I, which names professional services
preguntas.explicacion: Procedures on inpatient facility claims under Part A are reported with the ICD-10 procedure coding system, which CMS maintains and updates each October. The clinical modification of ICD-10 is for diagnoses, and the two levels of HCPCS carry professional services and the products and supplies billed outside them.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Vancomycin", section Monitoring
preguntas.subtema: CPT D2 2C k45 · PBT II.A II.D · CCMA 3E2 k125 · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2
preguntas.pregunta: A vancomycin trough is ordered and the next dose is due at 10:00. When should it be drawn?
opciones: Within the 30 minutes before the 10:00 dose, at steady state
Immediately after the 10:00 infusion has finished running
Exactly 2 hours after the 10:00 dose has started
At any point between doses, as long as the time is recorded on the tube
preguntas.explicacion: A serum trough is ideally obtained within 30 minutes before a dose is given, under steady-state conditions, which are typically reached after the third dose; the usual target trough is 10 to 20 μg/mL. The peak, by contrast, occurs immediately after the intravenous infusion is completed. A random time between doses is neither.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10 Codes
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · CMA III.G.1.b · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: When do new ICD-10 codes take effect each year?
opciones: October 1, for encounters and discharges from that date onward
January 1, for encounters and discharges from that date onward
July 1, halfway through the federal fiscal year for that update
The date each Medicare contractor loads the files into its system
preguntas.explicacion: Updated diagnosis and procedure codes take effect on October 1: CMS announces the new ICD-10-PCS codes and the CDC the new ICD-10-CM codes, and they apply to discharges and patient encounters from that date. January 1 is the start of the calendar year used for other purposes, and contractors load the files to meet the national date rather than setting their own.

preguntas.fuente: SEER Training Modules, Anatomy & Physiology, Cardiovascular System, Physiology of the Heart, Cardiac Cycle; and Heart (introduction); and OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.3 Cardiac Cycle, Ventricular Systole
preguntas.subtema: PBT I.A.1 · CCMA 2A k37 · CMA I.C.6.g(4) (2027: I.C.6.f(4)) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: At a normal heart rate, how long is one cardiac cycle, and how much blood does the adult heart pump each minute?
opciones: About 0.8 second; about 5 liters per minute
About 0.8 second; about 8 liters per minute
About 0.5 second; about 5 liters per minute
About 0.8 second; about 130 mL per minute
preguntas.explicacion: One cardiac cycle is a single heartbeat, contraction (systole) followed by relaxation (diastole), and at a normal rate it takes 0.8 second; over a minute an adult heart moves around 5 liters. The 130 mL figure is what one ventricle holds at the end of diastole, a volume per beat and not an output per minute, and 0.5 is the daily swing in degrees, not a length of time.

preguntas.fuente: DOL, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Medical Assistants — Licenses, Certifications, and Registrations
preguntas.subtema: Licensure vs certification · CCMA 1A k3 · RMA I.C.2.a · NCMA 4.1
preguntas.pregunta: A medical assistant asks whether certification is required in order to work. What is accurate across most of the country?
opciones: Most states do not require it, though employers may prefer or require it
Every state requires it before a medical assistant may take vital signs
No state may require it, because the credential is entirely voluntary
It is required only in states that also license physician assistants
preguntas.explicacion: Some states do require medical assistants to graduate from an accredited program, to be licensed or certified, or to meet other prerequisites, and the state licensing agency is where to check. Most states do not require certification, but employers may prefer it or insist on it, and several organizations offer it. Some employers also ask for basic life support certification.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Licensed Healthcare Professional; and (f)(1)(ii)(C)
preguntas.subtema: Who does the evaluation · CPT D1 1D 1H k33 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 3C9 k97 · CMA I.B.4.d / 2027 I.B.3.d · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 4.11
preguntas.pregunta: Who may perform the post-exposure evaluation the bloodborne pathogens standard requires?
opciones: A licensed professional whose scope of practice covers vaccination and follow-up
Only a physician licensed in the state where the exposure incident happened
The employer's safety officer, who then signs the written opinion for the file
Any registered nurse in the facility, working under the employer's supervision
preguntas.explicacion: The definitions in paragraph (b) create the term licensed healthcare professional for exactly this: someone whose legally permitted scope of practice lets them independently carry out what paragraph (f) requires, the hepatitis B vaccination and the post-exposure evaluation and follow-up. Paragraph (f)(1)(ii)(C) puts the work in the hands of a licensed physician, or of some other licensed healthcare professional, or of someone they supervise, so it is not confined to physicians, and it is not something a safety officer or an employer may supervise.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5B · PBT III.A.1 · CCMA 3E11 k143 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a · CMA I.C.8.c
preguntas.pregunta: A urine specimen is collected an hour after a contrast-enhanced scan from a patient who jogged to the appointment. Which two readings should be treated with caution?
opciones: Specific gravity, raised by the contrast, and the electrolytes, moved by exercise
Nitrite, raised by the contrast, and the pH, moved by the exercise beforehand
Bilirubin, raised by the contrast, and the ketones, moved by the exercise
Protein, raised by the contrast, and the specific gravity, moved by exercise
preguntas.explicacion: Contrast media can lift the specific gravity falsely, and exercise can shift both the specific gravity and the electrolyte concentration of the specimen. Neither is the laboratory's doing, which is why the collection history counts: an alkaline pH can read as protein, and bacteria multiplying in a pot left standing will fake a positive blood pad while dragging the pH with them.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA Brief 3636, Hazard Communication Standard: Labels and Pictograms, Signal Words and Hazard Statements
preguntas.subtema: Signal words · CPT D1 1A k24 · PBT VI.G.1 · CCMA 3C k107 · CMA I.B.7.b / 2027 I.B.6.b · RMA II.B.7.d.i III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8 · CMAA 3A k41
preguntas.pregunta: A chemical carries two hazards: one warrants the signal word Danger and the other Warning. What appears on the label?
opciones: Only Danger, since one signal word appears and it is the more severe
Both words, each next to its own hazard statement
Only the word Warning, since the less severe word applies to the mixture as a whole
Neither; when hazards conflict the label shows pictograms only
preguntas.explicacion: There are only two signal words. Within a hazard class, Danger marks the more severe hazards and Warning the less severe ones, and a label carries a single signal word no matter how many hazards the chemical has; when one hazard calls for Danger and another for Warning, only Danger appears. The hazard statements, by contrast, are all included, and may be combined to improve readability. Pictograms never replace the signal word; they are a separate required element.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Urine 24-hour volume (003425), How the Test is Performed; and PMC, PMC3936984 Delanghe & Speeckaert, Preanalytical requirements of urinalysis (2014), Use of preservatives
preguntas.subtema: 24-hour labeling · CPT D2 2P k50 · PBT V.B.1 · CCMA 3D4 k113 · CMA I.C.8.a · RMA III.C.4.a.i · NCMA 2C.14
preguntas.pregunta: Which information must the patient write on a 24-hour urine container when the collection is finished?
opciones: Name, the date, and the time the collection was completed
Name, the date, and the time the first void was discarded
Name, date of birth and the volume of each individual void
Name, the test ordered and the preservative that was added
preguntas.explicacion: The patient labels the container with his or her name, the date and the time of completion, and returns it as instructed. The completion time is what defines the end of the timed period; the volume of each void is never recorded separately, because the laboratory measures the total volume of the pooled urine, and any preservative is added and labeled with a hazard symbol by the laboratory, not by the patient.

preguntas.fuente: PMC, "Detection of haemolysis, a frequent preanalytical problem in the serum of newborns and adults" (EJIFCC 2020, PMC7109500), Results and Discussion
preguntas.subtema: CPT D5 5I · PBT III.A.2 · CCMA 3D9 k138 · NCMA 2C.15 · RMA III.C.4.a
preguntas.pregunta: A newborn's serum returns a hemolysis index around 700 and the neonatologist still wants the C-reactive protein. What does the laboratory expect at that level?
opciones: The C-reactive protein would read low, so the figure is not reportable
The C-reactive protein would read high, so the figure is not reportable
The C-reactive protein can be issued with a note, as is done for LDH
The C-reactive protein is unaffected, since hemoglobin interferes optically
preguntas.explicacion: Specific proteins withstand hemolysis better than many routine chemistry analytes, but severe in vitro hemolysis still reaches them: above an index of roughly 622 mmol/L it is underestimated. In 199 newborn samples it was rejected for that reason, and a repeat draw two to five hours later brought the index down and made every result reportable.

preguntas.fuente: MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Blood pressure measurement
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k47 · CMA I.A.1.a · RMA III.E.2.e · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: How often is blood pressure screened in a healthy 25-year-old whose readings run below 120/80?
opciones: Every 3 to 5 years, for adults aged 18 to 39 without other risk factors
Every year, which is the interval used for all adults from the age of 18
Every 3 to 5 years, for adults of any age whose readings are below 120/80
Every 6 months, since a young adult has no baseline established yet
preguntas.explicacion: Adults from 18 to 39 with readings under 120/80 and no other risk factors are checked every 3 to 5 years. Yearly checks are for adults of 40 and over, and for anyone at increased risk, including people who are overweight or have obesity and people already reading 120/80 or higher.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule: Disclosure Accounting
preguntas.subtema: Accounting of disclosures · CCMA 7 k219 · CMA II.E.1.c · RMA II.B.4.f · CMAA 3C k36 · NCMA 4.3
preguntas.pregunta: A patient asks for an accounting of disclosures. What period does it cover, and what is left out of it?
opciones: The six years before the request, leaving out treatment, payment and operations disclosures
The six years before the request, including every release the practice made in that time
The two years before the request, leaving out each release made to a business associate
The whole life of the record, leaving out only disclosures the patient authorized in writing
preguntas.explicacion: The accounting reaches back six years at most from the date of the request. Whole categories never appear on it: disclosures made for treatment, for payment or for health care operations; those to the individual or her personal representative; those for notification, disaster relief or facility directories; those made under an authorization; those of a limited data set; those for national security; those to correctional institutions; and those incidental to a permitted use.

preguntas.fuente: MyPlate, USDA: What is MyPlate?
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1D k25 dietary guidelines · CMA I.A.6.g · 2027 I.A.6.g · RMA I.A wellness and nutrition a · NCMA 2B.21
preguntas.pregunta: How many food groups does MyPlate use to organize a day's eating?
opciones: Five: fruits, vegetables, grains, protein foods, and dairy
Four: fruits, vegetables, grains, and protein foods
Five: fruits, vegetables, grains, protein foods, and oils
Six: fruits, vegetables, grains, dairy, protein foods, and sweets
preguntas.explicacion: MyPlate, which replaced the Food Guide Pyramid in 2011, is built on five groups: fruits, vegetables, grains, protein foods, and dairy along with fortified soy alternatives. Oils are counted and recommended in the healthy pattern but are not one of the five groups, and no group exists for sweets.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.1.1
preguntas.subtema: Equipment assembly · CPT D3 3A · D1 1E k28 · PBT II.J · CCMA 3E3 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.4
preguntas.pregunta: Which part of any blood-drawing procedure is described as the most important, and when is it done?
opciones: Planning ahead, usually at the start of the session
Planning ahead, usually once the patient is seated
Site selection, usually at the start of the session
Site selection, usually once the tourniquet is on
preguntas.explicacion: Planning ahead is called the most important part of any such procedure, and it is normally done as a phlebotomy session begins rather than patient by patient. It sits alongside a suitable location, quality control and the standards of care set for patients and staff.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Anatomy, Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve", sections Introduction and Clinical Significance
preguntas.subtema: Nerve injury · CPT D3 3L k68 k74 · PBT II.I II.K · CCMA 3E13 k131 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.12
preguntas.pregunta: Which area of skin loses sensation when the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve is injured?
opciones: The medial forearm and the skin over the olecranon, stopping at the wrist
The medial forearm and the medial half of the palm, including two fingers
The lateral forearm and the skin over the thumb, stopping at the wrist
The whole forearm and the back of the hand as far as the finger tips
preguntas.explicacion: The nerve supplies the skin of the medial forearm together with the skin overlying the olecranon, and none of the forearm cutaneous nerves cross the wrist, so the hand is spared. Damage during a venipuncture has produced painful paraesthesias, dysaesthesias and numbness in that territory.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Physiology, Fever", Issues of Concern
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k52 · CMA I.A.1.d · RMA III.E.3 Temperature e · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas.pregunta: Average temperatures differ by site. Which order matches the published averages, from lowest to highest?
opciones: Axillary, then oral, then tympanic, then rectal
Oral, then axillary, then rectal, and last tympanic
Tympanic, then rectal, then oral, then axillary
Rectal, then tympanic, then axillary, then oral
preguntas.explicacion: The averages reported by site climb in this order: armpit 35.97 °C (96.75 °F), mouth 36.57 °C (97.83 °F), ear 36.64 °C (97.95 °F) and rectum 37.04 °C (98.67 °F). Reading the same patient at two sites therefore gives two different numbers, and a value without its route beside it cannot be interpreted.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68, 6A · CCMA 5I k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: One code classifies a diagnosis together with the complication it produced. What is such a code, and when is a second one added?
opciones: A combination code; a second is added when it lacks the specificity required
A manifestation code; a second is added because it may never be listed first
A default code; a second is added when the record gives no further detail
A placeholder code; a second is added to fill the seventh character position
preguntas.explicacion: A combination code is one code classifying two diagnoses together, or a diagnosis together with a manifestation associated with it, or a diagnosis together with an associated complication. Only the combination code is assigned where it fully identifies the conditions or where the Index directs it, and an additional code goes on as a secondary one only when the combination lacks the necessary specificity.

preguntas.fuente: HealthCare.gov, Glossary: Balance billing; and Glossary: Allowed amount
preguntas.subtema: Third-party billing · CMAA 4 k61, 6C k87 · CCMA 5L k185 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 23
preguntas.pregunta: A provider charges $100 for a service and the plan's allowed amount is $70. Billing the patient the remaining $30 is called what?
opciones: Balance billing, which a preferred provider may not do for covered services
Balance billing, which any provider may do once the deductible has been met
Coinsurance, which the patient owes as a percentage of the allowed amount
A contractual adjustment, which the provider records as revenue not collected
preguntas.explicacion: Billing the patient the gap between the charge and the allowed amount is balance billing, and the glossary uses this exact arithmetic as its example. A provider inside the network has agreed to the allowed amount and may not bill the difference for covered services, so it happens mostly out of network. Coinsurance is the patient's percentage share of the allowed amount, and the write-off of that gap by a contracted provider is the contractual adjustment.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Abdominal Regions and Quadrants
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 2A k36 · CMA I.C.6.f (2027 I.C.6.e) · RMA I.A.1 · NCMA 1.1
preguntas.pregunta: A patient points to pain in the right lower quadrant. Which line arrangement created that quadrant?
opciones: One horizontal and one vertical line crossing at the umbilicus
Two horizontal and two vertical lines crossing below the ribs
One horizontal line at the ribs and one at the top of the pelvis
Two vertical lines dropped from the midpoint of each clavicle
preguntas.explicacion: The abdomen is divided in two ways. The quadrant method, the one used most in clinical work, uses a single horizontal and a single vertical line that intersect at the navel, giving four quadrants. The more detailed regional method uses two horizontal and two vertical lines and gives nine regions.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Terminating the Therapeutic Relationship", Clinical Significance: Standardized notification
preguntas.subtema: Termination of care · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.d(2)(a) · NCMA 4.9
preguntas.pregunta: How much notice must a patient get before care is terminated?
opciones: The period the state's law sets; 30 days is often treated as reasonable
The period the insurer's contract sets, with 60 days as the minimum
A fixed federal minimum of 30 days, counted from the date of mailing
No fixed period, because notice is an ethical rather than a legal duty
preguntas.explicacion: How many days count as reasonable is a matter for state statutes, health departments and medical boards; 30 days is often considered reasonable, and longer may be needed in rural areas where replacement care is harder to find. Notice always goes in writing, and many states require certified mail with return receipt to the last address on file.

preguntas.fuente: HHS OCR, Genetic Information; and EEOC, Genetic Information Discrimination
preguntas.subtema: Sharing information · CCMA 7E k220 · CMA E.2.a(4) · NCMA 4.3 · CMAA 3C k36
preguntas.pregunta: What do the two titles of the Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act cover?
opciones: Title I covers health coverage; Title II covers employment decisions
Title I covers employment; Title II covers research participation
Title I covers health coverage; Title II covers genetic laboratories
Title I covers hiring; Title II covers promotion, pay and training
preguntas.explicacion: The 2008 law splits in two. Title I bars health coverage from discriminating on the basis of genetic information, and the rules for it are written by the Treasury and by the Departments of Labor and of Health and Human Services. Title II bars it in employment, with enforcement by the commission on equal employment opportunity; it took effect on November 21, 2009.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate", section Interfering Factors
preguntas.subtema: Pre-analytical error · CPT D3 k9 k57 · PBT II.G II.J · CCMA 3E7 k129 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(d) · RMA III.C.4 · NCMA 2C.6
preguntas.pregunta: An ESR specimen is drawn at 08:00 and reaches the analyser at 11:30. Why may the result be reported lower than it should be?
opciones: Testing should begin within two hours; standing changes the red cell shape
Testing should begin within twelve hours; standing dilutes the citrate added
Testing should begin within thirty minutes; standing lets the plasma evaporate
Testing should begin within twenty-four hours; standing warms the specimen up
preguntas.explicacion: Timely handling matters for this test: it should be started within two hours of collection, because red cells that stand too long lose their biconcave shape and stack less readily, which lowers the reading. Anisocytosis and poikilocytosis interfere with stacking in the same direction.

preguntas.fuente: OIG, General Compliance Program Guidance (2023), Element 4: Effective Lines of Communication
preguntas.subtema: Auditing and compliance · CMA III.G.2 (2027 III.G.2) · CMAA 3 k46 · CCMA 7A · NCMA 4.6
preguntas.pregunta: Which written policies does the OIG guidance say should reach every employee so that concerns are actually reported?
opciones: Confidentiality and non-retaliation policies, given out to all employees
The code of conduct and the privacy notice, given out to all employees
The schedule of consequences and incentives, given out to all employees
The risk assessment findings and audit plan, given out to all employees
preguntas.explicacion: The fourth element is about keeping the lines to the compliance officer open. Policies on confidentiality and on non-retaliation should be written and put into every employee's hands, so that people feel able to raise questions and report possible fraud. The guidance adds that whistleblowers ought to be protected from retaliation, a principle the False Claims Act already carries.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010), Annex F, Blood spillage
preguntas.subtema: Spill cleanup sequence · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.e · CCMA 3C5 k108 · CMA I.B.6.b / 2027 I.B.5.b · RMA III.A.2.c · NCMA 2A.9
preguntas.pregunta: In the WHO blood spill procedure, what happens right after the broken glass has been removed with tongs?
opciones: Absorb the fluid with paper towels, wipe with detergent, then apply hypochlorite
Apply hypochlorite directly to the wet blood, then wipe with paper towels
Rinse the area with running water, then discard the towels in regular waste
Remove gloves and wash hands, then record the incident before cleaning further
preguntas.explicacion: The sequence is fixed: put on non-sterile gloves; lift the glass with tongs or with a pan and brush, never by hand, and drop it into a sharps container or, if the pieces are too big, wrap them in paper inside a separate container; soak up as much fluid as possible with disposable paper towels; wipe with water and detergent until nothing is visible; saturate the area with 0.5 percent hypochlorite; rinse the pan, brush and tongs under the tap; take the gloves off; wash with soap and water and dry on single-use towels; and record the incident if a specimen was lost or somebody was exposed.

preguntas.fuente: WHO, Guidelines on Drawing Blood: Best Practices in Phlebotomy (2010), Section 2.2.3, Step 9: Clean contaminated surfaces and complete patient procedure
preguntas.subtema: Labeling · CPT D3 3R k22 · PBT III.B · CCMA 3E12 · NCMA 2C.14 · CMA I.C.7.a(1)(a) · RMA III.C.4.a.ii
preguntas.pregunta: Which set of details does the WHO describe as the information typically required on a specimen label?
opciones: Both names, the file number, the date of birth, and the date and time of collection
First and last names, date of birth, ordering physician and the working diagnosis
First and last names, home address, social security number and time of collection
First and last names, file number, name of the test ordered and the phlebotomist's initials
preguntas.explicacion: Step 9 says the label must be clearly written with what the laboratory requires, which is usually both of the patient's names, the file number, the birth date, and the day and hour the blood was taken; the labels and forms are rechecked before dispatch. Address or social security number are extra identifiers for confirming who the patient is, not as the label content the WHO lists.

preguntas.fuente: CMS, ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY 2026
preguntas.subtema: Diagnostic coding · CMA III.G.1.b (2027 III.G.1.b) · CMAA 5 k68 · CCMA 5G k184 · RMA II.A.3.a · NCMA 3.8
preguntas.pregunta: The note does not say which side was affected, and the coder reaches for an unspecified code. When is that the right choice?
opciones: When the record does not hold enough detail to assign a more specific code
When the record holds detail for which no specific code has been created
When the provider cannot be reached to be queried before the claim goes out
When the payer's own policy accepts unspecified codes on outpatient claims
preguntas.explicacion: A code titled unspecified is the one to use when the record does not hold enough information to assign something more specific. Codes titled other, or other specified, do a different job: they come in when the record does give detail but no specific code exists for it. Where a category carries no unspecified code, the other specified code may serve for both.

preguntas.fuente: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 1.6 Anatomical Terminology, Directional Terms
preguntas.subtema: CCMA 1B k13 · CMA I.C.6.e (2027 I.C.6.d) · RMA I.B.1.a · CMAA 1 k11 · NCMA 1.2
preguntas.pregunta: A note states that the skin is superficial to the bones and the brain is deep to the skull. What do those two terms measure?
opciones: How close a structure lies to the surface of the body
How far a structure lies from the midline of the body
How far a structure lies from the point of attachment
How high a structure lies compared with the head end
preguntas.explicacion: Superficial and deep form a pair about depth alone: superficial is closer to the body surface, deep is farther from it. Distance from the midline is medial and lateral, distance from the trunk within a limb is proximal and distal, and height relative to the head is superior and inferior.

preguntas.pregunta: The tubes are filled and the patient is still in the chair. What is the first of the closing steps?
opciones: Discard the used device into the sharps container
Write the labels for the tubes that have been drawn
Perform hand hygiene once more, ahead of every other step
Place the tubes into the leak-proof transport bag
preguntas.explicacion: The step that closes the procedure opens with discarding the used needle and syringe, or sampling device, into a sharps container a needle cannot pierce. Only then come the label and form check, the sorting of other waste, hand hygiene again, and a last look at the labels before dispatch.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(b), Definitions: Regulated Waste
preguntas.subtema: Sharps containers and regulated waste · CPT D1 k30 k32 · PBT VI.G · CCMA 3C 3C8 k108 · CMA I.B.6.a / 2027 I.B.5.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: Which of the following counts as "regulated waste" under the OSHA standard?
opciones: Gauze caked with dried blood that could release it while being handled
A pair of exam gloves worn for a draw, with no blood on them at all
An alcohol swab used to clean the skin before the needle, with no blood on it
A gauze pad with one dry spot of blood that cannot be released during handling
preguntas.explicacion: The definition covers five things: blood or OPIM (other potentially infectious materials) that is liquid or semi-liquid; items that would release it in that state if squeezed; items caked with dried blood or OPIM that could shed it while being handled; contaminated sharps; and pathological or microbiological waste containing blood or OPIM. The caked gauze is the third case. Gloves and a swab with no blood on them would release nothing if squeezed and are not caked, and a pad with one dry spot that cannot release anything fails the same test: the definition asks for dried blood that is caked AND capable of coming off during handling.

preguntas.fuente: StatPearls, "Urinalysis", section Results, Reporting, and Critical Findings (Chemical Examination: Glucose, nitrite note); MedlinePlus, Medical Tests: Nitrites in Urine; MedlinePlus, Medical Encyclopedia: Leukocyte esterase urine test (003584)
preguntas.subtema: Nitrite sensitivity · PBT IV.A.1 · CCMA 3D3 · CMA I.C.10.a.(2) · RMA III.C.4.b.v · NCMA 2B.19
preguntas.pregunta: A patient with burning on urination has a dipstick that is positive for leukocyte esterase but negative for nitrite. How should the nitrite result be understood?
opciones: A negative nitrite does not rule out infection, because the pad has low sensitivity
A negative nitrite rules out a bacterial infection, because the pad is highly specific
A negative nitrite means the specimen was too dilute for any of the pads to be trusted
A negative nitrite means the leukocyte esterase reaction must have been a false positive
preguntas.explicacion: Nitrite is not normally there at all, and when the pad turns positive it is highly specific for infection of the urinary tract. Its sensitivity is low, though, so a negative nitrite does not rule infection out. Many of the bacteria behind UTIs turn urinary nitrate into nitrite, which is what the pad picks up, and an abnormal leukocyte esterase by itself already points to a possible urinary tract infection.

preguntas.pregunta: A group practice bills Medicare electronically under its group number but registered for eligibility checks under an individual number. What is wrong with that?
opciones: The eligibility enrollment has to carry the same number used to bill claims
The eligibility enrollment has to carry the individual number of each provider
The eligibility enrollment has to carry a separate number issued by a contractor
The eligibility enrollment has to carry the number of the vendor that transmits it
preguntas.explicacion: The enrollment asks for the individual or group National Provider Identifier, whichever one is used to bill Medicare claims electronically. A practice that registered for electronic claims under its group number must use that same group number when it registers to check eligibility. The vendor or clearinghouse supplies its own unique identifier separately, and more than one of those can be linked to a single enrollment.

preguntas.pregunta: Which law turned the sharing of electronic health information into the default expectation, and where do its exceptions live?
opciones: The 21st Century Cures Act of 2016, with the exceptions set out in 45 CFR Part 171
The HITECH Act of 2009, with the exceptions set out in 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C
The Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015, with exceptions in 42 CFR Part 424
The Plain Writing Act of 2010, with the exceptions set out in 45 CFR Part 160
preguntas.explicacion: The 2016 Cures Act turned the sharing of electronic health information into the default expectation and gave the Secretary authority to name activities that are reasonable and necessary and therefore do not amount to information blocking. Those exceptions live in 45 CFR Part 171 and are voluntary: fitting one buys an actor certainty, while missing one does not automatically mean blocking occurred, since every case is judged on its own facts.

preguntas.subtema: CCMA 3A7 k50 · CMA I.A.1.i · RMA III.E.3 Respiration d · NCMA 2B.7
preguntas.pregunta: An adult is breathing 26 times a minute at rest. Which term is charted?
opciones: Tachypnea, the term used once an adult passes 20 breaths per minute
Bradypnea, the term used once an adult falls under 12 breaths per minute
Hyperpnea, the term for breathing that has grown deeper without growing faster
Apnea, the term for the pauses that break up an otherwise regular pattern
preguntas.explicacion: Above 20 breaths a minute the adult is tachypneic; below 12 the term is bradypnea. Tachypnea turns up with exercise and pregnancy, and with sepsis, asthma, pneumonia, diabetic ketoacidosis or a pulmonary embolism, so the term describes the finding and does not name a cause.

preguntas.fuente: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030(d)(2)(xiv) and (g)(1)(i)(H), contaminated equipment
preguntas.subtema: Contaminated equipment for servicing · CPT D1 k32 · PBT VI.G.4.d · CCMA 3C5 k108 · CMA I.B.7.a / 2027 I.B.6.a · RMA III.A.2.c III.C.5 · NCMA 2A.8
preguntas.pregunta: A centrifuge with blood inside its rotor chamber cannot be fully decontaminated before the repair technician arrives. What does the standard require?
opciones: A readily observable label saying which parts remain contaminated, and telling the technician
Sending the centrifuge for service in a red bag, which replaces the label
Decontaminating it anyway, since the standard allows no exceptions for equipment
Recording the contamination in the sharps injury log before the technician touches it
preguntas.explicacion: Paragraph (d)(2)(xiv) requires equipment that may be contaminated to be examined and decontaminated before servicing or shipping, unless the employer can show that is not feasible; in that case (d)(2)(xiv)(A) demands a readily observable label per (g)(1)(i)(H) stating which portions remain contaminated, and (d)(2)(xiv)(B) requires that information to reach the employees concerned, the service representative and the manufacturer before anyone handles it. A red bag substitutes for a label on waste, not on equipment, and the sharps injury log records percutaneous injuries only.

preguntas_es.fuente: StatPearls, "Patient Rights and Ethics", Issues of Concern: Treatment Refusal (by Both Patient and Physician)
preguntas_es.subtema: The provider's refusal · CPT D1 1D k26 · PBT VI.E · CCMA 7E k212 · CMA II.E.4 · RMA I.C.4 · NCMA 4.1
preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Puede un médico negarse a tomar a un paciente o a dar un tratamiento que se le pidió?
opciones: Sí, como cuando el tratamiento no está indicado por la historia que se le dio
Sí, pero sólo donde otro profesional de la salud ya haya aceptado tomarlo
No, una vez que la persona quedó registrada como paciente del consultorio
No, salvo que una emergencia en otro sitio le vuelva imposible la agenda
preguntas_es.explicacion: El derecho corre en las dos direcciones. Un médico puede en muchas circunstancias negarse a entrar en la relación o a dar un tratamiento: puede llegarle un referido para un tratamiento en particular y parecerle que tomarlo no está justificado, o la historia que le dieron puede no indicar el tratamiento del todo. El privilegio es viejo, viene de la época hipocrática, y aun así ninguna ley lo protege tan ampliamente como la profesión reclama, y las leyes que sí lo protegen se apoyan por lo común en la libertad de religión.

preguntas_es.pregunta: Se ajustan unas muletas axilares. ¿Dónde debe quedar la almohadilla del hombro y cómo debe quedar el codo?
opciones: A unos dos dedos por debajo de la axila, con el codo flexionado unos 30 grados
Pegada a la propia axila, con el codo flexionado a unos 30 grados
Unos dos dedos por debajo de la axila, con el codo mantenido casi recto
Unos cuatro dedos por debajo de la axila, con el codo flexionado a 90 grados
preguntas_es.explicacion: La almohadilla queda a unas dos pulgadas, o dos dedos, de la axila con el hombro relajado; el mango se coloca para que el codo se doble unos 30 grados, y las puntas descansan a unas seis pulgadas por fuera de los pies. Se le dice al paciente que nunca apoye la axila en la almohadilla. Los folletos para pacientes dan la separación como de una a una pulgada y media, medida de la misma manera.

preguntas_es.subtema: Glove exception for blood donation · CPT D1 1J k36 · PBT VI.G.4.g · CCMA 3C3 k100 · CMA I.B.4.b / 2027 I.B.3.b · RMA III.A.3.a.ii · NCMA 2A.4
preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿En qué entorno puede un empleador decidir que los guantes no se exigen de rutina en cada flebotomía?
opciones: Un centro de donación voluntaria de sangre, con condiciones como guantes para quien está en formación
Un laboratorio clínico, si aplica las precauciones universales a todas las muestras
Una estación de extracción ambulatoria, si el flebotomista no tiene cortes en las manos
Cualquier centro, si el empleado documenta que los guantes reducen la destreza manual
preguntas_es.explicacion: El párrafo (d)(3)(ix) exige guantes para los procedimientos de acceso vascular con una sola salvedad, la del (d)(3)(ix)(D): el centro de donación voluntaria de sangre cuyo empleador juzga innecesario ponérselos de rutina. Aun ahí el empleador tiene que reevaluar la política de forma periódica, tener guantes disponibles para quien los quiera, nunca desalentar su uso, y exigirlos cuando el empleado tiene cortes o heridas en la piel, cuando la contaminación de la mano es probable —por ejemplo con un donante poco cooperador— y durante la formación en flebotomía. Ningún otro entorno recibe la excepción.

preguntas_es.subtema: Legal terms · CCMA k221 · CMA E.4.c · RMA I.C.3 · NCMA 4.8
preguntas_es.pregunta: En un caso de mala praxis, ¿qué es lo primero que se le pide al testigo pericial médico?
opciones: Establecer el estándar de atención que se aplicaba a ese caso
Establecer los daños que debería recibir la familia del paciente
Establecer si se debería revocar la licencia del demandado
Establecer cuál de las dos partes dijo la verdad en el descubrimiento de pruebas
preguntas_es.explicacion: El papel del testigo pericial (expert witness) en un caso de mala praxis (malpractice) tiene tres partes, y la primera es establecer qué estándar de atención (standard of care) se aplica al caso. Después viene una opinión sobre si la atención se apartó de él y, sólo entonces, si lo hizo, una opinión sobre si eso causó la lesión alegada. Los daños le tocan al jurado, y la licencia es asunto de la junta estatal.

preguntas_es.pregunta: Después de una extracción con un sistema de tubo al vacío, ¿cómo dice la OMS que se deben descartar la aguja y el portatubos?
opciones: Descartar el portatubos y la aguja juntos, como una sola unidad, siempre que se pueda
Desenroscar la aguja a mano y echarla en el recipiente para objetos punzocortantes, quedándose con el portatubos
Volver a tapar la aguja con las dos manos y después quitarla del portatubos para reutilizarlo
Dejar la aguja puesta en el portatubos y poner los dos en la bolsa de desechos regulados
preguntas_es.explicacion: La sección 3.1.1 manda descartar el portatubos (tube holder) y la aguja como una sola pieza donde se pueda; si hay que reutilizar el portatubos, la aguja se quita con la técnica del cucharón (one-hand scoop technique) o con un recipiente para objetos punzocortantes que tenga una ranura para soltarla, siempre con una sola mano. El anexo E añade que una aguja usada al descubierto nunca se desarma con las manos desnudas, y OSHA prohíbe volver a taparla y quitarla con las dos manos, salvo donde no haya otra alternativa posible.

preguntas_es.pregunta: ¿Qué productos quedan fuera del alcance de la guía de la FDA sobre mecanismos de prevención de lesiones por punzocortantes?
opciones: Los recipientes para objetos punzocortantes y los dispositivos para volver a tapar la aguja
Las palomillas y los dispositivos de lanceta retráctil
Las jeringas de insulina y sus capuchones naranjas
Las agujas de recolección de sangre con un protector
preguntas_es.explicacion: Esa guía cubre los dispositivos médicos que llevan una pieza activa o pasiva que resguarda al usuario de una lesión por punzocortante. Dice con todas las letras que no trata los recipientes para objetos punzocortantes (sharps container) ni los dispositivos para volver a tapar la aguja (recapping), que tienen una guía propia aparte.

preguntas_es.subtema: CCMA 3A4 k49 · CMA I.A.1.b(1) · RMA III.E.3 Pulse c · NCMA 2B.6
preguntas_es.pregunta: El latido bajo los dedos es irregular. ¿Cómo se cuenta la frecuencia?
opciones: Durante un minuto entero, porque un conteo más largo es más exacto cuando el ritmo es irregular
Durante 15 segundos multiplicados por 4, lo que agiliza la admisión de pacientes sin perder exactitud
Durante 10 segundos multiplicados por 6, y luego se repite en la otra muñeca para comparar
Durante 30 segundos multiplicados por 2, y luego se redondea al múltiplo de 10 latidos más cercano
preguntas_es.explicacion: Los conteos cortos multiplicados suelen bastar con un pulso regular: 30 segundos por dos, o incluso 10 o 15 segundos por 6 o por 4. Un ritmo irregular rompe ese supuesto, porque los latidos no están repartidos por igual, así que se cuenta el minuto entero. Redondear un valor registrado a la decena más cercana es un error documentado, no una regla.

preguntas_es.pregunta: El panel de coagulación de un paciente vuelve una y otra vez hemolizado. ¿Qué dos rasgos de la extracción se señalan para protegerlo?
opciones: Una venopunción atraumática y el menor tiempo de torniquete posible
Un volumen de tubo grande y un tiempo de torniquete tan largo como aguante la vena
Un paciente en ayuno y una punción puesta sobre la vena basílica
Un segundo tubo de descarte y una aguja más fina que el calibre veintitrés
preguntas_es.explicacion: Para el trabajo de coagulación la punción debe ser atraumática y hacerse sin demora, y el torniquete debe quedarse puesto el menor tiempo posible, porque los dos fallos producen artefactos como la hemólisis. El calibre (gauge) que se sugiere va del diecinueve al veintidós, y para los ensayos de factores se prefiere el extremo más ancho.

preguntas_es.pregunta: El conductor de una clínica lleva las muestras de sangre al laboratorio del hospital cada tarde. Además de una gradilla o un soporte acolchado para los tubos, ¿qué debe llevar el vehículo según la OMS?
opciones: Un kit para derrames de sangre, para poder limpiar sin riesgo una muestra rota por el camino
Una centrífuga portátil, para poder separar el suero si el viaje se retrasa
Una incubadora de dióxido de carbono, para que las muestras de cultivo mantengan viables sus organismos
Un segundo juego de tubos vacíos, para poder volver a recolectar una muestra rota al llegar
preguntas_es.explicacion: Para transportar muestras de sangre fuera de un hospital, la OMS (WHO) pide que el vehículo lleve un kit para derrames (spill kit) de sangre, porque una muestra se puede romper durante el transporte igual que en el área de flebotomía; el derrame se maneja después con guantes y, en los derrames grandes, una bata o un delantal, toallas de papel que van al desecho infeccioso, y una solución de blanqueador recién preparada. Varios tubos viajan en una gradilla o en un soporte acolchado justamente para evitar esa rotura.

preguntas_es.subtema: Gestational screening preparation · CPT D4 4H · PBT II.D patient preparation · CCMA 3E k139 fasting · RMA III.C.4.e · NCMA 2C.2 pre-test conditions
preguntas_es.pregunta: Una paciente citada para el primer paso de la detección gestacional de dos pasos pregunta qué debe hacer con la comida antes. ¿Qué se le dice?
opciones: Ni ayuno ni cambio de dieta: el paso de detección no necesita ninguno de los dos
Nada de comer ni beber, salvo sorbos de agua, durante 8 a 14 horas antes
Comer una dieta libre con 150 g de carbohidratos al día durante 3 días
Comer un desayuno ligero exactamente una hora antes de la cita
preguntas_es.explicacion: Para el paso de detección la paciente no tiene que prepararse ni cambiar su dieta de ninguna manera: bebe el líquido con glucosa y se le extrae sangre una hora después. El ayuno (fasting) de 8 a 14 horas es de la prueba de seguimiento de 3 horas y de la prueba de 75 g de un paso; la carga de carbohidratos de tres días es una condición de la prueba de tolerancia a la glucosa oral diagnóstica fuera del embarazo. Comer normalmente en los días previos es la única indicación que se da.

preguntas_es.pregunta: Un lactante de 4 meses que pesa 5 kg necesita una muestra capilar. ¿Qué sitio indica la tabla 7.1 de la OMS y en qué parte de él se pone la lanceta?

El talón, en la curva posterior, donde la piel es más gruesa
El dedo medio o el anular, en el lado de la yema
El pulgar o el índice, en el lado de la yema
preguntas_es.explicacion: La tabla 7.1 asigna la punción del talón a los lactantes desde el nacimiento hasta unos 6 meses y de unos 3 a 10 kg, y la lanceta va en la superficie plantar medial o lateral; la punción del dedo es para niños de más de 6 meses y de más de 10 kg. El capítulo 7 dice que el talón posterior se debe evitar porque el hueso queda sólo a 2,33 mm de la piel, y la propia tabla advierte contra el pulgar y el índice.

preguntas_es.subtema: Government insurance plans · CCMA 5 k181 · CMAA 6 k74 · RMA II.A.1 · NCMA EKB 25
preguntas_es.pregunta: Una paciente que se muda a otro estado pregunta si su Medicaid funcionará igual allí. ¿Cómo se fijan las reglas?
opciones: El gobierno federal fija pautas generales y cada estado escribe sus propias reglas
El gobierno federal escribe un único conjunto de reglas que rige en todos y cada uno de los estados
Cada estado escribe sus reglas sin ninguna pauta federal de ningún tipo por encima
El mercado de seguros de cada estado escribe las reglas de sus propios planes estatales
preguntas_es.explicacion: Medicaid, un seguro de salud del gobierno, ayuda a muchísimas personas de bajos ingresos a pagar sus cuentas médicas. Las pautas generales del programa vienen del gobierno federal, pero las reglas son de cada estado, y un estado puede pedirle a la persona que pague parte del costo de algunos servicios. La elegibilidad puede depender de la edad, el embarazo, la ceguera, la discapacidad, los ingresos y recursos, y la situación migratoria.

preguntas_es.pregunta: En una venopunción de rutina, ¿qué forma de consentimiento describe obtener el paso 2 de la OMS?
opciones: Consentimiento verbal, después de conversar la prueba con el paciente
Consentimiento por escrito, firmado por el paciente y atestiguado por el personal
Consentimiento implícito, que se ve en la presencia del paciente en la clínica
Consentimiento que da el médico que ordena en el formulario del laboratorio
preguntas_es.explicacion: El paso de la OMS (WHO) dice: converse la prueba que se va a hacer y obtenga el consentimiento verbal, y añade que el paciente puede rechazarla en cualquier punto antes de la recolección. StatPearls describe la documentación por escrito del consentimiento informado en general, pero el paso de flebotomía de la OMS se apoya en un sí hablado después de una explicación. Nada en ninguna de las dos fuentes deja que la firma de quien pide la prueba sustituya a la del paciente.

preguntas_es.subtema: CMA I.A.4.b · CCMA 3A3 · NCMA 2B.4
preguntas_es.pregunta: En el esquema PQRSTU, ¿qué le pregunta al paciente la letra U?
opciones: Qué cree el paciente que le está causando el síntoma con el que vino
Cuánto tiempo ha durado el síntoma y si viene y después se va otra vez
Si hay alguna actividad que mejore el síntoma o que lo empeore
Dónde se siente el síntoma y si se corre hacia algún otro lugar
preguntas_es.explicacion: La U es de understanding (comprensión): le pregunta al paciente qué cree que está detrás del problema. Provocación y paliación cubren lo que lo empeora y lo que lo alivia; región, dónde está y si se irradia; y tiempo, cuándo empezó y si es constante. El esquema se usa para el dolor y sirve igual para la náusea, la comezón o la falta de aire.

opciones: Los vasos más pequeños, de 5 a 10 μm de ancho, que conectan arteriolas y vénulas
Las arterias más pequeñas, de alrededor de 30 μm de ancho, que conectan las arterias con los capilares
Vasos de pared delgada, de 8 a 100 μm de ancho, que llevan la sangre hacia las venas
Venas superficiales que corren en el techo de la fosa cubital del brazo
preguntas_es.explicacion: Los capilares son los vasos más pequeños del cuerpo, de 5 a 10 micrómetros de diámetro, y unen las arteriolas con las vénulas; la muestra capilar se toma por lo común con una punción del talón o del dedo, y en los capilares más estrechos apenas cabe un eritrocito. Las arteriolas promedian 30 micrómetros o menos y las vénulas de 8 a 100 micrómetros, y las venas superficiales de la fosa cubital son sitios de venopunción, no capilares.
